f.d: @#/ /gdams ngag mdzod/ shangs chos pod gnyas pa/ (na)
Shangpa Kagyu: The Tradition of Khyungpo Naljor, Part Two
Tāranātha’s Commentaries on the Six Dharmas of Niguma
@#/ /zab lam ni gu chos drug gi khrid yig zab don thang mar brdal ba zhes bya ba bklags chog ma bzhugs so/ /
1. Tangdalma: Displaying the Profound Meaning. A Guidebook on the Profound Path of Niguma’s Six Dharmas, the One Sufficient Reading[1]
(2)@#/ /na mo gu ru/
namo guru
zab lam ni gu'i chos drug gi khrid yig zab don thang mar brdal ba zhes bya ba/
This is the guidebook on the profound path of Niguma’s Six Dharmas called Displaying the Profound Meaning.
pha bla ma la phyag 'tshal lo/ / gsol ba 'debs so/ / skyabs su mchi'o/ / byin gyis rlobs shig /
Father guru, I bow to you. I supplicate you. I take refuge in you. Grant your blessings.
bla ma dang ni rdo rje 'chang / / tha dad nyid du ma dmigs pas/ / bla ma'i zhabs la phyag 'tshal lo/ / thugs yid dbyer med ngang du gnas/ /
Without a notion of separation between guru and Vajradhara, I bow at the feet of the guru and live with our minds as one.

sangs rgyas chos dang dge 'dun lha zhes jo bo dkon mchog gsum/ / grub mchog dbang po'i tshul 'dzin zhu ba de'i ye shes phyogs brgyar 'bar/ / chos kyi sku las ma g.yos snyan pa'i grags pas sa gsum khyab/ / srid zhi kun dang mnyam nyid khyed la rtag par phyag bgyi'o/ /

The Three Jewels, lords of the gods, the Buddha, the dharma, and the sangha, took the guise of a mighty adept whose timeless awareness of melting bliss blazes in a hundred directions, and whose acclaim fills the three regions without even leaving the dharmakāya, equally serene in both existence and peace: to you I forever prostrate.
man ngag zab mo mtha' yas kyang / / yid ches mngon rtags nyams myong kun/ / dus mtha' 'dir yang 'byung 'gyur ba/ / mkha' 'gro ni gu'i zhal gdams 'di'o/ /
Though profound esoteric instructions are endless, in these end-times, what will produce confidence, signs of success, and experience are the personal teachings of Ḍākinī Niguma.
de la 'dir ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro ni gu'i chos skor 'di dag / spyir mdo rgyud thams cad kyi zab don dgongs 'dus yin la/ khyad par du yang /
These dharma cycles of Niguma, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness, generally summarize the intent of all Sutra and Tantra. {3} More specifically,

mthar thug (3) ston pa rnam pa lnga'i rgyud ces bya ba/ / gtum mo ston pa'i mthar thug dgyes mdzad dang / / las rgya ston pa'i mthar thug 'khor lo sdom/ / sgyu lus rmi lam mthar thug gsang 'dus dang / / 'od gsal mthar thug ma hA mA ya dang / / phrin las mthar thug rdo rje 'jigs byed do/ / ces pa ltar/ rgyud sde lnga'i don gyi bcud phyung ba'i rdzogs pa'i rim pa ches zab mo yin la/

they contain the most profound completion-phase practices drawn from the quintessential meaning of the Five Tantras. As is said: These tantras are known as the five culminations: Hevajra is the culmination of Fierce Inner Heat. Cakrasaṃvara is the culmination of karmamudrā. Guhyasamāja is the culmination of Illusory Body and Dream. Mahāmāya is the culmination of Lucid Clarity Vajrabhairava is the culmination of enlightened activity.

de yang rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas rdo rje 'chang chen po nas/ da lta'i bar du brgyud pa las/ gdams ngag zab mo'i brlan drod ma yal/ byin rlabs chu bo'i bka' rgyun ma nub/ grub thob brgyud pa'i zam ma chad/ nyams dang rtogs pa'i 'char sgo ma 'gags/ chos bdag mkha' 'gro'i bka' rgya ma nyams pa'i man ngag rtsod med grags pa kun khyab de yin/

Moreover, the profound instructions from the lineage that began with the perfect Buddha, Great Vajradhara, until the present have not dried up, the flow of teachings from its river of blessings has not ebbed, the bridge of adepts in the lineage has not collapsed, the doors of rising experience and realization have not closed, and the dharma masters who hold the sealed precepts of the ḍākinī have not been compromised. This, then, is the indisputable esoteric instruction whose fame pervades everywhere.
de lta bu yang / dag pa'i sa la bzhugs pa/ sangs rgyas rdo rje 'chang chen po'i zhal mngon sum du gzigs shing / gsung gi snang ba la spyod pa/ ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro ni gu ma'i zhal nas/
She who dwells on the pure stages, who sees the actual face of Buddha Great Vajradhara, and hears his speech—Niguma, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness—made this pronouncement:

chos 'di shes pa nga dang / slob dpon (4) lwa ba pa min pa rgya gar na yang med/ de las kyang gnyid thun gcig la chos thams cad yongs su rdzogs pa ni/ khyod kho na las gzhan med do zhes dbugs 'byin par mdzad pa/
In all of India, these dharmas are known only to myself and Master Lavapa. {4} Not only that, no one but you has ever received the entire dharma transmission in a single slumber.[2]

grub pa'i dbang phyug khyung po rnal 'byor pa/ mtshan gzhan lo tsA ba tshul khrims mgon por grags pa de nyid sku gsang ba 'dus pa/ gsung ma hA mA ya/ thugs dgyes mdzad rdo rje/ yon tan 'khor lo sdom pa/ phrin las rdo rje 'jigs mdzad de/ ye shes dkyil 'khor lnga'i ngo bo dang gnyis su med par bzhugs la/ de ltar yin par grub thob a mo g+ha badzra chen pos kyang lung bstan pa/ gzhan yang mthar thug lnga dang ldan pa zhes/ mtshan yongs su grags pa de ni chos 'di sgyur ba po yin no/ / chos gzhan rnams kyi lo paN gyi dod longs sku ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro ma nyid dang / mkhas grub chen po sprul pa'i sku de yin cing / de yang rdo rje 'chang chen po nyid nas brtsams te brgyud pa bdun gyi bar du snyan brgyud dang chig brgyud kyi bka' rgyas btab/ de rjes nas chos 'dis sa steng thams cad khyab 'gro bar lung bstan pa ltar dngos su'ang de ltar byung ba yin/

Thus she reassured the mighty adept Khyungpo Naljor, also known as Lotsāwa Tsultrim Gönpo. He was himself of a single essence with the five mandalas of timeless awareness: his body was Guhyasamāja, his speech was Mahāmāya, his mind was Hevajra, his qualities were Cakrasaṃvara, and his awakened activity was Vajrabhairava. That this was so had even been prophesied by the adept Amoghavajra.[3] Khyungpo Naljor is thus also known as Endowed with Five Culminations. That widely renowned person is the translator of this teaching. In contrast to the masters and translators of other doctrines, this one has the saṃbhogakāya ḍākinī of timeless awareness herself [as master] and the nirmāṇakāya great learned adept [Khyungpo Naljor as translator]. Furthermore, for seven generations beginning with Great Vajradhara, the lineage bore the command seal of an aural (or “heard”) one-to-one lineage. It was prophesied that after [the seventh generation], this dharma would pervade everywhere over the land. And so it would actually come to pass.

'dir bka' rgya 'grol ba po 'gro mgon sangs rgyas ston pa'i thugs kyi sras thu bo rnam pa gsum las/ mkhas grub gzhon nu grub dngos kyis khrid yig mdzad pa dang / mkhas grub shangs ston tshul khrims mgon gyi gsung rnams/ mkhas btsun rgyal mtshan 'bum gyis khrid yig tu mdzad nas bla ma nyid la spyan lam du phang ba dang / slob dpon gnas rnying pa a'i seng ge dang / sprul sku rin chen blo gros kyi gsung las byon pa rnams/ gser gling pa bkra shis dpal gyis yig ris su mdzad pa rnams kyang / chos drug gi khrid yig sogs dmigs pa rnams zhus dag (5) pher ba lta bur yod/ spyir chos tshul 'di skor la/ snyan brgyud yi ger 'god pa'i bka' drin che ba ni/ mkhas btsun rgyal mtshan 'bum nyid yin te/ 'di kho nas yi ger mdzad pa mang ngo / / de ltar na/ lugs 'di la tshad mar gyur pa'i mkhas grub rnam pa gsum gyi gdams ngag gi rgyun thams cad rang re'i chos brgyud 'di la tshang bar bzhugs/ nang sel so so nas gyes pa'i brgyud lugs mi 'dra ba nyi shu rtsa bzhi yang 'dir tshang ba lags so/ /

It was Drogön Sangye Tönpa who finally lifted the command seal. He had three senior spiritual sons. The learned adept Zhönu Drup wrote the actual guidance manual and the learned adept Shangtön Tsultrim Gön gave teachings. The learned Venerable Gyaltsen Bum created a guidance manual [based on those], which was presented to the guru himself and verified. Master Nenyingpa, Ayi Senge, and nirmāṇakāya Rinchen Lodrö all came with teachings, which were written down by Serlingpa Tashi Pal. So there were serviceable, edited versions of all the visualizations, such as those of the Six Dharmas. {5} But in general, concerning this dharma system, the most helpful master in committing this aural tradition to writing was the learned and venerable Gyaltsen Bum himself, the single most prolific writer. The standard of authenticity in this tradition is the instructions of the aforementioned three learned adepts. The continuity of those instructions is completely contained in our own present dharma lineage. In addition, there were twenty-four different lineage traditions that diverged from the originals, all of which are also represented here.

skabs 'dir bla ma'i rnam thar rgyas pa lung bklag dgos pa'i dbang du byas na/ rnam thar rgyas pa rang ngag nas bshad mi dgos kyang / rin chen sna bdun gyi lo rgyus che ba ci rigs pa brjod na legs so/ / 'dir mkhas grub chen po khyung po rnal 'byor pa des/ / rgya gar mkhas pa brgya dang lnga bcu'i thugs bcud longs pa nyid kyi phyir/ mdo sngags bshad sgrub kyi chos mtha' yas pa zhig mnga' zhing / gzhan la'ang gsungs tshul rags rim tsam rnam thar na bzhugs pa der gda'/ de rnams kyi nang nas deng sang ma nub par bzhugs pa rnams gzhung bsrangs/ / cha lag gzhan gyis kyang cung zad brgyan te/ shangs pa bka' brgyud kyi chos skor du yongs su grags pa ltar na/ mkhas grub khyung po nyid las byung ba'i chos skor dang / phyis 'phel ba'i chos skor gnyis yod/

At this point, there is no need for me to recount the extensive life stories, given the required reading transmissions for their extensive biographies. Nevertheless, it would be good to mention the appropriate major stories of the Seven Jewels [of the early one-to-one lineage]. The learned great adept Khyungpo Naljor received the spiritual quintessence of one hundred and fifty wise Indian masters, so he retained infinite doctrines of Sutra, Tantra, exegesis, and practice. Only a rough account of how these were taught to others is found in his biography. Of all those teachings, what remains extant these days is the original approach embellished slightly by auxiliary teachings. Thus what is widely known as the Dharma Cycle of Shangpa Kagyu consists of two sections: the dharma cycle produced by the learned adept Khyungpo himself and that which was disseminated later.

dang po la/ ni gu'i chos skor/ su kha'i chos skor/ rdo rje gdan pa'i chos skor/ mai tri pa'i chos skor/ rA hu la'i chos skor/ gzhan man ngag thor bu dang bcas pa rnams yod/ yang na smin byed dbang gi skor/ grol byed lam gyi skor/ rgyab rten lung gi skor/ bka' srung mgon po'i skor/ zhes dbye ba bzhir mdzad pa yang yod pa las/ ye shes mkha' 'gro ni gu nas brgyud pa'i grol byed lam (6) gyi skor la/ rtsa ba ni gu chos drug / sdong po phyag rgya chen po/ yal ga lam khyer rnam gsum/ me tog mkha' spyod dkar dmar/ 'bras bu 'chi med 'chug med de/ gser chos lnga'am/ khrid chen lngar grags pa dang / khrid chung bdun la sogs pa ji snyed cig yod pa las/

The first comprises the dharma cycles of Niguma, Sukhasiddhi, Vajrāsana, Maitrīpa, and Rāhula, along with other miscellaneous instructions. Alternatively, there is a classification into four: the cycle of maturing empowerments, the cycle of the liberating path, the cycle of the supportive scriptural transmissions, and the cycle of the command-guard protectors. Of those, the cycle of the liberating path that derived from Niguma, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness, includes what are known as the Five Golden Dharmas or Five Great Guides: {6} the roots are the Six Dharmas, the trunk is Amulet Mahāmudrā, the branches are the Three Integrations, the flowers are the Red and White Celestial Goddesses (Khecarī), and the fruit is the Immortal and Infallible state. Also there are any number of other instructions, such as the seven lesser guides, and so forth.

dang po chos drug la/ thog ma'i sngon 'gro/ dal 'byor rnyed dka'/ 'chi ba mi rtag pa/ 'khor ba'i nyes dmigs/ las rgyu 'bras/ chos kyi phan yon/ 'bras bu'i bzhugs tshul sogs bstan pa la 'jug pa'i rim pa sogs dang mthun par go bde bar bshad nas cung zad bsgom du gzhug go /

First, for the Six Dharmas, one should explain the initial preliminaries—the difficulty of finding the freedoms and endowments, death and impermanence, the shortcomings of cyclic existence, karmic cause and effect, the benefits of the Holy Dharma, the abiding nature of the fruition, and so forth—in accordance with the Stages of Entering the Doctrine[4] and other sources. Explain [these to the students] in an easily comprehensible style and have them meditate for a bit on these subjects.
khrid dngos
The Actual Guidance
['di] la dbye na/ sngon 'gro dang / dngos gzhi'i khrid gnyis so/ /
dang po
I. Preliminaries
['di] la/ thun mong dang / thun mong ma yin pa gnyis so/ /
dang po
A. Common Preliminaries
['di] la skyabs su 'gro ba dang / sems bskyed pa gnyis so/ /
Teaching Session 1.
de'i dang po skyabs 'gro ni/
1. Going for Refuge

slob dpon gyis spyir skyabs 'gro'i go babs rgyas bsdus 'tshams pa bshad cing / skabs 'dir dmigs pa la/ skyabs 'gro bzhi skor spyi dang mthun pa 'bogs pa'i phyag len yang 'dug mod/ spros pa la dga' ba rnams kyi ror/ de yang ma legs pa ma yin kyang / chos 'di nyid kyi khyad chos zab don skyabs 'gro chig 'gril ma 'di byin rlabs dang ldan pa'i zhal rgyun ma chad pa lags pas/ phyag bzhes rgyun gyi nyams len 'di la mdzad pa yin no/ / de yang dben pa'i gnas su stan bde ba la 'dug / lus gnad spyi dang mthun par bcas/ / sems rnal du phab/ rang gzhan thams cad la gzhig 'grel zhig bcug / ga re bdag dang mkha' khyab kyi sems can thams cad 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal bzod glags med pa/ dus mtha' med par myong dgos pa 'di a tsam ci rang drag snyam du bsam/ da ni 'di las nges (7) bar skyob thub pa'i skyabs zhig dgos par 'dug na/ skyabs gnas dkon mchog gsum gcig tu 'dus pa'i ngo bo mtshan ldan bla ma dam pa las gzhan mi 'dug pas/ rtsa ba'i bla ma kho na la cis kyang skyabs zhu dgos snyam pas/

The preceptor explains the general long or short style of refuge as appropriate. Regarding the visualization on this occasion, while there is certainly the custom of imparting the fourfold refuge in accordance with the general standard, that is for those who like elaboration. Of course, there is nothing wrong with that. However, our dharma tradition boasts a special profound method—refuge rolled into one. This possesses the certain blessings of an unbroken oral transmission, so this continual practice of the lineage masters is what is done. For this, sit on a comfortable seat in a secluded place, assume the standard physical posture, allow the mind to fall naturally, and carefully consider everything about yourself and others. Think about this: “Why is it that I and all sentient beings throughout space have to experience the unbearable sufferings of cyclic existence without end? Alas, what is to be done?” {7} Now, when there is the need of a refuge that is capable of providing assured protection from all this, it is none other than an authentic holy guru who is the single embodied essence of all sources of refuge and Three Jewels. Therefore, think that no matter what, you must request refuge only from your root guru.

rang nyid gang du gnas pa'i yul phyogs khang khyim kun yang dag pa'i zhing du mos/ rang gi mdun gyi nam mkhar seng khri pad+ma nyi zla'i gdan la drin can rtsa ba'i bla ma dam pa nyid sku dngos de ka la bkrag mdangs gzi brjid 'od du 'bar ba/ rang la dgyes pa'i zhal 'dzum bag can/ sangs rgyas kun 'dus/ chos kun 'dus/ dge 'dun kun 'dus/ dngos dang brgyud pa'i bla ma kun 'dus/ yi dam zhi khro rab 'byams kun 'dus/ mkha' 'gro chos skyong srung ma kun 'dus pa'i bdag nyid can yin/ drin can rtsa ba'i bla ma mkhyen snyam pa bya/ de nas rang gi tshe 'di'i dngos kyi pha ma dang / rang la gnod par byed pa'i dgra dang bgegs/ rang nyid gang du gnas pa'i yul phyogs de'i gzhi bdag rnams kyis gtso byas pa'i khams gsum sems can thams cad kyang / nye 'khor phyogs mtshams thams cad khyab par 'khod nas/ rang dang lhan cig tu skyabs 'gro byed par mos te/ ngag tu/

Imagine that everything in the region and building where you are staying is the pure realm. In the space before you, imagine a lion throne with a seat of lotus, sun, and moon, upon which your kind, holy root guru actually appears in real form, radiant and brilliant in an effulgence of light. The guru appears with a smiling countenance, pleased to see you. That guru is the unified epitome of all buddhas, all dharma, all sangha, all actual and lineage gurus, the whole pantheon of peaceful and wrathful deities, and all ḍākinīs and dharma protectors and guardians. Think, “Kind root guru, consider me.” Then imagine that all sentient beings of the three realms—led by your actual parents of this life, hostile enemies and obstructors, and the local ground masters—completely surround you in all cardinal and intermediate directions. Imagine that they go for refuge along with you, saying:

ma nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i sems can thams cad skyabs kun 'dus kyi ngo bo bla ma rin po che la skyabs su mchi ba lags so/ / zhes ci nus su brjod cing / bdag dang sems can thams cad sngon chad 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal sna tshogs pas 'jigs pas/ da ni khyed la skyabs zhu/ skyabs bslu ba med pa khyed la blos ling gis bkal ba lags/ re sa mgon skyabs gzhan na med do/ / thugs rje chen pos bskyab tu gsol snyam pa'i 'dun pa drag po dung dung pa rgyun chags su bya/ (8) thun 'jog khar skyabs yul bla ma de la mos gus dung pa byas pas/ de nyid 'od du ltem ste zhu nas rang la thim/ bla ma dang rang sems dbyer med du mos/ de ka'i ngang du cung zad mnyam par bzhag / de ka la thun mtshams byed na/ dge ba byang chub tu bsngo/ dmigs skor gcig go /

All sentient beings, my mothers, equal to the reaches of space, go for refuge in the precious guru, the unified essence of all refuges. Repeat that as much as you can and think, “Until now, I and all sentient beings have lived in fear of the myriad sufferings of cyclic existence. Now, we ask you for refuge. We place our complete trust in you as our unfailing refuge. We have no other hope, no other protector, no other refuge. Please, out of compassion, grant us refuge.” Supplicate in this way with constant intense yearning again and again. {8} At the end of the session, foster strong intentional devotion to that guru, the object of your refuge. This causes the guru to fill up with light and then melt and dissolve into you. Imagine that your mind is inseparable from the guru. Rest in equipoise for a while in that state. If there is to be a session break, dedicate the merit to awakening. This is one round of visualization.
Session 2.
gnyis pa sems bskyed ni/
2. Arousing the Mind of Awakening
sngar ji skad bshad pa'i skyabs 'gro de sngon du btang nas/ slar yang rang gzhan snod bcud/ nam mkhas gar khyab sems can gyis khyab pa rnams la blos gzhig 'grel bcug ste/

First complete taking refuge as it was explained before. Again have [the students] consider themselves and others, the environment and its inhabitants, and the sentient beings that pervade wherever space pervades as follows:

ga re nam mkha' 'dis gar khyab sems can gyis khyab par 'dug / 'di thams cad re re nas pha dang ma dang mdza' bshes su ma gyur pa cung zad kyang med/ de yang lan re tsam ma yin gyi/ skye ba dpag tu med par pha ma sogs su gyur pa yin/ 'di rnams 'dod ni bde ba 'dod kyang / myong ni sdug bsngal 'ba' zhig myong ba cis kyang snying re rje/ de bas na 'di rnams sdug bsngal med cing bde ba dam pa la bdag gis 'god par bya/ mthar thug pa na 'di rnams kyi sgrib gnyis bag chags dang bcas pa sbyangs nas/ rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang la 'god dgos par 'dug / de yang thabs gzhan gyis mi nus pas bdag gis sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang thob par bya/ sangs rgyas de yang dam pa'i chos kyi don bsgom pa las 'byung ba'i phyir/ da res zab lam mthar thug chos drug zab mo 'di bsgom snyam du bsam/

Why is it? Wherever space pervades is also pervaded by sentient beings, each of whom has been my father, mother, and friend without exception. Not just once, but for innumerable lifetimes they became my parents. The desire they all have is for happiness, yet their experience is only that of suffering. How pitiful! Therefore, I must establish them in true happiness that is free of suffering. Ultimately I need to establish them in the state of perfect buddhahood once their twofold obscurations and habitual patterns are purified. There is no way to do that unless I myself attain buddhahood. And since buddhahood arises from meditating on the meaning of the Holy Dharma, I will now meditate on these profound Six Dharmas, the culmination of the profound path.

ngag nas 'di skad ces/ nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i sems can thams cad kyi don du/ rnam pa thams cad mkhyen pa rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang thob par bya/ de'i phyir du zab lam ni gu'i chos drug nyams su blang bar bgyi'o/ / zhes brjod de/ don yid la bsam dgos pas/ tshig de yang dal bus brjod cing nan tan cher bya/ thun gyi dngos (9) gzhi'i nyams len de kho na bskyar gyin bsgom pa yin/ thun gyi mjug tu dge ba byang chub tu bsngo ba re yang dgos pa lags/ dmigs skor gnyis pa'o/ /

Say the following: All sentient beings, equal to the reaches of space, must attain the state of an all-knowing perfect buddha. To that end, I will practice the profound path of Niguma’s Six Dharmas. Repeat those words slowly and with great emphasis while contemplating the meaning. {9} Spend the main part of the session meditating only on that practice repeatedly. At the end of every session, you must dedicate the virtue to awakening. This is the second round of visualization.
gnyis pa thun mongs ma yin pa'i sngon 'gro la/
B. Uncommon Preliminaries
dag byed a'i stong ra dang / stong ra nad gdon sel byed/ rtags gsum stong ra'i khyad par te/ rtsis 'go gsum du dbye ba yin/
The Purifying A of Inner Space, the inner space that dispels sickness and spirits, the special inner space of three signs this is divided into three headings.
Session 3.
dang po ni/
1. The Purifying A of Inner Space

dmigs chen yin te/ de yang sngar bshad pa'i skyabs 'gro dang sems bskyed lan bdun bdun tsam re sngon du btang nas/ slar yang rang gi spyi bor gdan bzhi rdzogs sam/ ji ltar 'os pa'i gdan la/ bla ma sku dngos de ka gsal btab nas/ mos gus kyi gdung shugs dang 'brel bas/

This is the principal visualization. First repeat the taking of refuge and arousing of the awakening mind as it was explained before, seven times each. Again imagine above your head the complete fourfold seat or whatever seat is suitable, and visualize the actual form of the guru there. In connection with intense feelings of devotion, repeat:

dus gsum sangs rgyas thams cad 'dus pa'i ngo bo bla ma rin po che/ sems can thams cad kyi don du/ bdag gi nad gdon thams cad zhi bar mdzad du gsol/ sdig sgrib thams cad 'dag par mdzad du gsol/ ting nge 'dzin khyad par can rgyud la skye bar mdzad du gsol/ ces gsol ba dos drag la yun ring du btab/

Precious guru, unified essence of all buddhas of the three times: for the sake of all sentient beings, I pray to you to pacify all my sickness and spirits, to purify all my negative acts and obscurations, and for special meditative absorption to arise in my being. Supplicate fervently and for a long time.

mthar bla ma 'od du zhu nas rang la thim/ de yan chad 'di'i dgos kyi sngon 'gro bla ma'i rnal 'byor yin/ de yang spyi bo nas zhugs te thim pas/ klad pa gti mug gi rang bzhin can de yal ba'i tshul gyis sbyangs/ thod pa dung khang gi gzhal yas khang lta bur gyur gsung ste/ don dngos ni/ rang tha mal du gsal ba'i lus ma 'di/ da lta'i gdos bcas 'di ga yin pa la/ mgrin pa yan chad phyi dbyibs rnam pa de ka yin kyang / nang sha khrag rus gsum spangs pa smos ci dgos/ phyi pags pa'i skya ri yang shin tu srab pa chu'i lbu ba lta bu kha dog dkar ba zhig tu bsam/ mgo bo'i nang du chos 'byung dkar po gru gsum pa/ khong stong dwangs gsal shel (10) bgyi snod lta bu/ rtsa ba phra ba thur du bstan pa mgrin pa'i mtshams su slebs/ gdengs ka che ba gyen du bstan pa la zur gsum yod pa'i zur gcig smin phrag gi thad dang / zur gzhan gnyis rna mchog g.yas g.yon gyi ltag tsam du nang nas pags pa la reg ge yod pa'o/ /

In the end, the guru melts into light and dissolves into you. The description up to this point was for the preliminary practice of guru yoga required in this meditation. Beyond that, [visualize that as the light] enters the top of your head and dissolves, it refines by way of getting rid of the brain, which has the nature of stupidity. It is said that the cranium becomes like a bone-mansion palace. What that actually means is that this body that you have regarded as ordinary solid matter, while it retains its same shape above the neck, inside has become not only devoid of flesh, blood, and bone but you imagine even the external skin as a very soft, faint outline like [the skin of] a water bubble, white in color. {10} Within the head is a white, tetrahedral source of phenomena, empty inside, radiant, and clear like a crystal vase. [It stands upside down], with its sharp apex facing downward, touching the juncture of the throat. The broad side with its three vertices faces upward with one vertex level with the eyebrows and the other two vertices at the temples by the right and left ears, just touching the inside of the skin outline.

chos 'byung de'i nang g.yas g.yon mdun rgyab gang la yang ma yo ba'i dbus drang thad du/ bla ma dang rang sems dbyer med spros bral skye med mtshon pa'i a yig dkar po dwangs gsal 'od kyi rang bzhin can 'od dkar po shin tu 'tsher ba 'phro ba/ chos 'byung gi kha mtshams dang a yig gi mgrin pa'i nyeg mtshams mtho dman mnyam pa tsam bsgom gsung / gang ltar a yig gi mgo bo chos 'byung gi kha mtshams las mtho nges pa bsgom/ /

Right in the center of that source of phenomena—not veering at all to the right, left, front, or rear—is a white letter A (ཨ) as the embodiment of your unborn, unembellished mind inseparable from the guru. It is radiant and clear, the intrinsic nature of light, and radiates extremely bright white light. It is taught that you should meditate on the height of the opening rim of the source of phenomena as level with the juncture of the “neck” of the A letter. In any case, the “head” of the A is definitely visualized as being higher than the rim of the source of phenomena.

thog mar de lta bur sgrims te 'bad pas gsal btab nas/ de rjes shes pa grims lhod ran po gcig gis/ a yig chos 'byung dang bcas par cung zad sems 'dzin/ de rjes a thung gi bzlas pa lan nyer gcig tsam shub shub por bzlas pas/ a las bdud rtsi'i rgyun sbom po dkar la dwangs pa 'od 'phro ba shugs dang ldan pa babs/ skad cig la chos 'byung mer gyis khengs nas chos 'byung gi kha'i phyogs thams cad nas zham zham byung / lus kyi dbus thog thag tu shugs dang ldan par song / 'khor ba thog ma med pa nas bsags pa'i sdig pa dang sgrib pa/ gnas skabs kyi 'gal rkyen nad gdon bar chad dkor sku glud dam tshig 'gal 'khrul la sogs pa thams cad phyir bdas par bsam dgos/

First clarify that with concentrated effort, but afterward focus lightly on the letter and source of phenomena with your consciousness balanced between concentration and relaxation. After that, quietly recite short A twenty-one times. This causes a thick stream of white, radiant, shining elixir to fall from the A. In an instant it fills the source of phenomena to the brim and splashes over the opening on all [three] sides, all the time surging to the center of the body. You must imagine that it pushes out the negativities and obscurations accumulated since beginningless cyclic existence, as well as all temporary adverse conditions, sickness, spirits, obstacles, [corruption from] misappropriated funds and sale of images, contraventions and errors in sacred pledge, and so forth.

sdig sgrib la dngos su kha dog med kyang dmigs pa gsal ba'i phyir dang / rten 'brel nus pa sna tshogs pa'i khyad par gyi phyir/ sdig sgrib sogs de dag thams cad dud khu'am sol khu lta bu'i rnam pas/ rgyun sbom pa rnams bu ga dgu nas mi shong (11) tshad par 'gro ba dang / 'bring po rnams rkang lag gi sen mo'i phrag dang / phra ba rnams skra'i rtse mo dang ba spu'i khung bu tshun chad nas kyang nag nu ru ru thon 'gro bar bsam/ de yang bdud rtsi dwangs gsal gyi rgyun gang du slebs pa'i mtshams de nas/ nad gdon sdig sgrib rnams sdod dbang med par steng nas 'og tu bdas 'gro ba dang / dbus nas mtha' la bdas 'gro bar bsam/

Negative acts and obscurations don’t actually have any color, but for the clarity of the visualization and because of the variety of special efficacious interdependent connections, those negativities, obscurations, and such take on a form like liquid smoke or liquid coal. {11} The very heavy streams that cannot flow out of the nine orifices break up—medium streams flow out from underneath the fingernails and toenails, while thin streams flow out from the tips of the hairs and pores. Imagine dark, winding streams exuding from the body. Imagine that at the borders of wherever the radiant and clear elixir reaches, any sickness, spirits, negative acts, and obscurations are unable to remain and are pushed down from above and out to the edges from the middle.

lus kyi sha khrag rus pa sogs mi gtsang ba'i rdzas thams cad kyang zhu ba ltar song nas/ sdig sgrib rnams dang lhan cig tu gar song med pa'i tshul gyis dag / de ltar lus kyi nang thams cad bkrus/ yang bdud rtsi'i chu rgyun skra dang ba spu'i rtsa ba nas phyir song ba rnams kyis lus kyi phyi nas kyang bkrus/ lus dwangs gsal dkar ba pags pa'i skya ri tsam la shel snod srab mo 'dra ba/ nang bdud rtsi dwangs gsal gyis gang ba'am/ yang na 'ja' 'od dkar po las grub pa lta bur song bar bsam/ phyi la bdas pa'i nad gdon sdig sgrib rnams nag bun nu nu sa 'og thag ring por song zhing / de yang yal bar bsam/ de dag dmigs pa 'jur po bar ma chad par bsgoms pa'i rjes la/ ngal gso ba'i tshul gyis shes pa dar cig klod la bzhag /

All impure physical substances—such as the flesh, blood, and bones—also disperse, as if melted away, vanishing together with the negativities and obscurations, thereby purified. In this way, the inside of the body is washed. Again, the elixir flows out of the roots of your hairs and pores, cleansing the body’s exterior. It becomes radiant clear white with just a faint outline of skin, like a polished crystal vase. Imagine that the body is filled with radiant clear elixir or else that it is made out of white rainbow light. The black ooze of sickness, spirits, negativities, and obscurations that passed outside falls far underground. Imagine that it too disappears. After you meditate vigorously with those visualizations, relax for a while to refresh yourself.

de yan chad dmigs pa tshar gcig yin/ bla ma'i rnal 'byor thun mgo'i de kas chog pas thun de nang du slar skyor mi dgos/ dmigs pa dngos gzhi de yang yang bskyar gyin bsgom/ de yang dper na thun re'i nang du dmigs pa lan brgya rtsa tsam/ thun yang bzhi lnga drug tsam bsgom thub na/ zhag bdun sogs la rtags myur bar 'ong / des mtshon te rang gi rtsol ba rab 'bring tha gsum dang sbyar ba'i rtags myur bul gyi khyad par 'byung ba yin no/ / 'di'i sdig sgrib dag par bsam pa'i skabs/ (12) lus thogs med 'ja' tshon lta bur sgom na gsal nyams 'char rig pa dwangs/ bdud rtsis gang bar sgom na lus zungs bzang / shel gong g.ya' dag pa lta bur sgom na/ rmi lam gsal snang skye ba yin gsung ngo / / dmigs skor gsum pa'o/ /

The above constitutes a single visualization. The guru yoga done at the start of the session is sufficient in itself—you needn’t repeat it within that session. The main visualization should be repeated again and again. So, for example, in one session you could do the visualization a hundred times. Then if you can meditate that way in four to six sessions a day, signs will show quickly in a week or so. As this indicates, the speed with which the signs occur is connected with the degree of effort you put into it—whether best, middling, or least. In terms of contemplating the purification of negative actions and obscurations, {12} it is said that if you meditate on the body as unimpeded like a rainbow, then experiences of clarity will arise and awareness will be lucid. If you meditate on being filled with elixir, the body’s vital energy will be excellent. If you meditate on the body as a pure crystal ball, lucid appearances will arise in dreams. This is the third round of visualization.
Session 4.
gnyis pa stong ra nad gdon sel byed
2. The Inner Space That Dispels Sickness and Spirits

['di] la/ nad sel ba dang / gdon sel ba gnyis yod/ de re re la yang dbye ba du ma yod mod kyi/ so sor na dmigs phran yang yin/ spyir nas dag byed a'i stong ra'i las tshogs tsam yin pas/ yongs bsdoms nas dmigs chen gcig gi dod du brtsi dgos/

There are two parts: dispelling sickness and dispelling spirits. Although they each have many subdivisions of individual minor visualizations, generally they are just applications of the Purifying A of Inner Space and should be counted all together as the equivalent of one major visualization.

de yang nad tshad pa lta bu la/ a las bdud rtsis rgyun kha dog dkar ba/ reg bya dang nus pa gnyis kar bsil ba'i rgyun babs te/ tsha ba'i gnas stod kyi yul lam/ gang nas de ka nas bu ga har re byung sgo de ka nas nad tsha ba de yang dmar 'dur 'dur phyir bdas par bsam/ de bzhin du nad grang ba la/ bdud rtsi kha dog dmar po reg bya dang nus pa gnyis ka tsha ba babs te/ grang ba'i yul ro smad kyi cha'am/ gang nas nas brdol te nad thams cad dkar 'dur 'dur thon par bsam/ rlung gi nad la bdud rtsi kha dog ser ba mar khu ltar bcud dang ldan pa babs/ lus kyi cha thams cad dam/ 'og sgo gnyis sam/ gang na sar bu ga byung ste/ nad rnams sngo 'dur ba'am nag 'dur gyis thon par bsam/ yang na rlung 'tshub ma'am du ba lta bur bun bun thur du 'gro bar bsam/ snying rlung la snying gi thad ka nas bu ga byung ste/ de nas 'gro bar bsam/ des mtshon nas nad gzhan thams cad la yang rigs 'gre/

Now, for something like sicknesses of heat, visualize a white stream of elixir flowing from the A. It is soothing both to the touch and in its cooling potency. The stream falls to the site of the heat, whether it is in the torso or elsewhere. Imagine that in that place, a hole opens up and the heat sickness in the form of red ooze is pushed out through that opening. Similarly, for sicknesses of cold, a stream of red elixir with both warming properties of touch and potency falls to the cold sites, whether in the lower body or wherever. Think that all the sickness as white ooze issues forth from those places and passes outside. For sicknesses of the winds, yellow elixir, like ghee, with properties of refined nutrients, descends. Imagine that a blue or black ooze of sickness exudes from all parts of the body, or from the two lower orifices, or wherever a hole opens up. You can also think of the sickness exiting downward like swirling winds or billowing smoke. For sicknesses of the heart, imagine that a hole opens up at the heart level and the sickness leaves from there. All other sicknesses are dealt with following these examples.

yang dmigs pa'i gzhi dag byed stong ra bzhin bsgoms nas/ a las khro bo so so'i sku'i rnam pa can gyi bdud rtsi ser ba drag po ltar 'bebs pa dang / khro chung gi tshogs dpag tu med pas lus kyi nang (13) go mtshams med par gtams/ me lce yang spros te thur dang phyogs mtshams su 'bar ba dang / bdud rtsi khro chu bzhu ba'i rgyun lta bu yang 'bebs te/ sngags kyi sgras skrag pa dang / mtshon cha brdeg pa dang / me ris sreg pa sogs kyis gdon gyi ris srog chags sna tshogs pa'i gzugs can de rnams lus kyi nang du sdod dbang med par phyir bskrad de/ phyi rol de nyid du tshar bcad cing / lhag ma tsam yang ma lus par bsam mo/ / gdon so so'i gnyen por khro bo gang dgos pa ni/ 'og gang 'dul gyi skabs dang 'dra'o/ / khro bo dang me dang khro chu lta bu ste spro ba gsum po dus gcig tu mi yong bas rim can du bya'o/ / dmigs skor bzhi pa'o/ /

Again, after you meditate on the main visualization of the Purifying A of Inner Space, imagine that elixir in the form of individual wrathful deities descends from the A like a fierce hailstorm. Innumerable hordes of small wrathful figures pack the inside of your body with no space between them. {13} Tongues of flame emanate, blazing downward and in all directions. Then a stream of molten bronze elixir descends. Frightening mantras, pounding weapons, burning mountains, and so forth drive out the bad spirits, who, without the power to remain inside your body, flee in the form of various embodied creatures. Imagine that, once outside, they are killed without any remainder. Wrathful deities needed as antidotes for particular spirits are described below in the section on taming (session 30). Those three emanations—wrathful deities, fire, and molten bronze—cannot be done at the same time, so do them consecutively. This is the fourth round of visualization.
Session 5.
gsum pa rtags gsum stong ra'i khyad par ni/
3. The Special Inner Space of Three Signs

dag byed a'i stong ra bsgoms pas sdig sgrib dag pa'i rtags rab dngos su shar ba ni/ 'di bsgoms pa kho nas lus ldang ba yang ba dang / shes pa gsal ba dang / rgyud 'jam zhing blo khug par 'ong / chags sdang sogs nyon mongs chung du 'gro ba dang / dad pa snying rje shes rab sogs rang shugs kyis cher song na'ang yin/ 'bring gnyid sad dus 'khrul snang nyams kyi tshul du 'char ba dang / tha ma rmi lam gsal por 'char ba la khrus byas pa dang / nam mkha' la 'phur ba dang / gos dkar po gyon pa la sogs pa'o/ /

The best signs of the purification of negativities and obscurations arise as actual phenomena after meditating on the Purifying A of Inner Space. Through this meditation alone, your body will become light when rising, consciousness will become clear, your character gentle, and your intellect tamed. Afflictions such as attachment and aggression will diminish; faith, compassion, wisdom, and other qualities will automatically increase. The intermediate signs will be experienced as part of the deluded appearances of waking life, while the lesser signs will arise similarly in clear dreaming: washing, flying in the sky, wearing white clothes, and so forth.

stong ra nad sel byed bsgoms pa'i nad thon pa'i rtags rab ni/ nad dngos su sangs pa yin/ 'bring nyams dang / tha ma rmi lam la 'khru skyugs dang / lus las rnag khrag thon pa sogs byung na yin/ stong ra gdon sel byed bsgoms pas/ gdon gyi gnod pa sel ba'i rtags rab/ dngos su nyer 'tshe zhi/ lus sems dga' bde skye/ bag dro'u re ba yong / 'bring nyams dang / tha ma rmi lam la/ srog chags gdug (14) pa can bcom pa dang / rang nyid dgra las rgyal ba dang / lus las srog chags thon pa la sogs pa 'byung ngo / /

Through your meditation on the Inner Space That Dispels Sickness, the best sign of having expelled the sickness is that you are actually cured. The intermediate sign is to experience, and the least sign is to dream, that you have diarrhea and vomiting, pus and blood being expelled from your body, and so forth. After you meditate on the Inner Space That Dispels Spirits, the best signs of having dispelled the harm done by spirits are that dangers are actually pacified, joy and well-being arise in body and mind, and a positive attitude develops. {14} The intermediate experience and the least dream signs are of vanquishing vile creatures, being victorious over one’s enemies, vermin leaving one’s body, and so forth.

de la rtags gsum ni sdig sgrib dag pa'i rtags/ nad sel ba'i rtags/ gdon sel ba'i rtags te gsum po de yin la/ de re re la yang dngos dang / nyams dang / rmi lam gyi dbye ba gsum gsum ste/ nad sel rtags kyi dbye ba dgur 'byung ba yin no/ /

Those three signs are the signs of purifying negativities and obscurations, the signs of dispelling sickness, and the signs of dispelling spirits. Each of those is also divided into three: actual, experiential, and dream signs, a total of nine subdivisions of the signs.

de la dang por rtags yong du re ba mi bya/ rtsis btab med par 'jog dgos/ rtags byung na zhen pa dang / rloms sems dang / dga' mi dga' byed du mi rung / 'di lta bu rten 'brel snang ba ma 'gags pa'i 'char sgo tsam yin gyi/ don gang du'ang ma grub pa sgyu ma lta bu'o/ / zhes re dogs spangs te bzhag pas/ slad kyi bar chad mi 'byung zhing lam du 'gro ba yin no/ / dngos kyi rtags rnams byung na des khyab/ sad dus kyi nyams la gsal snang du shar ba yin na/ lan cig shar ba kho nas rtags su byed/ rmi lam tsam la nges pa med pas/ shin tu gsal ba dang / lan mang du byung ba dang / sad nas kyang blo'i mdangs 'gyur tshabs che bar byung na rtags su byed pa lags so/ / rtags kyi rnam gzhag rgyas par yig rnying na gsal/ 'di la dmigs thun bcad pa'i dmigs pa med kyang / rtags shar ba lam du srol tshul de ka dmigs pa yin pas/ dmigs skor lnga pa'o/ /

In the beginning, do not hope for those signs to happen; just keep practicing without expectations. When signs do occur, do not become attached, conceited, or inappropriately happy or sad. Think, “Such signs are just the avenues for the appearance of unimpeded interdependent connections. There is no real meaning, it is just illusion.” Let go of hopes and fears and settle down. Then obstacles will not arise later and you will travel the path. The appearance of actual signs [of purification] stands on its own. If experiences that arise in the waking state appear clearly, then even a single occurrence may be considered as a sign. It is not so definite for dreams, but if the signs are extremely clear, occur repeatedly, and there is a noticeable change in your mental health when awake, then they can be considered genuine signs. An extensive presentation of signs can be found in the old books. Here, this visualization session does not actually contain a visualization, but the customary way to apply the arising of signs on the path does constitute a visualization. So this is the fifth round of visualization.
gnyis pa dngos gzhi
II. Main Practice Instructions

['di] la/ gtum mo/ sgyu lus/ rmi lam/ 'od gsal/ 'pho ba/ bar do ste drug yin la/ de dag kyang rang rang gi byed las che ba dang bcas pa brjod na/ thabs lam bde drod rang 'bar/ sgyu lus chags sdang rang grol/ rmi lam nying 'khrul rang dag / 'od gsal gti mug rang sangs/ 'pho ba ma bsgoms sangs rgyas/ bar do rgyal ba longs sku'o/ /

There are six parts: Fierce Inner Heat, Illusory Body, Dream, Lucid Clarity, Transference, and Intermediate State. If these are listed with their principal functions, they are (1) the Path of Methods, naturally blazing bliss-warmth; (2) Illusory Body, naturally liberated desire and anger; (3) Dream, naturally purified double delusion; (4) Lucid Clarity, naturally clarified stupidity; (5) Transference, buddhahood without meditation; and (6) Intermediate State, the victors’ saṃbhogakāya. {15}
de la
A. Naturally Blazing Bliss-Warmth, the Path of Methods
dang po thabs lam bde drod rang 'bar la/ (15) gtum mo nyid kyi sngon 'gro dang / dngos gzhi dang / rjes gsum mo/ /
First, the natural blazing of bliss and warmth on the path of methods has three parts: (1) the preliminary, (2) the main practice, and (3) the concluding practices.
Session 6.
dang po ni/
1. Preliminary

spyir khrid kyi dngos gzhi yin kyang / gtum mo rang gi dngos gzhi la ltos pa'i sngon 'gror 'gyur bas/ sngon 'gro lus gnad ma'i stong ra zhes bya/ drod shin tu myur bas gtum mo me rgod kyi dmigs pa zhes kyang bya ste/ de la yang skyabs sems sngon du btang nas/ thog ma'i sngon 'gro bla ma'i rnal 'byor cig dgos pas/ rang lha skur sgom pa'am/ re zhig tha mal pa'i nga rgyal gyis kyang rung ste/ spyi bor gdan bzhi rdzogs su bsgoms pa la/ gtum mo'i skabs 'dir sna tshogs pad+ma mi byed/ pad+ma dkar por bsgom/ der bzhugs pa'i bla ma yang sku dngos su sgom na yang sku mdog dkar ba/ 'od zer dkar po 'phro bar bsgom/ rdo rje 'chang du sgom na yang / sku mdog ston zla ltar dkar bar bsgom mod/ chos drug gi skabs thams cad du/ bla ma sku dngos su bsgom pa nyid gtso che ba yin gsung nas phyag len 'debs par mdzad/ lar sku dngos kyi rnam pa la mos sam/ rdo rje 'chang gi rnam pa la mos/ gang la mos pa de nyid sku bde ba'i nyams rgyas shing / zhal 'dzum bag dang ldan pa/ rang la byin gyis rlob rlob 'dra ba cig bsgom/

In general, this is the guide for the main practice, but in terms of Fierce Inner Heat itself, it has its own preliminary called the Inner Space of Fire, the vital point of the body. It is also called the Fireball [or Wildfire] visualization of Inner Heat since it accelerates the generation of heat. In this practice, after you go for refuge and arouse the awakening mind, it is necessary to meditate on guru yoga as the initial preliminary. Therefore, meditate on yourself in the form of the deity, or sometimes it is appropriate to maintain pride as an ordinary person. Meditate as before on the complete fourfold seat above your head, but in this case of Fierce Inner Heat, the lotus in the seat is white rather than multicolored. If you meditate on the actual form of the guru who sits upon it, meditate that the guru is also white in color and radiates white light. If you meditate on the guru as Vajradhara, then definitely meditate on him being white like the autumn moon. On all occasions in the Six Dharmas, the meditation on the guru’s actual form was said to be foremost and that has been the practice. But whether you imagine the actual form of the guru or the form of Vajradhara according to your preference, meditate on that very form with a blissful countenance, smiling amiably, and sending you continuous blessings.

dus gsum sangs rgyas thams cad 'dus pa'i ngo bo bla ma rin po che/ sems can thams cad kyi don du/ bdag gi lus la bde drod kyi ting nge 'dzin khyad par can skye bar mdzad du gsol/ sems la bde stong gi ting nge 'dzin khyad par can skye bar mdzad du gsol/ ces gsol ba drag tu btab/

Then supplicate with intense feeling: Precious Guru, unified essence of all buddhas of the three times. For the sake of all sentient beings, bless me that the special absorption of bliss-warmth arises in my body. Bless me that the special absorption of bliss-emptiness arises in my mind.
Outer Visualization

mthar bla ma bdud rtsi'i ngo bor zhu/ rang gi spyi bo nas zhugs te thim/ rang gi tha mal rnam smin gyi lus ngag yid gsum nam mkha' la 'ja' yal ba ltar sang ste dag / ye shes lha'i sku gsung thugs su (16) gyur pa ni/ rang nyid bcom ldan 'das ma rdo rje phag mo sku mdog dmar mo/ phyag g.yas rdo rje thur du cung zad sdigs pa/ g.yon thod khrag thugs kar bsnams pa/ gcer bu rus pa'i rgyan lnga dang / mi mgo skam po lnga'i dbu rgyan/ rlon pa lnga bcu'i do shal can/ pad nyi mi ro mgo bo g.yas su bstan pa'i steng na/ zhabs g.yas brkyang gi stabs kyis bzhugs pa/ me dpung 'bar ba'i dbus na gnas pa/ spyan gsum dbu skra grol ba sogs cha byad spyi dang mthun/ gang ltar yang rang rdo rje phag mo sku mdog phyag mtshan rnam pa gang gsal gsal cig ci nus su gsal btab ste cung zad sems bzung / de phyi'i dmigs pa yin/

Finally, the guru melts into the essence of elixir, which enters the crown of your head and dissolves. Your ordinary fully ripened karmic body, speech, and mind vanish into thin air like a rainbow, clean and pure. {16} Transformed as the awakened body, speech, and mind of the awareness deity, you are the Conqueror Vajravārāhī with a red body, slightly menacing with a vajra pointing downward in the right hand and holding a blood-filled skull cup in the left. She is naked, wears the five bone ornaments, a crown of five dry human skulls, and a garland of fifty freshly severed heads. She stands with right leg extended on a supine human corpse with its head bent to the right, upon a lotus and sun seat, abiding in the midst of towering flames. She has three eyes, loosened hair, and so forth—the usual general attributes. In any case, imagine yourself as Vajravārāhī in form and attributes as well as you can, and hold that for a short time.
Inner Visualization

de nas rang lha skur gsal ba'i lus nang la sems gtad pas/ lus kyi nang sha khrag rus gsum sogs gang yang med pa'i stong sang nge ba/ phyi pags pa'i rnam pa yang shin tu srab pa/ nang khong stong de yang 'od dmar po drod kyi rang bzhin gyis khyab pa/ dpe dar dmar gyi gur ram/ khru ma phus btab pa lta bu zer ba de yin/ skra'i rtsa ba dang ba spu'i rtsa ba tshun chad kyang sbubs stong du sbu gu sag ge bsgom dgos gsung / gang ltar na'ang rang lus rdo rje phag mo'i skur gsal ba de'i lus nang stong sang nge ba/ spyi bo nas zhabs mthil gyi bar dang / zhabs mthil nas spyi bo'i bar dang / phyag zhabs kyi sor mo'i rtse mo'i bar kun du rim pas gsal btab cing nang stong sang nge ba la sems gtad/ nang gi dmigs pa'o/ /

Then, with yourself clearly appearing in that divine form, turn your attention to the inside of the body. The inside of the body has no flesh, blood, bones, or any matter whatsoever; it is utterly empty. The outline of skin is also extremely fine, while the hollow interior is pervaded by red light that is the nature of heat. It is said to be like a red silk tent or a blown-up balloon. One is instructed to meditate on everything, including the roots of the hairs and the pores, as hollow cavities. In any case, your body appears clearly in the form of Vajravārāhī and is utterly empty inside. Imagine sequentially the utter emptiness from the top of the head to the soles of the feet and from the soles of the feet to the top of the head and down to the tips of the fingers and toes of the hands and feet, and focus on that. This is the inner visualization. When applying this as a guide of one’s own experience, then it is most excellent to maintain both outer and inner visualizations for several days each.
Wildfire Visualization

nyams khrid rang byed na/ phyi nang gnyis po 'di la'ang so sor zhag shas re bskyangs na shin tu legs/ de nas me rgod kyi dmigs pa dngos ni/ skabs de nas lus gnad me thab drug chings bya ste/ rkang pa gnyis re mig ltar bsnol la tsog pu bya/ rkang ngar g.yas pa nang dang g.yon pa phyi la yong ba byed/ lag pa g.yas g.yon bar lhu g.yas (17) g.yon la bsnol mar 'jus/ gru mo gnyis pus mo'i steng du yong bar byas la sgal tshigs bsrang / lta stangs sogs lus gnad lhag ma spyi dang 'dra/

For the actual Wildfire visualization,[5] from now on assume the physical vital point called sixfold binding stove.[6] That is, sitting with legs drawn up and crossed like a trellis. Place your right calf inside and the left outside. Cross your arms and with your hands grasp the opposite arms’ biceps. {17} Rest your two elbows on your knees and hold your back straight. Maintain the rest of the standard physical vital points, such as the yogic gazes.

de nas thun gyi dang po la rlung ro dal la ring ba lan gsum bus/ rlung sbyor dngos ni/ de rjes steng rlung ran par rngubs te lte 'og tu mnan/ 'og rlung rang gnas su bcing / yar 'then pa mi dgos/ dmigs pa ni rang gi lte ba'i thad dang / de'i thad kyi rgyab dang / mkhal khung g.yas g.yon gnyis te gnas bzhir me'i gong bu dbyibs zlum po/ kha dog dmar ba/ reg bya tsha ba/ me lce lhab lhab 'bar ba rang ma yin pa la/ 'bar tshad tshad pa sol me ngar ma bus pa'am/ lcags sregs kyi gong bu dmar lhang ba lta bu bzhi sgroms su gsal btab/ rlung 'jam rlung bzung ba'i ngos nas lto ba g.yas su bskor ba gcig dang / g.yon du bskor ba gcig byas pas/ me gong bzhi po de drag tu 'thabs nas me lcags gtsubs pa lta bu'i me stag / dmar skyas lus kyi nang thams cad 'od dmar chem chem khyab pas/ lus tsha 'u ru ru byung bar bsam/ de ltar mi bde ba med med du rlung bzung nas cung zad mi bde ba snyam byed na/ dang por shugs chung ba/ bar du shugs che ba/ mthar sang ste rlung bus/ rlung thengs gcig go / yang snga ma ltar bzung zhing dmigs pa yang snga ma ltar bsgom/ thun mjug tu dge ba bsngo'o/ /

Then, at the beginning of the session, expel the dead air three times, slowly and at length. Following this, the actual joining of the winds breathing exercise (rlung sbyor) is to inhale moderately and then press the upper wind down below the navel. The lower wind is held in its own place, so drawing it upward is unnecessary. The visualization is to imagine a foursquare formation of four fireballs in four places—directly in front of your navel, directly behind it, and at the right and left kidneys. The fireballs are round in shape, red in color, and hot to the touch. Here they are not exactly blazing with flickering tongues of flame, but imagine instead that they are about to ignite like coal before it is fanned or like red-hot burning iron balls. While holding the winds in a gentle breath (’jam rlung), rotate the belly once to the right and once to the left. That causes the four fireballs to collide violently and give off reddish sparks like the striking of flints. Imagine the whole inside of the body pervaded by glittering red light, making a rumbling sound in all parts of the body. When that becomes uncomfortable and you think you cannot hold it any longer, expel the breath slowly at first, strongly in the middle, and then finally exhale totally. This is one breath. Hold it as before and meditate on the visualization again. Dedicate the virtue at the end of the session.

de ltar zhag shas rlung thebs re la dmigs pa dang g.yas g.yon du skor ba tshar re re kho na sbyangs/ / de nas rim pas zhag shas nas g.yas skor g.yon skor re re bsnan/ grangs kyi tha ma grangs la nges bzung rang med kyang / g.yas skor bcu gnyis dang g.yon skor bcu gnyis tsam du longs song tsa na me'i nus pa rnyed par 'gyur ro gsung / thun mtshams su yan lag lnga sbyongs (18) re sngon du 'gro bas/ gtsubs shing dang gtsubs stan ma'i 'khrul 'khor ci nus su sbyang ngo / / dmigs skor drug pa'o/ /

Over the course of a few days, train only in applying the visualization for one breath and one right and left rotation of the belly. Gradually, after a few days, add one more right and left rotation each. Though there is no exact minimum number, it is taught that if you can perform twelve right rotations and twelve left rotations, you will gain the capability of fire. {18} In between the sessions, after you do the five-branch training[7] each time, train as much as possible in the yogic exercises of Drilling Stick and Drilling Base.[8] This is the sixth round of visualization.
gnyis pa gtum mo'i dngos gzhi
2. The Main Practice of Fierce Inner Heat
['di] la/ gtum mo zas su za ba/ gos su gyon pa/ stan du 'ding ba/ rta bzhon pa ste bzhi las/
This has four parts: (1) Eating the Food of Inner Heat, (2) Wearing the Clothes of Inner Heat, (3) Spreading the Seat, and (4) Riding the Windhorse.
Session 7.
dang po ni/
a. Eating the Food of Inner Heat
gtum mo zas su za ba ste/ chos 'di'i lugs kyi gtum mo'i dmigs pa'i gtso bo yin te/ 'di la yang shes rab dang / mos pa'i khyad par gyis dmigs pa rgyas 'bring bsdus gsum yod do/ /

In this dharma tradition, this is the main visualization for Inner Heat. There are three levels of visualization depending on the differences [in practitioners’] wisdom and interest: (1) extensive, (2) intermediate, and (3) brief.
de la dang por rgyas pa ni/
i. Extensive Visualization

sngar bzhin skyabs 'gro sems bskyed bla ma'i rnal 'byor rnams sngon du btang / rang lhar gsal ba dang lus nang stong ra bca' ba yang sngar bzhin byas te/ de rjes lus gnad rkang pa sems dpa'i skyil krung lhod kyis byas te rgya che bar bcas lag mthil pus mo'i steng du bkab ste lag ngar bsrang / lhag ma lus gnad spyi dang 'dra/ thun gyi mgo 'dir rlung ro dgu sprugs su 'bud de/ dang por dal la ring ba gsum/ bar du drag la thung ba gsum/ tha mar ro stod gcud cing 'bud pa gsum/ de rnams lag len bltas pas gsal/

First go for refuge, arouse the awakening mind, and practice guru yoga as before. Again, as before, imagine yourself as the deity with the empty space inside the body. After that, assume the vital points of the body with your legs placed in bodhisattva position, relaxed and wide. Place your palms on your knees with arms straight. The rest of the vital points conform to the standard practices. At the outset of this session, do the ninefold shake-up of dead air: the first three slow and long, the next three strong and short, and the final three twisting the torso while exhaling. These will be clear from looking at the actual practice.

de nas rang gi lus la rtsa gsum 'khor lo bzhi yi ge gnyis dang bcas pa gsal 'debs/ de yang lus kyi g.yas g.yon gang la yang ma yo ba'i dbus drang thad/ mdun rgyab kyi dbang du byas na rgyab phyogs la cung zad nye bar/ rtsa dbu ma a wa d+hU ti chos bzhi ldan du gsal 'debs/ de yang chu shing gi sdong po ltar drang ba ste/ ya yo khyar khyer khyag khyog med pa/ til gyi mar me ltar gsal ba ste rang 'od 'phro ba/ rgya skyegs kyi khu ba ltar dmar ba ste rgya tshos kyis bcos pa'i mdog lta bu/ pad+ma'i snal ma ltar phra ba ste shin tu srab pa'o/ /

Then clearly imagine your body with three channels, four chakras, and two syllables. Visualize the central channel, avadhūtī, as straight in the dead center of your body, neither to the right nor the left. In terms of front or back, it is slightly closer to the back. It has four characteristics: it is as straight as the trunk of a plantain tree, without kinks, curves, or turns; it is as clear as a sesame oil lamp, shining with its own light; it is as red as lac dye, like the color made from vermillion powder; and it is as thin as a lotus petal, which is extremely fine.

yongs kyi phyi dbyibs sbom phra ni/ mda' smyug 'bring po tsam ste/ dbu ma de'i yas sna spyi bo tshangs bug la zug ces (19) gsung ste/ de yang dngos su rus pa'i tshangs bug dang ta mi sgom ste/ 'on kyang tshangs bug gi thad spyi gtsug gi yas mtha' nas mar sor gnyis tsam gzhal ba'i sar sleb pa yin/ mas sna lte 'og sor bzhi'i thad du zug par bsgom/ dbu ma de khong stong yas sna mas sna gnyis ka bcad khar yod cing / de'i g.yas su ro ma dmar po dang / g.yon du rkyang ma dkar po ste gnyis po dbu ma bzhi gshags su btang ba tsam gyi tshad dam/ yang na gro sog tsam yang gsung ste gang ltar bsgoms kyang 'dra/ de gnyis spyi bo nas lte 'og sor bzhi'i bar dbu ma dang lhan cig tu gsum gshibs ltar yod pa/ yas mas kyi sne ni ro rkyang gnyis ring ba las/ 'og tu ro rkyang gnyis dbu ma las sor bzhi tsam gyi ring ba'i ro rkyang gi sne de gnyis yar slog ste/ dbu ma'i mas sna'i nang du chug tsam byas pa/ yas sna gnyis po dbu ma'i yas sne'i rgyab phyogs mtheb sor gcig tsam gyi thad du song / de mtshams nas nyis gshibs su byas pa dbu ma'i yas sna'i steng nas bkab cing / de nas mdun du 'khyogs te/ ro ma'i sne sna bug g.yas dang / rkyang ma'i sne sna bug g.yon du zug pa'o/ /

The total thickness of its external shape is about that of a medium-sized arrow. It is said that the upper end of that central channel touches the cranial aperture. {19} However, you do not meditate on the actual bone of the cranial aperture but rather that the central channel reaches to a point two finger-widths below the crown of the head, directly below the aperture. Meditate on the lower end four finger-widths below the navel. That central channel is empty inside with both the upper and lower ends cut off. To its right is the red rasanā (Tib. ro ma) channel, and to the left the white lalanā (rkyang ma) channel. It is taught that these two channels measure about a fourth of the width of the central channel, or about the width of a wheat stalk; however you prefer to meditate on them is the same. Those two extend from the top of the head to four finger-widths below the navel, together with the central channel like three parallel lines. The upper and lower ends of the rasanā and lalanā are slightly longer, with the lower ends extending for four finger-widths and turning up into the lower end of the central channel. The upper ends of those two reach to one thumb-width behind the upper end of the central channel. From that juncture, they join up over the upper end of the central channel and cover it. Then they curve to the front, the rasanā ending in the right nostril and the lalanā in the left nostril.

de ltar ro rkyang dbu ma gsum po gsum gshibs su yod pa las/ lte ba'i thad dang / snying ga'i thad dang / mgrin pa'i spom sa'i thad dang / spyi bo'i dbu ma'i yas sna nas mar rtse sor gnyis tsam gzhal ba'i thad te bzhi po de rnams su rtsa 'khor gyi lte bzlum po a long khong seng can lta bu/ ro rkyang dbu ma gsum dbus kyi srog shing 'dra ba la/ des sked dkris byas pa lta bu ste/ de lta bu'i lte ba las rtsa 'dab rnams rtsa sbubs can gyi rnam pa gdugs kyi rtsibs ma bzhin du skyes par gyur pa las/ lte ba sprul pa'i 'khor lo rtsa 'dab drug cu re bzhi (20) gdugs rtsibs ma can gan rkyal du bzhag pa lta bu/

In this manner, the central channel, rasanā, and lalanā are parallel except at the level of the navel, the level of the heart, the level of the Adam’s apple at the throat, and two finger-widths below the upper end of the central channel. In those four places there are channel chakras (wheels) that are round at the hub like an empty ring. The rasanā, lalanā, and central channel are like a central axis, with [the channel chakras] wrapped around them like a belt. The hollow tubes of the channel “petals” fan out from that hub like the spokes of a parasol. The emanation chakra at the navel has sixty-four petals that appear like the spokes of an upside-down parasol. {20}

snying ga chos kyi 'khor lo rtsa 'dab brgyad gdugs rtsibs ma can nyid lta bu/ mgrin pa longs spyod kyi 'khor lo rtsa 'dab bcu drug gdugs 'degs lta bu/ spyi bo bde ba chen po'i 'khor lo rtsa 'dab sum cu so gnyis/ gdugs kyi rtsibs ma lta bu/ 'khor lo bzhi kar phyi rim nang rim gyi dbye ba med/ grangs de rnams mu ded yin/ thams cad kyang kha dog dmar po/ lcags bsregs ltar 'od dmar lham me ba bsgom/ rtsa dbu ma'i nang yas sna'i phyogs su haM yig dkar po mgo bo thur du lta ba/ thig le'i rang bzhin nyams bde zhing bsil ba zhu la khad khad pa bsgom/ dbu ma'i mas sne'i nang rtsa gsum 'dus mdor/ raM yig dmar po mgo bo gyen du lta ba/ me'i rang bzhin shin tu tsha ba/ dbu ma'i mas sna nas sor bzhi gzhal btsam gyi thad bshang sgo'i phyogs su rlung gi dkyil 'khor zla gam sngon po g.yo ba'i rang bzhin gdan thabs su yod pa/ bcad kha mdun la bstan pa rnams sgom mo/ /

The dharma chakra at the heart has eight petals exactly like the spokes of a parasol. The enjoyment chakra at the throat has sixteen petals like a raised parasol. The great-bliss chakra at the head has thirty-two petals like the spokes of a parasol. In all four chakras there is no separation of the outer rim and inner rim, and whatever the number [of spokes], they all touch the perimeter [of the central channel]. Meditate on them as red in color and glowing with red light like molten metal. Inside the central channel at the upper end is an upside-down white syllable haṃ. It has the nature of a vital drop, feels blissful and cool, and is about to melt. Inside the lower end of the central channel at the place where the three channels converge, there is a red upright syllable raṃ. It has the nature of fire and is extremely hot. Four finger-widths directly below the lower end of the central channel, near the anus, there lies a blue semicircular wind mandala. It is the nature of movement and functions as a seat, with its straight side facing forward. Meditate on all that.

dmigs pa'i gzhi de ltar gsal thebs nas/ yang rlung ro cig dal bus bsal/ de nas steng rlung shar te rngubs pa lte 'og tu bskyur stabs su mnan/ de dang mnyam du 'og rlung bskum ste/ lte bar kha sbyor du bzung / cung zad mi bde ba snyam byed na gzhil bar bya ste/ de yang sngar rlung bzung ba de nyid cung zad kyang phyir ma btang bar slar yang rngubs chung gang nus bya ste/ lte ba'i gnas su g.yas g.yon dbus gsum du 'then gnon byas nas kyang gang thub bzung / yang mi bde ba snyam byed na/ dang por shugs chung ba/ bar du shugs che ba/ mthar sang gis btang ba rnams la bslab/ de ma thag tu yang rngubs te sngar bzhin bsgom/ ma goms gong du ngal na rlung thengs bzhi'i mtshams sam/ (21) brgyad dang / bcu gnyis sam/ bcu drug gam/ nyi shu'am/ nyer bzhi'am/ nyer brgyad dam/ so gnyis kyi mtshams su ngal gso yi/ gang 'dod 'dod du bzhag tu mi rung ngo / /

Once you have clarified that basic visualization, slowly exhale the dead air one time. Then when the upper wind arises, inhale and press it down in a manner that leaves it below the navel. At the same time, draw up the lower wind, holding the joined winds at the navel. If you think it is rather uncomfortable and you are about to expel it, inhale as many small gulps of air as you can without letting out any of the air held previously. Push and press [your belly] to the right, left, and center in the area of the navel and hold the air as long as you can. When it makes you feel uncomfortable again, first let it out gently, then strongly, and finally empty it out. Train with those [breathing exercises] immediately afterward by inhaling and meditating as before. Until you become accustomed to this, {21} you can rest after four, eight, twelve, sixteen, twenty, twenty-four, twenty-eight, or thirty such breaths. It is inappropriate to stop whenever you want.

dmigs pa ni/ rlung rnams sna sgo nas zhugs/ ro rkyang gi lam brgyud de/ lte 'og rtsa gsum 'dur mdor sleb/ 'og rlung bskums pas bshang sgo'i rlung gi dkyil 'khor las rlung po kha dog sngon po shin tu phra ba zhig mdung tshugs su langs te dbu ma'i mas snar chud/ de ltar ro rkyang dang thur sel gyi rlung gsum po gcig tu 'dus pas raM yig la bus pas/ raM las gtum mo ye shes kyi me lhag ste 'bar/ mar me 'bar ba lta bu de'i rtse mo shin tu phra zhing rno ba spu shad dmar po lta bu/ phra ba/ gsal ba/ 'tsher ba cig je ring je ring la 'bar/ rlung thengs 'ga' re song ba na/ spyi bo'i haM la reg reg 'dug par bsam/ de nas rim pas haM zhu ba las byang chub kyi sems kyi rgyun dar dkar po'i snal ma brkyang ba tsam babs/ je ring je ring la lte ba'i raM la thim par bsam/

In the visualization, the air enters through the nose, travels down the rasanā and lalanā, and arrives at the junction of the three channels below the navel. By contracting the lower wind, a very fine blue wind from the wind mandala at the anus rises like a piercing spear and enters the lower end of the central channel. The three winds of the rasanā, lalanā, and the downward-clearing wind gather together and fan the raṃ syllable. This ignites the timeless awareness of inner heat, which blazes up from the raṃ. It burns like a candle, with a very sharp, fine point, like a red needle—fine, clear, and bright. It grows longer and longer. After taking a few breaths, imagine that it stays touching the haṃ in the head. Then gradually the haṃ melts and from it the stream of bodhicitta falls like a white silken thread stretching out. Imagine that it gets longer and longer until it dissolves into the raṃ at the navel.

spyir gtum mo la/ me kho na la dmigs pa/ thig le la dmigs pa/ 'bar 'dzag la dmigs pa gsum yod pa las 'di phyi ma yin/ de la'ang 'bros 'ded dang / skra shad 'dzings pa lta bu dang / phyed mar khyab pa la sogs pa'i lugs sna tshogs yod kyang / 'di bar pa yin/ de yang dbu ma'i dbus su bar 'dzag gnyis ka rgyun mi 'chad pa la zer te/ de las kyang dbu ma'i dbus kyi nang gzhir bzhag pa las/ mdun gyi phyogs su me 'bar ba dang / rgyab kyi phyogs su byang chub kyi sems 'bab pa bsgom dgos gsung / gtum mo 'bar ba'i me 'od gang du slebs pa des lus nang du tsha 'ur gyis byung ba dang / byang chub kyi sems 'bab pa'i 'od skya yaM byung ba na/ lus thams cad (22) bde cham gyis byung bar mos pa gnyis re mos su yid la bya'o/ /

In general, there are three kinds of visualizations for Fierce Inner Heat: visualizing only fire, visualizing vital drops, and visualizing blazing and dripping. Of those, this is the latter. There are also various styles such as “escape-and-chase,” “brushing tangled hair,” “half-pervading,” and so forth. This constitutes the middle one. Both the blazing and the dripping in the middle of the central channel are said to be uninterrupted flows. However, given the basic context of the interior middle of the central channel, it is taught that you should meditate on the fire blazing in the anterior side and the bodhicitta falling in the posterior side within it. Wherever the firelight of blazing inner heat reaches, it creates the rumbling sound of heat inside the body. When the strand of whitish light of descending bodhicitta appears, think that the whole body is filled with bliss. {22} Alternate those two visualizations in your mind.
thun mtshams su dge ba byang chub tu bsngo/ de ltar na dmigs pa rgyas pa ste/ dmigs skor bdun pa'o/ /
Dedicate the virtue to awakening after each session. This extensive visualization is the seventh round.
dbang rtul la 'di spod sgom du byed na/ rtsa gsum dang 'khor lo bzhi dang yig 'bru dang rlung sbyor dang 'bar 'dzag rnams la thun re re byas na'ang 'ong ba lags/

For those of duller capabilities to get a taste of these meditations, it is effective to practice each one of these separately: the three channels, the four chakras, the syllables, joining the winds, and blazing and dripping.
gtum mo zas su za ba'i dmigs pa 'bring po ni/
ii. Intermediate Visualization for Eating the Food of Inner Heat
rtsa 'khor lo bzhi lte ba sked dkris 'dra ba dang bcas pa'i skor de rnams bor nas/ lhag ma sngar ltar bsgom pa kho na'o/ /
Dispense with the part about the four channel chakras along with their belt-like wraps around the center and just meditate on the rest as described above.
dmigs pa bsdus pa ni/
iii. Brief Visualization

de'i steng du ro rkyang gnyis kyang spangs pa ste/ 'di la mi 'dra ba'i khyad rlung sna sgo nas rngubs pa gnyis dbu ma'i g.yas g.yon nas mar mdung tshugs su song / lte 'og nas sor drug gam brgyad tsam du mar sleb pa de/ 'og rlung yar bskum pa'i rlung dang phrad pa na/ de la brdabs pa ltar yar thabs su yar log ste thams cad dbu ma'i mas snar zhugs/ raM la bskul bar bsam dgos/ gzhan 'dra/

As well as [what was eliminated in the middling visualization], also disregard the rasanā and lalanā channels. The difference here is that the two winds inhaled through the nose descend like spears cast to the right and left of the central channel and land six or eight finger-widths below the navel. When the lower wind is drawn up and meets these winds, it is as if they are struck and turned back up, thereby causing all the winds to enter the lower end of the central channel. You need to imagine that they activate the raṃ. The rest is the same.

de ltar na dmigs pa 'bring bsdus gnyis po/ dmigs pa rgyas pa'i nang du tshud pa yin pas logs su mi 'dren/ dmigs skor bdun pa nyid du 'dus/ de'i rgyu mtshan rgyas 'bring bsdus gsum kar bla ma las thob par byas nas/ rang gi mos pa dang mthun par gang rung gcig kho na bsgom rgyu yin pa'i phyir ro/ / dmigs skor gcig yin kyang 'chad pa'i tshe chos thun so sor byed pa ni mi 'gal lo/ /

Thus both the intermediate and brief visualizations are really contained within the extensive visualization and there is no need to treat them separately, so [all three] are included in the seventh round of visualization. The reason for that is that once the disciple has received all three from the guru, they only need to meditate on whichever one suits their own interests. But even though it is one round of visualization, it is fine to treat them as separate teaching sessions when explaining them.

'dir mkhas btsun rgyal mtshan 'bum gyis mdzad pa sogs khrid yig rnying pa rnams na/ sngon gro me'i stong ra la rkang pa skyil krung dang / dngos gzhi gtum mo zas za la me thab drug chings byed par bshad na'ang / bla ma'i zhal la ltos pa'i phyir man ngag dkrugs te bshad pa yin/ lag len gong du (23) bshad pa kho na byed dgos so/ / gtum mo zas su za ba 'di gtum mo'i dngos gzhi yin/

Here, the classic guidebooks, such as the one created by the learned Venerable Gyaltsen Bum,[9] explain that during the preliminary practice of the Empty Space of Fire, one sits in the cross-legged vajra position, while during the main practice of Eating the Food of Inner Heat, one uses the position of the sixfold binding stove. {23} But with regard to the guru’s teachings, these esoteric instructions have been explained out of order. We must only rely on the practice as it was described above. Eating the Food of Inner Heat is the main practice of Fierce Inner Heat.
gzhung las/ / rang lus thabs ldan rtsa gsum 'khor lo bzhi/ / a haM 'bar 'dzag skad cig dga' bzhis brgyan/ / ces gsungs pa'i bstan don dngos yin no/ /

The source text states: One’s own body is the means, with three channels and four chakras. The A blazes and haṃ drips, adorning the instances with four ecstasies.[10] This is really the intended meaning.

raM yig bsgoms pa la lte ba'i a thung sgom ba'i don tshang ba dang / dmigs pa 'bring bsdus gnyis la 'khor lo bzhi dngos sum bsgoms kyang / rtsa dbu ma yongs rdzogs bsgoms pa'i phyir/ dbu ma nyid 'khor lo bzhi kar gyi lte ba yin pas/ don 'khor lo bzhi car tshang ba yin no/ /

Meditation on the syllable raṃ is basically the meaning of meditation on the navel’s short A. Although there is no actual meditation on the four chakras in the intermediate and brief visualizations, since there is the meditation on the completely perfect central channel, and since that very central channel is the core of the four chakras, they are in fact included [in the shorter visualizations].
Session 8.
gnyis pa gtum mo gos su gon pa ni/
b. Wearing the Clothes of Inner Heat

dmigs pa'i rtsa ba gtum mo zas su za ba cung zad goms pa zhig gis bya ste/ 'di la phyi'i dmigs pa grang ba yid la mi byed/ gnas khang rdo rje'i rang bzhin nam/ lcags sregs kyi sa gzhi dang / rwa gur la me 'ur 'ur 'bar bar bsgom/ rang lha sku dang / rgyan phyag rgya lnga/ na bza' stag lpags mi lpags/ thams cad kyang me lce yal la la 'bar bar bsam/ nang gi dmigs pa lte 'og sor bzhir raM las 'bar ba'i mes lus nang thams cad gang bar bsam/

This is to be done by someone familiar with the main visualization of Eating the Food of Inner Heat. For the outer visualization, do not engage in the idea of cold. Instead, meditate on your dwelling place as the nature of vajras or as if the ground and walls are molten iron, rumbling with the sounds of burning. Think of yourself in the deity’s form, adorned with the five symbolic ornaments and wearing clothes of tiger and human skin. Imagine everything ablaze with lapping tongues of fire. For the inner visualization, imagine that a fire blazing from the raṃ four finger-widths below the navel fills the entire inside of the body.

lus gnad tsog pu/ lag gnyis pus mo'i phyi nas 'khyud dbugs shad brag la 'gro ba byed ces bshad na'ang / man ngag gab pa yin pas/ lag pa gnyis nang du bsnol te/ g.yas kyi lag mthil g.yon gyi mkhal khung dang / g.yon gyi lag mthil g.yas kyi mkhal khung la bkab/ phyi nas pus 'khyud kyis sdoms pa yin/ rlung gi gnad/ gzhil ba lan gnyis re'am/ gsum re lus stobs dang bstun nas bya/ thun mtshams su gtsubs shing gtsubs stan gyi 'khrul 'khor la 'bad/ 'dis drod 'phral du skyed/ lus rngul na gos srab tu btang zhing / (24) lus la dril phyis bya'o/ / yang dngos gzhi zas su za ba ma bsgoms par me'i stong ra yun ring du bsgoms pas kyang 'di bsgom du rung ngo / / dmigs skor brgyad pa'o/ /

The vital physical posture is to sit with the knees drawn up. Although it is explained that the two hands encircle the knees, causing the breath to enter the interstices of the flesh, it is an arcane esoteric instruction. Rather, cross the hands inside, with the right palm covering the hollow of the left kidney and the left palm covering the hollow of the right kidney.[11] The knees encircle and press [the arms] from the outside. The vital point of the winds is to take two or three small breaths each time, in keeping with your physical strength. Between sessions, apply yourself to the yogic exercises of Drilling Stick and Drilling Base. This will produce warmth immediately. If you perspire, wear light clothing and wipe down your whole body. {24} If you have not meditated on the main practice of Eating the Food of Inner Heat, but you have practiced the Inner Space of Fire for a long time, it is suitable to do this meditation. This is the eighth round of visualization.
Session 9.
gnyis pa stan du 'ding ba ni/
c. Spreading the Seat

phyi'i dmigs pa gos su gyon pa dang 'dra ba las/ lhag por gdan lcags bsregs kyi pad+ma dang nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor me lce 'u ru ru 'bar ba la rang nyid gnas pa lhag por bsgom/ nang gi dmigs pa lte ba'i thad du raM dmar po 'od lhag ge ba la sems gtad/ rlung gnad 'jam rlung rgyun chags su bzung / nyin par dang nam stod de ltar byas nas gnyid log khar/ rab skyil krung / 'bring tsog pu/ tha ma sngas mtho ru bcug / glo g.yas pa 'og tu bcug / pus brang sbyar/ lus sum ltab tu nyal/ sems lte ba'i raM la gtad pa'i ngang nas gnyid du 'gro bar bya/ 'di'i dgos pa ni/ gtum mo bsgoms pas gnyid kyi 'od gsal zin pa dang / nyin par bsgoms pa'i drod kyi rgyun de mtshan mo mi yal ba'i phyir yin/ 'di yang me'i stong ra'am/ zas su za ba gang rung gcig cung zad 'byongs pas bsgom na don ston par the tshom med pa yin no/ / dmigs skor dgu pa'o/ /

The outer visualization is the same as in Wearing the Clothes of Inner Heat except that in addition you meditate on a burning iron seat with the lotus and sun mandalas blazing and rumbling with tongues of flame while you sit there. For the inner visualization, turn your attention to an intense light from the red raṃ at the navel level. The vital point of the breath is to continually hold the gentle breath. If that is done during the day and in the evening, then when it is time to sleep, the best position is the cross-legged vajra posture, the middling is sitting with the legs drawn up, and the least is to raise [your head] with a pillow and lie on your right side, drawing the legs up to the chest, thus creating three “folds.” Fall asleep while focusing on the raṃ at the navel. The purpose of this is that meditation on inner heat leads to the recognition of the lucid clarity of sleep. This way the continuity of warmth from daytime meditation will not be dissipated at night. This is certain to show results if the meditation is done after some training with either the Inner Space of Fire or Eating the Food of Inner Heat. This is the ninth round of visualization.
Session 10.
bzhi pa rlung rtar zhon pa ni/
d. Riding the Wind Horse

rtsa ba'i dmigs pa dang rlung 'byongs pa cig gis yun ring du sgom na/ rta mchog dang mnyam pa'i 'gros 'byung ngo ces pa lta bu rtags dang yon tan gyi tshul du 'byung ba yin/ da lta lag tu longs nges la zla ba gcig gnyis tsam rlung sbyangs pa'i las dang po pas sgom na/ lam gyi 'gro 'dug gis rtsa rlung 'khrugs pa dang / khams rnyogs par mi 'gyur zhing / 'gro 'dug nyid lus sbyongs su 'gro ba'i phan yon yod do/ /

Someone who has meditated for a long time in the main visualization and the breathing exercises will have experienced the appropriate signs and qualities, having, as is said, “a gait equal to the supreme steed.” Now, if you are a beginner in wind-training who has just taken up definite practice for one or two months were to meditate [on these practices], you would avoid disturbances of the channels and winds and compromised health when traveling or staying on the road. You would gain the benefits of physical training just by going or staying in itself.

de yang lam du 'jug pa'i sngon du rlung khug pa nyer gcig tsam bzung / de skabs dngos gzhi'i dmigs pa'am/ yang na mi rtog pa rkyang pa (25) bsgoms kyang btub/ dngos ni lam du 'gro ba'i tshe/ lag pa stod skyil bcas/ rlung 'jam rlung bzung / dmigs pa ni rlung gi lha mo dkar ljang gshog pa can gnyis kyis mchan khung nas btegs te/ gang 'dod pa'i gnas su phyin par bsam gsung / 'dir rlung khug pa ces pa ni/ gong du bshad pa'i rlung thengs bzhi bzhi ba de la zer ba yin/ de nyer gcig la rlung thengs brgyad cu gya bzhi yod/ de yang las dang po bum can ma 'grub pa rnams kyi dbang du byas par 'dug / yun ring bzung nus pa rnams la grangs de tsam mi dgos/ khrid yig rnams na mi gsal yang skabs der bar lhu 'jus pa'i stod skyil tsam pos mi chog / khu tshur mchan khung du bcug pa'i stod skyil bcas nas/ rlung gi lha mos btegs pa sgom dgos ces/ sangs rgyas kun 'dus rtsa ba'i bla ma gsung ngo / / dmigs skor bcu pa'o/ /

Furthermore, before setting out on the path, you should practice twenty-one rounds of breathing while doing the main visualization.
