Meditation in mere nonthought will also work. {25} Mainly, when it’s time to go, cross your arms over your chest and hold gentle breathing. Visualize that two light-green winged wind goddesses pick you up by the armpits and carry you wherever you wish. In this case, the so-called round of breathing was explained before as taking four-times-four breaths. In a set of twenty-one, there are eighty-four breath [retentions]. This concerns beginners who have not gained proficiency in vase breathing. Those who can hold the breath for a long time do not need to do so many. Although it is not clear in the guidebooks, on these occasions it is not enough to merely cross the arms over the chest, holding the biceps. You must put your fists in your armpits when you cross your arms and then meditate that the wind goddesses lift you up. That is how it was taught by my root guru, the embodiment of all buddhas. This is the tenth round of visualization.
gsum pa rjes kyi khrid
3. Concluding Practice Guide
['di] la/ srid pa'i dbang zhu ba dang / gegs rang grol gnyis so/ /
This has two parts: taking the Empowerment of Existence and Naturally Liberating Obstructions.
Session 11.
dang po ni/
a. Taking the Empowerment of Existence

man ngag 'di thob phyin chad nas/ gtum mo bsgoms pa'i mjug thun mtshams la 'jug khar 'di tshar gcig nges par bsgom dgos te/ de yang rang gi spyi bor seng khri pad dkar nyi zla'i gdan la/ rtsa ba'i bla ma sku dngos sam/ rdo rje 'chang gang du bsgoms kyang rung mod kyi/ rtsa ba'i bla ma nyid bsgom pa zab par bzhed/ gang ltar yang sku mdog dkar la 'od zer 'phro ba/ de nyid skyabs gnas kun 'dus su shes/ mchod yon dang / me tog la sogs pa'i nyer spyod dang / khang bzang bzhugs khri/ na bza'/ rin po che'i gter dang / dpag bsam gyi shing dang / 'dod 'jo'i ba dang / rgyal srid sna bdun dang / bkra shis lha mo brgyad la sogs pa/ mdor na phyogs dus kun gyi mchod pa bzang dgu thams (26) cad 'bul ba ni/ phyi'i mchod pa'o/ /

From the time you have received these esoteric instructions, at the conclusion of a meditation on Fierce Inner Heat, you must definitely do this meditation once to start a session break. Upon a lion throne, white lotus, sun, and moon seat above your head, visualize the actual root guru or Vajradhara. Of course, either way is appropriate, but it is believed that meditating on the root guru him- or herself is more profound. In any case, you know that this white form radiating light is the union of all refuges. Offer the traditional sense offerings such as offering water and flowers, magnificent mansions and thrones, clothes, a treasure of jewels, wish-fulfilling trees, bountiful cows, the seven royal possessions, the eight goddesses of auspiciousness, and so on—in short, all the finest offerings from all times and directions. {26} This is the outer offering.

de nas sha lnga bdud rtsi lnga la sogs pa'i dam rdzas rnams ye shes kyi bdud rtsir byin gyis brlabs te 'bul ba ni nang gi mchod pa'o/ / bde ba skyed byed rigs kyi yum 'bul ba ni gsang ba'i mchod pa'o/ / de thams cad sgyu ma rmi lam ltar shes pa ni de kho na nyid kyi mchod pa'o/ / de ltar mchod pa bzhi rdzogs su phul nas/ 'di skad ces/

Then offer the pledge substances, such as the five meats and five elixirs, consecrated as the elixir of timeless awareness. This is the inner offering. The presentation of a bliss-inducing consort of [an appropriate] family is the secret offering. Knowing that all of that is like illusion and dream is the offering of suchness. After you present these four offerings completely, say these words:

dus gsum sangs rgyas thams cad 'dus pa'i ngo bo bla ma rin po che la/ phyi me tog bdug spos/ nang sha lnga bdud rtsi lnga/ gsang ba bde stong gi ye shes/ yang gsang de kho na nyid kyi mchod pa dam pa rnams 'bul lo/ / bzhes nas bdag la dbang bzhi rdzogs par bskur du gsol/ /

ces gsol ba drag tu btab pas/ bla ma'i sku las ye shes kyi bdud rtsi'i rgyun dkar la dangs pa nyams bde ba dang ldan pa drag tu babs/ spyi bo nas zhugs/ smin mtshams yan chad gang / bum dbang thob/ sku'i dngos grub stsal/ yang bdud rtsi'i chu rgyun gyis mgrin pa yan chad gang / gsang dbang thob/ gsung gi dngos grub stsal/ yang snying ga yan chad gang / shes rab ye shes kyi dbang thob/ thugs kyi dngos grub stsal/ yang bdud rtsi'i chu rgyun lte ba sogs nas brgyud/ rkang mthil yan chad lus kyi nang thams cad gang / dbang bzhi pa thob/ sku gsung thugs kyi dngos grub thams cad stsal/ bla ma nyid kyang 'od du ltem ste zhu nas rang la thim/ bla ma'i sku gsung thugs dang rang gi lus ngag yid gsum dbyer med gcig tu gyur pa la mnyam par bzhag / de rjes dge ba bsngos nas thun mtshams la 'jug pa yin/

Through your fervent supplication, a bright white bliss-inducing stream of awareness elixir rushes down from the guru’s body. It enters through the top of your head and fills your body above the eyebrows. You receive the vase empowerment, and it bestows the spiritual powers of awakened body. Again the stream of elixir fills your body above the throat. You receive the secret empowerment, and it bestows the spiritual powers of awakened speech. Again the stream of elixir fills your body above the heart. You receive the wisdom-awareness empowerment, and it bestows the spiritual powers of awakened mind. Again the stream of elixir flows past the navel and so forth, filling the whole body to the soles of the feet. You receive the fourth empowerment, and it bestows all the spiritual powers of the awakened body, speech, and mind. The guru also fills up with light and melts, dissolving into you. The guru’s awakened body, speech, and mind blend inseparably as one with your own body, speech, and mind. Settle in equipoise. After that, dedicate the virtue and begin the session break.

dmigs pa 'di bla ma la ma thob gong du der zad/ thob phyin chad gdams ngag 'di'i lugs kyi gtum mo'i dmigs pa'i rigs (27) bsgom pa thams cad la/ thun gyi mjug tu 'di tshar re nges par bsgom dgos pas/ gtum mo'i dmigs pa'i rjes chog lta bur 'gyur ba'i phyir/ rjes kyi khrid du bsdus pa yin la/ spyir 'di nyid dmigs pa gzhan dang ma sbrel bar logs su bsgom pa'i srol yang yod cing / bla ma'i sku las dbang bzhi len pa'i gnad don thams cad tshang zhing / spros pa'i bsre bslad med pas/ byin rlabs kyi tshan kha shin tu che'o/ /

Before you receive this visualization from the guru, there is no issue. {27} But once you receive it, then it is required in this system of instructions for all kinds of Fierce Inner Heat visualizations to definitely meditate once in this way at the end of each session, since it has become like the concluding rite of the visualization and is included in the guides for concluding practices. In general, there is also a custom of meditating on this separately, not conjoined with any other visualization. Everything of significance is included in the vital point of taking the four empowerments from the guru’s form, and since it is not polluted by being mixed with any elaborations, the potency of its blessings is tremendous.
skabs 'gar zhag gsum mam/ lnga'am/ bdun sogs 'di kho na la dril te bsgoms na/ sgom gang la yang bogs bla na med par phyin par 'gyur ro/ /
If you occasionally concentrate just on this practice for three, five, seven, or more days, it will become an unsurpassable enhancement for whatever other meditation you do.

gtum mo'i mjug tu nges par bsgom dgos pa'i rgyu mtshan ni/ gtum mo dngos gzhi bsgoms pa'i bde drod kyi nyams myong brtan par byed pa dang / rlung stod du 'tshangs pa thur du 'bebs pa dang / rtsol ba drag pos lus zungs la gnod pa'i rigs la/ 'dis lus zungs gso ba ting nge 'dzin gyi bcud len du 'gyur ba dang / thun mtshams su grib sogs bar chad srung ba dang / gtso bor byin rlabs brtan pa'i sgo nas ye shes skyed pa'o/ / dmigs skor bcu gcig pa'o/ /

The reason that it is absolutely necessary to meditate on this at the end of practicing Inner Heat is that it stabilizes the meditative experiences of bliss and warmth from meditation on the main practice of Fierce Inner Heat; it brings down the winds stuck in the upper body; it heals the physical constituents that were harmed in various ways from exerting too much effort and allows you to extract the nutritious essence of meditative absorption; it guards against obstacles such as contamination in the session breaks; and, most of all, it generates timeless awareness by stabilizing the blessings. This is the eleventh round of visualization.
Session 12.
gnyis pa gegs rang grol ni/
b. Naturally Liberating Obstructions

spyir gegs sel rgyas pa gzhan du shes dgos kyang / khrid kyi dkyus la 'di tsam 'byung ste/ gtum mo bsgom pa phal cher la rlung stod du 'tshang ba dang / 'og tu kun+da'i gegs 'byung ba yin/ de yang 'ga' zhig la gnyis kar 'byung ba'ang yod/ phal cher la gang rung re 'byung ba shas che/ gegs kyi rnam pa gzhan rnams ni re re tsam ma gtogs 'byung ba dkon no/ /

In general, you should learn the details of removing obstructions from other sources. Just two topics will be covered in the course of this guide: the usual problems that occur while meditating on inner heat are the winds being stuck in the upper body, and the obstructions of kunda (generative fluid) below. There are some people who have both of these problems, but most will have one or the other. It is rare that other kinds of obstructions occur outside of a few individual cases.
de la stod gegs bsal ba ni/
Dispelling the Obstructions of the Upper Body

thabs lam gtum mo bsgom pa'i skabs su ro stod na ba dang / mgo la zug gzer skye ba dang / shes pa 'phyo ba sogs byung na/ (28) sngon 'gro nyams su blangs pa'i rjes su/ rang lus stong sang nge ba gsal btab ste/ rlung thengs gcig gnyis shig sngon du btang / gang na sar bu ga zlum po sum tshoms nor bu mig gsum 'dra ba gsal btab/ lag gnyis khu tshur mdun du brkyangs te/ slar khu tshur gyi rgyab nu steng dang / lag ngar rtsibs logs la thebs par byed pa dang mnyam por kha nas ha thung drag tu 'don/ nad rnams bu ga nas dud pa'am rlung tshubs kyi rnam pas phyur phyur phyir rgyang ring du 'gro ba dang / lus kyi nang stong sang sang song bar mos/ lus thams cad na na lus khrol tshags lta bur sgom pa khyad par yin/ lus gyi cha shas 'di rang na ba'i nges gzung med par shes pa 'phyo ba sogs byung na snying rlung gi byed las yin pas/ snying dkar nag gi mtshams su bu ga sgom na legs gsung ngo / / dmigs skor bcu gnyis pa'o/ /

During meditation on Fierce Inner Heat in the path of methods, if there is pain in the upper torso, shooting pains in the head, or feeling mentally upset, [apply the following visualization]. {28} After practicing the preliminaries, imagine your own body as utterly empty. First do one or two sets of breathing, then imagine that there is a group of three round openings in the affected area, like a three-eyed gemstone. Make two fists and extend the arms in front, then with the back of the fists, strike above the breasts, and strike the ribs with the upper arms. At the same time, forcefully shout a short “ha.” Think that the pain leaves through the holes like smoke or like a windstorm, billowing out and moving far away. Your body inside becomes utterly empty. If the entire body hurts, the special meditation is to imagine it as a sieve. If you cannot determine exactly which part of the body is in pain, and the mind is upset, then it is probably the function of wind at the heart. For that it is said to be good to meditate on a hole at the heart’s white-black juncture (i.e., center of the chest). This is the twelfth round of visualization.
smad kun da'i gegs bsel ba ni/
Dispelling the Obstructions of Kunda in the Lower Body

rab dgag sgrub dang bral ba'i blos sel/ 'bring dbang bskur dang tshogs 'khor gyis sel/ tha ma dmigs pa dang 'khrul 'khor gyis sel gsung / yang chags sred dang bag chags kyi rgyu las byung ba yin na/ dgag sgrub dang bral bas sel/ grib dang dam sel yin na/ dbang bskur dang tshogs 'khor gyis sel/ gang 'dzag dang nad gzhi yin na/ dmigs pa dang 'khrul 'khor gyis sel yang gsung ngo / / 'dir 'dzag srung bka' rgya ma'i dmigs pa sbyor rgyu yin na'ang / bka' rgya ma yin pa'i phyir mang po 'tshogs pa'i nang du mi 'chad pas zur tsam smos pa de kas chog /

The best method is to dispel obstructions with an attitude that is free of denying or affirming. The middle method is to dispel them through empowerment conferrals and communal feasts. The least is to dispel them through visualizations and yogic exercises. So it is taught. It is further said that if excessive attachment and habitual clinging has caused the problems, they are dispelled by being free of denying or affirming. If caused by contamination and broken pledges, they can be dispelled by empowerment conferrals and communal feasts. If caused by emissions, they can be dispelled through visualizations and yogic exercises. Here, there is the option of applying the visualization of the sealed command to guard against emissions. However, since it is a sealed command, don’t explain it in a large assembly; it is sufficient to mention it on the side.

de la thun gcig byed dam mi byed blo dang sbyar ro/ / yang slob ma gal che nyung ngu la dmigs pa de 'bogs nas/ de nyid dmigs skor bcu gsum par 'gyur ba yang shes par bya'o/ / yang dkyus (29) ltar na/ gtum mo la gzhung tshig gis zin pa'i dmigs pa bdun yod/ rtsa tshig gis dngos su ma zin kyang gtum mo'i thon chos sam/ bde drod kyi bogs 'don khyad par can byin rlabs bla ma'i gtum mo 'di yin/ ces mtshams sbyar nas/ byin rlabs bla ma'i gtum mo skabs 'dir ston te/ de'i dmigs pa yang logs su shes par bya'o/ /

This can be considered a separate session or not, as you like. But if that visualization is given to a few important disciples as an enhancement, then it would be considered the thirteenth round of visualization. {29} In the usual sequence, there are seven visualizations related to Fierce Inner Heat that are described in the source texts.[12] Although not actually attested in the root verses, [there is a further] teaching to arouse or enhance bliss-warmth with the special Fierce Inner Heat of the Guru’s Blessing. With that preamble, the Fierce Inner Heat of the Guru’s Blessing should be taught on this occasion. However, the visualization for that must be learned elsewhere.

de ltar na de rnams kyis ni rang lus thabs ldan gyi gtum mo rgyas par bstan pa yin la/ 'di'i yan lag tu gtum mo'i gzhung khrid kyi man ngag 'khrul 'khor rnams kyang lag len du 'debs pa shin tu gal che'o/ / gzhan lus shes rab kyi gtum mo'i skor ni man ngag rnol zab pa yod kyang re zhig gleng brjod med par 'jog /

All of the preceding descriptions have presented thoroughly the Fierce Inner Heat that employs one’s own body as the method. As a supplement to those, it is very important to implement the yogic exercises from the esoteric instructions of the source guides. Concerning the practices of Fierce Inner Heat based on another’s body, a wisdom consort, there are pointed, profound esoteric instructions. But for the time being, we set them aside without comment.

mkhas grub gzhon nu grub kyi zhal na re/ dpal ldan shangs pa'i bka' brgyud 'di rgya gar gyi rdo rje gdan pa dang / bod yul gyi sangs rgyas glang ri pa'i rnam thar skyong dgos/ gtsang sgom gyi brgyud 'dzin yin/ 'jol nyog gi brgyud 'dzin min gsung ngo / /

The learned and accomplished Zhönu Drup said: This glorious Shangpa Kagyu must emulate the life stories of the Indian Vajrāsana[13] and the Tibetan Sangye Langripa.[14] We are holders of the lineage of meditation in purity. We are not holders of the lineage of wanton behavior.[15]
gnyis pa sgyu lus chags sdang rang grol gyi
B. Illusory Body, Naturally Liberated Desire and Anger
gdams ngag la/ dbang po rab bla ma dam pa grogs su bsten pa/ dbang po 'bring tshig gzhan gyis bar ma chod par khrid pa/ dbang po tha ma mal gcig tu ting nge 'dzin bskyed pa'o/ /

This instruction has three parts: (1) Relying on the Friendship of a Holy Guru for those of the highest capabilities, (2) Guidance without Interruption by Other Words for the average, and (3) Developing Meditative Absorption in a Single Sitting for the lowest.
dang po
1. Relying on the Friendship of a Holy Guru
['di] la/ mos gus bla ma'i lam khyer dang / cir snang bden med lam khyer gnyis so/ /
This has two parts: (1) Integrating Devotion to the Guru and (2) Integrating the Unreal Nature of Whatever Appears.
Session 13.
dang po mos gus bla ma'i lam khyer ni/
a. Integrating Devotion to the Guru

dbang po rab kyi skabs 'dir sgyu lus kyi dmigs pa'i rkang chen gcig tu yang byed la/ spyir sgyu lus la sogs pa chos lnga po thams cad kyi dmigs pa'i gzhi ma yang 'di yin no/ / de yang 'di ltar skyabs 'gro sems bskyed nges par sngon du btang / dag byed stong ra sgom mi sgom nyams (30) dang sbyar/

This section for those of the highest capabilities contains one major visualization for Illusory Body. In general, this is the foundation of all visualizations in the Five Golden Dharmas, not just for Illusory Body. So in this case as well, you must first complete going for refuge and arousing the awakening mind. Whether or not you meditate on Purifying Inner Space depends on your experience. {30}

de nas rang gzhan thams cad la gzhig 'grel zhig bcug ste/ ga re/ lar 'dus byas thams cad la rtag pa'i go skabs med/ sgos su 'gro ba rigs drug gi sems can thams cad 'chi ba las ma 'das/ de yang myur du 'chi/ nam 'chi cha med/ 'chi ba la dam pa'i chos ma yin pa cis kyang mi phan/ de phyin chad da ni zas gos longs spyod kha drag dbang thang gtam snyan mi snyan dgra 'dul gnyen skyong sogs gang gis kyang dgos pa mi 'dug / ces kyang phan pa mi 'dug / da phyin chad gang dga' ci dgar thong snyam pa/ nam 'chi cha med dang / cis kyang dgos med kyi 'dun pa dung dung ba sbyangs/ de ka la cung zad ngal gso/ /

Then begin an investigation of everything pertaining to self and other. “How is it? Generally there is no chance that anything composite is permanent. Specifically, all sentient beings of the six types of migrators do not transcend death. Furthermore, we will die soon, our time is uncertain, and nothing but the Holy Dharma will be of service at that time. From now on, we will have absolutely no need of food, clothes, possessions, influence, power, good or bad reputation, defeating enemies, protecting friends, and so on. Nothing at all will help. From now on, just happily let go, whatever happens.” In this way, contemplate the unpredictability of death and the absence of necessities; train with intense yearning and then rest for a while in that.

de nas rang skad cig gis yi dam lhar gsal 'debs te/ de yang ni gu'i chos drug 'di rgyud sde thams cad kyi dgongs pa yin pas lhag pa'i lha gong du bsgoms kyang rung ba yin/ de'i nang nas kyang rgyud sde lnga'i don gyi bcud bsdus pa yin pas rgyud sde lnga'i dkyil 'khor gyi gtso bo gang blo la 'thad pa cig tu bsgoms kyang legs mod/ mnyam med rin chen brtson 'grus man chad brgyud pa nas brgyud pa'i phyag len du/ bde mchog lhan skyes nyid du bsgom par mdzad pa nyid byin rlabs kyi rgyun dang ldan pa'i rim pa yin pas/ rang nyid skad cig gis 'khor lo bde mchog lhan skyes sku mdog sngon po/ zhal gcig phyag gnyis rdo rje dang dril bu 'dzin pas yum la 'khyud pa/ zhabs g.yon bskums pas 'jigs byed nag po dang / g.yas brkyang bas dus mtshan dmar mo mnan pa/ stag lpags kyi smad dkris/ thod skam gyi dbu rgyan/ thod rlon gyi do shal/ rus pa'i rgyan drug / thor tshugs la zla ba phyed pa dang sna tshogs rdo rje la sogs pas brgyan pa/ yum rdo rje phag mo dmar mo gri gug thod pa 'dzin (31) pa dang mnyam par sbyor ba/ me dpung 'bar ba'i dbus na bzhugs par bsgom/ de yang dang por bsgrims te gsal btab/ de nas lha sku snang stong tsam sgyu ma lta bu de la cung zad sems gtad de rig pa khong lhod kyis bzhag /

Then visualize yourself instantly as the yidam deity. Regarding that, since Niguma’s Six Dharmas are the intent of all tantra classes, it is appropriate to meditate on your special deity, whatever it is. Among those, it is certainly fine to meditate on whichever one of the principal deities in the Five Tantras’ mandalas that you find agreeable, since it contains the quintessence of the meaning of all five tantras. The practice of the lineage since the time of the incomparable Rinchen Tsöndru[16] has been to meditate on Coemergent Cakrasaṃvara. Thus it is the succession endowed with the continuity of blessings. Therefore, meditate that you instantly become Coemergent Cakrasaṃvara, blue, with one face, embracing Vajravārāhī with two hands holding vajra and bell. He stands with left leg bent, pressing on black Bhairava, and right leg straight, pressing on red Kālarātri. Wrapped in a tiger-skin skirt, he is adorned with a crown of dry skulls, a garland of wet heads, the six bone ornaments, the crescent moon and crossed vajra in his hair topknot, and so forth. He is in union with red Vajravārāhī, who holds a flaying knife and skull cup. {31} They stand in the midst of a blazing bonfire. At first, concentrate and visualize clearly. Then focus lightly on the deities’ forms and just empty appearance, like an illusion. Let awareness relax inwardly.

de ma thag tu bla ma bsgom ste/ de yang rang gi rigs bdag gi tshul du spyi bo nyid du bsgom pa thob thang yin/ 'on kyang rnam pa mi bde na rang gi spyi bo'i steng gi nam mkha' drang thad la bsgom/ de yang rnam pa mi dod na/ mdun gyi phyogs steng gi nam mkha' la zhal tshur bstan pa bsgoms kyang rung ste/ gang ltar na'ang seng khri sna tshogs pad+ma nyi zla rnams brtsegs pa'i gdan la/ rang gi rtsa ba'i bla ma sku bkrag mdangs gzi brjid phun sum tshogs pa dang ldan par bsgoms te/ sgyu lus la sogs pa chos phyi ma lnga po 'di rnams kyi skabs/ rdo rje 'chang du sgom na/ sku mdog sngon por byed/ 'on kyang lag len bla ma sku dngos nyid sgom par mdzad pa ka gtso che'o/ /

Then immediately meditate on the guru. The received method is to meditate on [the guru] above the head in the manner of one’s family’s chief deity. However, if that image is not easy, meditate on the guru in the space directly above your head. If you don’t like that image, it is also acceptable to meditate on the guru facing you from the space in front. In any case, imagine a lion throne upon which is a stacked seat of a multicolored lotus, sun, and moon. Meditate on your own root guru siting there, glowing with a radiant complexion, magnificent and brilliant. In the case of Illusory Body and that of the other Five Dharmas, if you meditate on the guru as Vajradhara, you make his body color blue. However, in practice the main directive has been to meditate on the actual guru’s form.

de nas dmigs pa spros pa'i dbang du byas nas/ rtsa ba'i bla ma'i thugs ka nas 'od zer 'phros/ brgyud pa'i bla ma thams cad spyan drangs te rtsa ba'i bla ma la thim/ bla ma kun 'dus su gyur/ de bzhin du yi dam zhi khro rab 'byams thams cad spyan drangs thim yi dam kun 'dus su gyur/ phyogs bcu dus gsum gyi sangs rgyas thams cad spyan drangs thim sangs rgyas kun 'dus su gyur/ lung rtogs kyi dam chos rnams yi ge'i gzugs kyi rnam par spyan drangs thim chos kun 'dus su gyur/ theg pa che chung gi 'phags pa'i dge 'dun thams cad spyan drangs thim dge 'dun kun 'dus su gyur/ mkha' 'gro chos skyong srung ma thams cad spyan drangs te rtsa ba'i bla ma'i sku la bstim chos skyong kun 'dus su gyur/ de ltar na rtsa ba'i bla ma nyid bla ma kun 'dus/ yi dam/ sangs rgyas/ chos/ dge 'dun (32) chos skyong kun 'dus mtshan thos pa tsam gyis 'khor ba ngan song thams cad las sgrol bar mdzad na/ gsol ba btab na lta smos kyang ci dgos snyam pa dang / gzhan yang sgo du ma nas mos gus drag tu bsgom/

For an elaborate visualization, light rays radiate from the root guru’s heart, invoking all the lineage gurus to melt into the root guru. The guru becomes the union of all of them. Similarly, the whole infinite expanse of peaceful and wrathful yidams are invoked and melt into the guru, who becomes the union of all yidams. All buddhas of the ten directions and three times are invoked and melt into the guru, who becomes the union of all buddhas. The Holy Dharma of scripture and realization are invoked in the form of letters and dissolve into the guru, who becomes the union of all dharma. All the noble sanghas of the greater and lesser vehicles are invoked and melt into the guru, who becomes the union of all sangha. All ḍākinīs, dharma protectors, and guards are invoked and melt into the body of the root guru, who becomes the union of all dharma protectors. That very root guru is the union of all gurus, yidams, buddhas, dharmas, sanghas, and dharma protectors. {32} If just hearing the guru’s name can liberate one from all the bad existences of samsara, there is no need to even mention the results of supplicating. Think about that and many other approaches in order to bring intense devotion to your meditation.

de nas gsol ba 'debs dgos te/ rang gi tshe 'di'i dngos kyi pha ma dang / rang la gnod par byed pa'i dgra dang gdon bgegs/ rang nyid gang du gnas pa'i gzhi bdag rnams gtso bor gyur pa'i 'gro ba rigs drug gi sems can thams cad kyang gnas 'di nyid du 'dus te/ drin can rtsa ba'i bla ma dam pa la lus gus pas phyag dang skor ba byed/ ngag gus pas gsol ba 'debs/ yid gus pas mos gus rtse gcig tu byed bar bsam/ de nas rang gis gsol 'debs ngag tu gyer ba na/ 'gro ba rigs drug gi sems can thams cad kyis kyang ram bu bteg pa'i tshul gyis ku di ri ri gsol ba 'debs par bsam zhing / ngag tu/

Then you need to supplicate. Gather around you all sentient beings of the six kinds of migrators, primarily this life’s actual parents, those enemies and obstructing spirits that would harm you, and the ground masters of the area where you are. Show physical respect toward the kind root guru by prostrating and circumambulating, verbal respect by supplicating, and mental respect by contemplating with undivided respectful devotion. Then when you chant the supplication, imagine that all sentient beings of the six kinds of migrators accompany you like a choir with the resounding of the supplication:

dus gsum sangs rgyas thams cad 'dus pa'i ngo bo bla ma rin po che/ sems can thams cad kyi don du/ bdag gis bdag 'dzin blos thongs par mdzad du gsol/ dgos med rgyud la skye bar mdzad du gsol/ sgyu lus 'byongs par mdzad du gsol/ rmi lam 'byongs par mdzad du gsol/ 'od gsal phyag rgya chen po mchog gi dngos grub da lta nyid du myur ba nyid du 'dug sa 'di nyid du thob par byin gyis brlab tu gsol/

Precious guru, unified essence of all buddhas of the three times, for the sake of all sentient beings, I pray to you to relinquish my self-fixation, to experience no needs, to master Illusory Body, to master Dream, and to attain the supreme spiritual power of Lucid Clarity Mahāmudrā, right now, quickly, on this very seat.

ces mos gus drag po phar la thim phod dang / tshur la sim phod kyi tshul gyis gsol ba 'debs/ dmigs pa rgya che na 'byung bzhi sa rdo ri brag rtsi shing nags tshal snod bcud thams cad las gsol 'debs kyi sgra 'u ru ru 'byung bar bsam mo gsung / de ltar na/ mos gus gsol 'debs kho nas thun gyi dngos gzhi bskyangs te/ thun 'jog khar bla ma 'od du ltems se zhu/ rang la gnyis su med par thim/ (33) de ka'i ngang la sems dus gsum gyi rnam rtog spangs nas lhod de bzhag /

Pray that your devotion is strong enough to reach over and dissolve [into the guru] and then return and dissolve into you. For an expanded visualization, it is said that you imagine the murmuring sound of supplication coming from the four elements—stones, mountains, cliffs, plants, trees, forests—all of the animate and inanimate world. In this way, spend the main part of the session solely on devotional supplication. At the close of the session, the guru fills with light and dissolves, melting and becoming one with you. {33} In that state, relinquish all thoughts of past, present, and future; relax and settle in.

thun mtshams su 'dun pa gsum dang ldan par bya bar bshad pa ltar ram/ yang na dbang po rab kyi skabs 'dir/ thun mtshams su yang 'dun pa gzhan gnyis do gal chung / bla ma'i mos gus rang dgos pa yin ces zhal nas gsung ba ltar/ re zhig spros pa gzhan spangs te mos gus kho na bsgom par bya'o/ / dmigs skor bcu gsum pa'o/ /

In the session breaks, it is said one should cultivate the three intentionalities.[17] Alternatively, during this occasion for those of highest capabilities, the other two aspirations are less emphasized—it is the guru devotion that you need. That’s how it was directly taught [to me]. Sometimes leave off other elaborations and meditate only on devotion. This is the thirteenth round of visualization.
Session 14.
gnyis pa cir snang bden med lam khyed ni/
b. Integrating the Unreal Nature of Whatever Appears

dmigs pa snga ma de bsgoms pas ji zhig nas/ snang ba thams cad bden med bkrag med du bun long ba/ da lta'i mtho dman bzang ngan nye ring bden bden po 'di thams cad g.yas med du shig gis 'gro ba zhig 'byung / de yang blos phar la bden med du bsgoms pa'i shugs tsam ma yin par mos gus kyi stobs kyis khong nas rang shar du 'byung ba yin/ de ltar byung na skabs der sgyu ma lta bu'i nyams shar ba zhes bya ba yin pas/ de nyid du rang gzhan snod bcud snang ba thams cad la sems gtad nas/ ga re 'di thams cad snang ni snang / bden ni mi bden/ sgyu ma lta bu yin/ rmi lam lta bu yin snyam pa'i 'dun pa shugs cher bskyed/ de rjes sgyu ma lta bu'o bden par med do snyam pa'i blo de ka'i rang ngo la che re bltas pas/ gang yang gzung du med pa yod/ de la lhod de mnyam par bzhag / gang shar de la bcas bcos mi bya'o/ /

After some time of meditating on the previous visualization, all appearances will become an unreal, insubstantial haze. All your current ideas about high and low, good and bad, near and far, that seem so true will vanish without a trace. This is not merely due to the effect of meditating on the lack of reality externally but arises naturally from within through the power of devotion. When that occurs, that situation is called the arising of illusion-like experience. So then turn your mind to all appearances in that manner—self, other, environment, and inhabitants. “What? This all appears? It does. Is it real? It is not. It is like an illusion. It is like a dream.” Thinking that, develop powerful intentionality. Afterward, look directly at that mind that is thinking “This is like an illusion; it is like a dream.” There is nothing at all to hold on to. Relax into that and rest in equipoise. Whatever arises, do not fiddle with it.

'di la nyams len gyi ngo bo sngar gyi mos gus bla ma'i lam khyer de ka'i ngang nas/ sgyu ma'i 'dun pa gcig lhag por ston pa ka yin/ res bla ma 'od du zhu rang la bstim nas/ sgyu ma'i 'dun pa bsgom/ res bla ma mdun nam spyi bor bzhugs bzhin pa'i ngang nas sgyu ma'i 'dun pa bsgom pa gnyis po gang 'os (34) 'os su bya/ dmigs skor bcu bzhi pa'o/ /

The essence of this practice is the previous integration of devotion to the guru. Within that state, you add the one further intentionality of illusion. Sometimes meditate that the guru melts into light and dissolves into you, and then meditate with intent on illusion. Sometimes the guru is before you or sits above your head, and in that state intentionally, meditate on illusion—whatever you prefer. {34} That is the fourteenth round of visualization.
2. Guidance without Interruption by Other Words for the Average

de lta bu nyams su blangs kyang 'phral du dge sbyor ma skyes na/ mos gus rab kyi tshad du phyin pa ma byung bas lan/ dbang po rab tu ma chung / da gnyis pa dbang po 'bring tshig gzhan gyis bar ma chod par khrid pa la/ rang lus snang stong lha sku sgom pa dang / cir snang sgyu ma'i lam khyer gnyis yod/

If you have taken this into practice as described but the applied virtue does not immediately arise, the problem is that your devotion does not measure up to the highest capability and you do not fit into that category. So now, for the Guidance without Interruption by Other Words for the average capability, there are two parts: (1) Meditating on One’s Body as the Empty Appearance of the Deity’s Form and (2) Integrating Whatever Appears as Illusory Body.
Session 15.
dang po ni/
a. Meditating on One’s Body as the Empty Appearance of the Deity’s Form

skyabs 'gro nas bla ma la gsol ba 'debs pa'i bar du dbang po rab kyi skabs ltar nyams su blang / thun gyi phyed tsam sum gnyis tsam bla ma'i gsol 'debs bya/ de nas bla ma 'od du zhu nas rang la bstim/ bla ma dang rang sems dbyer med la cung zad mnyam par bzhag / der rnam rtog gcig thol gyis skye tshad pa na/ rang gi lus sems la cher gyis bltas nas/ rang nyid lha skur gsal btab/ de la gzhig 'grel zhig btang ste/ ga re/ lha skur snang ba 'di yang rang gi sems kyi snang ba las gzhan phyi rol du grub pa cung zad tsam yang med/ lha sku 'di kho na sems yin/ sems kho na lha sku 'dir snang ba yin snyam du 'dun pa drag tu sbyong ba 'di gnad gcig yin/ yang sems kyi ngo bor yang bden dngos su ma grub snang ba tsam ma gtogs phyi nang bar gsum gang na yang mi 'dug / ngo ti 'di 'dra zhig yin bya ba gcig kyang mi gda'/ snang ni snang bden ni mi bden/ sgyu ma lta bu'o zhes 'dun pa drag tu sbyong ba 'di gnad gnyis pa yin/ de nas sgyu ma lta bu'o snyam mkhan kho rang gi ngo bo la bltas pas 'dun pa de yang rang sang zhi/ gang shar ngos bzung med pa la che re 'jog pa 'di gnad gsum pa'o/ / de ltar gnad gsum dang ldan pa'i 'dun pa de nyid yang yang bsgom dgos/ dmigs skor bco lnga pa'o/ /

Practice from the refuge up through the supplication to the guru as in the instructions for those of highest capabilities. Do the supplications for half or two-thirds of the session. Then the guru melts into light and dissolves into you. Rest awhile in equipoise with your mind inseparable from the guru. There, when a thought spontaneously arises and increases, look directly at your body-mind while visualizing yourself clearly as the deity, and conduct an inspection: “How is it? This appearance of the deity’s form is nothing other than my mind’s perception. Apart from that, nothing in the least exists externally. This deity’s form is only my mind, and mind is only the deity’s form appearing here.” This vigorous training with intentionality is the first vital point. Again, look at the essence of mind: no actual valid thing is established. Other than a mere appearance, it has no outside, inside, or in between whatsoever. There is no way to say “it is truly like this.” For sure it appears, but in reality it is not real. It is like an illusion. This vigorous training with intentionality is the second vital point. Then by looking at the essence of the one who thinks “it is like an illusion,” that intentionality itself subsides in its own ground. This wide-open stare that does not identify whatever arises is the third vital point. You need to meditate with the intentionality of those three vital points again and again. This is the fifteenth round of visualization.
Session 16
gnyis pa ni/
b. Integrating Whatever Appears as Illusory Body

gnad gsum po de dag snang ba gzhan thams cad la rim gyis spo (35) zhing sbyong ba yin te/ de yang rang lus snang stong lha sku'i dmigs pa de thog mar bsgoms nas/ de ma yal ba'i ngang nas thog mar rang gi gnas khang dang rdzas longs spyod thams cad la/ sems kyi snang ba las gzhan du med pa dang / sems de yang sgyu ma lta bu dang / sgyu mar 'dzin pa yang dbyings su yal ba'i rig pa rang shar gyi rang 'gros skyong ba la bslab/ de la goms nas rang dbang ba'i zas nor 'khor g.yog yul zhing sogs yod na de dag dang / chags sdang skye ba'i yul dgra gnyen la nges par sbyang / de la goms nas rim gyis snang ba thams cad la gnad gsum po de sbyar ro/ / thun mtshams thams cad du 'chi ba mi rtag pa'i 'dun dang / bla ma'i mos gus dang / snang ba gang shar bden med sgyu ma lta bur bsgom pa ste/ gsum po gang rung gcig dang ma bral bar bya'o/ / 'di la 'dun pa gsum sbrags zer ro/ / de ltar na dmigs skor bcu drug pa'o/ /

The training is to progressively transfer those three vital points to all other appearances. {35} Begin by meditating on that visualization of your own body as the empty appearance of the deity’s form. Then without allowing that to fade, first focus on your dwelling place and all your belongings. Train in thinking that they are nothing other than the mind’s perceptions, that mind is also like an illusion, and that even fixation on illusion evaporates into basic space. Maintain the natural movement of naturally arisen pure awareness. Once you become familiar with that, train well with whatever you control—food, wealth, companions, servants, land, fields, and so forth—as well as the friends and enemies that are the objects of your desire or anger. Once you get used to that, gradually apply those three vital points to all appearances. In all the session breaks, meditate with intentionality on death and impermanence, devotion to the guru, and the unreal, illusory-like nature of whatever arises. Never be without one of those three. They are known as the three intentionalities. This is the sixteenth round of visualization.
gsum pa dbang po tha ma mal gcig tu ting nge 'dzin skyed pa
3. Developing Meditative Absorption in a Single Sitting for Those of the Lowest Capabilities

['di] la/ sad pa bzhi dang bral ba cig dgos/ bzhi ni 'gro 'dug mang po dge sbyor gyi sad/ 'pho bskyas mang po dge sbyor gyi sad/ blo sna mang po dge sbyor gyi sad/ long gtam mang po dge sbyor gyi sad/ de rnams spangs te bsgom dgos/ de la dbye na/ 'gro drug sgyu mar 'char byed/ nad gdon sgyu ma lam khyer/ 'char byed yon tan tshogs drug / zhen med sgyu ma rang shar ro/ /

For this, you must be free of the four frosts: too much movement is like frost for applied virtue, changing residence too many times is like frost for applied virtue, many plans is like frost for applied virtue, and much perverse discussion is like frost for applied virtue. The categories are (1) Making the Six Kinds of Migrators Arise as Illusion, (2) Integrating Sickness and Spirits as Illusion, (3) the sixfold set of qualities that develop, and (4) the natural arising of unattached illusion.
Session 17
dang po 'gro drug sgyu mar 'char byed ni/
a. Making the Six Kinds of Migrators Arise as Illusion

skyabs 'gro nas brtsams te bla ma la gsol 'debs kyi bar gong dang 'dra ba las/ thun gyi sum cha tsam thub pa byed gsung / de yang thems yig gi dngos bstan ltar na/ sgyu lus dbang po rab 'bring gnyis la gsol 'debs lnga/ dbang po tha ma la gsol 'debs bzhi zhes gsungs te/ de'i don ni/ (36) rab 'bring gnyis las sgyu lus 'byongs par mdzad du gsol/ / rmi lam 'byongs par mdzad du gsol/ / zhes so sor dbye ba dang / tha ma'i skabs su/ sgyu lus rmi lam 'byongs par mdzad du gsol zhes gcig tu bsdoms pas gsol 'debs bzhir 'gyur ba'i don yin kyang phyag len dang zhal gyi rgyun la/ dbang po rab 'bring tha ma gsum la de lta bu'i dbye ba mi dgos te/ gsum ka la gsol 'debs lnga byed pa dang / bzhi byed pa la khyad med gsung /

Begin with the refuge up through the supplication to the guru, the same as before, except that it is taught that you can spend one-third of the session on that. According to the actual presentation in the Inventory,[18] there are five supplications for both those of best and average capabilities, while only four supplications for those of least capabilities. {36} The reason for that is that the best and average practitioners supplicate with two separate lines: “Please let me accomplish Illusory Body. Please let me develop Dream,” whereas for those of lesser capabilities, they are combined into the single line: “Please let me accomplish Illusory Body and Dream,” effectively making four supplications. However, the actual practice and personal advice that have come down to us is that this division into three categories of best, average, and least capabilities is unnecessary. It does not matter whether all three types do five supplications or four supplications.

de nas bla ma rang la thim pa'i rjes su rang gi lus lha sku'i rnam pa nang stong sang nge ba'i smad kyi cha la sems gtad pas/ der chos 'byung gru gsum kha dog dkar zhing gsal ba/ rtsa ba phra ba thur bstan de bshang sgo'i thad tsam nas mar la zug pa/ gdengs ka che ba gyen du bstan pa'i zur mdun ma de lte ba'i thad dang / zur gzhan gnyis mkhal khung g.yas g.yon gyi phyogs su bstan pa/ dangs gsal 'od kyi rang bzhin can cig bsam/ de la sems gtad pas de'i nang du 'gro ba rigs drug gi sems can rnam pa sna tshogs pa rnams lus longs spyod mdog dbyibs cha lugs cha byad rnams spyi tshul tha dad pa/ rang rang gi bde sdug myong tshul sna tshogs dang bcas pa rnams kyis chos 'byung gi nang khrig mer gyis gang bar bsam/

After the guru dissolves into you, focus your attention on the lower part of your utterly empty deity’s form. There you imagine a tetrahedral source of phenomena, white and clear. Its narrow apex faces down and reaches directly above the anus. The wide-open side faces up with the front vertex at the navel and the other two vertices face the direction of the right and left kidneys. Imagine that it is radiant and clear with the nature of light. Turning your attention to this, the sentient beings of the six kinds of migrators appear within it in their various forms and their general distinct modes of body, possessions, color, shape, clothing, and attributes, along with their individual and varied ways of experiencing happiness and sadness. Imagine that they are packed into the source of phenomena.

de yang rang rgyud la 'gro ba tha dad du skye ba len pa'i rgyu las nyon gyi bag chags thams cad rigs drug so so'i gzugs su shar ba yin snyam pa dang / lte 'og na rigs drug gi snang ba 'char ba'i rtsa yig yod pa rnams gzugs brnyan de dang der shar ba yin snyam ba'i mos ba yang cung zad bya/ de rjes de rnams nyid rigs drug dngos yin pa'i tshul du mos pa las/ sems kyi rtsi kha lte ba'i rigs drug la gtad cing / spyir mkha' khyab kyi (37) sems can thams cad dmigs yul du byas nas ga re 'di rnams snang ni snang / bden ni mi bden/ ces bden med kyi 'dun pa drag tu sbyang / yang 'di rnams bden med la bden par gzung bas 'khor bar 'khyams pa snying re rje snyam snying rje brtse lhag pa bsgom/ yang 'di rnams 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal las bla mas bskyab tu gsol/ / pha bla ma mkhyen snyam pa/ bla ma'i mos gus kyi gdung shugs dang 'brel par gsol ba zhig kyang btab po/ /

Think, “All the habitual patterns of karma and afflictions that are the causes of taking birth as the variety of migrators are present in my mind stream and have arisen in the bodies of each of the six kinds.” Also, reflect awhile on the following thought: “Below my navel there are root syllables that give rise to the appearances of the six kinds, and so those images arise there.” Following that, more than imagining those very images to be the actual six kinds of beings, focus with the pinpoint of mind on the six kinds of beings below the navel and make all sentient beings throughout space the general object of visualization. {37} Then think, “How is it? They appear, but they are not real.” Train vigorously with the intentionality that they are unreal. Also meditate with higher love and compassion, thinking, “It is so sad that they all cling to the unreal as if it were real and so wander in cyclic existence.” Further, make a supplication while connecting with powerful feelings of guru devotion: “Guru, please offer them refuge from their sufferings in cyclic existence. Beloved guru, please consider them.”

de nas de rnams la sems che re gtad pa na/ rigs drug gi sems can de dag gcig yal/ gnyis yal/ re re nas rim pas yal te/ mthar chos 'byung gi nang stong sang song ba la sems gtad/ da rjes nas lus dang chos 'byung la yal ba sogs kyi dmigs pa'i spros pa'ang mi dgos te/ gtad so thams cad dang bral ba'i 'dzin med la shig ge bzhag / yang de la ma gnas na rang gzhan snod bcud thams cad la dmigs te sgyu ma lta bu'o/ / med bzhin du snang ba'o/ / snang bzhin du ma grub pa'o zhes shes par bya/ des dmigs pa tshar gcig song / de nyid yang yang bsgom pa'o/ / 'di la dmigs pa gtad so'i gnad brgyad yod de/ chos 'byung la dmigs pa/ rigs drug la dmigs pa/ 'gro drug bden med du sbyang ba/ snying rje bskyed pa/ bla ma'i gsol 'debs/ rigs drug stong par sbyong ba/ rang babs skyong ba/ snang srid sgyu ma'i 'dun pa'o/ / lar dmigs pa cig la 'di bas zab pa med ces gsung /

Then, as you gaze with open attention at those six kinds of sentient beings, one of them disappears. Then a second disappears. Then one after another vanishes. In the end, the source of phenomena becomes empty inside. Focus on that. Further elaborations of the visualization after that, such as the disappearance of your body and the source of phenomena, are not necessary. Rest relaxed without fixation, free of all focus. When you can no longer stay in that state, envision the whole of the environment and its inhabitants and know: “It is like an illusion. Nonexistent yet appearing. Appearing while not real.” That completes a single visualization. Meditate on it again and again. There are eight vital points on which to focus in this visualization: visualizing the source of phenomena, visualizing the six kinds of beings, training in the unreal nature of the six kinds of migrators, arousing compassion, supplicating the guru, resolving the six kinds of beings into emptiness, maintaining a natural repose, and intentionally cultivating apparent existence as illusion. It is said there is no other visualization more profound than this.

thun mtshams kyi nyams len ni 'di la'ang 'dun pa sum sbrags kho na ste/ de yang dang po nyid nas 'dun pa gsum po gang rung cig sleb par bya snyam pa tsam gyis gar yang mi rung bas/ thog mar gang yang (38) rung ba gcig thun mtshams su sleb pa'i thabs la 'bad/ tshul des gsum kar la re re bzhin du bslabs nas/ mthar gsum po gang rung re dang ma bral bar bya snyam pa'i 'dun pa btang na/ gang rung re dang ma bral bar yong pa yin/ dper na/ thog mar thun mtshams su 'chi ba mi rtag pa'i 'dun pa rtag tu sleb par bya snyam pa'i go cha gyon nas/ thun mtshams su mi rtag pa gang dran thub thub bya/ tshul de lta bus thun mtshams su dran pa'i bya ra bas gzhur na zla ba gcig gam gnyis tsam na/ thun mtshams phal cher du mi rtag pa'i 'dun pas sleb 'ong / de byung na re zhig de bor nas tshul de kas bla ma'i mos gus la bslab/ de yang byung ba na/ yang re zhig de gnyis ka bor nas sgyu ma'i 'dun pa la tshul de kas bslab/ de yang thun mtshams phal cher du byung na/ de rjes gsum po gang rung cig dang ma bral ba'i 'dun pa tsam btang bas/ gsum po gang rung re dang ma bral bar yong ba yin no/ / dmigs skor bcu bdun pa'o/ /

The practice during session breaks is solely the threefold intentionality regarding these subjects. However, merely thinking to train from the start in whichever of those three is preferable is not appropriate at just any time. {38} At the beginning, exert yourself in the methods of session-break training in whichever one is suitable. That will ensure training in each of the three separately. Finally, if you establish your intention by thinking, “I will stick with whichever of the three is appropriate,” you will in fact never be without the appropriate one. For example, right at the start of the break, don the armor of thinking, “May the intentionality of death and impermanence always come to me,” and then recall impermanence as much as you can during the session break. In that way, when you post the sentinel of mindfulness in the session breaks, the intentionality of impermanence will develop in most of the session breaks after just one or two months. When that happens, set it aside for a while and pursue guru devotion in the same way. Then, once that works, again set aside both of those and train in the same way with the intentionality of illusion. Once that occurs in most of the session breaks, afterward merely formulating the intention to stay with whichever of the three is suitable will be enough to ensure that happening. This is the seventeenth round of visualization.
Session 18
gnyis pa nad gdon sgyu ma lam khyer la/
b. Integrating Sickness and Spirits as Illusion

khrid yig gsum dang zur 'debs rnying pa rnams na/ don 'dra yang rnam grangs nges med la don tshad ma tshang yang ci rigs 'dug na'ang nges tig can 'di yin te/ nad lam du khyer na/ na bar snang ba 'di yang / las ngan sdig sgrib sbyong ba dang / dge sbyor gyi bskul ma yin pas mtshan ldan bla ma'i thugs rje'i 'jug pa yin/ sku drin re che snyam pa byas nas/ nad bla ma'i rang bzhin du mos/ gsol ba drag tu btab/ mthar bla ma dang nad dang / rang sems gsum dbyer med du che re mnyam par bzhag / lugs gcig go / /

Whereas the three guidebooks and supplements of old contain similar content with different enumerations and varying degrees of completeness, this is the definitive commentary. To integrate sickness, think, “This appearance of sickness will purify negative actions and obscurations and is encouragement for virtuous action. Therefore, it represents the compassion of the qualified guru. How kind!” Regard the sickness as the nature of the guru and supplicate intensely. Finally, rest in wide-open equipoise of these three inseparable: the guru, the sickness, and your mind. That is one way.

yang na bar snang ba 'di 'khrul pa yin/ gnas tshul la na ba dang / na mkhan yod ma myong / med bzhin du na bar snang ba rmi (39) lam du na ba dang 'dra snyam na ba'i thog de khar sgyu ma rmi lam gyi dran 'dun drag tu bya/ mthar na bar snang ba rang sems su shes/ de la'ang gtad so med pa sgyu ma lta bu la mnyam par bzhag / lugs gnyis pa yin/

Alternatively, think, “This appearance of sickness is a delusion. In the actual mode of being, there is no existent sickness or sick person. The nonexistent appearance of sickness is like the sickness in a dream.” {39} Thus intensely apply the intentionality of recalling illusion and dream directly to that sickness. At the end, understand that the appearance of sickness is your own mind and rest in equipoise of illusory-like nature without particular focus. That is a second way.

yang na bar snang ba 'di sgyu ma lta bu med bzhin du snang ba yin/ snang ba 'di blos gang byas yin snyam pas steng rlung drag tu mnan/ lte ba'i chos 'byung gi nang nas mar nad rnams song / chos 'byung gi gsham je ring je ring la sa 'og thag ring por song zhing / nad kyang de'i nang nas mar song ba/ gnyis gar sa 'og tu 'ja' ltar yal bar bsam/ lugs gsum pa ste 'di sngon chad zhal shes yin/ de ltar nad lam khyer gsum mo/ /

Or think, “This appearance of sickness is like an illusion in that it does not exist and yet it appears. What is my mind doing with this appearance?” Press the upper wind down forcefully. All sickness has gone down into the interior of the source of phenomena at the navel. The bottom of the source of phenomena grows longer and longer until it reaches far below the ground, and the sickness also descends with it. Imagine them both vanishing underground like a rainbow. That is a third way, from previous oral advice. So there are three integrations of sickness.

gdon lam khyer la yang gsum ste/ gdon gyi gnod pa dge sbyor gyi bskul mar shes nas/ bla ma'i thugs rje yin pa dang / bla ma la gsol ba 'debs pa dang / bla ma dang / gnod byed dang / rang sems gsum po rang bzhin gsal stong du ro mnyam pa'i ngang bskyang ngo / /

The integration of spirits also has three options. Once you understand that the harm done by spirits is a call to virtuous practice, it becomes the guru’s compassion. Supplicate the guru and maintain a state where the guru, the harm, and your mind are all of equal value in their nature of clarity and emptiness.

yang na gnod par byed pa po'i 'dre gdon yang med bzhin du snang / snang bzhin du ma grub/ de bzhin du gnod pa'i bya ba nyer 'tshe sdug bsngal dang / gnod pa 'byung ba'i yul rang nyid lta bu sems can de yang med bzhin du snang / snang bzhin du ma grub/ sgyu ma lta bu yin/ rmi lam lta bu yin/ 'di la bden par 'dzin pa re 'khrul snyam du 'dun pa drag tu sbyangs pa'i mthar/ gnod byed du snang ba ngam ngam pa de ka'i ngo bo la bltas te che re 'jog go /

Alternatively, remember that the harmful demon spirit appears while not existing, and while appearing it is not truly established. It is like an illusion. It is like a dream. To fixate on it as real is totally deluded. Train vigorously with that intentionality. In the end, look at the essence of that spontaneously appearing harm-doer and rest in a wide-open state.

yang na chos 'byung dang 'gro ba drug sogs gong bzhin bsgoms la/ gnod byed du snang ba de mdun du dmigs/ sgyu ma lta bu'i 'dun pa'i rtsis zin pa'i ngang nas/ rlung nang du 'jug pa dang lhan cig gdon de yang (40) sna sgo nas bcug ste/ lte ba'i chos 'byung gi nang du sleb/ chos 'byung shin tu yangs por song / rlung bzung ste dkrug 'khor byas pas/ chos 'byung gi kha 'ubs kyis 'dus pas 'bros sa med/ gnod byed de yang rigs drug gi gnas thams cad du 'khyams pas/ so so'i sdug bsngal mthong zhing myong / las 'bras la yid ches/ gnod sems zhi/ byang chub kyi sems dang ldan par bsam/ slar yang rlung phyir bsel ba na/ gnod byed de sna sgo nas rgyangs te thon/ thag je ring je ring la yal bar bsam pa'am/ yang na lan chags sel ba'i gtor ma byin te gshegs su gsol/ 'di la nang sel dmigs pa drug yod kyang / dmigs chen gcig tu brtsi ba'am gnyis su brtsi ba'ang yod/ 'dir gcig tu bsdoms te/ dmigs skor bco brgyad pa'o/ /

Otherwise, meditate on the source of phenomena and six kinds of beings and so forth as before. Then visualize the apparent harm-doer in front of you. While keeping the recollection of illusion-like appearance, imagine that as you inhale, the spirit enters through your nose at the same time. {40} It arrives inside the source of phenomena at your navel. The source of phenomena has become huge. Hold your breath and twist around. The opening of the source of phenomena is drawn together so that there is no escape. That harm-doer now wanders through all the places of the six kinds of beings, seeing and experiencing their individual sufferings. It comes to believe in karmic cause and effect, its malicious mind is pacified, and it attains the awakening mind. Then when you breathe out again, that harm-doer is expelled through your nose. Imagine that it goes farther and farther away until it vanishes altogether. Or you can give it a torma to repay your karmic debts and request it to leave. Within all this there are six visualizations, but they are also counted as one major visualization or as two. Here they are combined into one. This is the eighteenth round of visualization.
gsum pa 'char byed yon tan tshogs drug ni/
c. The Sixfold Set of Qualities That Develop

sgyu lus dang po tha ma'i dmigs pa bsgoms pa'i gnas skabs kyi phan yon bshad pa ste/ 'di la dmigs pa logs pa med/ de yang drod skye ba dang gcig / thig le brtan pa dang gnyis/ rmi lam sbyong spel dang gsum/ 'gro drug gi yul snang dang bzhi/ sems can smin grol dang lnga/ sgyu ma rang shar dang drug go /

This is an explanation of the benefits of Illusory Body to be given at the beginning of the meditation on the visualization for those of lesser capabilities. There is no new visualization here. The benefits are (1) the arising of warmth, (2) the stabilizing of the vital drops, (3) the refining and increasing of dreams, (4) the appearance of the regions of the six migrators, (5) the ripening and liberating of sentient beings, and (6) the natural arising of illusion.
dang po ni/ lte ba dang dbu ma'i mes sna gtum mo'i rtsa yig yod sa'i gnas la gnad du bsnun pa yin pas/ drod rang shugs la skye'o/ /

(1) Since [Illusory Body practice] emphasizes the navel and the lower end of the central channel, which is the vital point of the area of the root syllable of Fierce Inner Heat, warmth rises up automatically.
gnyis pa ni/ dbu ma'i mas snar sems gtad par song bas/ rlung yang der 'gag / des rtsa kha sdom/ thig le zin cing brtan par 'gyur ro/ /
(2) Since you focus your mind on the lower end of the central channel, the winds are blocked there and that closes the channels, holding the vital drops and stabilizing them.

gsum pa ni/ dbu ma'i mas sna rtsa mdud gru gsum gyi nang du rigs drug gi rtsa yig yod pas/ de la gnad du bsnun par song ba'i phyir/ rmi lam du yang rigs drug gi gzugs brnyan dang / (41) yul phyogs sna tshogs pa'i rnam pa can gyi sbyong spel sprul bsgyur dus gcig tu 'byung ngo / /

(3) Since the root syllables of the six kinds of beings are inside the triangular channel knot at the lower end of the central channel, and because this targets the vital point, {41} in dreams you will be able to refine, increase, emanate, and change the images of those six kinds and their various habitats simultaneously.
bzhi pa ni/ rigs drug gi rtsa khams la rlung sems kyis gnad du bsnun pa yin pas/ rigs drug gi gnas lkog gyur rnams mthong ba'i yul snang gtan la 'bebs thub bo/ /
(4) Since you apply wind-mind to the channels and constituents of the six kinds of beings, you will be able to ascertain the appearances of their hidden places.
lnga pa ni/ mkha' khyab kyi sems can thams cad la stong nyid snying rje bla ma'i mos gus gsum gyi sgo nas rang gzhan mnyam nyid du bsgoms pa yin pas sems can smin grol nus pa'o/ /

(5) Since this is meditation on the equality of self and other by means of guru devotion, emptiness, and compassion regarding all sentient beings throughout space, you will have the ability to ripen and liberate sentient beings.

drug pa ni/ lte ba sprul pa'i 'khor lo ni gnyid sad dus kyi 'khrul pa 'char ba'i gzhi yang yin/ de la gnad du bsnun na sad dus kyi 'khrul pa dag byed sgyu lus kyi rtogs pa rang shar du 'byung ba'i nus pa yod pa'ang yin pa las de la gnad du bsnun pa yin pas/ sgyu lus kyi rtogs pa zhes bya ba rtog bral gyi lha sku snang stong snang ba rab 'byams sgyu ma lta bu rang shar du yong ba'o/ /

(6) The emanation chakra at the navel is the basis for the arising of delusion during waking time. When that vital point is targeted, it purifies the waking delusions and makes it possible for the realization of illusory body to arise of itself. And since that is the application of the vital point, this so-called realization of illusory body brings the nonconceptual deity’s body of empty form, the natural arising of the whole apparent universe as an illusion.
bzhi pa zhen med sgyu ma rang shar ni/
d. The Natural Arising of Illusion Free of Attachment

dbang po tha ma kho na'i khyad chos ma yin te/ spyir sgyu lus kyi rtogs pa tshad du phyin pa'i rtags bshad pa'o/ / de yang sgyu lus bsgoms pas da lta nas chags sdang mtho dman gyi a 'thas 'di je chung du song nas/ mthar bde sdug chags sdang thams cad yul stongs te/ rang gi g.yas nas mi gcig gis bstod pa la dga' ba med/ g.yon nas cig shos kyis smad pa la mi dga' ba med/ rang ngam rang phyogs gtam snyan pa dang / nom pa sogs thob pa la dga' ba med/ gtam mi snyan pa dang yo byad shor ba la mi dga' ba med pa de'i tshe/ sgyu lus kyi nyams rtogs la brtan pa thob pa yin/ ji skad du/ / tsan dan ste'u mtshungs pa la/ / chags bral zhes ni brjod pa yin/ / ces (42) bshad pa lta bu'o/ / phyi ma 'di gnyis la dmigs skor brtse rgyu med/ chos thun ni gcig gam gnyis ji ltar 'os pa'o/

This is not a special teaching just for those of lowest capabilities but rather an explanation of the signs of successful realization of Illusory Body in general. Meditation on Illusory Body reduces your current obstinate reification of attraction and aversion, high and low. In the end, the realm of all joy and pain, love and hate, will be emptied. You would not be pleased when a person to your right heaps on praise or displeased when someone on the left criticizes you. You won’t be overjoyed at good news or profits concerning you and yours or displeased at hearing bad news or suffering loss. At that point, you have stabilized the experiential realization of Illusory Body. This is like the saying: Equality of sandalwood tree and ax is what we call free of attachment.[19] {42} These last two subjects are not counted as rounds of visualization. They comprise one or two teaching sessions as appropriate.
gsum pa rmi lam nying 'khrul rang dag gi
C. Dream, Naturally Purified Double Delusion
khrid la/ rmi lam bzung ba/ sbyang ba/ spel ba/ sprul pa/ sgyur ba/ yul snang gtan la dbab pa sde drug go/ /
In this guidance there are six parts: (1) recognizing dreams, (2) refining, (3) increasing, (4) emanating, (5) changing, and (6) ascertaining objective appearances.
dang po rmi lam bzung ba
1. Recognizing Dreams
['di] la/ rang zin thig le dbang bzhi'i gnad kyi gdams pa dang / de la ma zin na gnad 'chug med dgu la brten pa'o/ /
This has two parts: (1) Instruction on the Vital Points of the Four Empowerments of Drops if self-recognized and (2) Relying on the Nine Infallible Vital Points if not recognized.
Session 19
dang po ni/
a. Instruction on the Vital Points of the Four Empowerments of Drops if Self-Recognized

'di rmi lam 'dzin pa'i dmigs pa'i rtsa ba gal che shos yin te/ de la bla ma'i rnal 'byor ni/ dmigs pa spyi khog thams cad sgyu lus kyi skabs dang mtshungs/ khyad par mi 'dra ba ni/ dus gsum sangs rgyas thams cad 'dus pa'i ngo bo bla ma rin po che/ sems can thams cad kyi don du bdag gis bdag 'dzin blos thongs bar mdzad du gsol/ dgos med rgyud la skye bar mdzad du gsol/ rmi lam zin par mdzad du gsol/ / ces gsol 'debs kyi mtha' bsgyur ba kho na yin/

This basic visualization of recognizing dreams is the most important. For the guru yoga, all the general contents of the visualization are the same as in Illusory Body, except for the one change in the end of the supplication: Precious guru, unified essence of all buddhas of the three times, for the sake of all sentient beings, I pray to relinquish self-fixation, to be without needs, and to recognize dreams.
'dir ma zad gzhan thams cad la yang 'dra ste/ gsol 'debs kyi tshig dang po gnyis thams cad mtshungs shing / tshig rkang gsum pa mtha' bsgyur ba kho na'o/ /
Everything else [in the later practices] also follows this pattern: the first two lines of the supplication is everywhere the same, and only the third line at the end is changed.

de ltar thun gyi sum cha tsam bla ma'i rnal 'byor bsgoms nas/ bla ma 'od du zhu rang la thim/ rang lus lha sku gsal stong du shar ba'i lus kyi dbus su rtsa dbu ma kha dog dkar ba dangs gsal shel gyi sbubs lta bu/ yar sna spyi bo dang / mar sna gsang bar zug pa/ dbu ma'i nang gi yas snar haM dkar po mgo bo thur du blta ba dang / mas snar hU~M dmar po mgo bo gyen du blta ba cig gsal btab/ gang shar la spyir bden med dang / sgos su rmi lam du shes pa'i rtsis bzung (43) nas bsgom pa cig thams cad du gal che/ spyi bo'i haM las thig le dkar po sran ma tsam cig hril gyis chad snying gar sleb/ nyon mongs pa gti mug dag / snying ga yan chad khog stod yang chod pa'am/ bde chod kyis song bar bsam/ gsang ba'i hU~M las thig le dmar po sran rdog tsam cig yar chad snying gar sleb/ nyon mongs pa 'dod chags dag / sked man chad khog smad yang chod pa'am bde chod kyis song / dkar dmar gnyis po snying gar 'dzom/ zhe sdang ni rang dag la song / snying ga'i thad bde sang ba dang / yang chod kyis song bar bsam/

Meditate on this guru yoga for one-third of the session, after which the guru melts into light and dissolves into you. In the center of your body, which has arisen as the clear empty form of the deity, is the central channel. It is white and radiantly clear like a crystal tube. The upper end reaches the inside of the cranium and the lower end the perineum. Visualize that inside the upper end of the central channel there is an upside-down white haṃ and in the lower end an upright red hūṃ. It is important in all cases to meditate while taking into account the wisdom that whatever arises is false in general and a dream in particular. {43} A pea-sized white drop breaks away from the haṃ in the head and arrives at the heart. Think that this purifies the affliction of stupidity and that the torso above the heart becomes light or blissful. Then a pea-sized red vital drop breaks off from the hūṃ at the perineum and arrives at the heart. This purifies the affliction of desire and the lower body below the waist becomes light or blissful. The two white and red drops meet at the heart and anger is naturally purified. The area of the heart becomes blissful or light.

de nas dbu ma'i nang snying ga'i thad kyi khong stong der/ thig le gnyis po 'bros 'ded kyi tshul du 'khor ba la sems gtad/ 'khor tshul g.yas skor dang g.yon skor rang gi blo la gang bde yin/ de la sems gtad de/ rmi lam rang yin snyam pa'i 'dun pa gsum bzhi zhig bya/ de nas thig le gnyis po de gcig rjes gcig gis zin pa'i tshul gyis reg tsam reg tsam 'dug cing 'khor ba la sems gtad/ rmi lam yin snyam 'dun pa drag tu sbyang / de rjes yang sngar bzhin las/ reg pa la brten nas lus sems bde chil chil yong bar mos/ de la'ang sgyu ma'i 'dun pa sbyang / de nas dkar po dmar po la thim dkar po yal ba'am/ de go bzlog kyang rung ste/ gang ltar yang gcig la cig shos thim/ de yang gtad yal du song bar bsam/ de ka'i ngang la ci yang mi bsam par cung zad bzhag /

Then focus your attention on those two drops chasing each other around inside the empty space of the central channel at the level of the heart. Their manner of circling around can be clockwise or counterclockwise, as you like. Recall the intentional notion of “this is indeed a dream” three or four times. The two drops circling around trying to capture each other barely touch. Focus on that while intensely training in the intentionality that it is a dream. The next [visualization] is the same except that you imagine bliss flowing into your body and mind as a result of the [two drops] touching. For this, also train with the intentionality of illusion. Then the white drop dissolves into the red one and disappears, or the other way around—either way, one dissolves into the other. As you focus on that, imagine that they vanish. Then rest for a while directly in that experience without thinking of anything at all.

de nas yang rang gzhan snang ba thams cad la sems gtad de/ 'di thams cad snang ni snang / bden ni mi bden snyam pa dang / khyad par du yang nga gnyid du song 'dug / snang ba 'di thams cad rmi lam rang yin pa 'dug snyam pa'i (44) 'dun pa drag tu sbyong ste/ dmigs pa tshar gcig song / yang rtsa dbu ma gsal 'debs pa sogs yang nas yang du de kho na bskyar gyin bsgom/

Again turn your attention to all the appearances of self and others and think, “All these appearances appear; in reality they are not real.” In particular, think, “I have fallen asleep. All this appearance is actually a dream.” Train vigorously with that intentionality. {44} This constitutes one visualization. Again, imagine the central channel and so forth over and over again, meditating repeatedly just on this.[20]

thun mtshams su yang sgyu ma'i 'dun pa'i dod du rmi lam gyi 'dun pa bcug nas/ 'dun pa gsum sbrags bya ste/ mi rtag pa dang / mos gus dang / rmi lam gyi 'dun pa ste gsum mo/ / rmi lam 'dun pa'i gnad bya ba yin pas 'gro 'chag nyal 'dug zas za ba gtam smra ba mdor na spyod lam thams cad du nga gnyid du song 'dug / rmi lam rmi bar 'dug / rmi lam rang yin ang snyam pa rgyun chags su byung na/ rmi lam zin pa la tshegs med pas 'di rang gal che'o/ / de ltar bsgoms pas myur du rmi lam zin par 'gyur ro/

During the session breaks, replace the intentionality of Illusion with that of Dream so that the threefold intentionality becomes impermanence, devotion, and dream. Since the intentionality of dreaming is the main point, during all daily activities—whether walking, moving, resting, eating, or talking—constantly think, “I have fallen asleep. I am dreaming a dream. Surely it is a dream.” If you maintain that, you will have no trouble recognizing dreams, so it is very important. You will quickly recognize dreams through meditating in this way.

yang las 'brel chung ba 'ga' la nyin par bstar chags su bsgoms kyang / 'phral du ma zin par 'gor na yang zla ba gcig gam/ zla ba phyed dang gnyis tsam gyi bar du zin du re ba dang / ma zin gyi dogs pa'i rtsis btab mi byed par ci dgar bskyur/ 'dun pa drag tu byed pa gal che/

However, the recognition of dreams is delayed in some people with weak karmic connections even if they meditate continuously like this during the daytime. They should not hope for recognition in a month or a month and a half, and not worry about the lack of recognition, but just let whatever happens happen. It is important to intensify intentionality.

spyir sngon gyi nA ro chos drug pa rnams/ dbang po rab tu gyur pa la/ / lo yis zin pa dag kyang srid zer/ lo gcig tsam bsgoms na rmi lam zin pa la brtan pa thob/ ces 'dod par 'dug / chos 'di'i lugs kyis dben pa'i gnas su grib kyis ma phog / long gtam dang ma 'dres/ nges 'byung skyo shas dang bcas par bsgoms na/ zhag bdun nam bcu tshun la 'go tho re ba zin yong /

In general, it was said by previous practitioners of Nāropa’s Six Dharmas that those of the highest capabilities might recognize dreams after a year. If you meditate for just a year, you will obtain stability in recognizing dreams. They hold that view. But in [Niguma’s] dharma tradition, if you meditate in an isolated place with renunciation and disillusionment and without being affected by polluting stains or involved with conversation, then you will begin to have occasional recognition in seven or ten days’ time.
de nas ma 'byams ma dred zhud kyis ma khyer bar sgoms na/ zla ba gsum mam bzhi tshun chod la rmi lam zin cing brtan pa thob par 'ong ngo / /
Then if you sustain the meditation without becoming dissipated or sloppy, you will recognize dreams in a period of three to four months and gain stability.

lar ma bsgoms pas kyang rmi lam lan re zin pa 'ong ste/ de 'dra stes dbang tsam yin gtad pa cang med/ (45) yang dang por bsgom ma thag rang du zin pa'ang yong ste/ rkyen gsar ngas kyis zin pa zer/ rjes la mi yong / de 'dras zin pa'i go mi chod/ rgyun 'thud mi thub/ 'dir dmigs pa'i stobs kyis zin pa dang / 'dun pa'i stobs kyis zin pa cig dgos/ de 'dras zin na 'di lan gcig zin pa'i rjes su nyams len ma bshol na gong 'phel du song nas bstar chags su zin yong pa la dka' las med pa yin no/ / dmigs skor bcu dgu pa'o/ /

Even if you don’t continue to meditate, you will recognize the occasional dream. But those are chance occurrences and not reliable. Also, you might randomly recognize a dream one time right after you first meditate [on lucid dreaming], and with this new circumstance say, “I recognize dreams!” But then it doesn’t happen again. This kind of recognition is not useful because it is not sustainable. {45} You must recognize dreams on the strength of the visualization and on the strength of intentionality. If you recognize dreams in that way and do not postpone your practice after a single recognition, lucid dreaming will increase and recognition will occur on a regular basis without difficulty. This is the nineteenth round of visualization.
gnyis pa gnad 'chugs med dgu la brten pa ni/
b. Relying on the Nine Unerring Vital Points if Not Recognized

dmigs pa snga ma'i spogs chog yin te/ spyir ni rang zin thig le dbang bzhi'i gnad nyid shin tu zab pas/ de kas rmi lam zin dgos kyang dgos 'ong yang 'ong / spogs chog 'di dag dgos pa cher mi 'ong / ci ste na/ dmigs pa snga ma 'bad pas bsgoms kyang zla shas ma zin na/ bogs 'don 'di rnams rim gyis bya ste/ de la gnad 'chugs med dgu zhes bya ba/ dus kyi gnad gsum/ tho rangs/ nam langs/ nyi ma rtse shar ro/ / lus kyi gnad gsum ni/ skyil krungs/ tsog pu/ seng ge'i nyal stabs gsum mo/ / dmigs pa'i gnad gsum ni/ rtog med la bzung ba gnyis dang / rtog bcas lam du khyer ba'o/ / de ltar dgu las/ skabs 'dir dmigs pa'i gnad gsum mo/ /

These are to boost the previous visualizations. In general, since the crucial four empowerments of the vital drop in self-recognizing dreams is extremely profound, using that to recognize dreams is an absolute must and will certainly produce those lucid dreams. So there is no great need for these enhancements. Nevertheless, if the former visualization does not produce recognition in a few months despite energetically meditating, then do these enhancements in sequence. The Nine Unerring Vital Points are three unerring points of time: dawn, daybreak, and sunrise; three vital points of body posture: full lotus, seated with legs drawn up, and reclining in lion pose; and three vital points of visualization: two that are nonconceptual and one that integrates concepts. Of those nine, here we will consider the three vital points of visualization.
Session 20
de la dang po rtog med la bzung ba dmigs pa'i gnad rgya bkyed pa ni/
i. Extensive Vital Visualization for Recognizing without Concepts

dbu ma yi ge gnyis dang bcas pa gsal 'debs pa sngar bzhin/ de rjes rlung ro bsal/ steng rlung nang du rngubs pa dang lhan cig haM las thig le dkar po chad te snying gar sleb/ 'og rlung yar 'then pas hU~M las thig le dmar po chad te snying gar sleb/ rlung kha sbyor du bzung skabs/ thig le gnyis po snying (46) gar 'khor ba la sems gtad/ rmi lam gyi 'dun pa bya/ bum dbang ngo / / de rjes rlung phyir bsal ba'i dus thig le dkar po sna bug g.yas dang / dmar po g.yon nas thon te/ smin mtshams su 'khor ba la sems gtad te/ rmi lam gyi 'dun pa drag tu bya/ gsang dbang ngo / / thig le de gnyis rang gi mdun thad du babs te/ dkar po dpal 'khor lo sdom pa yab dang / dmar po rdo rje phag mor gyur/ kha sbyor lhan cig skyes pa'i skur gyur pa la sems gtad te rmi lam gyi 'dun pa drag tu bya/ shes rab ye shes kyi dbang ngo / / yum yab la thim/ de yang mkha' dbyings su yal bar bsams te/ mi rtog pa la mnyam par bzhag / dbang bzhi pa'o/ /

Imagine the central channel with the two syllables as before. After that, clear away the dead air. As you inhale the upper winds, a white drop breaks off from the haṃ and arrives at the heart. As you draw up the lower wind, a red drop breaks off from the hūṃ and arrives at the heart. When you hold the joining winds, the two drops circulate in the heart. {46} Focusing on them with the intentionality of dreaming is the vase empowerment. When you again exhale, the white drop emerges from the right nostril and the red drop from the left. They swirl around at the point between your eyebrows. Focusing on that with the intense intentionality of dreaming is the secret empowerment. Those two drops fall in front of you. The white one becomes glorious Cakrasaṃvara and the red one becomes Vajravārāhī. They join as the form of coemergent union. Focusing on that with the intense intentionality of dreaming is the wisdom-awareness empowerment. Imagine that the mother dissolves into the father, imagine that Cakrasaṃvara dissolves into Vajravārāhī, and that also vanishes into the expanse of space. Resting in the equipoise of nonthought is the fourth empowerment.
de las langs pa na rmi lam gyi 'dun pa drag tu sbyang / de nyid yang yang bskyar gyin bsgom/
Upon arising from that, train vigorously with the intentionality of dreaming. Meditate on that process again and again.

thun mtshams kyi spyod lam sngar dang 'dra/ mtshan mo nyal khar mdun gyi lhan skyes yab yum dbyings su yal ba de ka'i ngang der rnam rtog gzhan gyis bar ma chod par gnyid du 'gro bar bya/ bar skabs su gnyid sad na/ dmigs pa de yongs rdzogs tshar re bsgom thub na legs/ ma thub na rmi lam gyi 'dun pa re bya'o/ /

In between sessions, maintain conduct as before. When you lie down to sleep at night, the coemergent couple in front of you vanishes into space; fall asleep within that very state without interference from any other thought. If you wake up during the night, it is best if you can meditate once on the complete visualization, but if you cannot, then cultivate the intentionality of dreaming.

nam smad gnyid kyi lhag ma cung zad re yod pa'i skabs der gnyid sangs te/ lus gnad bcas/ sngar gyi dmigs pa de ka la 'dun pa drag po dang bcas nas bsgom/ de rjes dus gnad gsum po gang rung gcig gi dus su sleb pa dang / lus gnad gsum po gang rung zhig bcas te/ dmigs pa sngar gyi de ka rim can du bsgoms nas/ mthar thams cad yal ba'i ngang la rnam rtog gzhan gyis bar ma chod pa'i ngang nas gnyid du 'gro bar bya/ sngar nas dmigs pa gong ma rang zin thig le de bsgoms pa'i goms shugs che bar yod na/ lan gcig po de ka la zin 'ong / (47) goms shugs ha cang che ba med kyang zhag 'ga' rer lan 'ga' re bskyar na zin 'ong ngo / / dmigs skor nyi shu pa'o/ /

In the second half of the night, when there is a little time left for sleep, wake up and assume the physical posture and meditate with intense intentionality on that exact previous visualization. Afterward, when whichever of the three crucial times is upon you, and with whichever of the three crucial postures is appropriate, meditate on the sequence of the previous visualizations. In the end, when everything vanishes, go to sleep in that state without any other thoughts interfering. If you have strong familiarity with the meditation on the above visualizations of self-recognizing [dreams with the] drops from before, then you will recognize dreams on the first time. {47} Even without really strong familiarity, you will have lucid dreams after a few days and a few tries. This is the twentieth round of visualization.
Session 21
ii.
ii. Short Basic Visualization

yang na dmigs pa'i gzhi mdor bsdus pa la bslab ste/ bla ma'i rnal 'byor sngar bzhin bsgom/ rang gi snying gar bla ma sku dngos sam/ rdo rje 'chang dkar po/ de'i thugs kar hU~M yig dkar po 'od kyi rang bzhin can cig bsgom/ bla ma la mos gus dang rmi lam gyi 'dun pa gnyis ldan du bsgoms te yid kyis gsol ba btab/ hU~M las 'od 'phros snang ba thams cad khyab/ rmi lam yin snyam pa bya/ snang ba thams cad 'od du zhu nas rang la thim/ bum dbang ngo / / rang yi dam du gsal ba la rmi lam gyi dran 'dun bya/ / de 'od du zhu nas snying ga'i bla ma la thim/ gsang dbang ngo / / de la'ang rmi lam gyi dran 'dun bya/ bla ma 'od du zhu nas hU~M la thim/ sher dbang ngo / / de nas hU~M yang 'ja' ltar yal bar bsams la/ de ka'i ngang bskyang / dbang bzhi pa'o/ / de nas rmi lam gyi 'dun pa drag tu sbyangs/ yang de nyid bskyar gyin thun grangs dang thun chad med par bsgom pa yin te/ lag len de ltar bsgom dgos so/ /

Alternatively, learn this short basic visualization. Meditate on the guru yoga as before. Meditate on the guru in your heart, either in the form of your actual guru or white Vajradhara, with a white syllable hūṃ the nature of light in the heart. Meditating with both devotion in the guru and the intentionality of dreaming, mentally supplicate. Light radiates from the hūṃ and pervades all appearance. Think that it is a dream. All appearance melts into light and dissolves into you. That is the vase empowerment. Imagine yourself as the yidam and recall the intentionality of dreaming. That melts into light and dissolves into the guru at your heart. That is the secret empowerment. For that, also recall the intentionality of dreaming. The guru melts into light and dissolves into the hūṃ. That is the wisdom empowerment. Then think that the hūṃ also vanishes like a rainbow, and maintain that very experience. That is the fourth empowerment. Train vigorously in the intentionality of dreaming and meditate repeatedly on this visualization without regard for the number or duration of the sessions. That is how you must practice.

'jag bsam gnyis kar gyi khrid yig las/ phyi snod bcud rang la bsdu ba mi gsal ba dang / nyin mo'i dmigs pa la 'od gsal du bsdu ba yang mi gsal ba ni/ lag len cung zad sbas pa yin la/ mkhas grub gzhon nu grub ni/ 'od gsal bzung ba'i skabs kyi dmigs pa bzhin rim pas spro bar yang bzhed do/ /

In the guidebooks of Jak[chen Gyaltsen Bum] and Sam[ding Zhönu Drup],[21] the dissolution of the environment and its inhabitants into oneself is not clear. Nor is the dissolution into lucid clarity in the daytime visualization. Apparently the practical application is somewhat hidden, but the learned adept Zhönu Drup also maintains that the [light] gradually radiates, as in the visualization for recognizing lucid clarity.

de gnyis la rtog med la bzung ba ces tha snyad mdzad pa'i rgyu mtshan dngos su las la sbyor ba'i skabs/ dmigs pa bsdus nas gnyid du 'gro ba'i bar la/ rnam rtog gzhan gyis bar ma chod pa/ bsam med du gnas pa cig dgos pa'i (48) don yin no/ / dmigs skor nyer gcig pa'o/ /

These two visualizations are designated as nonconceptual recognition because during their actual application, from the time of the dissolution of the visualization until you fall asleep, no other discursive thoughts should intervene.
