That means that you must remain without contemplation. {48} This is the twenty-first round of visualization.
Session 22
gnyis pa rtog bcas lam khyer ni/
iii. Integration of Concepts

sngon 'gro sngar dang 'dra ba las/ rang gi mgrin pa'i rtsa 'dab bzhi/ pad+ma dmar po 'dab ma bzhi par gyur ba'i lte bar oM dmar po de'i 'od dmar pos mgrin pa'i phyogs thams cad khyab par bsgom/ rlung bum can nam 'jam rlung bzung ste/ nyin phyed yan la bdag cis kyang do nub rmi lam zin par bya/ rmi lam la rmi lam du ngo shes par bya/ zhes 'dun pa drag po btang / nyin phyed man chad lang gnyid du song 'dug / snang ba 'di rmi lam yin par 'dug snyam pa'i 'dun pa drag tu bya/ srod thun la da ni myur du rmi lam 'ong bas 'di nyid du ngo shes par byed dgos snyam pa'i 'dun pa gtong / de yang da lta'i sad dus kyi snang ba rags pa 'di nub gnyid 'thug po rang du ma song ba'i bar dir/ gnyid dang snang ba'i bar gyi rnam rtog ces bya ba/ rna bar sgra tsi rong ba'am/ lus sprid pa snyam dang / thib thib non pa'am/ smin mtshams su sbring sbring ba dang dbugs thum thum pa lta bu'i nyams gyi rjes su/ mi khyi la sogs pa'i 'gro ba dang / khang khyim dang / lam kha la sogs pa'i rnam pa srib tsam srib tsam 'ong ba/ 'og 'gyu las ni gsal/ rmi lam dngos las cung mi gsal ba'i snang cha srab srib tsam 'byung ba de la gnyid dang snang ba'i bar gyi rnam rtog zer ba yin/

First do the preliminary as before, except that the four-spoke chakra at the throat becomes a four-petaled red lotus. Meditate that the red oṃ at the center of the lotus generates red light that permeates all areas of the throat. Hold the vase breathing or the gentle breathing. Before midday, set a powerful intention: “No matter what, I will grasp my dreams tonight. I will recognize dreams as dream.” After midday, intensify intentionality by thinking, “I have fallen asleep. These appearances are dreams.” In the evening session, set the intention by thinking, “Now dreams will soon come. I must know them to be dreams.” Also, [the experience] between the current waking state of coarse appearances and before entering actual deep sleep is called conceptual thought between sleep and appearance. There are sensations such as sounds buzzing in the ears, or the body feeling numb and heavily pressed down, or tingling at the point between the eyebrows, and labored breathing. After that, vague impressions occur, such as the movement of humans and dogs, and the shapes of houses and roads, and such. The movement of the undercurrent is clear, but the actions of a real dream are still somewhat unclear, yielding only vague and indistinct forms. This is said to be the thoughts between sleep and [waking] appearances.

skabs 'dir de rmi lam du ngo shes par byed dgos snyam du 'dun pa drag tu sbyang / gnas skabs de gsum la 'dun pa bsgyur ba ma gtogs dmigs pa 'dra/ dus gnad gsum du lus gnad gsum bcas nas 'dzin tshul yang gong dang 'dra mod/ dmigs pa'i yul stong par bsdus nas 'jog pa de mi byed pas/ oM yig la sems gtod cing / / da lta (49) rang gnyid dang snang ba'i bar gyi rnam rtog yong ba 'di ngos 'dzin dgos snyam pa'i 'dun pa shugs ha kyang drag pa min tsam bsten pa'i sgo nas gnyid du 'gro bar bya/ der gnyid dang snang ba'i bar gyi rnam rtog byung na/ 'di ka rmi lam yin snyam pa'i 'dun pa bag tsam btang ste/ thur sel cung zad bskum gsung / 'on kyang bcas bcos mang na gnyid dengs 'gro bas 'dun pa bag tsam gyi ngang nas gnyid du 'gro bar bya/ gnyid dang snang ba'i bar gyi rnam rtog ngos 'dzin cing / de yang 'dun pa rtog bcas kyis 'dzin pas rtog bcas lam khyer ces bya'o/ /

In this situation, vigorously train your intention by thinking, “I must recognize that as dream.” On those three occasions, apart from changing the intentionality, the visualization is the same. While the way of grasping dreams during the three vital times with the three vital body postures is the same as above, here do not dissolve the visualization objects into emptiness and enter that state. {49} Instead, turn your attention to the oṃ syllable and think, “Now comes the thoughts between my falling asleep and appearances. I should identify this.” By means of relying on moderate intentionality, not too intense, let yourself fall asleep. There, when thoughts occur between sleep and appearance, apply just a slight intentionality in thinking it is a dream. It is taught to squeeze the downward expelling wind [at that time]. However, if there is too much contrivance your sleep will disperse, so go to sleep within the state of slight intentionality. You identify the conceptual thoughts that occur between sleep and appearance, and also identify them by means of conceptual intentionality, so it is called integration of concepts.
'di rmi lam mi zin pa mi srid pa'i gdams pa'o gsung /
This is said to be an instruction through which it is impossible not to recognize dreams.

'dir 'jag bsam gser gling pa gsum kar gyi khrid yig las/ mgrin pa'i oM gyi bshad pa zur tsam mdzad nas chams te bzhag / nyin bar gyi dmigs pa sngar gyi dmigs pa ka bsgom gsung rtog med gnyis la kha 'phangs tshul mdzad pa dang / 'jag chen gyis/ yang na dmigs pa gnyis kyi bogs 'don du/ de gnyis rang mi sgom par rmi lam gyi 'dun pa spyi ldog de sbyong bar gsungs pa rnams kyis man ngag zhal shes la ltos pa'i dbang du mdzad pa'o/ / dmigs skor nyer gnyis pa'o/ /

On this subject, the guidebooks of Jak, Sam, and Serlingpa[22] only mention the explanation of the oṃ at the throat as an aside and leave it at that. It is taught to meditate on the previous visualization as the daytime visualization, and to distribute the two nonconceptual visualizations. Alternatively, Jakchen says that in the enhancements of the two visualizations, one does not actually meditate on those two themselves but trains with the general intentionality of dreaming. These comments are made with reference to the understanding gained from oral esoteric instructions. This is the twenty-second round of visualization.
gnyis pa rmi lam sbyong ba ni/
2. Refining Dreams

rmi lam zin pa la brtan pa thob nas rmi lam sbyong ba dgos pa yin te/ de yang rmi lam 'dzin pa'i dmigs pa bor nas/ sbyong ba kho na la bsgril ba'i dbang du byas pa yin/ 'dzin pa'i dmigs pa ma dor bar bstar chags su bsgom kyin yod na/ nub re bzhin rmi lam lan re bzhin zin yong ba'i mtshams nas sbyong ba'i dmigs pa yang bsgoms te/ 'dzin sbyong phyogs gcig tu byas pas chog go / de la bzhi ste/ lus (50) kyis sems sbyang ba/ sems kyis lus sbyang ba/ bdag med mas sbyang ba/ 'dun pas sbyang ba'o/ /

You need to refine the dreams once you have attained stability in recognizing them. This is the time to set aside the visualization for identifying dreams and concentrate solely on refining them. But if you continue to meditate regularly on identifying dreams, you may meditate on the visualization for refining dreams at the point when you recognize a few dreams each night. It is acceptable to practice both recognizing and refining at the same time. {50} This has four parts: (1) Refining the Mind through the Body, (2) Refining the Body through the Mind, (3) Refining through Nairātmya, and (4) Refining through Intentionality.
Session 23
de la dang po ni/
a. Refining the Mind through the Body

bla ma'i rnal 'byor yan chad rmi lam bzung ba'i skabs dang 'dra ba las/ rmi lam 'byongs par mdzad du gsol zhes 'don pa bsgyur/ de nas dmigs pa dngos ni/ rang nyid gnas pa'i 'og na/ brag phyams lta bu g.yang sa shin tu che ba zhig 'dug par bsam/ rang nyid kyang g.yang sa de'i kha mtshams mda' gang tsam gyi steng gi nam mkha' la 'dug par bsam/ de nas mar bltas pas yang ting gis 'byung / de tsa na nga gnyid du song 'dug / snang ba 'di rmi lam gyi snang bar 'dug / rmi lam gyi snang ba la skrag rgyu ci yod snyam ste/ chad kyis lhungs su bcug / sa la tob ter ma lhungs tsam la/ de nyid du yal bar bsam pa'am/ yang na yar la ye re re 'phur nas 'ongs te/ g.yang gi khar sngar bzhin 'dug par mos/ tshul de lta bu yang yang sbyong / dmigs pa 'di la rang yi dam du gsal ba dang / tha mal gyi rnam pas sbyong ba gnyis kas rung bas nges med du bsgom/ yang g.yang sa'i rtser lus gcig bzhag nas/ de las 'od kyi thag pa dang 'brel ba'i lus gcig 'bab 'dzeg byed pa yang bshad de/ zhal khrid la 'di mi gsung / dmigs skor nyer gsum pa'o/ /

The practice is the same as in recognizing dreams up through guru yoga, except for a change in the intentionality [in the last line of the supplication] to “…and to refine dreams.” Then for the main visualization, imagine that there is a huge chasm, like a cliff precipice, below the place where you are standing. Then imagine that you yourself are at the edge of that chasm, suspended about an arrow’s length in the space above it. When you look down, you experience vertigo and become terrified. At that point, think, “I have fallen asleep. This appearance is a dream appearance. No reason to be afraid of that.” Let go and allow yourself to fall. Just before you hit the ground, imagine that it all disappears into suchness, or that you can fly back up to the top where you stood on the edge. In this manner, refine the dream again and again. In this visualization you can appear as the yidam or in your ordinary form; it makes no difference in the meditation. There is also an explanation where you can leave one body at the edge of the precipice with another body tied to it by a cord of light that falls and climbs back out. This was not taught in the oral guidance. This is the twenty-third round of visualization.
Session 24
gnyis pa sems kyis lus sbyong ba ni/
b. Refining the Body through the Mind

sngon 'gro gong dang 'dra/ rang yi dam gyi skur gsal ba'i sgo dgu ru hU~M yig sngon po 'od kyi rang bzhin chen po re dang / ba spu'i bu ga thams cad du hU~M sngon po 'od 'tsher ba phra mo dpag tu med pas go mtshams med par khyab/ hU~M thams cad mgo bo nang du lta ba'o/ / rmi lam gyi 'dun pa drag tu sbyang / hU~M thams cad las 'od zer sngon po dangs gsal 'od kyi thag pa btang ba bzhin du sngo (51) ta la la lus kyi nang du 'phros/ 'od rnams 'dus shing 'dus te gcig tu 'dres/ lus kyi phyi nas kyang g.yogs/ lha'i rnam pa 'dal te thams cad 'od kyi gong bu gcig tu song / yang rmi lam gyi 'dun pa drag tu sbyang / 'od kyi gong bu de mtha' nas rim gyis yal/ je phra je phra la khu tshur tsam/ mthe bong tsam/ sran chung tsam/ yungs 'bru tsam/ mthar de yang mi dmigs par sbyangs te/ sems rtog med la mnyam par bzhag / yang rnam rtog skyes na rmi lam gyi 'dun pa drag tu sbyang ngo / / dmigs skor nyer bzhi pa'o/ /

The preliminaries are the same as before. Imagine that there are large blue hūṃ syllables, the nature of light, in the nine orifices of your body as the yidam. In all of your pores there are infinite fine hūṃs of vivid blue light covering the entire body without gaps. The tops of all the hūṃs face inward. Train vigorously in the intentionality of lucid dreaming. Radiant clear blue light from all the hūṃs radiates out like ropes of light shooting into your body. {51} The light gathers in and blends together, covering even from the outside of the body. The deity’s shape is pervaded, and everything becomes a single globe of light. Again vigorously practice the intentionality of dreaming. That globe of light gradually vanishes from the edges, becoming smaller and smaller until it is the size of a fist, then a thumb, then a small pea, then a mustard seed, and finally is refined away altogether. Rest the mind in equipoise without thought. As conceptual thought arises, practice vigorously the intentionality of dreaming. This is the twenty-fourth round of visualization.
Session 25
gsum pa bdag med mas sbyong ba ni/
c. Refining through Nairātmya

gzhan sngar ltar las/ dngos gzhi ni/ rang 'khor lo sdom pa yab rkyang du gsal ba'i mdun du rdo rje bdag med ma/ sku mdog sngon mo gri gug thod khrag kha TAM 'dzin pa/ lang tsho dang bde ba rgyas pa zhig bsgom/ sku de che na mda' gang khru gang tsam/ chung na sor bzhi'am mthe bong tsam/ de dag gi bar gang bde yin/ de'i gsang bar oM a swA hA/ zhes bya ba'i sngags kyi yig 'bru gsal bar bsgom/ rmi lam gyi dran 'dun drag po'i ngang nas/ sngags de lan nyer gcig sogs ci rigs par bzlas pas/ de las 'od zer sngon po sngo tal gyis byung / rang he ru kar gsal ba'i sku la phog pas/ rang nyid lha sku sngar las kyang sngo zhing dangs pa/ gsal ba cig tu song / lus thams cad bde bas khyab par bsam/

This is the same as before, except that in the main practice you visualize yourself as Cakrasaṃvara. Vajra Nairātmya is before you, blue, holding a flaying knife, blood-filled skull cup, and khaṭvāṅga. Meditate that she is blooming with youth and bliss. Visualize her size as no larger than one arrow’s length, or one cubit, and no smaller than four finger-widths, or thumb size—whatever is comfortable within that range. Meditate that the syllables of the mantra oṃ a svāhā appear clearly at her genitals. Within a state of intense recollection of the intention of dreaming, repeat that mantra twenty-one times or however many is suitable. This instantly causes blue light rays to arise from it and strike your clear form as Heruka, intensifying its bluish radiance and vividness. Imagine that your whole body is filled with bliss. {52}

yang rmi lam gyi 'dun pa dang bcas nas/ bdag med ma'i sku la sems gtad pas/ bdag med ma de nyid 'od zer sngon po nyams bde ba dang ldan pa cig tu ltem gyis zhu/ rang nyid he ru ka'i skur gsal ba'i gsang ba'i sgo nas zhugs 'od des sku lus kyi nang thams cad khyab/ sngar las kyang sngo zhing dangs la gsal bar song / lus sems thams cad bde bas (52) gang bar mos/ de nyid je dangs le dangs la nam mkha' la 'dres shing thim par bsam/ der cung zad bzhag ste/

Again, with the intentionality of lucid dreaming, turn your attention to the form of Nairātmya. This makes Nairātmya herself overflow and melt with the blue light rays and the experience of bliss. The light enters through the opening of the secret place of your Heruka form and pervades the whole body inside. It becomes more clearly blue and radiant than before. Imagine your whole body-mind filled with bliss. Think that this becomes brighter and brighter until it mixes with space and dissolves. Rest there awhile.

yang rmi lam gyi 'dun pa drag tu sbyong ba sogs sngar bzhin/ dmigs pa 'di la mkhas grub rgyal mtshan 'bum ni rang gi dbang po'i rtse la hU~M bsgom gsung pa yod kyang / zhal khrid la de mi mdzad/ su kha'i 'dres shor ram gsung ngo / / dmigs skor nyer lnga pa'o/ /

Again practice with intense intentionality of dreaming and so on as before. Regarding this visualization, Khedrup Gyaltsen Bum said to meditate on a hūṃ at the tip of the organ, but this was not stated in the oral guidance. It was thought perhaps to be a mix-up from Sukhasiddhi’s [instructions]. This is the twenty-fifth round of visualization.
Session 26
bzhi pa 'dun pas sbyang ba ni/
d. Refining through Intentionality

bla ma'i rnal 'byor yan chad sngon 'gro sngar bzhin/ 'di la ni dmigs pa'i gzhi gcig tu nges pa med de/ 'dun pa kho nas rtsal nges med du sbyong bas na 'dun pas sbyong ba'o/ / de yang nga'i lus na tsha sdug bsngal skyed par byed pa de mal na yong bar 'dug / snang ba 'di rmi lam gyi snang ba yin/ lus 'di yang rmi lam gyi yid lus yin/ rmi lam gyi snang ba dang / yid kyi lus la ci sbyangs sbyangs su 'gro ba yin snyam pa'i 'dun pa drag po rgyun chags su byas nas/ rang gi mdun na 'dug pa'i ka ba gyang rtsig pa thog phubs sogs la yar thal mar thal phar thal tshur thal thogs med du sbyang /

The preliminaries up through guru yoga are the same as before. In this case, there is no definite basic visualization; it is called refining through intentionality because you practice with the dynamic energy of intentionality alone, without a specific visualization. “My body that creates sickness and suffering is actually in bed. These appearances are dream appearances. This body also is the mental body of dream. These dream appearances and the mental body can be refined in whatever way I choose.” Cultivate this intention continuously. Then if a pillar, wall, ceiling, or so forth appears before you, refine [the appearance] by passing through it without obstruction—up and down, back and forth.

gzhan yang dkar khung phra mo la 'dzul ba sogs dang / g.yang sa dang / chu dang / me dang / gcan gzan sogs la thog brdzis su byed pa dang / nam mkha' la 'phur ba dang / sa la 'dzul ba dang / chu'i steng nas 'chag pa sogs mdor na ci dran dran gyi tshul gyis sbyangs pas chog pa las/ khyad par du rnam rtog choms dka' ba'i rigs 'dzin chags kyi dngos po dang / 'jigs skrag dang / ang dang / ngo tsha dang / skyug bro skye ba'i rigs rnams la/ res 'ga' thug phrad du thog brdzis bya/ res 'ga' sgyu ma rmi lam gyi 'dun pas bza' gtad med par bya/ res 'ga' nyam nga med par zlog sgom bya/ res 'ga' (53) skad cig gcig la thogs med du bcom mo/ / dmigs skor nyer drug pa'o/ /

Additionally, practice such things as slipping through small windows; subjugating cliffs, water, fire, wild animals; and flying in the sky, entering the ground, walking on water, and so forth. In short, it is fine to practice with whatever comes to mind. But train especially with conceptual thoughts that are difficult to overcome, the type of things that you are attached to or the type that cause fear, anxiety, shame, and disgust. Sometimes shatter [those thoughts] upon contact, sometimes disregard them through the intentionality of dream and illusion, sometimes use fearless counteractive meditation, and sometimes readily vanquish them moment by moment. {53} This is the twenty-sixth round of visualization.

lus kyis sems sbyong ba rmi lam rtsal sbyong yin/ sems kyis lus sbyong ba 'od gsal dang bsre ba yin pas phrugs gcig tshang / bdag med mas sbyong ba 'od gsal dang bsre ba yin/ 'dun pas sbyong ba rtsal sbyong yin pas rmi lam sbyong tshul gnad phrugs gcig de la tshang bas/ gang zag gcig gis de gnyis gang rung re bsgom par bya'o/ /

Refining the Mind through the Body is refining dream’s dynamic energy. Refining the Body through the Mind is blending with lucid clarity, so [Dream and Lucid Clarity] are included in one practice. Refining through Nairātmya is blending with lucid clarity. Refining through Intentionality refines the dynamic energy, so the vital point of refinement of dreams is included in that practice. A single individual should meditate on whichever of those two [pairs] is appropriate.
gsum pa rmi lam spel ba
3. Increasing Dreams
['di] la/ thugs phrad du spel ba dang / gang 'dul du spel ba gnyis/
This has two parts: (1) Increasing Whatever Is Encountered and (2) Increasing for Whatever Is to Be Tamed.
dang po
a. Increasing Whatever Is Encountered
['di] la yang 'byung bzhi phra rags la spel ba dang / sems can phra rags la spel ba gnyis/
There are two parts to the first part: (1) Increasing Subtle and Coarse Four Elements and (2) Increasing Subtle and Coarse Sentient Beings.
Session 27
dang po ni/ /
i. Increasing Subtle and Coarse Four Elements

sngon 'gro sngar dang 'dra ba las/ rmi lam spel nus par byin gyis rlobs zhes mtha' bsgyur la gsol ba btab/ de nas dper mtshon na/ rang gi mdun du sa'i gong bu zhig mthong gin 'dug na/ nga gnyid du song 'dug / 'di rmi lam gyi sa yin par 'dug / ci spel ba der 'gro snyam nas/ gnyis su spel snyam tsa na gnyis su song / de bzhin du thog ma re zhig gsum nas bcu la sogs pa'i bar du spel/ yang rim pas bsdus pas rtsa ba'i gcig pur song / mthar rim pas bslabs shing sbyangs pas/ gang 'dod 'dod du spel yang nus rtsa ba'i sa gcig pu la bsdu bar yang nus pa 'byung ngo / /

The preliminaries are the same as before, except that the last line of the supplication is changed to “Bless me with the ability to increase dreams.” Then, for example, if you see a clump of earth in front of you, think, “I have fallen asleep and this is a dream. Whatever way I increase will work.” If you think of increasing it to two, it will become two. Likewise, in the beginning, alternate increasing from three to ten and so forth, then gradually gather them back into the original one. Ultimately, by training gradually and refining, you will gain the ability to increase [the dream object] to whatever you desire and gather it back into the original one.

de yang nyin par dmigs pa 'di yang yang bsgoms pas/ mtshan mo rmi lam zin/ spel ba'i dmigs pa 'di dran nas bsgoms kyang / kha cig la thog mar spel ba dang / bsdu ba mi 'byung ba yang yod te/ yang 'dun pa drag pos bsgoms nas/ zhag shas nas cung zad spel thub par 'ong / de nas rim pas je bzang du 'gro/ 'ga' zhig la (54) thog ma nyid nas spel nus pa'ang yong / 'dir ma zad sprul bsgyur la yang de dang 'dra/ dang po sa'i gong bu lta bu cig la goms par byas nas/ spro bsdu thub pa na/ de nas gzhan la'ang rim gyis bslab ste/ sa khams rags pa ri lta bu nas/ phra ba rde'u'am sa rdul gyi bar la bslab/ chu khams rags pa chu bo dang / mtsho la sogs pa nas phra ba chu thigs kyi bar la bslab/ me khams rags pa me dpung chen po nas phra ba me stag gi bar la bslab/ rlung khams rags pa rlung 'tshub chen po nas/ phra ba srog chags phra mo'i dbugs 'gyu ba tshun chad la'ang bslab/ 'dir 'byung bzhi zhes pa bem tshos sems med thams cad la zer ba yin te/ phyi snod kyis bsdus pa thams cad la sbyong ba yin/ dmigs skor nyer bdun pa'o/ /

By your meditating on this visualization again and again during the daytime, you will recognize dreams at night. Then recall this visualization for increasing and meditate on it [during the dream]. Despite this, there are some who cannot increase and gather back right away. In that case, meditate again with intense intentionality and after a few days, some capacity for increasing will develop and gradually will get better. {54} Some practitioners can increase dreams right from the start. Not only that, they are able to achieve emanating and changing dreams. Once you get used to practicing with something like a clump of earth and are able to expand and contract it, train successively in other objects. Train in coarse forms of the earth element, such as a mountain, down to a subtle one, such as a pebble or dust mote. Train in coarse forms of the water element, such as a river or lake, down to subtle forms, such as a drop of water. Train in coarse forms of the fire element, such as a huge conflagration, down to subtle forms, such as a spark. Train in coarse forms of the wind element, such as a big tornado, down to subtle forms, such as the breathing of a tiny creature. Here, “four elements” refers to all material phenomena that are without sentience. It means to train with everything included in the external environment. This is the twenty-seventh round of visualization.
Session 28
gnyis pa sems can phra rags la sbyang ba ste/
ii. Increasing Subtle and Coarse Sentient Beings

sngon 'gro gong dang 'dra/ rang gi mdun du zug phrang du mi lta bu zhig mthong na/ nga gnyid du song 'dug / 'di rmi lam gyi snang ba'i mir 'dug / ci spel spel yin snyam pa dang / gcig gnyis gsum nas bcu'i bar du spel zhing / gong bzhin bsdu ba sogs bya/ des mtshon pa'i rta glang sogs sems can dngos su mthong ba thams cad la bslab ste/ rags pa rta glang la sogs pa nas phra ba 'bu srin phra mo'i bar la bslab bo/ / dmigs skor nyer brgyad pa'o/ /

Preliminaries are the same as before. If you encounter a human or other being in front of you, think, “I have fallen asleep and this is a person appearing in my dream. I can increase them in any way.” Increase that appearance from two or three up to ten, then gather it back and so forth as before. As this exemplifies, train with all sentient beings, such as horses and cows, that you actually see. Train with the large beings, such as horses and cows, down to very subtle ones, such as tiny insects. This is the twenty-eighth round of visualization.
gnyis pa gang 'dul la bslab pa
b. Increasing for Whatever Is to Be Tamed
['di] la/ 'jig rten pa'i gang 'dul dang / 'jig rten las 'das pa'i gang 'dul gnyis/
This has two parts: (1) Taming with Mundane Beings and (2) Taming with Transcendent Beings.
Session 29
dang po 'jig rten pa'i gang 'dul du spel ba ni/
i. Taming with Mundane Beings

gtso bor srog chags kyi gzugs la sbyong ba yin/ me chu sogs sems med la yang sbyong ni sbyong ba yin te me'i gnyen por chu spel sprul byed pa lta bu'o/ (55) dper na/ mdun du byi ba lta bu cig mthong na/ 'di rmi lam gyi byi ba yin/ 'di la 'dul byed cig spel dgos snyam pa byas te/ der byi la cig byung / des byi ba de btul bar bsam/ de nas ci spel spel yin snyam pas/ byi la mang por spel nas 'dul ba'i dmigs pa byed pa'o/ / de bzhin du bye'u la khra lta bu dang / khyi la spyang ku/ gcan gzan gzhan la stag dang / stag la seng ge dang / seng ge la me dpung / me la chu/ mi la srin po sogs la yang sbyar bar bya'o/ / dmigs skor nyer dgu pa'o/ /

The first, increasing whatever mundane beings are to be tamed, mainly concerns training with the forms of living beings. Training with nonsentient fire, water, and so forth is also a training, such as when one practices the increase of water as an antidote to fire. {55} Suppose you see something like a mouse before you. Think, “This is a dream mouse. I must increase something to tame it.” Then a cat shows up, and you think that it can tame the mouse. Then, thinking that whatever you try to increase will increase, multiply the cat many times and do the visualization of taming. Similarly apply this by increasing hawks for small birds, wolves for dogs, tigers for other animals, lions for tigers, fire for lions, water for fire, cannibal demons for humans, and so forth. This is the twenty-ninth round of visualization.
Session 30
gnyis pa 'jig rten las 'das pa'i gang 'dul du spel ba ni/
ii. Taming with Transcendent Beings

rang ngam gzhan la gdon gyi gnod byed yod na/ rang gi mdun du khro bo'i rgyal po gcig byung nas/ des gnod byed kyi gdon de zhags pas 'ching ba dang / zhabs kyis gnon pa dang / mtshon chas gtub pa dang / me ris sreg pa dang / sngags kyi sgra drag po bsgrags pas skrag nas dran med du brgyal bar byed pa sogs thabs sna tshogs kyis slar ldangs thes med par bcom par bsam/ yang khro bo de lta bu mang por spel bas kyang 'dul bar bsam/ de la ye shes khro bo gang gis kyang / gdon rigs thams cad 'dul bar nus mod te/ gtso che ba'i gang 'dul gyi dbang du byas na/ rgyal po dang btsan 'dul ba la rta mgrin/ steng gdon la phyag na rdo rje/ sa bdag klu gnyan spyi la bya khyung / klu srin la 'jam dpal nA ga rak+Sha/ bdud kyi bar chad la mi g.yo ba/ rbod gtong la gtsug tor 'khor los sgyur ba/ gdon spyi la 'jam dpal rdo rje 'jigs byed bsngags zhes gsung ngo / / dmigs skor sum cu pa'o/ /

For increasing transcendent beings, when there is a spirit harmful to you or to others, imagine that the king of wrathful deities appears before you and binds that harmful spirit with lassos, tramples it underfoot, slashes it with weapons, burns it with fire, and terrifies it into an unconscious faint with the roar of wrathful mantra. Imagine that these and various other vanquishing methods render it unable to rise back up. Again, increase the number of such wrathful deities and imagine taming the spirit. Although any wrathful wisdom deity is certainly capable of taming all kinds of bad spirits, it is said that the following are most effective in terms of those to be tamed: Hayagrīva for taming gyalpo and tsen spirits, Vajrapāṇi for upper spirits, Garuḍa for ground masters and general malignant nāgas, Mañjuśrī Nāgarakṣā for cannibal nāgas, Acala for obstacles of devils, Uṣṇīṣa Cakravartin for curses, and Mañjuśrī-Vajrabhairava Mantra for bad spirits in general. This is the thirtieth round of visualization.
bzhi pa rmi lam sprul pa'i
4. Emanating in Dreams
gdams ngag la/ thug phrad du sprul pa dang / gang 'dul du (56) sprul pa gnyis/
There are two parts in this instruction: (1) Emanating Whatever Is Encountered and (2) Emanating for Whatever Is to Be Tamed. {56}
dang po thug phrad du sprul pa
a. Emanating Whatever Is Encountered
['di] la dbye na/ /'byung bzhi phra rags su sprul pa dang / sems can phra rags su sprul pa gnyis so/ /
This has two categories: (1) Emanating as the Subtle and Coarse Four Elements and (2) Emanating as Subtle and Coarse Sentient Beings.
Session 31
dang po ni/
i. Emanating as the Subtle and Coarse Four Elements

sngon 'gro'i skabs rmi lam sprul nus par byin gyis brlab tu gsol/ / ces mtha' bsgyur nas gzhan gong dang 'dra/ rang gi mdun du sa'i gong bu lta bu cig mthong na/ nga gnyid du song 'dug / sar snang ba 'di rmi lam gyi sar 'dug / nga rang yang 'di dang 'dra bar sa'i gong bur sprul dgos snyam 'dun pa btang zhing / de ma thag tu rang nyid sa'i gong bu de 'dra ba cig tu song / rmi lam rang yin snyam du cung zad bsgoms/ yang de 'phro bcad nas gzhan la mig gtad yengs su bcug ste/ rmi lam gyi 'dun pa drag po bya/ de lta bu yang yang bskyar zlos byed kyin bsgom mo/ /

During the preliminaries, change the last line of the supplication to “Please bless me with the ability to emanate in dreams.” All else is the same. Then, for example, if you see a clump of earth in front of you, think, “I have fallen asleep and this appearance of earth is dreamed earth. I also should emanate as a clump of earth like this.” With this intention, you instantly become a clump of earth just like that. Then meditate for a while thinking, “This is certainly a dream.” When that thought is interrupted and you become distracted by something else, cultivate intense intentionality for lucid dreaming. Meditate in this way, repeating it again and again.
des mtshon nas 'byung bzhi phra rags gzhan thams cad la yang sbyar te/ dmigs skor so gcig pa'o/ /
Apply the process exemplified here to all the other subtle and coarse elements. This is the thirty-first round of visualization.
Session 32
gnyis pa sems can phra rags su sprul pa
ii. Emanating as Subtle and Coarse Sentient Beings

yang snga ma rnams kyis rigs 'gre/ rang gi mdun du mi gcig mthong na/ e ma 'di rmi lam gyi mir 'dug / bdag kyang 'di lta bu gcig tu sprul dgos snyam pa bya/ de ma thag rang nyid kyang de 'dra bar song bar bsam/ rmi lam gyi 'dun pa dang bcas te cung zad sems bzung / yang 'phro bcad te rmi lam yin snyam pa byed/ de lta bu la bskor zlog bya'o/ / srog chags gzhan la sbyor tshul yang gong dang 'dra/ dmigs skor so gnyis pa'o/ /

This follows the process of the previous [visualizations on increasing]. If you see a person in front of you, think, “Oh! This is a dream person. I also should emanate as someone like this.” Imagine that you instantly become like that. With the intention of dreaming, hold the mind there for a bit. Again, when that thought is interrupted, think, “This is a dream,” and in that way go back and forth. The way to apply this to other living beings is the same as above. This is the thirty-second round of visualization.
gnyis pa gang 'dul du sprul pa
b. Emanating for Whatever Is to Be Tamed
['di] la/ 'jig rten pa dang 'jig rten las 'das pa gnyis yod/ /
This has two parts: (1) mundane and (2) transcendent.
Session 33
dang po ni/
i. Emanating as Mundane Beings

gzhan sngar dang 'dra ba las/ rang gi mdun du byi ba lta bu cig mthong na/ 'di rmi lam gyi byi bar 'dug / 'di 'dul dgos de la bdag byi lar sprul bar bya snyam pas/ rang nyid de ma thag (57) byi lar song / byi ba de lhag med du bcom par bsam/ des gzhan rnams la yang rigs 'gre/ dmigs skor so gsum pa'o/ /

This is the same as before except that when you see something like a mouse, you think, “This is a dream mouse. I must tame it by emanating as a cat.” {57} Immediately you become a cat. Imagine that you tame that mouse, leaving nothing behind. In that way, follow the process for the other examples. This is the thirty-third round of visualization.
Session 34
gnyis pa 'jig rten 'das pa'i gang 'dul ni/
ii. Emanating as Transcendent Beings

rang ngam gzhan gyi don du bdag nyid rtog dpyad yod pa'i 'dre gdon de mdun du 'dug par bsam/ 'di rmi lam gyi 'dre gdon yin/ 'dul dgos snyam du rang skad cig gis khro bo chen por gyur nas/ zhags pas 'ching ba dang / bcom brdeg byed pa sogs gong bzhin 'dul thabs byas pas lhag ma tsam yang med par brlag par byas/ rmi lam rang yin ang / dngos por grub pa ni cung zad kyang med snyam pa bya/ de ltar yang yang bskyar ro/ / gzhan gong spel ba'i skabs bzhin no/ / de la spel ba ni mdun du yod pa de spel ba yin/ sprul pa ni rang nyid sprul pa yin te/ de yang phal cher la spel ba ni cung zad bla zhing de las sprul pa cung zad dka' bas/ spel ba sngon dang / sprul pa rjes su bstan pa yin no/ / der ma zad 'jig rten 'das pa'i gang 'dul gyi skabs/ thog ma dmigs pa ma 'byongs ba'i dus na/ rmi lam rang du rang nyid sprul thub kyang pha rol po de mi thul ba la/ khro bo gcig mdun du byon nas btul na thul ba cig 'ong / de'i rgyu mtshan rang la mi tha mal dang gces 'dzin gyi bag chags yod pas/ rang pham dogs kyi nyam nga yod/ mdun gyi lha la de lta bu med pa'i rgyu mtshan gyis yin gsung / dmigs skor so bzhi pa'o/ /

For the sake of yourself or others, imagine that a demonic spirit that you have discovered is before you and think, “This is a dream demon. I must tame it.” Immediately you become a big wrathful deity and—using the same previous methods of binding and beating into submission—destroy it without remainder. Think, “Ah, this is actually a dream. There is not a bit of a truly existent thing.” Repeat this process again and again. The rest is the same as described above in the section on increasing dreams. “Increasing” means to increase whatever you find before you. “Emanating” means you yourself emanate. For the most part, increasing is a bit easier, while emanating is more difficult, so increasing is presented before emanating. Not only that, in the practice of emanating transcendent beings to tame whatever needs taming, before the visualization is mastered, you might be able to emanate yourself in a dream but unable to subdue the adversary. But if a wrathful deity arrives before you and tames it, subjugation can occur. It is said that the reason for that is the habitual pattern of clinging dearly to yourself as an ordinary human, which causes self-defeating despair. But when a deity stands before you, that is not the case. This is the thirty-fourth round of visualization.
lnga pa rmi lam bsgyur ba'i
5. Changing Dreams
gdams ngag la/ 'byung bzhi phra rags su bsgyur ba/ sems can phra rags su bsgyur ba/ lha sku sna tshogs su bsgyur ba/ snang stong zhen bral du bsgyur ba ste bzhi las/

This instruction has four parts: (1) Changing Subtle and Coarse Four Elements, (2) Changing Subtle and Coarse Sentient Beings, (3) Changing Various Deities’ Forms, and (4) Changing into Empty Appearance Free of Attachment.
Session 35
dang po ni/
a. Changing Subtle and Coarse Four Elements

rmi lam bsgyur nus par (58) byin gyis brlab tu gsol/ / ces mtha' bsgyur/ gzhan sngon 'gro la khyad med/ phyi ma gsum la'ang des rigs 'gre/ rang gi mdun du bum pa lta bu zhig 'dug na/ nga gnyid du song bar gda'/ bum par snang la 'di yang rmi lam du gda'/ rmi lam gyi bum pa la gang byas byas yin ci bsgyur bsgyur yin snyam pa'i 'dun pa shugs drag pos bum pa 'di me thab du bsgyur dgos snyam tsa na me thab tu song / de ka bar bsgyur snyam pa na ka bar song / de dag la sogs pa gang dran dran du ngo bo tshad dbyibs grangs kha dog nges med du bsgyur/ de ltar bum pa lta bu cig sna tshogs su bsgyur thub nas/ sa chu me rlung sa rdo ri brag rtsi shing nags tshal sogs nang phan tshun rnam pa sna tshogs su bsgyur tshul zad pa med pa la bslab bo/ / dmigs skor so lnga pa'o/ /

In the supplication, change the last line to “Bless me with the ability to change dreams.” {58} Other than that, there is no difference in the preliminaries. This is the same for the next three sessions. If there is something like a vase in front of you, think, “I have fallen asleep. This appearance of a vase is actually a dream. I can do whatever I want with a dream vase; if I try to change it, it will change.” With the force of this intentionality, when you think that you must change this vase into a stove, it will become a stove. When you think of changing it to a pillar, it becomes a pillar, and so forth. Whatever you recall, the change happens accordingly, whether of the object’s essence, size, shape, number, or color. In this way, when you are able to change something like a vase in various ways, train in the unending possibilities of changing inanimate objects—earth, water, fire, wind, rocks, mountains, cliffs, trees, forests, and so on—back and forth into various forms. This is the thirty-fifth round of visualization.
Session 36
gnyis pa sems can phra rags su bsgyur ba
b. Changing Subtle and Coarse Sentient Beings

yang des rigs 'gre/ rang gi mdun du mi lta bu zhig mthong na/ 'di rmi lam gyi mi yin/ ci bsgyur bsgyur yin/ gang bsams bsams yin snyam pas de rta ru bsgyur snyam tsa na rta ru song / de yang glang po cher bsgyur/ de yang ba lang rnga mong la sogs par bsgyur te/ de yang mi dang dud 'gro srog chags nang phan tshun rnam pa sna tshogs par bsgyur ro/ / 'byung bzhi dang sems can du bsgyur ba'i skabs 'di dag tu kha dog ma nges pa/ dbyibs ma nges pa/ tshad ma nges pa/ grangs ma nges pa sna tshogs par bsgyur ba'ang dgos so/ / dmigs skor so drug pa'o/ /

This follows the same process. If you find a person before you, think, “This is my dream person. However I change it, it will change. It will change however I wish.” If you think of changing it to a horse, it becomes a horse. Then change it to an elephant. Then again change it to an ox, a camel, and so on. Change living beings, such as humans and animals, back and forth into various forms. On these occasions of changing the four elements and sentient beings, you should change them into various indefinite colors, shapes, sizes, and numbers. This is the thirty-sixth round of visualization.
Session 37
gsum pa lha sku sna tshogs su bsgyur ba ni/
c. Changing Various Deities’ Forms

gzhan rnams sngar dang 'dra ba las/ bden med dang rmi lam gyi 'dun pa drag po'i ngang nas/ rang nyid bde mchog lhan skyes kyi sku gsal (39) par bsgom/ ga re nga gnyid du song 'dug / lha skur snang ba 'di yang rmi lam du 'dug / gang bsgyur ba der 'gro snyam pas/ rang nyid bde mchog de dgyes mdzad du sgyur dgos snyam pa na/ dgyes mdzad du song / de yang gsang 'dus su/ de ma hA mA ya ru/ de rdo rje 'jigs byed du bsgyur ba sogs yi dam lha'i ngo bo sna tshogs su bsgyur/ de bzhin du lha gcig kyang sku mdog ma nges pa sna tshogs su bsgyur te/ dkar po sngon po dang / de dmar por bsgyur ba la sogs pa dang / de bzhin du zhal phyag ma nges pa sna tshogs su bsgyur te/ zhal phyag mang po nyung ngur bsam pa dang / nyung ba mang por bsgyur ba dang / gdong brnyan sogs sna tshogs par bsgyur ba'o/ / dmigs skor so bdun pa'o/ /

This is the same as previously, except that while you are within the state of intense intentionality of dream and the lack of reality, you meditate on yourself as the clear form of Coemergent Cakrasaṃvara. {59} Think, “What? I have fallen asleep. This appearance as a deity’s form is a dream. I can change it to anything.” Thinking that you as Cakrasaṃvara should be changed to Hevajra, you become Hevajra. Then again change to Guhyasamāja, then to Mahāmāya, then to Vajrabhairava, and so forth—changing into the essence of various yidam deities. In a similar way, change a single deity’s color into various colors, such as white to blue, and that to red, and so forth. Also change the faces and arms to various indefinite forms, such as changing many faces and arms to few, few to many, or changing facial images and so forth to different ones, however you wish. This is the thirty-seventh round of visualization.
Session 38
bzhi pa snang stong zhen bral du bsgyur ba ni/
d. Changing into Empty Appearance Free of Attachment

lha sku sna tshogs su bsgyur ba sngon du btang / de yang rtsa ba'i lha sku rgya cher spel/ spel ba thams cad sna tshogs su bsgyur/ de thams cad la sgyu ma lta bu rmi lam lta bu'i 'dun pa drag tu sbyang / yang lha skur snang ba dang / snang mkhan gyi sems la cher re bltas pas/ sgyu ma sgyu 'dzin dang bral/ de ka'i ngang der gang yang mi dmigs pa'i 'od gsal phyag rgya chen po rang shugs su 'byung / yang de lta bu'i ngang nas rtsa ba'i lha skur skyed pa sogs gong bzhin yang yang sbyang / de ltar sbyangs pas mtshan mo rmi lam gyi dus su lha sku mang nyung ci rigs la de ltar bsgom pa 'byung / de nas je mang la 'gro/ mthar rmi lam du lha sku nam mkha' khengs pa gcig gis gcig ma bsgribs pa/ de thams cad kyang bde la zhen pa med pa/ gsal la rtog pa med pa/ snang la rang bzhin med pa ste/ mtshan nyid (60) gsum ldan du 'char/ de'i tshe rmi lam nying 'khrul rang dag gi dge sbyor klungs su phebs pa yin no/ /

Previously you changed into various deity forms. Then you increased the size of the primary deity, changed all those that you increased, and trained vigorously in the intentionality that they are all like illusions and dreams. Now, by your looking openly at the appearance of the deity’s form and the mind of the one to whom they appear, the illusion will be free of fixation on that deceit. Within that state, the lucid clarity of mahāmudrā without any frame of reference will arise on its own. Generate the principal deity’s form from within that state and train repeatedly as before. By your training like that, during nighttime dreaming the meditation on any appropriate number of deities will occur. Then they will multiply even more. Finally, the deities’ forms in your dream will fill all space yet without obscuring each other. All that will arise with three characteristics: bliss without attachment, clarity without concept, and appearance without intrinsic nature. {60} At that point, you have arrived at the natural state of the applied virtue of Dream, naturally purified double delusion.

de yang sgyu ma ces pa ni/ sad dus dang / rmi lam du bden med kyi 'dun pa sbyangs pa de'i shugs kyis/ a 'thas med par yul le/ mtho dman med par mnyam khad de shar ba de la zer/ sgyu mar 'dzin pa dang bral ba ces pa ni/ 'di kun 'khrul snang du shar ba tsam las gtad pa rang ci yod snyam pa'i blo cig yod pa de yang dbyings su yal te/ dgag sgrub kyi 'dzin pa dang bral ba de yin/ skabs der gang yang mi rtog bzhin du nyams myong gi ro bde bar shar ba de 'od gsal yin/ de ka la phyag rgya chen po zer te/ sems kyi gnas lugs yin pas so/ /

The term “illusion” means the arising of near equanimity without reification regarding high or low objects that is the result of training with intentionality in the lack of reality during waking and dreaming. “Free from fixating on illusion” indicates an attitude of “What do I care; all this is merely the arising of deluded appearance.” Then even that thought vanishes into the expanse, leaving you totally free of the fixations of denial or affirmation. That occasion, when you taste the experience of nonthought and bliss, is lucid clarity. It is also called mahāmudrā, as it is the abiding nature of the mind.

yang de ka'i ngang nas lha sku gsal stong rang shar du byung ba de la yang phyag rgya chen po zhes bya'o/ / bde la zhen pa med pa ni/ rmi lam du lha sku rang shar ba'i dus/ lus sems gnyis ka la bde nyams lam me shar yang nga rgyal rlom sems med cing / bde ba de la yang sred pa med pas/ bde ba byung ma byung la dga' mi dga' med pa cig 'ong / gsal la rtog pa med pa ni/ lha sku'i rnam pa shin tu gsal bar snang yang de rang shar yin te/ rnam rtog gi rtsol ba med pa'o/ / snang ba rang bzhin med pa ni/ snang yang bden pas stong zer ba'i spyi skad de yang 'dir 'jug pa tsam yin mod te/ 'on kyang 'dir ni lus ngag sems dang / gzugs sgra dri ro reg bya'i snang ba cig car shar ba de/ rig pa rang gsal gcig po'i ngor mnyam khad de shar ba ma gtogs/ snang ba so so rnams la dngos po tha dad gang yang med par nyams su myong ba'o/ / dmigs skor so brgyad pa'o/ /

When the clear, empty form of the deity arises spontaneously from within that state, it is also called mahāmudrā. “Bliss without attachment” concerns the time of the self-arising deity’s form: although a vivid experience of bliss arises in both body and mind, you have no pride or conceit. And since you do not crave that bliss, there is no pleasure or displeasure whether it arises or not. “Clarity without concept” means that even though the form of a deity’s body appears extremely clearly, it arises by itself without conceptual effort. As for “appearance without intrinsic nature,” they say, “Although [something] appears, it is empty of true reality.” This is very general, and naturally it does apply here. However, in this case the simultaneous arising of body, speech, and mind, as well as form, sound, smell, taste, and texture, arise in near equanimity to the perception of the single natural clarity of pure awareness. Apart from that, your felt experience is without any distinctions of entities whatsoever in those individual appearances. This is the thirty-eighth round of visualization. {61}

rmi lam gyi skabs 'di dag tu/ 'byams gcod kyi (61) man ngag kyang gal che ste/ 'byams gcod rgyas pa ni logs su bstan pa ltar yin pas khrid kyi dkyus la mi 'chad cing / 'byams gcod nyer mkho zhal shes mar grags pa ni gzhan du gsal lo/ /

During these practices of lucid dreaming, the esoteric instructions on severing diffusion are very important, but since they are extensively elucidated elsewhere, they are not explained in the course of this guidance. The instruction known as Direct Advice on the Required Severing of Diffusion is also found elsewhere.[23]
drug pa yul snang gtan la dbab pa
6. Ascertaining Objective Appearances
['di] la/ dbang po rab dmigs med gsal mkhyen/ / 'bring gang bsams gsal mthong / tha ma yid lus mkha' lding / dman pa dmigs pa'i yul snang ste bzhi yod pa las/

This has four parts: (1) Clearly Knowing without Visualizing for those of highest capability, (2) Clearly Seeing Whatever You Think for average capability, (3) the Garuḍa of the Mental Body for those of lesser capability, and (4) Ascertaining Objective Appearances for those of least capability.
Session 39
dang po dmigs med gsal mkhyen ni/
a. Clearly Knowing without Visualizing
sbyor ba'i skabs su 'bad rtsol med kyang / lkog gyur gyi don thams cad nyin mo sad dus dang / mtshan mo rmi lam kyi skabs thams cad du mthong ba'o/ /
Even without effort in application, you see the hidden meaning of everything during all situations of waking life in the daytime and dreaming at night.
'bring gang bsams gsal mthong ni/
b. Clearly Seeing Whatever You Think
nyin mo 'dun pa gang gtad pa de thams cad mtshan mo rtsol med rang shar du mthong ba'o/ /
Whatever you focus on with intentionality in the daytime is seen arising at nighttime without any effort.
tha ma yid lus mkha' lding ni/
c. The Garuḍa of the Mental Body

sngon 'gro gzhan 'dra ba la/ yul snang gtan la phebs par mdzad du gsol/ / zhes mtha' bsgyur nas gsol ba btab/ dmigs pa dngos ni/ bdag do nub sangs rgyas kyi zhing 'di lta bu lta ba'am/ lkog gyur 'di lta bu blta bar bya/ zhes 'dun pa drag tu btang / da nas rmi lam dngos yin snyam pas rang nyid yi dam gyi skur gsal ba de nyid dam/ lus kyi rnam pa gzhan du sprul kyang rung ste/ nam mkha' la yer gyis 'phur bas gnas der phyin cing dgos don rnams mthong bar bsams pas/ mtshan mo rmi lam du'ang de ltar 'byung ba'o/ / 'dir yid lus mkha' lding ces pa'i mkha' lding ni/ nam mkha' la 'phur 'gro ba'i don tsam ka yin na'ang / la la mkha' lding bya khyung lta bur sprul nas 'gro ba'i don du 'chad pa'ang yod do/ / dmigs skor so dgu pa'o/ /

The preliminaries are the same as before, except for changing the last line of the supplication to “May I ascertain objective appearances.” For the actual visualization, cultivate an intense intentionality, thinking, “Tonight I will see such-and-such pure land of the Buddha” or “I will see such-and-such hidden thing.” Then, thinking that it is actually a dream, imagine yourself as the yidam deity or some other appropriate physical form that you emanate. Imagine that you fly up into the sky and arrive there to see that place that you intended. In this way, the same will occur during the nighttime dreams. Here “garuḍa of the mental body” refers only to the ability to fly. However, some people also explain it to mean that you emanate as something like a garuḍa that can fly and go to those places. This is the thirty-ninth round of visualization. {62}
bzhi pa dman (62) pa dmigs pa'i yul snang gi
d. Ascertaining Objective Appearances
gdams ngag la gsum ste/ bdag med ma yul snang gsal byed/ a yul snang gsal byed/ thig le'i yul snang gsal byed do/

There are three esoteric instructions in this final section: (1) Illuminating Objective Appearances with Nairātmya, (2) Illuminating Objective Appearances with Vital Drops, and (3) Illuminating Objective Appearances with A.[24]
Session 40
dang po ni/
i. Illuminating Objective Appearances with Nairātmya

sngon 'gro snga ma dang 'dra/ rang gi lte ba'i 'og tu 'od kyi rang bzhin gyi thod pa phyi dkar la nang dmar ba/ de'i nang du oM a swA hA/ kha dog sngon po 'od zer sna tshogs 'phro ba'o/ / de las 'od zer 'phros/ chos 'byung dang rang lus gang / ba spu'i bu ga nas 'phros/ phyi snod kyi 'jig rten gzhal yas khang / nang bcud kyi sems can yi dam du bsam/ 'od zer gyi rtse mo las mchod pa dpag tu med pa sprul/ gdod nas bzhugs pa dang gsar du song ba'i yi dam lha tshogs thams cad mchod par bsam/ gzugs su snang tshad lha sku/ sgra grags tshad sngags/ dran rigs thams cad sgyu ma rmi lam du dran par bya/ yang 'od zer tshur 'dus te/ lte ba'i sngags kyi yig 'bru la thim/ de nyid rje btsun rdo rje bdag med ma'i skur gyur/ sngags kyi sgra di ri ri 'dug / mchod pa phul/ yul snang gtan la phebs par mdzad du gsol/ / ces gsol ba btab/

The preliminaries are the same as before. Imagine a skull cup made of light below your navel, white on the outside and red on the inside. The blue syllables oṃ a svāhā inside it radiate with multicolored light rays. The light rays fill the source of phenomena and your body, and radiate out through the pores. Imagine that the external environment of the world is a divine palace and that the inner inhabitants, the sentient beings, are yidams. Imagine infinite offerings emanating from the tips of the light rays presented to all the hosts of yidam deities that were there all along and those that are new. Remember that the extent of all physical form is divine form, all sound is mantra, and all memory and awareness are illusion and dream. Again the light rays reabsorb and dissolve into the mantra syllables at your navel. That turns into the form of Exalted Vajra Nairātmya vibrating with the sound of the mantra. Present offerings and supplicate with, “May I ascertain objective appearances.”

nyin par gyi dmigs pa zhal khrid nges can 'di yin/ gzhan 'jag lugs la sngags las 'od zer lan dang po spros pas/ bdag med mas dbu byas pa'i yi dam sna tshogs byung / gnyis pa spros pas mchod pa 'bul/ snga ma sna bug g.yas dang / rting ma g.yon nas spro/ bsam sdings pa/ lte bar thod pa'i nang du bdag med ma/ de'i lte bar thod pa'i nang du sngags bsgom/ 'od zer spro thengs gcig ka yin te/ sna bug g.yas nas byed/ lugs gnyis kar la 'od zer tshur bsdu ba med do/ / 'od zer sngags la bsdus te (63) lhar skyed pa 'di/ gser gling pa'i khrid yig la snang ngo / /

This is the definitive oral guide for the daytime visualization. Elsewhere, in the Jak system, when the light rays emanate from the mantra the first time, various yidams appear with Nairātmya in the lead. Then a second emanation [of light rays] presents the offerings. The former radiates from the right nostril and the latter from the left nostril. In the Samdingpa system, you meditate on the mantra inside a skull cup at Nairātmya’s navel inside the source of phenomena at your navel. The light emanates just once, radiating from the right nostril. In both of these systems, there is no reabsorption of the light rays. This description of light rays reabsorbing into the mantra and the generation of the deity appears in Serlingpa’s guidebook. {63}

mtshan mo nyal kha'i dmigs pa ni/ sngar gyi dmigs pa de tshar gcig bsgoms pa'i rjes la/ mchod pa bzhi rdzogs su phul/ yi dam gyi lha khyed kyis do nub kyi gnas skabs su bdag gis/ sangs rgyas kyi zhing dpag tu med pa mthong ba dang / mchod pa rgya chen po 'grub par mdzad du gsol/ / ces pa dang / 'dod don dmigs bsal phra mo yod na/ de dang de mthong bar mdzad du gsol/ / ces kyang bya/

The visualization for going to sleep at night is first to do the previous visualization one time, and after that, present the complete four offerings. Then supplicate with “Yidam Nairātmya, during the night tonight, please allow me to see infinite buddha realms and make vast offerings.” If you have some particular minor desire in mind, then request that with “Please allow me to see such-and-such place.”

de nas bdag med ma zhal tshur bstan te/ thugs ka'i thad ka shin tu dangs pa la gang lta bar 'dod pa'i yul de me long la gzugs brnyan shar ba ltar khra sal le mthong bar bsam/ des rmi lam gyi dus su yul snang gtan la phabs so/ / thod pa'i tshab tu chos 'byung bsgom kyang rung gsung ngo / / dmigs skor bzhi bcu pa'o/ /

Then Nairātmya turns to face you. Imagine that the area of her heart becomes extremely bright and there you see the desired place appearing vividly like an image in a mirror. That will ascertain the objective appearances at the time of dreaming. It is taught that you may meditate on a source of phenomena in place of the skull cup. This is the fortieth round of visualization.
Session 41
gnyis pa thig le yul snang gsal byed ni/
ii. Illuminating Objective Appearances with Vital Drops

sngon 'gro sngar ltar la/ rang lhar gsal ba'i lus kyi dbus su/ rtsa dbu ma kha dog dkar po dwangs gsal 'od kyi rang bzhin sbom phra sba lcag tsam pa/ yas snar haM dkar po mgo bo thur bstan/ mas snar hU~M dmar sngo mgo gyen bstan/ lte bar a thung dmar po yang gyen bstan no/ /

Do the preliminaries as before. Visualize yourself as the deity with the central channel in the center of the body. It is white and radiant, the nature of light, with the thickness of a bamboo cane. At the upper end, white haṃ faces head-down, and at the lower end, purple hūṃ stands right side up. At the navel, red short A (a-chung) also faces up.

rlung ro bsal steng rlung rngubs pas haM las thig le dkar po sran rdog tsam chad nas snying gar sleb/ 'og rlung bskum pas hU~M las thig le dmar sngo sran 'bru tsam yang chad/ lto ba zhom slog gis byas pas/ a las thig le shin tu dmar ba sran ma phyed tsam pa zhig yar chad/ de gnyis kyang snying gar sleb/ thig le gsum po gcig tu 'dres/ dkar la dmar ba yid tsam sngo ba'i mdangs chags pa (64) gcig tu song / de 'od mer re 'dug pa la cung zad sems gtad/ yul snang blta bar bya snyam pa'i 'dun pa dang lhan cig rlung phyir bsal bas snying ga'i thig le las 'od zer dkar dmar thag pa'am sbrul 'dra rung zhig rgyangs te byung nas sna bug g.yon nas thon/ gang blta bar 'dod pa'i gnas der song / 'od des mun khung du sgron me bteg pa ltar yul de khra gsal gyis mthong ba'am/ yang na 'od zer de sbubs stong lta bur byas/ de'i nang nas bltas pas mthong bar bsgoms kyang rung gsung / dmigs pa 'di'i rlung gnad dang thig le dmar sngo de zhal shes yin/ dmigs skor zhe gcig pa'o/ /

Exhale the dead air and then inhale, causing a white drop the size of a round pea to separate out from the haṃ and ascend to the heart. Contract the lower vital wind, causing a pea-sized purple drop to break off from the top of hūṃ. Draw in the belly, causing an extremely red drop the size of half a pea to break off the top of A. Both of those also arrive at the heart. The three essence drops merge into a single white drop, slightly red with a tinge of blue. {64} Focus your attention briefly on its radiance. Think that you will see the appearance of the place. At the same time as that intentionality, clear out the breath. Through that, pinkish light emerges from the drop at the heart and stretches out like a rope or a snake, leaving through the left nostril. It goes to whatever place you wanted to see. That light illuminates like a torch placed in a dungeon and you see the place vividly. Alternatively, it is also taught that you can make the light rays into a hollow tube and when you look through it you see the place. In this visualization, the vital point of winds and the red-blue vital drop come from the oral instructions. This is the forty-first round of visualization.
Session 42
gsum pa a yig yul snang gsal byed ni/
iii. Illuminating Objective Appearances with A

sngon 'gro dang rtsa dbu ma sngar bzhin bsgom/ dbu ma'i nang lte bar a dkar po dwangs gsal 'od kyi rang bzhin can bsgom/ rmi lam gyi 'dun pa dang bcas bum can 'jam rlung cung zad bsgom/ de mtshams nas a las 'od zer dkar po'i thag pa rgyang ter spros/ rtsa dbu ma la thogs med du song sna bug nas thon te gang blta 'dod pa'i phyogs der song nas mun khung du sgron me bteg pa ltar khra gsal gyis mthong ba'am/ 'od kyi sbu gu nas lta ba gang rung bya'o/ / dmigs skor zhe gnyis pa'o/ /

Meditate on the preliminaries and the central channel as before. Within the central channel, meditate on a white A at the navel, radiant and clear—the nature of light. With the intentionality of lucid dreaming, meditate a bit on the vase breathing or gentle breathing. Transition to visualizing a string of white light rays stretching out from the A and emanating out through the central channel without obstruction, emerging from the nostrils and going to the area that you want to see. Then, like placing a torch in a dark dungeon, you can see clearly now. Or you can look through a tube of light, whichever you prefer. This is the forty-second round of visualization.

dman pa yul snang gi dmigs pa gsum po 'di/ gang zag gcig gis gsum ga bsgom dgos pa rang ma yin/ gang rung re res kyang chog pas don la snga phyi'i go rim med/ tshogs su 'chang pa'i skabs/ bshad pa'i go rim la/ khrid yig rnying pa gsum na thog mar bdag med ma/ de nas a yul snang gsal byed dang / de rjes thig le yul snang gsal byed bshad yod kyang / 'dir phyi ma gnyis go rim bsnor ma ni/ dmigs pa rgyas 'bring bsdus gsum gyi rim pa'i dbang du byas (65) pa'o/ /

Regarding these three visualizations for those of least capability, a single individual does not necessarily need to meditate on all three; it is fine to do whichever one is appropriate. The point is that there is no specific order of former or latter. When explaining it to a group, the sequence of explanation according to the three old guidebooks is first Nairātmya, then Illuminating Objective Appearances with A, and lastly Illuminating Objective Appearances with Vital Drops. However, here the last two have been reversed because they are presented according to the extent of the visualizations: extensive, intermediate, and brief. {65}

gsang 'dus rim lnga'i gdams ngag sogs su/ spel sprul bsgyur gsum/ sbyong ba'i nang tshan du byas kyang / chos 'dir sbyong ba las logs su byed pa mi 'gal te/ sbyong ba ces pa'i ngos 'dzin la mi 'dra ba'i khyad yod pa'i rgyu mtshan gyis yin no/ / de yang gzhan de dag tu ni/ rmi lam gyi rtsal sbyong thams cad la sbyong ba zer bar 'dug / 'dir ni rmi lam zin pa'i rjes su sna tshogs su bsgyur ba'i rtsal ma skyes pa skyed par byed pa'i thabs kyi nang sel gcig la sbyong ba dang / de nyid gong nas gong du spel ba la/ 'byongs nas spel sprul bsgyur gsum byed ces pa'o/ / yul snang lta ba ni/ rmi lam gyi rnam thar du grags pa/ yon tan skyes pa'i rtags ston pa tsam yin no/ / yang man ngag gzhan las bzung ba sbyong ba gcig tu byed pa ces 'byung ba'i phyi ma ni/ rmi lam 'od gsal sogs su bsre ba la zer/ 'dir sems kyis lus sbyang ba dang / bdag med mas sbyang ba dang / bsgyur ba phyi ma gnyis la sogs pa'o/ /

In the instructions on The Five Stages of the Secret Assembly[25] and other sources, refining, emanating, and changing are classified as subcategories of refining dreams. In this teaching they are placed separately from refining, but this is not a contradiction because refining can be identified in a number of specific ways. In those other [sources], all [methods] of refining the dynamic energy of dreams are simply called refinement. Here, after recognizing that you are dreaming, the particular method to develop the dynamic energy of changing the dream in various ways that has not yet developed is refining. To increase that more and more, the three [methods of] increasing, emanating, and changing are done following refinement. Viewing the appearance of places is known as total freedom in dreaming, but it is merely a sign that qualities have developed. Also, one finds other esoteric instructions combining dream recognition and refinement into one. The latter is called a blend, such as [blending] Dream with Lucid Clarity, and so on. Here, it refers to such practices as Refining the Body through the Mind, Refining through Nairātmya, and the last two changing [practices of Changing Various Deities’ Forms and Changing into Empty Appearance Free of Attachment].

des na rmi lam gyi gdams ngag la/ dang por rmi lam la rmi lam du ma shes na/ chos tshan 'di'i dge sbyor gyi rtsa ba stongs pas/ thog mar rmi lam rmi tshad zin pa cig dgos/ don de la 'dzin pa'i gdams ngag ston/ de nas rtsal phyogs med du 'byongs pa cig dgos pa la/ rmi lam nyid kyi snang ba la dbang 'byor ba'i phyir/ sbyong ba snga phyi gnyis dang / spel ba dang / sprul ba dang / bsgyur ba dang po gnyis dang / yul snang rnams byung ba yin/ rmi lam de nyid du mchog gi dge sbyor dngos gzhi skyed pa la/ rmi lam 'od gsal du 'jug pa dang / rmi lam lha sku rang shar du 'jug pa gnyis yod pa las/ dang po ni sbyang ba bar pa gnyis yin/ phyi ma ni lha sku (66) sna tshogs dang snang stong zhen bral du bsgyur ba'o/ /

In the instructions for Dream, if you do not first recognize that you are dreaming, then the very basic applied virtue of this dharma teaching is missing. So right from the start you need a grasp of dreams as dreams. For that reason, the instructions on recognition are presented [first]. Then you need to refine the dynamic energy in every way. In order to gain control over the appearances of dreams, there are the former and latter refining practices, increasing, emanating, the first two changing practices, and the appearance of places. To develop the main practice of supreme applied virtue in Dream itself, there are two practices: involving dreams in lucid clarity and involving dreams in the self-arising of the deity’s form. For the first, there are the two middle visualizations of refining. For the latter, the last two changing practices: changing into various deities’ forms and changing into empty appearance free of attachment. {66}

de ltar shes na mkhas rlom kha cig ni gu'i chos drug rmi lam gyi gdams ngag mang yang gnad chung zer ba'i bab col gyi smra ba de dag 'brel med byung rgyal gyi tshig tu go bar 'gyur ro/ / chos drug 'di'i dbu zhabs kyi gdams ngag thams cad las dang po pa nyid la mchog tu phan pa 'phral du rtags thon thon pa kho na yin gyi/ las dang po pa la phan pa ci yang med pa'i bshad pa mtho mtho mo la gdams ngag tu rlom pa de 'dra gtan ma yin cing / yang blun po rang bzo'i chos gzhung la brten pha'i legs bshad kyang med/ man ngag la brten pa'i lag len yang med pa'i 'ad 'ud shab shob rnams dang ni ye mi 'dra bar yang nges shes 'drongs so/ /

Understood in this way, the mindless words of certain arrogant scholars who say, “There are many instructions in Niguma’s Six Dharma Dream practice but they are of little import” should be known as totally irrelevant nonsense. Everything in these Six Dharmas, from top to bottom, is of supreme benefit to beginners and triggers the immediate arising of signs of success. It is never like those “high” instructions explained by braggarts that have no benefit for beginners whatsoever. The self-made dharma of those fools is certainly not the excellent explanations based on scriptural dharma. Nor does this bloated deceit remotely resemble the practical teachings based on esoteric instructions. Of this I am sure.
bzhi pa 'od gsal gti mug rang sangs kyi
D. Lucid Clarity, Naturally Clarified Stupidity
khrid la/ sngon 'gro/ dngos gzhi/ rjes kyi khrid gsum bdog /
There are three parts to this guidance: (1) preliminaries, (2) main practice, and (3) concluding practices.
dang po
1. Preliminaries
['di] la/ rtsa ba mi rtag skyo shas/ yal ga spyod lam dam rdzas/ lo 'dab thabs lam rang mdangs/ gsol 'debs me tog 'char byed te bzhi las/

This has four parts: (1) the roots are impermanence and disillusionment, (2) the branches are conduct and pledge substances, (3) the leaves are the innate radiance of the path of methods, and (4) the flowers that grow from supplications.
dang po rtsa ba mi rtag skyo shas ni/
a. The Roots: Impermanence and Disillusionment

nges par 'chi ba dang / nam 'chi cha med pa dang / 'gro drug khams gsum 'khor ba thams cad sdug bsngal du shes pas cis kyang dgos med kyi blo drag tu bsgom/ snga nas mi rtag pa'i khrid ma bskyangs na smos ci dgos/ bskyangs pa tsho yang skabs 'dir mi rtag pa'i khrid bskyar nas bsgom dgos/ spyir chos kyi bskul ma 'chi ba mi rtag skyo shas shas cher bsgoms pas shes pa dangs shing grung ba cig 'byung / des shugs brtas te gnyid kyi dus na'ang / rig pa dwangs ba cig 'byung / des kyang 'od gsal zin bla/ yang skyo shas can de rig pa la lcag chug gzeg thon pas gnyid 'thug po'i skabs kyang dran (67) pa 'byung sla ste/ dper na/ nyin mo rig pa la sgrin chug pa'i dogs pa yod na mtshan mo gnyid chung bar 'gro bas mtshon no/ / de ltar na/ ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro mas kyang / 'chi ba rgyud skyes 'od gsal 'char/ ces gsung /

Meditate intensely with the attitude of needing nothing, which comes from the knowledge that you will definitely die, that the time of death is uncertain, and that everything in the cycle of the three realms and six migrations is suffering. To say nothing of those who have not upheld the guidance on impermanence before, even those who have maintained it need to meditate on it again on this occasion. In general, the inspiration for dharma practice is mainly meditation on death, impermanence, and disillusionment because this makes for a lucid and intelligent consciousness. This momentum strengthens, such that lucid awareness occurs even during dreams, facilitating the recognition of lucid clarity. Also, for those who are disillusioned, it acts as a whip to inspire their awareness so that even during deep sleep it is easy to recall. {67} For instance, if someone is hypervigilant during the daytime, they won’t sleep much at night. Similarly, the Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness said: As mortality arises in the mind stream, lucid clarity dawns.
gnyis pa yal ga spyod lam dam rdzas la/
b. The Branches: Conduct and Pledge Substances

spyod lam ni/ ji skad du/ spyod lam dal la kha zas snum/ / rdul thon las rnams spang bar bya/ / ces 'byung ba ltar/ nad pa'i spyod lam bzhin du bya ba byed dgos rnams dal bus byed/ kha zas snum pa ste/ lus la 'phrod pa mang nyung ran par bsten/ mchong rgyug dang rtsal 'gran dang 'dzing kha dang gzhu 'gengs sogs rtsa rlung 'khrugs par 'gyur ba dang rdul thon pa'i spyod lam spang gsung / dam rdzas ni spyir tshogs dang gtor ma bzang du bshams te 'bul/ mkha' 'gro sde lnga la gtor ma phul/ myur mdzad ye shes kyi mgon po la yang gtor ma phul nas gsol ba 'debs/ gtor ma 'bul ba'i skabs/ gu gul dang / ma hA maM sa'i bdug spos gtong zhes gsung /

As for conduct, it is said: Be leisurely in conduct and eat greasy food. Give up activity that makes you sweat. Move very slowly like an invalid. Eat greasy food (i.e., heavy and nutritious) that is neither too much nor too little according to your physical constitution. It is advised to avoid activities that disturb the channels and winds and make you sweat, such as jumping, running, competitive sports, wrestling, and archery. Regarding pledge substances, in general you should arrange communal feasts and tormas for offering. Offer torma to the five classes of ḍākinīs. Also offer torma to the Swift-Acting Awareness Protector [Mahākāla] and make supplications. When offering torma, it is recommended to also offer incense of frankincense and mahāmāṃsa.
gsum pa lo 'dab thabs lam rang mdangs ni/
c. The Leaves: Innate Radiance of the Path of Methods

sngar gtum mo'i rnal 'byor la goms pa yin na/ rgyun gyi rnal 'byor la bsgoms pa de kas go chod pa yin pas logs pa mi dgos/ de man 'jam rlung bum pa can zla re tsam sbyong ba sngon du 'gro bar byed/ 'od gsal dngos gzhi'i dmigs pa bsgom skabs kyang snga dro'am/ phyi dro gang 'thad re la ngal dub tu mi 'gyur ba tsam gyi rlung thun re bsgom par bya'o/ / rlung gi rnal 'byor gyis khams dangs snyigs phyed/ dangs ma'i mdangs las 'od gsal 'char ba yin pas/ rtsa rlung bsgom pa gnad du che/ spyir chos drug gi ya gyal 'od gsal ni/ (68) gnyid kyi 'od gsal gtso bor 'chad pa'i skabs yin pas/ gtum mo dang 'od gsal zhes so sor bgrangs pa yin gyi/ gzhan du na nyin mo'i 'od gsal skyed pa'i thabs kyi mchog cig gtum mo 'di yin/ ril 'dzin rjes gzhig sad sud dang / phra thig than thun gang las kyang 'di stobs che'o/ /

If you are already familiar with Fierce Inner Heat yoga, that meditation on a regular basis is sufficient and there is no need for anything else. If not, then first train with gentle breathing and vase breathing for one month each as a preliminary. During the visualizations of the main practice of Lucid Clarity, meditate on sessions of vital-wind practice either in the morning or in the evening to avoid becoming fatigued. The yoga of vital winds separates the elements of pure essence from the residue. Since lucid clarity arises from the radiance of pure essence, meditation on channels and winds is extremely important. {68} In general, of the Six Dharmas, Lucid Clarity is mainly explained in relation to the lucid clarity of sleep, and so Inner Heat and Lucid Clarity are counted separately. On the other hand, the most excellent method to generate daytime lucid clarity is Inner Heat. This is more powerful than any [visualizations of] dissolution, final dissolution, gradual dissolution, or some subtle vital-essence drops.
bzhi pa gsol 'debs me tog 'char byed ni/
d. The Flowers That Grow from Supplications

ji skad du/ 'od gsal 'char byed bla ma'i mos gus dang / zhes gsungs pa ltar 'od gsal 'char ba la bla ma'i mos gus gal che/ 'o na bla ma'i mos gus ni sgom thams cad la gal che yi/ 'od gsal kho na la gal che bar smos pa ci yin snyam na/ spyir bla ma'i mos gus kyi rten 'brel 'grig pa zhig kun la dgos kyang / nyin bar gyi dge sbyor rnams rang gi rtsol bas kyang bsgom du btub la/ rmi lam gyi gnas skabs na yang rmi lam nyid kyi snang ba sna tshogs dang / dran rtog gi blo rags pa 'di yod cing / de yod pas nyin mo'i bag chags rmi lam du khrid pa'i phyir/ rang gi rtsol ba dang 'dun pas sleb rgyu gcig kyang yod pa'i phyir byin rlabs kho na la ltos pa rang yang min/ gnyid 'thug po'i dus na dran rtsol med pa'i phyir/ gnyid kyi 'od gsal 'di ni/ skabs de nyid du rang shar du byung na ma gtogs/ gzhan bsgom thas med pa'i phyir/ lus la gnad du bsnun pa'i rten 'brel dang / bla ma dang lhag pa'i lha'i byin rlabs 'dzom pa la re ba yin no/ /

As is said, “Devotion to the guru causes lucid clarity to arise.” For lucid clarity to arise, guru devotion is very important. You may think, “But guru devotion is important in all meditation, why say that it is important only for Lucid Clarity?” In general, it’s true that guru devotion sets up the auspicious connections for all practice. However, virtuous applications in the daytime can be achieved by your own efforts in meditation. While dreaming, there are various appearances of the dream itself and the coarse mind of thoughts and memories. When those occur, your daytime habitual patterns can guide you in the dream. Therefore, your own efforts and intentions effect your dreams; you need not rely on blessings alone. At the time of deep sleep, however, since there is no effortful recollection, the lucid clarity of dream must arise by itself; there is no reason for another meditation. The hope is in the auspicious connections from applying the vital points of the body and the conjunction of blessings of the guru and special deities.

de ltar sngon 'gro bzhi po de la sngar ma bstan pa'i dmigs pa gsar pa rkang tshugs med pas/ dmigs skor logs su mi 'dren/ chos thun gcig la rdzogs pa'am/ gnyis sam gsum sogs gang ltar byas kyang 'dra'o/ (69)

Since these four preliminaries do not provide a basis for any new visualizations that were not presented before, they are not counted as separate cycles of visualization. They can be completed in one, two, three, or however many teaching sessions. {69}
gnyis pa dngos gzhi
2. Main Practice
['di] la/ 'od gsal bzung ba dang / lam khyer dang / bsre ba dang / mthar thug ste sa bcad bzhi'o/ /
There are four divisions in this Lucid Clarity: (1) recognizing, (2) integrating, (3) blending, and (4) ultimate lucid clarity.
dang po
a. Recognizing Lucid Clarity
['di] la/ bdag med ma la brten te 'od gsal 'dzin pa/ a yig la brten te 'od gsal 'dzin pa/ bla ma la brten te 'od gsal 'dzin pa ste gsum mo/ /
This has three parts: (1) Recognizing Lucid Clarity Based on Nairātmya, (2) Recognizing Lucid Clarity Based on the Letter A, and (3) Recognizing Lucid Clarity Based on the Guru.
Session 43
dang po ni/
i. Recognizing Lucid Clarity Based on Nairātmya

thun gyi sngon 'gro byings de sgyu lus kyi skabs su bshad pa dang 'dra ba las/ khyad par ni/ rtsa ba'i bla ma sku dngos su bsgom na yang / cha byad ral pa'i thor tshugs dang / rus pa'i rgyan drug dang / stag lpags kyi smad dkris sogs dur khrod kyi chas dang ldan pa cig bsgom/ ci ste rdo rje 'chang du sgom na yang / rdo rje 'chang he ru ka zhi ma khro spyan gsum pa/ sku la dur khrod chas brgyad rdzogs pa cig bsgom/ gsol 'debs kyi skabs su/ 'od gsal zin par mdzad du gsol/ / ces mtha' bsgyur ba'o/ /

The preliminaries for this session are mostly the same as in Illusory Body practice. The difference is that when you meditate on the guru’s actual form, it possesses the attributes and attire of the charnel ground, such as the hair being pulled up in a topknot, the six bone ornaments, the tiger-skin skirt, and so on. But if you meditate on the guru as Vajradhara, meditate on him as semi-wrathful Vajradhara Heruka with three eyes and all eight charnel-ground accessories. Change the last line of the supplication to “…and to recognize lucid clarity.”

de rjes su re zhig rang tha mal du gsal ba lta bu'i klad rgya'i steng thod pa'i 'og / spyi bo'i thad der pad+ma dang nyi ma'i gdan sran ma phyed bkas tsam/ de'i steng du gdan de ka dang 'tshams pa'i rdo rje bdag med ma sku mdog sngon mo gri gug thod pa kha T+waM ga bsnams pa/ zhabs g.yon brkyang pa'i gar stabs can sku chung la yan lag dod pa gsal btab/ de'i thugs kar yang a dkar po spu shad kyis bris pa ltar phra ba gsal la 'tsher ba cig bsgom/ de las 'od zer 'phros/ thog mar klad pa gti mug gi rang bzhin can de sbyangs/ de nas lus kyi nang gang bas sha khrag rus gsum yang dag ste/ lus 'od lus su gyur par bsam/ de yang yi dam gyi skur bsgoms na ka bzang gsung pas dpal sdom pa lhan skyes su ka bsgom/ der bdag med ma'i thugs ka'i a yig (70) la sems gtad de cung zad bsgom/ de nas a de las 'od zer 'phros/ bdag med ma'i sku gang / de las 'od zer 'phros/ rang lus kyi nang thams cad mun khung du sgron me bteg pa ltar khra gsal gyis song / yang rang gi ba spu'i khung bu nas phar 'phros/ snang ba thams cad khra gsal gyis gsal bar bsam/ tshul de kho nas yang thog mar thugs ka'i a la sems gtod pa dang / yang 'od zer spro ba sogs spel gyin bsgom pa las/ thugs ka'i a la sems gtod pa yun ring du bya/ de 'dra lan 'ga' re song ba'i mtshams su/ shes pa rang babs su lhod kyis klod nas gang gnas re bzhag /

After that, imagine for a moment your ordinary form. On the cranial membrane below the skull, right at the crown, there is a lotus-sun seat the size of a split pea. On top of that and proportional with it, imagine Vajra Nairātmya. She is blue, holding a flaying knife and khaṭvāṅga. Her left leg is help up in dancing pose. Visualize her tiny form with prominent limbs. Meditate on a fine, razor-thin white A in her heart, clear and shining. Light rays emanate from it. First the brain, the nature of stupidity, is purified. Then the whole body is filled inside and the flesh, blood, and bones are purified. Imagine that your body becomes a body of light. It is said to be even better to meditate on yourself in the yidam’s form, in which case, meditate on Coemergent Cakrasaṃvara. Focus your attention there on the letter A in Nairātmya’s heart and meditate for a bit. {70} Then light rays emanate from that A and fill Nairātmya’s form. Light rays radiate from her form and fill your whole body inside with brilliant light, like placing a lamp in a dark dungeon. Think that it shines forth from all your pores, turning all appearances into shining light. In this method alone, first focus on the A in Nairātmya’s heart and then meditate on the light rays radiating and spreading, but focus on the A in the heart for longer. After practicing in that way a few times, let consciousness fall in its own place and relax into relaxation, resting for as long as you abide.

de lta bu bskyar gyin rtag tu bsgom/ thog ma zhag mang por rtsol ba skyed de de ltar bsgoms pas/ skabs 'gar bde sal le ba rnam rtog med par rang shugs su gnas pa yang dum re 'ong ste re dogs su ma song ba byed/ de 'dra byung na de ka la gang gnas su bzhag pas chog / yang de sangs pa na sngar bzhin 'dun pa drag pos bsgom/ mtshan mo nyal ba'i skabs bdag med ma'i thugs ka'i a la sems gtad de gnyid du 'gro bar bya'o/ / dmigs skor bzhi bcu zhe gsum pa'o/ /

Always meditate with this repeating process. Initially, you must exert effort for many days, but after meditating that way occasionally, an experience of abiding in nonconceptual lucid bliss will occur on its own. Don’t entertain hopes and fears about this experience reoccurring. If it happens, it is enough to rest in that for as long as it lasts. When it passes, meditate as before with intense intentionality. When you go to bed at night, focus on the A in Nairātmya’s heart and go to sleep. This is the forty-third round of visualization.
Session 44
gnyis pa a yig la brten pa ni/
ii. Recognizing Lucid Clarity Based on the Letter A

sngon 'gro snga ma dang 'dra/ rang yi dam du gsal ba'i lus kyi dbus su rtsa dbu ma dkar po sba lcag tsam gsal btab/ de'i nang lte ba'i thad dam lte 'og sor bzhi gang rung du a yig dkar po dangs gsal 'od kyi rang bzhin can cig gsal btab/ a yig de la dar cig sems bzung / a las 'od zer 'phros/ dbu ma'i nang khengs/ de las 'od zer 'phros/ rang lus kyi nang shin tu gsal bar byas/ rang gi ba spu'i bu ga nas 'od zer 'phros/ snang ba (71) thams cad khra gsal gyis khyab/ nyal ba'i tshe lte 'og gi a la sems gtod/ gzhan ji ltar nyams su len lugs rnams snga ma dang 'dra/ dmigs skor zhe bzhi pa'o/ /

The preliminary is the same as before. Visualize the central channel, white and about the size of a bamboo cane, in the center of your body as the yidam. Inside that at the level of the navel or four finger-widths below the navel, as you like, imagine a white letter A, radiantly clear with the nature of light. Mentally hold that A letter for a moment. Light rays radiate from the A, filling up the inside of the central channel. Light rays emanate out of that and make the inside of your body extremely clear. Light rays shine out of your pores and infuse all appearance with vivid clarity. {71} When going to bed, focus on the A below the navel. The other ways to bring it into experience are the same as before. This is the forty-fourth round of visualization.
Session 45
gsum pa bla ma la brten te bzung ba ni/
iii. Recognizing Lucid Clarity Based on the Guru

yang sngon 'gro snga ma ltar btang la/ rang lhag pa'i lhar gsal ba'i snying gar pad+ma dang zla ba'i gdan la/ rang gi rtsa ba'i bla ma rdo rje 'chang du sgom na rdo rje 'chang sku mdog dkar po spyi dang 'dra ba dang / sku dngos su bsgom na yang / sku sha mdangs dkar zhing 'od zer dkar po 'phro ba/ zhal 'dzum mu la le/ spyan sim me bzhugs pa cig bsgom/ sku che chung gi tshad kyang che na sor bzhi tsam/ chung na mthe bong gi tshad tsam/ de'i bar ji ltar 'os pa bsgom/ de'i thugs kar thig le dkar la dmar ba'i mdangs chags pa'am/ shin tu dkar ba gang bsgoms kyang rung / tshad kyang bla ma'i sku las dpags nas bya ste/ sku gzugs sor bzhi tsam bsgom na de rgya sran tsam/ sku mthe bong tsam bsgom na/ de sran chung tsam bsgom/
