Do the preliminary practice as before. Visualize yourself as the special deity with your root guru on a lotus-moon seat at your heart. If you meditate on the guru as Vajradhara, he is white with the usual attributes. If you meditate on the actual form of your guru, imagine that he or she has a glowing white complexion and radiates white light rays, smiling joyfully and with peaceful eyes. The body size is four finger-widths at the most or one thumb size at the least. Meditate that there is a vital drop at the heart, either radiant white tinged with red or else utterly white. The size should be relative to the guru’s form: if you meditate on a four-finger-width body, then the drop is the size of a fava bean; if the body is thumb-sized, then the drop is the size of a small bean.

des bar ma rnams la'ang mtshon/ gang ltar na yang bla ma'i thugs ka'i thig le 'od 'phro ba de la sems gtad de cung zad mnyam par bzhag / thugs ka'i thig le las 'od 'phros/ sku khra gsal te khyab/ / thugs rgyud bde bas gang /
This goes for anything in between as well. In any case, light radiates from that vital drop in the guru’s heart and pervades the body with brilliant clarity, filling the mind stream with bliss.

sku'i cha thams cad nas 'od zer byung / rang lus kyi nang shin tu gsal bar khyab/ rang gi ba spu'i khung bu nas 'od zer 'phro ba/ snang ba thams cad khra gsal gyis khyab par bsam/ bla ma'i thugs ka'i thig le la 'gyang tsam sems gtad/ de nas 'od zer spro ba'i dmigs pa re byed pa slar nas slar du goms par bya'o/ / nyal ba'i tshe bla ma'i thugs ka'i (72) hU~M la sems gtad de nyal/ bsgom lugs gzhan rnams snga ma bzhin no/ / dmigs skor zhe lnga pa'o/ /

Light rays shine from every part of the guru’s form, pervading your own body with brilliant clarity inside and out. Imagine that light rays stream from all your pores, suffusing all appearance with brilliant clarity. Focus your attention on the vital drop in the guru’s heart for a prolonged period. Then again do the visualization of radiating light rays, alternating between them again and again to familiarize yourself. At bedtime, focus your attention on the syllable hūṃ in the guru’s heart and lie down. {72} Other meditation styles are the same as before. This is the forty-fifth round of visualization.

'di 'od gsal 'dzin pa'i dmigs pa'i dngos gzhi gtso bo de yin no/ / rgyu mtshan ni/ snying ga chos kyi 'khor lo ni/ gnyid 'thug po'i 'khrul pa 'byung ba'i gnas kyi gtso bo yang yin/ de la gnad du bsnun pas lam bsgoms na/ 'khrul pa de'i gnyen po 'od gsal 'char ba'i gnas kyi yang gtso bo yin pas so/ / 'o na gzhan gnyis la'ang gnad de yong thang ba la snyam na/ 'di 'dra'i rigs la nges pa med te/ spyir gnyid 'thug po'i 'od gsal 'char ba'i gnas drag shos de snying ga yin kyang / thog mar gnas der rlung 'jug dka' ba'i skabs shig / rtsa dbu ma'i gnas gzhan du gnad du bsnun na/ der rlung 'dus pa'i 'od gsal gyi nyams myong cig 'phral du skye bar 'gyur/ de yang yang goms pa na/ des sna drangs te 'dun pa cung zad bsgyur ba kho nas 'bad rtsol med par snying gar rlung sems 'dus pa'i 'od gsal 'char ba nyid la yang tshegs med do/ / thabs 'di rmi lam sogs gzhan la'ang rigs 'gre'o/ / des na 'od gsal 'dzin pa'i dmigs pa gsum po 'di/ gang blo la bde ba cig 'bad pas bsgoms nas nus pa thon par bya dgos mod/ gang zag gcig gis gsum kar bsgom dgos pa rang yang ma yin no/ /

This is the primary visualization for the main practice of grasping lucid clarity. That is because the dharma chakra at the heart is the main site where delusion occurs in deep sleep. If you meditate on the path by targeting that vital point, then it is also the main site where lucid clarity arises, the antidote for that delusion. But you may wonder if the other two methods are of any help in applying that vital point. Visualizations of that kind are not definite. In general, the best place for lucid clarity of deep sleep to arise is the heart. However, in the beginning, when it is difficult to insert the vital winds there, you can have the immediate experience of lucid clarity from the gathering of the winds if you target other places of the central channel. Then if you familiarize with that repeatedly, it will lead to the effortless confluence of winds and mind at the heart with just a minor shift in your intentionality. Lucid clarity itself will then arise easily. This method should also be applied to Dream and the others. Therefore, you do need to meditate with effort until you gain ability on whichever of these three visualizations for recognizing lucid clarity suits your mentality. It is not absolutely necessary for a single individual to meditate on all three.
Session 46
gnyis pa 'od gsal lam khyer
b. Integrating Lucid Clarity
['di] la/ nyin mo sku gsum lam khyer dang / mtshan mo sku gsum rang shar ba zhes sa bcad gnyis su byed kyang nyams len dmigs pa gcig kho na ste/ nyin mo sku gsum lam khyer nyid do/ /

Although there are two headings in the outline [of The Inventory by Khyungpo Naljor] for this—Integrating the Three Kāyas in the Daytime and Self-Arising of the Three Kāyas at Nighttime—in practice there is only one: Integrating the Three Kāyas in the Daytime.

de yang dang por 'di thun mtshams kyi nyams (73) len la gal che ste/ sgyu lus skabs su/ 'dun pa gsum sbrags bshad pa'i dod yin/ de yang rtsa ba mi rtag skyo shas dang / gsol 'debs me tog 'char byed du bshad pa bzhin/ 'od gsal gyi thun mtshams su yang / mi rtag pa dang / bla ma'i mos gus sngar sgyu lus su bshad pa bzhin dgos la/ sgyu lus dang rmi lam la/ sgyu ma dang rmi lam gyi 'dun pa dgos pa'i dod/ 'dir sku gsum lam khyer gyi 'jog stangs de dgos pa'i don yin no/ /

With regard to this, in the beginning the practice in the session breaks is very important. {73} It replaces the threefold intentionality explained in the context of Illusory Body—that is, the explanations of the root as a sense of impermanence and disillusionment and the supplication that grows the flowers. Accordingly, in the session breaks of Lucid Clarity practice, you need to meditate on impermanence and guru devotion as explained before in Illusory Body. Then, as a substitute for the necessary intentionality for recognizing illusion and dream in the practices of Illusory Body and Dream yoga, here you must apply the Integration of the Three Kāyas.

bsam sdings pa'i khrid yig ni/ thun thun mtshams kyi gsal kha med/ 'jag chen a la sems gtod pa bzhin du grims lhod ran par bya/ zhes gsung ste/ de'i go ba ni a yig gi skangs na rig pa yengs kyang ma yengs bcur bcur du yang ma song ba mnyam rjes thams cad du bsgom gsung ba de yin pas/ thun thun mtshams gnyis kar du bsgom pa'i don yin/ de la spyir thun gyi skabs su yang 'jog tshul de ka dang mthun pa yin mod kyi/ thun gyi nyams len byed tshul logs su bshad zin pas/ 'dir ni thun mtshams kho na'i dbang du byas pa'o/ / de yang bdag zas za 'gro 'chag / nyal 'dug / spyod lam kun du sku gsum lam khyer 'di dran pa zhig byed dgos snyam pa'i 'dun pa yang yang btang gin 'gro 'dug sogs bya byed gang byed pa'i skabs der/ gang shar de ka la sems gtad te/ shes pa khong klod/ rang zhal lta shes tsam bya/ de'i tshe mig gi lta stangs kyang ha re bzhag / de yang thog ma thun mtshams yin yang sos dal du 'dug pa'i skabs/ dran pa bsten pa tsam gyis 'phral 'phral du sleb 'ong / de nas bya byed brel po kun la 'dra rim pas (74) bsre bar bya'o/ /

In Samdingpa’s guidebook, there is no clear distinction between sessions and session breaks. Jakchen states, “While focusing attention on the syllable A, maintain a balance between concentration and relaxation.” We can understand this to mean that while visualizing the letter A, though awareness wanders, don’t try too hard to prevent that distraction. It means to meditate [this way] at all times in equipoise and subsequent attainment, indicating meditation in both sessions and session breaks. In general, this instruction is certainly in keeping with the manner of placement during meditation sessions. However, the session practice has already been explained elsewhere, so here it applies only to the session breaks. When you eat, walk, move, lie down, sit, and so on—during all daily activities—think that you must remember this Integration of the Three Kāyas. So set your intentions again and again while walking and sitting and so on. During whatever activities you engage, focus your attention directly on whatever happens, relax consciousness inward, and glance at your own nature just enough to recognize it. During those times, hold your gaze with wide-open unblinking eyes. Also, at first, even though it is a session break when you are supposedly resting in a leisurely way, just recalling this will cause sudden experiences. Then eventually you can even apply this to all busy activity. {74}

de yang snang ba sna tshogs gang shar ba de'i steng gi gsal cha de gsal ba sprul sku/ rang zhal la cher re bltas pas cir yang ma yin pa de stong pa chos sku/ snang ba sna tshogs pa shar ba la bzo bcos ma byas pa de dang / ngos bzung ci yang med pa de sems gsal rig tsam gyi steng de na/ ngo bo dbyer med gcig car ro gcig tu shar ba de/ rang rig rang gsal longs spyod rdzogs sku lam khyer ro/ /

Furthermore, the clear aspect connected with whatever myriad appearances arise is the clarity of nirmāṇakāya. Looking openly at your own nature and not seeing anything at all is the emptiness of dharmakāya. Just the mere awareness and clarity of mind arises at once as a single taste, essentially inseparable, without any fabrication regarding the various appearances, and without any recognition [of them]. That is the innate awareness and innate clarity of saṃbhogakāya. That is the integration.
de ltar na thog mar thun mtshams kyi dge sbyor 'di la legs par bslab/ de rjes phal cher la 'di lam du khyer thub pa nas/ skabs 'di'i 'dun pa gsum po gang rung re dran par bya'o/ /
In this way, first train well in this applied virtue in the session breaks. After that, when you can mostly integrate that, recall any of the three intentions that are suitable for the occasion.

mtshan mo sku gsum rang shar ni/ thun gyi skabs su dmigs pa la drag tu bcur ba dang / thun mtshams su sku gsum lam khyer bsgoms pa de'i mthu las/ mtshan mo gnyid 'thug po'i dus su 'od gsal zin pa na/ gsal stong zung 'jug gi sku gsum rang shar du 'byung ngo / / gnyid dus kyi gsal ba ni/ snang ba rags pa sna tshogs pa 'di dag de dus mi 'char bas/ rig pa nyid kyi gsal cha dang / 'char sgo rtags kyi snang ba sna tshogs pa'o/ / dmigs skor zhe drug pa'o/ /

The three kāyas arise by themselves at night through the force of intense application of the visualizations during the sessions and the meditation of integrating the three kāyas during session breaks. When you grasp lucid clarity at nighttime in deep sleep, it is the natural arising of the three kāyas, the unity of clarity and emptiness. Regarding clarity during sleep, at this time myriad coarse appearances do not arise. Rather, it is the clear aspect of awareness itself and the various appearing signs of experience that arise. This is the forty-sixth round of visualization.
gsum pa bsre ba
c. Blending Lucid Clarity
['di] la/ gsal stong bsre ba/ mnyam rjes bsre ba/ nyin mtshan bsre ba/ bde stong bsre ba ste bzhi las/
This has four parts: (1) Blending Clarity and Emptiness, (2) Blending Equipoise and Postmeditation Attainment, (3) Blending Day and Night, and (4) Blending Bliss and Emptiness.
Session 47
dang po ni/
i. Blending Clarity and Emptiness

sgom mnyam gzhag gi dus/ sems cir yang ma grub pa 'dra ba de bsgoms pas rkyen byas nas stong sang sang ba ci yang med pa 'dra ba zhig 'char/ thun mtshams su yang gdong gtad kyi dngos po 'di dag gang yang mi 'dug snyam pa 'byung ste/ stong nyams rkyang pa shar ba yin/ skabs der thun dang thun mtshams thams cad du mig nam mkha' la gtad/ (75) rig pa hur byung / stong sang nge ba'i gzhi de la bltas pas/ stong pa de la gsal cha rim gyis rnyed de gsal stong du 'gyur/ yang thun gyi skabs su/ rnam rtog med pa la rig pa gsal seng nge dga' bde dang bcas pa 'byung / thun mtshams su'ang de la sred pa che/ rang rtsis skye bar 'dug na/ gsal ba rkyang pa'i nyams skyes pa yin pas/ thun thun mtshams thams cad du sems dangs sang nge ba/ gsal rjen ne ba/ de'i ngo bo la lta gzhigs drag tu bcug pas thogs pa'i dngos po zhig pa ltar chems se song nas ngos bzung du med pa cig 'ong / de'i ngang la bzo bcos med par bzhag / sems la bltas nas kyang sgyu ma lta bu'o zhes yang yang dran pa gsal stong du 'char te/ de ltar na gsal ba stong pa la bsre ba'o/ / dmigs skor zhe bdun pa'o/ /

During meditative equipoise there is an experience of your mind not existing at all. That meditation is the condition for an experience of utter emptiness, as if there were nothing whatsoever. Even during the intervals between sessions, the thought occurs to you that all the things you face do not exist. That is the arising of the experience of unaccompanied emptiness. In those situations, whether in sessions or breaks, turn your eyes to the sky, rouse your awareness, and regard the basis of that utter emptiness. {75} Through that, you will gradually discover clarity in that emptiness and it will become emptiness-clarity. Also, during the sessions, when there are no conceptual thoughts, vivid clarity accompanied by joy and bliss will occur. There may be strong craving for that experience during session breaks. If a sense of self-complacency is present, that is the arising of the experience of unaccompanied clarity. Therefore, during all sessions and breaks, look at the essence of mind’s pristine radiance and bare clarity and scrutinize it intensely. Through that it will vanish and leave nothing to recognize, as when tangible things disintegrate. Rest within that state without fabrication or contrivance. When you look at the mind, recall again and again that “it is like an illusion.” Clarity and emptiness will arise. In this way, blend clarity and emptiness. This is the forty-seventh round of visualization.
Session 48
gnyis pa mnyam rjes bsre ba ni/
ii. Blending Equipoise and Postmeditation Attainment

spyir rjes thob mtshan nyid dang ldan pa cig yin na/ mnyam gzhag dang ched du bsre mi dgos kyang / 'dir thun la mnyam gzhag dang / thun mtshams tsam po la rjes thob ces btags pa'o/ / de yang thun gyi skabs su rtsol bas bcos pa ma yin par sems gsal stong du du ma re gnas pa yang yang byung kyang / thun mtshams su dang po'i tha mal pa zad ma de ka ma gtogs/ gsal stong gi nyams ye mi sleb pa 'dug na/ thun gyi skabs su nyams cung zad shar ba'i dus der/ spyod lam gang yang rung ba cig la bsre ba'i 'dun pa gtod ste/ dper na/ da ltar bdag skor ba byed pa'i skabs su/ nyams 'di bskyang bar bya snyam pa'i 'dun pa yang yang btang / thun las langs pa'i skabs su yang de ka'i rgyun dran pas bzung / lag tu 'chang rgyu lta bu dran 'dzin gyi (76) rtags cig kyang bzhag /

In general, if you have genuine postmeditation attainment, it is not necessary to intentionally blend it with resting in equipoise. But here we are applying the terms equipoise (mnyam gzhag) to meditation sessions and postmeditation attainment (rjes thob) only to the intervals between sessions. Now during the sessions, resting momentarily in the empty clarity of mind without contrived effort may occur again and again, but in the breaks there is nothing other than that initial ordinary state. The experience of empty clarity just never happens. If that’s the case, then when that slight experience arises, set the intention to blend it with whatever you are doing. For instance, repeatedly develop intentionality by thinking, “Now while I am doing circumambulations, I will nurture this experience.” When you arise from a session of meditation, also hold the continuity of that thought with mindfulness. Even set up a sign to remind yourself, like something carried on your hand. {76}

de nas skor ba byed pa'i skabs su/ sku gsum lam khyer du bshad pa bzhin ngang de bskyangs pas/ thun gyi skabs su bshad pa lta bu'i gsal stong gi nyams de sleb 'ong / de ltar zhag 'ga' re song na rtsol ba chen po mi dgos par 'ong ste/ de la goms nas spyod lam gzhan thams cad la'ang rim pas sbyang / 'di ni mnyam gzhag gi nyams myong rjes thob la bsre ba yin/ rjes thob mnyam gzhag la tshur bsre ba ni mi dgos/ 'ga' zhig la rjes thob kyi nyams myong bzang po shar nas/ des mnyam gzhag la bog 'thon pa cig 'ong ste/ de shugs 'byung la 'ong gi bcos pas mi phan no/ / dmigs skor zhe brgyad pa'o/ /

Then when the time comes to circumambulate, maintain the Integration of the Three Kāyas just as it was described, so that the experience of empty clarity in the meditation session will happen just as it was described. In this way, after a few days have passed, you will not need to exert great effort. Once you are familiar with it, other activities will all gradually be affected. This is the blending of the experiences of equipoise with postmeditation attainment. There is no need to blend the postmeditation attainment back into the equipoise. Some practitioners have excellent experiences in postmeditation, which will also be an enhancement of their experience in equipoise. But that happens automatically; it won’t help to contrive it. This is the forty-eighth round of visualization.
Session 49
gsum pa nyin mtshan bsre ba ni/
iii. Blending Day and Night

nyin mo thun gyi skabs la gsal stong gi nyams shar yang / mtshan mo gnyid 'thug po'i skabs su ye ma slebs na/ thun gyi skabs su dmigs pa gsum po gang rung cig la brten nas/ rlung bum pa can bsgom zhing rig pa drag tu bzhur/ gsal stong gi nyams shar ba'i dus/ do nub gnyid kyi dus su'ang 'di kho na ltar bsgom rgyu yin snyam pa bag tsam re 'dun pa btang gin/ thun mtshams su yang snga dro 'dun pa cung zad bya/ dgongs mo dang srod kyi thun mtshams la 'dun pa drag tu sbyong ba gal che/ nyal khar yang 'jam rlung khug pa kha re bzung zhing dmigs pa bsgom/ mthar rang gi lus dang sems la sems gtad te cher re bzhag pa'i ngang nas gnyid du 'gro bar bya/ des nges par gnyid kyi dge sbyor zin 'ong ngo / / yang 'ga' zhig la mtshan mo'i dge sbyor bzang po thog mar skyes nas/ nyin par nyams myong de dran pa tsam gyis nyin bar gyi dge sbyor la bogs 'byin par byed pa cig (77) kyang yod te/ 'di yang rang shugs la 'byung ba ka yin no/ / 'od gsal la ni de lta bu dgos pa ci rigs pa 'byung la/ rmi lam rtsal sbyong la ni/ mtshan mos nyin mo la ched gtad bogs 'byin dgos pa yang shin tu mang ngo / / dmigs skor zhe dgu pa'o/ /

Even if experiences of empty clarity arise during the daytime sessions, they may not show up in the deep sleep of the nighttime. If so, rely on a suitable one of the three session visualizations. Then meditate with the vase breathing and intensely squeeze your awareness. When an experience of empty clarity arises, think with a modicum of intentionality, “Tonight when I sleep, this is exclusively what I will meditate on.” Then, in the morning break, also develop your intention somewhat. In the afternoon and evening session breaks, it is important to train with intense intentionality. Then, at bedtime, hold a few gentle breaths and meditate on the visualization. Finally, turn your attention to your body and mind and go to sleep within a state of settled openness. That will definitely allow you to grasp the applied virtue of sleep. For some practitioners, the excellent applied virtue of the nighttime arises right from the start, and by merely recalling those experiences during the day, the applied virtue of the daytime is enhanced. {77} This also happens automatically. In regard to Lucid Clarity, this [blending] occurs appropriately as needed. In the energy training of Dream, there are very many methods, since the nighttime experiences enhance the intentional focus in the daytime. This is the forty-ninth round of visualization.
Session 50
bzhi pa bde stong dbyer med du bsre ba ni/
iv. Blending Bliss and Emptiness Inseparably

sems gsal ba dang / stong pa dang / mi rtog pa'i nyams kyis drangs pa'i dga' ba de la nyams bde ba rgya chen po 'byung yang / ched du gnyer nas stong par bsre ba mi dgos/ gsal ba nyid sgyu ma lta bur shes pas rang chod la 'gro/ zhu bde'i nyams rnams stong par bsre dgos pa yin te/ gzhan lus shes rab kyi bde ba'am/ rang lus thabs ldan gtum mo'ang / sgyu lus dbang po tha ma lta bu'am/ thig le dbang bzhi'i gnad dam/ 'od gsal 'dzin pa'i dmigs pa gsum lta bu bsgoms pas/ rlung dbu mar thim pa'i bde drod skyes pa lta bu la bsre dgos pa yin te/ de yang bde nyams lan re tsam byung 'phral la bsre ba skad byas na/ nyams de sangs 'gro bas mi bya la/ de yang yang 'ong zhing brtan po yod na bsre dgos/ nga rgyal dang sred zhen mngon gyur pa med na/ de'i rang zhal bltas pa tsam gyis bde bar snang ba ma 'gags bzhin du/ ngos bzung med par lhod de shigs se song ba de ka bskyangs pas chog / sred zhen dang rlom sems skye na/ bde ba de nyid la sgyu ma lta bur 'dun pa skyangs shing / mthar sgyu 'dzin dang bral ba'i phyag rgya chen po la bzhag na bde stong dbyer med du 'gyur ro/ /

Tremendous bliss will arise in the joy brought on by experiences of mental clarity, emptiness, and nonthought. But it is not necessary to seek it out and blend it with emptiness. This will happen on of its own accord by knowing that the clarity itself is like an illusion. It is necessary to blend with emptiness in the experiences of melting bliss: the bliss from [practices with] another’s body, the knowledge consort; the Inner Heat of one’s own body as the method; the Illusory Body like that for those of lesser capability; the Vital Points of the Four Empowerments of Drops; or the likes of the three visualizations for grasping lucid clarity. Meditation on those practices causes the bliss-warmth of the winds dissolving in the central channel to arise. In such cases, it is necessary to blend [with emptiness]. This is not to say that you should blend immediately after each experience of bliss. That would dispel the experience, so don’t do that. You only need to blend after the experience comes again and again and becomes stable. If you do not manifest pride and attachment, just looking at your own nature causes the unhindered appearance of bliss. Relax into that and let go without identifying it and maintain just that. That is sufficient. If attachment and conceit do arise, train with the intentionality of the illusion-like nature of that very bliss. Ultimately, when you rest in mahāmudrā, free of fixation on illusion, it becomes bliss and emptiness inseparable.

bsre ba bzhi po de dag thams cad kyi gnas skabs su/ thun mtshams spyod lam gang byed kyang / yang nas yang du (78) gang shar de la glang po che'i lta stangs kyis had de chad de 'jog pa kho na dgos/ mnyam gzhag gi dus su yang rtog med kyi nyams bde gsal gang shar dang / rtog bcas dmigs pa la gnad du bsnun pa'i dus thams cad du yang de ka ltar 'jog pa gnad du che/ lar thun thun mtshams su bde sdug mtho dman 'jig rten chos brgyad thams cad la sgyu ma lta bur shes pas/ da lta 'jig rten pa'i bzang ngan mtho dman nye ring gi rnam gzhag skad skad po 'di'i a 'thas zhig pa rang gal che'o/ / dmigs skor lnga bcu pa'o/ /

During all four of those occasions of blending, no matter what activity you are up to during the breaks, {78} all you need is to look repeatedly at whatever arises with the elephant’s gaze and enter in open astonished awareness. At the time of resting in equipoise, with whatever experiences of conceptual clarity and emptiness arise and whenever you are applying the vital points of conceptual visualizations—at all those times it is crucial to enter that same state. Then again, in session or in break, know that happiness and suffering, high and low, and the eight worldly concerns are all like an illusion. This will destroy the reifications of good and bad, high and low, near and far—the celebrated categories of the modern world. This itself is important. This is the fiftieth round of visualization.
bzhi pa mthar thug ni/
d. Ultimate Lucid Clarity

dang por nyin mo dang mtshan mo'i 'od gsal gang la'ang / 'od gsal gyi rtogs pa skye ba'i dang por gsal stong dbyer med kyi 'od gsal 'byung / tshogs lam gyi thad yin/ de nas bde stong dbyer med kyi 'od gsal 'byung / sbyor lam gyi thad yin/ de nas zab zhi spros bral gyi 'od gsal 'byung / ma dag sa bdun gyi thad sor sleb/ de nas dbyer med mthar thug gi 'od gsal 'byung / dag pas gsum gyi skabs yin/ de rjes dag pa gnyis ldan gyi 'od gsal te/ rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas gyi sa ye shes chos sku'o/ / 'di dag gi don rgyas par bshad na mang mod kyi 'dir ma spros so/ / 'di ni spyir 'od gsal zhes bya ba gnas lugs kyi don rtogs tshul la sa mtshams phye ba yin/ gnyid kyi 'od gsal gcig po'i dbye ba ma yin no/ / 'di la dmigs pa logs pa med pas dmigs skor du mi bgrang / chos thun gcig lta bu ji ltar 'os pa'o/ /

In the beginning, whether Lucid Clarity of the daytime or the nighttime, the first realization to arise will be the lucid clarity of inseparable clarity and emptiness. This corresponds to the path of accumulation. Then the lucid clarity of inseparable bliss and emptiness arises. This concerns the path of application. Then the lucid clarity of profound peace free of embellishment arises. This corresponds to arriving at each of the seven impure stages. Then the lucid clarity of consummate inseparability arises. This is the occasion of the three pure stages. After that is the lucid clarity endowed with dual purity; the dharmakāya of timeless awareness through perfect awakening. Of course, if one were to explain this subject extensively, there would be much more, but I will not elaborate here. In general, the term lucid clarity (’od gsal) here has been defined as the manner of realizing true nature, not as a category of the Lucid Clarity of sleep per se. There is no particular visualization here, so it does not count as a round of visualization. It could be taught in sessions as appropriate.
gsum pa rjes kyi khrid
3. Concluding Practices
['di] la/ dam tshig spyi dang bye brag / gegs sel nyes skyon rang dag / bogs 'don the tshom gcod byed/ khyad (79) 'phags 'char sgo ngos 'dzin/ nyams rtogs nyin mtshan khyad par te lnga las/

This has five parts: (1) general and specific sacred pledges; (2) removing obstructions, the self-purification of faults and mistakes; (3) enhancement practices that resolve doubt; (4) identifying special perceptions; and (5) divisions of daytime and nighttime, experiences and realizations. {79}
dang po ni/
a. General and Specific Sacred Pledges

spyir sdom gsum las rang gis gang blangs ba'i bslab bya rnams ma nyams pa gal che/ nyes ltung can la sgom rnam par dag pa mi skye zhing / sngar skyes rnams kyang nyes ltung byung na nyams 'gro bas so/ / de'i nang nas kyang gsang sngags kyi dam tshig ma nyams pa rtsa ba yan lag gi ltung bas ma gos pa dgos te/ dam tshig de dag nyams na sgom gyi re ba lta zhog / 'di dang phyi mar mtho ris kyi bde ba tsam yang med te/ ngan song gsum la zang thal du 'gro bas so/ /

In general, it is important not to impair the training of whichever of the three levels of vows you have taken. Even previous experiences could degenerate if a fault or mistake occurs. Above all, the flawless sacred pledges of Secret Mantra must not be tainted by the root and branch downfalls. If those sacred pledges are damaged, forget about hopes for meditation; there won’t be even a modicum of higher-realm happiness in this or the next life because you will go directly to the three miserable realms.

de dag spyi'i dam tshig yin la/ gzhan mnyam rjes kyi dam tshig mtha' dag sgrub nus na der yang 'dus/ 'on kyang dam bca' 'chag med yin yin po'i bya spyod kyi rim pa mang pos sems 'khrug par yang mi byed de/ nyams len dang 'bral med kyi ngang nas/ bla ma'i mos gus dang ma bral ba/ rten kun da byang sems ma nyams pa/ tha mal chags sdang gi yul snang thams cad sgyu ma lta bur sgoms nas/ chags sdang gi dbang du mi gtong ba rnams 'od gsal sgos kyi dam tshig go /

This applies to sacred pledge in general. Furthermore, if you are able to practice all the sacred pledges of equipoise and postmeditation, those are also included in that. However, many kinds of activities to ensure that your oaths have not shifted may disturb the mind even more, so do not do that. Without ever parting from your practice or from devotion to the guru, do not compromise the kunda bodhicitta, which is the support of practice, and meditate on all ordinary objects of attraction and aversion as illusion-like without falling under their power. These are the sacred pledges particular to Lucid Clarity.

'dir 'od gsal ces bya ba yang / chos drug gi nang tshan mtshan mo'i 'od gsal kho nar ma zad/ nyin mtshan gyi 'od gsal thams cad yin pas/ bsre ba sgyu lus spyi khyab la go bar bya la/ 'pho ba bar do'ang bsre ba'i yan lag yin pa'i phyir/ dam tshig 'di ni dam tshig spyi 'gro yin no/ /

Although here we say “lucid clarity,” it does not refer only to the nighttime Lucid Clarity in the Six Dharmas but to all Lucid Clarity of daytime and nighttime. Therefore, it should be understood to apply generally to the blending with illusory body, as well as to the practices of Transference and Intermediate State because those are branches of Blending. Thus this sacred pledge covers all the sacred pledges.
gnyis pa gegs sel nyes skyon rang dag ni/
b. Removing Obstructions, the Self-Purification of Faults and Mistakes

spyir thabs lam dang 'brel ba gegs sel gyi yi ge sna tshogs pa ni gzhan du gsal la/ 'dir gsal stong 'dzin med/ snang stong rang shar/ bde stong zhen bral (80) rnams nyams myong gi ye shes yin pa la/ de rnams kyi mi mthun phyogs kyi bdud ni/ 'dzin pa rnam rtog rang ga mar shor ba 'di yin pas/ rnam rtog gi rang zhal bltas nas rang grol rang dag rang stong du ngo 'phrod par bsgom/ de yang rnam rtog sems yin/ sems skye med mtha' dang bral ba'i gnad kas gang shar la bzo bcos med par bltas pas 'char sgo'i rang tshugs zhig / snang ba dang stong pa ris su ma chad pa'i rang 'gros la 'jog pa dang / yang skabs 'gar 'char sgo sna tshogs pa'i snang ba dang rig pa thams cad sgyu ma lta bur shes pa'i 'dun pa drag pos ar la gtad te bzhag go / / de gnyis kho nas gegs dang gol sa sdug bsngal thams cad las grol bar 'gyur ro/ /

In general, the texts about dispelling obstructions connected with the path of methods is presented elsewhere. Here, empty clarity without fixation, empty appearance that arises by itself, and empty bliss without attachment are all the timeless awareness of experience. {80} The devil that is the antithesis of those is to get lost in fixating on regular conceptual thought. Therefore, look at the very nature of those thoughts and meditate on recognizing their self-liberated, self-purified, self-empty state. Furthermore, conceptual thought is mind, and mind is unborn and unlimited. With that vital point, look at whatever arises without contrivance or fabrication and autonomous perceptions will vanish. Remain in the natural movement [of thoughts] that do not incline toward either appearance or emptiness. Again, sometimes push it to extremes with the intense intentionality of knowing that all awareness and appearances of the various perceptions are like an illusion. Just these two methods will liberate you from all the sufferings of obstructions and erroneous directions.
gsum pa bogs 'don the tshom gcod byed ni/
c. Enhancement Practices That Resolve Doubt

kha cig rang gi nyams myong la the tshoms med par nges shes thag chod kyis bogs 'don yang gsung / 'ga' zhig tshad med gnyis kyis bogs 'don yang gsung / de las kyang 'di ltar bya ste/ khyad par du snang ba sna tshogs dang / bde sdug chags sdang gi yul rnams kyi steng du/ sgyu lus rmi lam gyi 'dun pa'i rtsal sbyong dang / mi rtog pa rnams hur thon pa sbyong ba dang / gnas nges med/ 'dug stangs nges med/ 'gro ldod spyod lam nges pa med pa la yang 'dun pa gang rung re shugs bskyed te yang yang bsgom pa rnams phyi'i bogs 'don yin/ rlung sems 'jur la 'debs pa'i thabs rtsa rlung gi sbyor ba drag po shi med ko med du gzir ba skabs skabs su bsgom pa nang gi bogs 'don yin/ bogs 'don gnyis po de 'dra re'i mthar rig pa'i rtsal chen po re 'ong bas/ de la thag chod kyi nges shes bskyed/ de bla ma'i (81) bka' drin du shes nas gsol ba 'debs/ de ltar ma rtogs pa'i sems can la snying rje re bsgom pa lags/ bogs 'don dgos na de la mdzod/ /

Some teach that having conviction in one’s own experience without any doubts enhances practice. Some teach that the two immeasurables are an enhancement. Apart from those, here is what you can do: refine the energy of intentionality of illusion and dream, and train vigorously in nonthought directly with the particular myriad appearances and objects of happiness and sadness, attraction and aversion. Generate the force of whatever intentionality is suitable in indefinite places, indefinite positions, and indefinite activities of going and staying. Meditating again and again this way is the outer enhancement. Occasionally meditating with intense focus unconcerned with life or death in the methods of conjoining vital winds and mind in the intense application of channels and winds is the inner enhancement. After each of those two enhancement practices, there will come a strong dynamic energy of awareness, generating the certitude of resolution. {81} Know it to be the guru’s kindness and pray. It is good to meditate with compassion for sentient beings who do not have such realization. Do this if you need to enhance practice.
bzhi pa khyad 'phags 'char sgo ngos 'dzin ni/
d. Identifying Special Perceptions
rgyas par logs su ston pa'i phyir skabs 'dir rgyas bshad mi dgos mod/ 'on kyang 'di skad ces gsal ba'i 'char sgo/ mi rtog pa'i 'char sgo/ bde ba'i 'char sgo/ zung 'jug gi 'char sgo ste bzhi yod lags/

Since this is extensively presented elsewhere, there is no need for a detailed explanation at this point. However, having said that, there are indeed these four topics: (1) the perception of clarity, (2) the perception of nonthought, (3) the perception of bliss, and (4) the perception of unity.

dang po ni/ 'od gsal nyams kyi gsal cha la gnyid dus su rtags snang dang / lus nyams/ sems nyams sna tshogs su 'char ba cig yin/ gnyis pa ni/ rna bar tsi rong ba dang / thibs thibs pa dang / 'jir 'jir gnon pa'o/ rlung sems dbu mar chud pa yin/ yang 'dar ba dang / 'phar ba dang / brgyal ba dang / yan lag phras song ba 'ong / rtsa mdud grol ba yin/ gzhan yang rnam shes nam mkha' la yas pa 'dra ba 'ong / mi rtog pa gsal snang chen po la 'dar yed pa 'dra ba'ang 'ong / de dag la dga' spro dang / rlom sems byung na dge sbyor la bogs mi thon/ nad gdon gyi rnam 'gyur yin par bzung na gegs su 'gro bas/ dga' mi dga' med par byung rgyal du bskyad/ gsum pa ni/ lus sems bde gsal du 'char ba yin/ bzhi pa ni nyin mtshan thams cad du 'bad rtsol med par 'od gsal 'char ba la zer ro/ /

First, for the clarity aspect of the experience of lucid clarity, there arise various appearances of signs during sleep, physical experiences, and mental experiences. Second, ringing in the ears, deep darkness, and oppressive heaviness will come. This is the wind-mind entering the central channel. Again, there will be experiences of shaking, quivering, fainting, and flailing limbs. This is the release of the channel knots. Further, there will be an experience like consciousness disappearing into the sky and a kind of trembling when experiencing the great clarity-appearance of nonthought. If you feel exultation and conceit about these, it will negatively impact your applied virtue. If you grasp them as the manifestations of sickness and spirits, they will become obstructions. Maintain a flexible attitude without liking or disliking what occurs. Third is the arising of bliss-clarity in body and mind. Fourth is the dawning of lucid clarity without effort or exertion in all times of day and night. So it is said.
rtsa ba'i lnga pa nyams rtogs nyin mtshan khyad par ni/
e. Divisions of Daytime and Nighttime, Experiences and Realizations

de yang lha sku dang thig le sogs blos bcos shing gsar du bsgom pa'i skabs der/ gsal mi gsal ji ltar byung yang 'od gsal yang min la lha sku rang shar yang min no/ / rig pa bsgrims (82) te bzhag pa'i skabs der rtsol ba'i 'dun rtog dang bcas bzhin du/ sems bag re gnas pa dang / bde gsal gyi nyams yod pa snyam byed pa cig 'byung ste/ de tsam cig gnyid sad kyi gnas skabs gang la byung kyang 'od gsal dngos ni ma yin/ 'od gsal gyi rgyur 'gro ba tsam ni yin no/ /

On the occasions of meditating on new, mentally created [subjects], such as a deity’s form or vital-essence drops, no matter the degree of clarity, it is neither lucid clarity nor the self-arising deity’s form. {82} When awareness is tightened up and you rest in that with diligent thoughts of intentionality, you will think that mind abides just a little and that you are having experiences of bliss and clarity. When just that occurs during any circumstances of waking life, it is still not real lucid clarity. It is just the cause that can lead to lucid clarity.

des na thun thun mtshams gang la yin kyang / kho rang gi skabs der ched btad rtsol ba ma byas par/ rang shar ba'i sems gsal stong bde ba mi rtog par shar ba de la 'od gsal zer/ nyin mtshan gang la byung kyang khyad med do/ / yang kho ra'i dus de na skyed 'dod kyi blo drag po mngon gyur med kyang / rang dang phyi rol du lha sku lam lam shar yong na/ sgyu lus lha sku rang shar zhes bya ba yin/ sad dus dang rmi lam la khyad med/

Therefore, whether in sessions or breaks, without exerting any purposeful effort in that particular situation, naturally arising mental clarity, bliss, and nonthought will dawn. That is called lucid clarity, whether it occurs in the day or the night. Also, around those times, if the deity’s form suddenly arises as oneself or externally without particularly wanting it to, then that is called the self-arising deity’s form of illusory body. It makes no difference if you are awake or dreaming.

nged sgom chen pa'i glen gtam mam/ ril sdug khur 'dra byas pa'i sdug yus tsam lags mod/ rgyud sde mkhan po dang mkhas pa rnams bkyon te mchi/ rang sa na blo gtad thub pa re myong thog na bdog / bka' bkyon kyang skrag rgyu tsam mi gda'/ bsgom nus na rang re las dang po pa mkhas rmongs kun la yang / dka' tshegs chen po rang yang mi dgos/ yun ring dgug sdod rang yang mi dgos par 'ong / rkyen byung dus su'ang cung zad sleb 'ong / sems la'ang phan pas 'phral bde zhing skyid par yang 'ong / sa lam mthon po'i sgyu lus dang / 'od gsal zung 'jug gi rnam gzhag tsam de rang re las dang po pas lag len du khel ba min/ da lta lag len du khel ba 'di rnams ka mthar de dag gi rgyu grung por 'gro ba yin/ myu gu chung ngu nas legs par bskyangs pas mthar ston thog 'ong ba dang 'dra'o/ (83)

Surely this must seem like the tall tales of a great meditator or the boastful complaints of sufferings endured in mountain retreats, at which tantric scholars and learned persons level criticism. But one can trust oneself when in one’s own territory. I have direct personal experience and no reason to fear criticism. If we are able to meditate, all of us beginners, learned and ignorant alike, we do not need to suffer actual great hardships or wait for a very long time. When conditions are right, a little something will happen. Since that will benefit the mind, it will also provide immediate joy and comfort. Beginners such as ourselves cannot carry the practice of the unity of Illusory Body and Lucid Clarity that is commensurate with the stages and paths [of a bodhisattva]. But ultimately these practical steps for our current situation will become the effective cause of those states. It is like when we carefully cultivate small sprouts that will become an abundant autumn harvest in the end. {83}

de lta bu'i 'od gsal la/ nyams kyi 'od gsal dang / rtogs pa'i 'od gsal gnyis yod/ de gnyis ka la nyin mo sad dus kyi 'od gsal dang / mtshan mo gnyid dus kyi 'od gsal gnyis su dbye bas bzhi ru song / bzhi ka la snang bcas dang / snang med gnyis gnyis su phye bas brgyad du 'gyur/ snang bcas bzhi la phyi dang 'brel ba bzhi dang / ma 'brel ba bzhi ste brgyad/ snang med bzhi la'ang / srab mo'i 'od gsal dang / 'thug po'i 'od gsal gnyis gnyis te brgyad/ de thams cad bsdoms pas bcu drug go / slob ma nyams myong shar ba yin na/ de dag gi ngos 'dzin zhib par bshad la/ khong rang la shar ba'i 'od gsal gang yin pa de ngo sprod/ slob ma nyams myong ma shar ba dang / sna tshogs 'dus pa'i tshogs pa la/ bcu drug dbye ba'i ming tsam ka bshad pa de kas chog go /

There are two types of lucid clarity: the lucid clarity of experience and the lucid clarity of realization. Those two can be subdivided into the lucid clarity of the daytime waking experience and the lucid clarity of nighttime sleep. Dividing each of those four into lucid clarity with appearances and without appearances makes eight. The four categories with appearances can be further divided into four related to outer appearances and four not related to outer appearances, making eight. The four categories without appearances can each be subdivided into shallow lucid clarity and deep lucid clarity, again making eight. Adding all that up makes sixteen [categories of lucid clarity]. For the disciples in whom experiences have dawned, identify these categories and explain them in detail. This will introduce the practitioners to the type of lucid clarity they have experienced. For the disciples who have not had experiences arise, or in a group of people with various levels of experience, it is sufficient just to name these sixteen divisions.

de ltar na bsre ba dang / mthar thug dang / rjes kyi chos lnga po 'di dag chos drug nang sel gyi 'od gsal gyis bcad du bsdus mod kyang / don la gtum mo/ sgyu lus/ rmi lam/ 'od gsal bzhi car gyi khrid bskyangs zin pa'i rjes nyams skyong ba'i khrid yin par shes so/ / rjes kyi chos 'di rnams la nyams len dmigs pa'i gnad gal che ba mang po 'dug kyang / phyis rim pas bsgom rgyu'i gdams ngag yin pas/ da lta 'phral khyer gyi dmigs skor du bcad pa ni mi mdzad pas/ chos thun mang nyung ji tsam byed skabs dang sbyar ro/ /

Although Blending, Ultimate Lucid Clarity, and the five concluding practices are included in the outline of Lucid Clarity, one of the Six Dharmas, in fact they should be understood as guides for sustaining the experiences after one has already applied the instructions of Fierce Inner Heat, Illusory Body, Dream, and Lucid Clarity. These concluding practices contain many important vital visualizations to take into practice. However, since they come last in the sequence as instructions in the meditation subjects, they are not included in the divisions of the visualization rounds for immediate use. Add them in however many teachings sessions are appropriate.

de ltar na de dag ni rtsa ba'i chos bzhi zhes kyang bya/ bsre ba sgyu lus zhes kyang bya ste/ bsre ba dang 'pho ba ces pa la/ rje mar pa lo tsA'i gdams ngag so so rnams na/ bsre ba'i rnam (84) gzhag mi 'dra ba mang po yod kyang 'dir mi 'chad/

These are called the four root dharmas, or Blending with Illusory Body. As for so-called Blending [and] Transference, there are many different categories of blending in the individual instructions of Lord Marpa the Translator that are not explained here.[26] {84}

gdams ngag 'di nyid kyi lugs la/ gong du bshad pa gsal stong bsre ba sogs bsre ba bzhi dang / gzhan yang bsre 'pho shes rab rnam bzhi'am rnam gsum zhes grags pa yin/ de la shes rab gsum ni/ log par shes pa'i shes rab/ kun rdzob shes pa'i shes rab/ don dam shes pa'i shes rab po/ /

In the tradition of this instruction, there are four types of blending, such as Blending Clarity and Emptiness. Further, there are what is known as the four or three wisdoms of Blending [and] Transference (bsre ’pho). The three wisdoms are the wisdom of mistaken wisdom, the wisdom of conventional wisdom, and the wisdom of ultimate wisdom.

de yang thabs khyad par can gyis bsgrubs pa'i bde ba chen po'i dbang du byas na/ dang por bde bar shar tsam na zag bcas chags pa'i blo gcig kyang 'dug pa de phyin ci log shes pa yin/ de rang sems sgyu ma lta bu'i bde bar shar ba de kun rdzob shes pa yin pas/ log pa de kun rdzob shes pa'i shes rab la bsre ba yin/ de yang bzo med dbyings su shar ba de don dam shes pa yin te/ kun rdzob de don dam shes pa'i shes rab la bsre ba yin/ gang shar thams cad kyi steng du dbyings shar de ngos bzung / de ye shes dang cir snang bsre ba yin/ des mtshon nas sad dus kyi snang ba bun long shar ba tsam 'di log pa'i shes pa/ de sgyu mar shar ba kun rdzob shes pa/ sgyu mar 'dzin pa dang bral ba'i rang 'gros de don dam shes pa/ de gang shar gyi steng du khyer ba de ye shes dang cir snang bsre ba'o/ /

In the context of the great bliss that is accomplished through special techniques, when at first there is a mere arising of bliss, an attitude of attachment to this dissipating experience distorts it. This is misguided knowledge. Then the bliss arises of one’s own mind like an illusion, which is the knowledge of conventional reality. That is the blending of the mistaken with the wisdom of knowledge of the conventional. The knowledge of the ultimate is the arising of the unfabricated experience of basic space. That is the blending of conventional knowledge with the wisdom of the ultimate knowledge. To recognize the arising of basic space directly in everything that arises is the blending of wisdom with any appearance. As that indicates, when just hazy appearances arise during waking hours, it is mistaken knowledge. When that arises as illusion, it is conventional knowledge. When there is natural freedom from fixating on that illusion, it is ultimate knowledge. When that is carried over to whatever arises, it is the blending of wisdom with any appearance.

yang rmi lam shar tsam de log pa/ de rmi lam dang sgyu mar shes pa kun rdzob/ sgyu 'dzin bral ba don dam/ de gnyid sad sogs kun tu khyer ba de ye shes dang cir snang bsre ba'o/ / gnyid 'thug po dran med du thibs song ba de log pa/ de la bde gsal du dran pa sleb pa de kun rdzob/ de rang bzhin bzo med du 'dug pa don dam/ des sad dus dang rmi lam la rgyas thebs pa de ye shes dang cir snang dbyer med do/ /

Similarly, when a lucid dream merely arises, it is mistaken; when you know that dream as illusion, it is conventional; and not fixating on that illusion is ultimate knowledge. When that is carried over into sleep, waking, and all states, it is the blending of timeless awareness with whatever appears. When you fall into unconsciousness in deep sleep, it is mistaken; when there is recollection of bliss and clarity within that, it is conventional; and when that remains naturally unfabricated, it is ultimate knowledge. When that seals the times of waking and dream, it is the inseparability of timeless awareness and whatever appears. {85}

shes rab bzhir phyed pa ltar na ye shes (85) cir snang dbyer med la/ zung 'jug shes pa'i shes rab ces ming 'dogs/ sgyu lus rmi lam skabs kyi rang shar lha sku ni kun rdzob don dam zung 'jug gsum ka'i cha ru yong gsung / yang thabs lam gyi bde ba sgyu lus dang bsre/ 'od gsal gyi bde stong rmi lam dang bsre/ sgyu lus dang rmi lam phan tshun du bsre zhes kyang gsung ste/ bsre ba'i don dbyer med du lam du khyer ba'i don lags pas so/ /

According to this classification of the four wisdoms, the inseparability of timeless awareness and whatever appears is termed the “wisdom of the knowledge of unity.” It is said that the self-arising deity’s form during Illusory Body and Dream has aspects of all three: conventional, ultimate, and unity. More blendings have also been taught: the blending of the bliss of the Path of Methods [Fierce Inner Heat] with Illusory Body, the blending of the bliss-emptiness of Lucid Clarity with Dream, and the blending back and forth of Illusory Body and Dream. Thus the meaning of blending is to integrate inseparably [two or more practices] on the path.

gzhan yang bsre ba'i gzhi gnas thabs bshad na/ skabs 'dir 'di dag go dgos te/ 'khor ba pa rnams kyi 'khrul pa thams cad bsdu na bzhi ste/ gnyid sad dus dang / gnyid 'thug po dang / rmi lam dang / gnyis sbyor gyi chags rtog ste bzhi po der 'dus/ bzhi po de gzhi chos dbyings kyi sku gsung thugs bde ba chen po bzhi la sgrib pa yin/ lam gyi ye shes snang stong dang / rig stong dang / gsal stong dang / bde stong bzhi pos rim gyis sgrib pa de rnams sel ba yin/ 'di'i skabs kyi rig stong ni mi rtog pa la zer/ de dag gi gtso bo yang rim pas/ sgyu lus dang / 'od gsal dang / rmi lam dang / gtum mo rnams yin/ de rnams bsgoms pa las 'bras bu mthar thug ni/ sprul sku/ chos sku/ longs sku/ bde chen gyi sku ste/ sku bzhi mngon du 'gyur ro/ /

Furthermore, if we are to explain the ground, abiding, and methods of blending, at this point the following must be understood. All delusion of samsaric beings can be subsumed into four states: waking, deep sleep, dreaming, and the passion of intercourse. Those four states obscure awakened body, speech, mind, and great bliss of the realm of phenomena [at the time of] the ground. Four timeless awarenesses on the path will dispel those obscurations: appearance-emptiness, awareness-emptiness, clarity-emptiness, and bliss-emptiness, respectively. In this context, awareness-emptiness is called nonthought. The primary practices [to remove those obscurations and develop those awarenesses] are, in order, Illusory Body, Lucid Clarity, Dream, and Fierce Inner Heat. The ultimate result of meditating on those is the actualization of nirmāṇakāya, dharmakāya, saṃbhogakāya, and sukhakāya.

yang ye shes lnga dang sbyor na/ sgyu lus me long lta bu/ 'od gsal mnyam pa nyid/ rmi lam so sor rtog pa/ gtum mo chos kyi dbyings kyi ye shes sgrub pa'i lam yin gsung bar thams cad 'dra la/ bya grub ni chos bzhi car gyi 'bras bu spyi la sbyor gsung ba dang / sor rtog bya grub gnyis kar kyi lam la sbyor gsung ba'ang 'dug ste man ngag gsung rgyun las/ (86) las rgya bya grub kyi lam du 'chad/ 'on kyang thams cad mi 'gal lo/ /

If those are correlated with the five types of timeless awareness, Illusory Body is the path to accomplish mirror-like awareness, Lucid Clarity is for equanimity awareness, Dream is for discriminating awareness, and Fierce Inner Heat is the timeless awareness of accomplishment of activities. Everyone agrees on those. As for the accomplishment of activities, it is taught that it corresponds in general to all four results, and it is also taught that both discriminating awareness and accomplishment of activities apply to Dream. {86} But in the teaching continuity of esoteric instructions, karmamudrā is explained as the path of accomplishment of activities. But there is no contradiction.
lnga pa
E. Transference, Buddhahood without Meditation
'pho ba ma bsgoms sangs rgyas la/ gzhung gi 'pho ba dang / lhan thabs kyi man ngag gnyis yod pa las/
Transference of consciousness, which enables buddhahood without meditation, has two parts: (1) Transference according to the source texts and (2) a supplementary esoteric instruction.
dang po la/
1. Transference in the Source Texts
gzhung las/ chos sku de bzhin nyid kyi 'pho ba/ zung 'jug yi dam gyi 'pho ba/ byin rlabs bla ma'i 'pho ba/ 'chug med mkha' spyod kyi 'pho ba'o/ /

First, from the sources, there are four parts: (1) Transference in the Suchness of Dharmakāya, (2) Transference in the Union with the Yidam, (3) Transference in the Blessings of the Guru, and (4) Transference to the Unerring Celestial Realm.
dang po ni/
a. Transference in the Suchness of Dharmakāya

'chi ba 'od gsal lam bu ngo 'phrod na/ gzhan rnams la 'chi srid 'byung rgyu de/ rnal 'byor pa la 'od gsal bde stong du rang shar bas gong 'pho ba'i gdams ngag la ma ltos te/ dus de nyid du rang grol ba'o/ / 'di la dmigs pa logs pa med pas dmigs skor la mi bgrang ngo / /

At death, when mother and child lucid clarity meet, there is no more cause for any further deaths and existences. Since the bliss and emptiness of lucid clarity arises naturally to the yogin, they do not depend on the instructions of Transference above. They will be naturally liberated right then and there. There is no separate visualization here, so it is not counted as a round of visualization.
Session 51
gnyis pa zung 'jug yi dam gyi 'pho ba ni/
b. Transference in the Union with the Yidam
sngon 'gro rnams sngar sgyu lus skabs dang 'dra ba las/ bar dor sangs rgya ba mdzad du gsol/ zhes gsol 'debs kyi mtha' bsgyur ba tsam gyi khyad par ro/ /
The preliminaries are the same as in the section on Illusory Body, except that the last line of the supplication is changed to “Please bless me with buddhahood in the intermediate state.”

rang lhar gsal ba'i spyi bo'i steng gi nam mkha' la rang gang mos pa'i yi dam de bsgom gsung / spyir de ltar yin yang nges khrigs ma byas na/ mi blun po'i yi dam la tshad gzung mi yong bas/ skabs 'dir 'khor lo sdom pa'am/ dgyes mdzad gang rung cig rang gi spyi bo'i mda' gang tsam gyi steng gi nam mkha' la bsgom/ rang gi lus kyi dbus su dbu ma kha dog dkar ba sngar bshad pa rnams dang 'dra ba la/ mar sna gsang bar zug pa kha zum pa/ yar sna spyi bo tshangs bug la reg pa/ skyi bo tshangs bug de dbu ma'i kha dang rgya khyon mnyam pa/ rgya mthongs kha bye ba bzhin du skya thal le yod pa cig bsgom/ dbu ma'i nang lte bar rang sems a dkar po dang / mas snar yi dam gyi sa bon hU~M sngon po (87) rlung gi rang bzhin cig gsal btab/

With yourself as the deity, meditate on whatever yidam you like in the space above your head. Though that is what is generally said, if it is not fixed, a foolish person’s yidam will not be well calculated. Therefore, on this occasion, meditate on either Cakrasaṃvara or Hevajra at a distance of one arrow’s length above your head. In the center of your body is the white central channel as it was described previously. The lower end reaches the perineum and is closed; the upper end touches the cranial aperture with its open end the same width as that of the aperture. Meditate on it as light and transparent, like an open skylight. Inside the central channel, clearly imagine your own mind as a white A at the navel, and the yidam’s seed syllable at the lower end, a blue hūṃ that is the nature of vital winds. {87}

de mtshams rlung ro bsal nas 'jam rlung bag tsam bzung / lte ba'i a dang gsang ba'i hU~M la sems drag tu gtad/ yang rlung phyir bsal ba'i dus/ kha nas 'bud na hig ring po dang / sna nas 'bud na hU~M ring byed dam sgra med kyi tshul gyis rlung shugs bkyed de bsal/ de skabs mas sna'i hU~M shugs dang ldan pa des lte ba'i a yang khyer te/ yi ge nyis brtsegs de dbu ma'i lam nas brgyud/ spyi gtsug tshangs pa'i bu ga nas rgyangs ter thon te yi dam gyi thugs kar sleb/ der gang yang mi bsam par dran med thabs su cung zad bzhag / skabs der rlung yang rang babs so/ /

At that point, clear away the dead air and hold the gentle breathing for a while. Concentrate intently on the A at the navel and the hūṃ at the perineum. Again as you exhale, make the sound of a long hrīk if you expel from the mouth or a long hūṃ if you expel from the nose, or don’t make any sound as you forcefully clear out the vital winds. At that point, the hūṃ at the lower end is forceful and carries the navel A upward. The two stacked letters travel up through the central channel and shoot far out of the cranial aperture, reaching the yidam’s heart. At that point, rest awhile in the way of no recollection without thinking of anything at all. In that situation, the vital winds will also fall naturally.

de lta bu bskyar gyin lan bdun tsam bsgom/ de rjes yi dam gyi thugs ka nas yi ge nyis brtseg thur la rgyang gis byung / spyi bo nas zhugs dbu ma'i lam nas brgyud te song / a yig lte bar bsngad/ hU~M yig gsang bar song ste ljid dang ldan par bsam/ dmigs pa thun chung gcig go /de ltar yang yang bsgom/ thun 'jog khar yig 'bru gnyis po sngar bzhin mar phab pa'i rjes la/ yi dam 'od du zhu nas rang la thim/ hU~M sngon po las 'phros pa'i 'od kyi kha gcod lta bus spyi bo'i tshangs bug 'grig por bkag par bsam/ de nyid 'pho ba'i rtags byung byung gi bar du bsgom/ de nas kyang nyin rer dmigs pa lan re tsam bsgom mo/ / dmigs skor nga gcig pa'o/ /

In this way, meditate repeatedly some seven times. Afterward, the two stacked letters fall downward from the yidam’s heart and enter your crown, traveling down the central channel. The A letter stays at the navel, and the hūṃ goes to the perineum. Imagine that they both become heavy. That is one short session of visualization. Meditate that way again and again. At the end of the session, after the two syllable letters have descended as before, the yidam melts into light and dissolves into you. Think that light radiating from the blue hūṃ becomes like a cover that firmly blocks the cranial aperture. Meditate in this way until the signs of successful transference begin to emerge. Then just meditate once on the visualization each day. This is the fifty-first round of visualization.
Session 52
gsum pa byin rlabs bla ma'i 'pho ba ni/
c. Transference in the Blessings of the Guru

sngon 'gro snga ma dang 'dra/ dngos gzhi'i skabs su yang rtsa dbu ma sngar bzhin bsgom/ dbu ma'i nang lte bar thig le dkar po gsung ba dang / ser po gsung ba sogs ci rigs yod kyang / lag len du (88) dkar la ser ba'i mdangs chags pa 'od 'phro ba/ nor bu ke ke ru dang 'dra ba/ zlum zhing 'gril ba bongs tshod sran rdog tsam cig gsal 'debs/ rlung sbyor yang snga ma dang 'dra/ thig le dkar ser de spyi gtsug nas yar rgyang thon te/ bla ma'i thugs kar thim/ de ltar dmigs pa bskyar gyin lan bdun song ba na/ mar 'bebs pa'i dmigs pa byed te/ lte bar thig le ljid dang ldan pa nyams bde ba cig bsgom/ de lta bu thun chung gcig ste de nyid bskyar gyin bsgom/ thun 'jog khar rlung sems lte bar phab pa'i rjes su/ bla ma la mos gus dung ba byas pas bla ma 'od du zhu/ spyi gtsug tshangs pa'i bu ga nas zhugs te thim pas lus sems bde bas khyab/ spyi bo tshangs pa'i bu ga de yang thig le dkar po gcig gis bkag par bsam/ tshul de lta bur rtags byung byung bsgom/ de ltar 'pho ba de gnyis ka la yang las la sbyor ba'i skabs/ yar 'pho ba 'ba' zhig bsgom gyi mar 'bebs pa mi dgos la/ thun mtshams su sgo bgag pa yang mi dgos so/ / dmigs skor nga gnyis pa'o/ /

The preliminaries are the same as before. In the main practice, also meditate as before on the central channel. It is taught that within the central channel there is a white vital drop at the navel. It is also said that it is yellow or whatever. {88} But in practice, it is white with a yellow radiance and radiates light, like a karketana gem (chrysoberyl). Visualize it as round and rolled up, the size of a pea. Apply the breathing technique as before. That white-yellow drop projects far out of the crown of your head and dissolves into the guru’s heart. After repeating this whole visualization seven times, do the visualization of the drop descending. Meditate on that drop resting in the navel, heavy, with an experience of bliss. That constitutes one short session. Meditate repeatedly on just that. At the end of the session, after the wind-mind falls to the navel, your loving devotion to the guru causes the guru to melt into light. It enters your cranial aperture and dissolves, filling your body and mind with bliss. Think that a white drop also blocks the cranial aperture on the crown of your head. Meditate in that way until showing signs of success. When applying those two methods of transference [at death], meditate only on the ascending transference [of the drop]. You won’t need the return descent, and you also won’t need to block the opening when the session ends. This is the fifty-second round of visualization.
bzhi pa 'chug med mkha' spyod kyi 'pho ba ni/
d. Transference to the Unerring Celestial Realm

spyir dkyus kyi man ngag gi sdebs yin kyang shin tu bka' gnyan ces gsung nas bka' rgya can du mdzad te tshogs su mi gsung / de bas na logs su shes par bya'o/ / dkyus kyi sa bcad kyis bsdus pa ma yin kyang / ye shes mkha' 'gro ma nyid kyi gsung 'pho ba bsdus pa gzhan yang rigs lnga tsam yod do/ /

In general, this is included in the lineup of esoteric instructions. However, it is said to be a severely restricted precept and so has been sealed, not to be taught in a group. Therefore, you must learn it from another source. The Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness herself taught five other methods subsumed in the subject of Transference, but they are not part of the regular outline.
gnyis pa lhan thabs kyi man ngag ni/
2. Supplementary Esoteric Instructions

skabs 'dir/ gzhung nas 'pho ba mang po bshad kyang / lag len ye shes skar khung ma la byed gsung / gzhung 'pho rnams la'ang lag len ye mi mdzad pa yin mod/ (89) 'di la phyag len gtso cher mang du 'debs pa la dgongs pa'o/ / 'di la sbyang ba dang las la sbyar ba gnyis yod/

Now, there are many explanations of Transference in the source texts, but in practice it is taught that one should practice the Skylight of Timeless Awareness (ye shes skar khung ma). Of course, this is not because those original Transference methods were never practiced {89} but rather in consideration of the many practitioners who made this their main practice. There are two parts here: (1) the training and (2) the applications.
Session 53
dang po sbyang ba ni/
a. Training

sngon 'gro sngar dang 'dra/ bla ma 'od du zhu nas rang la thim pa'i rjes su/ rang lus lha sku khong stong du bsam/ rtsa dbu ma yang yi dam gyi 'pho ba'i skabs su bshad pa bzhin bsgom/ dbu ma'i nang lte ba'i thad du chos 'byung gru gsum dkar po/ / rtsa ba phra ba thur bstan/ gdengs ka gyen bstan/ zur gcig mdun la bstan pa/ rgyab gzhung gi ngos la logs gcig bstan par bsgom/ de'i dbus su rten gang la yang ma reg pa'i a yig dkar po/ sran chung ngam/ yungs 'bru'i tshad tsam gsal 'debs/ tshad che chung ma gtogs chos 'byung dang a yig gi bzhugs tshul stong ra'i skabs dang 'dra/

The preliminaries are the same as before. After the guru melts into light and dissolves into you, imagine your body becomes the empty hollow form of the deity. Meditate on the central channel as described in the yidam Transference. Inside the central channel, meditate on a white tetrahedral source of phenomena at the level of the navel. The fine tip faces downward, while the wide-open part faces upward with one vertex facing the front and the back surface [between the other two vertices] aligned with the back. Within that is the white letter A, situated without touching any support. Imagine it clearly the size of a small pea or a mustard seed. Other than the size, the rest of the visualization of the source of phenomena and the white A letter is the same as in the purifying inner space preliminary practice.

de rjes rlung ro bsal/ rlung bum can shugs drag po yun thung tsam cig bzung / lte ba'i a la sems drag tu gtad/ rlung bzung ba'i ngang de ka nas lto ba tshigs pa'i phyogs la cung zad bcer tsam dang / a dkar po de 'phar tsam byung nas yang sngar shul du bsdad/ de bas cung shugs che bas bcer ba na/ yang sngar las mtho tsam 'phar ba las sngar gyi sar bsdad/ yang de 'phral skad cig la drag tu bcer te thub tshad du bsdad pas/ rlung stod du khong gis 'gril yong / dmigs pa chos 'byung gi kha thag gis brdabs pas/ de'i rlung gis bdas pa bzhin du rang sems a dkar po de mda' 'phangs pa bzhin du dbu ma'i lam brgyud spyi bo tshangs bug nas thon/ nam mkha' la ye re re song / dbyings mthon po mthon por sleb nas nam mkha' la yas par bsams te/ dbyings dang nam mkha' rig pa gsum dbyer med du 'dres pa la (90) had de bzhag / dmigs pa de lta bu bskyar gyin lan bdun tsam bsgom/ yang 'bebs pa ni nam mkha'i dbus su a dkar po cig lam te grub/ de mar babs spyi bo tshangs bug nas zhugs/ dbu ma'i nang nas mar lam lam lam dal bus babs/ lte ba'i chos 'byung gi dbus su brtan cing brjid dang ldan pa'i tshul gyis sbring nge 'dug par bsam/ de thun chung gcig yin/

Exhale the dead air and then hold the vase breath forcefully for a short time. Focus intently on the white A. While holding the breath, slightly squeeze your belly toward your spine. The white A lifts up a bit and then returns to its former place. When you squeeze a little harder, it rises higher than before, and again comes to rest in its place. Then suddenly squeeze as hard as you can for an instant, forcing the vital winds to concentrate in the upper body. Visualize that the sides of the source of phenomena strike each other, which causes your mind as the white A to shoot up like an arrow through the central channel as if chased by the winds. It comes out of the cranial aperture and continues high into the sky. As it reaches higher and higher into space, imagine that it vanishes into the sky. Space, sky, and awareness—these three blend inseparably. {90} Rest openly just there. Do that visualization again and again, some seven times. Then, for the descent, a white A suddenly appears in the middle of the sky. It falls down through your cranial aperture and descends slowly down the path of the central channel. It lands in the center of the source of phenomena in the navel and remains there in its proper place, firm and heavy. This constitutes a single short session.

de ltar yang yang bsgom/ thun chen re'i nang du thun chung de'ang nyer gcig gam/ bcu gcig gam/ bdun tsam re byed/ de lta bu'i thun bzhi'am drug sogs byas na rtags myur du 'ong ste/ rtsol ba che chung gi rim pas zhag bdun nam/ zla phyed dam/ zla gcig tsam la rtags rab 'bring tha ma gsum gang rung cig 'byung bar the tshom med do/ /

Meditate in this way again and again. In each long session there should be twenty-one or eleven or seven such short sessions. Practicing that way in four or six or so sessions a day will quickly bring the signs of success. There is no doubt that the relative best, middling, or least signs will occur in a week, or two weeks, or a month, depending on your degree of effort.

de yang rtags rab spyi bo 'bur ba brdol te chu ser sogs byung na'ang yin/ dmigs pa btang res kyi ltag pa'i rtsa gnyis rengs shing / mig sprid chil ba dang / dran med du 'gro tshad pa byung na yin/ 'bring ni spyi bo 'bur ba tsam dang / mdun rtse chung gi rtsa rgyangs pa lta bu'o/ tha ma spyi bo za zhing 'gul la 'khyigs pa 'ong / des mi yong gong ma gnyis gang rung gcig rang dgos gsung / dmigs pa gsal shos cig la 'di bsgom tsam na yun ring du dran med du brgyal ba 'byung ste/ de la rin po che'i snod byang mas spyi gtsug bkab na/ thal ba'i nyes pa mi 'byung gsung / 'on kyang de 'dra'i rigs la tshigs pa brdung ba dang 'bebs kyis phab na legs so/ /

The best sign is a lump swelling up on the top of your head, oozing pus from there, and so forth. Also, each time you do the visualization, if the two tendons in the back of the head stiffen, the eyes feel numb, or you become unconscious, these are also signs. The middling sign is just the lump on the head and, in front, something like the [neck] arteries stiffening. The least sign will be itching and pulsating on the top of the head. If these signs do not appear, it is said that you should do one of the two visualizations above. If you faint into unconsciousness for a long time by just meditating on the visualization that is the most clear, it is taught that covering your head with a bowl made of precious materials will prevent the problem of passing away. However, for this kind of problem it is best to strike your joints and do the forceful drop yogic exercises (’bebs).

de ltar rtags byung nas nyin re bzhin dmigs pa tshar re bsgom dgos/ spyir da lta 'pho bas rtsa lam 'byongs na/ nam zhig 'chi tshe 'pho ba'i gsal 'debs med kyang / (91) sngar rtsa sgo bye zhing rtsa lam byang ba de nyid nas phal cher 'gro yang re re tsam ma nges pa las gsal 'debs byung na 'chug pa med/ sgom 'phro bzhag nas yun ring lon na/ dgos dus gsal mi thebs pa yang srid pas/ da lta sbyangs pa'i rgyun mi nyams pa'i phyir thun re bsgom pa yin/ lhag ma sgyu lus sogs bsgom pa khe che'o/ /

Once the signs have arisen, you should meditate on each visualization once a day. In general, if you refine the channel path through practicing Transference now, even if the transference visualization is not clear at the time of death, one can usually project out through the channel path since it was opened and cleared previously. However, it is not sure whether that will work every time, so better if there is a clear visualization to effect an infallible [transition]. If you set aside your interest in this meditation and a long time passes, it’s possible that clarity will not arrive in the hour of your need. Therefore, in order to keep the continuity of training undiminished, this is a meditation for [a once daily] session. The remaining sessions should involve important meditations such as those of Illusory Body.
las la sbyar ba ni
b. Application

sngar bshad pa dang 'dra ste/ myur du 'chi ba'i rtags nges pa can byung na/ yo byad la ma chags par bya/ rang gang mos pa la mchod 'bul dang / sbyin gtong byed/ khon dang sel yod pa rnams la dngos dang brgyud pa'i sgo nas bshags sbyang bya/ nye du sogs la chags pa'i blo spangs te/ 'brel thag bcad nas bsgom dgos so/ / 'dir rdzas kyi 'pho ba'ang bshad pa 'grub na ni legs/ med ka med ni min no/ / dmigs skor nga gsum pa'o/ /

This is the same as described before. When sure signs of imminent death arrive, do not be attached to your property. Offer it to whomever inspires you and donate to charity. Acknowledge and repair any grudges or exclusions that you [have created], in person or indirectly. Relinquish the attitude of attachment to those close to you. You must cut the ties of connection and meditate. At this point, there is also an explanation of transference using substances, which is good to practice but not indispensable. This is the fifty-third round of visualization.

de yan chad la gtum mo'i skabs su rtsa dbu ma dmar por bsgom/ gzhan rnams la'ang phyi dkar nang dmar sogs khrid yig rnams su mi 'dra ba ci rigs bshad kyang lag len du dkar po kho na mdzad/ ye shes skar khung ma la chos 'byung gi stabs dbu ma cung zad sbom par bsgom dgos/ thig le dbang bzhi'i gnad la'ang de dang 'dra/ chos 'byung yang phyi dkar nang dmar sogs ci rigs bshad mod te/ bar do'i skabs ma gtogs/ chos drug gzhung gi dmigs pa'i chos 'byung thams cad dkar po kho nar mdzad pa zhal rgyun yin/ thabs lam dang 'od gsal gyi skabs na lus thams cad dbu mas khyab par bsgom lugs re yig rnying kun na bshad mod kyang / las dang po pa'i skabs na de rang phan chung mi dgos gsung ste khrid kyi (92) dkyus la mi mdzad do/ /

Regarding everything up to this point, in Fierce Inner Heat practice you meditate on the central channel as red. For all the other practices, it is described in different ways in the many other guidebooks, such as white on the outside and red on the inside, and so forth. But in actual practice it is exclusively white. In the Skylight of Timeless Awareness practice, you need to meditate on the central channel as slightly wider when the source of phenomena is within it. It is the same in the Vital Points of the Four Empowerments of Drops. Of course, there is the explanation of the source of phenomena as white outside and red inside and so forth as appropriate. But other than the occasion of the Intermediate Stage, in the visualizations of the source texts for the other Six Dharmas, it is the oral tradition to always make the source of phenomena white. During the Path of Methods and Lucid Clarity, there is the custom of meditating on the whole body pervaded by the central channel, as described in all the old books. However, for beginners, this won’t actually bring much benefit, so it is said to be unnecessary, and was not mentioned in the course of instruction. {92}
drug pa bar do rgyal ba longs sku ni
F. Intermediate State, the Victors’ Saṃbhogakāya

['di] rnam pa bzhi ste/ rab bar do dang po'i 'od gsal chos sku rang shar/ 'bring rgyal ba longs sku rang shar/ tha ma sprul sku 'gag med rang shar/ spyir gnad 'chug med kyi gdams ngag ste/ sa bcad bzhi yod la/

This has four parts: (1) the Natural Arising of Dharmakāya in the Lucid Clarity of the First Intermediate State for the best, (2) the Natural Arising of the Victors’ Saṃbhogakāya for the average, (3) the Natural Arising of Unrestricted Nirmāṇakāya for the lesser, and (4) instructions of general unerring vital points.
de'i dang po ni/
1. The Natural Arising of Dharmakāya in the Lucid Clarity of the First Intermediate State for the Best

gong 'pho bya 'pho byed dang bral ba dang don gcig ste/ de yang bar do dang po ces pa ni/ 'od gsal ma bu 'dres pa'i ye shes 'chi sems bde stong 'od gsal du gnas gyur pa de yin te/ bar do'i dang por byung bas so/ / de la 'chi ba chos sku zhes bya/ de las langs pa na tha mal pa rnams la bar do 'byung ba'i dod la lha sku sgyu ma lta bu rang shar du 'byung ba de la 'od gsal rang shar zer/ 'od gsal las rang shar ba'i go ba yin no/ / de yang sad dus su bde stong dang lha sku rgyun mi 'chad/ gnyid 'thug po thams cad 'od gsal du chug / rmi lam gyi rtsal spyod zad pa yang med la dag snang lha sku rang shar ba'i gang zag de la bar do dang po'i 'od gsal rang shar chos sku 'di 'byung ba yin no/ / 'di la dmigs pa logs pa med/ skabs 'dir de dag gi rnam gzhag rgyas par 'chad 'dod na/ chos thun gcig gnyis sogs ji ltar 'os pa byed/

This carries the same meaning as previous descriptions of the absence of something transferred or a transferring agent. The first intermediate state refers to the timeless awareness arising in the merging of mother and child lucid clarity when the mind at death transforms into the lucid clarity of empty bliss, since that arises during the first intermediate state. That is called the dharmakāya of death. When one arises from that state, instead of continuing through the intermediate states of ordinary individuals, the deity’s form arises by itself like an illusion. That is called the natural arising of lucid clarity, but it should be understood as the natural arising from lucid clarity. Those who have experienced the empty bliss and deity’s form without interruption during waking hours and entered lucid clarity at all times in deep sleep, even if they have not finished the energy training of Dream, may have this natural arising of the pure vision of the deity’s form. This is an individual to whom the dharmakāya arises naturally in the lucid clarity of the first intermediate state. There is no separate visualization connected with this section. If you wish to explain these subjects in detail, do so in one or two or however many teachings sessions is suitable.
Session 54
gnyis pa 'bring rgyal ba longs sku rang shar ni/
2. The Natural Arising of the Victors’ Saṃbhogakāya for the Average

sngon 'gro babs sgyu lus dang 'dra ba las/ bar do longs sku thob par mdzad du gsol ces mtha' bsgyur/ bla ma rang la thim pa'i rjes su/ rang dang snang ba thams cad la bltas te/ srid pa bar do dngos yin snyam pa'i 'dun pa yang drag po sbyangs/ 'gro drug 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal dang / chags sdang nyon mongs kyi nyes dmigs dran pa'i skyo shas drag po yang bya/ bar do'i skabs 'dir/ 'khrul na 'khrul tshabs (93) che ste chags sdang gi rnam rtog re res kyang skad cig la dmyal bar yang bskyur rung / lam bsgoms na grol tshabs kyang che ste/ da ltas da dus su lo zlar bsgoms pa las kyang / 'dir dar cig re bsgoms pa yang bogs dang chod che ba yin/ da nyon mongs kyi dbang du mi gtong bar ma 'khrul ba cig byed dgos/ bla mas gnang ba'i rgyal ba longs sku bsgom par bya snyam du bsam/

The preliminaries stay the same as in Illusory Body, except that the last line of the supplication is changed to “May I attain saṃbhogakāya in the intermediate state.” After the guru dissolves into you, regard yourself and all appearances. Train intensively with the thought “This is really the intermediate state of becoming.” Cultivate strong disillusionment as well by recollecting the sufferings of the six kinds of migrators in cyclic existence and the shortcomings of afflictive desire and anger. {93} Contemplate this, thinking, “In this situation of the intermediate state, if there is delusion, it is really strong delusion; each thought of desire or anger can instantly turn into hell. Although meditation [during the time of] the path also brings powerful liberation, now a single moment of meditation here is more effective and enriching than months and years of meditation during waking life. Now I must not be deluded and fall under the power of afflictive emotions. I will meditate on the saṃbhogakāya of the victors as given me by my guru.”

stong pa'i ngang las rang gi mdun du chos 'byung sngon po rtsa ba phra zhing gdengs kha gyen du bstan pa cig bsgom/ 'di rang bzhin ma rtogs pa rnams la ma'i mngal du 'dug / rtogs pa rnams la 'og min chos kyi pho brang rang yin ang snyam du bsam par bya/

From within emptiness, a blue source of phenomena appears before you. Its tip is pointed down and its wide opening faces upward. Think, “To those without natural realization, this is the mother’s womb. To those with realization, surely this is the actual palace of the Unsurpassed Pure Land (Akaniṣṭha).”

de nas rang nyid de'i dbus su phyin/ rang sems hU~M yig sngon po che zhing 'od 'bar ba cig tu gyur/ de las 'od 'phros chos 'byung la phog / 'das pa'i mngal skyes kyi lan chags dang bag chags thams cad sbyangs/ da ltar ba'i mngal skyes kyi las thams cad kyang dag / ma 'ongs pa skye bar 'gyur ba'i sgo bkag / skye gnas gzhan gsum gyi bag chags rnams zhor la rang dag par bsam/ bar do yin ang snyam hU~M de yongs su gyur pa las rang skad cig gis 'khor lo bde mchog lhan skyes su bsgom/ bar do yin ang snyam spyi bor gdan bzhi rdzogs kyi steng du bla ma bsgom/ bar do'i skabs 'dir longs sku thob par mdzad du gsol/ / zhes rtse gcig tu gsol ba btab/ de ltar dmigs pa sgom pa'i skabs thams cad du bar do rang yin snyam pa'i 'dun pa rgyun chags gal che/ dmigs skor nga bzhi pa'o/ /

Then you yourself arrive in its center. Your mind becomes the blue letter hūṃ, large and blazing with light. The light rays radiating from it strike the source of phenomena. Imagine that all the habitual patterns and karmic debts of your previous womb birth are purified. Similarly, all karma for womb birth is purified, and the doors to future births are blocked. The habitual patterns of the three other places of birth are consequently self-purified. With the thought “This is surely the intermediate state,” meditate that the hūṃ is completely transformed and you instantly become Coemergent Cakrasaṃvara. Thinking, “This is surely the intermediate state,” meditate on the guru upon a four-tiered seat on your head. Supplicate with single-pointed focus: “Please let me obtain the saṃbhogakāya now in this intermediate state.” It is important to constantly develop the intentionality of thinking, “This is actually the intermediate state” at all times while meditating with this visualization. This is the fifty-fourth round of visualization.
Session 55
gsum pa tha ma sprul sku 'gag med rang shar ni/
3. The Natural Arising of Unrestricted Nirmāṇakāya for the Lesser

dmigs pa snga ma de rdzogs par bsgoms (94) nas/ de'i steng du 'di bsnan te/ 'di thams cad bar do yin snang ba 'di bsgyur bar bya'o snyam pas/ gzugs su snang tshad 'khor lo sdom pa'i skur bsgyur dgos snyam pa byas tsa na/ thams cad he ru ka yab yum du khrong khrong song / sgra grags tshad sngags yi ge bdun pa lta bu gcig tu bsgyur snyam pa byas tsa na/ sngags de nyid du 'ur 'ur byung / bde sdug chags sdang sogs yid dran rtog yul dang bcas pa thams cad sgyu ma lta bu rmi lam lta bu zhes nyin par drag tu bsgom/ rmi lam shar ba na de nyid du sgyur ba gsum po dran par byas pa tsam gyis nyon mongs sdug bsngal thams cad las rang grol bar 'gyur ro/ /

Add this one after completing meditation on the previous visualization. {94} Think, “This is all the intermediate state; I can change all this appearance.” As soon as you think all appearing form is the body of Cakrasaṃvara, everything stands up as the Heruka couple. As soon as you think of changing the entire range of sound into something like the seven-syllable mantra, that mantra itself resounds. During the day, meditate intently on all mental thoughts and memories—happiness and sadness, desire and anger, and so forth—as like illusion and dream. When dreams come up, merely recalling those three transformations will release you from all afflictions and sufferings. [This is the fifty-fifth round of visualization.]
Session 56
bzhi pa spyi gnad 'chugs med ni/
4. General Unerring Vital Points
