skabs 'dir bla ma phal cher 'di skad gsung ste/ 'dir dbang po tha ma'i yang tha ma ces spyi gnad 'chugs med dbang po dman pa'i nyams len gyi dbang du byas nas/ bshad ma thag pa sprul sku 'gag med kyi dmigs pa yongs rdzogs kho na bsgom pa'i steng du/ 'di snon par mdzad pa 'ba' zhig 'dug ste/ lar bar do'i dmigs pa phyi ma gsum po rkang tshugs pa gsum ma yin/ snga ma snga ma la phyi ma phyi ma bsnan pa'o/ / zhes gsung ngo / / phyogs gcig nas de ltar yin mod kyang / de kho nar byas na spyi gnad 'chugs med ces pa'i spyi sgra nus med du 'gro bas/ dmigs pa 'di dbang po 'bring gi nyams len la yang snon dgos pa srid/ tha ma'i nyams len la yang snon dgos ces pa'i don du snang zhing / de ltar na bar do rang dbang po rab 'bring gsum gyi nyams len du 'dus pas/ dbang po bzhi pa'i rnam gzhag mi dgos par mngon la/ tha ma yig gi mchan bu dang / tshig gsal du'ang / (95) spyi gnad 'chugs med gsung ba ma gtogs/ dbang po'i rim pa dang sbyar ba med do/ / des na 'bring dang tha ma'i dmigs pa gang ltar yang rung ste/ dmigs pa 'di bsnan te bsgoms na 'chugs pa med ces pa'i don yin par snang ngo / /

On this subject most gurus say, “This is for the least of the lesser. These general infallible vital points, in terms of being a practice for those of the lowest capability, are explained immediately after fully completing the visualizations of unimpeded nirmāṇakāya, and exclusively as an addition to that meditation. Moreover, the last three Intermediate State visualizations do not stand on their own, but they are each added to the previous one.” From one point of view, this is certainly true. However, if it is only taken in that way, then the name “general unerring vital points” loses its meaning. It is possible that this visualization should be added to the practices for the average practitioner. But to say it should also be added to the practice for those of lesser capability also makes sense. Since the teachings on the Intermediate State are subsumed into practices for highest, average, and lesser capabilities, there is actually no need to posit a fourth level. {95} The notes and clarification in The Inventory and the Clarification only mention general infallible vital points but do not connect it with the levels of capability. Therefore, it is appropriate as a visualization for either average or lesser. Meditating on this added visualization seems to give meaning to the term unerring (chugs med).
ji skad du/ bla ma yi dam sgyu lus gsum/ / 'bral ba med par lam du khyer/ / bar do'i 'jigs pa chen po la/ / 'chugs pa med pa'i man ngag gces/ / zhes pa ltar/
As it is said: Guru, yidam, and illusory body; integrate these three constantly. For the great fears of intermediate state, unerring esoteric instructions are crucial.[27]

bar do'i 'dun pa drag pho dang bcas pas/ spyir 'gro ba rigs drug gi nang nas skye 'gro pho thams cad dang / khyad par du zhe sdang skye ba'i yul thams cad rang nyid gnas pa'i chos 'byung gi g.yas zur phyogs su 'khod par bsgom/ mchod pa bzhi rdzogs su phul nas/ bar dor longs sku thob par mdzad du gsol/ zhes bya/ yang 'gro ba rigs drug tu gtogs pa'i sems can mo thams cad dang / khyad par 'dod chags skye ba'i yul thams cad chos 'byung gi g.yon zur bu 'khod par bsgom/ mchod pa bzhi rdzogs su phul nas/ bar dor longs sku thob par mdzad du gsol/ ces gsol ba btab/ slar yang bla ma'i mos gus dang / rang gzhan lha skur gsal ba dang / bden med kyi 'dun pa shugs bskyed pas rgyab brten no/ /

With intense intentionality for the intermediate state, meditate that among the six types of beings, all males, and particularly those who arouse your ire, are gathered on the right side of the source of phenomena where you are. Present the complete four offerings and say, “Please let me obtain the saṃbhogakāya in the intermediate state.” All the females of the five types and especially those that arouse your desire are all gathered on the left side of the source of phenomena. After presenting the complete four offerings, supplicate with, “Please let me obtain the saṃbhogakāya in the intermediate state.” Again, with devotion to the guru and the clarity of yourself and others as the deities’ forms, generate powerful intentionality regarding the lack of reality [of those appearances], to be a support practice.

de ltar yang yang bsgom/ / rten bud med kyis bsgom pa'i dbang du byas na/ chags sdang skye ba'i yul go brje bar bya'o/ / yang rang gang du gnas pa'i chos 'byung sngon po de shin tu yangs par bsgoms pa'i g.yas g.yon gyi nang thur du de dag bsgom dgos pa yin na'ang / der bsgom mi bde dmigs pa mi gsal na/ de'i thad kyi bar snang nam mkha' thams cad dang phyi rol du'ang (96) bsgom du rung gsung / yang bla ma'i zhal nas thog mar rang yi dam de/ chos 'byung gi mdun gyi zur la zhal bstan pa yin kyang / skabs 'dir chos 'byung gi rgyab phyogs la zhal bsgyur bas/ rigs drug lha skur bsgyur ba la mdun gyis phyogs par 'ong / mchod pa dang gsol 'debs byed dgos pas de ltar bya gsung / dmigs skor nga drug pa'o/ /

Meditate again and again in this way. From the point of view of female meditators, the objects that arouse desire and anger are reversed. Although you should meditate that the blue source of phenomena where you are is extremely spacious and that they are all within it to the right and left sides, if that is difficult to visualize, it is said to be suitable to meditate that they are all in the space directly above or even outside [the source of phenomena]. {96} Also, my guru said that at first you as the yidam face the front side of the source of phenomena, but at this point turn to face the back of it because the six kinds of beings have changed into the forms of deities who come before you, and you need to make offerings and supplications to them. This is the fifty-sixth round of visualization.

de ltar na dmigs skor lnga bcu nga drug gi steng du stong ra nad gdon sel byed dang / sgyu lus dbang po tha ma'i sa bcad phyi ma gnyis dang / 'od gsal gyi mthar thug dang / rjes kyi sa bcad lnga dang / 'pho ba bar do'i dang po re re rnams bsnan pas chos thun drug cu re bdun yin la/ da lta tshig khrid tsam thob chos su byed pa la thun gyi nges pa med do/ / dmigs thun dngos su yod med la ma rag par thun re la dmigs pa re'i tha snyad sbyar nas/ dmigs pa drug cu rtsa bdun ces kyang bya'o// //

On top of these fifty-six rounds of visualization, there is also the Inner Space Dispelling Sickness and Spirits, the last two subcategories of Illusory Body for those of lowest capabilities, Ultimate Lucid Clarity, the five parts of the concluding practices [of Lucid Clarity], and the [two] Transference practices in the first intermediate state. That makes sixty-seven teaching sessions in all.[28] Here, “teaching session” (chos thun) designates only the word guidances; the actual number of sessions are indefinite. If each visualization were assigned to each session independently of whether or not there is an actual session of visualization, we could call it sixty-seven visualizations [rather than teaching sessions].
III.
III. [Conclusion]
na mo gu ru/
namo guru

zab lam ni gu'i chos drug 'di la/ yan lag mtha' rgyas su ston pa'i rgyas pa dang / spyi nye bar bsdus ba'i 'bring po dang / don ma tshang med pa'i bsdus pa dang / gnad mthil du bsgril ba'i shin tu bsdus pa ste bzhi yod/

In this profound path of Niguma’s Six Dharmas, there are four [styles of transmission empowerments]: (1) the extensive style wherein all the branches are presented in detail, (2) the intermediate style that condenses them in general, (3) the concise style that leaves no topic incomplete, and (4) the extremely concise style that condenses the vital points.
dang po ni/
A. The Extensive Style wherein All the Branches Are Presented in Detail

chos drug bka' bcur grags pa'i dbang rnams kyang rdzogs par bskur/ rmi lam gyi khrid rdzogs mtshams su sgyu lus stan thog gcig ma dang / 'dzin pa rang grol/ sbyong ba rnam gnyis/ dmigs pa lnga skor sogs dang 'byams gcod rgyas pa nas len gyin 'chad pa yin/ 'od gsal rdzogs mtshams su 'od gsal 'char sgo ngos 'dzin dang lhan thabs su 'bri bar 'gyur ba'i 'dam ka tsho yang ston pa yin 'dug ste/ 'on kyang phyis kyi phyag len la dmigs pa kha skong de rnams mi byed (97) par gda'/ dbang rnams rdzogs par bskur ro/ /

Here, the empowerments for the Six Dharmas known as the Ten Permissions (bka’ bcu) are conferred in full. At the juncture of completing the guidance in Dream, there were the explanations taken from the Illusory Body in a Single Sitting, the Natural Liberation of Fixation, the two refinement practices, the cycle of five visualizations, and so forth, as well as the extensive [instruction] on preventing excess (’byams gcod). At the juncture of completing Lucid Clarity, the recognition of the doors of perception in lucid clarity and the choices found in the supplementary writings were presented. However, the more recent practice is not to do those additional visualizations but to confer the empowerments in their entirety. {97}

de la bka' bcu po so so'i dus 'tshams skabs su bab pa der bskur bar 'dod na/ dang por bde mchog lha lnga'i dbang bzhi rdzogs bskur/ sngon 'gro spyi dang / skyabs 'gro sems bskyed song mtshams su/ yi dam 'bogs pa'i tshul yin pas/ bde mchog lha lnga'i ting nge 'dzin gyi dbang de bskur/ chos drug bka' bcu dngos la mi the yang / rgyud sde lnga'i ting nge 'dzin gyi dbang de yang stong ra'i khrid kyi skabs gang 'os re ru mdzad kyin ni 'dug / sngon 'gro'i khrid tshar/ gtum mo'i khrid ma tshugs pa'i mtshams der gtum mo'i sgos bka' bskur/ gtum mo dang / sgyu lus kyi bar skabs su/ sgyu lus kyi sgos bka' byed/ de dang rmi lam gyi khrid kyi bar du rmi lam gyi sgos bka' byed/ de dang 'od gsal gyi khrid kyi bar du/ 'od gsal gyi sgos bka' byed pa rnams la mi 'dra ba med/

With regard to that, if you want to confer the empowerment during the specific time for each of the Ten Permissions, first confer the complete four empowerments of the Five-Deity Cakrasaṃvara. At the juncture following the general preliminaries, taking refuge, and arousing the mind of awakening, confer the empowerment of Five-Deity Cakrasaṃvara absorption empowerment, because it is the way of enhancing the yidam. Even though this isn’t included in the actual Ten Permissions of the Six Dharmas, there is the empowerment of the Five Tantras’ Deities absorption empowerment that is normally given at a suitable time during the guidance for Purifying Inner Space. When the guidance for the preliminaries is finished but Fierce Inner Heat has not yet begun, confer the particular permission (sgos bka’) for Fierce Inner Heat. Between Fierce Inner Heat and Illusory Body, do the particular permission for Illusory Body. Between that and the guidance in Dream, do the particular permission for Dream. Between that and the guidance in Lucid Clarity, do the particular permission for Lucid Clarity. These do not vary.

rgyas pa'i skabs 'dir sgyu lus dbang mo che ni/ kha cig bsre ba sgyu lus gyi dkyil gyi thad rang yin gsung nas/ rmi lam sbyong spel gyi skabs gang 'thad du byed/ la la bsre ba'i mjug yin pas gsung 'od gsal gyi dngos gzhi song mtshams su mdzad te khyad chen po rang med na'ang / phyi ma 'thad par sems/

On this occasion of the extensive transmission, regarding the Great Empowerment of Illusory Body, some say that it is given directly in the midst of blending with illusory body, and they do it whenever suitable during the refining and increasing of dreams. Yet others say that since it is the conclusion of Blending, it should be done at the juncture after the main practice of Lucid Clarity. There’s no great difference in those two, but I think the latter makes more sense. {98}

de bzhin du 'pho ba dang / bar do'i sgos bka' yang so so'i khrid kyi 'gor mdzad pa la mi 'dra ba med/ 'pho ba bar do spyi'i bka' de/ skabs sna tshogs gcig tu byed kyang bar do'i khrid kyi mjug tu byed pa nyid legs so/ /

Similarly, to do each of the particular permissions for Transference and Intermediate State during the instructions for each makes no difference. To give a general permission for both Transference and Intermediate States together, it would be best to do it at the end of the guidance on Intermediate State.

bdag gi rnam rtog ltar na/ lha lnga'i ting nge 'dzin gyi dbang bskur dang / rgyud sde lnga'i ting nge 'dzin gyi dbang bskur gnyis las/ gang rigs gcig kun gyi tha mar byas na legs par (98) 'ong ngo sems so/ /

In my opinion, it will work best to confer the Five-Deity Cakrasaṃvara absorption empowerment or the Five Tantras’ Deities absorption empowerment, whichever of those two is appropriate, at the end of everything.

de la chos drug gi bka' bcu ni/ byin rlabs sgo 'byed kyi bka' gnyis/ byin rlabs khog phubs kyi bka' gnyis/ byin rlabs gzhung shing gi bka' drug go / de la bar pa gnyis ni spyi'i bka' gnyis la zer ba dang / phyi ma drug ni sgos bka' drug la ngos 'dzin pa la rtsod pa med/ dang po gnyis kyi ngos 'dzin la/ kha cig bde mchog lha lnga dang / rgyud sde lnga'i dbang bsdus pa gnyis la 'dod pa yang yod do/ / de ltar 'dod mkhan gyi nang tshan la la ni/ bde mchog lha lnga'i dbang rgyas pa yod pa ma tshor ba yang yin la/ kha cig ni dkyil chog gi gzhung don ma khrol bar dbang bskur byed ma shes par snang / gzhan 'ga' ni lha lnga'i dbang bskur che ba ni/ ni gu'i lugs kyi smin byed yin kyang chos drug sgos kyi min pas/ bka' bcu la mi bgrang zer te/ mdor na 'di la phyis byung lag len byed pa nyung bar byung ngo / /

The Ten Permissions of the Six Dharmas are as follows: two permissions that open the door to blessings, two permissions that establish the blessings, and six permissions that are the main support of blessings.[29] The middle two are called the two general permissions, while the latter six are identified as the particular six permissions. There’s no argument there. In the identification of the first two, however, some hold that they refer to the concise empowerments of Five-Deity Cakrasaṃvara and Five Tantras’ Deities. Among those who hold that belief, there must be some who are unaware of the existence of an extensive empowerment for Five-Deity Cakrasaṃvara, while others seem not to know how to perform the empowerment because they don’t understand the source text for the mandala ritual. Certain others say that while the major empowerment of the Five Deities is the ripening [empowerment] in Niguma’s tradition, it is not specific to the Six Dharmas and so is not counted in the Ten Permissions. In short, in these later times, there were few who follow the tradition.

de'i rgyu ni 'di ltar yin te/ 'gro mgon rin po che'i rjes su/ mkhas grub rnam gsum dngos slob dang bcas pa'i skabs su/ 'di lag len du dar bar yod cing mchod phreng la sogs pa'i lhan thabs 'ga' re mdzad mod/ cho ga dngos zor yang zhing gzhung gzhan la kha 'phangs pa dang lag len khyer bde ba'i stabs/ yi ge gsal po cher ma mdzad par snang /

The reason for that is as follows. After Drogön [Sangye Tönpa] Rinpoche, during the time of the three learned adepts [Zhönu Drup, Shangtön Tsultrim Gön, and Gyaltsen Bum] and their direct disciples, while the practice custom spread, some supplements were created, such as Garland of Offerings.[30] It seems the actual rituals were lightened up, [details] were borrowed from other sources, the manner of implementing the practice was simplified, and the manuals that were composed were not very clear.

de la yang spyir mkhas grub gzhon nu grub ni/ phyi dkyil gcig tu dbang bskur rgyas pa ma song pa la phyag chen chos drug sogs ye mi gnang ba yin par 'dug / dam bsgrags kyang cher mdzad par gda'/ mkhas grub gzhan gnyis kyis dam sbrags rang ma mdzad kyang phyag len de dang 'dra/ de ltar yin yang phyis kyi rnams sgom chen pa spyi 'di'i mig dkyus shor/ rgyud sde lnga'i dbang chen mo (99) 'di lo dang zla ba mang por grabs byas nas lkog bshams pa'i lan re tsam bskur ba ma gtogs/

Also, in general, the learned adept Zhönu Drup would never have given [the higher teachings] such as mahāmudrā or the Six Dharmas to anyone who had not received the extensive empowerments into an outer mandala. He was very strict about those restricted practices. The other two learned adepts did not keep such harsh restrictions, but they practiced along those lines. It was like that, and those who came later simply followed suit since this was the general custom of those great meditators. {99} They would only occasionally give the great empowerment of the Five Tantras’ Deities in secret after many years and months of preparations.

dbang bzhi rdzogs kyi rigs 'phral 'phral mdzad pa ma lcogs nas/ rang ngam gzhan la dbang rgyas pa gang rung de snga rol nas thob na rab byed/ de min smin byed rgyas pa gzhan ye ma thob cing lha lnga'i smin byed tsam yang ma byas par khrid 'debs pa'i srol cig byung / de phyin chad sla chos kyi dbang gis lha lnga rgyas pa la don gnyer cher ma byung ba'i skyon du 'dug / de ni byed ma shes chos drug gi bka' bcu po bgrang dgos byung bas/ lha lnga'i dbang rgyas pa'i tshab la cig shos de bcug pa tsam mo/ /

Unable to give the likes of the complete four empowerments all at once, they [preferred it if disciples] had previously received this or other appropriate extensive empowerments. When that did not happen, there arose a custom of giving the guidances even [to disciples who] never obtained the extensive ripening empowerments elsewhere, and without even the ripening Five-Deity Cakrasaṃvara. Subsequently, due to this being the gurus’ practice, they had no great desire to bestow the extensive empowerment of Five-Deity Cakrasaṃvara, and this was the problem. They did not know how to do it. But when they needed to confer the Ten Permissions, they just replaced the extensive empowerment of Five-Deity Cakrasaṃvara by another [shorter absorption empowerment].

gzhan yang ye shes mkha' 'gro'i lugs 'di la chos drug nyid lam gyi rkang dang rtsa ba yin pas spyi'i smin byed yin na/ chos drug gi rkang dang 'gal snyam pa'i log rtog mi bya'o/ / des na byin rlabs sgo 'byed kyi bka' gnyis ni/ bde mchog lha lnga'i dbang che chung gnyis yin/ rgyud sde lnga gtso bsdus kyi dbang ni/ yi dam gtod pa yin pas spyi khyab du gser chos thams cad dang 'brel ba'ang yin mod/ gzhung bka' nyer lnga rang la mi bgrang ngo / /

Furthermore, in this tradition of the Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness, since the Six Dharmas are the bases and roots of the path, [their empowerments] do constitute the general ripening, so do not entertain the wrong idea of thinking something is contrary to the bases of the Six Dharmas. Thus, the two permissions that open the door to blessings are the two great and small empowerments of Five-Deity Cakrasaṃvara. The empowerment of the Principal [Deities] of the Five Tantras,[31] as it is concerned with yidam practice, is certainly connected pervasively to the Golden Dharmas in general. However, it is not counted in the actual twenty-five source permissions.[32]
de ltar na chos drug nyid la yan lag mtha' rgyas su byed tshul de ltar yin la/
This has shown the way to confer the extensive Six Dharmas with all branches complete.
gnyis pa spyi nye bar bsdus pa 'bring ni/
B. The Intermediate Style That Condenses Them in General

byin rlabs sgo 'byed kyi dbang sgyu lus dbang mo che kho na la bsdu/ de yang deng sang phal cher rjes su byed kyin 'dug na'ang / bka' gzhan rnams mi byed pa'i stabs khrid kyi thog mar byas na legs/ sbyong ba rnam gnyis sogs cha lag rnams mi dgos/ khrid dmigs gzhung rkyang de yongs su rdzogs par byed pa'o/ /

The empowerments of opening the door to blessings are contained exclusively in the Great Empowerment of Illusory Body. These days, most masters follow this style. But [rather than] not doing the other permissions, it would be good to do them at the beginning of each [Dharma’s] guidance. The two kinds of refinement and other subsidiary practices are unnecessary. {100}
gsum pa don ma tshang ba med pa bsdus (100) pa ni/
C. The Concise Style That Leaves No Topic Incomplete
sgyu lus dbang mo che de bskur dgos/ khrid tshul 'di la sngon 'gro dang / dngos gzhi gnyis zhes/
The Great Empowerment of Illusory Body must be conferred. In this manner of concise guidance, there are the two parts called the preliminaries and the main practice.
dang po ni dag byed a'i stong ra ste dmigs skor gcig / skyabs sems sngon du byed dgos kyang dmigs skor logs su mi 'dren no/ /
The first, which is the Purifying A of Inner Space, is the first round of visualization. Although refuge and the mind of awakening must go before that, they are not counted separately.
dngos gzhi la chos drug las/ gtum mo la sngon 'gro lus gnad me'i stong ra/ dngos gzhi gtum mo zas su za ba/ rjes srid pa'i dbang zhu ba ste dmigs skor gsum mo/ /

In the main practice of the Six Dharmas, Fierce Inner Heat has three rounds of visualization: the preliminary is the Inner Space of Fire, the vital point of the body; the main practice is Eating the Food of Inner Heat; and the concluding practice is taking the Empowerment of Existence.
sgyu lus la/ rang lus snang stong lha sku/ cir snang sgyu ma'i lam khyer/ 'gro drug sgyu mar 'char byed te gsum mo/ /
The three parts of Illusory Body are One’s Body as the Empty Appearance of the Deity’s Form, Integrating Whatever Appears as Illusory Body, and Making the Six Kinds of Migrators Arise as Illusion.

rmi lam bzung ba la/ rang zin thig le dbang bzhi'i gnad dang / rtog bcas lam khyer gnyis/ sbyong ba la zung du sdebs pa gang rung gcig go gsung yang / sems kyis lus sbyong ba dang / 'dun pas sbyong ba gnyis sdeb/ yul snang gi nang nas thig le yul snang gsal byed te/ rmi lam kyi khrid la rtsa ba'i sa gcod/ bzung ba/ sbyong ba/ yul snang gsum la dmigs skor lnga'o/ /

In Dream, recognizing has two: the Vital Points of the Four Empowerments of Drops in self-recognition and Integration of Concepts. For refining dreams, although it is said that one may choose a suitable pair of visualizations, basically there are the two: Refining the Body through the Mind and Refining through Intentionality. From the visualizations in Ascertaining Objective Appearances, Illuminating Objective Appearances with Vital Drops [is counted here]. Thus, in the basic outline of the Dream guidance, there are five rounds of visualizations in three categories: recognizing, refining, and [ascertaining] objective appearances.

'od gsal gyi skabs su/ mi rtag skyo shas dang / bla ma'i mos gus thun gyi sngon 'gror btang / thabs lam rang mdangs dang / spyod lam dam rdzas dang / lam khyer rnams thun mtshams kyi spyod pa la btang / bzung ba'i dmigs pa gsum po gang rung cig bsgom gsungs kyang / bla ma la bzung ba kho na lag len gyi mthil du mdzad/ de ltar na 'od gsal gyi khrid la bzung ba dang / bsre ba'o/ / bsre ba la gsal stong bsre ba dang / nyin mtshan bsre ba'o/ / zhes bsdus don byed de/ yongs nas bla ma la bzung ba/ gsal stong bsre ba/ nyin mtshan bsre ba ste/ 'od gsal la dmigs pa gsum mo/ /

During Lucid Clarity, [contemplating] impermanence and disillusionment, and guru devotion are done as preliminaries in the sessions. Make innate radiance the path of methods and make the pledge substances and integration the path of conduct during the breaks between sessions. Although it is said that one may meditate on whichever of the three visualizations for recognizing lucid clarity is appropriate, make just the recognition based on the guru the main practice. In that way, the guides on Lucid Clarity summarize the structure as: “recognizing and blending; in blending, there is blending clarity and emptiness and blending day and night.” In total, there are three visualizations in Lucid Clarity: Recognizing Lucid Clarity Based on the Guru, Blending Clarity and Emptiness, and Blending Day and Night.

'pho ba la ye shes skar khung ma ste dmigs pa gcig go / bar do la (101) rgyal ba longs sku lam khyer dang / gnad 'chug med gnyis bsdoms nas dmigs chen gcig ste/ de ltar na/ chos drug bsdus ba dmigs chen bcu bdun no/ /

Transference has only the one visualization, that is the Skylight of Timeless Awareness. {101} Intermediate State has one major visualization by adding the integration of the Victors’ Saṃbhogakāya with the Unerring Vital Points. So that makes seventeen major visualizations contained in the Six Dharmas.
gnad mthil du dril ba ni
D. The Extremely Concise Style That Condenses the Vital Points
['di] stan thog gcig ma ste/ logs su 'chad par 'gyur ro/ /
This is the single-sitting practice that is explained elsewhere.[33]
[Concluding Verses and Colophon]
de ltar mkha' 'gro'i gsung gi bcud/ / zab don bla ma'i zhal bum 'di/ / yig bris mang du yod na yang / / de dag rnams lam ltos so/ /
This distillation of the ḍākinī’s speech, a vase for the guru’s profound expressions, has been made without relying on the multitude of writings there are.
zhal rgyun smar khrid ma chad pa/ / blo la 'thems par byas nas ni/ / yig rnying khungs ma'i sbas skungs rnams/ / mdzug btsugs byed na mkhas pa yin/ /
Filling the mind to overflowing with the continual stream of oral teachings, one is skilled if one can put one’s finger on valuable secrets hidden in old books.
lar ni nyams myong rgyun med na/ / khrigs bkod tsam gyis ga la phan/ / bla ma'i byin rlabs nyams myong rgyun/ / sems la thebs pa gal re che/ /
But without continual felt experiences, how will mere compositions help? It is crucial to plant in your mind the guru’s blessing stream of experience.
ces pa zab lam ni gu chos drug gi dmigs rim rgyas bsdus gab 'khrugs med par bkod pa 'di yang tA ra nA thas so// /
This sequence of extensive and concise visualizations for the profound path of Niguma’s Six Dharmas was arranged without concealment or disorder by Tāranātha.
sarba mad+ga laM// // (102) (103)
@#/ /zab lam ni gu chos drug gi gzhung khrid ma mo'i lhan thabs kha skong bzhugs so/ //
2. A Supplement to the Source Guide on the Profound Path of Niguma’s Six Dharmas[1]
(104)@#/ /na mo gu ru/
namo guru

ye shes mkha' 'gro ni gu ma'i zhal gdams so/ / chos drug stan thog gcig ma dang / / gzhung khrid rgyas pa'i zhal gdams yod/ / rin chen 'od kyi phreng ba dang / / dri med 'od kyi phreng ba dang / / nyams myong yon tan rgya mtsho dang / / sgyu lus stan thog gcig ma ste/ / bsre ba'i zab khrid rnam bzhi yod/ /

These are the oral instructions of Niguma, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness. The Six Dharmas in a Single Sitting and extensive oral instruction on the source guide, with a selection of four profound guides: Jeweled Light Garland, Stainless Light Garland, Ocean of Experiential Qualities, and Illusory Body in a Single Sitting.
de ltar sde tshan drug po 'di/ / chos drug mkhan la dgos nges yin/ / ces so/ /
These six sets are definitely required for experts on the Six Dharmas.
I.
I. Six Dharmas in a Single Sitting
zab lam chos drug stan thog gcig tu dril ba ni 'di yin te/ de yang sngon 'gro dang / dngos gzhi gnyis las/
This is the profound path of the Six Dharmas rolled into a single sitting, which has preliminaries and main practice.
dang po
A. Preliminaries
['di] la/ thun mongs dang / thun mongs ma yin gnyis/
There are two parts to the preliminaries: common and uncommon.
dang po thun mongs pa ni/ skyabs 'gro sems bskyed gnyis yin la/
The common preliminaries contain two practices: going for refuge and arousing the awakening mind.
gnyis pa la/ dag byed a'i stong ra dang / bla ma'i rnal 'byor ro/ /
The uncommon preliminaries consist of the Purifying A of Inner Space and guru yoga.

de ltar na/ skyabs sems dag byed stong ra gsum/ spyir khrid yig rgyas pa dang 'dra ba las/ skyabs yul gyi bla ma ma bsdus par bzhag pa la sems bskyed kyi rjes su/ stong ra'i gsol 'debs byas nas rang la bstim/ de rjes stong ra sgom pa yin/ /

Three of these—refuge, awakening mind, and inner space purifier—are generally the same as in the extensive guidebook, except that the dissolution of the guru in the refuge object is left until after the arousing of awakening mind. Then the guru dissolves into oneself after doing the supplication of the inner space. After that comes the meditation on inner space. {105}

gnyis (105) pa bla ma'i rnal 'byor ni/ rang gi mdun gyi nam mkha' la gdan bzhi rdzogs kyi steng du/ bla ma sku dngos kho na bsgom/ skyabs gnas kun 'dus su ye nas grub par sgom pa las tshur bstim pa sogs dmigs pa'i spros pa mi dgos/ mos gus kyi gdung shugs drag pos/

In guru yoga, meditate only on the actual form of the guru sitting on the complete four-tiered seat in the space in front of you. Meditate on the guru present since forever as the union of all refuge objects. You don’t need elaborate visualizations such as gathering and dissolving [of each refuge object into the guru]. Then supplicate with intense yearning devotion:

dus gsum sangs rgyas thams cad 'dus pa'i ngo bo bla ma rin po che/ sems can thams cad kyi don du bdag gis bdag 'dzin blos thongs par mdzad du gsol/ dgos med rgyud la skye bar mdzad du gsol/ sgyu lus rmi lam 'byongs par mdzad du gsol/ 'od gsal phyag rgya chen po mchog gi dngos grub da lta nyid du myur ba nyid du 'dug sa 'di nyid du thob par mdzad du gsol/

Precious guru, unified essence of all buddhas of the three times, for the sake of all sentient beings, I pray to you to relinquish my self-fixation, to experience no needs, to master Illusory Body and Dream, and to attain the supreme spiritual power of Lucid Clarity Mahāmudrā right now, quickly, on this very seat.

ces pa kho nas gsol ba drag tu btab/ 'di la sems can thams cad snying khongs su bcug pas chog / 'gro drug gis dngos su gsol ba 'debs pa'i dmigs pa mi dgos/ mthar bla ma 'od du zhu nas rang la bstim pa'i ngang du cung zad mnyam par bzhag go /

Supplicate intensely with only this prayer. It is sufficient to keep all sentient beings in your heart; you don’t need the visualization of the six kinds of migrators actually supplicating along with you. Finally, the guru melts into light and dissolves into you. Rest in that equipoise for a little while.
dngos gzhi
B. Main Practice
1. Fierce Inner Heat

['di] la gtum mo sgom par 'dod na/ lus (106) gnad rnam snang chos bdun spyi dang 'dra bar bya ba las/ mig thad kar blta/ lag mthil gyis pus mo mnan no/ / rang nyid rdo rje phag mo rang lus dang bzhugs tshul mthun pa cig bsgom/ rang gi lus kyi nang stong sang sang ba/ lus kyi dbus su rtsa dbu ma chos bzhi ldan ring thung sogs dkyus dang 'dra/ de'i nang lte 'og sor bzhi na raM dmar nag nas 'bru tsam/ lte bar nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor sran chung tsam gyi steng du/ a shad dmar ser ring thung sor gang tsam phra mo cig bsgom/ de rang gi rtsa ba'i bla ma'i ngo bo yin snyam mos gus dung pa bya/ de nas spyi bor haM dkar po mgo bo thur du blta ba dang / steng gi nam mkha' la rang gi rtsa ba'i bla ma sku mdog dkar zhing zhal 'dzum pa gzi brjid 'bar ba gcig bsam/ thun gyi 'gor rlung ro dgu phrugs su 'bud/ de nas rlung sbyor ba bzhi ldan drag tu bsgom/

If you wish to practice Fierce Inner Heat, {106} assume the vital physical sevenfold posture of Vairocana as usual, except focus your eyes directly in front and place the palms of your hands on your knees. Meditate on yourself as Vajravārāhī with your body and mode of presence in accord. The inside of your body is empty and clear. In its center is the central channel with its four characteristics. Its length and so forth are the same as in the main text. Within that, four finger-widths below the navel, is a dark-red letter raṃ the size of a barley grain. At the navel is the sun-disk mandala, the size of a pea. Upon that, meditate on a fine, orange A-stroke, one finger-width high. Cultivate yearning devotion by thinking of it as essentially your root guru. Then imagine an upside-down white haṃ in your head and your root guru in the space above you, radiantly white and smiling, blazing with charisma. At the outset of this session, do the ninefold shake-up to expel dead air. Then meditate with the forceful fourfold breathing exercise.

dmigs pa ni/ rlung nyid dbu ma'i mas sna nas zhugs/ raM la bus/ de las me lce dmar nag sor bzhir 'bar/ me'i ngo bo lte ba'i a shad la bskul/ a shad las me dmar ser 'ur gyis 'bar/ spyi bo'i haM cung zad zhu/ me lce tshangs bug nas thon te rgya cher 'bar/ me lce'i rtse mo las mchod pa sna tshogs sprul/ bla ma la mchod pa bzhi rdzogs kyis mnyes bar bsam/ me lce'i 'od las bde drod kyi mchod pa phul/ sangs rgyas kun 'dus kyi ngo bo bla ma de yang byang chub kyi sems kyi bdud rtsir zhu/ me lce dang lhan cig tshur byon/ tshangs bug nas zhugs/ bdud rtsi spyi bo'i haM yig la 'dres/ thig le'i rgyun nar gyis babs/ mgrin par sleb pas dga' ba bum dbang / snying gar sleb pas mchog dga' gsang dbang / lte ba'i a shad la thim pas khyad dga'/ sher dbang / de las bdud rtsi babs par la thim pas/ lhan skyes dang dbang bzhi pa'o/ / zhes dran par bya/

Visualize that the wind enters into the lower end of the central channel and fans the raṃ. Tongues of dark-red fire blaze up four finger-widths high. This stimulates the A-stroke at the navel, the essence of fire. Crackling orange fire blazes up from the A-stroke, causing the haṃ in the crown of the head to slightly melt. The tongues of fire emerge from the cranial aperture and blaze expansively. Various offerings emanate from the tips of the flames. Imagine that they make the four complete offerings that delight the guru. The light of the flames presents offerings of bliss and warmth. That guru, the unified essence of all buddhas, melts into the elixir of bodhicitta, returning together with the flames and entering into the cranial aperture. The elixir mixes with the haṃ letter inside your head, and right away a stream of vital-essence drops falls down. As it reaches your throat, you experience ecstasy [and receive] the vase empowerment. As it reaches the heart, it causes sublime ecstasy; the secret empowerment. It dissolves into the A-stroke at the navel and bestows special ecstasy and the wisdom empowerment. From that, the elixir falls into the raṃ and you experience coemergent ecstasy and the fourth empowerment. Recollect this [from the previous description]. {107}

de nas kyang 'bar 'dzag skra shad (107) 'dzings pa dkyus dang 'dra ba bsgom pa las/ khyad par ni raM gyi me dang a shad kyi me gcig tu 'dres pa 'bar ba dang / haM gi thig le yang a shad brgyud te raM la thim par sgom pa ni khyad par ro/ / 'di ni gtum mo zas su za ba/ byin rlabs bla ma'i gtum mo/ srid pa'i dbang zhu ba ste gsum kar dmigs pa gcig la dril ba yin 'bar ba dang / haM gi thig le yang a shad brgyud te raM la thim par sgom pa ni khyad par ro/ / 'di ni gtum mo zas pas/ gnad shin tu che'o/ /

This meditation is similar to the regular blazing and dripping practice called Brushing Tangled Hair (skra shad ’dzings pa). The difference is that here you meditate that the fires of the raṃ and the A-stroke merge together and blaze, and that the dripping of the drops passes through the A-stroke and dissolves into raṃ. This combines three visualizations into one—Eating the Food of Inner Heat, the Inner Heat of the Guru’s Blessing, and taking the Empowerment of Existence—so it is of great importance.

yang 'di la gtum mo 'bar ba la sems gtad te/ rlung drag tu bus pa'i phyi 'dzin khong 'dren drag po dang / / thig le 'bab pa la sems gtad nas drag tu rngubs nas thur sel gyi sgo gnyis la gzir ba dang / de thams cad la sems nam mkha' la yas su bcug / lto ba phyir bkyed nas lus gcu zhing rtsal sprugs drag po byed pa dang / ha la zhes brjod pa ni/

Also in this practice, when you focus your attention on the blazing of inner heat, forcefully expel the breath, hold it outside, and draw up forcefully inside. When you focus your attention on the falling vital-essence drops, violently inhale gulps [of air] and squeeze the two orifices of the downward-clearing winds. At all those times, keep the mind high in the sky. Push your belly out and twist your body while forcefully stirring up the energy [by shaking] and utter “hal.”
thabs lam gnyis pa'i man ngag rlung sbyor gcig la lam rdzogs pa ste/ 'di nye brgyud bka' gsar pa cig yin no/ / gtum mo stan gcig ston tshad rang la 'di 'chad pa min/ shin tu gsang ba'o/ /

This is an esoteric instruction of a second path of methods that completes the path in a single breathing exercise. It is a new teaching from a direct lineage. This is not explained as part of the teaching session on Fierce Inner Heat in a Single Sitting. It is very secret.

spyir 'di la chos drug stan thog gcig ma zer/ gtum mo'i rnal 'byor 'di la yang sgos su gtum mo stan thog gcig mar ming 'dogs mdzad/ gzhan sgyu lus sogs re re nas phul ba la de dang de stan thog gcig ma'i tha snyad mi byed do/ /

The general teaching here is called Six Dharmas in a Single Sitting. Furthermore, this yoga of Fierce Inner Heat is given the particular name of Fierce Inner Heat in a Single Sitting. The other [five dharmas] such as Illusory Body and so forth have not been separately designated each with the moniker “in a single sitting.”
gnyis pa sgyu lus ni/
2. Illusory Body

rtsa ba'i bla ma nyid mdun nam spyi bo'am snying gar bsgoms kyang rung / gang na bzhugs pa'i phyogs sam mkha' khyab tu bzhugs pa la gsol ba btab kyang rung ste/ pha bla ma pha bla ma/ bla ma rang mkhyen/ drin can rtsa ba'i bla ma khyed la gsol ba 'debs so/ / ces mos gdung drag po snying la 'brab pa cig bsgoms nas de'i ngang la lhod kyis bzhag /

You may meditate on your root guru in front, above your head, or in your heart. It is also suitable to supplicate the guru in whichever of those places or as dwelling throughout space. Father guru! Mother guru! Guru, consider me. Kind root guru, I pray to you. Meditate with intense heart-piercing devotion and then relax into that state.

rang lha skur lam tsam gsal btab ste/ rang gzhan snang ba thams cad la dmigs (108) nas/ 'di thams cad med bzhin du snang ba 'khrul ba'i snang ba yin pa la bzang ngan bde sdug chags sdang mtho dman nye ring 'byor rgud dga' mi dga' gtam snyan mi snyan sogs la a 'thas kyi zhen pas spang blang dgag sgrub byed pa 'di rang a re 'khrul/ gtad pa rang ci yod/ rmi lam lta bu rang yin ang zhes sbyangs nas/ g.yos med du chal song ba de ka la bzo bcos med par bzhag / dbang po rab 'bring gi nyams len thams cad de la 'dus/

Suddenly visualize yourself in the deity’s form. Consider the appearance of yourself and all others: {108} “All of this is the deluded appearance of things that are nonexistent yet appear. Good and bad, happiness and sadness, desire and anger, high and low status, friends and strangers, prosperity and decline, likes and dislikes, praise and blame, and so on are all concerned with accepting or rejecting delusional reifications due to clinging to their solidity. How foolish of me! Why be concerned? In fact, it is an illusion, a dream.”

de ma thag rang lhar gsal ba'am/ tha mal gyi rnam pa gang yin yang rung ste/ nang stong sang nge ba'i lte 'og tu chos 'byung dang rigs drug sgom pa sogs 'gro drug sgyu mar 'char byed dkyus dang mthun par bsgom mo/ / 'di la dbang po rab 'bring tha gsum gyi gnad so sor tshang ba yin kyang gcig tu dril nas bsgom pa yin pas dmigs skor gcig kho na'o/ /

Train vigorously with those thoughts and when you are beyond judgment, maintain that state without fabricating anything. All the practices for those of highest, average, and lesser faculties are included here. Then immediately visualize yourself as the deity, or as your ordinary self, as you wish. Meditate according to the main course of the practice on the six kinds of beings and the source of phenomena below your navel in the clear, empty interior of your body, and so on, making those six kinds of migrators arise as illusion. The vital points of the practices for those of highest, average, or lesser faculties are each included here, but as they are combined into one meditation, it is considered a single round of visualization.
3. Dream
gsum pa rmi lam la bzung ba dang / sbyong ba dang / yul snang blta ba'o/ /
In Dream practice, there is recognizing, refining, and viewing objective appearances.

dang po ni rang zin thig le dbang bzhi'i gnad kho na ste/ de yang dmigs pa de tshar gsum tsam re bstud nas 'jur bar bsgoms pa'i rjes su/ rang gzhan snod bcud dgra gnyen longs spyod thams cad la bden med kyi 'dun pa drag tu sbyangs shing / de ka'i ngang la gang shar bzo med du 'jog / tshul de lta bu yang yang goms bar byed pa yin/

The first is solely the Vital Points of the Four Empowerments of Drops for self-recognition. Meditate on the visualization for that just three times in close succession. After that, train with intense intentionality in the unreal nature of yourself and others, the habitats and inhabitants, enemies and friends, all enjoyments, and so forth. Within that state, settle without fabrication in whatever arises. Familiarize yourself with that again and again.
gnyis pa sbyong ba ni/ 'dun pas sbyong pa kho na yin te dkyus bzhin yin/ 'on kyang sgyu ma lta bu'i 'dun pa dang / rang bzhin dbyings kyi ngang skyong ba de gal che'o/ /

The second, refining dreams, is solely to Refine through Intentionality as described in the main text. However, the most important parts are the intentionality of illusion-like nature and to sustain a state of natural basic space.

gsum pa yul snang ni/ rang gi snying gar hU~M yig dkar po dwangs gsal 'od kyi rang bzhin cig bsgom/ rmi lam sgyu ma'i 'dun pa dang / yul snang blta 'dod drag tu bya/ hU~M las 'od kyi thag pa lta bu cig rgyang ste (109) 'phros/ gang lta 'dod pa'i dngos po de zhags pas drangs ba ltar tshur byung nas snying ga'i hU~M la thim/ hU~M gi 'od kyis snang ba thams cad khra gsal le gsal ba la sems gtad de bsgom/ skabs 'dir bum can bsgom pa gal che/ lar/ ma zin 'byams dang gol sa gsum/ / bsod nams tshogs kyis bcad par bya/ / ces 'byung ba/ rmi lam sgyu lus kyi skabs su gal che bar bzhed/

Third, for Ascertaining Objective Appearances, meditate on a radiant clear white hūṃ in your heart, the nature of light. Rigorously cultivate the intentionality that all is dream and illusion and your desire to see the appearance of a place. Light radiates from the hūṃ, extending out like a rope. {109} It snares whatever place or thing you wish to see and pulls it in, dissolving into the hūṃ at your heart. The light from the hūṃ illuminates all appearance with shimmering radiance. Focus your attention there. During this practice, it is important to meditate with vase breathing. As is said: Cultivation of merit cuts through these three: nonrecognition, excess, and deviation. This is held to be very important in the contexts of Dream and Illusory Body practices.
bzhi pa 'od gsal la/
4. Lucid Clarity

'od gsal 'dzin pa'i dmigs pa'i gtso bo yin pas/ bla ma la brten nas 'dzin pa de nges par bsgom/ de kas zin na legs/ ma zin na rno khyad du a yig la brten nas 'dzin pa yin te/ rang gi dbu ma'i mas snar a dkar po bsgom/ steng rlung nan nan/ 'og rlung then then byas pas/ a de gsang ba'i rtsa bar lhan lhan song / gsang ba'i rtsa lam nas kyang gcus kyog kyog pa'i ngang nas rdo rje nor bu'i dbus su kha dog sngon po 'od 'tsher ba cig tu gyur/ mgo nang bstan du log shugs drag pos phyi la 'gro 'dod kyang bu ga dog po la ma shong bas 'gro mi thub par lhan lhan 'dug pa la yud cig sems drag tu gtad/ yang de ka'i snang ba ma 'gags tsam la had de chad de bzhag / de ltar yang yang bsgom/

Since it is the principal visualization for recognizing lucid clarity, you must definitely meditate on this based upon the guru. It is best if you have grasped it through that method. But if you have not grasped it, based on this especially potent [meditation on] the letter A you will come to it. Imagine a white A at the lower end of the central channel inside your body. Press down continually on the upper winds and continually draw the lower winds, until the A falls steadily down to the base of the perineum. It winds its way, constantly twisting, through the genital channel, and when it reaches the center of the vajra’s glans it becomes shining blue in color. The head [of the syllable] turns back and faces inward. It tries to force its way out with great strength, but it cannot fit through the hole and remains there steadily. Focus intently on that for a moment. Again, rest there in startled wonderment, merely not blocking that appearance. Meditate on that again and again.

'od gsal 'dzin lugs spyi dang 'dra/ 'dzin pa la lhag par bsngags so/ / 'di kho nas gnyid kyi 'od gsal la zin 'ong / stan thog gcig ma rang gi 'od gsal gyi dmigs pa de phyi ma 'di kho na yin/ bla ma la brten pa'i dmigs pa de/ spyi'i khog phubs rgyab rten yin gyi/ stan thog gcig ma'i skabs kyi dmigs pa rang min no/ /

This way to grasp lucid clarity is the standard way and is highly praised for its ability to do that. You will come to recognize the lucid clarity of sleep by this alone. The visualization of Lucid Clarity in a Single Sitting in particular is only this latter one. The visualization based on the guru is a general supportive framework and is not the actual visualization for the occasion of the single-sitting practice.
a la brten pa 'di rten bud med kyis sgom na/ lte 'og sor brgyad tsam du dbu ma'i mas snas sleb pa'i mas sna de kar bsgom/ rlung gi (110) gnad sogs gzhan 'dra'o/ /

Women who do the meditation based on the A visualize the lower end of the central channel extending eight finger-widths below the navel and meditate on that lower end. The vital points of the winds and so on are the same. {110}

de ltar rtsa ba'i chos bzhi po de thams cad cha tshang sgom na/ thog mar re re bzhin zla ba gnyis gsum sbyangs pas nyams myong sne re rnyed 'ong / de rjes nyin zhag phrugs gcig gi nang du bzhi cang sgom na/ tho rangs sam snga thun la gtum mo/ gung thun la sgyu lus/ dgongs thun la rmi lam/ srod thun la 'od gsal bsgom zhes khrigs ka 'di bzhin yang mdzad/ 'on kyang mtha' gcig tu ma nges so/ / de bzhin du bzhi car bsgom par mi nus na/ gsum sdebs sam/ gnyis sdebs sam/ re re bsgoms pas kyang don khyad par can 'grub par 'gyur ro/

If you intend to meditate on the entire practice of all these four main dharmas, begin by training with each one for two or three months to gain a bit of experience in them. After that, if you meditate on all four within a single day, practice Fierce Inner Heat at dawn or the early session, Illusory Body in the middle session, Dream in the afternoon session, and Lucid Clarity in the evening session. That is one way to arrange it, but not necessarily the only method. If you cannot meditate on all four dharmas in that way, you will still accomplish special meaning by meditating on three or two or even one.

stan thog gcig ma ces pa yang rtsa ba'i chos bzhi po la brtsi ba yin te/ 'pho pa bar do kha skong yin pas rgyas bsdus gang bstan kyang 'dra'o gsung nas go babs lhod yangs su mdzad kyang / lag len du 'di ltar mdzad te/

The name “single sitting” is applied only to these four root dharmas. Transference and Intermediate State practices are considered supplementary, so it is said that they may be taught however extensively or briefly. Despite this loose status, in practice you should perform them as follows.
'pho ba ni/
5. Transference

spyi bo tshangs bug rgya mthongs kha phye ba bzhin du yod par bsgom/ a la brten pa'i 'od gsal 'dzin pa de kho na bzhin las/ lte 'og sor bzhi'i a de rlung phyir 'bud pa dang lhan cig dbu ma'i lam nas brgyud/ nam mkha'i dbus su mda' 'phangs pa bzhin du song nas mkha' dbyings mthon por yal bar bsgom/ yang a de nam mkhar grub mar babs tshangs bug nas zhugs te dbu ma'i mas snar phyin par bsam/ 'di la 'gro 'ong spel ma rang bsgoms pas chog / sgo dgag pa'ang mi dgos gsungs so/ /

Meditate that the cranial aperture on your head is wide open like a skylight. It is similar to grasping lucid clarity based on the letter A, except that there is an A four finger-widths below the navel and as you exhale that A travels up the central channel to the cranial aperture. It shoots out into the midst of the sky like an arrow and vanishes high into the expanse. Imagine that the A reappears in the sky and falls down through your cranial aperture and down to the lower end of the central channel. It is taught that it is enough to meditate on just the alternating of [consciousness] going up and coming down; you needn’t meditate on blocking the door [of the cranial aperture].
drug pa bar do ni/
6. Intermediate State

rang gi mdun du chos 'byung sgom pa nas/ spyi bor bla ma bsgom pa'i bar gzhung khrid kyi dbang po 'bring dang 'dra/ gnad 'chug med kyi dod la/ 'gro ba rigs drug gi gnas dang / gzugs sgra dri ro reg bya bzang ngan thams cad la sgyu ma dang / bar do'i 'dun pa sbyangs/ (111) mngal sgong gi gnyis sbyor sogs gsal btab nas bar dor shes pas yi dam yab yum du bsgyur/ de la'ang mngon zhen med par sgyu ma lta bu'o/ / zhes dran par byed pa yin/ yan lag gi chos 'di gnyis kyang nye brgyud kyi cha shas cung zad yin/ de ltar na stan thog gcig mar sdud tshul 'di sngon chad yi ger 'khod pa cher med pa'i zhal rgyun yin/ gtum mo'i rlung sbyor gnyis pa dang / yul snang dang / a yi 'od gsal dang / yan lag gi chos 'di gnyis la dmigs pa'i sde bsgyur ba cung zad re yod pa 'di nye brgyud yin yang gsungs te/ yul snang dang 'od gsal yang yig rnying gis zin pa lags/ gzhan rnams ni man ngag rnying pa kho na'o/ /

This is the same as the meditation for those of average faculties in the source guidebook, starting from the meditation on the source of phenomena in front of you up to the guru above your head. In place of the unerring vital points, train in regarding the realms of the six kinds of migrators and all form, sound, smell, taste, and texture as illusion, and engage the intentionality of the intermediate state. {111} Clearly imagine [your future] parents’ intercourse [that results in] womb or egg birth and, knowing that it is the intermediate state, transform them into the yidam couple. Remember that they are like an illusion and harbor no attachment to their reality. These two subsidiary dharmas are minor portions of direct lineages. Similarly, this abridged style for a single sitting is an oral transmission, rarely written down in former times. There have been small changes to the second breathing exercise of Fierce Inner Heat, the [practices of] Ascertaining Objective Appearances, the Lucid Clarity of A, and these two subsidiary dharmas. These are also said to be from the direct lineages, though one finds Ascertaining Objective Appearances and Lucid Clarity in the old books as well. Everything else is exclusively the ancient esoteric instruction.
II.
II. Sealed Visualizations
da ni khrid rgyas 'bring gnyis la dgos pa'i dmigs pa bka' rgya ma rnams bshad par bya'o/ /
Now to explain the sealed [instructions] of necessary visualizations for the extensive and intermediate guidances (session 7 in Tangdalma).

de la gtum mo'i thon chos byin rlabs bla ma'i gtum mo dkyus ni/ gtum mo nyid kyi bla ma'i rnal 'byor sngon du song bas/ rang rje btsun ma bzhugs tshul rang lus dang mthun pa'am/ rang lus tha mal du 'jog pa gang yin yang 'dra/ nang stong sang nge ba'i stong ra bca'/ lus gnad tsog pu'am skyil krung gang gis kyang rung / rang gi lus kyi dbus su rtsa dbu ma kha dog dmar po spom phra spos dong tsam pa gsungs/ mas sna lte 'og sor bzhi dang / yas sna spyi bor zug pa/ spyi bo tshangs bug shin tu yangs pa/ 'phang lo tsam zer te/ dbu ma'i spom phra dang bstun dbu ma'i kha dang tshangs bug mnyam pa thal le bsgom/ dbu ma'i nang lte ba'i thad du nyi ma'i gdan la rang gi rtsa ba'i bla ma/ ral pa'i thor tshugs dang / rus rgyan dang / stag lpags can skyil krung gis bzhugs pa/ me'i rang bzhin gang la reg kyang thogs med du 'tshig 'gro (112) ba cig bsgom/ yig rnying 'ga' zhig na spyi bor haM bsgom pa bshad kyang phyag len du mi mdzad/ de nas rlung ro bsal te sbyor ba bzhi ldan drag tu bsgom/

This is a teaching session of Fierce Inner Heat in the regular course of Inner Heat of the Guru’s Blessing. First complete the guru yoga from Fierce Inner Heat itself. [Then visualize] yourself as Exalted [Vajravārāhī] in a posture consistent with your own body. Remaining in your ordinary form is also acceptable. Either way, inside is the inner space of emptiness and clarity. The vital physical posture may be squatting with legs drawn up or cross-legged, whichever is suitable. In the center of your body, the central channel is said to be red and the width of an incense stick. The lower end begins four finger-widths below the navel and the upper end touches inside the crown of the head. The cranial aperture is very wide, said to be the size of a spindle. Meditate that the opening of the central channel and the cranial aperture are equal and open, commensurate with the width of the central channel. Within the central channel, at the level of the navel, is a sun seat upon which is your own root guru. The guru sits in cross-legged posture with hair drawn up in a bun, bone ornaments, and a tiger skin. Meditate on that guru as being the nature of fire that burns up whatever touches it. {112} In some of the old texts there is an explanation of meditating on haṃ in the head, but in practice that is not done. Then clear out the dead air and meditate intensely with the four-part breathing exercise.

dmigs pa ni/ rlung kha sbyor du bzung bas bla ma'i sku las me lce 'ur gyis 'bar/ me lce rtsa dbu ma'i nang du mi shong ba tsam du yar la 'bar te/ spyi bo tshangs bug nas thon pa na/ me lces nam mkha' khengs/ bla ma yi dam sangs rgyas byang chub sems dpa' mkha' dbyings gang ba thams cad la mchod pa sna tshogs sprul te phul/ me 'od nyid bde ba'i mchod par gyur/ de thams cad bdud rtsi byang chub kyi sems su zhu/ me lce dang lhan cig tshur byon/ bdud rtsi spyi bo'i tshangs bug nas zhugs/ dbu ma'i lam nas brgyud de/ bla ma'i sku la babs pas lcags sregs la snum blug pa bzhin du sor sgra dang / tshig sgra dang / 'ur rgyang dang bcas te/ lus kyi nang thams cad me lce drag pos 'ur 'ur shig shig tu khengs par bsam/ rlung thengs bdun sogs ji ltar 'os pa bsgom/ 'dis drod la bogs thon/ rtsa zug rlung zug sel ba la bsngags/ spyir bla ma'i byin rlabs bskul ba yin pas gegs thams cad sel zhing yon tan thams cad skye ba la bsngags so/ /

Visualize that holding the joined winds (rlung kha sbyor) causes tongues of rumbling fire to blaze from the guru’s body [at your navel]. The flames don’t fit inside the central channel, so they blaze upward and out the cranial aperture, filling space with tongues of flame. They emanate various offerings that are presented to the guru, yidams, buddhas, and bodhisattvas who fill the space. The firelight itself becomes the offering of bliss. All of that melts into the elixir of bodhicitta and returns together with the flames. That elixir enters through your cranial aperture, travels down the central channel, and flows into the guru’s form. Like oil poured on burning metal, it makes sounds of whistling, sizzling, and distant rumbling. Imagine that your whole body is filled with the rumbling and crackling of fierce tongues of fire. Meditate on this for seven breaths or whatever is suitable. This practice enhances [the experience of] warmth. It is praised for relieving the pain of channels and winds. In general, since it evokes the guru’s blessing, it is commended for dispelling all obstructors and developing all qualities.
The Empty Space of the Inner Channels

nang rtsa'i stong ra bca' ba zhes bya ba ni/ dang por dbu ma gro sog tsam bsgom/ de nas je sbom je sbom la mda' smyug 'bring po tsam/ rta lcag tsam/ je phra je phra la gro sog tsam 'gro bar bsgom zhing / 'jam rlung bzung ba de ka la zhag shas bsgom/

At first, meditate on the central channel as the size of a wheat stalk. Then it grows thicker and thicker until it is the size of a medium arrow shaft, then a horse whip. Then it shrinks narrower and narrower down to a wheat stalk. As you meditate on that, hold the gentle breath. Meditate on that for a few days.

yang dbu ma sbom phra lag ngar tsam du bkyed cing / sba lcag tsam du bsdu ba zhag shas bsgom/ de nas mda' dong tsam du bkyed cing / lag ngar tsam du bsdu ba zhag shas bsgom/ de nas lus dang (113) mnyam par bkyed cing / mda' dong tsam du bsdu ba zhag shas bsgom/ de rnams la 'jam rlung bsgom/ de nas dbu ma blos 'khyud ched du rgya dbangs bkyed cing / lus dang mnyam par bsdu ba la bslab/ 'di la bum can drag rlung 'dzin no/ /

Again meditate that the width of the central channel expands to the size of a wrist, then contracts to the size of a bamboo whip. Do that for a few days. Then meditate for a few days on it expanding to the size of an arrow quiver, then shrinking back to wrist size. {113} Then meditate for a few days on it expanding to the size of a body, then contracting back to the size of a quiver. During all those, meditate with the gentle breathing. Then train in expanding the central channel to the furthest extent that the mind can encompass and contracting it back down to the size of the body. In this, intensely hold the vase breathing.
de nas dbu ma phar bkyed tsa na nam mkha' la yas/ nang du bsdus pa'i skabs rta rnga tsam du song ba la sems gtad/ 'di la rlung sbyor zhi drag nges med du sbyang ngo / /

Then focus the attention on expanding the central channel outward until it vanishes in space, then when contracting it inward it becomes no bigger than a horse’s tail hair. In this, the breathing exercise is either gentle or intense, it is not definite.

'di thog mar sgom na/ rtsa rlung gi gegs mi 'byung ba yin/ bar du sgom na dmigs pa gtad kyang rlung sems dbu mar 'jug pa'i thabs yin/ mthar sgom na 'od gsal mtha' dbus med pa nam mkha' lta bu 'char/ rtsa bsgoms pas stong nyid rtogs bya ba de yong ba yin gsungs/ 'on kyang re zhig stong pa'i nyams tsam 'char ro/ /

If you meditate on this at the outset, obstructions to the channels and winds won’t occur. If you meditate on it in the middle, even though you focus on the visualization, it is a method for the wind-mind to enter into the central channel. If you meditate on it in the end, lucid clarity without center or circumference will dawn like the sky. It is taught that meditation on the energy channels brings about the realization of emptiness. However, sometimes only the experience of emptiness arises.
Dispelling Obstructions of Kunda in the Lower Body

gegs rang grol gyi skabs/ smad kun da'i gegs bsal ba'i skabs/ tha ma dmigs pa dang 'khrul 'khor gyis bsal ces pa la/ thog mar rlung khug pa kha re bzung / de nas rang gi gsang gnas bde skyong gi 'khor lo'i thad du hU~M dmar po mgo bo nang du bstan pa/ zhabs kyu phyi'i phyogs la bstan pa cig bsgom/ yang pad+ma dmar po 'dab ma brgyad pa yu ba rdo rje'i rtsa nang na yod cing / me tog 'dab ma rgyas ba nor bu'i bu ga'i phyi na yod pa/ rtsa ba ba thag lcags kyu lta bu de hU~M gi zhabs kyu la sbrel bar bsgom/ lus kyi dbus su rtsa dbu ma yang khrol le ba bsgom/ lus nya bzhi bsgrim/ lto ba tshigs pa la gcer/ lce phugs su zlog / mig spyi bor gtad/ lag pa gtsug tor gyi phyag rgya spyi bor mgo gzhug zlog / ngag nas hU~M 'dren drag la ring ba bya/

In the section on Naturally Liberating Obstructions (session 12) there is the section on dispelling obstructions of kunda (generative fluid) in the lower body. There, it says, “The least is to dispel them through visualizations and yogic exercises.” With regard to that, first hold some rounds of breathing [exercises]. Then meditate that in your secret place, at the bliss-sustaining chakra, is a red hūṃ with the top pointing inward and the lower hook (the vowel sign, zhabs kyu) facing outward. Also there is a red eight-petaled lotus with its stem inside the vajra channel (urethra), and its flower petals outside the gem (glans). Meditate that the lotus stem ends in a hook that attaches to the lower hook of the hūṃ. Meditate also that the central channel in the center of the body is wide open. Constrict the four muscles [of the arms and legs] and squeeze the belly up against the spine. Turn the tongue back and turn your eyes up to the crown. Make the uṣṇīṣa mudra facing backward with your hands above your head. Intensely utter a long drawn-out hūṃ.

dmigs pa ni gsang ba'i hU~M shugs chen pos gyen la 'ongs pa na/ de'i zhabs kyus pad+ma'i rtsa ba nas then (114) pas me tog rdo rje'i bu ga la ma shong ste/ rdo rje rgyu ma phyi nang slog pa bzhin du song nas/ hU~M gis yar then dbu ma'i lam brgyud/ spyi bo'i steng du hU~M dang / nor bu phyi nang log pa rgyang der 'dug par bsam/ de'i ring la rlung phyir bzung ngo / /

The visualization is as follows: When it happens that the hūṃ in the secret place moves up with great force, its lower hook (zhabs kyu) pulls the lotus stem but the flower does not fit through the vajra’s opening. {114} The vajra is inverted upward into the intestine and the hūṃ pulls it up through the central channel.[2] Imagine that the hūṃ and the inverted gem (nor bu) stretches above the crown of your head. Hold the breath outside for the duration.

'di yang yang bsgoms pas/ gang bas 'dzag pa dang / chags pas 'dzag pa dang / nad gzhis 'dzag pa dang / rmi lam du 'dzag pa ste/ de rnams la shin tu bsngags/ lar 'dzag pa drug kar chod de/ 'on kyang dam sel gyis 'dzag pa la bshags bsdams dang / grib kyis 'dzag pa la khrus chog dang / gnyis ka'i thun mongs su tshogs gtor gal che gsungs/

Repeated meditation on this is highly praised for [stopping] emissions due to fullness, emissions due to desire, emissions due to underlying sickness, and emissions in dreams. It also stops the six kinds of emissions. However, for emissions due to lapses in sacred pledge, confession and renewal is recommended, and washing rituals for emissions due to contamination (grib). For both situations in common, communal feasts and torma offerings are said to be important.
Nairātmya

rmi lam sbyong ba'i skabs/ bdag med ma la brten nas sbyong ba dang / yul snang gi skabs bdag med ma la brten pa dang / 'od gsal bdag med ma la brten nas 'dzin pa rnams la bdag med ma nyid la yi dam byed na des chog / ma yin na rang skad cig la bdag med mar bskyed la/ oM a swA hA/ zhag bdun phrag gcig gam gnyis sam gsum 'bad de bzla/ gtor chung zan ril sha chang gis brgyan pa/ yi ge 'bru gsum gyis byin gyis brlabs/ oM a A i I r-i r-I l-i l-I e ai o au aM swA hA/ lan bdun bzlas pas phul/ gtor chung de dus med du gtong / de lta bu sngon du song nas dmigs pa dngos gzhi bsgom pa'i skabs kyang / lha bsgom pa dang / gtor ma 'bul ba de ma chag pa dgos/ bum chu gcig la sngags stong tsam bzlas/ des nyin mo yang khrus byed cing nyal khar yang 'khrud/ khyad par yig brgya bzla zhing kha lag 'khru ba yang gal che'o/ / de ltar byas na mkha' 'gro'i byin rlabs kyi stobs yin pas/ dmigs pa 'di rnams rno zhing shin tu myur gsungs/

For the practices of Refining Dreams Based on Nairātmya (session 25) in the section on refining dreams, Illuminating Objective Appearances with Nairātmya (session 40), and Recognizing Lucid Clarity Based on Nairātmya (session 43), it is sufficient if you have made Nairātmya herself the yidam. If not, instantly create yourself as Nairātmya and diligently repeat oṃ a svāhā for one or two or three weeks. Make a small torma ball of dough decorated with meat and alcohol and consecrate it with the three seed syllables. Repeat oṃ a ā i ī ṛi ṛī ḷi ḷī e ai o au aṃ svāhā seven times and offer it. There is no definite time to send out that small torma. Once that has been done, during meditation on the main visualization, you should continue to meditate on the deity and offer torma. Recite one thousand mantras for the vase water. Use it to wash in the morning and before bed. In particular, it is important to recite the hundred syllables while washing your face and hands. If you do all this, since it is the power of the ḍākinīs’ blessings, it is said that the visualizations will be sharp and come quickly. {115}
'od gsal (115) gyi skabs/ 'jag chen gyis bdag med ma dkar mor bshad/ lar dkar sngo gang byas kyang 'dra gsungs/ nyams len gyi rgyun sngon mo nyid ka mdzad do/ /
In the section on Lucid Clarity, Jakchen described Nairātmya as white, then again as light blue, either way. In the regular practice she is blue, so there are two styles.
'byams gcod kyi snying po ni/
The Essence of Severing Excess[3]

rmi lam skabs su sad 'byams la/ mgrin pa dang snying gar rtsa 'khor 'dab ma bzhi pa re bsgom/ kha dog spyi dang mthun/ snying gar hU~M dmar po/ mgrin par oM dmar po/ oM las 'od kyi skud pa dmar po cig byung / snying ga'i hU~M la lan gsum du dkris te/ thang nge sbring nge bskor te lhag ma yar log / sne mgrin pa'i AHnyid la 'byar bar bsam/ hU~M la sems gtad te gnyid log pas sel/

In the section on excessive insomnia, meditate that there is a four-petaled lotus at the throat and at the heart in the standard colors. A red hūṃ is at the heart and a red oṃ at the throat. A thread of red light emerges from the oṃ and encircles the hūṃ at the heart three times, wrapping tightly around. The rest of the thread turns back up and the tip attaches to the āḥ (oṃ?) at the throat. Focus your attention on the hūṃ. This will dispel insomnia.

'khrul 'byams la mgrin par sngar bzhin dang / spyi bor rtsa 'dab bzhi pa'i lte bar haM dkar po mgo bo thur bstan gsal btab/ yang oM las 'od zer gyi skud pa byung / spyi bo'i haM la lan gsum du dkris nas/ slar log skud pa'i sne mgrin pa'i oM nyid la 'byar bar bsams nas spyi bo'i haM la sems gtad pas 'khrul 'byams sel gsungs te/ 'di zin ma thag 'khrul 'gro ba la bsngags/

For excessive delusion, visualize the throat the same as before and a white upside-down haṃ in the center of a four-spoked [chakra] in the crown of the head. Again a thread of light emerges from oṃ and wraps around the haṃ in the head. Imagine that the thread turns up again and its tip attaches to the oṃ at the throat. Then focus your attention on the haṃ at the crown. This is said to dispel excessive delusion. It is praised [as a remedy for] delusion that occurs immediately after recognition [of a dream].

ye nas rang mi zin pa'i 'khrul 'byams la/ rtog bcas lam khyer gyi skabs der/ mgrin par rtsa 'dab bzhi pa'i lte bar oM dmar po/ 'dab ma bzhi la/ a nu ta ra/ rlung bum can dang / rmi lam 'dzin pa'i 'dun pa drag tu sbyangs/ nyal khar rmi lam gyi 'dun pa drag po'i ngang nas/ a yig nu la thim/ de ta la/ de ra la/ de oM la thim/ oM la rig pa gtad pa'i ngang nas gnyid du 'gro bar bya'o/ / des 'khrul 'byams sel lo/ /

For the excessive delusion of never self-recognizing dreams, in the context of Integration of Concepts (session 22), there is a red oṃ in the center of the four channel-petals at the throat. On the four petals are a–nu–ta–ra. Hold the vase breath and cultivate powerful intentionality for recognizing dreams. At bedtime, in a state of intense intentionality of dreaming, the a letter dissolves into the nu, that into ta, that into ra, and that dissolves into oṃ. While focusing the awareness on oṃ, go to sleep. That will clear up excess delusion.
Dispelling Excessive Delusion in Lucid Clarity

'od gsal gyi skabs su 'khrul 'byams sel ba la/ spyir 'od gsal 'dzin tshul spyi dang 'dra ste/ dang por dmigs pa gang (116) yang rung ba la brten nas/ rang shugs la 'od gsal zin na legs/ rmi lam las 'od gsal zin pa sne rnyed pa dka' bas/ dmigs pa'i stobs kyis zin pa yin na/ dbang po'i rim pa dang bstun te/ zla ba gcig gam/ gnyis sam/ gsum tshun la 'byung / stes dbang gis lan re tsam zin pa la ni nges pa med/ gal te de tsam du 'bad kyang bstar chags su zin pa ma byung na/ sbogs chog la brten nas btsan thabs su 'dzin dgos/ de yang dmigs pa gtad res kyis gnyid bde chod chod yang sang sang ba byung na myur du zin no/ / yang gnyid 'thug po la nyams ma bde log log pa dang / 'dre gnon bzhin du jir jir gnon pa byung na yang myur du zin yong ba'i rtags yin no/ /

In general, this is the same as the regular way to recognize lucid clarity. First, depending on any of the visualizations, the best is to grasp lucid clarity on its own strength. {116} But since grasping lucid clarity is more difficult to get a handle on than in dreaming, if you are recognizing it on the strength of the visualization, it may take one month, or two months, or as long as three months, depending on the level of capability. Occasionally you might recognize it by accident a few times, but this is not assured. If, somehow, you regularly exert effort to that extent but still do not recognize lucid clarity, you need to use the forceful methods of the enhancement ritual (spogs chog). After focusing on that visualization a few times, if your sleep is pleasant and light, then you will quickly recognize lucid clarity. If your sleep is heavy and unpleasant, you continually fall back asleep, and you feel oppressed as if demons are weighing on you, that also is a sign that recognition will quickly ensue.

'dir zla ba gcig nas gsum gyi bar du dmigs pa bsgom pa la ni rtsol ba cher bya/ do nub zin nam sang nub zin nam mi zin pa e yin snyam pa'i re dogs kyi tsab tsob mi bya bar rtsis btang med par bsgyur na/ yong snyam med pa cig la zin yong ba shas che/

Make a great effort to meditate on this visualization for one month up to three months. Do not be rushed by hopes and fears, thinking, “Will I get it tonight or tomorrow night or not at all?” Let go of anticipation. Mostly it comes when you don’t expect it.
Forceful Methods

ye ma zin na btsan thabs kyi sbyor ba ni/ da ni zhag bdun sogs myur du 'dzin par bya snyam pa'i skabs/ bla ma'i mched grogs la tshogs 'khor gyi mchod pa phul/ bshags bsdam bya/ 'od gsal zin par smon lam btab/ de nas bzung nub re bzhin mkha' 'gro sde lnga dang / myur mdzad mgon po'i gtor ma bya zhing / 'od gsal zin par phrin las gzhol/ zhag bdun tsam gyi sngon nas/ khrus dang gtsang sbra la 'bad cing / spyod lam dam rdzas la gzab pa gal che/ de rjes zhag gsum tsam gyi sngon nas nyin mo gnyid ye ma shor bar bya/ mtshan dus kyi gnyid kyang sum cha bzhi cha tsam phri/ dmigs pa dang 'dun pa drag tu bya/

This is the application of forceful methods if you never grasp lucid clarity. For this circumstance, think, “Now I will quickly recognize it in seven or so days.” Present the communal feast offerings to the fellow disciples of your guru, confess and renew promises, and pray to recognize lucid clarity. Offer torma to the five classes of ḍākinī and Swift-Acting Protector every evening and request their activity to help in recognizing lucid clarity. For a week before [practicing], it is important to be diligent in washing and cleanliness and cautious with conduct and sacred substances. After that for three days, never sleep in the daytime and reduce nighttime sleep by a third or a fourth. Intensify the visualization and intentionality. {117}

man ngag gzhan gyi (117) lugs kyis rlung bzung na rmi lam yong pas 'od gsal gyi skabs su rlung mi 'dzin gsung yang / man ngag 'di'i lugs kyis rmi lam byung yang a'u rtsi/ rmi lam 'od gsal du 'gyur 'gro ba la tshegs med/ 'od gsal gyi gzhug la rmi lam byung na grogs yin/ lha sku rang shar bya ba de de nas 'ong gsung / spogs chog gi skabs 'dir rlung bsgom pa gnad du che bar bzhed/

The esoteric instructions of other traditions recommend not holding breathing exercises during the practice of Lucid Clarity because it will encourage dreaming. However, in this tradition the esoteric instructions teach that it is not a problem if dreams come. Dreams easily become lucid clarity; if dreams arise in the wake of lucid clarity, they are allies. It is taught that the natural arising of the deity’s form comes from that. The meditation on the winds during this occasion of the enhancement ritual is considered crucial.

dmigs pa dngos ni snying gar rtsa pad+ma sngon po 'dab bzhi'i rnam pa can gyi lte ba la hU~M sngon po/ 'dab ma bzhi la a nu ta ra bzhi gsal 'debs/ thams cad kyang sngon po'o/ / hU~M la sems gtad/ shes pa rig stong ngos bzung / yang hU~M las 'od 'phros yi ge bzhi la phog / 'od du ltem ltem/ de las 'od 'phros rang lus 'od du ltem ltem pa/ de las 'od 'phros snang ba thams cad 'od du ltem ltem par song / yang hU~M la sems gtad nas rig stong skyong ba sogs de ka 'dra ba lan kha re song ba na/ snang ba thams cad 'od du zhu nas rang la thim/ yang hU~M la sems gtad/ rang lus 'od du zhu nas yi ge lnga la thim/ yang hU~M la sems gtad/ pad+ma dang yi ge bzhi po yang hU~M la thim/ de la sems gtad/ hU~M yang 'ja' yal ba ltar song ba'i ngang la rig ge bar mnyam par bzhag / mtshan mo nyal ba'i tshe/ hU~M la sems gtad pa'i ngang nas ka gnyid du 'gro bar bya'o/ /

In the actual visualization, the heart channel [chakra] is in the form of a blue four-petaled lotus with a blue hūṃ in its center. Clearly visualize the four letters a–nu–ta–ra on the four petals, all of them blue. Focus on hūṃ. Recognize consciousness as empty awareness. Then light radiates from hūṃ and strikes the four letters. They fill up with light. The light radiates from that and fills your body. Light radiates from that, filling all that appears with light. Focus your attention again on hūṃ and maintain [the experience of] empty awareness and so forth. When you have repeated the process several times, all appearance melts into light and dissolves into you. Again focus your attention on hūṃ. Your body melts into light and dissolves into the five letters. Again focus your attention on hūṃ. The lotus and the four letters also dissolve into hūṃ. Focus on that. The hūṃ also vanishes like a rainbow; rest in wakeful equipoise within that state. At bedtime, focus your attention on the hūṃ and fall asleep in that state.

de dag du ka zin yong ba shas che/ gal te ma zin na zhag bdun pa'i nub mo gtor bsngo spyi de sngar bzhin byas la/ thod pa mtshan ldan dum bu gcig pa sngas 'og tu sba gsung yang / man ngag gab pa yin/ spyir de yang mi 'gal mod/ don ni thod pa mtshan ldan gnyis rnyed na rab/ ma rnyed na gcig / de yang ma rnyed na/ rin po che'i (118) snod gas chag med pa gnyis su kha zas bzang dgu la gtor mar bcos/ 'byor na sha chen cung zad kyis brgyan/ gnyis kar byin gyis brlabs nas/ mgron spyan drangs te gcig 'od gsal zin pa na gtang rag tu 'bul lo byas dar gyis bkab ste sbas la bzhag / cig shos gtor ma bsngos te/ sgrub khang gi phyi rol du mi btang bar de nyid du bzhag / gtor ma gta' mar bzung ba de rang gi sngas mgo'i phyogs su bsham dgos/ gtor bsngo'i skabs su gu gul dang / tshil chen gyi dud pa btang ngo / /

Recognition will come to most people following those methods. In case it does not, do the general torma offerings every evening for seven days as described before. It is taught that you should hide a single-piece authentic skull[4] under your pillow, although this is a concealed esoteric instruction. In general, there is certainly nothing wrong with this. But the import is that if you can find two perfect skulls it is best, or if not, then one, {118} but if you cannot find even that, use two unbroken containers made of precious material. In each of them, make tormas of many excellent ingredients. Adorn them with a little human flesh, if available. Once you consecrate them, invite the guests. State that one of them will be offered as gratitude for recognizing lucid clarity, cover it with silk, and leave it thus concealed. The other one is to be dedicated, but just leave it as is and do not throw it outside of the retreat place. You should keep it as collateral, placing it at the head of your pillow. When you dedicate the torma, send it out with the smoke of frankincense and human fat.

rang nyal ba la grogs dam tshig can nyams myong yod pa de 'dras 'od gsal zin ma zin lta bar 'jug pa sogs go yul spyi dang 'dra mod kyang / rgyu mtshan du mas 'grub dka' ba'i phyir lag len du mi mdzad de/ de phyin gtor ma dam rdzas sogs sus kyang ma mthong bar rang gcig pur byed pa gnad che gsung / nam 'od gsal zin byung ba na/ gta' mar bzhag pa'i gtor ma de yang nangs par gtang rag gi tshul du bsngo/ 'on kyang de ma thag phyir mi gtang bar zhag gsum nas bdun gyi bar nub re bzhin gtor ma de ka gsos nas bsngos/ mthar skya rengs shar ba'i dus cig khang stengs sam/ dur khrod dam ri rtser btang ngo / /

In general, it is understood that when you sleep you should arrange for a companion who upholds their sacred pledges and who has experience to watch whether or not you are grasping lucid clarity. However, in practice this is not done because it is difficult to achieve for many reasons. From this point on, no one should see the tormas and sacred substances. It is said to be extremely important to do the practice alone. When recognition of lucid clarity occurs, in the morning give thanks by dedicating the torma that was held as collateral. However, don’t throw it outside right away—keep it for three to seven days and refresh it every evening and rededicate it. Finally, one morning at the break of day, take it to the roof of the house or to a graveyard or mountaintop.

'od gsal lan cig zin pa'i mtshams nas/ sngar gyi 'phros las mtshams dam du bcad nas dmigs pa dang / 'dun pa drag pos bzhur te bsgoms na bstar chags su zin 'ong / de ka la zhud bsrungs nas zla ba gcig gnyis song na/ cung zad brtan pa thob yong de nas 'byung ba lus 'khrugs byung ba dang / grib sogs rkyen gyis bsgyur ba'i skabs ma gtogs/ nub re la lan re tsam re nges par zin 'ong / bde gsal gyi nyams rang cher med pa la dran pas zin tsam de yang yang yong (119) zhing yun yang ring rab skyong thub pa 'ong ba lags/ gnyid 'thug po thams cad la 'od gsal rtag tu zin 'ong ba la ni/ shin tu yun ring goms shing rtse gcig tu bsgom dgos pa yin no/ /

From the time that you have once recognized lucid clarity, leave the previous elaborations and enter strict retreat, paring it down to the visualization and intense intentionality. If you meditate in that way, continual recognition will come. Maintain that reduced practice and after one or two months you will attain a measure of stability. Other than the conditions caused by disturbance of the body’s elements or contamination and such, you will certainly recognize [lucid clarity] once each night. By being attentive to minor experiences of bliss-clarity and merely recognizing them, they will happen again and again and the ability to maintain them for a longer time will come. {119} As for always recognizing lucid clarity at all times during deep sleep, this requires a very long time of familiarization and single-pointed meditation.
de yang gsal stong gi 'od gsal tsam dge sbyor thun mong ba yin la/ bde stong dbyer med kyi 'od gsal ni dngos gzhi'o/ /
Besides, the mere lucid clarity of clarity-emptiness is held in common with applied virtue. The lucid clarity that is inseparable from bliss-emptiness is the main practice.
Problems during Both Dream and Lucid Clarity

rmi lam dang 'od gsal gnyis kar gyi thun mong du dmigs pa gtad nges kyis gnyid mi phebs na/ rang gi snying gar muM smug nag las 'od zer na bun 'dra ba 'phros te/ lus kyi phyi nang thams cad khyab pa yang yang bsgom/ kha zas bcud can bsten/ dal brel ran par bcags pas sel/ rmi lam dang 'od gsal zin ma thag chu nang nas theg pa ltar yer gyis byung nas sad 'ongs te/ de la lus kyi smad kyi cha'i dbus su sems gtad pas sel/ de yang nyin mo dmigs pa de ka yang yang bsgom zhing / 'di lta bu gnyid dus kyang yang yang bsgom rgyu yin snyam pa byas/ blo rtsab tsob mi bya bar lhod de bzhag / mtshan mo rmi lam 'od gsal zin pa rang gi dus kyang sad dogs chen po byas na sad 'ong bas lhod kyis byed pa gal che/

If you cannot go to sleep while focusing on these visualizations of either Dream or Lucid Clarity, then meditate again and again on a dark-brown muṃ at the heart radiating light rays like a fog that pervades everything inside and outside of your body. Rely on heavy, nutritious food and move in a measured way to clear this up. Sometimes you wake up as soon as you recognize dreams or lucid clarity, like a vehicle suddenly appearing out of water. This will be cleared up by focusing your attention in the center of the lower part of your body. You might think that meditating repeatedly on the visualization in the daytime means that you should meditate repeatedly that way during sleep. Don’t trouble yourself—relax. If you are overly worried about waking up when you recognize dreams or lucid clarity at night, then it will happen. So it is important to calm yourself.
de ltar na sad 'byams ni/ rmi lam zin ma thag dang / 'od gsal zin ma thag pa la rtag tu sad 'ong ba'i ming yin/ de lta bu byung na thabs de kas sel/
