Excessive insomnia (sad ’byams) is the name given to the condition of always waking up as soon as you recognize dreams or as soon as you recognize lucid clarity. If that happens, these methods will clear it up.

dmigs pa dang 'dun pa rgyun du sbyangs kyang rmi lam dang 'od gsal zin dus med/ bsgoms ma bsgoms med pa 'dra ba de la 'dir 'khrul 'byams zer/ rim lda gdan rdzogs sogs man ngag gzhan la lan brdugs 'byams su grags/ rmi lam zin ma thag 'khrul 'gro na/ man ngag 'di'i lugs kyi 'khrul 'byams stobs chung ba zer/ nA ro'i gdams par grags pa rnams na (120) dred 'byams zer/ gnyid kyi 'od gsal la dred 'byams 'di cher mi 'ong / rmi lam la 'di rang mang bas sel thabs gal che/

If at no time is there recognition of dreams and lucid clarity even though you continuously practice the visualization and intentionality, such that it makes no difference whether you meditate or not, that is called excessive delusion (’khrul ’byams). According to other esoteric instructions, such as in Five Stages Complete in One Sitting,[5] this is known as excessive discipline response.[6] If you become deluded immediately after recognizing dreams, this is called less powerful excessive delusion in the esoteric instructions of this tradition. In the well-known instructions of Nāropa, it is called excess stubbornness (dred ’byams). {120} This excess stubbornness does not often affect the lucid clarity of sleep, but it is common in this Dream practice, so methods to clear it up are important.

nyal khar 'dun pa btang res kyi/ rmi lam 'dzin pa'i skabs yin na/ gnyid 'thug por song nas rmi lam mi 'ong / 'od gsal gyi skabs yin na gnyid mi phebs/ de la stong 'byams zer/ rmi lam ma byung ba la nyin mo rlung sbyor mang du byas pas ka phan/

Set your intention each time you fall asleep. If dreams do not come once you have entered deep sleep when practicing recognition of dreams, or if sleep does not come when practicing Lucid Clarity, that is what’s called excessive emptiness (stong ’byams). It will help to do a lot of breathing exercise during the day for this scarcity of dreams.

gnyid 'thug po dang rmi lam gyi skabs su 'dzag gegs 'byung ba la bde 'byams zer/ de yang rmi lam du ni chags pa'i rkyen dang / bag chags dang / gdon rkyen sogs sna tshogs yin/ dngos dang rmi lam gang la'ang de byung tsa na/ rmi lam gyi rtsal yang phal cher nyams 'gro/ skabs 'gar lan re lan gnyis khyad med pa 'dra byung na'ang rim pas nyams 'gro zhing / khyad par rmi lam kyi dge sbyor gsal stong bde ba'i lha sku bkrag can de rtsa ba nas 'jig / 'od gsal gyi skabs byung na ni lan re kho nas 'od gsal nyams 'gro/ dam sel dang / gdon rkyen dang / gang 'dzag gis yin na/ slar bsgoms kyang rgyang tsam sor chud pa dka' bar yod/ gang ltar de thams cad la sel thabs gegs rang grol gyi skabs bzhin no/ /

The problem of emission during deep sleep and Dream practice is called excessive bliss (bde ’byams). This has various causes, such as desire within the dream, habitual tendencies, and the influence of spirits. Whether for real or in dreams, when this happens the dynamic energy of dreams is usually compromised. It may seem that it makes no difference if it happens occasionally once or twice, but gradually it leads to deterioration. In particular, it will destroy the very roots of the virtuous application of Dream—the clarity-emptiness and the brilliant form of the deity. If this occurs even once during the practice of Lucid Clarity, it will lead to the deterioration of lucid clarity. If [emissions] are due to lapsed sacred pledge, or the influence of spirits, or fullness, even if you meditate again it will be distant and difficult to restore. In any case, the methods for clearing up all of those issues is in the section on Naturally Liberating Obstructions (session 12).

'byams pa ces pa lan re lan gnyis la mi zer gyi/ yang yang byung bas lang shor chen por song ba'i ming ngo / / 'on kyang ma 'byams gong thog ma nas ka gcod pa gal che gsung / de dag kyang ngang thung zhing 'dod thag nye ba'i dbang du byas kyi/ rtsis btab med par rtag tu nyams su len pa la nam zhig na 'byams pa thams cad rang shugs kyis chod par 'gyur ro/ /

“Excessive” does not apply to one or two occurrences. It is a term for something that arises again and again, that has become entrenched as a really bad habit. Nevertheless, it is said to be very important to cut it off right from the start, before it becomes excessive. This concerns those who are very impatient and expectant. For those who continually practice without calculating results, at some point all excesses will end automatically.
Transference

'pho ba'i skabs su 'chug med mkha' spyod kyi 'pho ba la sngon 'gro gzhung 'pho gzhan dang 'dra/ rang (121) gi spyi bo'i steng gi nam mkha' la chos 'byung gru gsum nyis rtseg phyi dkar la nang dmar ba/ bde bar rgyu zhing bde bar 'char ba/ de'i dbus su rje btsun rdo rje rnal 'byor ma sku mdog dmar mo/ g.yas rdo rje phyar ba/ g.yon thod khrag thugs kar gtod pa/ mchan khung du kha T+wAM ga sku g.yas 'gying zhabs bsgrad pa'i stabs kyis bzhugs pa/ rgyan dang cha byad yongs su rdzogs pa/ pad nyi dang mi ro mgo g.yon du bstan pa'i gdan la bzhugs pa/ 'khor tshogs dpag tu med pa dang bcas pa bsgom/

In the section on Transference to the Unerring Celestial Realm (session 52), the preliminary is the same as in other source texts on Transference. {121} Meditate that in the space above your head there is a double-stacked tetrahedral source of phenomena, white outside and red inside. Its cause is bliss, and it arouses bliss. In its center is Exalted Vajrayoginī. She is red and brandishes a vajra with her right hand and a blood-filled skull cup at her heart with her left hand, a khaṭvāṅga in the bend of her elbow. She stands in a left-leaning pose with her legs in a wide stance. All her ornaments and accessories are totally complete. She stands on a seat of lotus, sun, and a man’s corpse with its head facing to the left. She has an immeasurable entourage around her.

rang lus tha mal du ka gsal ba'i rkang mthil gnyis dang bshang lam du raM yig me'i rang bzhin can gsal btab/ de las me lce 'ur gyis 'bar nas lus thams cad zhu zhing khol/ ye shes bdud rtsi'i rang bzhin du gyur/ rje btsun rdo rje rnal 'byor ma'i phyag gi thod par yang song zhing / gtso 'khor thams cad kyi zhal rang du'ang gsol bas thugs rgyud bde bas tshim par gyur/ de lta bu lan gsum bsgom/ de nas rang nyid he ru ka yab rkyang du gyur/ lus kyi dbus su rtsa dbu ma spyi dang 'dra/ lte bar rnam shes kyi ngo bo a dkar po dang / gsang gnas su rlung gi ngo bo hU~M sngon po 'od 'phro ba zhig gsal btab/ 'jam rlung cung zad bzung / rlung phyir bsal ba'i tshe hika ring po brjod/ de'i tshe gsang ba'i hU~M gi rlung shugs kyis lte ba'i a khyer te/ dbu ma'i lam brgyud spyi bo nas thon/ bcom ldan 'das ma rdo rje rnal 'byor ma'i gsang ba'i sgo nas zhugs/ thugs ka tsam du sleb par mos/

Visualize your own body in its ordinary form. Imagine the letter raṃ, the nature of fire, in the two soles of your feet and at the anus. Tongues of fire blaze up with a rumble from those letters, melting and boiling your whole body. It becomes the nature of the elixir of timeless awareness, as does the contents of the skull cup in Exalted Vajrayoginī’s hand. She and all the entourage along with yourself drink of it, satisfying their mind streams with bliss. Meditate in this way three times. Then you become Heruka as sole father. Within your body is the central channel as usual. Visualize a white A, the essence of consciousness, at the navel and a blue hūṃ, the essence of vital winds, in the perineum, radiating light. Slightly hold the gentle breath. When you exhale the breath, utter a long drawn-out “hik.” At that time, the force of the winds of hūṃ in the perineum carries the A at the navel up through the length of the central channel and out the cranial aperture. Imagine that it enters through Bhagavatī Vajrayoginī’s vagina and arrives at her heart.

de nas man ngag gi yig rnying rang nas/ de lta bu'i dmigs pa lan gsum bskyar/ de rjes rdo rje rnal 'byor ma (122) mkha' dbyings mthon por gshegs pa dang / yang mar phebs pa sogs bsgom par bshad kyang / lag len la de ltar mi mdzad te/ sngar gyi dmigs pa de lta bu lan bdun skyor/ re re bzhin rang sems dang / rdo rje rnal 'byor ma dang / stong pa gsum dbyer med du bsres pa la mnyam par 'jog / mthar rang sems dang rdo rje rnal 'byor ma'i byin rlabs dbyer med pa bdud rtsi dkar la dmar ba'i mdangs chags pa'i rnam par song gsang ba'i sgo nas byon/ bdud rtsi'i rgyun rang nyid yi dam gyi skur gsal ba'i spyi gtsug nas zhugs/ spyi bo'i 'khor lo gang bum dbang / mgrin pa gang gsang dbang / snying ga gang shes rab ye shes/ lte ba gang dbang bzhi pa thob/ rtsa thams cad byang chub kyi sems kyis gang / nyams bde bas khyab pa la cung zad mnyam par bzhag / de lta bu yang yang bsgom pa yin/

The esoteric instructions in the old texts explain that you should repeat this visualization three times, after which you meditate that Vajrayoginī ascends to the realm of space, then descends, and so on. {122} However, this is not done in practice. Do the previous visualization seven times, each time these three—your own mind, Vajrayoginī, and emptiness—blend inseparably. Rest in the equipoise of that. In the end, your mind inseparable from Vajrayoginī’s blessings in the form of white elixir with a red radiance emerges from her vagina. The stream of elixir enters the cranial aperture of you as the yidam. As it fills the crown chakra, you obtain the vase empowerment. Filling the throat, the secret empowerment; filling the heart the wisdom awareness; and filling the navel, the fourth empowerment. All the channels are filled with bodhicitta. The experience of bliss pervades all; rest awhile in equipoise. This is the meditation to be done again and again.

thun 'jog khar rdo rje rnal 'byor ma chos 'byung dang bcas pa 'od du zhu/ / spyi bo nas zhugs te rang nyid la thim/ spyi bo tshangs bug gi sgo yang baM yig dmar po mgo bo thur du blta ba/ 'od zer 'phro bas bkag par bsam/

To conclude the session, Vajrayoginī and the source of phenomena melt into light, enter through the crown of your head, and dissolve into you. Imagine that there is a red upside-down letter vaṃ in the opening of the cranial aperture that radiates light rays that block the opening.

'chug med mkha' spyod kyi 'pho ba 'di la yig chung gcig yod/ mkha' 'gro ma ni gu las byung ba bdag khyung po rnal 'byor ba'i lugs so zer ba de yin no/ / gzhan 'pho ba bar do spyi bka' rang gi dmigs pa de ka 'chug med mkha' spyod kyi 'pho ba yin gsungs pa grags che/ yang rdo rje rnal 'byor ma'i phyag mtshan gyi 'pho ba la ngos 'dzin pa'ang yod de 'di dang mthun shas che/ mkha' spyod dmar mo'i 'pho ba la 'chug med 'pho ba'i mtshan byang btags pa gcig kyang yod pas 'dzug tshugs ma byung na 'di ngos zin pa dkon par 'ong / 'chug med mkha' spyod gsar (123) pa tsho re zhig pha ri la zhog ang / /

There is a short text on this called Transference to the Unerring Celestial Realm.[7] It is the one that says [in the colophon], “This is my, Khyungpo Naljor’s, tradition, which I received from Ḍākinī Niguma.” It is well known that the visualizations in the other general precepts of Transference and Intermediate State are called “transference to the unerring celestial realm.” As well, a transference of Vajrayoginī’s hand implement[8] has been identified as this, which is somewhat similar. The term “unerring transference” (’chug med ’pho ba) has also been applied to the Red Khecarī Transference. So it seems that unless it has been definitely established, [the correct] identification will become rare. {123} Please keep any new “unerring celestial realms” far away.

yang sgrub po gang zhig chos 'di la brten pa'i gzhan lus sgom pa yin na/ bla ma'i rnal 'byor thams cad la bla ma nyid shes rab dang bcas pa'am/ rdo rje 'chang chen po yum can du bsgom par bya'o/ / ces pa'ang gsung rgyun gcig go /

If there are practitioners who meditate on another’s body based on this teaching, meditate in all guru yoga practices that the guru has the wisdom [partner] or that Great Vajradhara is with the mother. This is the traditional teaching.
Concluding Words

'dir smras pa/ dpa' bo dang bcas rnal 'byor ma dpal bye ba'i gtsug rgyan ni gu ma/ / gang gi zhal bum bdud rtsi'i rgyun de srid 'di'i nyes kun dag byed te/ skal ldan yongs kyi snying gi gsos gyur 'di 'dra thob pa'ang skal pa bzang / / gang phyir 'di la gzhan dring mi 'jog cung zad goms pa'i snang ba'ang thob/ / ces bya'o/ ! /

Niguma, crown jewel of a million glorious yoginīs with their heroes, who purifies all flaws of this existence with the stream of elixir from the vase of her mouth, and nurtures completely the hearts of the fortunate, who are sublimely fortunate to receive such as this, since I have attained the appearance of some familiarity independently of others.
III.
III. Summary of Jeweled Light Garland
na mo gu ru/
namo guru

rin po che 'od kyi phreng ba zhes pa'i man ngag gi gzhung / mnyam med rin chen brtson 'grus kyis mdzad pa de'i nyams len gyi snying po ni/ man ngag thams cad lus gsum la gnad du bsnun par 'dus pa yin/

This is the essence of the practices in the source esoteric instruction Jeweled Light Garland by the incomparable [Mokchokpa] Rinchen Tsöndru.[9] It is a summary that targets the vital points of the three bodies of all esoteric instructions.

de la rnam smin gyi lus ni/ rtsa ba dug gsum gyis bskyed/ rgyu las kyis 'phangs/ rkyen 'byung ba lngas bsgyur ba'o/ / rgyu mtshan des na dngos por 'dzin pa'i nyon mongs rtag tu ldang / rgyu'i rjes su 'gro bas rang dbang med/ 'byung ba lnga'i gnod pa phyi snod la brten nas kyang 'byung / nang nad dang dgra dang gdon gsum du ldang / de yang las dang nyon mongs de dang po yid kyis bskyed/ bar du bag chags kyi tshul gyis bsags/ mthar bde sbug tu rnam par smin pa yin/ sad dus 'di la 'khrul pas rmi lam bag chags kyi lus la yang 'khrul te/ nyon mongs las dang bde sdug ldang /

First is the fully ripened body (rnam smin gyi lus). Its basis is the three poisons from which it arises. Its cause is the impetus of karmic action. Its contributing conditions are the five elements that transform it. For those reasons, the afflictive emotions that fixate on the reality of things always rise up. The result of these causes is that there is no independence. The harm by the five elements occurs based on the external environment. Internally, sickness, enemies, and malicious spirits rise up. Actions and afflictions are first generated by mentation (yid). In the interim they accumulate as habitual tendencies, and in the end they fully ripen as happiness and suffering. The body of habitual tendency (bag chags kyi lus) in dreams is more deluded than the delusion of this waking time. Afflictions, karma, and happiness and suffering rise up.

de gnyis las 'khrul pas yid lus la yang 'khrul te/ nyon mongs las dang sdug bsngal gyi snang ba shar/ yid lus kyi skabs der (124) sngar gyi nyon mongs sogs kyis rgyu byas/ de dus kyi gsum pos rkyen byas nas/ yang rnam smin gyi lus bskyed pa sogs 'khor lo 'khor ba ltar 'khyams pa yin/

The mental body (yid lus) [of the intermediate state] is even more deluded than those two. The appearances of afflictions, karma, and suffering arise. {124} There, during the time of the mental body, the previous afflictions and so forth act as a cause and at that time all three—[afflictions, karma, and suffering]—as the contributing conditions. Then again the fully ripened body is created and so forth; one wanders [from body to body] like a cycling wheel.

de la rnam smin gyi lus kyi 'khrul pa dag byed kyi thabs la/ sems 'khrul pa'i dngos kyi gnyen por sgyu ma lta bur shes pa dang / 'khrul pa de la brten lus kyi rgyu byas pas lus la gnad du bsnun pa cig dgos so/ /

You need techniques to purify the delusion of the fully ripened body. That would be the understanding of illusoriness as an antidote to the actual delusion of the mind and a method that targets the vital points of the body, since it was that delusion that acted as the cause for the body.
A.
A. Illusoriness
de la 'dun pa rgyun chags dang / man ngag btsan thabs gnyis so/ /
This has two parts: (1) continual intentionality and (2) esoteric instructions on forceful methods.
des na dang po ni/
1. Continual Intentionality

brgyud pa'i bla ma sogs skyabs gnas thams cad rtsa ba'i bla ma la bstim ste/ gsol ba rgyun chad med par btab/ rang lus dang snang ba thams cad bden med sgyu ma lta bu'i 'dun pa drag tu sbyang / thun mtshams thams cad du yang sgyu ma'i 'dun pa khar phog snar phog tu sbyang / de ltar bsgoms kyang nyin par sgyu ma lta bu dang mi rtog pa yang bogs ma thon/ mtshan mo rmi lam yang mi zin na/

When all the sources of refuge, such as the lineage gurus, dissolve into the root guru, you make continual supplications. You train intensely in the intentionality that your own body and all appearances are not real, like an illusion. In all session breaks, also train with the intentionality of illusion by admonishing yourself with harsh [statements about illusoriness]. If you meditate like that but it still does not enhance your [realization of] illusoriness and impermanence in the daytime, and you don’t recognize dreams at night, then you need the second part.
gnyis pa man ngag btsan thabs kyis 'dzin pa ni/
2. Esoteric Instructions on Forceful Methods to Recognize [Dreams]

nyin mo lung stong du gcer bur mchongs rgyug byed pa la sogs pa nyam nga med pa'i spyod pa mang po dang / bla ma yi dam mkha' 'gro rnams la gnad la bor ba'i gsol ba btab/ mtshan mo nam smad skyil krung ltag bsnyes dang / tsog pu dang / seng ge'i nyal stabs gsum po gang rung byas nas/ rmi lam bsgyur ba'i 'dun pa drag po'i ngang nas gnyid du 'gro bar bya/ der rmi lam dam du ma zin 'ong / gnyid sad pa'i dus na/ shar dang snang dang don byed nus/ / shes nas grol bar byed pa yin/ rmi lam dang da lta'i snang ba gnyis/ dang por shar tsam gyi gnas skabs dang / de'i ngang la gnas nas rnam 'gyur sna tshogs su snang ba dang / rang dus nyid nas don byed (125) nus pa ste gsum po'i sgo nas khyad par med/ gnas tshul la cung zad kyang ma grub par yang khyad par med/ sgyu ma lta bu'o snyam 'dun pa drag tu sbyang / de ltar nan tan du bsgoms pas rmi lam zin ni 'ong /

In the daytime, engage in many fearless behaviors, such as running and jumping naked through an empty valley. Pray to the guru, yidam, and ḍākinīs to get to the point. At night, during the second half, assume one of three positions: cross-legged and leaning back, sitting with legs drawn up, or the lion’s reclining position. Go to sleep while in a state of intense intentionality to transform dreams. There, you will come to realize various dreams.[10] [Blend them] when you wake from sleep. Understanding arising and appearance and ability to function will be liberating. Both in dreams and in the current perceptions—from the circumstances of their initial arising, the various changing perceptions after you remain in that state, and your ability to function from that very moment [of their arising]—in terms of those three, there is no difference [in dreaming and waking]. {125} And since their abiding nature is not even slightly existent, there is absolutely no difference. Think, “It is like an illusion” and cultivate fierce intentionality. By persistently meditating in that way, you will come to recognize dreams.

sbyong ba la yang bag tsha byung na/ da lta'i bden zhen gyi 'gab 'dre 'brangs pa yin pas/ de la 'di snyam du na tsha sdug bsngal bskyed pa'i lus de mal na yod/ 'di ni yid kyi lus yin na 'jigs rgyu sogs ci yod snyam pas gang zin du sbyang / cung zad 'byongs nas 'byung bzhi sprul bsgyur la bslab/ rig pa dang rlung dpangs gtod te nyi zla'i steng du 'gro ba dang / gting du smad nas rgya mtsho'i gting du 'gro ba dang / lha'i gnas sogs nyul/ bde ba can sogs zhing khams blta/ po Ta la dang ri bo rtse lnga dang lcang lo can du rigs gsum mgon po'i zhal blta gdams ngag zhu/ dgyes rdor bde mchog sogs kyi dkyil 'khor la mchod cing dbang dang gdams ngag zhu/ rang gzhan rigs drug snod bcud thams cad yi dam lha'i dkyil 'khor du bsgom/ snang stong sgyu ma lta bur shes par bya/

If you become apprehensive while refining dreams, it is because the hidden demon of clinging to the reality of here and now follows after you. In that case, think, “The body that produces sickness and suffering is in bed; this now is a mental body, so what is the reason for fear and such.” Thinking that, refine whatever you recognize. Once it is somewhat refined, train in emanating and changing the four elements. Elevate your awareness and vital winds and soar above the sun and moon. Dive down to the depths and move through the ocean. Wander in the places of the gods and elsewhere. View the pure realms of Sukhāvatī, Potala, Wu-t’ai-shan, and Aḍakavatī. See the lords of the three families and request their teachings. Make offerings to the mandalas of Hevajra, Cakrasaṃvara, and others and request empowerment and instruction. Meditate on yourself and others—all the environment and its inhabitants of six kinds of beings—as the yidam deities in the mandala. Understand that these empty appearances are like an illusion.

yang thog ma lha skur shar ba de tha mal pa'i lus su log 'gro na/ 'khrul pa'i bag chags kyi shugs rjes su 'brang ba yin pas gnyid sad ma thag tu dmigs pa dang sgyu ma'i 'dun pa drag tu bsgom/ dpe'i sgyu ma ni me long gi gzugs brnyan la bstod smad dga' ba med pa bsgom/ don gyi sgyu ma ni shar tsam nyid nas bden med la bzhag / gnyis med sgyu ma lha sku snang stong du shar bar bya/ snang stong bde ba dpe dang bsre/ de don dang bsre/ de zung 'jug tu bsre ba'o/ /

Also, at first when you arise in the deity’s form, if you then revert to your ordinary body, it is because the force of deluded habit adheres. Therefore, as soon as you wake up, meditate on the visualization and the intense intentionality of illusion. The illusion example is like your reflection in a mirror, to which you can address praise or blame without feeling pleasure [or displeasure]; meditate on that. Ultimate illusion is not real from the moment it arises; rest in that. Nondual illusion is the arising of the deity as appearance-emptiness. Blend appearance-emptiness bliss with example. Blend that with the ultimate. Blend that in unity.

gzhan yang sgyu ma'i dpe gsum gyis mtshon pa dang / 'dod chags (126) dang bral ba dang / shes rab rnam gsum dang / rnam thar gsum dang / phyi dang nang gi phar phyin drug dang / phyag rgya bzhi dang / dga' ba bzhi dang / ting 'dzin gsum sogs thams cad de ka la tshang / rmi lam sogs su gdon gyi cho 'phrul thams cad rang dag la 'gro/ 'gro drug lha skur shar bas bar do dag par the tshom med do/ /

Furthermore, the referents of the three examples of illusion, the freedom from desire, {126} the three wisdoms, the three [doors of] liberation, the outer and inner six perfections, the four seals, the four ecstasies, the three absorptions, and so forth are all included in that.[11] Apparitions of spirits in dreams and otherwise will all be naturally purified. The six kinds of migrators will arise as deities and the intermediate state will be purified, without doubt.
gnyis pa ni
B. Methods That Target the Vital Points of the Body

de ltar nyams su blangs kyang / dang por skye dka'/ bar du 'byongs dka'/ tha mar brtan pa thob pa dka' na/ mos gus dang / 'dun pa'i gnad sngar gyi de ka'i steng du lus la gnad du bsnun pa'i man ngag dgos te/

Even though you practice along those lines, if at first [dreams] arising is difficult, in the middle refining is difficult, and in the end attaining stability is difficult, then in addition to devotion and the previous vital points of intentionality, you need esoteric instructions to target the vital points of the body.

de yang lus gnad seng ge'i nyal stabs bya/ mgrin par pad+ma'i dbus su oM dmar po 'dab ma bzhi la a nu ta ra bsgom te/ rmi lam 'dzin pa'am sbyong ba'i 'dun pa drag po sbyang / des rmi lam gyi bogs thon par the tshom med/ sad dus kyi snang ba nas rmi lam la 'jug kham dang / gnyid phri phri ba dang / gnyid la hrum gyis song ba dang / rmi lam 'char ka ma ste/ dus bzhi po der rlung sems 'du ba'i gnad mgrin pa na yod pa'o/ / de klu sgrub kyi gdams pa yin no/ /

Assume the vital physical posture of the reclining lion. Meditate on the lotus in the throat with red oṃ in its center and a–nu–ta–ra on the four petals. Cultivate the intentionality of recognizing or refining dreams. Have no doubts that this will enhance the Dream practice. The throat is the vital point where wind-mind gathers during four times: when about to enter dreams from the appearances of waking time; when sleep approaches; when sleep is upon you; and when about to have a dream. That is Nāgārjuna’s instruction.

yang snying ga'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus su mar me lta bu 'od dkar la rtse mo dmar ba sor bzhi pa cig bsgoms la/ de la rig pa bcug cing rlung yang cung zad bsdams/ nyin mtshan du de ltar bsgoms na/ nyin mtshan gyi 'od gsal gnyis kar 'char/ 'od gsal gyi man ngag bsgom bde zhing / dmigs pa gsal 'dus zab pa 'di lta bu gzhan la med/ grub thob lwa ba pa'i gdams ngag yin gsung /

Also, in the center of the channel chakra in the heart, meditate on white light like a candle with a red tip four finger-widths high. Hold your awareness in that and constrict the breathing somewhat. If you meditate in this way day and night, then lucid clarity will arise both day and night. This kind of felicitous meditation instruction on Lucid Clarity—with clear, concise, and profound visualization—is not found elsewhere. It is taught as the instructions of the adept Lavapa.

yang smin phrag gnad kyi sgor/ thig le dkar la 'tsher ba/ snum la 'dril ba/ (127) che ste mthe bong tsam/ chung na rgya sran tsam nyams bde ba cig gsal btab/ de la rlung sems drag tu bcug / 'di 'od gsal gyi 'dun pa dang sbyar na 'od gsal zin/ rmi lam gyi 'dun pa sbyar na rmi lam zin pa yin na'ang / gtso bor sad dus sgyu lus kyi gdams ngag yin/ gnyid sad dus kyi snang ba/ dpral ba'i 'khor lo dang sbyor ba'i lung yod pa bzhin no/ / 'di rnal 'byor ma skal pa bzang po'i bzhed pa yin no gsung /

Also, at the opening of the vital point between the eyebrows, imagine there is a vital drop—luminous white, oily, no bigger than a thumb, no smaller than a bean, and blissful. {127} Intensely insert wind-mind there. If this is accompanied by the intentionality of lucid clarity, then you will recognize lucid clarity. If it is accompanied by the intentionality of dreams, dreams will be recognized. This is mainly an instruction for realizing illusory body during waking life. It is similar to the [practice] during waking appearances of joining the winds at the throat chakra. It is taught as the approach of Yoginī Kalpa Zangmo.

rje btsun rmog lcog pa nyid kyi rnam thar na/ gdams pa 'di gsum bur sgom las brgyud par bshad pas/ de ltar yang yin mod kyi/ mgrin pa'i yi ge la sems gtod pa 'di/ 'od gsal dang rmi lam gyi spogs chog gi skabs na yod pa dang / smin mtshams kyi thig le rmi lam gyi dbang gi skabs na yod pas/ mkha' 'gro ni gu ma nyid kyi gdams pa dang 'brel zhing / snying ga'i mar me yang thig le la 'od gsal 'dzin pa dang gnad gcig cing / lwa ba pa dang ni gu ma gnyis kyang gdams ngag byin rlabs kyi rkang gcig par bshad pas/ ni gu'i chos drug dang ma 'brel ba ma yin no/ / 'di yang gtum mo ma gtogs/ bsre ba sgyu lus kyi gnad kun rdzogs pa man ngag gi rkang yongs su tshang ba cig go / rin chen 'od phreng gi man ngag go ! / lam dri med 'od phreng las chos drug gi snying po 'di tsam gsungs so/ /

In the life story of Venerable Mokchokpa, it is explained that these three instructions came from the lineage of Burgom.[12] Although that is certainly the case, this [instruction to] focus the attention on the letters in the throat is also contained in the section on enhancement practices for Lucid Clarity and Dream [in Niguma’s Six Dharmas]. The vital drop between the eyebrows in found in the section on empowerment of Dream practice. Therefore, these instructions are related to the teachings of Ḍākinī Niguma. The practice of the candle at the heart is the same vital point as grasping lucid clarity in the vital drop, which is explained as the same basis of instruction blessings from both Lavapa and Niguma. Therefore they are not unrelated to the Six Dharmas of Niguma. Furthermore, other than Fierce Inner Heat, this [teaching] fully contains the basic esoteric instructions of all the complete vital points for blending [dream] with illusory body. This concludes the esoteric instructions from Jeweled Light Garland.
IV.
IV. The Heart of the Six Dharmas from Stainless Light Garland of the Path[13]

sngon 'gro'i skabs gsum la skyabs 'gro logs su ma gsungs kyang kha 'gengs dgos/ sems bskyed spyi dang mtshungs/ bla ma'i rnal 'byor logs su byed de/ sgyu lus kyi skabs dang mtshungs pa las/ byang chub kyi sems rtogs pa dang / stong nyid rtogs pa rgyud la skye bar (128) gsol ba 'debs/

In the section on the three preliminaries, going for refuge is not mentioned separately but should be added. Arousing the awakening mind is the same as usual. Guru yoga is done separately [for each dharma], basically the same as in the Illusory Body practice (session 13), except for the supplication: “I pray that realization of the mind of awakening and the realization of emptiness arise in my being.” {128}
'jug tu bla ma'i skyabs 'gro ma nam ma re mdzad/

To begin [the main practices], go for refuge in the guru each time by saying: All sentient beings, my mothers, equal to the reaches of space, [go for refuge in the precious guru, the unified essence of all refuges.]
dngos gzhi thabs lam la byin rlabs bla ma'i gtum mo bsgom/ rlung rtar zhon pa yang 'di ka yin gsung /
In the main practice of the Path of Methods, meditate on the Inner Heat of the Guru’s Blessing. This is also said to be the [Inner Heat practice of] Riding the Wind Horse.
de nas srid pa'i dbang zhu ba yang bsgom te dmigs pa gnyis yod/
Then meditate on receiving the Empowerment of Existence. There are these two visualizations.

sgyu lus la rang lus snang stong lha sku dang / 'gro drug sgyu mar 'char byed gnyis sbrags te bsgom/ spyir dben pa bsten/ bla ma'i mos gus kyis rkyab phul/ tshe 'di pa skyabs kyi mi dang mi 'grogs/ spyod lam thams cad rang bzhin med rtogs kyis zin par bya/

In Illusory Body, meditate on the two techniques together: One’s Body as the Empty Appearance of the Deity’s Form and Making the Six Kinds of Migrators Arise as Illusion. In general, rely on seclusion with guru devotion as the support.[14] Do not befriend those who take refuge in this life. In all activities, keep to the realization that [all phenomena] lack any true nature.

chos drug rgyas pa'i skabs/ deng sang sgyu lus sgos kyi dbang bkar grags shing gab bsgyur dgos rgyu de ting nge 'dzin gyi tshul gyis len/ gdams ngag 'di'i dbang du byas na/ bsre ba sgyu lus spyi'i tshar gsum khug pa yin gsung / lar gtum mo'i dbang yin/ khrid 'di 'phogs na/ gtum mo'i dbang 'di ka sgo 'byed kyi dbang du bskur ba yin par bshad do/ /

In the context of the extensive Six Dharmas, these days one needs the revealed secret known as the particular permission of Illusory Body.[15] Take that in the style of a meditative absorption [empowerment]. In terms of this instruction [of Stainless Light Garland of the Path], it is said that blending becomes three times better than in the general practice of Illusory Body. Also it is the empowerment of Fierce Inner Heat: it is explained that to bestow this guidance, the actual empowerment of Fierce Inner Heat is conferred to open the door.
rmi lam 'dzin pa'i dmigs pa gsum yod/
There are three visualizations for recognizing dreams.

dmigs pa dang po ni/ spyi bor haM dkar po/ gsang bar phaT dmar skya/ haM las thig le chad bde mchog dkar por gyur/ phaT las thig le chad pas rje btsun mar gyur te/ kha sbyor du bzhugs pas lus sems bde bas khyab/ mdun du'ang de lta bu bsgom/ rmi lam gyi 'dun pa sbyangs/ mtshan mo gnyid du 'gro khar mdun gyi de rang nyid kyi snying ga'i lhan skyes la thim/ de yang 'od du lam pa la mtha' nas yal mi dmigs par bzhag /

The first visualization is of a white haṃ in the top of the head and a pink phaṭ in the perineum. A drop of vital essence breaks off from the haṃ and becomes white Cakrasaṃvara. A vital drop breaks off from phaṭ and becomes Exalted [Vajravārāhī]. Their union [at your heart] pervades your body and mind with bliss. Meditate on the same thing in front of you. Cultivate the intentionality of recognizing dreams. At night, when going to sleep, the deities in front dissolve into the couple in your heart. That also [melts into] dazzling light that vanishes from the outside inward; then rest without visualization.
dmigs pa gnyis pa rang zin thig le dbang bzhi'i gnad rang yin/
The second visualization is self-recognition [based on] the Vital Points of the Four Empowerments of Drops.

dmigs pa gsum pa rtog med la bzung ba gnyis kyi bla ma la brten pa de yin/ sbyang ba ni/ 'dun pas sbyang ba la mdzad de/ (129) spel sprul bsgyur gsum yang de ka'i ngang nas byed/ yul snang gi dmigs pa yang stan thog gcig ma'i skabs su bshad pa de bsgom/

The third visualization, from the two [techniques for] Recognizing Dreams without Concepts, is the one based on the guru (session 21). Dreams are refined through intentionality. {129} Increasing, emanating, and changing dreams are also done in that [way]. For the visualization of ascertaining objective appearances, meditate as was explained [previously] in the section on [the Six Dharmas] in a single sitting.
gnyid kyi 'od gsal 'dzin pa'i man ngag bla ma la brten nas 'od gsal 'dzin pa de kho na len par mdzad/
In the esoteric instructions for grasping the lucid clarity of sleep, practice only Recognizing Lucid Clarity Based on the Guru.
des rtsa ba'i chos bzhi'i don gyi snying po tshang / 'pho ba bar do'i dmigs pa logs su mi dgos/ 'dod na khrid rgyas par 'byung ba bzhin no/

This completes the heart of the meaning of the four root dharmas. Separate visualizations for Transference and Intermediate State are unnecessary. If you wish, follow the [instructions in] the extensive guidance.
nyams len gyi tshul 'di la brten pa'i sgom chen pa la dgos pa'i go don mang po yod pa rnams ni/ 'gro mgon sangs rgyas ston pa nyid kyi bka' las shes par bya'o/ /
Great meditators who follow this style of practice have need of many significant points, which can be learned from the [actual text] taught by the protector of migrators, Sangye Tönpa himself.
V.
V. Esoteric Instructions from Ocean of Experiential Qualities[16]

yang nyams myong yon tan rgya mtsho las 'byung ba'i man ngag ni/ gang zag 'ga' zhig lus ngag gi rtsol ba zhen pas/ thabs lam sgom par mi nus pa'am/ blo rigs kyis bsgom par mi spro na'ang / gsang sngags kyi rdzogs rim nyams len la kha 'chad pa med te/ sgyu lus rmi lam 'od gsal gsum gyis lam thams cad cha tshang la ma nor ba yin gsung /

Some individuals who are attached to physical and verbal effort either cannot meditate on the Path of Methods or else are not interested in meditating on it due to their particular mindset (blo rigs). However, that does not disqualify them from practicing the completion phase of Secret Mantra. It is said that all paths are complete and correct within the three [practices] of Illusory Body, Dream, and Lucid Clarity.

de yang dal 'byor rnyed dka'/ 'chi ba mi rtag pa/ 'khor ba'i nyes dmigs rnams shes pas nyams len la 'dun pa bskyed/ gzhi lam 'bras bu thams cad zab pa dang rgya che ba zung 'jug tu go / de ltar ma rtogs pa'i sems can la sems bskyed tshad med bzhi dang 'brel ba byed/

The understanding of the free and endowed, difficult-to-find [human life], death and impermanence, and the shortcomings of cyclic existence will produce the intention to practice. Know that all the ground, path, and fruition are the unity of profundity and vastness. Arouse the awakening mind and the related four immeasurable attitudes toward sentient beings who do not realize this.

dngos gzhi la dang po sgyu lus dbang po rab 'bring gsum gyi/ rab ni mos gus bla ma'i lam khyer nyid yin pa las/ bla ma'i bzhugs gdan pad zla kho na dang / bla ma sku dngos yin pa la mtshan dpes brgyan pa bskyed/ gsol 'debs kyi skabs/ sgyu ma la sgyu mar ngo shes pa dang / rmi lam la rmi lam du ngo shes par mdzad du gsol/ / zhes pa (130) gsung ba yod kyang mtha' gcig tu ma nges pas don gcig pa'i phyir/ gzhung khrid ltar byas pas chog gsung /

In the main part, first is Illusory Body for those of best, average, and lesser capabilities. The best is the [same as the practice of] the actual integration of devotion to the guru, except that here you visualize the guru’s seat as only a lotus and moon and the guru’s body as their actual one but adorned with the signs and marks [of perfection]. On the occasion of supplication, say, “[Precious guru], I pray to recognize illusion as illusion” and “I pray to recognize dreams as dreams.” {130} That is what [the text] says, but that is not the only way. Since the meaning is the same in the source guidance, it is acceptable to follow that.

dbang po 'bring ni rang lus snang stong lha sku nyid yin pa las/ snang ba thams cad kyi steng du 'dun pa zhor byung du sbyang / snang cha bskyed rim/ stong cha rdzogs rim/ dbyer med bde ba chen por ngo sprad/

For those of average capability, the practice is One’s Body as the Empty Appearance of the Deity’s Form. The difference is that you train along the way in intentionality directly with all appearance: the appearing aspect is creation phase, the empty aspect is completion phase, and their inseparability points to great bliss.
tha ma ni 'gro drug sgyu mar 'char byed yin/ chos 'byung phyi dkar la nang dmar ba dang / skabs 'dir sgyu ma'i 'dun pa kho na las 'dun pa gzhan gyi spros pa mi byed do/

For those of least capability, [the practice is] Making the Six Kinds of Migrators Arise as Illusion. The source of phenomena is white outside and red inside, and, in this context, just cultivate the intention of [recognizing] illusion; don’t embellish with the other intentions.

rmi lam la nyin par sgyu ma rmi lam gyi 'dun pa nyid dang / mtshan mo rang zin thig le dbang bzhi'i gnad dang / rtog bcas la bzung ba gnyis sbrags te bsgom/ de la cung zad brtan pa thob na/ 'dun pas sbyong ba nyid bsnan te/ gang zin dpag tu med par sprul pa la sogs pa zin sbyong sprul bsgyur thams cad cha mnyam rang shugs su 'byung / yul snang ni thig le la brten pa de bsgom te/ thig le'i 'od kyis gang blta ba'i yul tshul drangs rang gi snying gar thim par bsgom pa de khyad par ro/ /

In Dream practice, cultivate the intentionality of recognizing illusion and dreams during the daytime, and meditate on both self-recognition in the Vital Points of the Four Empowerments of Drops and the Integration of Concepts together in the nighttime. When you gain some degree of stability in those, add Refining Dreams through Intentionality. Then whatever dream you do recognize can be increased infinitely and so forth: recognizing, refining, emanating, and changing will all occur automatically in equal measure. For Ascertaining Objective Appearances, rely on the meditation of the vital drops (session 41), with the difference that the light of the drop draws in whatever place you wish to view and it dissolves into your heart.

yang mtshan mo nyal khar blta ba'i yul dang / snying ga'i thig le gnyis 'od kyi thag pas sbrel/ ya nga sogs kun la sgyu ma ltar bsgom/ skabs 'dir bsre 'pho shes rab rnam bzhi'i sgo nas cung zad tsam ngo sprod bya/

Also, when going to sleep at night, the viewed object and the drop at the heart are connected by a rope of light. Meditate that fear and so on are all like an illusion. On this occasion, give a short introduction to blending and transference by means of the four wisdoms.[17]

de nas gnyid kyi 'od gsal 'dzin pa ni/ a yig la brten pa yin te/ 'di'i khrid yig gi dkyus la/ rang gi lte 'og sor bzhi bcal bar zhes pa yod kyang de'i mchan bu rang mchan na/ dbang po'i rtse mo'am gsung ba yod de/ rgyud sde dang mthun pa'i gnad dam pa yin/ stan thog gcig ma'i de ka la dgongs par mngon/ dngos bstan (131) a dkar po gcig nor bur bsgom pa'o/ / 'od gsal bde stong las snang ba sna tshogs 'char ba ni/ 'od gsal las lha sku rang shar 'byung ba'i gnad yin par bshad do/ / rgyas par 'gro mgon sangs rgyas nyid kyi gsung du blta'o/

Then to grasp lucid clarity of sleep, you rely on the letter A (session 44). In the course of the guidance manual it states, “Measure four finger-widths below one’s navel.” However, a note, which is [the author’s] own note, says “or at the tip of the organ.”[18] This is a sublime vital point that accords with the tantras. It appears that this was the intent in The Single Sitting [texts]. {131} In the actual teaching, you meditate on a white A in the gem. Regarding the various appearances that arise from the bliss-emptiness of lucid clarity, it is said that the vital point is the deity’s form arising naturally from lucid clarity. For more detail, see Drogön Sangye [Tönpa’s] own exposition.
[General Comments]

de dag las rin chen 'od phreng gzhung gi tshul du mdzad pas gleng brjod gang yang med/ lam dri med 'od phreng dang 'di gnyis la khrid logs pa mi byed de/ chos drug las gzhan du med pas so zhes gsungs pa dang / ngag sgros la sngon chos drug khrigs chags 'di/ yi ger 'god pa bka' rgya ma grol ba'i skabs/ brjed tho lta bur khrid yig bsdus pa 'dra min mdzad pa yin gsung ba sogs yod kyang / chos drug rang spyir snyan brgyud kyi bka' rgya ma grol ba'i skabs yin na ni/ dam dum yi ger bris kyang bka' rgya la gnod pa dang / 'dra min bris na brjed thor shin tu mi rung ste/ dkyus de brjed pa'i rgyur ngos 'gyur bas de 'dra ni ma yin no/ /

Of those texts, Jeweled Light Garland was written in the style of a source text, so there is no editorial account whatsoever. This and the Stainless Light Garland of the Path do not constitute separate guidances, for it is said “there is nothing other than the Six Dharmas.” There is talk that this arrangement of the Six Dharmas was set down before the command seal on written compositions was lifted and that they were composed as various concise manuals, like memoranda. Such things are said. But if it was a time before the command seal of the aural transmission was lifted on the Six Dharmas in general, writing such literary fragments would harm the command seal, and writing various things as memoranda would be highly inappropriate. These false statements that [they were written] so as not to forget things is not the case.

des na 'di gnyis 'gro mgon sangs rgyas kyi gsung yin pas bka' rgya grol ba yin/ dmigs pa 'dra min phran bu yod pa rnams 'dam kha yin par shes par bya dgos/ des na 'di gnyis ye shes mkha' 'gro ni gu ma'i snyan brgyud kyi gdams pa'i snod du gyur pa la/ gdams skor yongs rdzogs rang mi dgos pa'i slob ma 'ga' zhig gi don du gnang / de rnams la yang nyams rtogs khyad par can mthar phyin skyes pa yin 'dug / khrid chen mo'i nang du don 'dus su chug kyang logs su byed pa mi 'gal te/ sgyu lus stan thog gcig ma bzhin no/ / des na mkhas grub chen po khyung pos sgyu lus stan thog gcig ma logs su phral nas mdzad pa bzhin du/ 'gro mgon ston pas kyang 'di (132) gnyis mdzad pa yin te/ skabs 'dir mdzad pa po bzang ngan la khyad med par go dgos so/ /

Therefore, since both are the teachings of Drogön Sangye Tönpa, the seal was released.[19] One must understand that the minor variations in the visualizations are meant as options. Therefore, these two [texts] are for the worthy recipients of the instructions in the aural transmission of Niguma, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness, and they were given for the benefit of a few disciples who did not need the entire instruction cycle. Furthermore, special experiential realization arose in them and they reached the culmination [of spiritual practice]. It is not a contradiction that these texts summarize the points in the major guidance and yet are done separately, just as in Illusory Body in a Single Sitting. In that case, the learned great adept Khyungpo [Naljor] extracted Illusory Body in a Single Sitting and composed it separately, just as Drogön Sangye Tönpa wrote these two texts. {132} You should understand that in this case there is no difference in the quality of the authors.

rin chen 'od phreng dang 'di gnyis la tshig bcad lhug gi khyad la rtog dpyod zhugs ma zhugs kyi stabs cig byung 'dug pa ma gtogs dgos don de dag la khyad med do/ / de ltar na khrid tshul rgyas pa'i nang nas dmigs pa'i gtso bo ji ltar 'os pa gud du phyung ba yin du chug kyang / skyes mchog de dag gis khrid kyi rnam grangs so sor byin gyis rlob par mdzad pa yin pas/ da ltar yang gdul bya so so'i blo rigs dang bstun nas khrid tshul 'di dag gis slob ma bkri ba yang shin tu legs shing 'os pa nyid do/ /

Jeweled Light Garland and these two texts differ only in style—in being verse or prose and in the inclusion or not of analysis. Otherwise, their goals are the same. Therefore, whatever was suitable of the principal visualizations has been extracted from the extensive styles of guidance texts and put [into these short texts]. Nevertheless, each of the numerous guides had been blessed in their creation by those sublime beings [who wrote them]. Therefore, even now it is most excellent and fitting to lead devotees using those kind of guides in accordance with the disciples’ individual mindsets.

spyir yang tshig khrid la gsung gi rgyun rgyas pa nyid tshig gi bslad ma zhugs shing / lhag chad nor 'khrul med pa zhig bla ma las thos shing blo la zin pa zhig dgos mod/ don nyams myong gi khrid la/ khrid yig rgyas pa'i gral bsgrig pa de ka mu ded rang du dgos pa ma yin te/ dmigs pa re re'am gnyis gsum la brten nas nyams myong tshad du phebs pa byung na/ des thams cad kyi rkang zin par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ /

In general, in the transmission of these extensive teachings in these word guidances, the words must remain uncorrupted and without errors of addition or duplication: you must definitely recall exactly what you heard from the guru. As for the meaning, in the experiential guides, it is not necessary to follow the exact order of the extensive guidebooks. The full measure of experience may be reached based on one individual visualization—or two or three—because they are all recognized as having a single foundation.

yang ci ste na/ chos drug gi gzhung khrid rgyas bsdus rnams ni bsgom par mi spro la/ ni gu'i chos drug gi ming dang ldan pa mos na/ 'di gnyis kyi snga ma la 'pho ba bar do tsam bsnan pa dang / rin chen 'od phreng dang / phyi ma 'di la de'i steng du gtum mo yang ji ltar 'os pa bsnan cing / snon tshul yang dkyus la bcug na grub thob gsung la bsre bslad du 'gyur nyen srid pas/ logs su bsnan na legs par 'gyur ro/ /

Those with no enthusiasm for meditating on the extensive or concise source guides on the Six Dharmas, but who are interested in claiming the name of Niguma’s Six Dharmas, could just add however they want the Transference and Intermediate State practices to the former of these two [texts] and add Fierce Inner Heat to Jeweled Light Garland and the latter [text]. But if these additions are inserted into the main course [of the instruction], it runs the risk of polluting the speech of the adepts. So it is best to add them as separate texts.

de las gzhan du ni gu chos drug gi khrid yig yin zer ba/ rje dge 'dun rgya mtshos nye bar sbyar ba lta bu ni/ ni gu mas ma gsungs/ khyung pos ma thos/ brgyud pa'i (133) bla ma sus kyang ma dgongs pa'i bcos ma ni gu'i chos zhes pa'i ming tsam la rgyug cing chos rgyus med pa'i blun po 'brid byed tsam du zad do/ / ci ste chos tshul gzhan las bshad pa'i dmigs rim rnam dag yin no zhe na/ de la ni gu'i chos kyi ming btags pas ci zhig bya/ shangs pa'i bka' brgyud kyi lugs kyi dmigs pa sna cig tsam yang med pa la shangs chos kyi ming btags pa de 'dras cir yang mi rung ngo / /

Contrary to that, there are those who claim to have “a guidance of Niguma’s Six Dharmas,” such as the one composed by Lord Gendun Gyatso.[20] But Niguma did not speak those instructions, Khyungpo did not hear them, and none of the lineage gurus ever realized them. {133} Just calling such a fabrication “Niguma’s Dharma” and running with it only deceives the fools with no clue about dharma. But, you may ask, what if it contains the genuine visualization sequence explained in another dharma system? Well, then why call it “Niguma’s Dharma”? It is totally inappropriate to assign the term Shangpa Dharma to something without even a single visualization from the Shangpa Kagyu tradition.
VI.
VI. Illusory Body in a Single Sitting[21]

sgyu lus stan thog gcig ma zhes bya ba ni/ mkhas grub chen po khyung po'i gsung them yig las/ sgyu lus stan thog gcig ma la/ / gsol 'debs bzhi la 'dun pa brgyad/ gsol 'debs bzhi ni dbang po tha ma'i skabs bzhin yin/ 'dun pa brgyad ni/ 'chi ba mi rtag pa/ bla ma'i mos gus/ gnyid du song bar shes pa/ sgyu ma rmi lam du shes pa/ sbyong spel sprul bsgyur rnams yin par gsungs/ nyams len gyi rim pa ni/ skyabs 'gro/ sems bskyed dag byed stong ra rnams sngon du btang / 'chi ba mi rtag pa'i skyo shas drag tu bskyed pa la dkyus las nan tan che tsam bya/ bla ma'i rnal 'byor ni sgyu lus dkyus dang 'dra/ bla ma rang la bstim pa'i rjes su rang lha skur gsal ba dang / phyi snang ba thams cad la yang sems gtad de/ gang gsal thebs thebs su lha skur gsal btab/ thams cad la cig car dmigs nas/ 'di thams cad rang gi sems snang yin la/ sems de yang bden med sgyu ma lta bu yin/ de las kyang khyad par du nga gnyid du song 'dug / snang ba 'di thams cad rmi lam rang yin ang snyam bden med kyi 'dun pa dang / rmi lam gyi 'dun pa gnyis spel gyin drag tu sbyangs/

The [practice] called Illusory Body in a Single Sitting is indicated by the great learned adept Khyungpo in his Inventory: In the Illusory Body of the Single Sitting, there are four (eight) supplications and eight intentions.[22] The four supplications apply [only to] the section on those of lesser [faculties]. The eight intentions are said to concern death and impermanence, guru devotion, knowing that you’ve gone to sleep, knowing illusion as dream, refining, emanating, and changing. The sequence of practice is going for refuge, arousing awakening mind, and the Purifying of Inner Space, which are to be done first. Then cultivate an intense feeling of disillusionment regarding death and impermanence and apply yourself diligently to the source text. The guru yoga is the same as in the main text for Illusory Body. After the guru dissolves into you, visualize yourself as the deity’s form. Turn your attention to all external appearance and try to visualize that also as the deity’s form. Visualize everything all at once and think, “All this is the perception of my mind. That mind is not real, it is like an illusion. Even more specifically, I have fallen asleep. All these appearances are actually dreams.” Thus enhance both the intentionality regarding the lack of reality and the intentionality about dreams. {134}

thun mtshams su'ang 'dun pa (134) sum sbrags g.yel med du bsgom zhing / lhag par yang rmi lam gyi 'dun pa bsnan/ nyal khar yang rmi lam gyi 'dun pa dang / bden med kyi 'dun pa drag tu sbyangs nas/ de ka'i ngang nas gnyid du 'gro bar bya/ rmi lam 'dzin pa'i gdams ngag gzhan mi 'tshal/ 'di kho nas chog par bzhed/ de rjes sbyong ba spel ba sprul pa bsgyur ba rnams chos drug rgyas pa bzhin bstan no/ / rgyas par na 'di la mkhas grub rgyal mtshan 'bum gyi khrid yig kyang logs su yod pa blta bar bya la/ gzhung khrid la nges po yod phyin/ yi ge 'di tsam gyis kyang de na mthong bar 'gyur ro/ / de ltar na/ chos drug gzhung khrid kyi skabs su dgos pa'i dmigs pa bka' rgya ma'i rigs dang / gdams ngag nyer mkho rgyas bsdus sna tshogs pa'i sde rnams bshad zin to/ /

In the session breaks, meditate without distraction on the three intentionalities together. Particularly add the intention for dreaming. At bedtime, train earnestly again in the intentionality of unreality and dreams, and then go to sleep in that state. Do not seek other instructions for lucid dreams; this is considered sufficient by itself. Afterward, continue with increasing, emanating, and changing dreams as taught in the extensive Six Dharmas. For more detail, there is a separate guidance manual by the learned and accomplished Gyaltsen Bum that you could look at.[23] Once you are sure of the source guides, you will see the meaning even in a few words. This concludes the explanations of this genre of required sealed visualizations in the context of the Six Dharmas source guidance and the various important extensive and concise instructions.
'dir smras pa/ /
Concluding Words
zab don 'khrul med 'di yin zhes/ / nges tig smra ba shin tu dkon/ / mi gra gshog phyir thob chos tsam/ / 'ol gcod byed pas rgyal khams gang / /
“This is the unerring profound meaning,” but such a guarantee is extremely rare. A teaching received just to draw folks in, a mere approximation, fills the land.
mi phal blun po phyogs mos kyis/ / chos 'dir 'jug pa phal che ba/ / ja jo nya ma shas che bas/ / zab don go ba dkon mod kyi/ / khog ngan blo skyon chags pa'ang nyung / /
Mostly fools with some interest mainly enter into this dharma. Mostly men and women who rarely understand the profound meaning, but few harbor evil or faulty attitudes.
che 'dod chos brgyad phyogs 'dzin gsum/ gcig las gcig che 'gran pa bzhin/ / dad pa go rtogs snying rje gsum/ / gcig las gcig chung 'gran pa bzhin/ /
Great ambition, eight concerns, and prejudice: these three compete for prominence. Faith, understanding, and compassion: these three compete for obscurity.
de ltar khyad chos drug ldan pa'i/ / dge bshes ming can zam zom 'ga'/ / rang gis bslabs pa'i kha bshad tsho/ /
Endowed with these six special features, some slackers called “geshe” lecture vainly of their own learning.

skye po phal la ma brin pas/ / nyag nyog 'khor du 'du re nas/ / chos rgyus med pa'i tshogs pa la/ / lung skyog rnams su chos 'di 'chad/ / chos tshul 'di la sbyangs pa yi/ / shes ldan rnams la ston nyan med/ (135)

Since it doesn’t sell to ordinary folks, they hope to gather a motley retinue and to this assembly with no knowledge of dharma explain this teaching of false scripture, where those knowledgeable in this dharma system would not hear them teaching. {135}
a po cang gi klog dar gyi/ / dpe de thugs su chud par mdzod/ /
Like the alphabet primer riddled by worms, take that example to heart.
hai/ / rang re skal ldan yin par nges/ / zab chos nges tig yod sar sleb/ / bla ma sbed kyang mi dgos par/ / chos la spyod pa e ma ho/ /
hey hey We are certainly the fortunate ones to have landed the guaranteed profound dharma. The gurus have no need to hide the dharma to engage—emaho!
zab lam ni gu chos drug gzhung khrid ma mo'i lhan thabs 'di yang rgyal khams pa tA ra nA thas smras pa'o// // mang+ga laM// // (137) (137)
A Supplement to the Source Guide on the Profound Path of Niguma’s Six Dharmas was spoken by the vagabond Tāranātha. maṅgalaṃ
@#/ /ni gu'i 'khrul 'khor rtsa 'grel bzhugs/
3. Niguma’s Yogic Exercises, Root and Commentary[1]
(138)@#/ /oM swa sti/ na mo gu ru/
oṃ svasti / namo guru
rtsa mdud dgrol dang rtsa srong dang / / dbu mar sdud dang rtsa 'grem bzhi'o/ /
Releasing the channel knots, straightening the channels, gathering into the central channel, and spreading through the channels are four.
langs 'dren bsgyur dang stod gnon gsum/ / rkang gcig rkang gnyis gcu ba dang / / bu chung tshul du 'phar ba lnga/ / kha 'byed gnyis ni bsnol dang bgrad/ /
Standing and spreading, transforming, and pressing the torso are three. One leg, two legs, twisting, small-child style, and leaping are five. The two openings are crossing and wide open.
dbu mar 'jug dang dbu mar 'dren/ / dbu mar sdud pa gsum du bzhed/ /
Inserting in the central channel, drawing up in the central channel, and gathering within the central channel are posited as three.
rnam snang rtags bcu don yod grub/ / gzir dang mnyam gzhag rkang g.yab dang / / kog langs sum sprug zhes bya brgyad/ /
Vairocana, bent neck, Amoghasiddhi, suppressing, equipoise, waving legs, sudden stand, and threefold shake are eight.
rtsa la bzhi dang thig le gsum/ / zug ses lnga dang kha 'byed gnyis/ / rdo rje gar la gsum yin te/ / nyon mongs sel la brgyad yod kyang / / gcig tu bsdus na bco brgyad yin/ /

Four are for channels, three are for vital drops, five are for pain relief, two are for opening, three are for the vajra dance, and eight are for dispelling afflictions, but if counted as one, that makes eighteen.
dang po skyil krung ro stod lan bdun gcu/ /
1. Cross-legged, twist the upper torso seven times.
gnyis pa langs la sked gzer rting 'khrab bdun/ /
2. Standing, [hands] on waist, heel-hop seven times.
gsum pa lag gnyis mchan khungs brla zur brkyang / /
3. Extend two hands from armpits to the sides of the thighs.
bzhi pa sar bsdad lus kun 'phur mnye bya/
4. Sit down and massage the whole body.
lnga pa spyi bor thal spar rting pa brdab/ /
5. Palms together above the head, strike the heels.
drug pa khu tshur g.yas g.yon res mos brkyang / /
6. Extend the right and left fists, alternating.
bdun pa mchan khung bsdoms la ro stod gcu/ / brgyad dgu gnyis la dbyug mchongs byed par brgyad/ / 'on kyang da lta lag len de mi byed/ (139)
7. Grasp the armpits and twist the upper torso. (8 and 9 are described as stick-jumping,[2] a practice not done now.) {139}
brgyad pa pus mthil sbyar langs lag brkyang 'khrab/ /
8. Stand with sole placed above knee, extend arms, hop.
dgu pa rkang lag rdeg stabs rting 'khrab gsum/ /
9. Legs and arms in striking pose, three heel-hops.
bcu pa sor bsnol brang 'geb lan gsum gcud/ /
10. Cover chest with intertwined fingers and twist three times.
bcu gcig langs sdod mgo bo bskor lcog sprug /
11. Standing and sitting, rotate and shake the head.
bcu gnyis rting 'khrab gsum mthar sa la 'bebs/ /
12. After three heel-hops, fall to the ground.
bcu gsum khu tshur brang gnon gcig shos 'phul/ /
13. Press the chest with one fist and fling out [the other].
bcu bzhi kha mig bgrad mtha' brkyang bskum sprug /
14. Open mouth and eyes, extend, contract, and shake extremities.
bco lnga nu rdeg rgod lding sprug dang bskor/ /
15. Strike the chest, vulture[-like], shake, and circle.
bcu drug bsnol nas 'then gnon sgyed rgu bya/ /
16. Cross [arms], draw up, press down, open, and close.
bcu bdun dpung bkab sked pa lan gsum sgyog /
17. Cover the biceps, and rotate the waist three times.
bco brgyad pa ni nyon mongs sel ba yin/ /
18. This is the dispelling of afflictive emotions:
byang chub phyag rgya g.yas g.yon steng 'og gcu/ /
[a.] With the mudra of awakening, twist right, left, above, and below.
srin 'dud ltag mnan ro stod g.yas g.yon gcu/ /
[b.] Hook ring fingers, press the neck, twist the upper torso right and left.
don grub phyag rgyar gzhag sha brdeb pa yin/ /
[c.] Assume Amoghasiddhi mudra and strike the flesh.
gzir ba 'bar rgya bskor zhing mig bskor bltas/ /
[d.] To suppress, circle the blazing mudra, gaze with roving eyes.
mchan bung bsdams shing gtsus nas slar yang blta/ /
[e.] Grasp the armpits, twist, and look again.
mnyam gzhag rdor skyil pho ba bsdams pa dang / /
[f.] With equipoise [mudra] and vajra position, hold the belly tight.
rkang g.yab gan rkyal tsog zan spu'i tshul/ /
[g.] Lying prone, wave legs, and knead dough.
kog langs sdigs mdzub phyogs bcu rnams su bskor/ /
[h.] Rise suddenly, point, and rotate in ten directions.
gsum sprug bsdam brkyang bshud cing sprugs pa yin/ /
[i.] Triple shake-up, bind, extend, rub, and shake. {40}
ye shes (140) mkha' 'gro ni gu'i chos drug gi /gtum mo'i gzhung khrid 'khrul 'khor bco brgyad yin/ / phyi ma brgyad du phye na nyi shu lnga/ / ces so/ /
In the Six Dharmas of Niguma, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness, these are the eighteen yogic exercises of the source guide on Fierce Inner Heat. If the last is divided by eight, there are twenty-five.

de yang rlung sbyong ba zla gcig tsam song ba nas/ gtum mo'i stangs zhag bdun/ gong bu 'thabs pa zhag bdun/ dngos gzhi zhag bdun/ bla ma'i gtum mo zhag bdun/ gos su gyon pa zhag bdun bya/ de nas 'khrul 'khor 'di rnams bslabs te yang yang sbyangs pas ngal dub med cing sgrim mi dgos par song ba na/ so so'i dmigs pa rnams la thun re re byed kyin sbyangs/ mthar 'khrul 'khor tshar re la dmigs pa thams cad tshar re 'gro bar byed/ thun bzhi'am drug tu tshar re ma chags shing gtum mo la 'bad na yon tan dpag tu med pa 'phral du 'byung nges pa yin no/ / de la sdom tshig gi don rnams bshad par bya ste/

After one month of training the vital winds, do one week in the style of Fierce Inner Heat,[3] one week on the colliding Fireballs, one week on the main practice, one week on the Fierce Inner Heat of the Guru, and one week on Wearing the Clothes [of Fierce Inner Heat]. Then learn these yogic exercises and train with them again and again. When they don’t tire you out and you don’t need to concentrate, train in the particular visualizations for each session. Finally, all the visualizations in each session of yogic exercises will pertain to the relevant yogic exercise. If you exert yourself in practicing Fierce Inner Heat without break during each of the four or six meditation sessions [a day], immeasurable qualities will quickly arise for sure. Now to explain the meaning of the above summary.
dang po rtsa mdud dgrol ba ni/
1. Releasing the Channel Knots
skyil krung lus gnad bcas la/ lag pa gnyis pus mo nas drangs te/ brla'i rtsa bar btsug / ro stod g.yas dang g.yon du gcud pa lan bdun bdun bya/

Assume the vital points of the body while sitting in cross-legged vajra position. Draw the two hands up from the knees and plant them at the base of the thighs (groin). Twist the upper torso to the right and to the left seven times.
gnyis pa rtsa drang por bsrang ba ni/
2. Straightening the Channels

lus gnad bca' gzhi gong ltar bcas/ lag pa brla'i rtsa bar slebs pa dang / kog gis langs la rlung 'phar byas/ lag pa rked gzer gyi ngang nas/ lto ba g.yas bskor g.yon bskor bya/ gshang sgor sdig pa re dang / ro stod bag tsam g.yas g.yon du gcu ba lhan cig tu bya zhing / de rjes rting 'khrab re dang spel ba lan bdun bya/ 'dis rtsa 'khrugs pa sel bas/ skra shad kyis skra gad byed pa dang 'dra'o/ /

Assume the basic vital body position as before. [When] the hands reach the groin, stand up suddenly and do a wind-jump [that raises the vital winds] (rlung ’phar). Holding the hands on the waist, rotate the belly to the right and to the left. Squeeze the anus each time while twisting the upper torso slightly to the right and left. After that, do a single heel-hop each and repeat [the sequence] seven times. Since this clears up disturbances of the channels, it is similar to doing [the practice called] Brushing Tangled Hair.
gsum pa dbu mar sdud pa ni/
3. Gathering into the Central Channel

snga ma'i 'phros la yin na/ rlung 'khrab cig byas pas chog / logs su byed na/ bca' gzhi gnyis pa dang 'dra bar bya/ lag pa khu tshur bcangs pa brla'i phyi 'phod tshos phyogs la brkyang zhing shed bcug la rting 'khrab gnyis gnyis kyi mtshams su/ 'phar rdeb re bya/ de 'dra lan bdun no/ /

If this is done as an extension of the previous [exercise], it is sufficient to do just one wind-jump. If it is done separately, assume the basic posture of the second [exercise]. Make tight fists with your hands and extend them forcefully down the exterior of the thighs toward the posterior. Do two heel-hops and then a single leap-and-fall (’phar rdeb) Do this sequence seven times.
bzhi pa rtsa 'grem ni/
4. Spreading through the Channels

rlung bsgyur zhig byas nas (141) dang por mgo dang / de nas ro stod/ de rjes lag pa/ rjes su smad dang / rkang pa brkyang ba la 'phur mnye bya/ khyad par lag pa dang rkang pa'i nywa bzhi rnams la/ phan tshun du bshud pa dang / rdung bar byed/ bzhi po de rnams rtsa dag par byed/

After expelling the breath, {141} first massage the head, then the upper torso, then the arms, then the lower body, then the extended legs. In particular, rub and strike the muscles of the four limbs against each other. This purifies the channels of those four [limbs].
lnga pa langs te 'grems pa ni/
5. Standing and Spreading

bca' gzhi gnyis pa dang 'dra ba las/ lag pa rim pas rtsibs logs brgyud yar brkyang / spyi bor thal mo sbyar/ sked pa nyag gis btang / mthur sel mthur du bsdig pa dang / srog steng du drang / lkog mas ol mdud drag tu mnan cing / 'phar rdeb byed pa las/ rting pa brdeb pa shugs che bar bya/ 'di yang lan bdun bya'o/ /

The basic posture is like that of the second one, except that the hands are gradually raised along the sides of the rib cage and extended up, and the palms come together above the head. Constrict the waist and push down on the downward-clearing wind. Draw up the life-force wind. Press down the chin strongly on the Adam’s apple. Rather than the leap-and-fall, do very strong heel-hops. Repeat seven times.
drug pa bsgyur ba ni/
6. Transforming

bca' gzhi gong bzhin byas la/ lag gnyis khu tshur brla'i zur la brkyang / lus g.yon du gcud nas/ rkang lag g.yas pa drag tu brkyang bskum bya/ yan lag dang lhan cig sor mo yang brkyang bskum bya/ de bzhin du g.yon la'ang bskyar/

Assume the basic [standing] posture as before. Extend the clenched fists along the sides of the thighs. Leaving the left [arm at the] side of the body, forcefully extend and contract the right leg and arm. Extend and contract the fingers along with the limbs. Repeat this with the left side.
bdun pa stod gnon ni/
7. Pressing the Upper Torso
bca' gzhi sngar bzhin las/ lag gnyis kyi sor mo rnams bsnol te brang la bkab/ mthe bos mchan khung logs nas bsdam/ ro stod g.yas g.yon du lan bdun gcu/ de gsum thig le dag byed do/ /

Assume the basic posture as before, except bind the chest by intertwining the fingers of the two hands to cover the chest and hooking the two thumbs under the armpits. Twist the upper torso to the right and left seven times. These [last] three will purify the vital-essence drops.
brgyad pa rkang gcig pa ni/
8. One-Legged Hop

bca' gzhi gnyis pa dang 'dra ba las/ rkang pa g.yon pa'i pus mo'i gong la g.yas pa'i mthil sbyar/ pus mo g.yas la skyed/ lag pa gnyis ka brkyangs te/ 'phar rdeb gsum byed/ de nyid g.yas g.yon go ldog pa'ang lan gsum bya/

The basic position is the same as in the second exercise. Place the sole of the right foot above the knee of the left leg. Open out the right knee. Extend both arms. Do three leap-and-falls. Do the same for the opposite side three times.
dgu pa rkang gnyis ni/
9. Two-Legged Hop

bca' gzhi gnyis pa bzhin las/ rkang lag g.yas pa gnyis mdun du g.yon bskor byas nas/ gyen du cung zad btegs te/ brla g.yas kyi rgyab zur du lag pa sor mo dang bcas pa shad kyis brkyang pa dang / rting pa'ang de phyogs su sa la brdab/ g.yon pa'ang de bzhin byed/ 'di'i gzhung las/ (142) brgyad pa dang dgu pa 'di gnyis la thog ma lag pa gcig gis 'khar ba la 'ju ba dang mjug tu gnyis kas 'jus nas ring du 'phar zhing dbyug mchong byed par bshad kyang / deng sang lag len mi byed par 'dug /

The basic position is the same as in the second exercise, except put the right arm and leg in front and rotate to the left, then raise them slightly higher. Stretch the hand and fingers straight out behind the right thigh. Stamp the heel on the ground in that direction. Do the same for the left. {142} The eighth and ninth exercises are described in the sources as first grabbing hold of a staff with one hand and later with two hands and then lifting off, pole-vaulting a long distance. However, this practice is not done nowadays.[4]
bcu pa gcu ba ni/
10. Twisting

sor mo bsnol bas brang dang mchan khung btsir ba bdun pa dang 'dra rung ba las/ langs pa'i skabs/ mgo dang ltag pa sgyed pa'i ngang nas g.yas g.yon lan gsum gcud/ de rjes rlung bsgyur byas te sa la bsdad nas/ mgo dang ro stod lan gsum gcud/ de nas pus mo btsugs pa'i phyed langs la/ lag pa g.yas pa sngar bzhin/ g.yon pa rgyab nas bskor te dpyi g.yas pa la 'jus pas/ ro stod g.yon du gcud/ de bzhin du go ldog par bya'o/ /

With fingers intertwined, squeeze the chest and armpits, apropos to the seventh exercise but standing up. While extending the head and neck, turn to the right and left three times. After that, expel the breath and sit down on the ground. Turn the head and upper torso three times. Then rise up halfway with the knees on the ground. The right hand remains as before, but reach around the back with the left hand toward the right hip and grasp it, thereby twisting the upper torso to the left. Do the same for the opposite side.
bcu gcig pa bu chung tshul ni/
11. Small-Child Style
bsngad la mgo bo bskor zhing mgo lcogs sprug pa lan gsum dang / langs nas kyang mgo bo bskor zhing mgo lcogs sprug pa lan gsum rnams bya'o/ /
While sitting, rotate the head and shake the head three times. Then standing, rotate the head and shake the head three times.
bcu gnyis pa 'phar ba ni/
12. Leaping
rting 'khrab lan gsum gyi mthar/ lag pa khu tshur brkyangs te/ 'phong sar brdab/ / de 'dra lan gsum bya/ de lnga rlung dang thig le thun mong dag par byed pa'o/ /
After three heel-hops, extend the clenched hands and land with the buttocks on the ground. Do that three times. Those last five exercises purify both the vital winds and the vital-essence drops.
bcu gsum pa rtsa dbu ma kha 'byed dang po ni/
13. First Exercise to Open the Central Channel

skyil krung bcas/ lus bsrangs/ lag pa khu tshur gnyis thad kar brkyang ba las/ g.yon khu tshur nu khar brdeg cing mnan/ g.yas 'phongs tshos g.yas kyi phyogs thad ka la bskum khru gang tsam du brkyang / de 'dra ba lan gsum byed/ de nyid go zlog pa'ang lan gsum byed/ 'di la g.yas g.yon bsnol ba zer/

Sit in cross-legged vajra position and straighten the body. Extend the two clenched hands directly in front. Strike and press near the breast with the left fist. Extend the right directly to the right of the buttocks for one cubit. Do that three times. Then do the opposite three times. This is called the crossing of right and left.
dbu ma kha 'byed gnyis pa ni/
14. Second Exercise to Open the Central Channel
rlung 'khrab byas nas langs/ lag pa brkyangs te pho ba sa la btsugs/ kha mig gdangs/ yan lag bzhi brkyang bskum bya zhing drag tu sprug pa'o/ / 'di la bsgrad pa'i mtha' zer/

Do a wind-jump and then stand. Extend the hands and lie down on the belly. Open the mouth and eyes wide. Extend and contract the four limbs and forcefully shake them. This is called the furthest opening.
bco lnga pa dbu mar 'jug pa ni/
15. Inserting [the Winds] within the Central Channel

bca' gzhi dang bstun nas langs/ / (143) rlung mthur la brdeg cing / lag pa brkyangs te nu khar brdeg pa lan gsum bya/ yang lag gnyis khu tshur brla'i zur du brkyangs la/ mthur sel drag tu 'then pa gsum bya/ yang lag pa rgod gshog bzhin brkyangs la rting 'khrab gsum byas nas/ lus drag tu sprug / yang rlung phyir bsal nas kyang drag tu sprug go /

Stand up from the basic position. {143} Press down the winds, extend the hands, and beat the chest three times. Again extend the clenched fists to the side of the thighs and forcefully draw up the downward-clearing winds three times. Now extend the arms like the wings of a vulture and do three heel-hops. Then shake the body violently. Again clear out the winds, exhaling while shaking forcefully.
bcu drug pa dbu mar 'dren pa ni/
16. Drawing Up in the Central Channel

langs te lag pa gnyis bsnol/ khu tshur g.yas g.yon gyis mchan khung dang / lag ngar gyis nu ma btsir/ rtsib logs g.yas dgang / mgo g.yon du 'khyog pa dang lhan cig rlung g.yas gyen 'then dang / de nyid go ldog pas g.yas mthur gnon bya/ g.yon la'ang des rigs 'gre/ de bzhin du ltag pa sgyed la mdun du 'then gnon dang sgur la/ rgyab la'ang 'then gnon bya/

Stand and cross the right and left hands and put them under the armpits, squeezing the breasts with the forearms. Fill up the right-side ribs [and hold the breath]. Bend the head to the left and simultaneously draw up the vital winds on the right. Reverse it, bending over to the right and following suit on the left [by drawing up the winds]. Similarly bend the neck and pull and press forward. Also pull and press to the back.
bcu bdun pa dbu mar sdud pa ni/
17. Gathering within the Central Channel

sngar bzhin langs la/ lag pa bsnol/ lag mthil dpung pa g.yas g.yon la bkab/ pho ba g.yas bskor g.yon bskor gsum/ ro stod g.yas g.yon du gcu/ sked pa g.yas g.yon dbus gsum du phar kyog tshur kyog bya zhing 'chun btsal lo/ / kha 'byed gnyis/ gar gsum zhes so sor bgrang yang chab cig tu 'ong bas kha 'byed gnyis dang / 'jug 'dren sdud gsum ste lnga la rdo rje gar gyi 'khrul 'khor zhes so/ /

Stand as before and cross the arms with the palms holding the right and left biceps. Rotate the belly three times to the right and three times to the left. Twist the upper torso to the right and left. Bend the waist back and forth to the right, left, and center, then regain control. The two openings [of the channel] and three dances are counted separately but come together as one. So the two openings and inserting, drawing up, and gathering—these five—are called the yogic exercise of the vajra dance.[5]
bco brgyad pa ni nyon mongs sel ba'i 'khrul 'khor zhes bya ste/
18. Yogic Exercises to Dispel Afflictive Emotions
de la nang tshan du phye na brgyad yod/
There are eight [or nine] subcategories:
dang po gti mug sel ba rnam snang gi phyag rgya ni/
a. Dispelling Stupidity [with] Vairocana’s Mudra[6]
byang chub mchog gi phyag rgya snying gar bcas nas/ mdun du brkyangs la/ g.yas g.yon steng 'og rnams su gcu zhing / nu ma dang pho bar brdeg /
Make the mudra of supreme awakening at the heart and extend it in front. Twist to the right and left, up and down, striking the breast and belly.
rgod pa sel ba ni/
b. Dispelling Agitation

skyil krung ngang nas srin lag gnyis 'dud pa'i sor mo gzhan rnams kyis ltag pa'i chu ba nas mnan te ltag pa dgug / ro stod g.yas g.yon du lan gsum drag tu gcu/ lag pa steng (144) du brkyangs te/ spyi bor thal lcag rgyab/ lan gsum/

Sitting in the cross-legged vajra position, hook the two ring fingers and with the other fingers press and bend the large ligament in the nape of the neck. Rotate to the right and left three times, twisting forcefully. Extend the hands above and slap the crown of the head with the palms three times. {144}
khra tshag sel ba ni/
c. Dispelling Reproach[7]
lag gnyis pus mo nas blangs te/ bzhag sha brdab cing mdun du brkyangs nas/ don yong grub pa'i phyag rgya bcas pa snying ga dang lte 'og tu brdab/ g.yon pa'i lag ngar bsrang nas gcud do/ /

Lift the two hands from the knees and slap the flesh of the buttocks and extend [the hands] in front and with the mudra of Amoghasiddhi. Hit the heart area and below the navel. Straighten the left arm and turn it out.
gnod byed gzir ba ni/
d. Suppressing Harm-Doers

skyil krung ngang nas/ lag pa 'bar ba'i phyag rgya bcas g.yas dang g.yon dang dbus dang steng phyogs nas cung zad rgyab la sgyed de/ g.yas g.yon du lan gsum gsum bskor ba dang lhan cig mig gdangs shing shugs bskyed pa'i lta stangs kyis mig kyang bskor ro/ /

Sitting in cross-legged vajra position, make the burning mudra to the right, left, center, and above, then slightly toward the back. Circle it three times to the right and three times to the left and, at the same time, open the eyes wide and rotate them as well with a powerful gaze.
zhe sdang sel ba mi bskyod pa'i phyag rgya ni/
e. Dispelling Anger with Akṣobhya’s Mudra

skyil krung byas nas dpyad phrag brdab/ sor bcu bsnol bas brang gi dbus rnams bsdams shing / gru mo phyir bkyed la g.yas g.yon du lan gsum gsum gcu ba dang / lag gnyis sa gnon byas te/ g.yas g.yon dbus gsum du khro bo'i sta stangs kyis blta'o/ /

Sitting in cross-legged vajra position, clap down the sides. Bind the center of the chest with the ten fingers intertwined and bend the elbows out, twisting to the right and left three times. Touch the ground with both hands, and look to the right, left, and center with a fearsome gaze.
da rgyal sel ba 'od dpag med kyi phyag rgya ni/
f. Dispelling Pride with Amitābha’s Mudra

rdo rje'i skyil krung gi ngang nas lag ngar bsrang ba'i mnyam bzhag shugs bskyed/ mnyam gzhag btegs nas pho bar brdeg cing bsdams/ yang lag ngar bsrang ba sogs lan gsum/ de rjes rlung phyir 'bud pa dang lhan cig ha drag po lan gsum brjod/

Sitting in cross-legged vajra position, straighten the arms and place them firmly in the position of meditative equipoise. Raise the arms in that equipoise position and slam them into the belly, holding them there. Again straighten the arms and so forth, repeating three times. After that, expel the air and at the same time intensely utter “ha” three times.
'dod chags sel ba ni/
g. Dispelling Desire

bca' gzhi'i ngang nas rkang pa g.yas g.yon res mos su lan gsum bskor zhing g.yab/ de nas gan rkyal du 'dug ste/ rkang pa g.yas brkyang g.yon bskum dang / g.yon brkyang g.yas bskum byed/ lag pa nam mkhar brkyangs nas zan bsnol ba'i phyag rgya bya/

From the basic position, circle the right and left legs by turns three times and hit [the ground] with them. Then lay back and extend the right leg while contracting the left, and extend the left while contracting the right. Stretch the hands up in space and make the gesture of kneading dough.
bde chen 'beb pa che ba ser sna sel ba ni/
h. Dispelling Greed, the Greater Descent of Great Bliss

skyil krung bcas pa las/ kag gis langs te 'doms 'jal brgyad/ rlung 'khrab bya/ sdigs mdzub byas te g.yas g.yon dang / steng 'og dang / mdun rgyab tu bskor/ rlung bskyur zhig byas la mchog sbyin brkyang (145) lus sgyed par bya/ 'di la kog langs zer ro/ /

From the cross-legged vajra position, stand up suddenly and spread the arms like a balance scale. Do a wind-hop (rlung ’khrab). Make the threatening pointing gesture, turning around to the right and left, up and down, front and back. Do one exhalation of the breath and extend the [mudra of] supreme generosity, raising the body. This is called sudden standing. {145}
bde ba 'beb pa chung ba ni/
i. Lesser Descent of Bliss

gsum sprug zhes bya ba lag pa g.yas g.yon gnyis steng nas 'og tu sprug pa dang / ro stod drag tu sprug pa la zer/ de'ang sems dpa'i skyil mo krung bcas nas/ gsum sprug bya/ de nas lag pa g.yas steng dang g.yon 'og tu byas la bsnol/ lag mthil gyen du bstan/ lag mgo g.yon gyi 'og tu g.yas bcug ste/ g.yas pa'i srin lag gis g.yon pa'i srin lag bsdam/ mdun du brkyang bas/ lag ngar gcud la bor ba dang / lag stabs de nyid go ldog pas kyang gcud la bor/ re re bzhin shugs 'jug thengs gsum gsum byed/ de nas g.yon khu tshur dpung pa'i thad ka nas mdun gyi g.yon zur la brkyang / g.yas kyi khu tshur gyis bshud thebs gsum bya/ g.yas pa la'ang de bzhin du bya/ yang gsum sprugs mthar 'bebs bya'o/ / phyi ma 'di la gsum sprugs zer te 'gyod pa dang / yid mi bde ba dang / rnam rtog sel ba yin/

The so-called threefold shake is to shake the right and left arms from top to bottom and forcefully shake the upper torso [while exhaling]. Sit in the bodhisattva posture and do the threefold shake. Then cross the hands with the right hand above the left, palms facing up. With the left hand touching underneath the right, the left ring finger hooks the right ring finger. Extend that forward and turn them [inward]. Then reverse the position of the hands and turn them inward. Do this three times each with some force. Then extend the left fist straight out from the shoulder and rub the arm three times with the right fist. Then do the same for the right [arm]. Again do the threefold shake and finally a forceful fall (’bebs). This last exercise is called the threefold shake. It helps dispel regret, depression, and discursive thought.
[Colophon]
