'khrul 'khor 'di rnams la/ so sor dmigs pa'i gnad re phal cher la yod de/ rtsa ba'i gzhung tshig las shes par bya'o/ / de ltar na 'di rnams ye shes mkha' 'gro ni gu'i zhal gyi gdams pa/ rlung sems dbu mar thim pa dang / rtsa mdud grol ba'i man ngag rang lus thabs ldan gtso bor gyur pa/ grol lam mchog sgrub kyi man ngag / lus sbyong bco brgyad pa zhes bya ba yin te/ 'di'i rtsa ba'i gzhung ni/ zhal shes cung zad gab pa dang / tshig mang po'i gseb tu 'thor bas sdud mi shes pa dag mang du yod la/ mi mkhas pas sbyar ba'i sdom than thun yod srid na'ang / lag len gsal por thon pa med par mngon pas/ 'di'i lag len nub tu nye bar mthong ba'i phyir/ mi nub cing rgyas par bya ba'i don du dpal ldan shangs pa'i bka' brgyud la mos pa cung zad thob pa/ tA ra nA thas ma sbas shing gsal bar bkod pa'o/ / (146) (147)

Most of these yogic exercises each have vital points of visualization that should be learned from the source text. These are the personal instructions of Niguma, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness. They are esoteric instructions for dissolving wind-mind in the central channel and releasing the channel knots, using one’s own body as the primary means. They are the esoteric instructions for the supreme accomplishment of the path of liberation that are known as the eighteen physical trainings (lus sbyong bco brgyad pa). Regarding the sources of this, the oral directions are somewhat arcane, and they have been scattered among a great many words. There are many who do not know how to arrange them. Although it is possible for uneducated persons to make some collections of them, a practical application does not actually emerge clearly. Since I saw that the practice was close to disappearing, in order to save it and spread it, I, Tāranātha, having attained some degree of devotion in the glorious Shangpa Kagyu, have laid it out clearly without restriction.
Tangtong Gyalpo and the Direct Lineage
@#/ /ye shes mkha' 'gro ni gu ma'i chos drug gi khrid kyi gnad yig snying po kun 'dus zhes bya ba bzhugs so// //
4. Collection of Essentials. Vital Words of Instruction on the Six Dharmas of Niguma, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness[1]
(148) @#/ /na mo lo ker shwa rA ya/
namo lokeśvaraya
gang zhig brjod bral lhun grub 'dus ma byas/ / kha sbyor bde chen longs sku gang 'dul shar/ / sku gsum bdun ldan rdo rje 'chang la sogs/ / rje mkhyen pas gzigs shig drin chen bla ma rnams/ /

“The one who is ineffable, spontaneously present, and unconditioned, the union as blissful saṃbhogakāya, arising to tame anyone, Vajradhara with three kāyas and seven aspects,”[2] and so on. Lords, see me with understanding, most kind gurus.
thugs brtse bas dgongs shig yi dam lha yi tshogs/ / dus 'bral bar med par skyongs shig dkon mchog gsum/ / 'gal rkyen spongs la mthun rkyen sgrubs shig mkha' 'gro chos skyong tshogs/ /
Think of me with affection, host of yidam deities. Protect me at all times, Three Precious Jewels. Remove adverse conditions and achieve conducive ones, ḍākinīs and protectors.
thang stong gi rgyal po/ / lung stong gi smyon pa/ zas gang byung gi bcud len po/ / rkyen gang byung gi ro snyoms po ngas theg pa chen po'i chos thams cad kyi nying khu phyogs gcig tu bsdus pa/

I—King of the Empty Plain, Madman of the Empty Valley, Extractor of the Essence of Any Food, Equalizer of Any Occurring Conditions—have gathered into one place the essential extract of all the teachings of the Great Vehicle.
ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro ma ni gu ma'i snyan brgyud kyi gdams pa khyad par can 'di 'chad pa la/ nyams su len pa'i rten gyi gang zag dang / nyams len dngos gnyis kyi
The explanation of this special instruction of the aural lineage of Niguma, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness, has two parts: (1) the person who is the support for practice and (2) the actual practice.
dang po ni
I. The Person

rgyud sde lnga'am/ 'khor lo sdom pa'i dkyil 'khor du dbang bzhi thob cing / dam tshig dang dad pa dang / brtson 'grus dang ldan pa/ 'chi ba mi rtag pa/ las rgyu 'bras 'khor (149) ba'i nyes dmigs sogs sngon 'gro'i chos rnams rgyud la skyes pa zhig dgos te/

This should be someone who has received the empowerment into the mandala either of the Five Tantras’ Deities or of Cakrasaṃvara; who possesses sacred pledge, faith, and diligence; and who has fully assimilated the preliminary teachings such as death and impermanence, karmic cause and effect, the shortcomings of cyclic existence, and so forth. {149}

ni gu ma'i rdo rje'i tshig rkang las/ / dbang bzhis smin byas dad dang brtson 'grus ldan/ / mi rtag skyo shas nyes dmigs sngon 'gro ba'i/ lam mchog 'di la gang gis 'bad gyur na/ / zla drug lo'am tshe 'dir sangs rgyas 'gyur/ / ces gsungs so/ /

As it states in Niguma’s Vajra Lines: Matured by four empowerments, faithful, and diligent, having first [experienced] impermanence, weariness, [and samsara’s] deficiencies, whoever strives at this sublime path will awaken in six months, a year, or in this lifetime.[3]
gnyis pa nyams len dngos
II. The Actual Practice
['di] la/ /sngon 'gro dang dngos gzhi gnyis/
This has two parts: (1) the preliminaries and (2) the main practice.
dang po ni/
A. Preliminaries

mdun gyi nam mkhar rin po che'i khri seng ge brgyad kyis btegs pa'i steng du pa~M las pad+ma'i sdong bu 'dab ma stong dang ldan pa/ de'i steng du raM las nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor 'od zer 'bum dang ldan pa/ de'i steng du a las zla ba'i dkyil 'khor stong gsum gyi tshad dang mnyam pa/ de'i steng du dar zab la sogs pa'i gdan sna tshogs pa'i steng du ngo bo rtsa ba'i bla ma rnam pa sangs rgyas rdo rje 'chang chen po sku mdog sngon po zhal gcig phyag gnyis pa/ g.yas rdo rje dang g.yon dril bu thugs kar bsnol nas 'dzin pa/ zhabs gnyis rdo rje skyil krung du bzhugs pa/ (150) sku gcer bu la rus pa dang rin po ches brgyan pa/ zhal 'dzum bag dang bcas pa/ spyan gsum dang ldan pa/ dbu skra sil bu sku rked yan chad khebs pa/ sku mthong ba tsam gyis sdig sgrib 'dags pa/ gsung thos pa tsam gyis phyir mi ldog pa'i sa la 'god nges pa/ snang la rang bzhin med pa zhig bsams la/ de'i mdun du bdag dang sems can thams cad kyis snying gi dkyil rkang gi khongs nas skyabs su 'gro bar bsams la/ ma nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i sems can thams cad dus 'di nas bzung ste/ byang chub snying po la mchis kyi bar du bla ma la skyabs su mchi'o/ / sangs rgyas la= chos la= dge 'dun la= yi dam la skyabs su mchi'o/ dpe gcig la 'di 'dug pa brtag / mchan/ zhes brgya rtsa sogs brjod/

In the space before you appears a jeweled throne supported by eight lions. On that, the stem of a lotus with a thousand petals arises from paṃ. Upon that, the mandala of the sun with a hundred thousand light rays arises from raṃ. And upon that, the moon mandala arises from āḥ, reaching the extent of the billionfold universe. There are various cushions of silk and so on, upon which sits my root guru in the form of Great Buddha Vajradhara. He is blue, with one face and two hands, holding a vajra in the right and a bell in the left, crossed over his heart. He sits with two legs crossed in vajra position, his naked body adorned by bones and jewels. {150} He smiles amiably. His loose locks fall down to his waist. Just seeing his form purifies negative actions and obscurations. Just hearing his voice is certain to place one in the state of a nonreturner. Imagine this appearing with no intrinsic nature. Before him you and all sentient beings go for refuge from the very bottom of your hearts: All sentient beings, my mothers, equal to the reaches of space, from today until the heart of awakening, go for refuge in the guru. We go for refuge in the Buddha. We go for refuge in the dharma. We go for refuge in the sangha. We go for refuge in the yidams.[4] Repeat one hundred or so times.

de nas/ ma nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i sems can thams cad bde ba dang bde ba'i rgyu dang ldan par gyur cig / sdug bsngal dang sdug bsngal gyi rgyu dang bral bar gyur cig / sdug bsngal med pa'i bde ba dang mi 'bral bar gyur cig / bde sdug nye ring chags sdang dang bral ba'i btang snyoms la gnas par gyur cig / ces tshad med pa bzhi bsgom/

Then the four immeasurable meditations: May all sentient beings, my mothers, equal to the reaches of space, have happiness and the causes of happiness. May they be free from suffering and the causes of suffering. May they never be separated from happiness that is free of suffering. May they dwell in equanimity, free of happiness or suffering, close or distant, attachment or aversion.
de nas/ sems can thams cad kyi don du sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang thob par bya/ de'i phyir du bdag gi lus ngag yid gsum dge sbyor gyi rim pa la 'jug par bgyi'o/ / zhes sems bskyed/
Arousing the mind of awakening: I will attain the state of a buddha for the sake of all sentient beings. Therefore, I will engage in the stages of applied virtue with body, speech, and mind.
de nas bla ma la gsol ba gdab pa ni/
Supplicating the gurus:
sangs rgyas rdo rje 'chang chen la gsol ba 'debs/ mkha' 'gro ni gu ma la= grub thob khyung po rnal 'byor la= rmog lcog rin chen brtson 'grus la gsol=
I supplicate Great Buddha Vajradhara. I supplicate Ḍākinī Niguma. I supplicate adept Khyungpo Naljor. I supplicate Mokchok Rinchen Tsöndru.
mnyam med skyer sgang pa chen po la= bla ma sangs rgyas gnyan ston la= chos rjes sangs rgyas ston pa la= mkhas grub shangs ston chos rje la=
I supplicate Great Nyame Kyergangpa. I supplicate Lama Sangye Nyentön. I supplicate Dharma King Sangye Tönpa. I supplicate wise adept Shangtön Chöje.
rgyal ba mus pa chen po la= bla ma rdo rje gzhon nu la= mtshan ldan nam (151) mkha'i rnal 'byor la/ byang sems sbyin pa bzang po la= grub thob brtson 'grus bzang po la=
I supplicate Great Gyalwa Mupa. I supplicate Lama Dorje Zhönu. I supplicate Tsenden Namkhai Naljor. {151} I supplicate Jangsem Jinpa Zangpo. I supplicate adept Tsöndru Zangpo.
thabs lam bde drod rang 'bar du byin gyis rlobs/ sgyu lus chags sdang rang grol tu= rmi lam nying 'khrul rang dag tu= 'od gsal gti mug rang sangs su=

Bless me to naturally produce bliss-heat on the Path of Methods. Bless me to naturally liberate desire and anger in Illusory Body. Bless me to naturally purify double delusion in Dream. Bless me to naturally dispel stupidity in Lucid Clarity.
'pho ba ma bsgoms sangs rgyas su= bar do rgyal ba longs sku ru byin gyis rlobs/ / zhes sam/ tshigs su bcad pa gang rung gis gsol ba drag tu gdab par bya'o/ /
Bless me to awaken without meditation in Transference. Bless me with the victors’ saṃbhogakāya in the Intermediate State. Supplicate intensely with this or whatever verses are suitable.
gnyis pa dngos gzhi
B. Main Practice

['di] la drug ste/ thabs lam bde drod rang 'bar/ sgyu lus chags sdang rang grol/ rmi lam nying 'khrul rang dag / 'od gsal gti mug rang sangs/ 'pho ba ma bsgoms sangs rgyas/ bar do rgyal ba longs sku'o/ /

This has six parts: (1) the Path of Methods, naturally blazing bliss-warmth; (2) Illusory Body, naturally liberated desire and anger; (3) Dream, naturally purified double delusion; (4) Lucid Clarity, naturally awakened stupidity; (5) Transference, buddhahood without meditation; and (6) Intermediate State, the victors’ saṃbhogakāya.
dang po thabs lam
1. Path of Methods
['di] la sngon 'gro dngos gzhi rjes gsum mo/ /
This has three parts: (1) preliminaries, (2) main practice, and (3) concluding practice.
dang po
a. Preliminaries
['di] la gsum ste/ dag byed a'i stong ra/ stong ra nad gdon sel byed/ rtags gsum stong ra'i khyad par ro/ /
This has three parts: (1) The Purifying A of Inner Space, (2) the Inner Space That Dispels Sickness and Spirits, and (3) the three special signs of inner space.
dang po ni/
i. The Purifying A of Inner Space

rang gi spyi bor paM las pad+ma dang a las zla ba'i dkyil 'khor gyi steng du rtsa ba'i bla ma rdo rje 'chang sku mdog dkar po rgyan cha lugs gong dang 'dra bar bsgoms te/ de la bla ma yi dam thams cad bstims la/ bla ma rin po che bdag gi nad gdon zhi bar byin gyis rlobs/ sdig sgrib 'dags par byin gyis rlobs/ ting nge 'dzin khyad par can rgyud la skye bar byin gyis rlobs/ zhes gsol ba btab/ 'og nas 'byung ba ltar srid pa'i dbang zhus nas ngag tu a zhes brjod pas rang gi smin mtshams dang rna ba g.yas g.yon tu zur re re gtad pa'i chos 'byung phyi dkar nang dkar stong sang nge ba lus dang mnyam pa zhig bsam mo/ / de ltar ma yengs par yang yang du bsgoms pas sdig sgrib dkor sku glud dam tshig gi nyams chags thams cad dag go /

Meditate as before on the guru as white adorned Vajradhara upon a lotus from paṃ and moon-disk mandala from āḥ above your head. Dissolve all the gurus and yidams into that. Then supplicate: Precious guru! Bless me to dispel sicknesses and bad spirits. Bless me to purify negative actions and obscurations. Bless me that special meditative absorption arises in my mind stream. Take the Empowerment of Existence as described below, then say “A.” Imagine a source of phenomena (tetrahedron) with each of its three vertices level with your midbrow and right and left ears. It is white inside and out, utterly empty, the size of your body. Meditating on that again and again without distraction purifies all negativity, obscuration, [corruption from] misappropriated and ransom offerings, and damaged sacred pledge. {152}
gnyis pa stong ra nad gdon (152) sel byed ni/
ii. The Inner Space That Dispels Sickness and Spirits

rang gi os ko dang rna ba'i rtsa ba gnyis su zur re re gtad pa'i chos 'byung phyi nang gnyis ka dkar ba rtsa ba gsang gnas su zug pa'i nang du sems skye med a dmar po zhig bsam/ ngag tu a a zhes ci rigs brjod pas a de 'od du zhu nas ngo bo bdud rtsi rnam pa ga bur ltar dkar ba reg bya bsil ba/ tsha ba'i nang thams cad zhi par byed pa'i nus pa dang ldan pa zhig bsam/

The source of phenomena’s three vertices each point toward the larynx and two bases of the ears. It is white both outside and inside, with the lower tip reaching the perineum. Within it, imagine your own unborn mind as white A. Repeat “A - A” as many times as appropriate. Thereby the A melts into light and becomes elixir in essence and white as camphor in form, cooling to the touch. Imagine it able to soothe all sickness from heat.

yang rang gi nu ma gnyis de'i thad kar sgral tshigs dang gsum la zur re re gtad pa'i chos 'byung phyi nang gnyis ka dmar po'i nang du rang sems skye med a dmar po zhig bsam/ yang gong bzhin brjod pas a de zhu nas ngo bo bdud rtsi rnam pa zangs zhun ltar dmar ba reg bya tsha ba grang ba'i nad thams cad zhi bar byed pa'i nus pa dang ldan pa zhig bsgom/

Again, the source of phenomena’s three vertices each point toward the two breasts and the spine directly behind them. It is red both outside and in. Within it, imagine your own unborn mind as a red A. Then, repeating as before, the A melts and becomes elixir in essence and red like molten copper in form, hot to the touch. Meditate that it is able to pacify all sickness from cold.

yang rang gi lte ba dang mkhal khung gnyis la zur re re gtad pa'i chos 'byung phyi nang gnyis ka smug po'i nang du rang sems a smug po zhig bsam/ ngag tu sngar bzhin brjod pas a de 'od du zhu nas ngo bo bdud rtsi rnam pa mar zhu ba'i dangs ma ltar smug pa/ reg bya 'jam pa/ rlung gi nad thams cad zhi bar byed pa'i nus pa dang ldan par bsam/

Again, the source of phenomena’s three vertices each point toward your navel and two kidneys. It is maroon both outside and inside. Within it, imagine your own unborn mind as a maroon A. Then repeating as before, the A melts and becomes elixir in essence and maroon like the refined essence of melted butter in form, soft to the touch. Imagine that it is able to pacify all sickness of the vital winds.

yang rang gi lte 'og sor bzhi dang dpyi mgo gnyis la zur re re gtad pa'i/ chos 'byung nag po'i nang du rang sems a nag po zhig bsam/ de la sngar bzhin brjod pas/ a de zhu nas ngo bo bdud rtsi rnam pa khro chu ltar khol ba reg bya shin tu tsha ba/ nad gdon sdig sgrib thams cad sreg pa'i nus pa dang ldan pa zhig bsams nas/ ngag tu a zhes brjod pas nad thams cad sngo dmar gyi rnam pa/ gdon thams cad sdig sprul sogs dang / sdig sgrib thams cad rnag khrag dang dud khu'i rnam pas ba spu'i bu ga thams cad dang / 'og sgo nas 'thon cing nang du yang tshag chom chom sreg par bsgom mo/ / 'di rnams rgyun du ma yengs (153) par bsgoms pas gang la dmigs pa'i nad gdon thams cad zhi bar myong bas grub bo/ /

Again, a black source of phenomena’s three vertices each point toward a spot four fingers below the navel and the two hips. Within it, imagine your own mind as a black A. Then repeating as before, the A melts into light and becomes elixir in essence and boils like molten bronze in form, extremely hot to the touch. Imagine that it is able to burn up all sickness, spirits, negativities, and obscurations. Then repeat A and meditate that it causes all sickness as purple shapes; all spirits as scorpions, snakes, and so forth; and all negativities and obscurations as pus, blood, and liquid coal that exude from all the pores and lower orifices while inside the body crackles and sparks with burning. {153} By continuously meditating without distraction on these visualizations, you will accomplish them when you experience that whatever sickness and spirits you targeted are all pacified.
yang na chos 'byung snga ma snga ma'i nang du/ phyi ma phyi ma rnams bsgoms kyang rung ngo / /
Alternatively, it is also appropriate to meditate on each later source of phenomena situated within the immediately previous source of phenomena.
gsum pa rtags gsum stong ra'i khyad par ni/
iii. The Special Inner Space of Three Signs

nyi zla shar ba/ nam mkha' la 'phur ba/ khang steng dang gangs ri sogs ri bo'i rtser phyin pa/ chur mi bying bar phyin pa/ ngo tsha ba'i rtog pa med pa gcer bu 'thon pa/ khrus byas pa/ gos dkar po dri ma med pa gon pa sogs ni sdig pa 'dag pa'i rtags so/ / 'khru skyugs dang rnag khrag 'dzag pa dang / lus la rdul mang po 'thon pa ni nad thon pa'i rtags so/ / sdig sbrul sdom sbal lcong 'bu srin thon pa ni gdon thon pa'i rtags so/ / de rnams dngos sam nyams snang ngam rmi lam sogs ci rigs su 'byung ngo / /

The signs of purification of negative actions are the rising sun, flying through the sky, arriving on the rooftop or a mountain peak such as a snow mountain, landing on the water without sinking, showing up naked without shame, washing, wearing spotless white clothing, and so forth. The signs of purging sickness are diarrhea and vomiting, exuding pus and blood, and perspiring profusely. Signs of expelling bad spirits are scorpions, snakes, spiders, frogs, tadpoles, and bugs leaving the body. All of those signs can occur for real or as a visionary experience or in dreams, and so on—however they occur.
gnyis pa dngos gzhi
b. Main Practice
['di] la lnga ste/ lus gnad me'i stong ra'am dbu ma chos bzhi ldan/ gtum mo gos su gyon pa/ zas su za ba/ gdan du bting ba/ srid pa'i dbang zhu ba'o/ /

This has five parts: (1) The vital point of the body: Inner Space of Fire or four attributes of the central channel, (2) Wearing the Clothes of Fierce Inner Heat, (3) Eating the Food, (4) Spreading the Seat, and (5) receiving the Empowerment of Existence.
dang po ni
i. The Vital Point of the Body: Inner Space of Fire

rang rdo rje rnal 'byor mar gsal ba'i lus tsog pu byas/ rkang pa gnyis bsnol ba'i mthil stan la gtad/ lag pa gnyis bsnol nas lhu ba g.yas g.yon gnyis la 'jus/ gru mo pus mo la bkal/ mgrin pa cung zad sgu bar byed pa'i me thab drug chings byas la spyi bor bla ma sdar bzhin bsgom/

Imagine yourself as Vajrayoginī and assume a sitting posture with your two legs drawn up and crossed [at the calves] and the soles of your feet on the mat. Cross your arms and grasp the right and left biceps [with the opposite hands]. Place your elbows on your knees and bend the neck slightly. This is called the sixfold-binding-stove posture. Meditate on the guru above your head as before, and pray:
bla ma rin po che bdag la bde drod kyi ting nge 'dzin skye bar byin gyis brlab tu gsol/ bde stong gi ting nge 'dzin skye bar byin gyis brlab tu gsol/ ces brjod/
Precious Guru! Bless me with the arising of bliss-warmth meditative absorption. Bless me with the arising of bliss-emptiness meditative absorption.

srid pa'i dbang zhus nas/ rang gi spyi gtsug nas gsang gnas kyi bar rtsa dbu ma mda' smyug ltar drang ba/ dong rtse ltar khog stong pa/ rgya skyegs kyi me tog ltar dmar ba/ til gyi zhun mar ltar dangs pa ste dbu ma chos bzhi ldan gsal gdab/ de'i g.yas na ro ma dmar po/ (154) g.yon na rkyang ma dkar mo/ / de gnyis kyi mas sna dbu ma'i nang du chud pa/ lte ba snying kha mgrin pa spyi bo ste gnas bzhir ro rkyang gnyis 'khril ba'i rtsa mdud re re yod pa/ spyi bo nas g.yas su ro ma g.yon du rkyang ma la rtsa phran bzhi bzhi gyes pa kha'i g.yas g.yon gnyis/ sna bug gnyis mig gnyis rna ba gnyis po rnams su sbrul mgo ltar tsheg ge yod pa/ bshang lam kyi sgor rlung gi mda' gzhu mchog ma la ba dan sngon po 'phyangs pa/ mde rtse ro rkyang gnyis kyi bar gyi dbu ma'i nang du chud pa/ mde'u'i rtser raM las me gla ba'i ril ma tsam rtsa ba phra ba/ rtse mo rno ba/ rked pa ldir ba/ reg bya tsha ba/ kha dog dmar ba ste chos lnga ldan gsal gdab/ spyi gtsug gi dbu ma'i nang du haM yig dkar po mgo bo mthur la lta ba bsam/

After you request the Empowerment of Existence, clearly visualize the central channel that extends from inside the crown of the head down to the perineum. It has four attributes: it is straight as an arrow, hollow inside like copper coins [with holes in the centers], red as a lac flower, and glossy as sesame oil. {154} To its right is the red rasanā channel and to the left the white lalanā channel, both entering the central channel at the lower end. Both the rasanā and lalanā have coiled channel knots at each of the four places—navel, heart, throat, and head. At the head, the [upper ends] of the rasanā on the right and lalanā on the left branch into four lesser channels: two go to the right and left of the mouth, two go to the two nostrils, two go to the eyes, and two go to the ears, open like cobra hoods. At the opening of the anus is the arrow of vital winds, its tip hung with blue banners. The tip of the arrowhead, between the rasanā and lalanā, enters the central channel. On the tip of the arrow is a fire from raṃ, the size of a deer pellet. Visualize this flame with five attributes: fine at the base, sharp at the point, bulging in the middle, hot to the touch, and red in color. Imagine the white syllable haṃ hanging upside down inside the central channel in the top of the head.

de nas rlung ro dal bus phyir bsal nas/ rlung mnyam rgyur byas te steng rlung dal bus nang du mar drang / 'og rlung dal bus yar 'then la steng 'og gi rlung lte bar kha sbyar bas/ 'og gi rlung g.yos pas me de gzug mo byi thur gyi dbyibs 'dra ba zhig lte 'og tu 'bar/ yang rlung bzung nas lte bar 'bar/ rlung 'dzin thengs gsum pa la snying gar slebs pa'i drod kyis spyi bo'i haM yig las thig le mu tig gi phreng ba lta bur babs/ snying ga'i me la phog bas sor sgra dang bcas pa bsam/ me ma shi ba dang me lce ma 'dar bar byed pa zab gnad gcig yin pas gal che'o/ /

Then, after slowly clearing out the dead air, slowly inhale equally [into two nostrils] while drawing the vital winds in and down. Then slowly draw up the lower wind, joining the upper and lower winds at the navel. By that, the lower winds move, causing that fire to blaze up below the navel in a shape like a porcupine [quill]. Taking another breath makes it blaze up to the navel. At the third retention of the breath, it arrives at the heart and its heat causes drops from the haṃ letter in the head to fall like a string of pearls. Imagine the drops striking the fire at the heart with a sizzling sound. The fire does not go out, nor does it flicker—these are profound vital points that are very important.

des thog mar drod skye/ de nas bde ba/ de nas bde stong gi ting nge 'dzin skye bar 'gyur bas chos drug gi rtsa ba lta bu yin no/ / 'di yang ni gu mas/ / rang lus thabs ldan rtsa gsum 'khor lo bzhi/ / a haM 'bar 'dzag skad cig dga' bzhis brgyan/ / shes rab kha kha mu kha'i snyoms 'jug gis/ / zag bcas zag med dga' bzhi rim bzhin no/ zhes pas bstan to/ /

By that process, first warmth will arise, then bliss, then the meditative absorption of bliss-emptiness. Thus it is like the root of the Six Dharmas. As Niguma herself said [in the Vajra Lines]: One’s own body is the means, with three channels and four chakras. The A blazes and haṃ drips, adorning the four instances with four ecstasies. Uniting with the wisdom’s khagamukhā, the dissipating and nondissipating four ecstasies arise in sequence.[5]
gnyis pa gtum mo gos su gyon pa ni/ (155)
ii. Wearing the Clothes of Fierce Inner Heat {155}

lus gnad dang dmigs pa sngar bzhin las lag pa bsnol ba'i mthil gnyis mkhal ma g.yas g.yon la bkab la/ lte ba dang de'i thad kyi rgyab mkhal ma g.yas g.yon gnyis su me cog sgong tsam bzhi bsams la sngar bzhin rlung kha sbyor bzung bas drod myur du skye ba myong bas grub bo/ / na so rgas po yin na me phug ron gyi sgo nga'am ngang pa'i sgo nga tsam bsam mo/ /

The physical posture and visualization are the same as the previous practice, except that the palms of the crossed hands cover the right and left kidneys. Think that at the navel and directly behind it and at the right and left kidneys there are four balls of fire the size of [bird] eggs. By joining the winds as before, you will experience the warmth arising quickly, which is the accomplishment. If an elderly person does this, the fireballs should be imagined as the size of pigeon or duck eggs.
gsum pa gtum mo zas su za ba ni/
iii. Eating the Food of Fierce Inner Heat

lus gnad gong bzhin la sngar gyi dmigs pa'i steng du chu rlung dkar po bus/ me rlung dmar po bzung ste rlung kha sbyar bas/ ! rkan nas me 'jigs rtags gnyis bar dpe gcig la mi snang / mchan/ su rung ba zhig babs pas/ ! lto ba'i nang thams cad mes dmar mer gang bar bsgom mo/ / de la gegs 'byung nye bas myong ba dang sbyar na/ dang po rlung gi rlung bus/ de nas me rlung bus/ de nas rlung rnams 'og nas 'byung ba'i kha dog ltar bus nas/ de nas sa rlung ser po so rtsa nas bzung bar dmigs la lte 'og gi rlung nang du drangs te kha sbyar bas lto pa ser mer gang bar bsam/ de nas chu rlung dkar po ya rkan nas bzung bas dkar mer gang / me rlung dmar po so bar nas bzung bas dmar mer gang / de nas rlung rlung sngon po bzung ste steng 'og gi rlung kha sbyor bas lto ba sngo mer gang bar bsgom/ des drod myur zhing gegs chung ngo / /

The physical posture is the same as before, but add this to the visualization: Breathe out a white water-wind, and [breathe in] and hold a red fire-wind. The joining of the winds causes a fearsome fire to fall from the palate.[6] Meditate on this filling the entire belly inside with red fire. In this, since the occurrence of obstructions is imminent, apply the following in response to your own experience. First expel the air-wind, then expel the fire-wind, then expel all winds with the colors described below. Then visualize inhaling and holding the yellow earth-wind by the roots of the teeth. By your joining that with the wind drawn up from below the navel, the belly fills with yellow radiance. Then it fills with a white radiance by holding the white water-wind from the palate. Then it fills with a red radiance through holding the red fire-wind from between the teeth. Then the belly fills with blue radiance through holding the blue air-wind and joining the upper and lower winds. With those methods, heat will come swiftly and obstructions will be minor.
bzhi pa gtum mo gdan du bting ba ni/
iv. Spreading the Seat of Fierce Inner Heat

lus gnad dang dmigs pa gong bzhin gyi steng du/ nyal ba'i tshe khyi nyal sgor mor bya/ gzhog g.yas 'og tu bcug ste nyal la rlung phyir phyung ba dang / sna nas me dmar nar byung bas mal sbug thams cad mes dmar mer gang bar bsams la/ rlung cung zad bzung nas bsgom mo/ /

In addition to the physical posture and visualization described above, at bedtime curl up in the sleeping-dog posture with your right side underneath. As you exhale, imagine that red fire emerges continually from your nostrils and fills inside all your bedding with red radiance. Hold the breath slightly and meditate.
lnga pa srid pa'i dbang bskur zhu ba ni
v. Receiving the Empowerment of Existence

spyi bor bla ma sngar bzhin bsgom/ de'i thugs ka nas 'od 'phros bla ma yi dam sangs rgyas byang chub sems dpa' thams cad rdo rje 'chang gi rnam (156) bar spyan drangs la bstim/ kun 'dus bla ma rin po che la lus longs spyod thams cad mchod pa phul la/ bla ma rin po che bdag la srid pa'i dbang bskur bstsal du gsol/

Meditate on the guru above your head as before. Light radiates from the guru’s heart and invokes all the gurus, yidams, buddhas, and bodhisattvas in the form of Vajradhara, who dissolve [into the guru’s heart]. {156} Present your body and all possessions to the precious guru, the embodiment of all. Say: Precious guru, please confer upon me the Empowerment of Existence.

zhes gsol ba btab pas bla ma'i zhabs kyi mthe bong las bdud rtsi'i rgyun dkar po byung / smin mtshams yan chad gang / lus kyi dri ma dag / bum pa'i dbang thob/ lam bskyed rim bsgom pa la dbang / 'bras bu sprul sku mngon du byas par bsam/

With that supplication, a stream of white elixir emerges from the guru’s big toe. [It enters through your head and] fills down to the eyebrows. Think that physical stains are purified and you receive the vase empowerment. On the path, you are empowered to meditate on creation phase and manifest the resultant nirmāṇakāya.
bdud rtsi dmar po byung / mgrin pa yan chad gang / ngag gi sgrib pa dag / gsang ba'i dbang thob/ lam rdzogs rim bsgom pa la dbang / 'bras bu longs sku mngon du byas/

Red elixir emerges and fills down to the throat. Think that verbal stains are purified and you receive the secret empowerment. On the path, you are empowered to meditate on the completion phase and manifest the resultant saṃbhogakāya.
bdud rtsi sngon po byung / snying ga yan chad gang / yid kyi sgrib pa dag / shes rab ye shes kyi dbang thob/ lam bskyed rdzogs zung 'jug bsgom pa la dbang / 'bras bu chos sku mngon du byas par bsam/

Blue elixir emerges and fills down to the heart. Think that mental stains are purified and you receive the wisdom-awareness empowerment. On the path, you are empowered to meditate on combined creation and completion phases and manifest the resultant dharmakāya.

mthar bla ma 'od du zhu nas rang la thim pas/ bla ma'i sku gsung thugs dang rang gi lus ngag yid gsum dbyer med par gyur/ lus ngag yid gsum gyi sdig sgrib bag chags dang bcas pa thams cad dag / dbang bzhi pa thob/ lam spros bral bsgom pa la dbang / 'bras bu sku bzhi mngon du byas par bsam mo/ / des sdig sgrib dang dam tshig nyams chags thams cad dag / gegs mi 'byung / ting nge 'dzin ma skyes pa skye/ skyes pa rnams gong nas gong du 'phel bar 'gyur ro/ /

Finally, the guru melts into light and dissolves into you. Think that the guru’s awakened body, speech, and mind become inseparable from your body, speech, and mind. Physical, verbal, and mental negativities and obscurations along with habitual patterns are all purified. You receive the fourth empowerment. On the path, you are empowered to meditate without embellishment and manifest the resultant fourth kāya. That purifies all negative acts, obscurations, and damages and violations of sacred pledge; prevents obstructions; engenders the absorptions that have not yet arisen; and increases those that have more and more.
gsum pa rjes
c. Concluding Practices
['di] la gnyis las/
This has two parts: (1) Naturally Liberating Obstructing Forces and (2) Riding the Horse of Vital Winds.
dang po gegs rang grol ni/
i. Naturally Liberating Obstructing Forces

nu ma gnyis de'i dbus te gsum dang de gsum gyi thad ka'i rgyab tu khro bo'i mig shin tu 'jigs pa gsum bsam/ lus kyi spyi bo nas rkang mthil gyi bar la/ ba spu'i bu ga thams cad khrol ma'i mig gam tshags se'i mig lta bu bsgom/ de'i mig rnams nas nad thams cad sngo dmar dang / gdon thams cad sdig sbrul dang sbal lcong sogs dang / (157) sdig sgrib thams cad dud khu'i rnam pas tshags se'i nang nas chu tshags pa bzhin bud par bsams la kha sbyor bzung ngo / / smad du kun+da'i gegs byung na 'khrul 'khor dang dbab bzung zlog dgram gyi dmigs pas bsal lo/ /

Imagine that there are terrifying, fierce eyes in the three places of your two breasts and midway between them, and the three corresponding places on your back. Meditate that all the pores from your crown to your soles are like the eyes (i.e., holes) in a sieve or colander. From those eyes, all sickness as the color purple; all spirits as scorpions, snakes, frogs, tadpoles, and so forth; and all negativities and obscurations in the form of liquid coal are expelled out like water pouring through a sieve. {157} Hold the joining of winds while contemplating that. If obstruction of the kunda (sexual fluid) in the lower body occurs, yogic exercises and visualizations of descending, holding, reversing, and spreading will clear it up.
rjes kyi gnyis pa rlung rtar zhon pa'i man ngag ni/
ii. Riding the Horse of the Vital Winds

rang gi mchan khung gnyis dang rkang mthil gnyis su/ rlung gi bya mo sngon mo re re bsam mo/ / rdo rje khu tshur gnyis gzhag 'og tu gzhug / gtso bor sa rlung phyir bus/ rlung rlung nang du bzung ste/ steng 'og gi rlung kha sbyor te gling bzhi ri rab dang bcas pa la bskor bar bsam mo/ / rlung 'byangs nas 'gro ba'i tshe bya mo bzhis nam mkha' la 'khyer bar bsam ste/ rlung bzung nas phyin na rta me chog dang 'dra ba'i 'gros 'byung ngo / /

This is the esoteric instruction for the second concluding practice. Think that there are blue wind goddesses at both your armpits and both soles. Put your two vajra fists under your arms. Mainly expel the earth-wind and inhale and hold the air-wind. Join upper and lower winds, and think that you circle the four continents and Mount Meru. Once the winds are trained, think that the four goddesses are carrying you in the air when you move. When you hold the breath and arrive back, you will move like the excellent horse.

'di rnams kyang ni gums/ / bcud pa sdus dag byed stong ra'i gnad gsum dang / / drod myur gtum mo'i chos drug rim bzhin te/ / ri bong dbab bzung zlog dgram rlung dang bsre/ / gnyis med ye shes chen pos brgyan par bya/ / zhes pas bstan pa yin no/ /

Concerning these practices, Niguma taught [in the Vajra Lines]: The inner space purifier gathers the quintessence in three vital points, and to quicken the heat, the Six Dharmas, Inner Heat in sequence: rabbit descending, holding, reversing, spreading, and blending with vital winds. Adorn with undissipating, great, nondual, timeless awareness.[7]
gnyis pa sgyu lus chags sdang rang grol
2. Illusory Body, Naturally Liberated Desire and Anger
['di] la gsum ste/ dbang po rab bla ma dam pa grogs su bsten pa/ 'bring tshig gzhan gyis bar ma chod bar 'khrid pa/ tha ma mal gcig tu ting nge 'dzin bskyed pa'o/ /

This has three parts: (1) Relying on the Friendship of a Holy Guru for those of the highest capabilities, (2) Guidance without Interruption by Other Words for the average, and (3) Developing Meditative Absorption in a Single Sitting for the lowest.
dang po ni
a. Relying on the Friendship of a Holy Guru

sngon 'gro sngar bzhin byas nas/ rang gi spyi bor pad+ma dang zla ba'i gdan la/ rtsa ba'i bla ma rdo rje 'chang chen po sku mdog sngon po rdo rje dril bu thugs kar bsnol nas 'dzin pa/ zhabs rdo rje skyil krung sku gcer bu la rus pa dang rin po che'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ / zhal 'dzum bag dang bcas pa/ spyan gsum dang ldan pa dbu skra sil bus sku phyed yan chad khebs pa/ mtshan dang dpe byad kyis brgyan pa/ nyi ma 'bum gyi gzi brjid dang ldan pa/ 'od zer 'phro bas bdag gi rgyud byin gyis rlobs bzhin pa (158) zhig bsams la/ de'i mdun du bdag gis byang drangs pa bzhin du sems can thams cad kyang ku di ri ri gsol ba 'debs par bsams la/

After doing the preliminaries as before, visualize your root guru as Buddha Great Vajradhara seated on the lotus-moon seat above your head. He is blue and holds a vajra in the right hand and a bell in the left, crossed over his heart. He sits with two legs crossed in vajra position, his naked body adorned by bones and jewels. He smiles amiably and has three eyes. His loose hair falls over half of his body, and he is adorned by the marks and signs of an awakened being, shining with the brilliance of one hundred thousand suns. Imagine the radiating light rays blessing your mind stream. {158} Imagine all the sentient beings that you are leading into his presence supplicating with a low murmuring sound:
bla ma rin po che bdag med rtogs par byin gyis rlobs/ bdag 'dzin thong bar= sgyu lus 'byongs par= / 'od gsal phyag rgya chen po mngon du 'gyur bar=
Precious guru, bless me to realize nonself. Bless me to abandon fixation on a self. Bless me to refine Illusory Body. Bless me to actualize Lucid Clarity Mahāmudrā.

zhes gsol ba drag tu gdab cing / bla ma rin po che bdag la mngon par dbang bskur du gsol/ ces gsol ba gdab pas/ gong thabs lam ltar dbang bskur bas mthar rang gi lus ngag yid gsum dang / bla ma'i sku gsung thugs dang dbyer med pa'i ngang du yun ring du mnyam par bzhag go / de las ldangs pa'i spyod lam thams cad dang / sems la ci snang thams cad la/ a snang ni snang / bden ni mi bden/ sgyu ma yin/ rmi lam yin ang snyam du bsam mo/ / gsol 'debs bla ma'i lam khyer dang / ci snang bden med lam khyer gnyis gsungs pa'ang 'di kho na la 'dus pa yin no/ / rdo rje theg pa'i lam rnams kyi gtso bo 'di kho na yin pas/ 'di la 'bad cing rtse gcig tu nyams su blangs na/ lam thams cad myur du bgrod pa yin te

Thus pray with intensity and make this request: Precious guru, please confer the manifest empowerment on me. With that supplication, the empowerment is conferred as before in the path of methods. At the end, rest for a long time in the state of equipoise, your body, speech, and mind inseparable from the guru’s awakened body, speech, and mind. After arising from that state, in all daily activities and all mental activities, think, “Ah! Appearances do appear but their reality is not real. It is illusion. Alas, it is a dream.” The supplications of Integrating Devotion to the Guru on the path and Integrating the Unreal Nature of Whatever Appears are both taught separately, but here they are uniquely combined. Since just this is the main practice in all Vajrayāna approaches, if you energetically cultivate this experience one-pointedly, it is the fastest way to traverse all paths.
ye shes mngon byung las/ / sa dang lam gyi rim pa rnams/ / bla ma'i mos gus lo zlas bgrod/ / bla ma'i snang ba ma bral na/ / sangs rgyas rnams dang 'bral med gnas/ / zhes dang /

As it states in Actualization of Timeless Awareness: The stages of the levels and paths will be traversed in months and years through devotion to the guru. If you never part from the guru’s appearance, you dwell constantly with the buddhas.[8]
ni gu mas/ / lam lda sa bcu'i rim pa rnams/ / mos gus stobs kyis bgrod par byed/ / bla ma'i snang ba mi 'bral ba/ / rgyud sde'i dgongs pa gnad kyi mchog / ces gsungs so/ /
And from Niguma: The stages of the levels and paths are traversed on the strength of devotion. The sublime vital point of the tantras’ intent is never to part from the guru’s manifestation.[9]
gnyis pa dbang po 'bring tshig gzhan gyis bar ma chod par 'khrid pa ni/
b. Guidance without Interruption by Other Words

bla ma'i rnal 'byor sngar bzhin byas la/ e ma sngar skyes pa'i sems can thams cad kyang 'chi/ da skye ba'i sems can thams cad kyang 'chi/ da lta ba'i sems can thams cad kyang mi 'chi bar tshe thar du (159) lus pa gcig kyang med pas/ nga yang nges par 'chi/ da yang 'dzam bu gling pa'i tshe la nges pa med pas 'chi ba'i rkyen mang / 'tsho ba'i rkyen nyung bas myur du 'chi ba yin ang snyam du bsams pas/

For those of average capabilities, do the guru yoga as before. Then think: Alas! All sentient beings born in the past are dead. Those born now will also die. Of all the sentient beings existing now, not even one will get out alive and remain. {159} I too will most certainly die. Not only that, our time on earth is uncertain and there are many causes of death but few that sustain life. I’m afraid I will die soon.

tshe 'di'i mtho dman gang la yang bsgrub 'dod kyi blo mi 'jug pa zhig nam byung byung gi bar du bsgom/ de nas shi bas ci lto snyam na shi ba'i 'og tu med par mi 'gro/ / gnas lugs kyi don cig ma rtogs par shi na/ rigs drug gi grong khyer drug po gang rung las 'gro sa med/ de rnams gang du skyes kyang sdug bsngal gyi longs spyod 'ba' zhig la spyod pa ma gtogs bde ba'i skabs ye med pas skyid pa mi 'dug ang snyam du bsam zhing / sangs rgyas thob 'dod kyi blo bcos ma ma yin pa zhig nam skye bar du bsgom/ a 'di thams cad rmi lam yin sgyu ma yin snyam pa'i dran 'dun yang dang yang du bsgom mo/ /

Meditate until such time as you disengage from any idea of accomplishing something for this life, lofty or lowly. If you think, “Oh what if I die?” [know that] after death you will not cease to exist. If you die without realizing the single meaning of the abiding nature, there will be no place to go other than whichever of the six realms of beings is fitting. And in whichever place you are reborn, there is nothing other than the experience of suffering; never a chance for happiness. So it is not nice. Contemplate that and meditate until such time as an uncontrived desire to attain buddhahood arises. Meditate again and again with recollection and intention, thinking, “Ah, this is all a dream, all an illusion.”

de nas paM las pad+ma dang a las zla ba'i gdan gyi steng du/ hU~M las 'od 'phros/ 'phags pa mchod/ sems can gyi don byas/ tshur 'dus yongs su gyur pa las/ rang nyid 'khor lo sdom pa sku mdog dkar po/ / rdo rje dang dril bu thugs kar bsnol nas 'dzin pa/ rus pa dang rin po ches brgyan pa/ snang ngo na gzugs su grub pa/ thogs bcas gyi gzugs su ma grub pa/ snang la rang bzhin med pa me long nang gi gzugs brnyan lta bu zhig bsgom/ de la lha yi sku mdog phyag mtshan rgyan cha lugs bzhugs tshul gyi rnam pa 'di 'dra ba rang gi blos bkod pa ma gtogs phyi rol du grub pa mi 'dug pas 'di 'dra ba 'di snang ni snang / bden ni mi bden rmi lam yin/ sgyu ma yin snyam du bsam zhing /

Then a lotus from paṃ and a moon from A appear. Upon that seat, hūṃ radiates light that makes offerings to the noble ones and performs the welfare of sentient beings. The light returns and completely transforms into oneself as white Cakrasaṃvara holding vajra and bell crossed over the heart and adorned by bones and jewels. To one’s perception, a form does exist, but a tangible form does not exist. Meditate on appearance with no intrinsic nature, like a reflection in a mirror. Contemplate how such forms as the deity’s color, implements, jewels, accessories, and posture are nothing other than an invention of your mind and do not exist out there. So think, “Such appearances do appear, but their reality is not real. It is illusion. Alas, it is a dream.”

gzhan yang sems kyi yul du snod bcud nye ring bar ma dga' sdug la sogs pa'i snang ba ci byung yang / long gtam sogs tshig gzhan gyis bar ma chod par/ ngag tu sgyu ma yin/ rmi lam yin zhes brjod cing / yid (160) la'ang sgyu ma rmi lam gyi dran 'dun ye ma nyams par bya'o/ / rang lus snang stong lha sku dang / ci snang sgyu mar la 'khyer gnyis gsungs pa'ang 'di kho na la 'dus pa yin no/

Furthermore, whatever appearance occurs as an object of mind—whether of the environment or its inhabitants, close or distant or neutral, happy or sad—continuously say, “It is illusion, it is a dream” without interruption by other words, such as idle conversation. {160} In your mind, also never let your intentionality of recollecting illusion and dream diminish. The teachings of [visualizing] one’s own body as the deity’s form of appearance-emptiness, and the integration of whatever appears as illusion are uniquely combined here.

khye'u rab snang gis zhus pa'i mdo las/ / chos rnams sgyu ma rmi lam zhes/ / gang gi tshig brjod dran gyur na/ / srid pa'i 'ching ba las grol nas/ / tshe 'di nyid du 'tshang rgya nges/ / zhes gsungs so/ /

It states in the Sutra of the Questions of *Kumāraprabha: It is said “all phenomena are illusions and dreams.” Whoever says and recalls these words will be released from the bonds of existence and definitely awaken in this very life.[10]
c.
c. Developing Meditative Absorption in a Single Sitting

de rnams la'ang myong ba re ma skyes na dbang po tha mar song ba yin pas/ gsum pa dbang po tha ma mal gcig tu ting nge 'dzin skye ba na/ sngon 'gro rnams gong bzhin byas/ rang 'khor lo sdom par gsal ba'i lte ba'i 'og tu chos 'byung mas yar rim pa bzhin du/ nag po/ ser po/ dmar ljang / dmar nag / dmar po/ dkar po rnams kyi nang du rim bzhin/ dmyal ba/ yi dwags/ dud 'gro/ mi/ lha ma yin/ lha rnams bsgom/ de la sems rtse gcig tu gtad nas 'di thams cad sgyu ma yin rmi lam yin snyam du bsam zhing ngag tu yang brjod/ snang ba thams cad bden med sgyu mar nam song bar du mal gyi drod ma yal bar byas la gzhi gcig tu bsgom mo/ /

If not a single experience has arisen based on those methods, then it means you are of the least capability. So the third option for those of lesser capabilities is to develop absorption in a single sitting. Do the preliminaries as before. Visualize yourself clearly as Cakrasaṃvara. Below the navel is a source of phenomena with the following colors in order from the bottom up: black, yellow, light brown, maroon, red, and white. Meditate on the beings within them as, respectively, hell beings, hungry ghosts, animals, humans, demigods, and gods. Once you have focused with single-pointed attention on that, think and say, “All of this is illusion. It is a dream.” Until such time as all the appearances become unreal illusion, meditate on a single seat without letting it cool off.

gzhan yang nad gdon la sogs pa'i gnod pa'am/ bde ba skyid pa la sogs pa'i snang ba ci byung yang sgyu ma yin rmi lam yin ces brjod cing bsams pas/ rigs drug skyu mar 'char byed dang / nad gdon sgyu ma'i lam khyer dang / 'char byed yon tan tshogs drug dang / zhen med sgyu ma rang shar rnams 'di kho na las 'byung ngo / / bsgoms pas shes so/ / bsdu na chos 'byung phyi dkar la nang dmar ba gcig gi nang du rigs drug bsgoms nas sngar bzhin bsams pas sgyu ma rang shar gyi yon tan rnams 'byung ngo / /

Moreover, whatever appearances occur—whether harmful ones such as sickness, spirits, and so forth or good and pleasant and so forth—repeat “It is illusion, it is dream” and contemplate that. [The four instructions called] Making the Six Kinds of Migrators Arise as Illusion, Integrating Sickness and Spirits as Illusion, the Sixfold Set of Qualities That Develop, and the Natural Arising of Illusion Free of Attachment are all included in this single practice. You will understand by meditating. For a concise version, meditate on the six kinds of beings within the source of phenomena that is white outside and red inside. Then contemplate as before and all the qualities of naturally arising illusion will develop.

de rnams ni ni gu mas/ / sgyu lus bden med dbang po rab 'bring gsum/ / 'bral med mos gus rang lus cir snang kun/ / snang stong zhen bral lha sku lam (161) khyer bya/ / chags sdang rang grol bcu bzhi'i sa thob 'gyur/ / ces gsungs pa'i nyams len gyi zhal gdams so/ /

Regarding all these, Niguma gave her personal instructions on cultivating experience with this verse: Illusory Body, unreal, is for those of highest, average, and lesser capability: with constant devotion, with one’s body, and whatever appears, integrate them as the deity’s form of empty appearance, free of attachment. {161} Desire and anger naturally liberated, the fourteenth stage will be attained.[11]
3. Dream, Naturally Purified Double Delusion

yang ni gu mas/ gang gi bsam pa thams cad yongs spangs nas/ / rmi lam 'dun pa'i gnad la 'bral med bya/ / nying 'khrul rang dag sgyu ma lam khyer gyi/ / yon tan rang shar nyin mtshan dus su 'byung / / zhes gsungs pa'i snyan brgyud rmi lam nying 'khrul rang dag la don drug ste/ rmi lam bzung ba/ sbyang ba/ spel ba/ sprul pa/ bsgyur ba/ yul snang blta ba'o/ /

Also in Niguma’s [Vajra Lines] it states: Whoever has completely abandoned all ideas, should constantly maintain the vital point of intention for dreaming. Double delusion will be naturally purified and the qualities of the stages of the path of illusion will naturally arise at all times of day and night.[12] Instruction for the Natural Liberation of Dream’s Double Delusion from the aural lineage includes six topics: (1) recognizing, (2) refining, (3) increasing, (4) emanating, (5) changing, and (6) viewing objective appearance.
dang po rmi lam bzung ba
a. Recognizing Dreams
['di] la gnyis te/ sngon 'gro dang dngos gzhi'o/ /
This has two parts: (1) the preliminaries and (2) the main practice.
dang po ni
i. Preliminaries

sngon 'gro gzhan rnams gong dang 'dra ba las/ bla ma'i rnal 'byor ni/ rang gi spyi bor pad+ma dang zla ba'i gdan la rtsa ba'i bla ma sangs rgyas rdo rje 'chang chen po sku mdog dmar po rdo rje dang dril bu thugs kar bsnol nas 'dzin pa/ rgyan cha lugs gong dang 'dra ba zhig bsgoms nas/

This is similar to the previous preliminaries, but in the guru yoga visualize your root guru on the lotus-moon seat above your head as red Buddha Great Vajradhara, crossing the vajra and bell over his heart, with ornaments and attributes the same as before.

bla ma rin po che bdag gis rmi lam zin par byin gyis rlobs/ rmi lam 'byongs par= rmi lam spel bar= rmi lam sprul par= rmi lam bsgyur bar= yul snang blta bar byin gyis rlobs/ zhes gsol ba gdab cing / bdag la dbang bzhi rdzogs par bskur du gsol/

Supplicate with: Precious guru, bless me to recognize my dreams. Bless me to refine my dreams. Bless me to increase my dreams. Bless me to change my dreams. Bless me to look into objective appearance. Please confer upon me the full four empowerments.
ces gsol ba btab pas/ bla ma'i dpral ba'i oM las oM dkar po byung / rang gi dpral bar thim pas/ bum pa'i dbang thob/ lus kyi dri ma dag / lam bskyed rim bsgom pa la dbang /

With that supplication, a white oṃ emerges from the oṃ in the guru’s forehead and dissolves into your forehead. You receive the vase empowerment, which purifies physical stains and empowers you to meditate on creation phase as the path.
bla ma'i mgrin pa'i AHlas AHdmar po byung / rang gi mgrin par thim/ ngag gi sgrib pa dag / gsang ba'i dbang thob/ lam rdzogs rim bsgom pa la dbang /

Red āḥ emerges from the āḥ in the guru’s throat and dissolves into your throat, purifying verbal obscurations. You receive the secret empowerment, empowering you to meditate on completion phase as the path.
bla ma'i thugs ka'i hU~M las hU~M sngon po byung / rang gi snying khar thim/ yid kyi sgrib pa dag / shes rab ye shes kyi dbang thob/ lam bskyed rdzogs zung 'jug bsgom pa la dbang /

Blue hūṃ emerges from the hūṃ in the guru’s heart and dissolves into your heart, purifying mental obscurations. You receive the wisdom-awareness empowerment, empowering you to meditate on combined creation and completion as the path.

mthar bla ma 'od du zhu nas rang la thim pas rang gi lus ngag yid gsum (162) dang / bla ma'i sku gsung thugs dbyer med pa'i ngang la yun ring du mnyam par bzhag / lus ngag yid gsum gyi sgrib pa bag chags dang bcas pa thams cad dag / dbang bzhi pa thob/ sku bzhi mngon du byas par bsam mo/ /

Finally, the guru melts into light and dissolves into you. {162} Your body, speech, and mind and the guru’s awakened body, speech, and mind become inseparable. Rest in that state for a long time. Your physical, verbal, and mental obscurations along with habitual patterns are all purified. You receive the fourth empowerment. Think that you will actualize the four kāyas.
'di rmi lam sogs chos drug gi sngon du bya'o/ /
This precedes the Six Dharmas, such as Dream practice.
gnyis pa rmi lam bzung ba'i dngos gzhi
ii. The Main Practice of Recognizing Dream
['di] la gnyis te/ rang zin dang / 'chugs med gnyis so/ /
This has two parts: (1) self-recognition and (2) infallible [vital points].
dang po ni/
A) Self-Recognition

rang gi spyi bor haM yig las thig le dkar po sran ma tsam zhig byung nas snying gar slebs/ gsang gnas nas thig le dmar po sran ma tsam zhig yar byung nas snying gar slebs/ de nas thig le dmar po des dkar po de ded de/ snying gar khra kho ro ro 'khor ba la sems gtad/ rmi lam sgyu ma'i dran 'dun bya/ / de ltar thig le 'khor ba bum dbang / reg la khad pa gsang dbang / reg pa shes rab ye shes dbang / gcig la gcig thim nas 'od du yal te mi dmigs par song bar bsam pa ni dbang bzhi pa'o/ / de ltar yang nas yang du bsgom zhing gnyid du 'gro khar thig le gcig la gcig thim nas yal te song ba'i mi rtog ba'i ngang la rmi lam bzung ngo / / zin pa'i tshul ni/ gnyid thum phras mang po 'byung / de nas 'jam zin rtsub zin gang rung gis/ a 'di rmi lam du 'dug snyam du zin pa 'byung ngo / /

A pea-sized white drop emerges from the haṃ letter in the crown of your head and arrives at your heart. A pea-sized red drop from the perineum ascends to your heart. Then that red drop chases that white drop round and round, making a swirl of vivid colors at the heart. Focus your attention on that and recall the intentionality for dreams and illusion. In this way, the circling of the drops is the vase empowerment, when they nearly touch it is the secret empowerment, when they touch it is the wisdom-awareness empowerment, and when they dissolve into one another and vanish into light and you are left with no idea of a reference point—then you have received the fourth empowerment. Meditate like that again and again. When you are about to sleep and the drops dissolve into each other and disappear, you may recognize dreams within that state of nonthought. The way to recognize them is to take many naps. Then, whether you have a gentle dream or a nightmare, think, “Ah, this is a dream” and recognize it.
gnyis pa 'chugs med
B) Infallible Vital Points

['di] la don dgur mdzad kyang bsdu na gsum du 'dus te/ lus gnad/ dus gnad/ dmigs pa'i gnad do/ / dang po ni lus gnad tsog bu'o/ / gnyis pa dus gnad ni skya rings shar nas nyi ma ma shar gyi bar ro/ / gsum pa dmigs pa'i gnad la gsum ste/ rtog med gnyis dang / rtog bcas gcig go /

This was created with nine topics, but it can be subsumed into three: vital points of body, vital points of time, and vital points of visualization. First, the vital point of the body posture is sitting with legs drawn up. Second, the vital point of time is first light, before the sun rises. Third, the vital point of visualization is threefold: two that are without conceptual thought and one with conceptual thought.
rtog med la 'dzin pa'i dang po ni/
1) The First Vital Point of Recognizing Dreams without Concepts

rang gi spyi gtsug gi haM las thig le dkar po mar byung / gsang gnas nas thig le dmar po yar byung snying khar 'phrad/ thig le gnyis sngar bzhin 'phros 'ded kyi tshul gyis 'khor ba la sems (163) gtad/ a nga gnyid du song 'dug / 'di rmi lam du 'dug snyam pa'i dran 'dun drag po bya'o/ / gnyid du 'gro khar thig le dkar po de sna bug g.yas nas thon/ dmar po de sna bug g.yon nas smin mtshams su khra kho ro ro 'khor ba la sems gtad/ sgyu ma rmi lam gyi dran 'dun bya/ de nas thig le dkar po de 'khor lo sdom pa sku mdog dkar po rdo rje dril bu thugs kar bsnol nas 'dzin pa/ dmar po de yum rdo rje phag mo dmar mo gri gug dang thod khrag 'dzin bar song nas/ kho ro ro 'khor ba la sems gtad/ 'di sgyu ma yin/ 'di rmi lam yin snyam du bsam/ mthar yum yab la thim/ yab 'od du yal nas mi rtog pa'i ngang la gnyid log nas rmi lam bzung ngo / /

A white drop descends from the haṃ in the crown of your head and a red drop ascends from the perineum; they meet at the heart. They chase each other around as before. Focus your attention on their circling and think, {163} “Ah! I have fallen asleep. This is in my dream.” Recall this with intense intentionality. When about to fall asleep, the white drop exits through the right nostril and the red one through the left nostril, circling around in a colorful swirl at the point between your eyebrows. Focus attention on that and recall the intention of illusion and dream. Then the white drop becomes white Cakrasaṃvara holding vajra and bell crossed over the heart. The red one becomes red Vajravārāhī holding flaying knife and blood-filled skull cup. Focus your attention on their circling around and think, “This is illusion. This is a dream.” Finally, Vajravārāhī dissolves into Cakrasaṃvara, who dissipates into light. Then sleep in a nonconceptual state and recognize that you are dreaming.
rtog med la 'dzin pa'i gnyis pa ni/
2) The Second Vital Point for Grasping Dreams without Concepts

dbyings rang bzhin gyi rnam par dag pa 'di/ bsal bya glo bur gyi dri ma dag pa zhig yin zhes brjod la/ rang 'khor lo sdom par gsal ba'i snying gar pad zla'i steng du 'khor lo sdom pa mtshon gang ba 'od zer 'phro ba zhig bsam la nga gnyid du song 'dug / 'di rmi lam du 'dug snyam du bsam/ gnyid log khar rang nyid snying ga'i 'khor lo sdom pa la thim/ de yang 'od du yal song ste mi dmigs pa'i ngang du rmi lam bzung /

Say, “This naturally pure basic space is purified of the adventitious stains that are to be cleared away.” Imagine yourself as Cakrasaṃvara with a thumb-sized Cakrasaṃvara on a lotus and sun in your heart that is emanating light, and think, “I have gone to sleep. This is in a dream.” On the verge of sleep, you dissolve into the Cakrasaṃvara in your heart. That also vanishes into light. Within that nonreferential state, recognize that you are dreaming.
gsum pa rtog bcas la bzung ba ni/
3) Recognizing Dreams through Conceptual Thought

rmi lam gyi lus tsog pu/ dus skya rengs shar nas nyi ma ma shar gyi bar/ rmi lam gyi rgyu ni yi ge haM/ rmi lam gyi gnad ni mgrin pa yin pas/ rang gi mgrin par yi ge haM dkar po 'od 'phro ba zhig bsams la/ rmi lam gyi ngo bo ni gnyid du song ma song gi bar gyi rnam par rtog pa yin pas/ gnyid du song nas rmi lam rags pa ma shar gyi bar der mi la sogs pa'i rnam rtog rab rib shar ba de dran pas bzung ste mig mi 'byed par 'di rmi lam du 'dug snyam du ngos bzung bas rmi lam mi zin mi srid do/ / des kyang ye ma zin na spyi bor thod pa'i (164) nang gi klad rgya'i steng du rdo rje bdag med ma dkar mo gri thod 'dzin pa/ nam mkha' la lding ba 'dra ba zhig bsgom/ des mi zin mi srid do/ / 'di rgyun du byas na gegs che bas bzhag go /

The body posture for Dream practice is sitting with legs drawn up. The time is from first light until sunrise. The basis of recognizing dreams is the letter haṃ. The place of dreams is the throat. Therefore, imagine the emanating light of the white haṃ letter in your throat. The essence of dream is the discursive thoughts just before falling asleep. Therefore, once you have gone to sleep but before the arising of obvious dreams, this is where dim thoughts of people and so forth arise and you can recognize them with attentiveness. Without opening your eyes, think, “This is happening in a dream” and recognize it. That way it is impossible not to recognize it as a dream. {164} However, if you still do not recognize it, then meditate on white Vajra Nairātmya holding flaying knife and skull cup within your cranium on the cranial membrane, as if she is hovering in space. Then it is impossible not to recognize. If you do this continuously, it can be a big hindrance, so then leave it.
gnyis pa rmi lam sbyang ba
b. Refining Dreams
['di] la bzhi ste/ lus kyis sems sbyong ba/ sems kyis lus sbyong ba/ bdag med mas sbyong ba/ 'dun pas sbyong ba'o/ /
This has four parts: (1) Refining the Mind through the Body, (2) Refining the Body through the Mind, (3) Refining through Nairātmya, and (4) Refining through Intentionality.
dang po lus kyis sems sbyong ba ni/
i. Refining the Mind through the Body
rang 'khor lo sdom par dkar po rdor dril 'dzin par bsgom/ 'di rmi lam yin par 'dug / rmi lam la ji ltar sbyar sbyang yin snyam du bsams nas g.yang sa lta bul bskyur bas 'od du yal song bar bsam mo/ /

Meditate on yourself as white Cakrasaṃvara holding vajra and bell. Think, “This is a dream. In dreams, I can refine things however I want.” Then, throw yourself into an abyss or something and think that you vanish into light.
gnyis pa sems kyis lus sbyong ba ni/
ii. Refining the Body through the Mind
rang 'khor lo sdom par gsal ba'i smin mtshams dang tshegs thams cad du yi ge hU~M sngon po re re bsgom/ de'i 'od kyis rang gi lus lha sku phyag rgya chen po gsal stong 'dzin med kyi ngang du spyad/ /

Meditate that you appear clearly as Cakrasaṃvara with blue hūṃ at the point between the eyebrows and in each of the joints. Their light refines your body into the deity’s form of mahāmudrā, and it is refined within that state of clarity-emptiness without fixation.
gsum pa bdag med mas sbyong ba ni/
iii. Refining through Nairātmya

rang 'khor lo sdom par gsal ba'i nor bu'i nang du hU~M dkar po mgo bo mthur du lta ba zhig bsam/ de la dmigs pa gtad de/ 'di rmi lam yin snyam du bsam zhing ngag tu hU~M zhes brjod pas hU~M de mgo bo gyen du log bas/ rdo rje bdag med ma sku mdog dkar mo gri gug dang thod pa 'dzin pa zhig lus kyi nang du bde phri li li song nas 'od du zhu ste/ lus kyi nang thams cad 'od dkar pos gang bas mthar yal te song nas phyag rgya chen po'i ngang du bzhag go /

Imagine yourself clearly as Cakrasaṃvara with a white downward-facing hūṃ inside the gem [of the sexual organ]. Focus attention on that visualization and think, “This is a dream,” while uttering hūṃ aloud. The hūṃ turns to face upward and becomes white Vajra Nairātmya holding flaying knife and skull cup, entering your body inside with trembling bliss and then melting into light. Your whole interior body is filled with white light and finally disappears altogether. Rest within the state of mahāmudrā.
bzhi pa 'dun pas sbyong ba ni/
iv. Refining through Intentionality
snod bcud phra rags ci mthong yang rmi lam du 'dug snyam du bsams nas/ rang gi lus phar thal tshul thal du sbyang /
Whatever you see, whether subtle or coarse, in the environment or its inhabitants, think, “It is a dream,” then refine by passing back and forth through it.
gsum pa rmi lam spel ba
c. Increasing Dreams
['di] la gnyis te/ thug phrad du spel ba dang / gang 'dul du spel ba'o/ /
This has two parts: (1) Increasing Whatever Is Encountered and (2) Increasing for Whatever Is to Be Tamed.
dang po ni
i. Increasing Whatever Is Encountered

sa yi dkyil 'khor la dmigs te 'di rmi lam du 'dug / rmi lam gyi snang ba la gang spel spel yin snyam du bsams nas gcig las bcu/ bcu las brgya/ brgya las stong / stong las khri/ (165) de las 'bum la sogs pa blos 'khyud tshad du spel nas/ rim pa log ge bas bar snang gang ba tsam du bsgom mo/ / de'i 'og tu chu'i dkyil 'khor sngar ltar spel lo/ / de nas me'i dkyil 'khor/ rjes su rlung gi dkyil 'khor gong ltar spel lo/ / des mtshon te 'byung bzhi phra rags dang sems can phra rags gang mthong yang rmi lam du bsams nas gong ltar spel lo/ /

Visualize the mandala of earth and think, “This is a dream. I can increase whatever appears in a dream.” Then increase one to ten, then ten to a hundred, then a hundred to a thousand, a thousand to ten thousand, {165} that to a hundred thousand, and so on—as far as your mind can encompass—then gradually reverse and meditate that they fill all of space. After that, increase the mandala of water as before, then the fire mandala, and after that increase the wind mandala as above. With this as an example, increase whatever you see—subtle or coarse forms of the elements or of sentient beings—thinking that it is a dream as before.
gnyis pa gang 'dul du spel ba
ii. Increasing for Whatever Is to Be Tamed
['di] la gnyis te/ 'jig rten pa'i gang 'dul dang / 'jig rten las 'das pa'i gang 'dul lo/ /
There has two parts: (1) taming with mundane beings and (2) with transcendent beings.
dang po ni
A) Taming with Mundane Beings

pha rol po 'bu lta bu la mang por spel nas/ rang bye'u mang por sprul nas bza' ba sogs kyis 'dul/ bye'u lta bu la rang khra lta bu sprul nas 'dul/ khyi la sbyang khyi/ spyang khyi la stag / stag la seng ge /mi la srin po la sogs rang la rang gi gnyen po de dang der sprul nas gsod pa dang bcing ba dang brdung ba la sogs pa bya ste 'dul lo/ /

After you have increased an external adversary, such as insects, then tame them by increasing yourself as many birds to eat them, and so forth. For something like birds, you emanate something like hawks and tame them. Similarly wolves for dogs, tigers for wolves, lions for tigers, cannibal demons for humans, and so forth—emanate the appropriate opponents for each of them to tame them by killing, binding, beating, and so on.
gnyis pa ni/
B) Taming with Transcendent Beings

pha rol klu lta bu la rang bya khyung rgyal po dang / pe kar lta bu la rta mgrin/ klu bdud dang klu srin la 'jam dpal ye shes sems dpa'/ gnod sbyin dang srin po lta bu la phyag na rdo rje gtum po sogs gdon de'i gnyen por bsngags pa'i khro bo sogs de dang der sprul nas 'dul ba dang khyur mid la bza' ba dang / phyag mtshan gyis gtubs pa dang me phung gis bsreg pa la sogs pa bya ste 'dul lo/ /

Emanate as the king of garuḍas for something like nāga adversaries, Hayagrīva for something like Pekar, Mañjuśrī Jñānasattva for something like nāga devils and nāga cannibals, wrathful Vajrapāṇi for something like yakṣas and cannibals, and so forth. For each bad spirit, emanate whatever wrathful being is known to be its opponent power and tame it by vanquishing, swallowing, beating with implements, burning in bonfires, and so forth.
bzhi pa rmi lam sprul pa
d. Emanating Dreams
['di] la'ang des mtshon no/ /
This was illustrated by [the instructions for increasing dreams].
lnga pa rmi lam sgyur ba ni/
e. Changing Dreams

sa'i dkyil 'khor 'di chur bsgyur/ chu'i dkyil 'khor mer bsgyur/ me'i dkyil 'khor 'di rlung du bsgyur/ rlung gi dkyil 'khor de nam mkha' la yal song bar bsams nas de'i ngo bor blta'o/ / de ni snod kyi 'jig rten bsgyur ba'o/ / bcud kyi sems can bsgyur ba ni/ dmyal ba rnams yi dwags su bsgyur/ yi dwags rnams dud 'gror bsgyur/ dud 'gro rnams mir bsgyur/ mi rnams lha min tu bsgyur/ lha min lhar bsgyur/ (166) lha rnams phyag rgya chen por bsgyur/ yang lha nas dmyal ba'i bar yas mar bsgyur/ de bzhin du ma dag pa'i 'jig rten 'di yang dag pa'i zhing khams su bsgyur ba la sogs pa rmi lam la brtan pa thob par bya'o/ / de thams cad la'ang 'di rmi lam du 'dug rmi lam gyi snang ba la gang bsgyur bsgyur yin snyam du bsam pa gal che'o/ /

Think that you can change this mandala of the earth into that of water, change the water mandala into that of fire, the fire mandala into that of wind, and the wind mandala into space, where it vanishes. Then look at the essence. This is the transformation of the world environment. To change the sentient beings that inhabit it, change hell beings into hungry ghosts, hungry ghosts into animals, animals into humans, humans into demigods, demigods into gods, and gods into mahāmudrā. {166} Similarly, change this impure world into a pure realm and so forth, thus gaining stability in dreams. During all of this, it is important to remember that this is just a dream and dream appearances can be changed into anything.
drug pa yul snang blta ba ni
f. Viewing Objective Appearance
lus gnad dang / sngon 'gro gong dang 'dra ba las/ rang yi dam du gsal ba'i lte ba'i 'og tu chos 'byung ngam/ thod pa phyi dkar la nang dmar ba bdud rtsis gang ba zhig bsam/

The physical posture and preliminaries are the same as before, except imagine that you appear clearly as the yidam with a source of phenomena or a skull cup below the navel. It is white outside and red inside and filled with elixir.
de nas rang gi sna bug g.yas nas tshur rdo rje bdag med ma dkar mo gri gug dang thod pa bsnams pa gar stabs can cig gis sna drangs nas yi dam gyi lha dpag tu med pa byon/
Then white Vajra Nairātmya, holding flaying knife and skull cup and dancing, leads infinite yidam deities inside through your right nostril.
lte 'og nas bdud rtsi bzhes pas dgyes par bsam/
yi dam gyi lha khyed rnams kyis bdag gis yul snang gtan la phebs par mdzad du gsol/ snyam du bsams pas bdag med mas sna drangs nas sna bug g.yon nas phyir thon nas nam mkha' la bzhugs nas
Think, “Yidam deities, please let me ascertain objective appearance.” Again Nairātmya leads them out through the left nostril and they remain in space.
phyag gis brda mdzad nas/ thog mar dmyal ba'i gnas bstan/ de nas yi dwags/ dud 'gro/ mi/ lha ma yin/ lha yi gnas/ de nas bde ba can la sogs dag pa'i zhing khams bstan par bsam mo/ /
With a symbolic hand gesture, they show you first the places of hell, then of hungry ghosts, animals, humans, demigods, gods’ realms, and finally Sukhāvatī and the other pure realms.

de ltar nyin mtshan gnyis kar bsam zhing / yul snang gtan la nam phebs bar du bsgom/ skabs su snod bcud du snang ba de yi byung gnas 'gro gsum rtsad bcad nas rang gi sems kyi cho 'phrul du thag bcad/ sems kyi byung gnas 'gro gsum yang rtsad bcad nas mthar phyag rgya chen po snang stong zung 'jug gi ngang du mnyam par bzhag go /

Contemplate this both day and night and meditate until such time as objective appearance is ascertained. Occasionally investigate the arising, abiding, and ceasing of the appearances of the environment and its inhabitants. Become absolutely certain that they are apparitions of your own mind. Then after investigating the arising, abiding, and ceasing of mind, rest in equipoise within a state of mahāmudrā, the unity of appearance and emptiness.

des na 'dir rab dmigs med gsal mkhyen/ 'bring gang bsam gsal mthong / tha ma yid lus mkha' lding / dman pa dmigs pa'i yul mthong ngo / / phyi ma la bdag med mas yul snang 'char byed/ as yul snang rang (167) gsal/ thig le yul snang gsal byed ces spros pa rnams ni 'di kho na nyams su blangs pas grub par yod do zab/ //

In this, the best is to apprehend clarity with no frame of reference. Average is to see clearly whatever you think. Lesser is to soar in space with the mental body. And the least is to see the object of visualization. In this latter, there are some [practices] called Raising Objective Appearance with Nairātmya, Natural Clarity of Objective Appearance with [the Syllable] A, {167} and Illuminating Objective Appearance with Vital Drops. You will gain accomplishment by practicing just these elaborations, they are so profound. ithi

de dag gi skabs su 'khrul 'byams/ sad 'byams/ bde 'byams sogs kyi gegs byung na bla ma la mos gus byas nas gsol ba gtab/ yi dam chos skyong la tshogs 'khor dang gtor ma dang / gegs sel gyi dmigs pa rmog lcog pas mdzad pa'i 'byams gcod du ltos shig /

On those occasions, if obstructions arise such as excessive delusion, excessive insomnia, or excessive bliss, supplicate the guru with devotion, do communal feasts and torma offerings for the yidams and dharma protectors, and see the visualizations for clearing away obstructing forces in Mokchokpa’s Severing Excess.[13]
bzhi pa 'od gsal gti mug rang sangs
4. Lucid Clarity, Naturally Awakened Stupidity
['di] la gsum ste/ sngon 'gro/ dngos gzhi/ rjes so/ /
This has three parts: (1) preliminaries, (2) main practice, and (3) conclusion.
dang po ni/
a. Preliminaries

mi rtag pa dang 'khor ba'i nyes dmigs bsam/ kha zas bcud can za/ spyod lam dal bar sdod/ thabs lam nan bskyed la bsgom/ bla ma yi dam mkha' 'gro chos skyong srung ma rnams la tshogs 'khor gtor ma 'bul/ 'od gsal mos gus kyi gnad yin pas bla ma la gsol ba drag tu gdab bo/ /

Contemplate impermanence and the shortcomings of cyclic existence. Eat nutritious food and remain peaceful in your daily activates. Meditate persistently to generate the path of methods. Offer communal feast and torma to the guru, yidams, ḍākinīs, dharma protectors and guards. Devotion is the vital point of Lucid Clarity, so earnestly supplicate the guru.
gnyis pa dngos gzhi
b. Main Practice
['di] la bzhi ste/ 'od gsal bzung ba/ lam du khyer ba/ bsre ba/ mthar thug gi 'od gsal lo/ /
This has four parts: (1) recognizing, (2) integrating, (3) blending, and (4) ultimate lucid clarity.
dang po
i. Recognizing Lucid Clarity

['di] la a la bzung ba ni/ rang 'khor lo sdom pa gsal ba'i snying gar a dkar po dri ma med pa 'od 'tsher ba zhig bsam/ de'i 'od kyis lus kyi nang gang / de nas rang gi lus kyi phyi nang thams cad dkar seng nge ba zhig bsgom la bzung ngo / / de la ma zin na rang bde mchog dkar por gsal ba'i thugs ka'i pad zla'i steng du rang 'dra ba'i 'khor lo sdom pa tshon gang ba'i thugs kar a dkar po nyungs 'bru tsam 'od 'phro ba zhig bsam/ de las 'od 'phros pas lus phyi nang thams cad dkar sing song / ba spu'i bu ga rnams nas 'od 'phros pas snod bcud thams cad dkar sing nge ba zhig tu bsgoms pas 'char ro/ / de la ma zin na thig le la bzung ba ni/ rang 'khor lo sdom pa tshon gang tsam du gsal ba'i smin mtshams thig le dkar po til (168) 'bru tsam 'od 'phro ba zhig la sems rtse gcig tu gtad de/ yem yengs par bsgoms na 'char bar nges so/ / yang na bdag med mal bzung ba ni/ gong rmi lam gyi skabs su bshad pa'i klad rgya'i mtshams kyi bdag med ma nam mkha' la lding ba 'dra ba de bsgom zhing thod pa dung khang lta bur bsgoms pas zin no/ /

First, Recognizing Lucid Clarity Based on the Letter A: Imagine yourself clearly as Cakrasaṃvara with a radiant, stainless white A at the heart. Its light fills the body inside. Then meditate on your body as totally brilliant white inside and out, and recognize that. If you don’t recognize it, then imagine yourself as white Cakrasaṃvara with an identical thumb-sized version of Cakrasaṃvara on a lotus and moon in your heart. In that heart, imagine a white A the size of a mustard seed radiating light. {168} The light emanating from that makes the whole body brilliantly white inside and out. Meditate on the light radiating from all the pores in the body and turning the entire environment and its inhabitants into clear light—then it will arise. If you don’t recognize it by that, then there is Recognizing Lucid Clarity Based on a Vital Drop.[14] With yourself as thumb-sized Cakrasaṃvara, imagine a white drop the size of a sesame seed emanating light at the point between your eyebrows and focus with single-pointed attention on that. If you meditate without any distraction, [lucid clarity] will surely arise. Otherwise, there is Recognizing Lucid Clarity Based on Nairātmya. As explained before in the section on Dream, meditate that Nairātmya seems to hover in the space at the cranial membrane while the skull itself is like a conch dome. By this, lucid clarity will be recognized.
ii-iv.
ii–iv. Integrating, Blending, and Ultimate Lucid Clarity

lam khyer sogs phyi ma gsum ni 'od gsal shar na spros te bogs 'don dang bcas pa rnams rgyas par rdo rje'i tshig rkang dang khyung po'i bsdus don bzhin du bla ma gong ma'i khrid yig tu gsal zhing bla mas ngo sprad pas chog go /

The last three parts are elaborations for after lucid clarity has arisen. These and the enhancement practices have been clearly elucidated in the guidebooks of previous masters according to the Vajra Lines and Khyungpo Naljor’s summary.[15] Those and the introduction by the guru are sufficient.
rjes la
c. Concluding Practices

dam tshig la rtsa ba dang yan lag gi ltung bas ma phog par bya zhing / bye brag tu 'od gsal la thig le ye shes kyi dwangs ma yin pas khams dkar po ba thag tsam yang ma nyams par bya'o/ / gzhan yang gegs sel bogs 'don 'od gsal 'char sgo ngos 'dzin nyams rtogs dang nyin mtshan gyi khyad par sogs bla ma gong ma'i gsung sgros su gsal lo/ /

Make sure you are not touched by downfalls of the root and branch sacred pledges. In particular, do not lose even a trickle of the white element, since the vital drops are the refined essence of timeless awareness in Lucid Clarity [practice]. Further dispelling of obstructions, enhancements, identification of the doors of perception of lucid clarity, experiential realization, the differences of daytime and nighttime practice, and other subjects will be clarified in the commentaries of previous gurus.

'di dag kyang ni gu mas/ 'od gsal 'char byed bla ma'i mos gus dang / / bde chen zag bcas zag med lta gding dang / / bde gsal mi rtog dbyer med rang shar 'byung / / sbyor dngos rjes gsum dus gnad brgyan par bya'o/ / zhes pa'i nyams len no/ /

Concerning these practices, Niguma states [in the Vajra Lines]: Lucid clarity arises through devotion to the guru and the great bliss with and without dissipation, the yogic gazes cause bliss, clarity, and nonthought inseparable to arise naturally. Adorn the preliminaries, main part, and conclusion with the vital points of time.[16]
lnga pa 'pho ba ma bsgom sangs rgyas ni/
5. Transference, Buddhahood without Meditation

ni gu mas/ / 'pho bya 'pho byed bral ba yang rab ste/ / 'bring dang tha mas chags sdang spang bya ste/ / dga' zhing mos gus dmigs pa rtse gcig gis/ / gyen du 'phangs shing smon lam brgyan par bya/ / zhes gsungs pa'i

In the Vajra Lines, Niguma said: Nothing transferred, no transference; this is for the very best. The average and lesser abandon desire and anger and with joy and devotion, project upward with single-pointed focus. Adorn this with aspiration prayers.[17]
nyams len la/ rab lta thog nas 'pho ba/ 'bring sgyu lus nas 'pho ba/ tha ma smon lam gyis 'pho ba'o/ /

This practice has three parts: (1) transference directly based on the view for the best, (2) transference based on illusory body for the average, and (3) transference through aspirations for the lesser.
dang po ni/
a. Transference Based Directly on the View for the Best

'pho bya 'pho byed bral ba'i rang sems spros pa'i mtha' thams cad dang bral ba/ nam mkha' dwangs ba lta bu bde gsal mi rtog pa'i ngang la rtse gcig tu 'jog pa'o/ / 'di la chos sku de (169) bzhin nyid kyi 'pho ba yang zer ro/ /

With your own mind free of all extremes of elaboration, such as an object or agent of transference, you rest single-pointedly in the state of bliss, clarity, and nonthought like the radiant essence of space. {169} This is also called transference to dharmakāya suchness.
gnyis pa dbang po 'bring sgyu lus kyi steng nas 'pho ba
b. Transference Based on Illusory Body for the Average
['di] la/ yi dam la 'pho ba dang / bla ma la 'pho ba gnyis/
This has two parts: (1) transference to the yidam and (2) transference to the guru.
dang po
i. Transference to the Yidam
['di] la sbyang ba dang / las la sbyor ba gnyis/
This has two parts: (1) training and (2) application.
dang po ni/
A) Training

rang gi spyi bor pad nyi'i steng du yi dam 'khor lo sdom pa sku mdog sngon po zhal bzhi phyag bcu gnyis pa yum la 'khyud pa/ yum rdo rje phag mo dmar mo gri gug dang thod pa 'dzin pas yab la 'khyud pa zhig shin tu gsal bar bsgom/ de la mchod pa 'bul/ yi dam dpal he ru ka bdag mkha' spyod kyi gnas su drang du gsol/ / ces gsol ba drag tu gdab/ he ru kas rigs kyi bu yar shog gsungs pa'i gnang ba byung bas rang gi sems 'od dkar po zhig tu gyur nas/ rtsa dbu ma'i nang nas yar song ste/ spyi gtsug nas rgyang thon/ yi dam yab yum gyi thugs kar thim/ de nas yi dam yab yum kyang 'og min gyi 'khor lo sdom pa zhal bzhi phyag bcu gnyis pa longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku'i thugs kar thim par bsam/ de'i thugs ka na a dkar po gcig yod pa la sems rtse gcig tu gtad/ de nas a de 'od dkar po zhig tu song ste yas mar byung rang gi tshangs bug nas dbu ma'i nang na mar zhugs/ snying gar slebs pas a dkar po zhig tu song ba la sems gtad/ de ltar yang dang yang du sbyangs pas/ rab la spyi bo brdol nas khrag chu 'dzag pa 'ong / 'bring la spyi bo 'phrigs pa la sogs pa 'byung / tha ma la yang spyi bo za gul ba yong / de rnams 'byongs pa'i rtags yin no/ / de'i gnas skabs rnams su rnam shes thal srid pas/ spyi gtsug na rin po che'i snod kyis mnan/ des thub bo/ /

Meditate with heightened clarity on the yidams standing on the lotus and sun above your head: blue Cakrasaṃvara with four faces and twelve arms embracing the mother. Mother Vajravārāhī, red, holding flaying knife and skull cup, embracing the father. Make offerings to them. Supplicate fervently: Yidam, Glorious Heruka, please lead me to the celestial realms. Heruka says: Child of good family, come on up. With this permission, your own mind becomes a [sphere of] white light.
