It enters and rises up the central channel, then projects far out from the cranial aperture and dissolves into the hearts of the yidam couple. Then imagine that the yidam couple also dissolves into the heart of saṃbhogakāya as four-faced, twelve-armed Cakrasaṃvara in Akaniṣṭha. Focus single-pointed attention on a white A in their hearts. Then again that A becomes a white light that comes down and enters through your cranial aperture, becoming a white A as it arrives at the heart. Focus your mind on that. Train in that way again and again. The signs of successful training are, in the best case, swelling on top of the head that oozes blood or lymph. The middling is throbbing and so on, and the least is itching in that area. In all cases, it is possible that the consciousness leaves the body. This can be prevented by pressing a container made of precious substances on your head.
gnyis pa las la sbyar ba ni/
B) Application

nam zhig 'chi ltas kyis phog pa'i tshe bla ma yi dam la tshogs dang gtor ma 'bul/ lus longs spyod nye 'brel la sogs pa yul yid du 'ong ba sogs (170) gsum la brten pa'i chags sdang rmongs gsum thams cad spangs la gong gi dmigs pa bzhin rtse gcig tu 'phos nas sems slar lus la mi ldog go /

At some point, when you are stricken by the signs of death, offer feasts and tormas to the guru and yidam. Abandon all attachment, aversion, and stupid [indifference] based on three types of objects—pleasant, unpleasant, [and neutral]—such as your body, possessions, friends, and family. {170} According to the visualization described above, transfer your mind with single-pointed attention and so not return to the body.
gnyis pa bla ma la 'pho ba
ii. Transference to the Guru
['di] la'ang gnyis las
sbyang ba ni/
A) Training

sngon 'gro gong dang 'dra/ rang yi dam du gsal ba'i spyi bor pad zla'i gdan la rtsa ba'i bla ma rdo rje 'chang gi rnam pa rgyan cha lugs rnams gong sgyu lus bzhin du bsgoms nas yan lag bdun pa 'bul/ bla ma sangs rgyas rin po che la gsol ba 'debs so/ / zhes yang yang brjod cing bdag mkha' spyod kyi gnas su drang du gsol/ bdag gis phyag rgya chen po mchog gi dngos grub da lta nyid du thob par byin gyis brlab tu gsol/ zhes gsol ba btab pas gong bzhin du gnang ba byung bas/ rang sems 'od dkar po zhig tu song ste rtsa dbu ma'i nang nas yar song / tshangs bug nas rgyang 'thon nas bla ma'i thugs kar thim pas bla ma yang 'od du yal nas mi rtog pa'i ngang du 'jog / yang na bla ma 'og min du 'khor lo sdom pa'i thugs kar thim pa sogs sngar dang 'dra'o/ /

The preliminaries are the same as above. With yourself as the yidam, meditate on your root guru in the form of Vajradhara on a lotus-moon seat above your head. He has the attributes and ornaments as described in Illusory Body instructions. Offer the seven-branch service and repeat again and again: Precious Buddha Guru, I supplicate you. Please lead me to the place of the celestial realm. Please bless me to attain right now the supreme spiritual power of mahāmudrā. With that supplication, you receive permission as before. Your mind becomes a white light that enters the central channel and moves upward. It projects through the cranial aperture and beyond, dissolving into the guru’s heart. The guru then vanishes into light. Rest within the state of nonthought. Alternatively, it dissolves into the guru’s heart as Cakrasaṃvara in Akaniṣṭha, as before.
las la sbyar ba'ang
B) Application
['di] gong gi rigs pas shes dgos so/ /
This should be understood from the previous directions.
tha ma smon lam gyis 'pho ba ni/
c. Transference through Aspirations for the Lesser

gang zag tha mal pa dmigs pa mi chun pa rnams la ni 'chi ba'i tshe chags sdang spangs nas dag pa'i zhing du skye ba la sogs pa'i smon lam rnam par dag pa gdab cing sangs rgyas kyi mtshan byin rlabs can sgrog pa la sogs pa bya ba yin no/ / 'chug med mkha' spyod kyi 'pho ba ni zhal gdams zur du yod do/ / sdig po che btsan thabs su 'tshang rgya ba'i 'pho ba'i man ngag / /

Ordinary people who cannot manage these visualizations should abandon attachment and aversion at the time of death and then make pure aspiration prayers to be reborn in the pure land, and so on. They should perform positive acts of great blessing such as chanting the names of the buddhas. There is a separate oral instruction for Transference to the Unerring Celestial Realm. It is an esoteric instruction for the radical method of transference to the awakened state for the very sinful. ithi
drug pa bar do rgyal ba longs sku la/
6. Intermediate State, the Victors’ Saṃbhogakāya

spyir 'khor 'das kyi chos thams cad bar dor bsdus nas bshad na/ rang bzhin lhun grub kyi bar do/ ting 'dzin bsam gtan gyi bar do/ rnam smin skye shi'i bar do/ rmi lam bag chags kyi bar do/ lugs ldog 'chi kha'i bar do/ lugs 'byung srid pa'i bar do ste drug las/

In general, one could explain all phenomena of samsara and nirvana in terms of six intermediate states (bar do): (1) the spontaneously present intermediate state of intrinsic nature, (2) the intermediate state of meditative stability in absorption, (3) the intermediate state of birth and death of the karmically ripened body, (4) the intermediate state of habitual dreaming, (5) the intermediate state of the reverse order dying process, and (6) the intermediate state of the arising order in becoming. {171}

'dir sbyang bya'i (171) bar do gtso che ba skyes nas ma shi'i bar gyi skye shi bar do dang / gnyid du song nas ma sad kyi bar rmi lam bar do dang / shi nas skye ba phyi ma ma blangs bar gyi srid pa bar do gsum yin pa las/ dang po ni/ sbyong byed sgyu lus bsgoms pas sbyangs la/ gnyis pa ni sbyong byed rmi lam sbyong spel gyis sbyang bar bya'o/ /

Here, we are concerned with the three main intermediate states to be refined: the intermediate state of life, between birth and death; the intermediate state of dream, between sleep and waking; and the intermediate state of becoming, between death and rebirth. Of these, meditation on Illusory Body is the method that refines the first. Refining and increasing dreams is the method that refines the second.

'dir skabs su bab pa srid pa bar do sbyong ba'i tshul la ni gu mas/ / bar do snang sogs 'od gsal longs sku dang / / gang 'dul sprul sku mtshams sbyor skyo shas gnad/ / chags sdang phrag dog 'od gsal lha skus sbyang / / sgrib gnyis rang dag sku gsum mngon du 'gyur/ / gzugs sgra sa chu snang mched la sogs pa'i/ / thim 'gros rang bzhin brgyad cu shes par bya/ / zhes gsungs pa'i nyams len la/ da lta'i gnas skabs su srid pa bar do 'dun pas sbyang ba'i tshul dang / /'chi ba 'od gsal shar nas bar do tshun chad du nyams su blangs nas 'tshang rgya ba'i tshul gnyis/

The present subject concerns the methods to refine the intermediate state of becoming. Niguma’s Vajra Lines states: In the intermediate state, [recognize] appearance and so on as lucid clarity, as the deity’s form, and take rebirth as nirmāṇakāya to tame whomever. The vital point is aversion. Desire, anger, and jealousy are refined by the deity’s form of lucid clarity. The two obscurations are naturally purified and three kāyas actualized. Form, sound, water, earth, dissolve appearance, increase, and so on. One should know the progression of dissolution of the eighty natures.[18] There are two parts in this practice: (1) how to train in the intermediate state of becoming in one’s current circumstances and (2) how to attain awakening by practicing in the intermediate state after the arising of the lucid clarity of death.
dang po ni/
a. How to Train in the Intermediate State of Becoming in One’s Current Circumstances

a tsa ma nga shi nas bar do na slebs 'dug / gdos bcas kyi lus med pas phyin pa'i shul la rkang rjes kyang mi 'dug / lus la khams dkar dmar med pas phyi rol du nyi zla'i 'od mi snang / rang gi grib ma'ang mi snang 'dug pa bar do na yod pa'i rtags yin/ nga la bla ma rin po ches bar do la bar do ngo shes par gyis la bar do rgyal ba longs skur nyams su long gsungs pa'i skabs der slebs 'dug pas re sa gzhan na med do/ / bla ma dkon mchog mkhyen snyam du gsol ba gdab cing / rab kyis lta thog tu 'jog / 'bring sgyu lus bsgom/ tha ma smon lam rnam par dag par gdab bo/ /

Think, “Alas! I’ve died and arrived in the intermediate state. Without a material body, I leave no footprints behind. Without the white and red elements of my body, the external sun and moon don’t shine. Even my shadow does not appear. These are signs of being in the intermediate state. My precious guru told me to recognize the intermediate state and to practice the victors’ saṃbhogakāya. Now that time has come. I have nowhere else to place my hopes. Guru and Jewels, think of me!” Thus supplicate. The best practitioners settle directly on the view, the average meditate on Illusory Body, and the lesser make pure aspirations.

yang skabs su nga shi nas bar do na slebs 'dug / de'i rtags res 'ga' ram 'brog chen po skya ngam me ba dang / res 'ga' dmar ngam me ba dang / res 'ga' nag ngam me ba'i snang ba 'dug / 'di bla ma'i gsung gis yang ba'i (172) gnas gsum yod gsungs pa der 'dug pas/ re sa gzhan na med sogs sngar bzhin bsgom/

Then sometimes think, “I’m in the intermediate state. The signs are sometimes a huge abyss that is deep gray, sometimes deep red, and sometimes a deep black. These must be what my guru taught as the three places of terror. I have nowhere else to place my hope,” and so on, meditating as before. {172}

yang skabs su nga bar do na 'dug / sa rlung log pas ri bo sogs grum pa'i sgra dang / de'i 'og tu 'chor ba'i snang ba dang / chu rlung log pas chu bo chen po'i sgra dang / des khyer ba'i snang ba 'byung / me rlung log pas nags mes tshig pa la sogs me'i sgra dang / des tshig pa 'dra ba'i snang ba 'byung / rlung gi rlung logs pa'i stobs kyis las kyi rlung chen po'i sgra dang / des khyer ba'i snang ba 'byung ba 'di bla mas bar dor 'jigs pa'i sgra bzhi 'byung gsungs pa der 'dug pas/ re sa gzhan na med do sogs gong bzhin bsgom/

Again, on some occasions think, “I’m in the intermediate state. As the earth-winds withdraw, there are sounds of mountains crumbling and I seem to fall below them. As the water-winds withdraw, there are sounds of a huge river and I seem to be carried away by it. As the fire-winds withdraw, there are crackling sounds of forest fires and so on and I seem to be burning. The force of the air-winds withdrawing makes the sound of a great karmic gale, and I seem to be blown away. My guru told me about four terrifying sounds that arise in the intermediate state—these are them. I have nowhere else to place my hope…(etc.).” Meditate as before.

yang skabs su nga shi nas bar do na 'dug / gnas ma nges pa res 'ga' lha khang dang / khang khyim la sogs pa'i snang ba 'char/ res 'ga' sa phug dang spyil po la sogs pa'i snang ba 'char/ grogs la nges pa med pa res 'ga' lha'i bu dang bu mo sogs yid du 'ong ba dang 'grogs/ res 'ga' 'dre dang srin po sogs yid du mi 'ong ba dang 'grogs pa'i snang ba 'char/ zas ma nges pa res 'ga' bdud rtsi dang res 'ga' mi gtsang ba sogs kyi dris tshims pa'i snang ba 'char/ gos ma nges pa res 'ga' re shags la sogs pa dang / res 'ga' dar zab la sogs gyon pa'i snang ba 'char/ snang ba ma nges pa da ltar rang rang gi /yul na yod pa la de ma thag gshed du yul gzhan du slebs pa'i snang ba 'char/ skyabs ma nges pa res 'ga' zam pa dang ngal stegs ljon shing la sogs pa la skyabs su 'gro ba'i snang ba 'char gin 'dug pas/ 'di bla mas bar dor ma nges pa'i rtags drug yod gsungs pa der 'dug pas/ re sa gzhan na med do zhes sogs gong bzhin bsgom/

Then sometimes think, “I have died, and now I’m in the intermediate state. The place is unpredictable: sometimes a shrine room or something like a home appears, sometimes a cave or a hut. The companions are unpredictable: sometimes a pleasant divine boy or girl appears as my friend; sometimes unpleasant demons and cannibals and so forth appear as my companions. The food is unpredictable: sometimes elixir, but sometimes rotten food and so forth appear that I imbibe through their odors. The clothing is unpredictable: sometimes I appear to be wearing rags and such, sometimes silks and such. The appearances are also unpredictable: now I appear in my own country and then suddenly I appear to have arrived in another country. Refuge is unpredictable: sometimes it appears that I go for refuge under a bridge, or a bench, or a tree. My guru told me about the six unpredictable signs of the intermediate state. I have nowhere else to place my hopes…(etc.).” Meditate as before.

gzhan yang nga shi nas bar do na slebs 'dug / khar seng ngas nye du sogs la gtam lab dus gtam lan yod pa la da gtam lan mi khug 'dug / zas su'ang dri (173) za bar 'dug / ri bo sogs la'ang thogs med du phyin nas gang 'dod pa'i sa der yud tsam gyis sleb par 'dug ces sogs zas za ba gtam lab pa gos gyon pa sogs mdor na spyod lam bzhi po thams cad du a bar do na sleb 'dug ces sogs dang / re sa gzhan na med do bla ma dkon mchog mkhyen no zhes gsol ba 'debs pa dang / de'i ngang nas rab kyis lta thog tu 'jog / 'bring sgyu lus bsgom/ tha mas smon lam rnam dag gdab po/ /

Furthermore, think, “I have died and arrived in the intermediate state. Yesterday, when speaking with my relatives, they answered, but now I cannot elicit a reply. As food I eat odors. {173} I pass unobstructed through mountains and so forth, instantly arriving wherever I please.” When eating food, making conversation, getting dressed, and so forth—in short, during all four kinds of activities—think, “Alas, I have arrived in the intermediate state…(etc.)” and supplicate with “I have nowhere else to place my hopes. Guru and Jewels, think of me!” Within that state, the best settle directly in the view, the average meditate on Illusory Body, and the lesser make pure aspirations.
gnyis pa 'od gsal shar nas bar do tshun chad du nyams su blangs nas 'tshang rgya ba'i tshul la
b. How to Attain Awakening by Practicing in the Intermediate State after the Arising of the Lucid Clarity of Death
rab bar do dang po'i 'od gsal rang shar/ 'bring rgyal ba longs sku rang shar/ tha ma sprul sku 'gags med rang shar/ spyi'i gnad 'chug med lam khyer ro/ /

(1) The Natural Arising of Lucid Clarity in the First Intermediate State for the best, (2) the Natural Arising of the Victors’ Saṃbhogakāya for the average, (3) the Natural Arising of Unrestricted Nirmāṇakāya for the lesser, and (4) general vital points for unerring integration.
dang po ni
i. The Natural Arising of Lucid Clarity in the First Intermediate State

rim gyis 'chi ba'i dbang du byas na/ dang po yul snang lnga thim pa'i tshul ni/ gzugs sgra la thim pas mig gis gzugs cung zad mi gsal du 'gro/ / sgra dri la thim pas rna bas sgra mi tshor/ dri ro la thim pas snas dri mi tshor/ ro reg bya la thim pas lces ro bcud mi tshor/ reg bya'i chos rlung la thim pas lus kyis reg bya rnams ji lta ba bzhin mi tshor zhing / lus kyi mdangs ngan du 'gro'o/ /

In cases of gradual death, first there is the manner of dissolution of the five objective appearances. Form dissolves into sound and the eyes see forms a little less clearly. When sound dissolves into smell, the ears don’t hear sounds. When smell dissolves into taste, the nose cannot perceive smells. When taste dissolves into textures, the tongue cannot perceive essential tastes. When the phenomena of textures dissolve into the vital winds, the body cannot feel touch accurately and the body’s complexion deteriorates.

'byung ba thim tshul ni/ dang po sa chu la thim pas lus kyi stobs nyams/ kha chu dang sna chu 'dzag / chu me la thim pas lce dang kha sna sogs gsher ba'i cha thams cad skam/ me rlung la thim pas lus drod mtha' nas sdud/ rlung rnam par shes pa la thim pas phyi nang gi dbugs kyi rgyu ba chad do/ / rnam shes 'od gsal la thim pas skad cig dang po'i skabs su khams dwangs ma dkar po chu'i rang bzhin spyi gtsug na yi ge haM gi rnam par gnas pa de thur du babs pas/ phyi rtags su zla ba shar ba lta bu dkar lam pa 'byung / nang rtags su du ba lta bu ban bun nam smrig rgyu lta bu lang lang 'od zer lnga dang (174) ldan pa 'phro ba 'byung / de'i dus su snang ba zhes pa'i rnam par mi rtog pa'i ye shes skad cig ma gcig dang por 'char ro/ / de'i stobs kyis zhe sdang las gyur pa'i rtog pa sum cu so gsum po 'gags shing / de'i dus su dgra mi sha bo la yang zhe sdang skye ba 'byung / /

Then the way the elements dissolve: First earth dissolves into water and the body’s strength declines. Saliva and mucus begin to drip. When water dissolves into fire, the moist parts such as the tongue, mouth, and nose all dry up. When fire dissolves into wind, the body’s warmth contracts inward from the extremities. When wind dissolves into consciousness, outer and inner breathing stops. When consciousness dissolves into lucid clarity, during the first instant the white constituent of refined essence that is the nature of water and abides in the form of the letter haṃ within the head, descends. The external sign of that is a white radiance like the rising moon. The internal sign is a smokelike haze or a mirage-like shimmer radiating five-colored light rays. {174} At that time of so-called appearance, the first instant of nonconceptual timeless awareness arises. The force of that [appearance] blocks the thirty-three thoughts that come from anger. At that time anger won’t arise even for a deadly enemy.

de'i rjes su khams dwangs ma dmar po me'i rang bzhin lte ba na gtum mo a thung gi rnam par gnas pa de gyen la 'bar bas/ phyi rtags su nyi ma shar ba lta bu la/ nang rtags srin bu me khyer lta bu dmar chems pa 'byung / de'i dus su mched pa zhes bya ba'i rnam par mi rtog pa'i ye shes sngar bas ches gsal la 'dzin pa med pa de la lhan ner gnas pa skad cig ma gnyis pa 'byung ste/ de'i stobs kyis 'dod chags las gyur pa'i rtog pa bzhi bcu 'gags shing / de'i dus su lha'i bu dang bu mo la yang 'dod chags mi skye ba 'byung ngo / /

After that, the red constituent of refined essence that is the nature of fire and abides at the navel in the form of the short A of inner heat, blazes upward. The external sign is like the sunrise. The inner sign is the arising of red sparkles like fireflies. At that time of so-called increase (mched pa), nonconceptual timeless awareness grows clearer than before and you remain relaxed without fixation. That is the occurrence of the second instant. Its force blocks the forty thoughts that derive from desire, and at that point desire will not arise even for a divine boy or girl.

dkar dmar gnyis po de dang por snying gar 'phrad pa'i bar du rlung sems gnyis tshug pa las/ phyi rtags su mun sros pa lta bu nag 'thibs pa yod/ nang rtags su mar me rlung gis ma bskyod pa lta bu gsal la mi rtog pa sing ba zhig 'byung / de'i dus su thob pa zhes bya ba'i rnam par mi rtog pa'i ye shes gsal la 'dzin pa thams cad dang bral ba de la lhan ner gnas pa skad cig ma gsum pa 'byung ste/ de'i stobs kyis gti mug las gyur pa'i rtog pa bdun po 'gag go /

When the two white and red constituents first meet at the heart, vital winds and mind enter between them. The outer sign is dense blackness like night. The inner sign is a refreshing nonconceptual state of clarity, like a steady flame unmoved by wind. At that time of so-called attainment (thob pa), there is nonconceptual timeless awareness free of all fixation to clarity. Resting relaxed in that state is the occurrence of the third instant. Its force stops thoughts that derive from stupidity.

snying gar khams dkar dmar gnyis kyi bar du chug pa'i rlung sems dbu mar chud pa las/ phyi rtags tho rangs skya rengs shar ba lta bu skya lam pa zhig 'byung / nang rtags ston ka'i nam mkha' la nyi ma'i mdangs phog pa lta bu 'byung zhing / bde stong gi nyams 'char bar 'gyur ro/ / de'i dus su nye bar thob pa rang bzhin gyi 'od gsal zhes bya ba zhen rtog kyi dri ma thams cad dang bral ba bde gsal mi rtog pa'i ye shes skad cig ma bzhi pa 'byung zhing / ye (175) shes des rang bzhin brgyad cu'i rnam rtog phra rags kyi cha dang bcas pa thams cad 'od gsal la thim par 'gyur ro/ / 'di la rang bzhin gyi 'od gsal zhes kyang bya/ 'chi ba 'od gsal chos sku'i pho brang zhes kyang bya/ bar do dang po 'od gsal rang shar zhes kyang bya zhing /

The wind-mind that had entered between the white and red constituents now enters into the central channel. The outer sign is a pale radiance like the break of day. The inner sign is like the striking radiance of the sun in the autumn sky. An experience of bliss-emptiness arises. At that time of so-called full attainment (nye bar thob pa) of intrinsic lucid clarity, there is freedom from all stains of clinging thoughts. The timeless awareness of bliss, clarity, and nonthought occur in this fourth instant. {175} That timeless awareness causes all eighty natural concepts in all their aspects of subtle and coarse to dissolve into lucid clarity. This is also called intrinsic lucid clarity, the palace of dharmakāya lucid clarity, or the naturally arising lucid clarity of the first intermediate state.

sngar 'od gsal 'dris yod pa'i gang zag dbang po rab rnams kyis rang bzhin gyi 'od gsal de dang / slar bsgoms pa'i 'od gsal gnyis ma bu 'phrod nas 'od gsal de nyid ngos bzung ste/ de'i ngang du rtse gcig tu gnas pas srid pa bar dor 'jug mi dgos par chos skur 'tshang rgya zhing / chos sku skya med de las ma g.yos bzhin gzugs sku gnyis rang shar lhun grub tu 'byung nas des 'khor ba ma stongs kyi bar du/ gang la gang 'dul gyis sems can smin grol la 'god par byed do/ /

Practitioners of the highest capability who have previous experience with lucid clarity will recognize this as lucid clarity itself because they identify this intrinsic lucid clarity with the lucid clarity of previous meditation, like a meeting of mother and child. Since they remain single-pointed within that state, there is no need to enter the intermediate state of becoming. They are awakened as dharmakāya. And while not wavering from that unborn dharmakāya, the two form kāyas arise naturally as spontaneous presence that remains until all of cyclic existence is empty, taming whomever in whatever ways to mature them and establish all sentient beings in liberation.
ye shes rol pa'i rgyud las/ / 'od gsal zin pa'i gang zag la/ / bar do'i grong khyer des mi mthong / / gzhan don gzugs sku'i snang ba 'char/ / dper na yid bzhin nor bu 'dra/ / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Display of Timeless Awareness Tantra states: Individuals who recognize lucid clarity will not see the city of the intermediate state. Form kāyas will arise to benefit others, as, for example, wish-fulfilling gems.[19]

de ni rim gyis pa'i dbang du byas pa gtso che ba tsam yin/ cig char ba la de 'dra ba'i rim pa'i nges pa med/ skyes bu tha mal pa 'chi ba'i 'byung ba sogs thim tshul dang / rnal 'byor pas bsgoms pa'i nyams 'char tshul 'dra bas/ du ba dang smrig rgyu sogs dang por 'byung ba'i nges pa med do/ / mdor na rgyal bas mdo rgyud las gsungs pa dang / bla ma sgom pa mtshan nyid dang ldan pa'i gsung dang / rang gis bsgoms pa'i myong ba gsum po mthun dgos kyis/ go yul dang myong ba so sor song na gyod byed cing / pho tshod tshabs su 'gro ba dka' bas chos par khas 'che ba tsho gzab dgos so/ /

This is just from the point of view of gradualist practitioners. For instantaneously [realized practitioners], that particular sequence is not definite. For an ordinary person, the dissolution of elements and so forth at death is like the way experiences arise in meditation for a yogin. So it is uncertain whether the first occurrence is of smoke or mirage and so forth. In short, the Victor’s sutras and the teachings of a guru with authentic meditation and one’s own meditative experiences—these three must be in accord. When knowledge and experience part ways, it is the cause for regret, and desperate boasting is a big problem. Those who would claim to be practitioners, take care!
gnyis pa 'bring rgyal ba longs sku rang shar ni/
ii. The Natural Arising of the Victors’ Saṃbhogakāya for the Average

dbang po 'bring la bar do dang po'i 'od gsal la gnas par ma nus pa'i gang zag (176) gis srid pa bar dor 'jug dgos shing / de'i bdun phrag dang po la longs sku thob pa'i phyir du 'bad dgos so/ / de la bdun phrag dang po'i zhag phyed dang bzhi tshun chad la skye ba snga ma'i lus/ yul/ khyim/ nor rdzas/ nye 'brel sogs kyi snang ba 'char bas/ dus der bar dor shes pa 'byung dka'/ de nas zhag phyed dang bzhi song nas phyi ma'i lus kyi snang ba yud tsam re shar nas snga ma'i lus snang des rtag ma thub pa dang / bkres skom sogs kyi sdug bsngal gyis nyen nas snga ma'i nye 'brel rnams kyi rtsar phyin nas zas skom blangs pas/ zas skom ster ba lta zhog gtam lan tsam yang mi smra bar rang gi ming nas 'bod cing mya ngan dang smre sngags 'don pa mthong nas a pa nga shi 'dug snyam du ngo shes pa 'byung / de'i tshe bla ma dam pa'i zhal nas bar do la bar dor ngo shes par gyis la rgyal ba longs sku nyams su long zhig gsungs pa'i dus der sleb 'dug snyam du shes pa sngar goms pa'i stobs kyis 'byung zhing de'i tshe bar do rgyal ba longs skur sangs rgyas pas chog /

A person of average capabilities who cannot settle into the lucid clarity of the first intermediate state must enter the intermediate state of becoming. They must strive in order to attain the saṃbhogakāya in the first week. Up to the first three and a half days of that week the appearances of the last life’s body, region, home, wealth, possessions, friends, and relatives arise. In that time, it is difficult to understand that it is the intermediate state. When three and a half days have passed, glimpses of the future body will arise fleetingly, and it becomes difficult to maintain the appearance of the last life’s body. When pained by hunger and thirst and other afflictions, you go to your previous friends and family to take food and drink. But they won’t even reply to your request, let alone give you food and drink. Once you see them calling your name, weeping and wailing, you’ll think, “Ah, I am dead,” and recognition will dawn. At that point, you’ll think, “My holy guru told me to recognize the intermediate state and practice the victors’ saṃbhogakāya. That time has come.” That understanding happens on the strength of previous familiarization, and you may now awaken as the victors’ saṃbhogakāya in the intermediate state.

re dga' snyam pa'i 'dun pa dang ldan pas bla ma la gsol ba btab nas bar do'i snang ba thams cad rang gi sems snang yin/ rang gi sems snang thams cad sgyu ma rmi lam yin snyam du bsams nas/ rang yi dam lha/ snod kyi 'jig rten gzhal yas khang / bcud kyi sems can lha dang lha mor bsgyur cing bsgoms pas sngar bsgoms pa'i stobs kyis/ rang rgyal ba longs sku mtshan dang dpe byad kyis brgyan pa snang la rang bzhin med pa gsal la rtog pa med pa/ bde la zhen pa med pa'i lha sku/ chos sku'i ngo bo/ / longs sku'i rnam pa/ sprul sku'i phrin las/ de gsum dbyer med pa'i bde ba chen po'i skur rang shar du 'byung ste/ des 'khor ba ma stongs kyi bar du gdul bya gang la gang 'dul gyis smin grol la 'god par byed do/ / sngar bsgoms pa zhig yin na de'i stobs kyis bar do'i (177) shes pa de da lta bas shes pa sum bcu 'gyur gyis gsal bas sangs mi rgya mi srid pas the tshom ma byed par sgoms shig / bdun phrag dang por sangs ma rgyas na sngar bsgoms pa'i stobs chen po med pa dang / dbang po yang tha mar song ba yin pas/

Sometimes supplicate the guru with thoughtful intention and remember that all appearances are your own mind’s appearances, and all the appearances of your mind are illusion and dream. Then meditate on yourself as the yidam deity and the world environment as the palace with the inhabiting sentient beings transformed into gods and goddesses. The force of your previous meditation causes you to appear as the victors’ saṃbhogakāya adorned with the major and minor marks—appearance without intrinsic nature, clarity without concept, and bliss without attachment. The deity’s form is dharmakāya in essence, saṃbhogakāya in form, and nirmāṇakāya’s enlightened activity. Those three combined as mahāsukhakāya arises of itself. That will remain until all of cyclic existence is empty, taming whomever in whatever ways to mature them and establish all sentient beings in liberation. {177} If you have meditated previously, your intermediate state consciousness will be thirty times clearer than your current consciousness. So there is no way not to attain awakening. Meditate without entertaining doubts.
gsum pa dbang po tha mas sprul sku 'gags med rang shar ni
iii. The Natural Arising of Unrestricted Nirmāṇakāya for the Lesser

zhag bdun phrag bdun gyi bar du bar dor gnas srid pas/ de la nga shi nas bar do na 'dug snyam pa'i sdug bsngal chen po 'byung zhing / de'i rjes la pha ma dang pho mo sogs la dmigs pa'i 'dod chags skyes nas de la brten pa'i phrag dog dang mig ser skye/ des mtshams sbyar nas 'khor bar skye ba len par 'gyur bas/ de la nga shi 'dug snyam pa'i dus der/ kye ma chags sdang skyes na de'i dbang gis 'khor bar skye ba len par 'gyur zhing des sdug bsngal bas/ da ni bde chen gyi zhing du mchog gi dngos grub thob par bya'o snyam pa dang / bar do'i snang ba thams cad bden med sgyu ma yin snyam du bsam zhing bla ma la gsol ba gdab/

If you have not attained awakening in the first week because your previous meditation was not powerful enough, you have turned out to have lesser capabilities. It is therefore possible that you will remain in the intermediate state for forty-nine days. You will think, “I have died and now am in the intermediate state” and feel great suffering. After that, desire will arise in regard to father or mother, male or female, and so on. Jealousy and envy will also arise based on that desire. That establishes the connection for taking rebirth in cyclic existence. Therefore, at the time that you think “I have died,” also think, “Alas! By the power of attraction and aversion arising, I will take a rebirth of in cyclic existence. Rather than that suffering, I will now attain the supreme spiritual power in the pure realm of great bliss.” Also think, “All these appearances of the intermediate state are illusions and do not truly exist,” and supplicate the guru.

de nas rang gi mdun du chos 'byung mthing nag gcig gi nang du rang sems hU~M sngon por gyur par bsam/ de las 'od zer kha dog sna lnga pa 'phros pas/ 'gro ba lnga'i bag chags dang dri ma sbyangs/ mngal sgo bkag par bsam mo/ /

Then imagine before you a dark-blue source of phenomena. Your own mind as a blue hūṃ is inside it. Five-colored light rays radiate from that and purify the habitual patterns and stains of the five kinds of migrators. Think that it blocks the door to a womb.

de nas hU~M de yongs su gyur pa las rang sems yi dam yab yum du bsgom/ bar do'i chags sdang gi yul pho mor snang ba de yang yi dam yab yum du bsgoms nas/ mchod pa 'bul zhing gsol ba btab/ sgra grags tshad sngags/ dran rtog thams cad lha sku phyag rgya chen po'i ngang du skad cig yud tsam mnyam par bzhag par/ phyi nang snod bcud thams cad dang rang lus snang stong zhen bral gyi sprul sku'i snang ba 'ba' zhig rang shar du byung nas/ dus de nyid du 'tshang mi rgya mi srid do/ /

Then meditate on the hūṃ completely transforming into your mind as the yidam couple. Also meditate on all the male and female appearances in the intermediate state that evoked attachment and aversion as the male or female yidam, and make offerings and supplications. All sound is mantra and all thought and memory is the mahāmudrā of the deity’s form. Rest in equipoise within that state for a moment. The entire external environment and internal inhabitants and your own body of empty appearance free of attachment will naturally arise as nothing but the appearance of nirmāṇakāya, and it will be impossible not to attain awakening at that point.
bzhi pa spyi gnad 'chug med lam khyer ni/
iv. General Vital Points for Unerring Integration

dbang po rab 'bring tha ma gsum ka'i skabs su bar do skyo (178) shas kyi gnad yin pas bar do'i dran 'dun dang / skyo shas drag po skyed cing bla ma la gsol ba gdab/ pho mor snang ba sogs mdor na bdag gzhan snod bcud thams cad gzhal yas khang dang bcas pa'i yi dam yab yum du bsgom/ sprul sgyur gyi dran 'dun ye ma nyams par bya'o/ / rgyas par bla ma gong ma'i gsung sgros rnams su shes par bya'o/ / de dag gis ni gu chos drug gzhal gdams mdo tsam du bshad pa'o/ / mdor na rtsod ldan snyigs ma'i dus 'dir/ sems can rnams log ltas rgyud gang ba'i stobs kyis chos par rloms pa rnams kyang phal cher tshong dus su 'o ma la chus bslad nas 'tshong ba bzhin du/ bla ma gong ma'i gsung dang rgyal ba'i bka' la rang gi rtog bzos bslad nas rang gzhan thams cad slu bar byed pas gong ma'i gsung dang them yig / rang gi myong ba dang sbyar nas lta ba rnam par dag pa dang ldan pas man ngag khyad par can 'di nyams su len pa'i dka' spyad bzod par byas te rtse gcig tu nyams su blangs na tsho 'di'am bar do tshun chad du sangs rgyas nas mkha' spyod kyi gnas su 'gro bar nges pa yin no/ /

A sense of disillusionment with cycle existence is the vital point for the Intermediate State in all three cases of practitioners with best, average, and lesser capabilities. {178} Therefore, remember intentionality and develop intense disillusionment while supplicating the guru. Meditate on appearances of male and female—in short, on oneself and others, the entire environment and all its inhabitants—as the divine palace with its yidam couples. Never allow your mindful intention of emanating and changing [appearances] to diminish. More extensive explanation can be learned from the teachings of previous masters. This explanation is a mere summary of the oral instructions on the Six Dharmas of Niguma. In conclusion, in these degenerating times of conflict, the force of beings full of perverse views makes people who arrogantly claim to be Buddhists mostly resemble merchants at the market selling watered-down milk. They pollute the teachings of past masters and the Victor’s words with their own contrived ideas and deceive themselves and others. But once you join your own experiences to the teachings and directories of the past, you will possess the totally pure view. Then when you forbear any hardships in practicing these special esoteric instructions and single-pointedly take them into your experience, in this life or during the intermediate state you will definitely attain awakening and then travel to the sacred celestial realm.

'dir yang ni gu mas/ / log ltas rgyud dkrugs rtsod ldan snyigs ma'i dus/ / yang dag chos ni nyin skar rus sbal spu/ / log chos tshong dus 'o ma'i chos spyod tshe/ / nyams myong lung dang thems yig rgyan par gces/ / lam gyi mchog gyur 'di nyid nyams len tshe/ / gzhan gyi dus min 'chi kha'am bar ma dor/ / bde stong zung 'jug sku gsum rang shar nas/ / rnam par dag pa'i mkha' spyod nyid du 'gro/ / zhes bka' rgya dang bcas nas gsungs so/ /

Here, Niguma states [in the Vajra Lines]: In the degenerating time of conflict when wrong views disturb our mind streams, genuine dharma is as daytime stars and turtle fur. In a time when perverse dharma is bartered as the milk of ethical behavior, cherish meditative experience adorned by scriptures and inventories. Those who practice this sublime path will naturally arise as the three kāyas, inseparable bliss-emptiness immediately, in this life, or in the intermediate state, and will go to the totally pure celestial realm.[20] Thus she spoke and sealed the instruction.
Colophon

ni gu chos drug gi zhal gdams gyi gnad yig snying po kun 'dus zhes bya ba/ bla ma rnams kyi zhal gdams phyogs gcig tu dril ba 'di ni lung stong gi smyon pas/ thar pa gling gi sgrub khang zhal dkar (179) lha gdong du nyams su blangs pa'i rtogs pa la dpes nas gnas mchog ri bo cher stag lo zla ba bdun pa'i tshes bcu mkha' 'gro 'du ba'i dus su yongs su rdzogs par sbyar ba'o/ / yi ge pa ni bka' bcu pa blo gros rgyal mtshan yin no/ / nyams rtogs yar ngo'i zla ltar gong nas gong du 'phel bar shog /

This Collection of Essentials from the personal instructions on the Six Dharmas of Niguma was collected from the personal instructions of all the gurus and included in one place by the Madman of the Empty Valley at the Shelkar Lhadong retreat center of Tarpaling, where I realized them through practice. With that exemplar, I fully completed it at the sublime sacred site of Riwoche on the day the ḍākinīs gather, the tenth of the seventh month in the year of the Tiger. The scribe was Lodrö Gyaltsen, holder of the ten precepts. May meditative experience and realization increase like the waxing moon.
mang+ga laM b+ha wan+tu/ (180) (181)
maṅgalaṃ bhavantu
@#/ /ni gu'i yan lag phyag chen ga'u ma'i khrid bzhugs so// //
5. Niguma’s Auxiliary Practice, Guidance in Amulet Mahāmudrā[1]
(182)@#/ /na mo gu ru/ /
namo guru
bde chen lhun grub 'dus ma byas/ / longs sku rdo rje 'chang chen sogs/ / bla ma rnams la phyag 'tshal nas/ / phyag rgya chen po 'dir bshad bya/ /
Spontaneously present unconditioned great bliss, saṃbhogakāya Great Vajradhara and others; I bow to all the gurus, and now explain mahāmudrā.
de la ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro ma ni gu ma'i gdams pa phyag rgya chen po ga'u ma la gsum ste/ sngon 'gro/ dngos gzhi/ rjes so/ /
The instruction on Amulet Mahāmudrā by Niguma, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness, has three parts: (1) preliminaries, (2) main practice, and (3) conclusion.
dang po
I. Preliminaries
['di] la gnyis te/ thun mong dang thun mong ma yin pa'o/ /
This has two parts: (1) common and (2) uncommon preliminaries.
dang po sngon 'gro thun mong ba ni/
A. Common Preliminaries

rang gi mdun gyi nam mkha'i gnas su rin po che'i khri pad+ma zla ba'i steng du ngo bo rtsa ba'i bla ma la rnam pa 'khor lo sdom pa sku mdog dkar po zhal gcig phyag gnyis pa rdo rje dang dril bu thugs kar bsnol nas 'dzin pa/ rus pa dang rin po ches brgyan pa/ snang la rang bzhin med pa zhig bsam/ de'i mdun du skyabs 'gro tshad med pa bzhi bsgom/ byang chub mchog tu sems bskyed de man+Dal 'bul/ yig brgya bzlas/ bla ma brgyud pa la gsol ba gdab/ 'chi ba mi rtag pa las rgyu 'bras 'khor ba'i nyes dmigs rgyas par bsgom/ sems can thams cad mar (183) shes pa dang / drin dran pa sogs kyis byams pa dang snying rje dgra lta bu la nam skyes kyi bar du bsgom pa ni spyi dang mthun no/ /

Imagine in the space before you a jeweled throne with a lotus and moon seat. Upon that is the essence of your root guru in the form of white Cakrasaṃvara with one face and two hands holding vajra and bell crossed over his heart, adorned by bones and jewels—an appearance with no intrinsic nature. Before him you go for refuge, meditate on the four immeasurables, and arouse the mind of awakening. Then offer a mandala, recite the hundred syllables, and supplicate the lineage of gurus. Meditate exhaustively on death and impermanence, karmic cause and effect, and the shortcomings of cyclic existence. Meditate on love and compassion until you feel it even for your enemy through recognizing all beings as your own mother, recalling their kindness, and so forth. {183} These are the standard practices.
gnyis pa thun mong ma yin pa'i sngon 'gro ni/
B. Uncommon Preliminaries

rang babs gsum gyi steng du 'jog pa ste/ de yang rang lus yi dam lhar gsal ba'i rkang pa rdo rje'i skyil krung / lag pa gnyis mnyam gzhag gi phyag rgya bca'/ sgal tshigs dang por bsrang / mgrin pa cung zad sgu bar bya/ mig thad kar rang sor blta/ lce rtse rkan la sbyar/ mchu so thad kar bzhag / lag pa'i gru mo nang du rlog bcug pas sgom shing gi tshab byas pa'i lus gnad legs par bca'/ de nas rtsa bzhi nywa bzhi lhod kyis lhod pa ni lus rang babs so/ / mchu 'byed 'dzum gyi rtsol ba dang bral zhing ngag smra brjod med pa ni ngag rang babs so/ / mig gi lta stangs dang bcas pas 'di bsgom snyam pa'i sgom 'dod kyi rtog pa dang bral te ma bcos par 'jog pa ni sems rang babs so/ /

This concerns resting directly in the three naturally settled states. With your body as the yidam deity, sit with your legs crossed in vajra position. Place your two hands in the mudra of equipoise, straighten up your spine, slightly bend your neck, look straight ahead with relaxed eyes, touch the tip of your tongue to your palate, leave the lips before your teeth, and lock your arms with the elbows turned inward as a substitute for a meditation support stick. Properly assume these vital points of the body. Then relax the four channels and four tendons. This is the naturally settled state of the body. Do not try to close or open your lips, and remain free of verbal utterances. This is the naturally settled state of the speech. Rest without any contrivance, including the desire to meditate with the idea that holding a yogic gaze is meditation. This is the naturally settled state of the mind.

de'i ngang la had de chad de gnas pa ni sngon 'gro'i tshad yin/ de 'dra de la (184) tha mal gyi shes pa zhes bya/ chad nas ngal bso ba la sogs pa'i gnas skabs su yud tsam re sems can kun la 'char te de ngos ma zin pas 'khor bar 'khyams par yin no/ / des na spyod lam bzhi po thams cad du dbang po drug gi yul du phyi'i yul drug po ci snang yang de dran pas bzung ste/ de'i ngo bo la ce re bltas pas gsal stong 'dzin med du cham song ba dang / nga'i sngon 'gro shar 'dug snyam ngos bzung te/ de la had de chad de bzhag go /

To abide in that state with a hiatus of openness is the measure of the preliminaries. {184} Something like that is called ordinary mind (tha mal gyi shes pa). All beings experience it occasionally in certain circumstances, such as resting after exhaustion. Not recognizing that is the cause of their wandering in cyclic existence. Therefore, grasp it with mindfulness no matter which of the six sense objects appear to the six sense organs during all four daily activities. Look directly at the essence [of that appearance] and you will fully experience empty clarity without fixation. Recognize that “now my preliminary practice has dawned” and settle in that with startled openness.

de'i skabs su sngar ma bsgoms pas shes pa 'phro na 'dis bogs 'don te/ phyi'i snang ba yul la ngos bzung ci 'dug / nang lus la ngos bzung ci 'dug / gsang ba sems la ngos bzung ci 'dug rig pas dpyad la blta/ bltas pas ngos bzung ma rnyed na de'i ngang la gzhag go / yang snang ba la sems 'phro na gang la 'phro ba'i yul gyi snang ba de dang po gang nas byung / da lta gang na gnas/ mthar gang du 'gags/ 'ol spyi la ma bzhag par legs par btsal/ de nas 'dzin med du bun song na de dran pas bzung nas de'i ngang du bzhag go / de ltar rtsad bcad/

If, on that occasion, consciousness continues to proliferate outward due to a lack of previous meditation experience, then apply the enhancement practices. Observe with logical analysis what there is that can be identified in external objective appearance. What can be identified internally in the body? What can be identified in the secret level of the mind? After such observation, if you cannot find anything to identify, then settle within that state. If your mind continues to project out to appearances, then [consider] that objective appearance itself. Whence did it arise in the first place? Now where does it dwell? Where will it go in the end? Don’t rest with a vague understanding but make a thorough search. If this becomes a hazy state without identification, then recognize it with mindfulness and settle into that state. Investigate it in that way.

yang gcod mkhan gyi sems de yang gang nas byung / gang du 'gro/ gang na gnas rtsad bcad la blta/ bltas pas sems cho lang 'gro yin 'dug na de'i ngo bo la blta zhing ye ma yengs par rig pa gcun/ gang du yang mi rtog par rtse gcig tu lhan ner gnas na de ka'i ngang du mnyam par gzhag go / yang de ltar byas kyang rtog pa 'phro na dran pas bzung la/ rtog pa gang skyes thams cad de ma thag rgyun rbad rbad bcad la bzhag go / de rnams kyi skabs nyams ci skyes pa thams cad byung rgyal du bskyang / de ltar byas kyang ye mi thub par 'phro na de dran pas bzung la rtog pa de'i rjes bcad la ci la 'phro ba lta bar byas nas rtog (185) pa'i mtshang rig rig gdar sha bcad par bya'o/ / de ltar ma yengs par bsgoms na gsal stong 'dzin med kyi nyams 'char bar the tshom med do/ / de lta bu'i sgo nas sngon 'gro'i khrid them nas rkun po'i ngo sprod bya'o/ / de'i rtags tshad ni lus ngag gi bya bas mi 'phrog pa'o/ / de'i bogs 'don lha sku rlung dang bsre ba sogs ni phyag rgya chen po rlung bsres kyi dmigs rim bzhin shes par bya'o/ /

Also, watch the mind that investigates—whence does it arise, where does it go, and where does it stay? When you observe the investigation itself, if you notice that mind has become scattered, look directly at the essence of that and intensify awareness with no distraction at all. When you remain serenely single-pointed without any thoughts whatsoever, rest in equipoise in that very state. If you follow those directions but conceptual thought still proliferates, then get a hold with mindfulness. As soon as a thought arises, cut off its trajectory completely and settle. On all those occasions, maintain a nonjudgmental attitude toward whatever experience arises. If that never works and thoughts still proliferate, to get a hold of it with mindfulness follow the aftermath of a thought to see where it goes. You will gain complete resolution by recognizing the hidden flaw of thoughts, [which is that they do not truly exist]. {185} When you meditate in that way without distraction, there is no doubt that the experience of empty clarity without fixation will arise. After fulfilling the instructions for the preliminaries through those methods, do the burglar’s pointing-out introduction.[2] The signs of success are that physical and verbal acts cannot rob [the experience]. The enhancement practices are to blend the vital winds in deity practice and so forth. You should learn the process of visualization for blending the winds in mahāmudrā.

'dir nye bar mkho ba'i rlung 'dzin lugs cung zad cig bstan na/ lus gnad legs par bca'/ rlung mnyam rgyu ru bzhag / de nas dang po rlung gi rlung sngon por bus/ de nas me rlung dmar por bus/ de nas chu rlung dkar por bus/ de nas sa rlung ser por bus/ de nas nam mkha'i rlung kha dog med pa ba spu'i bu ga thams cad nas song bar bsam zhing rlung phyir bus la/ de nas dang po sa rlung dal bus sna bug nas drangs nas 'og rlung 'then la lte bar ser mer ba la sems gtad la bzung / de nas mi thub na dal bus phyir gtang / de'i rjes su chu rlung snying gar drangs nas gong ltar 'dzin/ de nas me rlung mgrin par drangs nas gong ltar 'dzin/ de nas rlung rlung spyi bor drangs nas gong ltar 'dzin/ de nas nam mkha'i rlung ba spu'i bu ga thams cad nas drangs nas lus kun la khyab par 'dzin no/ / yang nas rlung dang me rlung / chu rlung dang rlung gi rlung zung du bsdebs nas bzung yang rung ngo / /

Now for a short presentation of the required practice of holding the breath. Assume the correct vital points of posture and let the winds (or breath) move evenly. Then first exhale blue wind-wind. Then exhale red fire-wind. Then exhale white water-wind. Then exhale yellow earth-wind. Then exhale colorless space-wind. As you exhale, think that all [those winds] have departed through all your pores. Then, first slowly inhale earth-wind through the nostrils while drawing up the lower wind. Focus your attention on the yellowness at the navel and hold it. When you can no longer hold it, slowly exhale. After that, draw in the water-wind to the heart and hold as before. Then draw in the fire-wind to the throat and hold as before. Then draw in the wind-wind to the head and hold as before. Then draw in the space-wind through all the pores and hold as it pervades the entire body. Alternatively, it is appropriate to do it in pairs: earth-wind with fire-wind and water-wind with wind-wind.
gnyis pa dngos gzhi
II. Main Practice
['di] la gnyis kyi/
dang po skyon bzhi rang grol ni/
A. Naturally Free of Four Faults

sems rang gi gnas lugs stong nyid dang 'du 'bral med kyang nye drags bsam mthong ba'i skyon gyis 'khor bar 'khyams so/ / dpe rang gi byad bzhin dang 'dra/ de yang me long gsal ba'i rkyen dang 'phrad na gzugs brnyan (186) rang gis kyang mthong ba bzhin du bla ma dam pa'i man ngag gi me long dang 'phrad nas nyams su blangs na sems kyi gnas lugs mthong bar nus so/ / phyag rgya chen po rang la 'char kyang dpes mtshon ma nus shing zab drags pas ngos ma zin/ rang babs su nam bzhag kyang 'char te sla drags pas yid ma chas par yengs med dang bral/ sku gsum rang la shar yang bzang drags pas blor mi shong bas nges pa ma skyes te thag chod dang bral ba'i skyon gyis 'khor bar 'khyams pa yin pas/ da ni skyon bzhi po spangs la bla ma'i man ngag la brten nas rang shar ngos bzung nges shes bskyed la thag bcad yengs med du bskyang ngo / /

The abiding nature of your mind is emptiness and unity beyond unity or separation, yet it is too close to see. This fault causes us to wander in cyclic existence. This is like your own face, [which you cannot see until] you come across the right condition of a clear mirror wherein you see your reflection. {186} Likewise, when you meet the mirror of the holy guru’s instructions and put them into practice, you can see the mind’s abiding nature. Mahāmudrā arises in oneself, but it cannot be indicated by examples or metaphors, so it is too profound to recognize. You can rest in the naturally settled states any time, but it is too easy to believe and so you are distracted. The three kāyas arise in oneself but they are too fine to comprehend and thus certitude does not arise. These faults that prevent decisiveness are the cause of wandering in cyclic existence. So now abandon those four faults. Once you rely on the guru’s esoteric instructions, you will recognize what is self-evident, develop certainty, and with absolute decisiveness maintain nondistraction.
gnyis pa mthar thug sku bzhi rang shar ni/
B. Ultimate Natural Arising of the Four Kāyas

mnyam rjes blos byas thams cad dang bral ba'i phyag rgya chen po rang shar du bzhag pa'i dus su/ sna tshogs su shar ba de sprul sku rang shar/ de la gsal 'dzin dang bral ba'i rtog med de chos sku rang shar/ gsal la rtog med bde bar shar bas longs sku rang shar/ de gsum gyi rang bzhin dbyer mi phyed pas mthar thug bde ba chen po'i sku rang shar ro/ / de nyid la mi rtog pa'i cha de ji lta ba/ 'dzin pa med par shes bya sna tshogs su snang ba de ji snyed pa'i ye shes/ de gnyis dbyer med pa dbyings ye shes dbyer med pa yin no/ / de dag gi bogs 'don ni/ chos thams cad stong zhing bdag med ma zhig yin pa la nga dang bdag tu bzung bas 'khor bar 'byams pa tsho snying re rje snyam du bsam pa dang / mos gus dung ba byas la gsol ba 'debs pa dang / de rnams gang la yang had de chad de bzhag par bya'o/ / dngos gzhi brtan pa'i tshad ni bsgom rgyu rdul tsam yang med/ yengs rgyu skad cig tsam yang med par nyin mtshan spyod lam thams cad rtog med kyi ngang du khor mor gnas pa'o/ /

At the time of resting in the naturally arising mahāmudrā, which is free from all equipoise, postmeditation, and mental fabrication, a variety of things arise. That is the natural arising of nirmāṇakāya. Nonconceptual freedom from fixation on that clarity is the natural arising of dharmakāya. The arising of bliss in that nonconceptual clarity is the natural arising of saṃbhogakāya. The indivisible nature of those three is the natural arising of the ultimate mahāsukhakāya. The nonconceptual aspect of that suchness is the timeless awareness of things as they are. The variety of appearances to be known without fixation is the timeless awareness of things in their multiplicity. The inseparability of those two aspects is the inseparability of basic space and timeless awareness. To enhance those [experiences], contemplate the wretchedness of all those who wander in cyclic existence due to attributing notions of me and mine to the fact that all phenomena are empty and hence nonself. Supplicate with yearning devotion. Rest in the openness of all of that at all times. The measure of stability in the main practice is that there is not even an iota of something to meditate on, yet there is not even an instant of distraction. You remain continually within that state of nonconceptuality day and night, during all activities. {187}
III.
III. Conclusion

mdor na rjes ni/ stong nyid (187) snying rje dbyer med pa'i ngang nas/ bsngo bya sngo byed dmigs pa'i dug bcom ste/ / chos kyi dbyings la mi bsngo shes gyur nas/ / dge kun rnam mkhyen sangs rgyas bsngo bar shog / ces sogs bsngo ba dang smon lam rnam par dag pa 'debs pa ni man ngag dam pa yin no/ /

In short, the conclusion is to recite perfectly pure dedications and aspirations such as the following. This is the sublime esoteric instruction. From within a state of inseparable emptiness and compassion, I vanquish the poison of referencing a dedication object or act. In the knowledge that there is no dedication in the realm of phenomena, may all virtue be dedicated to omniscient buddhahood.
[Colophon]

nying khu'i yan lag gi chos skor las lta ba'i khrid phyag rgya chen po ga'u ma'i nyams len mdor bsdus pa 'di yang lung stong smyon pas rang gi myong ba dang sbyar nas/ gnas mchog dpal ri bo cher sbyar ba'i yi ge pa ni bka' bcu pa blo gros rgyal mtshan yin no/ / sarba mang+ga laM//

From the quintessential auxiliary practices, this guide to the view, a summary of the practice of Amulet Mahāmudrā, was written by the Madman of the Empty Valley, having applied my own madness. It was composed in the sublime sacred site of glorious Riwoche. The scribe was Lodrö Gyaltsen, holder of the ten precepts. sarva maṅgalaṃ
@#/ /ni gu'i yan lag lam khyer gsum gyi khrid bzhugs so/ /
6. Niguma’s Auxiliary Practice, Guidance in the Three Integrations[1]
na mo gu ru/ /
namo guru

ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro ma ni gu ma'i snyan brgyud kyi yan lag skor las/ 'phyugs med lam khyer gsum gyi nyams len la gsum ste/ snang ba la brten nas bla ma lam du khyer ba/ yi dam lam du khyer ba/ sgyu ma lam du khyer ba'o/ /

The practice of the Infallible Three Integrations on the Path from the auxiliary cycle of the aural lineage of Niguma, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness, has three parts that are based on appearances: (1) integration of the guru, (2) integration of the yidam, and (3) integration of illusion.
dang po ni/
I. Integration of the Guru Based on Appearances

rang gi mdun gyi nam mkha'i gnas su/ paM las pad+ma 'dab ma bzhi pa/ de'i lte ba dang 'dab ma rnams su/ a las zla ba'i dkyil 'khor re re/ de'i dbus su rtsa ba'i bla ma 'khor lo sdom pa sku mdog dkar po zhal gcig phyag gnyis pa rdo rje dang dril bu thugs kar bsnol ba/ shar du dgyes rdor dkar po rdo rje dang dril bu thugs dkar bsnol ba/ lhor gsang ba 'dus pa ser po rdo rje dang dril bu thugs kar bsnol ba/ nub tu ma hA mA yA dmar po gong dang 'dra ba/ byang du rdo rje 'jigs byed ljang gu gri gug thod khrag thugs kar steng 'og tu 'dzin pa/ thams cad kyang rus pa dang rin po che'i rgyan gyis brgyan par bskyed/ de dag gi dpral bar oM dkar po/ mgrin par AHdmar po/ thugs kar hU~M sngon po/ lte bar (188) hU~M sna tshogs pa de las 'od 'phros pas rang 'dra ba'i ye shes sems dpa'i rnam par bla ma yi dam sangs rgyas thams cad spyan drangs la bstim/ rigs lnga spyan drangs te dbang bskur bas/ thams cad la rgyal pa rigs lngas dbu brgyan par bsgoms la/

A four-petaled lotus arises from paṃ in the space before you. In its center and on each of the four petals moon mandalas arise from A. In the center, the root guru appears as white Cakrasaṃvara with one face and two hands holding a vajra and bell crossed over his heart. White Hevajra holding vajra and bell crossed at his heart is on the petal in the east, yellow Guhyasamāja holding vajra and bell crossed at his heart is in the south, red Mahāmāya the same as above is in the west, and green Yamāntaka holding a flaying knife and blood-filled skull cup above and below his heart is in the north. Visualize them all adorned by ornaments of bones and jewels. White oṃ is in their foreheads, red āḥ in their throats, blue hūṃ in their hearts, and multicolored hūṃ in their navels. {188} Light radiates from those and invokes the gurus, deities, and buddhas in the forms of awareness beings identical to those [visualized], into which they dissolve. Invoke the five families, who confer empowerment. With that, all the deities become crowned by the buddhas of the five families.

bla ma rin po ches bdag la mngon par dbang bskur du gsol/ / zhes gsol ba btab pas/ bla ma'i dpral ba nas oM dkar po byung / rang gi dpral bar thim/ bum dbang thob pa sogs gong gtum mo dang 'dra/ mgrin pa nas AHdmar po byung / rang gi mgrin par thim/ thugs ka nas hU~M sngon po byung / rang gi thugs kar thim/ de nas phyogs bzhi'i lha bzhi po de gtso bo la thim/ de gdan dang bcas pa 'od du khra spung song ba dang rang la thim pa'i ngang du mnyam par bzhag go /

Then supplicate: Precious guru, please confer the actual empowerment on me. A white oṃ emerges from the guru’s forehead and dissolves into your forehead. You obtain the vase empowerment and so forth, as in the previous section on Fierce Inner Heat. A red āḥ emerges from the throat and dissolves into your throat. A blue hūṃ emerges from the heart and dissolves into your heart. Then the four deities in the four directions dissolve into the principal figure. The principal and his seat melt into a colored array of light and dissolve into you. Rest in equipoise in that state.

de nas skyabs 'gro sems bskyed 'chi ba mi rtag pa bsam pa sogs kyi sngon 'gro rnams bsgom/ de nas rang yi dam du gsal ba'i spyi bor pad zla'i gdan la rtsa ba'i bla ma 'dzum yal le ba sku mdangs dang ldan pa zhig bsgoms nas bdag gis byang drangs pa bzhin du/ sems can thams cad kyang gsol ba 'debs par bsam zhing / bla ma rin po che la gsol ba 'debs/ bdag 'dzin blo yis thongs par byin gyis rlobs/ / dgos med rgyud la skye bar byin gyis rlobs/ / sgyu lus rmi lam 'byongs par byin gyis rlobs/ 'od gsal phyag rgya chen po mngon du 'gyur bar byin gyis rlobs/ zhes gsol ba drag tu btab/ de nas gzugs gang snang ba thams cad la 'di nga'i bla ma dam pa yin snyam du bsam/ khyad par chags yul gyi gzugs sdug pa/ zhe sdang gi yul gyi mi sdug pa sogs bla mar mos pa'i dran pa ye (189) ma nyams pa bya'o/ / de nas nga'i bla ma 'dis/ nga 'di ltar 'khor ba las bsgral nas thar pa bla na med pa la bkod pa drin che snyam du bsams la/ phyag mchod sogs yan lag bdun pa bya'o/ / de nas cir snang thams cad bla mar thag bcad/ bla ma rang sems su thag bcad/ rang sems spros bral du thag bcad la/ snang stong zung 'jug tu nyams su blang zhing / de'i ngang nas bsdo ba smon lam rnam dag gdab par bya'o/ /

Then meditate on the preliminaries, including going for refuge, arousing the awakening mind, contemplating death and impermanence, and so on. With yourself visualized clearly as the yidam, meditate on your root guru with a brilliant smile and radiant form, sitting on a lotus-moon seat above your head. Imagine, with yourself in the lead, all sentient beings earnestly supplicate: Precious guru, I pray to you! Bless me to relinquish fixation on the self. Bless me with the feeling of contentment in my being. Bless me to refine Illusory Body and Dream. Bless me to actualize Lucid Clarity Mahāmudrā. Whatever forms appear, think, “These are all my holy guru.” In particular, whether they are beautiful forms that inspire attachment or unattractive forms that inspire aversion, and so on—never forget your conviction that they are the guru. {189} Then think, “This is how the guru will liberate me from cyclic existence and establish me in the state of awakening. How kind!” Do prostrations, offerings, and all the seven branches of service. Then be absolutely certain that whatever appears is the guru. Be certain that the guru is your own mind. Be certain that your mind is free of embellishment. Take into practice the unity of appearance and emptiness, and within that state, make pure prayers of dedication and aspiration.
gnyis pa snang ba la brten nas yi dam lam du khyer ba ni/
II. Integration of the Yidam Based on Appearances

rang gi mdun du pad+ma 'dab ma bzhi pa'i lte ba dang 'dab ma rnams kyi steng du zla ba'i dkyil 'khor/ de'i dbus su 'khor lo sdom pa sku mdog dkar la sngo ba'i mdangs chags pa/ zhal gcig phyag gnyis pa rdo rje dang dril bu 'dzin pas yum la 'khyud pa/ rus pa dang rin po ches brgyan pa/ de'i pang na yum rdo rje phag mo sku mdog dmar mo gri gug dang thod pa 'dzin pas yab la 'khyud pa/ shar gyi 'dab ma la mkha' 'gro ma dkar mo/ byang du lA ma ljang gu/ nub tu khaN+Da ro he dmar mo/ lhor gzugs can ma ser mo rnams g.yas gri gug phyar zhing g.yon thod khrag thugs kar 'dzin pa/ gru mo na kha T+wAM ga /zhabs g.yas brkyangs pas ro'i gdan mnan cing / g.yon pa bskum pas skyil grung phyed pa'i gar stabs kyis bzhugs pa/ thams cad kyang rus pa dang rin po ches brgyan pa/ me ri 'bar ba'i dbus na bzhugs pa'o/ / de nas gong bzhin ye shes pa gzhug / dbang bskur bas rigs lngas dbu brgyan par bsams la/

Moon mandalas appear on the center and petals of the four-petaled lotus before you. Cakrasaṃvara is in the middle, white with a blue radiance, with one face and two hands holding vajra and bell while embracing his partner, and adorned by bones and jewels. On his lap, red Vajravārāhī holds a flaying knife and skull cup while embracing her partner. White Ḍākinī is on the eastern petal, green Lāmā in the north, red Khaṇḍarohā in the west, and yellow Rūpiṇī in the south. They all brandish flaying knives with their right hands and hold blood-filled skull cups to their hearts with their left hands, with khaṭvāṅgas in the crooks of their elbows. They stand with their right legs extended, pressing down on the corpse that is their seat, and their left legs partially bent in dancing posture. All of them are adorned by bones and precious jewels, and stand amid blazing fire. Then, as before, the awareness beings enter them. Imagine that after they receive empowerment they become crowned by the five families.
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyis bdag la mngon par dbang bskur du gsol/ /
All tathāgatas, please confer the actual empowerment on me. {190}

zhes gsol ba btab pas/ (190) gong ltar gtso ba'i gnas gsum las yi ge 'bru gsum byung / rang gi gnas gsum du thim/ dbang gsum thob/ lus ngag yid gsum so so'i sgrib pa dag / lam bskyed rim rdzogs rim bskyed rdzogs zung 'jug bsgom pa la dbang / 'bras bu sku gsum mngon du byas par bsam mo/ / de nas 'khor gyi lha mo bzhi gtso bo yab yum la thim/ de 'od du khra spung song ste rang la thim pas dbang bzhi pa thob/ sgrib pa thams cad dag par bsam mo/ / de nas rang yang 'khor lo sdom pa yab yum/ gzugs su snang ba thams cad kyang 'khor lo sdom pa yab yum snang la rang bzhin med pa shin tu gsal bar bsgoms la/ de la mchod pa 'bul/ de nas rang gis yi dam gyi snying po yi ge bdun pa bzlas pas/ gzugs su snang ba yi dam gyi lhar gsal bas kyang sngags de ri ri bgrang bar bsgoms nas/ sgra grags tshad sngags su shes par bya'o/ / de ltar lha dang sngags su snang ba thams cad kyang rang gi sems su thag bcad/ rang sems spros bral du thag bcad la bsgom/ rjes bsngo ba bya'o/ /

With that supplication, the three seed syllables arise as before from the three places of the principal figures. They dissolve into your three places. You receive the three empowerments. The respective obscurations of body, speech, and mind are purified. On the path, you are now empowered to meditate on creation phase, completion phase, and the unity of creation and completion. The result will be the actualization of the three kāyas. Then the four goddesses dissolve into the principal couple. They in turn become a colored mass of light that dissolves into you, bestowing the fourth empowerment. Think that all your obscurations are purified. Meditate with heightened clarity on yourself and all apparent forms as the Cakrasaṃvara couple—appearance without intrinsic nature. Present offerings to them. Then recite the yidam’s seven-syllable essence mantra. With all apparent form visualized as the yidam, meditate on the audible sound of the mantra and know that all sound is mantra. In this way, decide for sure that all appearance of deity and mantra is your own mind and that your own mind is free of embellishment. Meditate on that. Afterward, do the dedication.

thun gcig la nyams su len na/ spyi bor bla ma bsgoms la gsol ba gdab/ rang gi lus dang snang ba thams cad yi dam/ sgra grags pa thams cad sngags grags stong / rtog pa thams cad sgyu ma rmi lam du thag bcad la bsgom/ mdor na spyi gtsug bla ma dang mi 'bral/ rang lus yi dam dang mi 'bral/ ngag gsol 'debs sam sngags bzlas pa dang mi 'bral/ bza' btung bdud rtsi dang mi 'bral/ dran rtog thams cad sgyu ma rmi lam dang mi 'bral/ mdun du bka' srung chos skyong dang mi 'bral bar nyams su blang bar bya'o/ / 'di ni mdo rgyud rnams kyi snying po/ mkha' 'gro'i srog snying lta (191) bu yin pas/ the tshom ma byed par nyams su longs shig / lo zla tsam gyis 'tshang rgya bar nges pa'i man ngag go /

If this is to be practiced in a single session, meditate on the guru above your head and supplicate. Cultivate decisive certainty that your body and all appearance is the yidam, that all sound is the empty resonance of mantra, and that all thought is illusion and dream. In short, never be apart from the guru on your head, your body as the yidam, and your speech as supplication or mantra recitation. Never separate from [the knowledge that] all food and drink is elixir, that all thought and memory is illusion and dream, and that the command guards and dharma protectors go before you. Practice in that way. This is the heart of the sutras and tantras. {191} Since it is like the ḍākinīs’ vital heart, practice it without hesitation. It is the esoteric instruction that definitely produces awakening in a matter of months or years.
gsum pa snang ba la brten nas sgyu ma lam du khyer ba ni/
III. Integration of Illusion Based on Appearances

snang ba thams cad sems su thag bcad/ sems sgyu ma rmi lam du thag bcad nas nyin par sgyu lus dang / mtshan mo rmi lam gyi sbyong spel sprul bsgyur sogs chos drug tu bstan pa bzhin nyams su blang bar bya'o/ / mdor na snang ba lam khyer ni/ mig gi yul du gzugs mdzes mi mdzes/ rna ba'i yul du sgra snyan mi snyan/ sna'i yul du dri zhim mi zhim/ lce'i yul du ro mngar mi mngar/ lus kyi yul du reg bya 'jam mi 'jam/ yid kyi yul du chos yid 'ong mi 'ong ci byung yang / de'i ngo bo la ce re bltas la/ snang ba ma 'gags/ 'dzin pa ma zhugs par gsal stong 'dzin med kyi ngang la ma yengs par bzhag go / de lta bu'i chos gsum po de nyams su blangs pas/ bla ma la mos gus thun mong ma yin pa skye ba dang / sgyu ma rang shar gyis snang ba thams cad bden med du bun 'gro ba dang / rmi lam rang zin gyis sbyong spel sprul bsgyur yul snang gtan la phebs pa dang / nyin par phyag rgya chen po gsal la rtog med du 'char ba dang / mtshan mo lha sku rang shar dang / 'od gsal phyogs med du 'char ba rnams ji lta ba bzhin du 'byung bas/ the tshom med par nyams su longs shig ang / /

Decide for certain that all appearance is the mind and that mind is illusion and dream. Then put into practice the refining, increasing, emanating, and changing of nighttime dreams as presented in the Six Dharmas. In short, the Integration of Appearances on the Path [applies to] visual objects whether beautiful or not, auditory objects whether pleasant or not, olfactory objects whether fragrant or not, gustatory objects whether delicious or not, tactile objects whether soft or not, and mental objects whether pleasant phenomena or not. Look directly at the essence [of those perceptions] and don’t block their appearance, but don’t become fixated. Rest without distraction in the state of empty clarity without fixation. The practice of those three teachings will produce the following results. Uncommon devotion in the guru will be born. All appearances will fade away through the natural arising of illusion. The self-recognition of dreams will lead to refining, increasing, emanating, and changing them, and the ascertaining of appearances. In the daytime, the nonconceptual clarity of mahāmudrā will dawn. In the nighttime, the deity’s form will appear by itself and unlimited lucid clarity will arise. These experiences will occur just as they were described, so have no doubts and put them into practice.
[Colophon]

nying khu'i yan lag las 'phyugs med bla ma lam du khyer ba/ yi dam lam du khyer ba/ snang ba lam du khyer ba'i man ngag 'di yang lung stong smyon pas rang gi myong ba dang sbyar nas/ gnas mchog ri bo cher sbyar ba'i yi ge pa ni bka' bcu blo gros (192) rgyal mtshan yin/ 'di rnams ni bsgoms pa'i dmigs rim tsam zhig gtso bor byas nas shin tu bsdus pa yin kyang / 'di kho nas don 'grub pa yod do/ / bsgoms pas shes so/ / bshad pa byed 'dod na rdo rje'i tshig rkang gi steng du bla ma gong ma'i yig cha bkod pa las rtogs dgos// //

These esoteric instructions on the infallible Integration of the Guru, Integration of the Yidam, and Integration of Appearances from the quintessential auxiliary practices was composed at the sublime sacred site of Riwoche by the Madman of the Empty Valley in conjunction with his own experiences. The scribe was Lodrö Gyaltsen, holder of the ten precepts. {192} These [compositions] describe mainly just the visualization sequences of the meditations and so are very concise. However, just this will accomplish your purpose; meditate and you will understand. If you wish to offer an explanation, you must realize the teachings through the textbooks by past masters who commented upon the Vajra Verses.
@#/ /ni gu'i yan lag lus sems 'chi med kyi khrid bzhugs so// /
7. Niguma’s Auxiliary Practice, Guidance in Immortal Body and Mind[1]
na mo gu ru/ /
namo guru

'dir nying khu'i yan lag lus sems 'chi med man ngag gis kha bskangs te nyams su len pa la 'phrul 'khor sum cu rtsa gnyis kyis rtsa thig rlung gsum sbyangs nas/ gdan bde ba la lus gnad tsog pu skyil krung gang bde byas la/ skyabs 'gro sems bskyed bla ma'i rnal 'byor rnams sngon du btang nas/

Here is appended the esoteric instructions of the quintessential auxiliary practice, Immortal Body and Mind. To practice this, refine the vital channels, drops, and winds with the thirty-two physical yogic exercises.[2] Then take a comfortable seat and assume the vital points of the body posture—either sitting with the legs drawn up or cross-legged. First go for refuge, arouse the awakening mind, and practice the guru yoga.

'di ltar bsam par bya ste/ 'chi zhes pa 'di lus 'chi'am sems 'chi/ lus 'chi'o snyam na rnam smin gyi lus 'chi'am bag chags kyi lus 'chi/ dang po ltar yang min te/ lus 'di sha khrag rus pa pags pa sogs tshogs pa'i bem po kho na yin pas de la 'chi ba ga la yod/ yod na sa rdo sogs kyang ci'i phyir mi 'chi/ bag chags kyi lus kyang mi 'chi ste/ 'chi na rmi lam du 'chi bas 'chi ba'i go chod dgos/ de ltar na rmi lam du shi ba rmis pa'i gang zag de dag gnyid mi sad dgos te/ shi zin sos su med pa'i phyir snyam du bsam zhing / mdor na sngon gyi las kyi 'phen pa zad nas rnam smin gyi lus 'di la sems ma gnas pa tsam la 'chi ba zhes btags pa yin gyis 'chi ba zhes pa don la ma grub bo zhes bsam zhing / lus 'chi med du nam gtan la pheb pheb bsgom par bya'o/ /

Then contemplate in this manner: Regarding so-called death—is it the body that dies or the mind that dies? If you think it’s the body, then is it the fully ripened body that dies or the body of habitual patterns? It is not the first because this body is merely inert matter consisting of a bunch of flesh, blood, bones, skin, and so forth. How can that die? If it can, then why don’t earth and stones and so on die? The body of habitual patterns also does not die. If it could die, then dreaming of death would effectively cause death. Thus people who dream of dying in a dream would never wake up because once dead, they would not revive. Think about that. In short, death is a designation for nothing other than the mere fact that the mind no longer dwells in the fully ripened body once the propensity of one’s previous karma runs out. Therefore, so-called death has no true existence. Keep meditating until you ascertain for sure that the body is deathless.

sems 'di 'chi'o snyam na/ de la sems 'chi med rang (193) grol zhes bya ba'i gdams pa khyad par can 'di nyams su len pa la/ skyabs 'gro sems bskyed sngon du btang nas/ rang skad cig gis pad+ma nyi ma/ 'jigs byed dus mtshan ma'i steng du 'khor lo sdom pa sku mdog sngon po zhabs g.yas brkyangs pas dus mtshan mo'i lto ba mnan pa g.yon bskums pas 'jigs byed nag po'i mgo bo bltabs nas mnan pa/ zhal gcig phyag gnyis pa spyan gsum dang ldan zhing zhal 'gyur zhing mche ba gtsigs pa/ ral pa'i thor cog spyi bor bcings pa'i rtse mor rin po che/ g.yon na tshes gcig gi zla ba/ 'tshogs ma'i steng na sna tshogs rdo rje/ phyag gnyis kyis rdor dril 'dzin pas yum la 'khyud pa/ mi mgo skam po lnga'i dbu rgyan/ rlon pa lnga bcu'i do shal/ rus pa'i rgyan drug dang ldan pa/ stag gi pags pa'i sham thabs grol ba gar dgu'i nyams dang ldan pa/ de'i pang na yum rdo rje phag mo dmar mo g.yas gri gug gis gdug pa can sdigs shing / g.yon thod khrag 'dzin pas yab la 'khyud pa/ gcer bu spyan gsum skra grol ba/ sku sha rgyas shing nu ma 'bur ba/ thod skam gyi dbu rgyan dang do shal can/ rus rgyan lnga ldan zhabs g.yon brkyang zhing g.yas bskums pas yab la 'khril ba/ gnyis ka'ang ye shes kyi me 'bar ba'i dbus na bzhugs pa zhig gsal bar bsgom/ de'i spyi bor bla ma bsgoms la gsol ba gdab po/ /

If you think it is the mind that dies, then counter that with the practice of this special instruction called Natural Liberation of One’s Mind as Immortal.[3] {193} First go for refuge and arouse the mind of awakening. Then instantly imagine yourself as blue Cakrasaṃvara standing on a lotus, sun, Bhairava, and Kālarātri, with right leg extended stomping on Kālarātri’s belly and left leg bent, pressing and bending black Bhairava’s head. With one face, two arms, and three eyes, Cakrasaṃvara grimaces and bares his teeth. A jewel is on the tip of the bound topknot of hair on top of his head, with a new-moon crescent on the left and a crossed vajra on the front. His two hands hold vajra and bell while embracing Vajravārāhī. He wears a crown of five dry human heads, a necklace of fifty fresh wet heads, and six bone ornaments. With his tiger-skin skirt loose, he displays the nine dance poses. In his lap, the red mother Vajravārāhī threatens wicked beings with the flaying knife in her right hand and embraces her partner with the left while holding a blood-filled skull cup. She is naked with three eyes and loosed hair. She is voluptuous with full breasts. She is adorned by the crown of five dry skulls, necklace, and five bone ornaments, her left leg outstretched and right leg wrapped around Cakrasaṃvara. Both of them stand in the midst of a blazing fire of timeless awareness. Meditate clearly on that and supplicate the guru above your head.
de nas nyams len la 'jug pa la gsum ste/ /
There are three parts to engage the practice.
I.
I. Preliminaries

dang po sngon 'gro ni yab kyi spyi bo'i skra mtshams su lha sku shin tu gsal ba de'ang mog mog por byed pa'i hU~M sngon po 'od zer sngon po 'phro ba zhig bsam/ / de nas hU~M las 'od byung bas (194) smin mtshams gsal sing song / de nas shangs yan/ spyan rtsa tshun gsal ba'i spyan gsum hrig hrig pa/ de nas rim bzhin mgrin pa/ thugs ka /lte ba/ gsang gnas kyi sbyor mtshams yan chad/ de nas pus mo long bu sen mo yan chod gsal sing ba byung byung bar bsgom/ yab kyi phyi sbyong ba'o/ / de nas yang hU~M las 'od zer sngon po byung / tshangs bug nas mar song bas shangs dang mgrin pa yan chad sngo sang song / de nas thugs ka /lte ba/ gsang gnas/ pus mo/ long bu/ sor mo'i nang yan chad sngo sing nge ba 'od kyi rang bzhin du bsgom/ yab kyi nang sbyong pa'o/ / de bzhin du yum gyi spyi bo'i steng gi skra mtshams su baM dmar po 'od zer dmar po 'phro ba zhig bsam/ de las 'od zer dmar po byung nas gong bzhin yum gyi phyi nang gnyis su sbyangs/ khyad par b+ha ga dang / nu ma dmar sing nge ba bsgom pa ni kha dog gsal 'debs pa'o/ /

First, for the preliminaries, imagine a blue hūṃ at Cakrasaṃvara’s hairline emanating blue light so bright that it obscures even the extremely clear form of the deity. {194} The light that emerges from the hūṃ illuminates from the point between the eyebrows up. Then it extends down to the nose, including the eyeballs, illuminating the three staring eyes. Then the light gradually continues down to the throat, heart, navel, and perineum, illuminating everything from there up. Finally it moves to the knees, calves, and toenails—meditate until all of it arises in limpid lucidity. That constitutes the outer refinement of the father deity. Then again blue light emerges from the hūṃ. It descends through the cranial aperture to the nose and then the throat, turning everything above them clear blue. Then it continues down to the heart, navel, perineum, knees, calves, and toes—meditate on everything above that as being the nature of a limpid blue radiance. That is the inner refinement of the father. Similarly, imagine a red vaṃ at the hairline of the mother deity’s head radiating red light rays. Red light refines the mother both outwardly and inwardly as before. Meditate particularly on the red radiance of her bhaga and breasts—this is the visualization of color.

de nas yab kyi spyan dbus ma nas rim bzhin gsal 'debs/ ral pa'i thor cog / rdor dril 'dzin lugs/ zhal mche ba bzhi gtsigs pa/ zhabs kyi 'chag stabs/ sgeg pa/ me phung la sogs pa re re nas gsal 'debs pa ni dbyibs bsgom pa'o/ / de bzhin du yum la yang dbyibs re re nas bsgom/

Then visualize sequentially [starting with] the father’s third eye: the topknot of hair, the way of holding the vajra and bell, the face with four canine teeth bared, the manner of standing, the grace, the bonfire, and so on, visualizing each one clearly. This is the meditation on shape. Meditate in the same way on each shape of the mother.

de nas yab kyi spyi bo'i nor bu/ zla phyed/ sna tshogs rdo rje/ 'khor lo/ rna cha/ mgul rgyan/ gdu bu/ ska rags/ thal chen te rus pa'i rgyan drug / mi mgo skam rlon gyi dbu rgyan dang do shal/ yum la'ang thal chen ma gtogs rus rgyan lnga/ mgo skam gyi dbu rgyan dang do shal sogs rim bzhin bsgom pa ni rgyan gsal 'debs pa'o/ /

Then [meditate on] Cakrasaṃvara’s crown jewel, crescent moon, crossed vajra, and the six bone ornaments—wheel, earrings, necklace, bracelets and anklets, belt, and smeared human ashes—and the crown of dry human heads and the long garland. Also, meditate on Vajravārāhī’s five bone ornaments (minus the ashes), and the crown of dry heads, long garland, and so forth, meditating on each of them by turn. This is the visualization of ornaments.

de lta bu'i yab yum gnyis ka'ang gsal stong (195) bde chen zung 'jug rang bzhin gyis 'od gsal ba zhig bsgom/ de yang gsal ba'i ngos nas ma 'dres la yongs su rdzogs pa/ stong pa'i ngos nas rang bzhin gang du'ang ma grub pa'i 'od kyi rang bzhin du bsams la/ 'di lta bu 'di rang gi sems nyid lha skur snang ba ma gtogs/ de las logs su phyi rol gyi don du bden par ma grub par thag chod chod bsgom/ dpe rmi lam dang chu zla bzhin/ de yang rmi lam du yul sna tshogs zhig rmis kyang / yul gyis tshur 'ong ba yang med/ rang sems kyis phar phyin pa yang med/ sems gnyid kyis bslad pa'i dbang gis sems nyid sna tshogs su snang ba yin gyis de las logs su bden par grub pa med de/ dpe chu nang gi zla ba las shes so/ /

Meditate in this way on the two, father and mother, as the union of empty clarity and great bliss—natural lucid clarity. {195} From the perspective of clarity, their [features] are unmixed and totally complete. From the perspective of emptiness, there is no established intrinsic nature whatsoever, only the nature of light. Contemplate that and think, in the same way, this very mind of mine appears in the form of a deity, but apart from that there is no valid existence in the external sense. Meditate until you are sure. The metaphors are dreams and water moons. Although you dream of various objects in a dream, the objects have not actually come into the dream, nor has your mind gone over there to [those objects]. Sleep distorts the mind such that the mind itself appears in myriad forms. Other than that, there is nothing truly existing. You should understand this by the metaphor of the moon reflected in water.
