de bzhin du rang sems 'od gsal lha sku shin tu gsal ba de gang nas byon/ gang du bzhud/ gang na gnas brtags pas gang nas kyang ma byon/ gang du'ang mi bzhud/ gar yang mi gnas par gsal stong zung 'jug spros pa'i mtha' dang bral bar thag bcad/ de 'dra'i rang sems lha sku dang dbyer med 'di sangs rgyas 'das pa rnams kyis kyang ma gzigs/ ma byon pa rnams kyis kyang gzigs par mi 'gyur/ da lta ba rnams kyis kyang ma gzigs so snyam du bsgom mo/ /

Similarly, examine your own mind that appears vividly as the deity’s body. Where does it come from? Where does it go? Where does it stay? Resolve that it does not come from anywhere, nor does it go anywhere, nor does it stay anywhere; it is the unity of clarity and emptiness free of the extremes of embellishment. Such a mind inseparable from the deity’s form has not been seen by all the past buddhas, nor will it be seen by all those to come, nor is it seen by them now. Contemplate that and meditate.
gnyis pa dngos gzhi ni/
II. Main Practice
sems gsal stong rang bzhin ma grub pa 'di 'chi med du bsgom pa la/ 'chi med kyi dmigs pa la bzhi las/ /
In the meditation on immortality of the mind, which is clarity-emptiness with no real intrinsic nature, there are four visualizations of deathlessness.

dang po ni/ de ltar dus gsum sangs rgyas kyis ma gzigs pa'i rang sems gsal stong de la na ba ma grub ste/ na bar snang ba de rang sems las nyon blo bur ba des bslad pa'i snang ba yin gyis/ don dam la na ba'i rgyu med/ (196) de med pas 'bras bu na ba yang med do snyam du/ sems na med du rtogs rtogs bsgom mo/ /

A. Sickness does not exist in that mind of clarity-emptiness that even the buddhas of the three times have not seen. The appearance of sickness is the appearance of contamination of your mind by karma and incidental afflictions. {196} Ultimately there is no cause for sickness. Without a cause, there can be no resulting sickness. Contemplate that and meditate until you realize that mind has no sickness.

gnyis pa ni/ de 'dra ba'i sems de la 'chi ba ma grub ste/ 'chi ba zhes pa lus bem po 'di dang / rnam rtog glo bur ba de bral bar snang ba de la btags pa tsam yin gyis/ brtags shing dpyad na 'pho bya 'pho byed dang bral ba gang du'ang mi bden pa'i stong nyid du nam thag ma chod bar du bsgom mo/ /

B. In such a mind, death does not exist. So-called death is just a designation for the apparent separation of this inert body and incidental discursive thought. If you really investigate it, there is no passing on and no thing that passes on. Meditate until such time as you are certain of the emptiness of no valid existence whatsoever.

gsum pa ni/ de 'dra ba'i sems de la sangs rgyas rgyu 'dug gam mi 'dug bltas pas sangs rgya rgyu med de/ sems can gyi dus dang sangs rgyas pa'i dus kyi sems kyi rang bzhin gnyis 'od gsal stong nyid du dbyer med do/ / sems kyi rang bzhin rnam dag de glo bur dri ma thams cad dang bral ba de la sangs rgyas zhes ming btags pa tsam yin no snyam du bsgom mo/ /

C. In such a mind as that, observe whether or not there is the cause of buddhahood. There is no cause of buddhahood. The nature of mind at the time of being a buddha and at the time of being a sentient being are both lucid clarity and emptiness inseparable. The term buddha is merely a designation for that totally pure nature of mind that is free of all incidental blemishes. Contemplate that and meditate.

bzhi pa ni/ de 'dra ba'i lha sku rang sems gsal stong de'i rang bzhin la bsams na 'khor ba ma grub ste/ 'khor ba bden par ma grub pas/ 'khor bar 'khor mkhan ma grub snyam du 'khor ba rang sems 'khrul pa'i snang bar thag nam chod chod bsgom mo/ /

D. When you think that way about the empty clear nature of your mind as the deity’s form, then cyclic existence does not exist. Since samsara has no valid existence, those who cycle in cyclic existence also do not exist. Contemplate that and meditate until you are absolutely certain that cyclic existence is the deluded appearance of your own mind.
gsum pa rjes ni/
III. Conclusion

de ltar rang sems 'chi med du thag bcad de nges shes bskyed la yengs med du bsgom/ bla ma la gsol ba gdab pa/ sems can la snying rje bsgom pa/ dge ba sems can thams cad kyi don du rdzogs byang du bsngo bas bogs 'don na mtshams med pa lnga byas pa yang 'chi ba'am bar dor 'tshang rgya na sgrib pa chung zhing skal pa dang ldan pa ni rgyun du sgom pa lta zhog / 'chi khar sku yongs rdzogs sam cha shas tsam gsal bas kyang sgyogs kyi 'khrul 'khor ram/ dwangs pa'i rdzing bur rdo brgyab pa'am/ tshes bco lnga'i nyi ma rgas (197) pa dang zla ba 'char ba dus mnyam pa bzhin du bar dor rgyal pa longs skur sangs rgyas te/ chos sku las ma g.yos par gzugs sku gnyis kyis gang la gang 'dul gyis sems can gyi don lhun grub rgyun chad med par byed do/ /

Meditate without distraction to produce certitude, becoming absolutely resolved that your mind is deathless as described. If this is enhanced with supplicating the guru, meditating on compassion for sentient beings, and dedicating the merit for all beings to attain perfect awakening, then even those who have committed the five acts of immediate retribution will be enlightened at death or in the intermediate state, let alone fortunate ones with few obscurations who meditate constantly. If the form [of the deity] arises completely or even partially at death, then like the mechanism of a cannon or a stone thrown into a still pond or the fifteenth day when the full moon arises as the sun sets, you will attain awakening as the victors’ saṃbhogakāya. {197} Without ever leaving dharmakāya, the two form kāyas continuously and spontaneously enact the welfare of beings by doing whatever it takes to tame them.

de lta bu'i gdams ngag med par lam sgrub pa'i rtsol ba cher byas kyang / chu bsrubs kyang mar mi 'byung ba bzhin du ngal ba don med yin cing / 'di 'dra ba'i gdams pa dang ldan zhing nyams su len pa de ni mdo rgyud thams cad kyi bcud phyungs nas btung pas las nyon 'khrul pa'i gcong nad bsal nas mkha' spyod du 'gro nges pa'i gdams pa yin pas nyams su len dgos so/ / 'di bas zab pa'i man ngag rgya bod gnyis na med pa yin no/ / pho grung mo grung brtson 'grus can tshe gcig la 'tshang rgya ba'i chos lags so/ / 'di dag gi rigs pas/ lus bem po 'di dang / / sems gsal stong gnyis ka 'khor ba nas sangs rgyas su 'chugs mi 'chugs/ sangs rgyas nas 'khor ba ngan 'gro nas bde 'gro sogs su 'chugs mi 'chugs pa ltas la/ lus dang sems 'chugs med du thag chod chod du bsgom mo/ /

Without such instructions as these, exerting great effort in practice will just result in meaningless exhaustion, like churning water to produce butter. But to have such instructions and put them into practice is to extract the vitality of all the sutras and tantras and drink it, curing the chronic disease of delusional karma and affliction. Then you will certainly go to the celestial realm. You need to practice with such instructions. There are no esoteric instructions more profound than these in all of India and Tibet. Indeed, it is a teaching by which intelligent men and women with diligence will awaken in a single lifetime. With the logic of these [instructions], observe whether both this corporeal body and this clear empty mind fall from cyclic existence to buddhahood or not, and whether or not they fall from buddhahood to bad migrations in cyclic existence and to happy existences, and so forth. Meditate until you become absolutely certain that body and mind are infallible.
[Colophon]

snying rus can tshe gcig la 'tshang rgya ba'i chos nyid khu'i yan lag gi chos skor las 'chi med dang 'chugs med kyi dmigs rim gsal ba 'di yang / lung stong smyon pas mkha' 'gro'i gsung bzhin nyams su myong bar byas nas/ gnas mchog ri bo cher stag lo zla ba drug pa'i tshes brgyad nas bdun pa'i bco lnga'i bar la nying khu'i lus yan lag dang bcas pa tshang bar sbyar ba'i yi ge pa ni bka' bcu pa blo gros rgyal mtshan yin/

This concludes the clarification of the visualization sequence of Immortal and Infallible from the cycle of quintessential auxiliary practices through which ardent practitioners will be enlightened in a single lifetime. I, the Madman of the Empty Valley, brought them into my experience according to the ḍākinīs’ teachings. The whole composition of the main and auxiliary quintessential instructions was written between the eighth day of the sixth month and the fifteenth day of the seventh month in the year of the Tiger at the sacred site of Riwoche. The scribe was Lodrö Gyaltsen, holder of the ten precepts.
dam chos 'di tshul bzhin nyams su len pa la (198) tshe 'di'i 'khri ba bcad pas don chen 'grub pa'i gtan gyi chus legs 'gro bar 'dug pas/ thams cad rtsol ba bskyed la rems/ / dge'o// /

To properly practice this Holy Dharma, cut the ties to this life. {198} Then will it become your ultimate strategy for accomplishing life’s great meaning. Everyone, exert yourselves vigorously with diligence!
nying khu'i yan lag phyag drug ye shes mgon po'i khrid bzhugs so// /
8. Niguma’s Auxiliary Quintessential Practice, Guidance in the Six-Armed Awareness Protector[1]
bla ma mgon po dbyer med la na mo/ / myur mdzad spyan ras gzigs la phyag 'tshal lo/
Homage to Guru-Protector inseparable. Homage to Swift-Acting Avalokiteśvara.

'dir nying khu'i yan lag tu bla ma khyung po lo paN gyis sbyar ba'i bla ma mgon po dbyer med kyi nyams len la/ mgon po 'di'i byin rlabs thob pa'i rnal 'byor pas gnas dben par skyabs 'gro sems bskyed sngon du btang nas/ rang gi spyi bor paM las sna tshogs pad+ma 'dab ma brgyad pa'i lte bar a las zla ba'i dkyil 'khor gyi steng du hU~M las sna tshogs rdo rje'i lte par hU~M sna tshogs kyis mtshan pa/ de las 'od 'phros 'phags pa mchod/ sems can thams cad kyi sdig sgrib sbyangs/ tshur 'dus yongs su gyur pa las/ rdo rje sems dpa' sku mdog sna tshogs pa/ zhal gcig phyag gnyis pa/ g.yas sna tshogs rdo rje/ g.yon des yu ba byas pa'i dril bu 'dzin pas yum la 'khyud pa/ de'i pang na yum rdo rje snyems ma sku mdog sna tshogs pa/ zhal gcig phyag gnyis ma/ g.yas gri gug g.yon thod khrag 'dzin pas yab la 'khyud pa/ gnyis ka'ang rus pa dang rin po ches brgyan pa'i dpral bar oM dkar po/ mgrin par AHdmar po/ thugs kar hU~M sngon po/ lte bar hU~M sna tshogs/ de las 'od 'phros pas bla ma yi dam sangs rgyas thams cad rdo rje sems dpa'i rnam par spyan drangs/

Here, as an auxiliary quintessential practice, is added the practice of Guru-Protector Inseparable by Lama Khyungpo Lotsāwa-Paṇḍita. The yogin who is to obtain the blessings of this protector should, in a secluded place, first go for refuge and arouse the awakening mind. Then [visualize] an eight-petaled multicolored lotus that arises from paṃ above your head. In its center, a moon-disk mandala arises from A, and upon that a multicolored vajra cross from hūṃ marked with a multicolored hūṃ at its center. From that, radiating light rays make offerings to the noble ones and purify the negativities and obscurations of all sentient beings. They gather back and completely transform into multicolored Vajrasattva with one face and two arms. His right hand holds a multicolored vajra and his left hand holds a vajra-handled bell while embracing his partner, multicolored Mother Vajragarvā, who sits in his lap. She has one face and two arms and holds a flaying knife in her right hand and feeds the father with a blood-filled skull cup in her left hand. They are both adorned by bones and jewels. White oṃ is in their foreheads, red āḥ at their throats, blue hūṃ at their hearts, and multicolored hūṃ at their navels. Those letters radiate light that invokes all the gurus, yidams, and buddhas in the form of Vajrasattva.

dzaHhU~M baM hoH gnyis su med par thim/ bcom ldan 'das bdag (199) gis tshe 'khor ba thog ma med pa nas bsags pa'i sdig sgrib nyas ltung dri ma'i tshogs thams cad byang zhing dag par byin gyis brlab tu gsol/

jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ—they become indivisible [with the visualized form]. {199} Bhagavat, I pray to you to cleanse and purify all negative acts, obscurations, faults, downfalls, and stains that I have accumulated in lifetimes since beginningless cyclic existence.

ces gsol ba btab pas/ thugs ka'i hU~M las bdud rtsi kha dog lnga ldan byung / yab yum gnyis ka'i sku gang / de gnyis kyi sbyor mtshams nas bdud rtsi byung / spyi bo tshangs pa'i bu ga nas byon/ sdig sgrib thams cad dud khu'i rnam par 'og sgo dang rkang mthil gnyis nas thon par bsams nas ngag tu yi ge brgya pa bzla/ mjug tu

Through supplicating with that, five-colored elixir arises from the hūṃ in their hearts. It fills both the couple’s forms and flows from the places of their union. That enters through the cranial aperture at the top of your head. All negativities and obscurations in the form of liquid coal comes out from your lower orifices and two soles. Imagine that while repeating the one hundred syllables. At the end say:
bdag ni mi shes rmongs pa yis/ / zhes sogs brjod/
I, through the darkness of ignorance…(bdag ni mi shes rmongs pa yis…etc.).

rdo rje sems dpa' bdag la thim pas/ rang rdo rje sems dpa' sku mdog sna tshogs pa/ phyag g.yas sna tshogs rdo rje thugs kar gtod de 'dzin pa/ g.yon des yu ba byas pa'i dril bu dkur brten pa/ zhabs g.yas cung zad brkyangs shing g.yon bskums pa/ dar dang rin po ches brgyan pa zhig tu bsam/ de nas rang gi mdun gyi nam mkha'i gnas su paM las pad+ma/ raM las nyi ma'i gdan la/ gaM las tshogs bdag dkar po gan rkyal du 'gyel ba'i steng du hU~M dkar po zhig bsam/ de las 'od 'phros gdug pa can thams cad tshar bcad/ tshur 'dus pa las dpal ye shes kyi mgon po sku mdog dkar po zhal gcig phyag drug pa/ zhabs gnyis bzhengs thabs su bzhugs pa/ phyag g.yas kyi dang pos yid bzhin gyi nor bu'i gri gug / bar pas thod pa'i phreng ba/ tha mas DA ma ru drag tu 'khrol ba/ g.yon dang pos thod khrag / bar pas rtse gsum/ tha mas rdo rje'i zhags pa bsnams pa/ spyan gsum dmar la zlum pa/ zhal bsgrad pa/ mche ba gtsigs pa/

Vajrasattva dissolves into oneself. Imagine yourself as multicolored Vajrasattva, holding in the right hand a multicolored vajra at the heart and a vajra-handled bell at the hip with the left, with right leg slightly bent and left straight, adorned by silks and jewels. Then, in the space in front of you, a lotus arises from paṃ and a sun seat from raṃ. Upon that, from gaṃ, imagine white Gaṇapati fallen on his back, with a white hūṃ on top of him. Light radiates from that and annihilates all evil ones. Imagine that the light gathers back in and from it arises Glorious Awareness Protector, white with one face and six arms, his two legs in the standing position. In his first right hand he holds a wish-fulfilling jeweled flaying knife, in the middle a skull rosary, and the last fiercely rattles a ḍamaru. In his first left hand he holds a blood-filled skull cup, in the middle a trident, and in the last a vajra lasso. He has three round, red eyes, a gaping mouth, and bared fangs. {200}

smin ma dang sma ra'i (200) ag tshom brjid pa/ dbu skra dmar ser gyen du brdzes pa/ mi mgo skam po lngas dbu brgyan cing / rlon pa khrag 'dzag pa lnga bcu'i do shal can/ rus pa'i rgyan drug dang sbrul gyis brgyan pa/ stag gi pags pa'i sham thabs la/ dar ljang gu'i ske rags bcings pa/ lto ba 'phyang zhing yan lag rnams sbom la rags pa/ dpral bar sin d+hU ras byugs shing / phyag zhabs rnams la dril bu g.yer khas brgyan pa/ glang po che'i pags pa rlon pa gos su gyon pa/ sangs rgyas mi bskyod pa'i dbu rgyan can/ ye shes kyi me 'bar ba'i dbus na bzhugs par bsam/

His eyebrows and beard tufts are brilliant. His orange hair streams upward. He has a crown of five dry skulls, a garland of fifty blood-dripping wet heads, and is adorned by the six bone ornaments and snakes. He wears a tiger-skin skirt tied with a green silk belt. His belly protrudes and his limbs are thick and solid. His forehead is smeared with vermilion. Large and small bells decorate his arms and legs. He wears a wet elephant skin. Buddha Akṣobhya crowns his head. He stands amid the blazing fire of timeless awareness.[2]

de'i gnas gsum byin gyis brlabs/ ye shes pa dgug gzhug byas la/ de'i spyi bo'i steng gi mtho gang tsam gyi steng du pad+ma dang zla ba'i gdan la/ rtsa ba'i bla ma sku mdog dkar po zhal gcig phyag gnyis pa/ g.yas thod pa'i DA ma ru'am nor bu rin po che/ g.yon gser gyi dril bu g.yer kha bsnams pa/ zhabs gnyis bzhengs thabs su bzhugs pa/ dar dang rin po che'i rgyan sna tshogs kyis brgyan pa/ zhi zhing 'dzum pa'i nyams dang ldan pa/ sku mthong ba tsam gyis sgrib pa 'dag cing / gsung thos pa tsam gyis phyir mi ldog pa'i sa la 'god nges pa/ 'od zer dpag tu med pa 'phro ba zhig bsgom/ de'i thugs ka nas 'od zer 'phros pas/ rtsa brgyud kyi bla ma dang yi dam thams cad spyan drangs la bstim mo/ /

Perform the consecration of his three places and the invocation and indwelling of the awareness being. Then imagine that a finger span above his head is a lotus and sun seat, upon which is your root guru, white, with one face and two arms. The right hand holds either a skull ḍamaru or a precious gem, the left holds a golden bangle bell, and the two legs are in the standing posture. The guru is adorned by various decorations of silks and jewels, with a peaceful and smiling countenance. Meditate that just seeing the body of the guru purifies obscurations and just hearing the voice definitely establishes you in the stage of no-return. Light rays radiate from the heart and invoke all the root and lineage gurus and yidams, who dissolve into the guru.

bzlas pa byed 'dod na/ mgon po'i thugs ka'i hU~M las sngags kyi phreng ba dkar po byung / rang gi zhal du zhugs/ lte bar thim pas nad gdon sdig sgrib thams cad dag cing bsregs par bsam zhing / ngag tu/

If you wish to do the recitation, [imagine that] a white mantra string arises from the hūṃ in Protector’s heart, enters your mouth, and dissolves into your navel, purifying and incinerating all sickness, spirits, negativities, and obscurations, while reciting the mantras: {201}
oM badzra ma hA kA la k+ShiM k+She tra (201) bi g+h+nAn bi nA ya ka hU~M hU~M phaDa phaDa sA hA/ zhes dang /
oṃ vajra mahākāla kṣiṃ kṣetra vighnān vināyaka hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā
oM badzra na ra kriM kriM hU~M hU~M phraT phraT swA hA/ zhes pa
oṃ vajra nara kriṃ kriṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā

ci rigs pa bzla'o/ /ma bzlas kyang ma tshang ba'i nyes pa med do/ / mdor na bla ma mgon po dbyer med la dad gus drag po byas pas/ bla ma las 'od zer dpag tu med pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa byung nas mgon po la phog pas mgon po 'od kyi rang bzhin du 'bar/ DA ma ru'i sgra sgrog / bla ma dang mgon po dbyer med par bsam/ mgon po las 'od zer bde ba'i rang bzhin dmar la smug pa 'phros pas/ bla ma 'od dang bde pa'i rang bzhin du 'bar/ DA ma ru dang dril bu'i sgra sgrog / mgon po dang bla ma dbyer med du gyur par bsams la gsol ba gdab pa ni/

Repeat however much is suitable. However, if you do not recite the mantra, there is no fault of omission. In short, by your intense devotion and faith in the inseparable guru and protector, unimaginably immeasurable light rays arise from the guru and strike the protector, causing him to blaze with the nature of light. He rattles the ḍamaru. Think of the guru inseparable from the protector. Then from the protector dark-reddish light rays, the nature of bliss, radiate and cause the guru to blaze with the nature of bliss. Guru rattles the ḍamaru and bell. Think of the Protector inseparable from the guru, and recite the supplication.
na mo bud+d+hA ya/ na mo gu ru b+h+yaH he badzra wI ra wI ri nI DA ka DA ki nI dzo ka dzo ki nI sarba bud+d+hA bo d+hi sa twA ya sha ra NaM gats+tshA mi/
namo buddhāya / namo gurubhyaḥ / hevajra vīra vīreṇīyī ḍāka ḍākinī joka jokiṇī sarva buddha bodhisatvaya śvaraṇaṃ gacchāmi
kye kye phyogs bcu dus gsum na bzhugs pa'i rtsa ba dang brgyud par bcas pa'i dpal ldan bla ma dam pa rnams kyis byin gyis rlobs shig /
kye kye! Glorious holy gurus, root and lineage gurus who dwell in the ten directions and three times, please grant your blessings.
yi dam lha tshogs rnams kyis=
Host of yidam deities, please grant your blessings.
sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa'i tshogs thams cad kyis=
All assemblies of buddhas and bodhisattvas, please grant your blessings.
dpa' bo dang dpa' mo/ mkha' 'gro dang mkha' 'gro ma/ rnal 'byor dang rnal 'byor ma'i tshogs thams cad kyis=
All hosts of heroes and heroines, ḍākas and ḍākinīs, yogis and yoginīs, please grant your blessings.

dpal ye shes kyi mgon po phyag drug pa'i lha tshogs ye shes la sgrib pa mi mnga' ba/ mthu dang nus pa la thogs pa mi mnga' ba/ thugs rje la phyi bshol mi mnga' ba/ byin rlabs la rgyang ring thung mi mnga' ba/

Deity hosts of glorious Six-Armed Awareness Protector, do not obscure your timeless awareness. Do not restrict your power and ability. Do not delay your compassion. Do not calculate the distance of your blessings.
khyed rnams kyis sku'i sgo nas byin gyis rlobs shig / gsung gi sgo nas= thugs kyi sgo nas= sku gsung thugs yon tan phrin las dang bcas pa mi zad pa'i sgo nas=

All of you: grant your blessings through your bodies, grant your blessings through your speech, grant your blessings through your minds, and grant your blessings through inexhaustible awakened body, speech, mind, qualities, and activities.
da lta nyid du byin= myur ba nyid du= 'dug sa 'di (202) ru byin gyis=
Bless me right now. Bless me quickly. Bless me on this very seat. {202}
sangs rgyas rdo rje 'chang chen la gsol ba 'debs so/ / dpal ldan sha ba ri dbang phyug la= mnga' bdag mai tri pa chen po la= grub thob rA hu la chen po la=
I supplicate Great Buddha Vajradhara. I supplicate glorious Śavarī the Mighty. I supplicate Lord Maitrīpa the Great. I supplicate adept Rāhula the Great.
grub thob khyung po rnal 'byor la= mnyam med rin chen brtson 'grus la= dpal ldan skyer sgang pa chen po la= bla ma sangs rgyas gnyan ston la=
I supplicate adept Khyungpo Naljor. I supplicate incomparable Rinchen Tsöndru. I supplicate glorious Kyergangpa the Great. I supplicate Lama Sangye Nyentön.
chos rje sangs rgyas ston pa la= mkhas grub shangs ston chos rje la= mus chen rgyal mtshan dpal bzang la= mkhas grub rdo rje gzhon nu la=
I supplicate Chöje Sangye Tönpa. I supplicate Khedrup Shangtön Chöje. I supplicate Muchen Gyaltsen Palzang. I supplicate Khedrup Dorje Zhönu.
mtshungs med nam mkha'i rnal 'byor la= byang sems sbyin pa bzang po la= pha rgod thang stong rgyal po la= phyag drug ye shes mgon po la=
I supplicate unequaled Namkhai Naljor. I supplicate Bodhisattva Jinpa Zangpo. I supplicate wild father Tangtong Gyalpo. I supplicate Six-Armed Awareness Protector.
bla ma mgon po dbyer med la= mgon po bla ma dbyer med la=
I supplicate Guru-Protector Inseparable. I supplicate Protector-Guru Inseparable.
zhes sogs dang / bla ma mgon po dbyer med bdag la dbang bzhi rdzogs par bskur du gsol/
Continue with this and Guru-Protector inseparable, please confer on me the complete four empowerments.

zhes gsol ba mang du btab pas mgon po'i dpral ba nas oM dkar po byung / rang gi dpral bar thim/ lus kyi sgrib pa dag pa sogs spyi dang mthun/ mgrin pa nas AHdmar po zhig byung / rang gi mgrin par thim/ thugs ka nas hU~M sngon po zhig byung / rang gi thugs kar thim/ de nas bla ma mgon po la thim/ mgon po 'od du zhu nas rang la thim pas me long nang gi gzugs brnyan lta bu la sems mnyam par bzhag / lus ngag yid gsum gyi sgrib pa dag / dbang bzhi pa thob snyam du bsam mo/

Through supplicating many times, a white oṃ emerges from Protector’s forehead and dissolves into my forehead, purifying physical obscurations…(etc., as usual). A red āḥ emerges from his throat and dissolves into my throat…(etc.). A blue hūṃ emerges from his heart and dissolves into my heart…(etc.). Then the guru dissolves into the Protector. Protector melts into light and dissolves into me; as though facing a reflected image in a mirror, mind rests in equanimity. Think that physical, verbal, and mental obscurations are purified and that you have obtained the four empowerments.
de nas bla ma mgon po dbyer med la/ / bdag ni gus pas skyabs su mchi/ / bdag gis sems can thams cad kyi/ / nyon mongs ma lus sel bar shog / ces bsngo'o/ /
Then dedicate by saying: To the Guru-Protector inseparable I go for refuge with devotion. May I dispel every affliction of all sentient beings.

tshigs su bcad pa 'di mthong ngam thos sam tha na gser yig tu bris te mgul du btags na mtshams med pa lnga byas pas kyang 'chi khar zhal (203) mngon gsum du mthong bar 'gyur zhing dag pa sa gsum la gnas par 'gyur ro/ / bar dor 'jug dgos srid na'ang der rjes su 'dzin par nges so/ /

If you see or hear or even write this verse in gold lettering to wear around your neck, even if you have committed the five acts of immediate retribution, {203} you will actually see [Guru-Protector] in the intermediate state and come to dwell on the three pure levels. If you possibly must enter the intermediate state, [Guru-Protector] will definitely look after you there.

yang na mgon po gnag la dkar ba'i mdangs chags par bsgoms kyang rung ngo / / yang gong dang 'dra ba las/ mdun du pad nyi dang tshogs bdag gi steng du mgon po ser nag rgyan cha lugs bzhugs stangs gong dang 'dra ba'i spyi bor pad zla'i steng du rtsa ba'i bla ma sku mdog gser btso ma lta bu zhal gcig phyag gnyis pa/ phyag g.yas yid bzhin gyi nor bu dang / g.yon gser gyi dril bu g.yer kha 'dzin pa rgyan cha lugs gong dang 'dra bar bsgom/ sngar bzhin gsol ba btab pas/ bla ma mgon po la thim/ mgon po rang la thim pa'i ngang du 'jog / bsngo ba gong bzhin bya'o/ /

Additionally, it is also suitable to meditate on the Protector as black with a white radiance. That is the same as before, except for the following: Upon the lotus-sun-Gaṇapati seat in the space before you, golden-black Protector adorned with accessories is in standing posture. As previously, the root guru is on a lotus-moon seat above his head, this time with a body like molten gold, one face and two arms, and holding a wish-fulfilling gem in the right hand and a golden small bell in the left. Meditate on that with the decorations and accessories as before. Through supplicating as before, the guru dissolves into the protector, and the protector into oneself. Remain within that state. Do the dedication as before.

yang mdun tu gong dang 'dra ba'i gdan gyi steng du mgon po dmar nag gi spyi bor pad zla'i steng du rtsa ba'i bla ma sku mdog dmar po/ phyag g.yas DA ma ru dang g.yon nor bu rin po che 'dzin pa/ rgyan dang cha lugs gong dang 'dra bar bskyed/ sngar bzhin gsol ba gdab/ dbang zhu/ bsngo ba bya'o/ /

Again, dark-red Protector stands before you on a similar seat, with red root Guru on a lotus and sun above his head. Guru holds a ḍamaru in the right hand and a precious gem in the left, adorned as before with decorations and accessories. Supplicate as before, receive the empowerments, and dedicate.

yang mdun du gdan gong dang 'dra ba'i steng du mgon po ljang nag phyag mtshan sogs gong dang 'dra bar bsgom/ de'i spyi bor pad zla'i steng du rtsa ba'i bla ma sku mdog ljang gu phyag g.yas DA ma ru dang / g.yon bdud rtsis gang ba'i bum pa bsnams pa/ cha lugs gong dang 'dra bar bsgom/ sngar ltar gsol ba btab/ dbang zhu bsngo ba bya'o/ /

Again, meditate on dark-green Protector standing before you on a similar seat, the hand implements and so forth the same as before. Green root Guru upon a lotus and sun above his head holds a ḍamaru in the right hand and an elixir-filled vase in the left, adorned as before with decorations and accessories. Supplicate as before, receive the empowerments, and dedicate.

yang mdun du chos 'byung nag po'i nang du hU~M nag po mgo mthur du bstan pa zhig bsgom/ hU~M zhes brjod pas chos 'byung de pad+ma dang nyi ma tshogs bdag gi gdan du gyur/ hU~M mgo bo gyen du (204) log pas ye shes kyi mgon po sku mdog mthing nag rgyan cha lugs sogs gong dang 'dra ba zhig bsgom/ 'khor gnod sbyin bzhi dang lha mo gzhung bzhin bskyed/ ye shes pa gzhug pa sogs gong bzhin/ de'i spyi bor rtsa ba'i bla ma sku mdog mthing nag zhal gcig phyag gnyis khro bo'i cha lugs can me phung 'bar ba'i dbus na bzhugs pa/ g.yas DA ma ru dang g.yon yid bzhin nor bu rin po che dbang gi rgyal po bsnams pa/ rgyan cha lugs bzhugs tshul gong dang 'dra bar bsgom/ sngar bzhin gsol ba btab/ dbang zhu/ bsngo ba bya'o/ / bla ma sku mdog dkar por byas kyang rung ngo / /

Again, meditate on a black source of phenomena with a black upside-down hūṃ inside. By your uttering “hūṃ,” that source of phenomena becomes the seat of lotus, sun, and Gaṇapati. {204} Meditate that the hūṃ turns right side up [and becomes] blue-black Awareness Protector with the decorations and accessories as before. Visualize his retinue of harm-doers (yakṣas) and the goddess according to the source texts. Invoke the awareness beings and so forth as before. Above his head, your root guru is deep blue with one face, two arms, and wrathful accessories, sitting in the midst of a blazing bonfire. The right hand holds a ḍamaru and the left hand holds the mighty sovereign wish-fulfilling gem. Meditate that the decorations, accessories, and manner of sitting are the same as before. Supplicate, receive the empowerments, and dedicate as before. It is also suitable to make the guru white in color.

yang mdun gyi nam mkha'i gnas su pad nyi tshogs bdag gi gdan dang bcas pa'i steng du/ ye shes kyi mgon po sku mdog sna tshogs pa rgyan cha lugs phyag mtshan gong dang 'dra bar bsgom/ de'i spyi bor pad zla la rtsa ba'i bla ma sku mdog sna tshogs pa/ g.yas DA ma ru dang / g.yon nor bu dbang gi rgyal po bsnams pa/ zhi ma khro'i rnam pa can/ rgyan cha lugs gong dang 'dra bar bsgoms la sngar ltar gsol ba gdab/ dbang zhus nas snang la rang bzhin med par blo bzhag / rjes su bsngo ba rnam par dag pa bya'o/ /

Again, in the space in front of you, meditate on the lotus-sun-Gaṇapati seat, upon which is Awareness Protector of various colors, with the ornaments, accessories, and hand implements the same as before. Above his head, on a lotus and moon, your root guru is variously colored, holding a ḍamaru in the right hand and the mighty sovereign gem in the left, with a countenance both peaceful and wrathful. Meditate on the same ornaments and accessories and supplicate as before. Receive the empowerments, then rest your mind in the intrinsic nonexistence of appearances. Afterward, make the totally pure dedications.

de ltar ma yengs par zla ba bdun bsgoms na tshe 'di nyid du 'tshang rgya bar byed do/ / tho rangs thun re bsgoms na 'chi khar chos sku dang gzugs sku thob/ dbang dang 'brel ba lan gcig thob na mtshams med pa lnga byas pa yang bar dor ni 'tshang mi rgya ba mi srid do/ /

If you meditate in that way without distractions for seven months, that in itself will produce enlightenment. If you meditate for one session every daybreak, you will obtain the dharmakāya and rūpakāya at death. If even once you make a connection with the empowerment, even if you have committed the five acts of immediate retribution, it is impossible that you would not reach enlightenment in the intermediate state. In this vein,

'di dag ni sha ba ri pas/ / ye shes mgon po'i spyi gtsug tu/ / dbang gi rgyal po bsgoms byas nas/ / 'od zer gzi brjid ldan par bsam/ / g.yel ba med par gsol btab na/ / sangs rgyas lo zlas 'grub par 'gyur/ /

Śavarīpa stated: If you meditate on the mighty sovereign on the crown of Awareness Protector, imagine the brilliance of light rays, and supplicate without distraction, you will attain awakening in years or months.

bla ma mgon po dbyer med 'di/ / mi rabs bdun la ma (205) spel cig / ye shes mgon po mdun byon nas/ / bdag 'dra sha ba ri ba la/ / lan gsum bar du gsungs nas kyang / / bka' rgyas btab nas mkha' la gshegs/ /

For seven generations do not disseminate this Guru-Protector inseparable. {205} Awareness Protector came to such as me, Śavarīpa, spoke on three occasions and sealed this command, then went into the sky.
e ma ngo mtshar rmad kyi chos/ / chig brgyud dag las ma spel cig /
Ema!—this amazing, wonderful dharma— do not spread beyond a one-to-one transmission.[3]
zhes gsungs pa'i nyams len no/ /
Practice this teaching.

nying khu'i chos skor gyi yan lag bla ma mgon po dbyer med du sgrub pa'i man ngag 'di'ang lung stong smyon pas rang gi myong ba dang sbyar te gnas chen ri bo cher sbyar ba'i yi ge'i rkyen ni bka' bcu pa blo gros rgyal mtshan yin no/ / rjes gnang dang man ngag ma thob pa la mi bstan no/ / shin tu zab i thi/ / dge'o// // (206) (207)

This esoteric instruction on accomplishing Guru-Protector Inseparable in an auxiliary quintessential dharma cycle was done by the Madman of the Empty Valley by applying my own experience, at the great holy site of Riwoche. The scribe was Lodrö Gyaltsen, holder of the ten precepts. Do not teach it to those who have not obtained the subsequent permission and esoteric instructions. It is extremely profound. ithi. Virtue!
Method and Wisdom. The Six Dharmas and Mahāmudrā
@##/ /dpal ldan shangs pa'i gser chos las/ rtsa ba ni gu chos drug gi khrid bsdus stan thog gcig ma'i nyams len ye shes DA ki'i zhal lung zhes bya ba bzhugs so// //
9. The Single Sitting, Words of the Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness. A Concise Guide to Niguma’s Six Dharmas, the Root of the Golden Dharmas of the Glorious Shangpa[1]
(208)@#/ /brtan g.yo'i khyab bdag bde ba che/ / gcig pu'i rang bzhin du ma'i gzugs/ / zab mo'i rim pa las skyes pa/ / bla med de la phyag 'tshal lo/ /
Great bliss, pervading the static and moving in myriad forms from a single nature, born from the stages of the profound: I bow to the unsurpassable.
rgyud rnams kun las dngos bstan cing / / grub mchog bye ba gshegs pa'i shul/ / nyams su blangs pas ye shes ster/ / chos drug stan thog gcig ma 'chad/ /
I present the Six Dharmas in a Single Sitting that is taught explicitly in all tantras, the legacy of a million supreme adepts that grants timeless awareness through practice.

de yang mthar thug ston pa rnam lnga sogs bla med kyi rgyud sde mtha' dag gi rdzogs rim snying por dril ba ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro'i zhal lung las rtsod med du byung zhing / mkhas grub khyung po rnal 'byor sogs skye mtha'i byang sems 'ba' zhig pa'i thugs bcud smar chos drod tshad yid ches 'phral du skyed pa 'di nyid rgyas par yig rnying rnams dang / khyad par rje btsun sgrol ba'i mgon po'i gsung rab las shes par bya zhing / stan thog gcig ma'ang de nyid dang dam pa'i skyes bu gzhan gyi yig cha mang du mchis mod/ 'dir de dag gi zab bcud dril zhing brgyud pa rnying pa la bka' (209) bab kyi gdams ngag gsar pas zur brgyan te bshad par bya'o/ / spyir sgo 'byed dang byin rlabs kyi bka' rnams thob cing rtsa ba'i chos bzhi'i myong ba ci rigs skyes pa'am/ ma skyes kyang khrid chen rdzogs pa zhig gis rgyun khyer nyams len tu bya ba ni 'di yin no/ /

These are the indisputable words of the Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness that combine the essence of the completion phase of all the highest tantras, such as the culminating five teachers.[2] It is the heart essence of Khedrup Khyungpo Naljor and the others, all of them in their final lives as bodhisattvas. It is the highest degree of spoken dharma that immediately produces confidence. It can be found extensively in the books of old, especially in the collected works of Venerable Drolwai Gönpo (Tāranātha).[3] There are certainly numerous manuals on single-sitting practices by him and other noble ones. Here I will condense the profound quintessence of those texts and adorn them with new instructions from the transmission of the ancient lineages. {209} In general, this is the daily practice for someone who has obtained the permissions that open the door and grant blessings and in whom some appropriate experiences of the four root dharmas has arisen. Even if they have not arisen, it is for one who has fully received the great guidances.
de la spyi dang khyad par gnyis/ spyi la sngon 'gro dang dngos gzhi gnyis/ sngon 'gro la'ang thun mong dang thun min gnyis so/ /
This has both (1) general and (2) special esoteric instructions:
I.
I. General Instructions
the general instructions comprise (1) the preliminaries and (2) the main practice.
A.
A. Preliminaries
There are (1) common and (2) uncommon preliminaries.
thun mong
1. Common Preliminaries

spyi la grags pa'i chos bzhis rgyud sbyangs pa sngon du song ba'i dbang du byas nas 'dir gsal 'debs khyug tsam bya ste/ gnas dben par stan bde bar lus gnad dkyus mthun bca'/ dal brgyad 'byor bcus brgyan pa'i mi lus yid bzhin nor bu las kyang ches rnyed par dka' ba 'di yang 'chi rkyen du mas mi rtag pas de ring tsam yang mi 'chi ba'i gding ni med/ shi nas dkar nag las kyi 'bras bu kho na dbang che zhing / mkha' khyab kyi sems can rnams kyang 'khor ba'i (210) sdug bsngal dar drags la yun ring bas gtses/ sdug bsngal 'di las skyob thub pa'i skyabs kyi rgyal po ni bla ma rin po che yin pas khyed las re sa med do snyam pa'i blo thag rbad kyis bcad/ chos 'di'i rang lugs kyi thun mong gi sngon 'gro dngos ni skyabs 'gro sems bskyed gnyis te/

These are the general, well-known four contemplations that refine the mind stream. But since they must precede all practice, here I will present a cursory clarification. Assume the usual posture on a comfortable seat in an isolated place. Contemplate as follows and intensify your resolve: This human body adorned with eight freedoms and ten endowments is more difficult to find than a wish-fulfilling gem. But due to many life-threatening conditions, it is impermanent and cannot be assured to last even for today. Once I die, only the results of my good or bad actions will hold sway. All sentient beings throughout space are also tormented in this way by the proliferation of samsaric sufferings. {210} Since the precious guru is the only sovereign who can give us refuge from this suffering, I have no other hope than you. The actual common preliminary in this doctrine’s own system has two parts: (1) going for refuge and (2) arousing the mind of awakening.
dang po ni/
a. Going for Refuge

sa phyogs dag pa'i zhing khams su mos/ mdun gyi nam mkhar seng khri sna tshogs pad+ma nyi zla bzhi brtsegs pa'i steng du drin can rtsa ba'i bla ma sku dngos de ka la bkrag mdangs gzi brjid 'od du 'bar ba/ rang la dgyes pa'i 'dzum zhal gyis gzigs pa/ phyogs bcu dus gsum gyi dkon mchog rtsa gsum ma lus pa 'dus pa'i bdag nyid du nges shes bskyed la/ bla ma rang mkhyen snyam pa'i blo gtad ling gis bskyur/ nam mkha'i mtha' khyab kyi pha ma sems can kun kyang rang dang lhan cig skyabs su 'gro bar mos te/ ngag tu/ ma nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i sems can thams cad skyabs kun 'dus kyi ngo bo bla ma rin po che la skyabs su mchi ba lags so/ / zhes ci nus brjod/ skyabs yul skabs 'dir bsdu bar mi mdzad/

Imagine the area as a pure realm. In the space before you appears a four-tiered seat consisting of a lion throne, multicolored lotus, sun, and moon. Upon that is your kind root guru in his or her actual form, with a brilliant countenance, charismatic and radiant with light, smiling at you with pleasure. Develop the certainty that the guru is the embodiment of the union of all the Three Jewels and Three Roots in the ten directions and three times. Completely entrust yourself while thinking, “Guru, consider me.” Imagine that all mother and father sentient beings throughout space also go for refuge along with you. Recite as much as you can: All sentient beings throughout space, my mothers, take refuge in the precious guru, the gathered essence of all refuges. You do not dissolve the refuge objects at this point.
gnyis pa ni/
b. Arousing the Mind of Awakening

sems can thams cad bdag gi pha mar ma gyur pa ni gcig kyang med pas shin tu gces shing phongs kyang 'khor ba na sdug bsngal mtha' med pa la spyod par 'dug / 'di rnams la drin lan tu phan gdags dgos/ de yang phan phyogs res mi phyin pas thams cad zung 'jug rdo rje 'chang chen po'i go 'phang la 'god pa'i phyir du snyan brgyud kyi thabs lam bsgom par bgyi'o snyam pa'i blo dung dung bas/ ngag tu/ nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i sems can thams cad kyi don du rnam pa thams cad mkhyen pa (211) rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang thob par bya/ de'i ched du zab lam ni gu'i chos drug nyams su blang bar bgyi'o/ / zhes yang yang brjod/

Think, “There is not a single sentient being that has not been my parent. They are very dear to me, but they are destitute, involved as they are in cyclic existence with its endless suffering. I must repay their kindness to me by helping them, and not just partially. In order to establish them in the totally unified state of Great Vajradhara, I will meditate on the path of methods of the aural lineage.” Say: For the sake of all sentient beings throughout space, I will attain the state of perfect omniscient awakening. {211} To that end, I will take up the practice of the profound path of Niguma’s Six Dharmas. Recite that again and again.
dkon mchog skyabs 'og chud pa dang / / skyes bu chen po'i blo skyes na/ / thar pa'i lam las mi zlog cing / / spyod lam kun kyang byang chub rgyu/ ! /
When you come under the refuge of the Jewels and develop the attitude of a great being, without regressing on the path of freedom, all activity becomes the cause of awakening.
sngon 'gro gnyis pa thun mong ma yin pa dag byed a'i stong ra ni/
2. Uncommon Preliminaries: The Purifying A of Inner Space
sngar bsgoms pa'i rtsa ba'i bla ma nyid slar yang gsal gdab ste mos gus kyi gdung shugs drag pos/
Again visualize your root guru as before and with intense feelings of devotion say:

dus gsum sangs rgyas thams cad 'dus pa'i ngo bo bla ma rin po che/ sems can thams cad kyi don du bdag gis nad gdon thams cad zhi bar mdzad du gsol/ sdig sgrib thams cad 'dag par mdzad du gsol/ ting nge 'dzin khyad par can rgyud la skye bar mdzad du gsol/

Precious guru, unified essence of all buddhas of the three times: for the sake of all sentient beings, I pray to you to pacify all my sickness and spirits, to purify all my negative acts and obscurations, and for special meditative absorption to arise in my being.

zhes gsol ba ci nus su btab pas bla ma 'od du zhu/ spyi bo nas zhugs te thim pas klad pa gti mug gi rang bzhin can de sbyangs nas yal/ mgrin pa yan chad mgo bo chu'i lbu ba lta bu kha dog dkar la reg bya srab pa'i nang du chos 'byung dkar po gru gsum pa dwangs gsal shel gyi snod lta bu/ rtsa ba phra ba mgrin par sleb cing gdengs ka g.yal ba gyen tu bstan pa'i zur gcig smin dbrag dang / zur gnyis rna ltag g.yas g.yon la reg tsam pa/ de'i dbus su drang thad du bla ma dang rang sems skye med mtshon pa'i a dkar po gsal dwangs 'od kyi rang bzhin can/ phyed cha chos 'byung nang du chud cing phyed tsam steng du 'thon pa/ rten med du lding ba la thog mar bsgrims te sems gtad/

Do that supplication as much as you can. Then the guru melts into light and enters through your cranial aperture, refining away the brain, which is the nature of stupidity. Your head above the neck becomes like a water bubble, white and soft to the touch. [Within the head] is a white tetrahedral source of phenomena, empty inside, radiant, and clear like a crystal vase. [It is suspended upside down] with its sharp apex facing downward at the throat. The broad side with its three vertices faces upward with one vertex level with the eyebrows and the other two vertices at the temples by the right and left ears, just touching [the inside of the skin outline]. Right in the center of that source of phenomena is a radiant clear white letter A—the embodiment of your unborn mind inseparable from the guru. Half of the letter is within the source of phenomena and half protrudes above the rim, suspended in space without support. First concentrate on that and focus your mind. {212}

de rjes shes pa grims lhod (212) ran pos ci nus sems 'dzin/ mi nus na a thung gi bzlas pa shubs bur lan nyer gcig tsam bzlas pas/ a yig las bdud rtsi dkar po'i rgyun shugs dang ldan par bab/ chos 'byung mer gyis gang ste zham zham lud pas lus phyi nang thams cad du khyab cing bkrus/ thog med nas bsags pa'i sdig sgrib bag chags dkor dang sku glud zos pa dam tshig nyams chags sogs dud khu sol khu'i rnam par ba spu'i bu ga dang dbang po'i sgo rnams nas phyir nag nu ru ru bdas/ lus kyi gdos bcas ljan ljin rnams kyang zhu ba ltar song zhing bdud rtsis phyi nas kyang bkrus te nag bun nu nu sa 'og thag ring por song nas yal/ rang lus shel gong g.ya' dag pa la thogs med 'ja' dkar po lta bu bdud rtsis gang bar bsams la shes pa lhod la bzhag / 'di nyid ched du bsgom skabs dmigs bzlas de rnams bskyar ba yin la bla ma'i rnal 'byor thog ma'i gcig des chog /

Afterward, hold the mind there by balancing your consciousness between concentration and relaxation. When unable to maintain that, quietly recite short A twenty-one times. This causes a stream of white elixir to cascade down from the A. It fills the source of phenomena to the brim and splashes over the opening, filling and washing your whole body inside and out. All beginninglessly accumulated negativities, obscurations, habitual tendencies, [corruption from] misappropriated funds, profit from the sale of images, contraventions and errors in sacred pledge, and such exude out through your pores and orifices in the form of liquid smoke or liquid coal and slither away darkly. The filthy substances of your body also dissolve and are expelled, while the elixir washes the outside of the body. The black soot goes far under the ground and disappears. Imagine that your body becomes a polished crystal vase filled with elixir like an unobstructed white rainbow. Then relax consciousness. When this is intended as a separate practice, the visualization and recitation are repeated. However, the initial guru yoga is sufficient.

dmigs pa 'di la yan lag gnyis te nad zhi byed ni/ tsha ba la bdud rtsi dkar bsil gyis nad dmar po'i rnam pa/ grang ba la bdud rtsi dmar zhing tsha bas nad dkar 'dur gyi rnam pa/ rlung dam 'dus pa la bdud rtsi ser la snum pas nad sngo 'dur gyi rnam pa sogs/ gang na ba'i thad de kar bug pa byung nas bdas pas rtsad nas dag par bsam/

This visualization has two branches: pacifying sickness and pacifying spirits. For sicknesses of heat, imagine that cool white elixir soothes red sickness. For cold sicknesses, red-hot elixir pacifies sickness that appears white and thick. For sicknesses of the vital winds or a combination [of winds, bile, and phlegm], yellow, oily elixir pacifies bluish thick sickness, and so forth. Wherever that sickness is located, a hole forms in front of it and it passes outside. Think that it is totally cured.

gdon zhi byed ni/ a las bab pa'i bdud rtsi gdon so so'i gnyen po khro bo ser drag lta bur gyur pa dang / me dpung dang khro chu khol ma'i rgyun sngags kyi sgra dang bcas pas lhag med du tshar bcad bar bsgom la mnyam par bzhag go /

For spirits, the elixir that falls from the letter A becomes the specific antidote to each spirit: wrathful deities descending like hail, fireballs, molten bronze rivers, and the roar of mantras. Meditate that the spirit is totally annihilated without remainder, and rest in equipoise.
sbyang bya gdod nas ma grub par/ / sbyong byed skye med yig 'bru nyid/ / spros pa kun zhi (213) dbu ma'i don/ / sbyong tshul kun gyi zla med pa'o/ ! /
What is to be refined has never existed. What refines is the letter of the unborn itself. All elaborations are pacified; meaning the middle way. This way of refining is unequaled by all others. {213}
dngos gzhi
B. Main Practice
chos drug gi
1. The Six Dharmas
dang pa thabs lam bde drod rang 'bar
a. Naturally Blazing Bliss-Warmth, the Path of Methods
['di] la sngon 'gro dngos gzhi rjes gsum mo/ /
This has three parts: (1) the preliminary, (2) the main practice, and (3) the concluding practices.
i.
i. Preliminary

sngon 'gro lus gnad me'i stong ra'am gtum mo me rgod ma ni/ rang bde mchog lhan skyes su gsal ba'am tha mal du'ang rung ba'i spyi bor seng ge brgyad kyis btegs pa'i rin po che'i khri yangs shing rgya che ba'i steng du pad+ma dkar po dang nyi zla'i steng du rtsa ba'i bla ma ston zla ltar dkar zhing zhal 'dzum bag can/ rang la byin gyis rlob rlob 'dra ba bsgom/ log rtog shas che ba dang mos blos yar gzhal dgos tshe rdo rje 'chang du bsgoms kyang rung ni rung / chos drug 'di'i khyad chos su bla ma sku dngos sgom par mdzad/ gong ltar skyabs gnas kun 'dus su mos pa sogs sgo du ma nas mos gus kyi gdung shugs drag pos/

The preliminary of Fierce Inner Heat is the vital point of the body called the Inner Space of Fire or Inner Heat Wildfire.[4] Visualize yourself as Coemergent Cakrasaṃvara or in your ordinary form. Above your head is a vast and wide bejeweled throne supported by eight lions. There, on a seat of white lotus, sun, and moon sits your root guru, white as the autumn moon and smiling. Meditate on the guru’s waves of blessing. If you tend toward wrong ideas or when you need to increase devotion, it is all right to meditate on the guru as Vajradhara. However, the special feature of these Six Dharmas is the meditation on the guru in his or her actual form. With the intense longing of devotion through multiple means, such as the notion described above, that the guru is the embodiment of all refuges, say:

dus gsum sangs rgyas thams cad 'dus pa'i ngo bo bla ma rin po che/ sems can thams cad kyi don du bdag gi lus la bde drod kyi ting nge 'dzin khyad par can skye bar mdzad du gsol/ sems la bde stong gi ting nge 'dzin khyad par can skye bar mdzad du gsol/

Precious guru, united essence of all buddhas of the three times. For the sake of all sentient beings, bless me that the special absorption of bliss-warmth arises in my body. Bless me that the special absorption of bliss-emptiness arises in my mind.

ces gsol ba drag tu btab pas bla ma bdud rtsi'i ngo bor zhu ba spyi bo nas thim/ rnam smin gyi lus sbyangs te rje btsun rdo rje rnal 'byor mar gyur pa ni/ dmar smug zhal gcig phyag gnyis g.yas rdo rje/ / cung zad 'thur sdigs thod khrag thugs kar g.yon/ / thod skam dbu rgyan thod rlon do shal 'phyangs/ / spyan gsum skra grol phyag rgya lnga yis brgyan/ / g.yas brkyang stabs kyis pad nyi mi ro dkar/ / mgo g.yas bstan steng me phung dbus na bzhugs/ /

Through your supplicating with intense feeling, the guru melts into the essence of elixir, which enters the crown of your head and dissolves, refining away your fully ripened karmic body. You become Exalted Vajrayoginī, dark red, with one face and two arms. The right hand is slightly menacing with a vajra pointing downward and the left holds a blood-filled skull cup to the heart. She wears a crown of the five dry human skulls and is bedecked with a garland of fifty freshly severed heads. Three eyes, loosened hair, and five bone ornaments adorn her. She stands in the posture of right leg extended on a white human corpse with its head bent to the right, upon a lotus and sun seat, amid towering flames. {214}

sku lus (214) kyi nang dar dmar gyi gur phub pa lta bu ba spu'i mthar thug pa tshun stong sang nge bar bsam/ lus gnad me thab drug chings bya ste tsog pu rkang ngar g.yas nang g.yon pa phyi la yod pa'i re'u mig ltar bsnol/ lag gnyis kyang bsnol te bar lhu gnyis 'jus pa'i gru mo pus mo'i steng du yong par bya/ sgal tshigs bsrangs/ lta stangs thad kar bzhag / lte ba'i thad kyi mdun rgyab gnyis dang mkhal khung g.yas g.yon dang bzhir me'i gong bu dmar la zlum pa/ shin tu tsha ba/ me lce 'bar tshad pa lcags sregs gong bu lta bu bzhi sgroms su gsal gdab/

Imagine that the inside of your bodily form is utterly empty down to the pores and is like a red silk tent. The vital point of the body is the sixfold-binding-stove position, sitting with the legs drawn up and the calves crossed, the right inside and the left outside, forming a cross. The two hands are also crossed, grasping the opposite biceps, with the elbows resting on the knees. Keep the backbone straight and rest the gaze straight ahead. Visualize a foursquare formation of four fireballs—directly in front and in back of your navel and at the right and left kidneys. They are round, red, and very hot, about to erupt into flames, like red-hot burning iron balls.

dmigs rdil de mi 'dor bzhin tu rlung ro dal la ring ba lan gsum 'bud/ steng rlung dal bus rngubs te lte 'og tu mnan/ 'og rlung yar mi 'then par rang sar bcings/ lte bar g.yas bskor gcig dang g.yon bskor gcig byas pas me gong rnams 'thabs te lus kyi nang thams cad me stags dmar skyas dmar chem chem tsha 'ur 'ur khyab par bsam la mi bde ba med med du 'jam rlung bzung / mi thub pa na dang por shugs chung / bar du che/ mthar sang gis bus/ de ltar bzhi brgyad sogs rlung theng gang lcogs bzung / cung zad byang nas g.yas bskor g.yon bskor re re rim par bsnan pas mthar bskor ba bcu gnyis re tsam thub pa na me'i nus pa rnyed par 'gyur zhing / yan lag lnga sbyong sngon tu 'gro ba'i gtsubs shing gtsubs stan ma'i 'khrul 'khor yang ci nus byas pas drod skye ba la myur ro/ /

Without stopping that visualization sequence, expel the dead air three times with long, slow exhalations. Inhale slowly and press the upper winds down below the navel. Hold the lower winds in place without drawing them up. Rotate the belly once to the right and once to the left, causing the fireballs to collide. Imagine that the whole inside of your body fills with the glittering red and crackling heat of the pink sparks of fire. Hold the gentle breath, ignoring the discomfort. When unable to hold it longer, expel the breath slowly at first, strongly in the middle, and then finally exhale totally. Do this four or eight times, holding down the breath as you are able. When you have practiced for a time, gradually add the rotations [of the belly], once to the right and once to the left. When you can perform twelve right rotations and twelve left rotations, you will gain the capability of fire. After doing the five-branch training, train as much as possible in the yogic exercises of Drilling Stick and Drilling Base, which will swiftly arouse the heat.
dngos gzhi gtum mo zas su za ba ni/
ii. Main Practice: Eating the Food of Fierce Inner Heat

lus gnad rkang pa sems dpa'i skyil krung lhod de rgya che bar bca'/ lag pa bsrangs te lag mthil gnyis pus mor bkab/ so mchu rang bab lta ltangs gong mtshungs/ sgal tshigs bsrang / (215) rkang pa'i mthe bong nang du dgug /

The vital points of the body are to sit with your legs in bodhisattva position, relaxed and wide, your palms on your knees with arms straight, teeth and lips resting naturally, and the gaze as described above. The spine is straight and the two big toes are turned inward. {215}

rang nyid rje btsun mar gsal ba'i stong ra'i dbus su rtsa a ba d+hU ti mda' smyug 'bring po tsam drang ba/ srab pa/ dwangs pa/ dmar ba ste mtshan nyid bzhi ldan/ yar sne tshangs bug dang mar sne lte 'og sor bzhir zug pa/ gnyis ka'ang bcad khar yod cing nang stong sang nge ba smyug ma khrigs bcad byas pa lta bu'i g.yas su ro ma dmar po/ / g.yon tu rkyang ma dkar po gnyis ka gro sog tsam pa bcas sum gshib las/ mar sne dbu ma las sor bzhi ring bar song ba'i sne yar log ste dbu ma'i nang du chud tsam pa/

Visualize yourself as Exalted Vajrayoginī with the central avadhūtī channel in the center of the empty internal space. The channel has the four characteristics of being straight like a medium-sized arrow, fine, radiant, and red. Its upper end reaches the cranial aperture, and its lower end is four fingers-widths below the navel. The openings of both ends are cut and inside they are clear and empty, like a bamboo stalk that has been cut straight through. To its right is the red rasanā channel and to the left the white lalanā channel, both about the thickness of a wheat straw. The three channels run closely parallel, except that the lower ends of the two are four finger-widths longer and turn back to just enter into the lower end of the central channel.

yar sne gnyis po dbu ma'i yar sne'i rgyab phyogs nas sor gcig tsam thad du 'khyogs/ de mtshams gnyis gshibs byas pas dbu ma'i yar sne'i steng nas bkab cing mdun tu gug nas sna bug gnyis su thug pa/ dbu ma'i yar sna'i nang du haM yig dkar po mgo thur bstan bde zhing bsil ba/ mas sna rtsa gsum 'dus mdor raM yig dmar po mgo gyen bstan shin tu tsha ba/ de las sor bzhi tsam gyi 'og thad bshang sgor rlung gi dkyil 'khor zla gam sngo skya bcad kha mdun bstan rab tu g.yo ba rnams gsal btab/

The two upper ends are one finger-width behind the central channel and bend straight from there. From that juncture their ends come together, covering the top of the central channel, then curve to the front and terminate at the two nostrils. Within the upper end of the central channel there is a white upside-down syllable haṃ, blissful and cool. Inside the lower end of the central channel, at the place where the three channels converge, there is a red upright syllable raṃ, extremely hot. Four finger-widths directly below the lower end of the central channel, near the anus, there is a light-blue semicircular wind mandala with its straight side facing forward, extremely volatile. Clearly visualize all that.

'bud pa dgu phrugs ni/ dang po dal la ring ba gsum/ de nas drag la thung ba gsum/ de nas ro stod gcud cing 'bud pa gsum ni/ lag pa g.yas pa'i mthe bong srin lag gis mnan cing mthe'u chung yang bkug / mdzub mo gung mo'i rgyab tu sbyar bas sna g.yon pa btsir/ g.yon mthe bong nang du bcug pa'i khu tshur mchan 'og g.yas par bcug pa g.yas kyi bar lhus mnan te g.yas kyi nu ma gru mo gcud la bor zhing sna g.yas nas rlung ro lan gcig sang gis 'bud/ de go zlog (216) pas g.yon nas gcig / slar yang g.yas nas gcig 'bud la cung zhig ngal gso zhing stong ra gsal gdab/ yang dal bus rlung ro gcig bsal nas steng rlung 'jam por rngubs pa lte 'og tu mnan/ 'og rlung yang cung zad 'then la kha sbyor du bzung /

For the ninefold shake-up of dead air, the first three are slow and long, the next three strong and short, and for the final three twist the torso while exhaling. Press the thumb of the right hand against the base of the ring finger, with the little finger also bent. Place the middle finger behind the index finger and press the left nostril. With the left hand, make a fist with the thumb inside and put it under the right armpit and press down with the right arm. The elbow squeezes the right breast as you completely exhale once from the right nostril. {216} Then reverse it and exhale once from the left. Then once again exhale from the right. Relax a little and refresh the visualization of the empty space. Again, slowly clear out the dead air once. Then inhale and with the upper winds press down below the navel. Also draw up the lower winds slightly and hold the joined winds.

dmigs pa rlung rnams sna sgo nas ro rkyang brgyud nas rtsa gsum 'dus mdor sleb/ rlung dkyil las kyang rlung kha dog sngon po mdud tshugs su langs te dbu mar chud/ rlung gsum pos raM bus pas me phra zhing rno ba gsal la 'tsher ba je ring 'bar/ rlung theng 'ga' re song nas spyi bo'i haM la phog pas byang sems dkar po'i rgyun bab/ je ring byung nas lte ba'i raM la thim par bsgom/ de'ang mdun phyogs su me dang rgyab phyogs su thig le'i 'bar 'dzag bya ste shas che ba la dgongs pa yin gsungs/ me 'od gang du byung ba'i lus kyi nang tsha 'ur ba dang / byang sems kyi 'od skya yam gang du byung ba der bde phril gyis byung ba gnyis la 'dun pa res mos gtad/

In the visualization, the winds all enter through the nostrils and travel down the rasanā and lalanā, arriving at the juncture of the three channels. Blue wind from the wind mandala rises like a piercing spear and enters the central channel. The three winds [of the rasanā, lalanā, and the downward-Shangpa clearing wind] fan the raṃ syllable, which produces a fine, pointed line of fire, clear and radiant, blazing steadily higher. After a few breaths, it strikes the haṃ in the head, causing a stream of white bodhicitta to fall. As this lengthens, meditate that it dissolves into the raṃ at the navel. It is said that the intention is mainly to focus on the blazing and dripping of the fire in front and the vital drops in back. Alternate your intention between the sound of heat inside your body wherever the light of fire occurs and vibrating bliss in whatever course the light of the bodhicitta takes.

de'ang rlung ji tsam thub thub tu bzung zhing cung zad mi bde na sngon ma phyir ma btang bar slar yang rngub chung gang nus bcas lte ba'i g.yas g.yon dbus gsum du 'then gnon byas te gzhil/ mi thub na gong ltar 'phang / de ma thag tu yang rngubs te bsgom/ ngal gso na rlung theng bzhi/ brgyad/ bcu drug la sogs pa'i mtshams su bya yi gang 'dod du bzhag mi rung / nyin mtshan gyi mtha' dang gung gnyis la spang zhing thog mar g.yon nam mnyam rgyu'i skabs su bzung ba'i 'go brtsam pa dang / dud rlung sogs spang blang bya ba rnams kyang gzhan las shes par bya'o/ /

Hold your breath as long as you can. When it becomes somewhat uncomfortable, inhale as many small gulps of air as you can without letting out any of the air held previously. Push and press your belly to the right, left, and center in the area of the navel. When you can’t [hold the breath any longer], let it out as before and then immediately inhale and meditate. If you need to rest, take a break after four, eight, sixteen (etc.) times; not just whenever you want to. Do not do this practice either at dawn or dusk, or at noon. At first, begin the breath-holding practice at the times when [the breath] moves from the left or equally [from both nostrils]. This and the acts of adopting or abandoning the evil winds and so on should be learned elsewhere.
rjes srid pa'i dbang zhu ba ni/
iii. Concluding Practices: Taking the Empowerment of Existence

bla ma gdan bcas gong ltar gsal gdab/ phyi mchod phyogs dus kun gyi mchod rdzas bzang dgu/ nang dam tshig dang ye shes kyi bdud rtsi/ gsang ba bde (217) skyed kyi rig ma/ 'khor gsum sgyu ma rmi lam ltar shes pa de kho na nyid de mchod pa bzhi rdzogs su phul bar bsam zhing / dus gsum sangs rgyas thams cad 'dus pa'i ngo bo bla ma rin po che la/ phyi me tog bdug spos/ nang sha lnga bdud rtsi lnga/ gsang ba bde stong gi ye shes/ yang gsang de kho na nyid kyi mchod pa dam pa rnams 'bul lo/ / bzhes nas bdag la dbang bzhi rdzogs par bskur du gsol/ /

zhes gsol ba drag tu btab pas/ / bla ma'i sku las ye shes bdud rtsi dkar la bde ba'i ngad can bab/ spyi bo nas zhugs/ smin mtshams yan chad gang / lus kyi dri ma dag / bum dbang thob/ mgrin pa yan chad gang / ngag gi dri ma dag / gsang dbang thob/ snying ga yan chad gang / yid kyi dri ma dag / shes rab ye shes kyi dbang thob/ lus thams cad gang / sgo gsum gyi dri ma mtha' dag dag / dbang bzhi pa thob/ bla ma 'od du zhu nas rang la thim/ bla ma'i gsang gsum dang rang gi sgo gsum dbyer med du mos la mnyam par bzhag /

Through your fervent supplication, a bright-white bliss-inducing stream of awareness elixir falls from the guru’s body. It enters through the top of your head and fills your body above the eyebrows. Physical stains are purified, and you receive the vase empowerment. It fills your body above the throat. Verbal stains are purified, and you receive the secret empowerment. It fills your body above the heart. Mental stains are purified, and you receive the wisdom-awareness empowerment. It fills the whole body. All stains of the three doors are purified, and you receive the fourth empowerment. The guru melts into light and dissolves into you. The guru’s awakened body, speech, and mind blend inseparably as one with your own body, speech, and mind. Settle in equipoise.
'di nyid dgos pa dang byin rlabs shin tu che bas skabs 'dir tshar re chag thabs med cing khol 'don phur tshugs su bsgom na bogs 'don thams cad kyi mchog go /

This practice has very great purpose and blessings, so on this occasion of Fierce Inner Heat it must be done each time without fail. If you meditate with ardent intentionality, it will become the most excellent of all enhancement practices.
stod smad kyi gegs rang grol sogs ni gzhung las shes par bya'o/ /
For the natural liberation of upper and lower obstructions, consult the source texts.[5]
bde stong phyag rgya chen po'i dngos/ / skye 'di nyid la myur ster ba/ / tsaN+Di rgyal ba kun gyi thugs/ / bsags sbyangs kun gyi mthar thug go ! /
Actual bliss-emptiness of mahāmudrā rises quickly through this gift, the heart of all victors: caṇḍālī, the ultimate accumulation and purification.
gnyis pa sgyu lus chags sdang rang grol ni/
b. Illusory Body, Naturally Liberated Desire and Anger

rang nyid 'khor lo bde mchog sku mdog mthing / / rdo rje dril bsnol phyag rgya drug gis brgyan/ / thor tshugs zla phyed sna tshogs rdo rjes mtshan/ / mgo phreng do shal stag lpags sham (218) thabs can/ / g.yon bskum g.yas brkyang 'jigs byed dus mtshan mnan/ / phag mo dmar mo gri thod 'dzin pas 'khyud/ me dpung dbus su pad nyi'i gdan la gsal/ /

Imagine that you are dark-blue Cakrasaṃvara with two hands holding vajra and bell, crossed [around Vajravārāhī]. He is adorned with the six symbolic ornaments and marked by the crescent moon and crossed vajra in the hair topknot, wearing a garland of wet heads and a tiger-skin skirt. {218} He stands with left leg bent and right leg straight, pressing on Bhairava and Kālarātri. He is embraced by red Vārāhī holding a flaying knife and skull cup. They stand on a lotus-sun seat in the midst of a blazing bonfire.

spyi bor gdan bzhi brtsegs la bla ma dag byed stong ra ltar gsal/ rdo rje 'chang du bsgom na sngon po bya/ de'i thugs ka nas 'od zer 'phros/ phyogs dus kyi bla ma yi dam sangs rgyas byang sems dpa' bo mkha' 'gro dge 'dun chos skyong thams cad spyan drangs te thim pas bla ma nyid dkon mchog kun 'dus kyi bdag nyid yin la yin bzhin par gyur/ mtshan thos kyang 'khor ba ngan song las sgrol na gsol ba btab na lta ci smos snyam pa sogs mos gus drag po dang / rigs drug sems can sogs snod bcud thams cad las gsol 'debs kyi sgra 'ur dir dir byed par bsams la/

Visualize the guru upon a four-tiered seat on your head as in the practice of Purifying Empty Space. If you meditate on the guru as Vajradhara, make him blue. Light rays emanate from [the guru’s] heart and invoke from the ten directions all gurus, yidams, buddhas, bodhisattvas, heroes, ḍākinīs, sangha members, and dharma protectors. They dissolve into the guru, who becomes the embodiment of the union of all the Jewels, and appears as just that. Develop intense devotion with thoughts such as “Just hearing the guru’s name liberates from the bad propensities of cyclic existence, let alone actually supplicating.” Imagine the murmuring sounds [of supplication] from all six kinds of sentient beings and so forth—the whole environment and its inhabitants—and say:

dus gsum sangs rgyas thams cad 'dus pa'i ngo bo bla ma rin po che/ sems can thams cad kyi don tu bdag gis bdag 'dzin blos thong bar mdzad du gsol/ dgos med rgyud la skye bar mdzad du gsol/ sgyu lus 'byongs par mdzad du gsol/ rmi lam 'byongs par mdzad du gsol/ 'od gsal phyag rgya chen po mchog gi dngos grub da lta nyid du myur ba nyid du 'dug sa 'di nyid du thob par mdzad du gsol/

Precious guru, unified essence of all buddhas of the three times, for the sake of all sentient beings, I pray to you that I relinquish my self-fixation, have no needs, accomplish Illusory Body, and cultivate Dream. Please bless me to attain the supreme spiritual power of Lucid Clarity Mahāmudrā right now, quickly, on this very seat.
zhes gsol ba drag tu btab nas bla ma rang la bstim/ de nas dmigs pa tsam la thab par bsngags pa'i gnad brgyad ni/
When you supplicate intensely, the guru dissolves into you. This visualization alone, praised for its profundity, has eight vital points:

rang lus lha sku stong sang nge ba'i smad cha'i nang du chos 'byung dkar po 'od kyi rang bzhin gru gsum pa'i zur gcig lte ba dang / zur gnyis mkhal khung gnyis la bstan pa/ rtsa ba phra ba gsang phrag dang kha gdengs g.yel ba gyen/ de la sems yud tsam gtad/ gnad dang po'o/ /

(1) One’s own body as the deity’s empty clear form contains in its lower part a white source of phenomena, the nature of light. This has three vertices: one at the navel and two facing the two kidneys. Its narrow point is at the perineum and its wide opening faces upward. Focus on that briefly.

de'i nang du rigs drug gi sems can (219) dpag tu med pa so so'i lus dang byed las bcas byung nas chos 'byung khrig gis gang bar bsgom/ rang nyid 'gro drug so sor skye ba'i las dang bag chags kyi rang gzugs su shar ba'o snyam pa dang / lte 'og tu 'gro drug gi snang ba 'char byed rtsa yig yod pa nyid gzugs su shar ba'o snyam pa'ang dran tsam bya/ gnyis pa'o/ /

(2) {219} Within that, you meditate on immeasurable sentient beings of the six kinds, each with their individual bodies and functions, densely packed into the source of phenomena. You think, “These are manifestations of my own karma and habitual tendencies for taking birth as each of those kinds of migrators.” Also recall, “Below my navel are the root letters that cause the arising of the appearances of the six kinds of migrators, and so their forms have arisen.”

mkha' khyab kyi sems can dmigs yul du byas/ sems kyi rtsi kha lte ba'i rigs drug la gtad de 'di rnams snang ni snang / bden ni mi bden/ bden med sgyu ma lta bu/ rmi lam lta bu yin snyam drag tu bsgom/ gsum pa'o/ /

(3) You make the sentient beings throughout space the object of your visualization and then turn your mental reckoning on the six kinds of beings at the navel. Think, “Do they appear? They appear. Are they real? They are not. They are like an illusion, like a dream.” Rigorously meditate on that.
'di rnams bden med la bden par bzung nas 'khor bar 'khyams pa snying re rje snyam pa'i snying rje lhang lhang bya/ bzhi pa'o/ /
(4) You think how sad it is that they all cling to what is not real as being real and wander in cyclic existence. Thus develop distinct compassion.
'di rnams 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal las bla mas nges par bskyab tu gsol/ pha bla ma rang mkhyen snyam du blo 'gel/ lnga pa'o/ /
(5) You supplicate the guru to afford them lasting refuge from the sufferings of cyclic existence: “Beloved guru, please consider them.”
de rnams gcig yal gnyis yal rim gyis chos 'byung stong sang nge song pa la sems gtad/ drug pa'o/ /
(6) One of them disappears, then a second disappears. The source of phenomena gradually becomes empty inside. You focus on that.
de nas gtad so ci'ang med pa'i 'dzin med ngang du shig ger bzhag / bdun pa'o/ /
(7) You rest relaxed without fixation, free of all focus.
de la ma gnas na rang gzhan snod bcud thams cad med bzhin tu snang ba sgyu ma lta bur thag bcad/
(8) When you can no longer remain in that state, you envision the whole of the environment and its inhabitants and resolve that it is nonexistent yet appearing, like an illusion.

thun mtshams su'ang mi rtag / mos gus/ sgyu ma'i 'dun pa gsum po gang rung dang ma bral bas ting nge 'dzin spel bar bya/ nad gdon sogs rkyen bzang ngan thams cad lam du khyer tshul gzhung las shes par bya'o/ /

During session breaks, increase the power of your meditative absorption by constantly cultivating the intentionality of impermanence, devotion, and illusion. Learn about how to integrate all good and bad conditions, such as sickness and spirits, from the source texts.
mdo rgyud kun gyis bstan bya'i bcud/ / bsgom na 'khor ba'i 'khrul 'khor 'jig / yon tan drug po shugs la 'char/ / snang stong rab 'byams e ma ho/ ! /
Meditate on this essence of all Sutra and Tantra: the deluded machinations of samsara vanish and the six qualities will arise automatically. Infinite appearance and emptiness—amazing!
gsum pa rmi lam nying 'khrul rang dag
c. Dream, Naturally Purified Double Delusion {220}
['di] la (220) gnyis te/
dang po bzung ba ni/
i. Recognizing Dreams

rang lus yi dam du gsal zhing spyi bor bla ma bsgom pa sogs sgyu lus skabs ltar dang / gsol 'debs kyang tshig rkang gsum po de ka ltar las/ sgyu lus sogs kyi tshab tu/ rmi lam zin par mdzad du gsol/ zhes mtha' bsgyur nas gsol ba drag tu btab pas/ bla ma 'od du zhu rang la thim/ rang lus lha sku gsal stong du shar ba'i stong ra'i dbus su rtsa dbu ma dkar po shel gyi ka ba lta bu/ yas sna spyi bo dang mas sna gsang gnas su zug pa/ de'i nang gi yar sner haM dkar po mgo bo thur du lta ba/ mar sner hU~M yig dmar po mgo bo gyen tu lta ba bsgom/ dbu ma yar mar phra zhing rked pa ldir ba nya dbyibs lta bur bsgom pa'ang gsungs mod/ blo rig dang bstun pa'i tshe na lag ngar tsam dang chung na sba smyug tsam bsgom pa rang legs/ dbu ma sbom na thig le 'khor bde ba yin kyang phra sbom can de cung mi legs/ gang shar thams cad la spyir bden med dang / sgos rmi lam du shes pa'i rtsis bzung nas bsgom pa kho na gal che/

Visualize your body as that of the yidam and meditate on the guru on your head as before during Illusory Body. The supplication is the same as before, except that the last line changes to “…and to recognize dreams.” After fervently supplicating, the guru melts into light and dissolves into you. In the center of the empty space of your body, which has arisen as the clear, empty form of the deity, the white central channel stands like a crystal column. The upper end reaches the head and the lower end the perineum. Meditate that inside the upper end of the central channel there is an upside-down white haṃ and in the lower end an upright red hūṃ. It has also been taught to meditate on the upper and lower ends of the central channel as very thin and the middle as being thick, like the shape of a fish. In any case, when you meditate on it in a way suitable to your own disposition, it’s best to imagine it no wider than your forearm and no narrower than a bamboo cane. If the central channel is wide, it is easy for the [visualized] vital drops to circulate in it, but if it is narrow, it is a little difficult. In all cases, the only important thing is to meditate while taking into account the knowledge that whatever arises is false in general and a dream in particular.

de nas spyi bo'i haM las thig le dkar po sran ma tsam zhig hril gyis chad/ snying gar sleb/ gti mug dag / snying ga yan chad bde yang phyod kyi song / mar sne'i hU~M las thig le dmar po sran ma tsam zhig chad/ snying gar sleb/ 'dod chags dag / khog smad bde yang phyod kyi song / dkar dmar gnyis snying gar 'dzom/ zhe sdang rang dag la song / snying ga'i thad bde yang phyod kyi song bar bsam/ bden med dang rmi lam gyi 'dun pa drag po'i ngang snying ga'i thad kyi dbu ma'i thig le gnyis po 'bros 'dod kyi tshul du g.yas bskor g.yon bskor rang gi blo (221) la gang bder 'khor ba la sems gtad/ bum dbang gi gnad do/ /

Then a pea-sized white drop breaks away from the haṃ in the head and arrives at the heart. This purifies stupidity. Your torso above the heart becomes light and blissful. A pea-sized red vital drop breaks off from the hūṃ at the perineum and arrives at the heart. This purifies desire. Your lower body below the waist becomes light and blissful. The two white and red drops meet at the heart and anger is naturally purified. Imagine the area of the heart filled with bliss and lightness. Within the state of intense intentionality regarding their lack of true existence and dreamlike nature, focus your attention on those two drops chasing each other around inside the empty space of the central channel at the level of the heart. Their manner of circling around can be clockwise or counterclockwise, as you like. {221} This is the vital point of the vase empowerment.

ji zhig na gcig rjes gcig zin gyis reg tsam reg tsam par mos/ gsang dbang ngo / / de nas reg pas lus sems bde phril phril song bar mos/ sher dbang ngo / mthar gcig la gcig thim gtad med du yal ba'i ngang dmigs med du bzhag / dbang bzhi pa'i gnad dang 'brel ba'o/ / bar bar du bden med dang rmi lam yin snyam pa'i 'dun pa kha shas re drag tu bya/ thun mtshams su mi rtag pa/ mos gus/ rmi lam gyi 'dun pa dang mi 'bral bar bya/

Then imagine that the two drops circling around trying to capture each other barely touch. This is the secret empowerment. Then imagine that their touching each other causes your body and mind to experience a thrill of bliss. This is the wisdom empowerment. Finally, one drop dissolves into the other and then vanishes, and you rest without a reference point. That is connected with the vital point of the fourth empowerment. In between [these visualizations], intensely recall a few times the notions that these are not real but a dream. In the session breaks, always maintain the intentional contemplation of impermanence, devotion, and dreams.
ii.
ii. Refining Dreams

zin pa la brtan pa thob nas/ gnyis pa rmi lam sbyong ba ni/ skabs 'dir 'dun pas sbyong ba ste/ bla ma'i rnal 'byor sogs sngar bzhin la gsol 'debs skabs/ rmi lam 'byongs bar mdzad du gsol/ zhes bsgyur/ 'dun pa kho nas rtsal nges med du sbyangs ste rmi lam gyi yid lus la ci sbyang sbyang yin snyam pa'i 'dun pa rgyun chags dang / ka ba rtsig pa sogs la zang thal/ bu ga phra mo la 'dzul zhing me chu gcan gzan g.yang sa sogs ya nga'i rigs la thog brdzis/ mkha' la 'phur zhing sa la 'dzul ba/ khyad par ngo tsha skyug bro sogs rnam rtog chod dka' ba'i rigs la res thog brdzis/ res bden med/ res zlog bsgom gyis nyin mo 'dun pas sbyang zhing mtshan snang la dngos su sbyang ngo / / spel ba sogs gzhung las shes/ ma zin na spog chog / zin pa brtan byed/ 'byams gcod la sogs pa gal pa che'i gdams ngag rnams kyang man ngag las shes par bya'o/ /

Once you have stabilized the recognition of dreams, there is the second phase of refining them. In this context it is to refine the dreams through intentionality. The practice is the same as in recognizing dreams up through guru yoga, except for a change in the supplication to “…and to refine dreams.” There is no definite [visualization] because you practice with the dynamic energy of intentionality alone. Think, “This mental body of dream can be refined in whatever way I choose.” Cultivate this intention continuously. Pass through pillars, walls, and so forth without obstruction. Practice slipping through small windows and so on. Practice direct subjugation of particular frightening situations, such as those involving fire, water, wild beasts, earthquakes, and so forth. Fly in the sky and penetrate under the ground. Train especially with conceptual thoughts that are difficult to overcome, the type that cause shame and disgust. Sometimes [remember that] they are unreal. Sometimes use counteractive meditation. In these ways, refine through intentionality in the daytime and actually refine dream appearances at night. Learn about increasing and other Dream practices from the source texts. You should also know the esoteric instructions concerning the profit ritual if you don’t recognize [dreams], stabilizing them when you do, severing diffusion, and other important instructions.
rmi lam lta bu'i chos rnams la/ / rtag tu rmi lam ltar shes na/ / rigs drug srid pa'i mngal kha stong / / gsal stong lha sku rang shar (222) ro/ /
When all dreamlike phenomena are always known to be like dreams, the womb of sixfold beings’ existence stays empty. The clear empty deity’s form arises by itself. {222}
bzhi pa 'od gsal gti mug rang sangs la/
d. Lucid Clarity, Naturally Clarified Stupidity

sngon 'gro'i tshul du mi rtag pa dung pa bsgom zhing skyo shas bskyed/ dngos gzhi 'od gsal bzung ba ni/ rang bde mchog tu gsal ba'i spyi bor gdan bzhi rdzogs kyi steng du/ rtsa ba'i bla ma ral pa'i thor tshugs rus rgyan stag lpags sogs dur khrod chas brgyad kyis brgyan pa/ rdo rje 'chang du bsgom na yang he ru ka zhi ma khro spyan gsum pa bsgom/ gsol 'debs snga ma'i mtha'/ 'od gsal zin par mdzad du gsol/ zhes bsgyur la mos gus chen pos gsol ba drag tu 'debs/ lus kyi dbus su rtsa dbu ma dkar po/ / de'i snying ga'i thad du pad+ma dkar po 'dab bzhi dang zla ba'i steng du rtsa ba'i bla ma dkar la 'od zer 'phro ba tshon gang ba/ thugs kar thig le dkar po sran ma tsam 'od 'phro ba la sems gtad de mnyam par bzhag /

In the standard preliminary, meditation on the pain of impermanence produces disillusionment. The main practice is the recognition of lucid clarity. You appear clearly as Cakrasaṃvara. Your root guru is on a complete four-tiered seat on your head, adorned by the eight charnel-ground attributes, such as the hair topknot, bone ornaments, and tiger-skin skirt. If you meditate on the guru as Vajradhara, meditate on semi-wrathful Heruka with three eyes. Change the last line of the supplication to “…and to recognize lucid clarity” and supplicate fervently with powerful devotion.
