Within the white central channel at the level of your heart, a thumb-sized figure of your root guru sits on a white four-petaled lotus and moon seat, white and emanating light rays. In that guru’s heart is a white pea-sized vital drop emanating light. Focus there and rest in equipoise.

de las 'od 'phros/ bla ma'i sku khra sa le khyab/ thugs rgyud bde bas gang / sku las 'od zer byung / rang lus khyab/ rang lus ba spu'i bu ga nas 'od zer 'phros/ snang ba thams cad khra gsal gyis khyab par bsgom/ thugs ka'i thig le la sems gtad pa dang 'od zer spro ba de ka yang yang bskyar/ bar bar shes pa rang bab tu bzhag pas skabs rer bde gsal mi rtog pa shugs 'byung du byung na re dogs med par bskyang /

The light that emanates from that suffuses the guru’s form and fills the mind with bliss. Light rays come from that form and pervade your own body, which then radiates light rays out of all its pores. Meditate that all appearances are pervaded by its brilliance. Focus on the drops at the guru’s heart and the emanation of light rays again and again. In between visualizations, let consciousness fall in its own place. Sometimes bliss, clarity, or nonthought will arise automatically, but just continue without hopes and fears.

gnyid du 'gro khar thugs ka'i thig le'am hU~M dngul chu'i mdog lta bu la sems gtad/ thun mtshams su mi rtag pa dang bla ma'i mos gus/ khyad par sku gsum lam khyer gyi 'jog stangs zhes pa/ mig glang po che'i lta stangs ha re bzhag / shes pa klod/ gang shar rang ngo skyong / snang ba sna tshogs kyi gsal cha sprul sku/ rang ngo shes pa'i (223) stong cha chos sku/ de gnyis dbyer med pa'i rang rig rang gsal longs skur shes pas lam du khyer/ chos brgyad kyi a 'thas bshigs/ rnam rtog rang gar ma shor bar rang grol rang dag cig thams cad du gal che/ bsre ba dang rjes gegs sel bogs 'don sogs gzhung las shes/

At bedtime, focus your attention on the vital drop or on a mercury-colored hūṃ in the guru’s heart. In the session breaks, recall impermanence and devotion to the guru. In particular, apply the Integration of the Three Kāyas: remain with your eyes in the unblinking elephant’s gaze, relax consciousness, and sustain the intrinsic essence of whatever arises. The aspect of clarity in the various appearances is nirmāṇakāya. {223} The emptiness aspect that recognizes its own essence is dharmakāya. Those two inseparable in the natural clarity of reflexive awareness is saṃbhogakāya. That knowledge is the integration [of the three kāyas]. The stubborn reification of the eight worldly concerns is destroyed. Without getting lost in the regular course of discursive thought, they are self-liberated and self-purified. This one thing is important to everything. Blending and the concluding practices, such as dispelling obstructions and enhancing, can be found in the source texts.
kun rtog 'pho ba dbyings su sbyang / / ma rig 'khor ba'i rdzun phug gtibs/ / snang bcas snang med 'od gsal nyid/ / lag gtod gdams pa'i snying khrag go/ ! /
Shifting concepts are purified in basic space. The false cave of samsara’s ignorance collapses. Lucid clarity, with or without appearance, is handed over by this heart blood of instruction.
lnga pa 'pho ba ma sgoms sangs rgyas ni/
e. Transference, Buddhahood without Meditation

skabs 'dir lhan thabs kyi man ngag ye shes skar khung ma la byed de/ rang lus lhar gsal spyi bor bla ma bsgom pa sogs sgyu lus skabs ltar la/ gsol 'debs mthar/ bar dor sangs rgyas bar mdzad du gsol/ / zhes bsgyur/ bla ma rang la thim/ lus kyi stong ra'i nang du rtsa dbu ma lag dar ram sba lcag tsam dkar po/ / mar sne gsang gnas su kha zum zhing / yar sne spyi bo'i tshangs bug tu had por yod pa/ dbu ma'i lte ba'i thad du chos 'byung dkar po rtsa ba thur dang gdengs ka gyen bstan/ zur gcig mdun dang gnyis g.yas g.yon tu bstan pa'i dbus gang la'ang ma reg pa'i a dkar po phra la gsal ba 'phar la khad pa zhig bsam/

Here we will use the supplementary esoteric instruction, the Skylight of Timeless Awareness. Visualize your own body as the yidam and meditate on the guru on your head, and so on, the same as in the section on Illusory Body. Change the last line of the supplication to “Please bless me with buddhahood in the intermediate state.” The guru dissolves into you. In the center of your body’s inner space is the white central channel. It is the width of [anywhere between] a forearm and a bamboo cane. The lower end reaches the perineum and is closed; the upper end touches the cranial aperture and is wide open. Inside the central channel is a white source of phenomena at the level of the navel. The fine tip faces downward while the open part faces upward with one vertex facing the front and the other two vertices facing right and left. Within that is the white letter A, suspended without touching anything. Imagine that it is very fine and clear and about to levitate.

rlung ro lan gsum bsal/ bum can shugs drag la yun thung ba zhig bzung / a la sems gtad/ 'og rlung 'then/ lto ba sgal tshigs la cung bcer bas a de cung 'phar nas sngar shul du bab/ de las drag par bcer bas sngar las mtho tsam 'phar sngar shul bsdad/ slar drag tu bcer ba dang mnyam chos 'byung gi kha thag ces brdab pas rlung gi shugs (224) kyis a de mda' 'phangs pa bzhin tu dbu ma'i lam brgyud tshangs bug nas thon/ nam mkha' mthon por sleb nas yal bar bsam la dbyings rig nam mkha' gsum 'dres pa la had de bzhag / de ltar lan bdun tsam bskyar/ 'bebs pa ni nam mkhar a dkar po zhig lam gyis grub pa tshangs bug nas zhugs/ dbu mar dal bus bab/ lte ba'i chos 'byung du brtan cing brjid dang ldan par 'dug pas lus bde phril gyis byung bar bsam/

Clear out the dead air three times, then hold the vase breath forcefully for a short time. Focus on the white A. Draw up the lower wind. Slightly squeeze your belly toward your spine. The white A lifts up a bit and then returns to its former place. When you squeeze a little harder, it rises higher than before and again comes to rest in its place. Again, squeeze as hard as you can. At the same time, the sides of the source of phenomena strike each other. {224} The wind force causes the white A to shoot up like an arrow through the central channel. It comes out of the cranial aperture and continues high into the sky, then vanishes. Space, sky, and awareness—these three blend inseparably. Rest openly just there. Do that visualization some seven times. For the descent, a white A suddenly appears in the sky. It falls down through your cranial aperture and descends slowly down the central channel. It lands in the center of the source of phenomena in the navel and remains there, firm and heavy. Imagine vibrating bliss arising in your body.
de thun chung gcig yin/
This constitutes a single short session.
thog mar sbyong skabs rtags ma thon bar de nyid yang yang bsgom/ rgyun tu dmigs pa tshar re las mi dgos/ thun mtshams su dbu ma'i yar sne zum par bsgom mo/ /

At first, while you are training, meditate again and again until you show the signs. In daily practice, you don’t need to do the visualization more than once. In the session breaks, meditate that the upper end of the central channel is closed.
las la bzang ngan ma mchis par/ / mkha' spyod dag pa'i zhing du skyel/ / zhag bdun tsam gyis gtan don 'grub/ / dman kyang 'di tsam 'bad na mtshar/ ! /
Regardless of good or bad karma, one is transported to pure celestial realms. In just seven days the final goal is attained. Even lesser folks who try this much—amazing!
drug pa bar do rgyal ba longs sku ni/
f. Intermediate State, the Victors’ Saṃbhogakāya

sngon 'gro snga ma ltar la/ bar do longs sku thob par mdzad du gsol/ / zhes gsol 'debs kyi mtha' bsgyur/ bla ma rang la thim/ rang dang snang ba thams cad srid pa bar do dngos yin snyam pa'i 'dun pa drag po sbyang / 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal/ chags sdang gi nyes dmigs la skyo shas bskyed/ bar do'i skabs 'dir rnam rtog skad cig mas gtan gyi bde sdug tshabs po che byed pas ma 'khrul bar ci nas bya snyam pa'i ngang / mdun tu chos 'byung sngon po rtsa ba phra zhing gdengs ka gyen tu bstan pa zhig bsgom/ 'di ma rtogs pa la ma'i mngal/ rtogs pa rnams la 'og min chos kyi dbyings kyi pho brang yin snyam du bsam/ rang nyid de'i dbus su phyin pas hU~M yig sngon po che zhing 'od 'bar bar gyur/ de las (225) 'od 'phros chos 'byung la phog pas/ 'gro ba rigs drug gi mngal du sngar skyes pa dang / da ltar skye ba'i lan chags dang bag chags thams cad sbyangs/ ma 'ongs pa'i skye sgo bkag / skye gnas gzhan gsum gyi bag chags kyang zhor la dag par bsam/ hU~M de yongs su gyur pa las rang nyid 'khor lo bde mchog lhan skyes su gsal ba'i spyi bor bla ma gdan bzhi rdzogs kyi steng du bsgom ste/ bar dor longs sku thob par mdzad du gsol/ / zhes gsol ba rtse gcig btab/

The preliminaries stay the same, except that the last line of the supplication is changed to “May I attain saṃbhogakāya in the intermediate state.” After the guru dissolves into you, train intensively with the thought “This really is the intermediate state of becoming.” Cultivate strong disillusionment with the sufferings of cyclic existence and the shortcomings of desire and anger. Think, “In this intermediate-state situation, a moment’s thought creates lasting happiness or severe suffering. No matter what, I must not be deluded.” Meditate on a blue source of phenomena in front of you. Its tip is pointed down and its wide opening faces upward. Think, “To those without realization, this is the mother’s womb. To those with realization, this is the palace of the Unsurpassed Pure Land.” Then you arrive in its center and become the blue letter hūṃ, large and blazing with light. {225} The light rays radiating from it strike the source of phenomena, purifying all the previous and current habitual patterns and karmic debts of womb birth in the six realms. The doors to future births are blocked. The habitual patterns of the three other places of birth are consequently self-purified. Meditate that the hūṃ completely transforms and you instantly become Coemergent Cakrasaṃvara with the guru upon a four-tiered seat on your head. Supplicate with single-pointed focus: “Please let me obtain the saṃbhogakāya in this intermediate state.”

gzugs snang thams cad bde mchog yab yum/ sgra ru grags tshad yi ge bdun pa/ yid kyi dran rtog thams cad rmi lam sgyu ma'i ngang tshul bden par ma grub par thag bcad/ chos 'byung gi g.yas zur du zhe sdang skye ba'i yul dang pho thams cad 'khor lo sdom pa/ g.yon zur du 'dod chags skye ba'i yul dang mo thams cad rdo rje phag mor gyur nas 'khod par mos la/ mchod pa bzhi rdzogs su phul/ bud med kyis bsgom na chags sdang skye ba'i yul go brje/ mos gus dang / lha sku dang / thams cad bar dor thag bcad cing de'ang bden med du shes pa ni rgyun chags su gal che'o/ / chu ka chad pa'i yur chu bzhin/ / bar do'i rnam rtog kha bsgyur na/ / yang srid srid par mi 'jug pas/ / da lta nyid nas goms 'dris gces/ /

All physical appearance is that of the Cakrasaṃvara couple. The extent of sound is the seven-syllable mantra. All thoughts and memories in the mind are dreams and illusions. Within that state, become utterly convinced that nothing truly exists. Imagine that in the right side of the source of phenomena, all those who arouse your anger and all males become Cakrasaṃvara. All those that arouse your desire and all females on the left side of the source of phenomena become Vajravārāhī. Present the complete four offerings. Female practitioners should reverse the objects that produce desire and anger. It is most important to constantly cultivate devotion, the deity’s form, and the conviction that everything is the intermediate state, while knowing them to be unreal. Like irrigation water from a cut-off pipe, concepts change course in the intermediate state and you won’t enter another life in existence; it is crucial to familiarize from now on.
[Concluding Remarks]

de dag kyang rtsa ba'i chos bzhi la thog mar nyams myong gi sne re ma rnyed par bsgom/ de nas yongs rdzogs su bsgom na snga dro gtum mo/ / nyin gung sgyu lus/ dgongs mo rmi lam/ mtshan mo 'od gsal/ yan lag gi chos 'pho ba dang bar do skabs su gang bab tu bsgom/ chos drug kar nyams su len mi nus na rang gis (226) gang 'dod de khol 'don byed nas bsgom/ skyabs sems stong ra thams cad kyi sngon tu 'gro dgos/ gtum mo kho na bsgom 'dod na lus gnad me'i stong ra rlung theng gsum bzhi tsam dang / gtum mo zas su za ba ci nus su bsgom/ rjes srid pa'i dbang zhu ba tshar gcig byed/ de kho nas thun bzhi'am drug sogs bcad/ gzhan la'ang des 'gre'o/ / de dag gis ni khrid yig ma bu rnams su dngos su bstan pa'i chos drug snying por bsdus pa bshad zin to/ ! /

At first, meditate on the four root dharmas until you have some kind of experience of each of them. Then, if you meditate on all of them in their entirety, do Fierce Inner Heat in the morning, Illusory Body at midday, Dream in the evening, and Lucid Clarity at night. Meditate on the auxiliary dharma cycles whenever it is convenient. If you cannot practice all six dharmas, separate out whichever one[s] you prefer and meditate on that. {226} Refuge, awakening mind, and Purifying Inner Space must all go first. If you wish to meditate only on Fierce Inner Heat, apply the vital points of the body, the empty space of fire, three or four breathing [cycles], and meditate on Eating the Food of Inner Heat as much as you are able. After that, take the Empowerment of Existence one time. Just this can be done in four or six or however many sessions. This applies to the others as well. This concludes the concise explanation of the essential Six Dharmas as it is explicitly presented in the source and subsequent guidebooks.
rtsa ba'i gnyis pa khyad par gyi man ngag las 'byung ba ni/
II. Special Esoteric Instructions

rtsa ba'i chos bzhi stan thog gcig rang du bsgom na/ skyabs sems stong ra yan sngar ltar la/ spyi bab nas bla ma'i rnal 'byor zhig bya ste/ bsgom tshul stong ra bzhin la/ gsol 'debs ni gdung shugs drag pos/

To meditate on the four root dharmas individually in single sittings, first go for refuge, arouse awakening mind, and purify inner space as before. Do the general guru yoga, meditating in the manner of the Purifying Inner Space. Do the supplication with intense feeling:

dus gsum sangs rgyas thams cad 'dus ba'i ngo bo bla ma rin po che/ sems can thams cad kyi don tu bdag gis bdag 'dzin blos thongs par mdzad du gsol/ dgos med rgyud la skye bar mdzad du gsol/ sgyu lus rmi lam 'byongs par mdzad du gsol/ 'od gsal phyag rgya chen po mchog gi dngos grub da lta nyid du myur ba nyid du 'dug sa 'di nyid du thob par mdzad du gsol/ zhes pas gsol ba drag tu btab/

Precious guru, unified essence of all buddhas of the three times, for the sake of all sentient beings, I pray to you that I relinquish my self-fixation, have no needs, accomplish Illusory Body, and cultivate Dream. Please bless me to attain the supreme spiritual power of Lucid Clarity Mahāmudrā right now, quickly, on this very seat. Supplicate intensely.

'di skabs bla ma dkon mchog kun 'dus su shes pa dang / sems can thams cad bsam 'og tu bcug pa tsam las skyabs yul tshur bstims ba dang / 'gro drug gis gsol ba 'debs pa'i dmigs pa mi dgos/ mthar bla ma rang la bstim ste mnyam par bzhag ! /

On this occasion, you only need to know that the guru is the union of all Jewels and to keep all sentient beings in your thoughts; you do not need to do the visualizations of dissolving back [into the guru] or the supplications by the six kinds of migrators. At the end, the guru dissolves into you and you rest in equipoise.
gtum mo stan thog gcig ma ni/
A. Inner Heat in a Single Sitting

lus gnad rnam snang chos bdun spyi ltar las/ lta stangs thad kar blta/ (227) lag mthil gnyis kyis pus mo mnan/ rang nyid rdo rje phag mo bzhugs tshul sogs rang lus dang mthun pa/ rgyan dang gdan sogs spyi mthun bsgom/ lus kyi nang stong sang nge ba'i dbus su ro rkyang spangs pa'i rtsa dbu ma mtshan nyid bzhi ldan ring thung sogs gong ltar la/ lte 'og sor bzhi'i nang du raM dmar nag nas 'bru tsam/ lte ba'i thad kyi nang du nyi gdan sran chung tsam la gnas ba'i a shad dmar ser sor gang tsam phra mo zhig bsgom de rtsa ba'i bla ma'i ngo bor yin snyam mos gus dung ba bya/ dbu ma'i yas snar haM dkar mgo 'thur bstan/

The vital points of the body are the same as the general seven-point posture of Vairocana, except that the gaze is to look straight ahead and the two palms rest on the two knees. {227} Meditate on yourself as Vajravārāhī—the manner of sitting and so forth in harmony with your own body. Ornaments, seat, and so on are the same as usual. In the middle of the clear, empty interior of the body is the central channel endowed with the four characteristics but without the rasanā and lalanā channels. Its length and other attributes were described before. Within it, four finger-widths below the navel, is a dark-red letter raṃ, the size of a barley grain. At the level of the navel, on a sun seat the size of a pea, is an orange A-stroke, one finger-width high and very fine. Meditate on that and cultivate a sense of devotion, thinking that it is the essence of your root guru. At the upper end of the central channel is a white upside-down haṃ.

steng gi nam mkha' bla ma dkar la 'dzum zhing gzi brjid 'bar bar bsam/ rlung ro dgu phugs su 'bud la sbyor ba bzhi ldan gyi rlung drag tu bzung bas/ rlung nyid dbu ma'i g.yon nas mdung tshugs su song / mas sna nas zhugs te raM bus pas me lce dmar nag sor bzhi 'bar/ bla ma'i ngo bo a shad bskul/ de las me dmar ser 'ur gyis 'bar/ spyi bo'i haM bsros/ me lces tshangs bug nas thon te rgya cher 'bar ba'i rtse mo las mchod pa bzhi rdzogs su sprul nas bla ma mchod/ me lce'i 'od las bde drod kyi mchod pa dang bcas pas mnyes par byas/ sangs rgyas kun 'dus kyi ngo bo de'ang byang chub sems kyi bdud rtsir zhu nas me lce dang lhan cig tshangs bug nas byon te spyi bo'i haM la 'dres bas thig le'i rgyun nar gyis bab/ mgrin par sleb/

Think of your guru in the sky above, white and smiling and blazing with charisma. Do the ninefold shake-up of dead air, then forcefully hold the breath with the four-stage application practice. The actual winds enter [through the nose] on the left [and right][6] of the central channel and, like a piercing spear, enter the lower end and fan the raṃ, causing a dark-red flame to rise up four finger-widths. This provokes the A-stroke, the guru’s essence, to blaze up with crackling orange flames. The haṃ at the head heats up and its flames come out the cranial aperture, spreading widely. The complete four offerings emanate from the tips [of the flames] and the offering of bliss-warmth comes from the light of the flames, all presented to the delight of the guru. That embodied essence of all buddhas melts into the elixir of bodhicitta and, together with the flames, enters through the cranial aperture and mixes with the haṃ in the head. A flow of vital drops stretches down to the throat.

dga' ba dang bum dbang / snying gar sleb/ mchog dga' dang gsang dbang / lte ba'i a shad la thim/ khyad dga' sher dbang / de las kyang bdud rtsi bab pa raM la thim/ lhan skyes dang dbang bzhi pa'o zhes don dran/ slar 'bar 'dzag skra shad (228) 'dzings pa gtum mo dkyus ltar bsgom pa las/ raM dang a shad kyi me gcig tu 'dres pa 'bar ba dang / thig le 'dzag pa a shad brgyud raM la thim par bsgom pa'o/ / 'di ni gtum mo zas su za ba/ byin rlabs bla ma'i gtum mo/ / srid pa'i dbang zhu ba gsum ga dmigs pa gcig la dril bas byin rlabs dang gnad shin tu che gsungs/

This [bestows] ecstasy and the vase empowerment. It arrives at the heart: sublime ecstasy and the secret empowerment. It dissolves into the A-stroke and the navel: special ecstasy and the wisdom empowerment. Elixir then falls from that and dissolves into the raṃ: coemergence and the fourth empowerment. Remember that this is the meaning [of the visualization]. {228} Again, meditate on the blazing and dripping like the Brushing Tangled Hair practice of regular Inner Heat practice, except that here you meditate that the fires of the raṃ and the A-stroke merge together and blaze, and that the dripping of the drops passes through the A-stroke and dissolves into raṃ. This combines three visualizations into one: Eating the Food of Inner Heat, the Inner Heat of the Guru’s Blessing, and taking the Empowerment of Existence. Thus it is said to carry great blessings and importance.

skabs 'dir rlung drag tu bus pa'i phyi 'dzin khong 'dren drag po'i ngang 'bar ba la sems gtad pa dang / drag tu rngubs te thur sel gyi sgo gnyis la gzir zhing zhu ba la sems gtad/ thams cad du sems nam mkha' la yas su bcug / lto ba phyir bkyed nas lus gcu zhing rtsal sprugs drag po byed pa dang / hal zhes brjod pa na rlung sbyor gcig la thabs lam yongs su rdzogs pa shin tu gsang ba'i man ngag nye brgyud do/ / thog ma nas stan gcig ma 'di bsgom pa min/ gzhung gi thabs lam la drod tshad rnyed nas rgyun khyer dang bog 'don tu 'di nyid bsgom par bya'o/ ! /

For this occasion, focus your attention on the blazing that occurs when you forcefully expel the breath, hold it out, and draw up from inside. Focus your attention on the melting when you inhale forcefully and squeeze the two doors of the downward-clearing winds. At all times, keep the mind high in the sky. Push out your belly and then twist your body while forcefully stirring up the energy and say “hal.” The entire path of methods is completely contained in this single practice of vital winds. It is an extremely secret esoteric instruction from the direct lineage. This single-sitting practice is not a meditation to start with. Do this meditation as a daily practice and enhancement practice after achieving a degree of warmth in the path of methods from the source.
sgyu lus la/
B. Illusory Body

rtsa ba'i bla ma spyi bo snying ga sogs su bsgom yang rung / gang na bzhugs pa'i phyogs sam mkha' khyab tu bzhugs pa la gsol ba btab kyang chog ste/ pha bla ma/ pha bla ma/ bla ma rang mkhyen/ drin can rtsa ba'i bla ma khyed la gsol ba 'debs so/ /

It is acceptable to meditate on your root guru on your head, in your heart, or elsewhere. Supplicate the guru in a particular place or even dwelling throughout space: Father guru! Mother guru! Guru, consider me. Kind root guru, I pray to you.

zhes mos gdung drag po snying la zug pa bsgoms nas de'i ngang du klod la bzhag / rang lha skur lam tsam gsal btab/ rang gzhan snang ba thams cad la bsam ste/ 'di thams cad med bzhin tu 'khrul ba'i snang ba yin/ bzang ngan chags sdang chos brgyad sogs la a 'thas kyi dgag sgrub byed pa re 'khrul/ gtad pa (229) ci yod/ sgyu ma rmi lam rang yin snyam drag tu sbyangs pas rtsis gdab med par song ba de kar bzo med du bskyang / de ma thag rang lus lhar gsal ba'am tha mal yin kyang rung ste lte 'og chos 'byung man chad dkyus ltar bsgoms pas dbang po rab 'bring tha ma'i nyams len gyi gnad gcig tu 'dus pa'o/ /

Meditate on intense heart-piercing devotion and then relax into that state. Suddenly visualize yourself in the deity’s form. Think about the appearance of yourself and all others: “All this is the deluded appearance of nonexistent things. Good and bad, desire and anger, the eight worldly concerns, and so on are all concerned with accepting or rejecting delusional reifications. {229} What’s there to be concerned about? In fact, it is an illusion, a dream.” Train vigorously with those thoughts, and when you are beyond judgment, maintain that state without fabricating anything. Then immediately visualize yourself as the deity or as your ordinary self if you wish. Meditate on the source of phenomena below your navel as in the regular practice. The vital points of the practices for those of highest, average, or lesser faculties are here condensed into one meditation.
rmi lam la/
C. Dream

bzung ba dkyus ltar rang zin thig le dbang bzhi'i gnad tshar gsum tsam 'jur nas bsgom pa'i rjes su/ rang gzhan snod bcud dgra gnyen longs spyod sogs la bden med kyi 'dun pa drag tu sbyang / de ka'i ngang gang shar bzo med du 'jog / de nyid yang yang goms par bya/ sbyang ba'ang gong ltar la sgyu ma lta bu'i 'dun pa dang rang bab kyi 'gros skyong ba gnad ltag par che/ yul snang gtan la dbab 'dod na/ snying gar hU~M dkar po dwangs gsal 'od 'phro ba bsgom/ rmi lam sgyu ma'i 'dun pa dang yul snang blta 'dod drag tu bya/ hU~M las 'od thag pa lta bu rgyangs kyi 'phros/ gang blta bar 'dod pa'i yul lam dngos po de 'od kyi zhags pas drangs nas snying ga'i hU~M la thim/ hU~M gi 'od kyis snang ba thams cad khra chem gyis gsal ba la sems gtad/ skabs 'dir bum can bsgom pa gal che/ sgyu lus rmi lam gyi dge sbyor skye ba la bsags rgyab yod pa zhig dgos te/ ma zin 'byams dang gol sa gsum/ / bsod nams tshogs kyis bcad par bya/ / zhes 'byung ngo / ! /

Recognizing dreams is the same as in the main course of instruction. Meditate three times in succession on the Vital Points of the Four Empowerments of Drops for self-recognition. After that, train with intense intentionality in the unreal nature of yourself and others, the environment and its inhabitants, enemies and friends, all enjoyments, and so forth. Within that state, settle without fabrication in whatever arises. Familiarize yourself with that again and again. Refining dreams is also the same as explained before, with the most important vital points to continue the mode of intentionality in illusion-like nature and natural repose. If you wish to ascertain objective appearances, meditate on a bright clear white hūṃ in your heart that radiates light. Rigorously cultivate the intentionality that all is dream and illusion and your desire to see the appearance of a place. Light radiates from the hūṃ, extending out like a rope. It snares whatever place or thing you wish to see and pulls it in and dissolves it into the hūṃ at your heart. The light from the hūṃ illuminates all appearance with shimmering radiance. Focus your attention there. During this practice, it is important to meditate with vase breathing. To develop the applied virtue from Illusory Body and Dream, you need the accumulation of merit as a support. As was said: Cultivation of merit cuts through these three: nonrecognition, proliferation, and deviation.[7]
'od gsal la/
D. Lucid Clarity

gong bshad de dmigs pa'i mthil yin mod/ des cis kyang ma zin na rno khyad ni/ lus nang dbu ma'i mar sner a dkar po bsam/ steng rlung nan nan/ 'og rlung 'then 'then byas pas (230) a de gsang ba'i rtsa bar lhan lhan song / gsang ba'i rtsa lam nas dkyus kyog kyog pa'i ngang nor bu'i nang du kha dog sngon po 'od 'tsher ba zhig tu gyur/ mgo nang bstan tu log / shugs drag pos phyi la 'gro tshad pa la bu ga dogs por ma shong bas lhan lhan 'dug pa la sems yud cig drag tu gtad/ yang de ka'i snang ba ma 'gag tsam la gtad de bzhag / de nyid yang yang bsgom/ 'di bud med kyis bsgom na dbu ma'i mar sne lte 'og sor brgyad tsam du sleb pa'i mar sne de la bsgom/ gzhan 'dra/ 'dzin pa la lhag par zab po/ ! /

Although what was explained before is the fundamental visualization, if you cannot grasp lucid clarity no matter what you do, the following is especially potent. Imagine a white A at the lower end of the central channel inside your body. Press down continually on the upper winds and continually draw the lower winds, until the A falls steadily down to the base of the perineum. {230} It winds its way, constantly twisting, through the genital channel, and when it reaches the inside of the gem (glans), it becomes a brilliant blue color. The head [of the syllable] turns back and faces inward. It tries to force its way out with great strength, but it cannot fit through the hole (urethra) and remains there steadily. Focus intently on that for a moment. Again, rest there in startled wonderment, merely not blocking that appearance. Meditate on that again and again. For women, meditate on the lower end of the central channel that reaches eight finger-widths below the navel. The rest is the same. This method of grasping lucid clarity is especially profound.
'pho ba ni/
E. Transference

lus nang dbu ma dkar po'i mar sner a dkar po/ / spyi bo'i tshangs bug had por yod par bsgom/ rlung phyir 'bud pa dang lhan cig lte 'og sor bzhi'i a de dbu ma'i lam dang tshangs bug brgyud/ nam mkha'i dbus su mda' 'phangs pa bzhin tu song nas dbyings su yal/ cung zad mnyam par bzhag / yang a de nam mkhar byung ba tshangs bug nas babs te dbu ma'i mar sner phyin par bsam/ 'di la 'gro 'ong spel ma bsgom pa las sgo dgag pa sogs mi dgos gsungs/ 'di la'ang 'chug med mkha' spyod dam/ ye shes skar khungs ma sngon tu 'gro dgos pa shes par bya'o/ ! /

Meditate on a white A in the lower end of the white central channel within your body and visualize that the cranial aperture is wide open. At the same time as you exhale the breath, the A that is four finger-widths below the navel travels up the central channel to the cranial aperture. It shoots out into the sky like an arrow and vanishes in the expanse. Rest for a bit in equipoise. Imagine that the A reappears in the sky and falls down through your cranial aperture and down to the lower end of the central channel. It is taught that you needn’t meditate on blocking the door [of the cranial aperture] and so on but just the alternating of [consciousness] going up and coming down. You should know, however, that the practices of Transference to the Unerring Celestial Realm or the Skylight of Timeless Awareness should precede this practice.
F.
F. Intermediate State

bar do'i skabs gong gsal gzhung khrid ltar las/ chags sdang gi yul chos 'byung nang du lhar gsal ba'i skor de mi bya bar/ 'gro ba rigs drug gi gnas dang / gzugs sgra dri ro reg bya bzang ngan thams cad la sgyu ma dang bar do'i 'dun pa sbyang / mngal sgong gi gnyis sbyor sogs gsal gdab/ bar do'i 'dun pas yi dam yab yum du bsgyur/ (231) de'ang sgyu mar shes pas zhen med kyi ngang skyong bar bya'o/ /

The section on the Intermediate State was clarified earlier according to the source guidebook. However, here you do not do the cycle of visualizing the objects of desire and anger within the source of phenomena as deities. Train with the intentionality that the abodes of the six kinds of migrators and all good and bad form, sound, smell, taste, and texture is an illusion and the intermediate state. Visualize the intercourse that results in womb birth, egg birth, and so on, and transform that into the yidam couple’s union by the intentionality of the intermediate state. {231} By knowing that to be illusion, maintain the state of nonattachment.
[Conclusion]

de ltar chos drug stan thog gcig tu nyams su len tshul zhal rgyun ma chad pa dang / byin rlabs bka' bab kyi gdams pa 'ga' zhig ye shes kyi mkha' 'gros rje btsun kun dga' grol mchog la dngos su stsal ba'i nye brgyud ches zab pa bcas smos zin to/ / 'di nyid la rtags thon rang byed na khrid chen rgyas pa dmigs rkang re bdun ma'am/ 'bring po dmigs rkang bcu bdun ma tsam la rtsa bar bzung / dmigs pa bka' rgya ma'i rigs rnams skabs dang bstun te len/ nyams myong gi sne zin nas 'dir bstan tsam gyis chog shes par byas na shin tu legs shing / 'dir bstan ma bu gnyis la'ang gnad thams cad tshang bar yod pas nyams len nus na 'di tsam gyis kyang dgos don 'grub par yod/ yang sgyu lus rmi lam kho na lta bu khol 'don sgro na de dag stan thog gcig ma zur du 'byung ba las shes par bya'o/ /

This extremely profound way of practicing the Six Dharmas in a Single Sitting comes from the uninterrupted oral teachings and some instructions of the blessing transmission that were actually taught by Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness in a direct lineage to Venerable Kunga Drolchok.[8] If you practice this until actual signs of success appear, take as your main source the extensive big guide with sixty-seven basic visualizations or the medium guide that has only seventeen visualizations.[9] Practice the visualizations from the class of sealed precepts as circumstances permit. Once you get a taste of meditative experience, it is really good to be content with just what has been presented here. Since all the vital points are contained here, both mother and child [versions], if you are able to put them into practice, you will accomplish your purpose with just this much. Also, if you are interested in extracting something like just the Illusory Body or Dream practices, you should learn them separately from the single-sitting practices.
thams cad la spyir gces pa'i gnad du/
General Valuable Vital Points on Everything

rtsa ba'i bla ma dkon mchog rtsa gsum kun 'dus/ yan lag gi bla ma gzhan thams cad de'i rnam 'phrul du shes pas sangs rgyas las kyang lhag pa'i mos gus ltem rkyang med pa ni spyir gsang sngags lam gyi srog rtsa med thabs med cing / khyad par dpal ldan rmog lcog pa'i zhal nas/ 'od gsal gtan la 'bebs pa sgyu ma/ sgyu ma gtan la 'bebs pa rmi lam/ rmi lam gtan la 'bebs pa dad 'dun/ dad 'dun ston byed bla ma/ des na rtsa ba'i bla ma la thams cad rag las par gsungs pas thabs lam skyong ba la shin tu gal che ba des go nus shing /

Your root guru is the union of the Three Jewels and Three Roots. Know that all other adjunct gurus are manifestations of that root guru. In general, the unshakable devotion that sees your guru as superior to even the Buddha is the indispensable life support of the path of Secret Mantra. In particular, as glorious Mokchokpa said: Illusory Body ascertains Lucid Clarity. Dream ascertains Illusory Body. Faith and intention ascertain Dream. The teacher of faith and intention is the guru. Therefore, everything depends on the root guru.[10] We can understand how important this is for maintaining the path of methods.

rang sems stong pa chos sku/ snang ba sprul sku/ dbyer med rang rig rang gsal longs (232) skur shes pas nyin mtshan kun tu ma yengs dran pa'i rtsis bzung nas lam du khyer/ de'i ngang du rlung bum can nam/ 'jam rlung ngam bar rlung ci nus 'bad pas gsal stong bde stong du shar ba kun sgyu ma lta bur shes shing / de'ang 'dzin med phyag rgya chen po'i ngang du bzhag ste mnyam bzhag gi nyams len rjes thob spyod lam thams cad dang bsres bas myur du brtan pa thob par 'gyur la/ rtag tu kun byang sems mi nyams pa dang / rnam rtog tha mal du mi 'chor ba'ang rnal 'byor pa'i dam tshig go /

That and to integrate it on the path by apprizing the unwavering recollection that your own mind’s emptiness is dharmakāya, appearance is nirmāṇakāya, and their inseparable innate awareness and innate clarity is saṃbhogakāya. {232} Within that state, exert yourself in whatever breathing practices you can—vase breathing, gentle breathing, or intermediate breathing. Know that what arises from that—the clarity-emptiness or bliss-emptiness—is all like an illusion. Rest without fixation in the state of mahāmudrā. By blending these experiences of resting in equipoise with all activities in postmeditation attainment, they will quickly become stabilized. Always avoid loss of kunda bodhicitta, and do not get lost in ordinary thinking—these are the yogin’s sacred pledges.

de ltar bsgoms pas lus ngag yid kyi nyams 'jam rtsub mtho dman bde sdug ji ltar byung yang dga' sdug spang blang re dogs med par sgyu ma rmi lam du shes nas byung rgyal du bskyang ba ni gegs sel gyi mchog yin zhing / dge sbyor legs par skyes pa sogs bzang ngan ci byung bla ma'i thugs rje kho nar shes pas gsol 'debs mos gus kho na la lam gyi gzhi 'cha' ba dang / ma rtogs pa'i sems can ris med pa la byams snying rje 'ba' zhig bskyed pa'i pan sems kyis dus 'da' ba ni bogs 'don dang 'gro don gyi rtsa ba'o/ /

By meditating in that way, whatever experiences arise in body, speech, or mind—gentle or rough, high or low, happy or sad—you understand to be illusion and dream without pleasure or displeasure, rejecting or accepting, hopes and fears. Then maintain that flexibility. This is the supreme dispelling of obstructions. Know that whatever good or bad thing happens, such as progress in your practice of virtue, is exclusively the guru’s compassion. Make supplication and devotion the sole foundation of your path. Pass the time with an altruistic mind that generates nothing but loving-kindness and compassion without bias toward all sentient beings who lack realization. This is the root of enhancement practices and the welfare of migrators.

de ltar bsgoms pas ji zhig na ched gtad kyi rtsol ba ma byas par sems bde gsal mi rtog pa'i 'od gsal mtha' dbus med par rang shar ba dang / bskyed 'dod kyi blo mngon 'gyur ba med bzhin tu lha sku'i snang ba gsal dwangs wa ler shar ba ni sgyu lus kyi lha sku rang shar zhes bya ste zab gsal dbyer med 'phags pa'i mngon rtogs dang chos mtshungs pa'o/ /

Through meditating in such a way, at some point, without making any effort on purpose, the lucid clarity of mental bliss, clarity, and nonthought will arise by itself without center or boundaries. That and the appearance of the clear radiant deity’s form will arise suddenly without any actual idea of wanting to create it. This is called the natural arising of the deity’s form of illusory body. This inseparability of profundity and clarity has equivalent qualities to the clear realization of the noble ones.

gzhan yang mkhas grub khyung yo'i zhal nas/ sgyu lus rmi lam la sogs pa'i chos 'di rnams nyams su len tsa na/ rmi lam mi 'tsham pa dang / DA kis gzugs sna tshogs su bsgyur nas ltas dang cho (233) 'phrul sna tshogs ston tu 'ong bas de la 'jigs mi dgos/ lar dus dang rnam pa thams cad du nga rang gis byin gyis brlab pa yin gsungs/ dbon ston skyer sgang pa la yi dam lhas gdams ngag gi gnas bsdus su stsal ba/

Furthermore, Khedrup Khyungpo Naljor said: Once you practice just these dharmas, such as Illusory Body, Dream, and so forth, you don’t need to be afraid of oppressive dreams, or the omens from various ḍākinī transformations, {233} or the various displays of apparitions that will come. You will have my blessings at all times and situations.[11] The yidam deity [Tārā] gave these concise instructions to Öntön Kyergangpa:
sgyu lus bden med gnad yin a 'thas bshigs/ / rmi lam 'dun pa'i gnad yin lam du khyer/ / 'od gsal mos gus gnad yin gsol bas thob/ / gzhan don snying rje'i gnad yin phyogs 'dzin spongs/ /

The vital point of Illusory Body is its lack of reality; destroy reification. The vital point of Dream is intentionality; integrate it on the path. The vital point of Lucid Clarity is devotion; attain it through prayer. The vital point of altruism is compassion; renounce prejudice.[12]

zhes pa'i gnad bzhi la gdams ngag gi rkang thams cad tshang zhing / 'gro 'dug / 'pho bskyas/ blo sna/ log lta mang po ste dge sbyor gyi sad bzhi la ma bskur ba nyams su blang na da lta dus snyig cing bstan pa'i gzugs brnyan tu gyur pa'i stobs kyis gzhung nas bshad tshod kyi mngon rtags chos phal cher la 'byung dka' yang / 'dir ni ye shes mkha' 'gro rnam pa gnyis kyis slob ma yang slob brgyud pa dang bcas pa rnams la thugs rjes bzung zhing / dag pa bde stong gi mkha' spyod du 'khrid pa khyung po nyid la lung bstan zhing / khyung po nyid kyis kyang /

These four vital points cover all the bases of instructions. Put them into practice without carrying the four frosts [that damage] applied virtue: movement, changing residences, many plans, and perverse views.[13] Now in this time of degenerations, it is mostly difficult for the signs of success to manifest as described in the source texts due to the influence of the doctrine having become a mere reflection [of its former state]. Nevertheless, if you practice in this case, there is a prophecy given by the two ḍākinīs of timeless awareness to Khyungpo Naljor that they will nurture with compassion his disciples and later lineage disciples and lead them to the celestial realm of pure empty bliss. And Khyungpo himself said:

nga las lhag pa nam yang med de nga dang mnyam pa'ang med la/ bdag gi brgyud 'dzin thams cad kyang kun las khyad par 'phags pas na/ bsags pa yang rab 'ba' zhig 'byung bar 'gyur ro zhes bden par gsungs pa ltar/ brgyud pa'i bla ma rin chen rnam lnga sogs phal mo che skye ba gcig gis thogs pa'i byang sems mthong thos dran reg thams cad ngan song las skyob nus par lung bstan thob cing chos brgyud ma chad bar du nyams rtogs skye bar byin gyis rlob pa grub thob so sos zhal gyis bzhes la/ bdag gi bla ma grub pa'i dbang po karma gzhan (234) phan 'od zer yan chad chos drug gi nyams myong gzhung nas bshad chod skyes shing / yi dam lha'i zhal mthong / bden gnyis dbyer med kyi rtogs pa mngon tu gyur pa tshig rkyang gi bshad sgros gtsang gtsang tsam ma yin pa blo gtad thub pa'i gdams ngag byin rlabs kyi drod ma yal ba yin/

There will never be someone better than I, or even someone equal. Also, all those who hold my lineage will be preeminent among all others, so it will consist only of those with excellent cultivation.[14] He spoke the truth. The gurus of this lineage, such as the five precious ones, were mostly in their last lives as bodhisattvas. They had received prophecies concerning their ability to provide refuge from the lower realms through all contact such as seeing, hearing, recalling, or touching them. Each of those adepts promised their blessings for experiential realization for as long as the lineage remained unbroken. {234} My teacher, the master of adepts Karma Zhenpen Özer,[15] and those before him developed the experiences of the Six Dharmas exactly as described in the source texts. They saw the yidam deities and actualized the realization of the two inseparable truths. This is not just a pseudo-pure manner of explanation by mere words. These are instructions that one can believe in; the warmth of their blessings has not dissipated.

spyir yang nyams su len pa lta ci smos/ dad pas mthong ba'am lan cig thos pa tsam gyis kyang mchog thun mong gi dngos grub 'byung bar the tshom med pa/ nyes pa'i skyon dang bral zhing legs pa'i yon tan rdzogs pa/ lo zla tsam gyis 'tshang rgya nges ba'i gser chos gcig brgyud ma zhes brgyud pa nas brgyud par bsngags pa yin te/ grub chen khyung po'i zhal nas/

In general, there is no doubt that supreme and common spiritual powers will be attained just by hearing once or seeing with faith these teachings, not to mention actually putting them into practice. Free of faults, full of qualities, and certain to bring awakening in a matter of months or years, the Golden Dharmas of the single lineage is praised as transmission from lineage [master] to lineage [master]. The great adept Khyungpo stated:

nga'i gdams ngag 'di gzhan las khyad par 'phags/ mgo byin na mgos phan thogs/ bar byin na bar gyis phan thogs/ gsham byin na gsham gyis phan thogs pa yin pas the tshom yid gnyis ma byed par brtson 'grus chen pos nyams su longs shig / bla ma sangs rgyas dngos las zhus pa/ DA ki dngos su 'du ba/ yon tan dngos su skye ba/ brgyud pa'i bka' babs dang ldan pa/ DA ki'i byin rlabs dang ldan pa/ gdams ngag gi nus pa dang ldan pa 'di nyams su longs shig / dbang po rab rnam smin/ 'bring bag chags/ tha ma yang bar dor 'tshang mi rgya mi srid pa yin no/ / bdag gis bka' babs dang gdams ngag gi gnad 'di lta bu rgya bod gang na'ang med par thag chod pa yin no/ /

These instructions of mine are superior to others. Given at the beginning, they are helpful from the start. Given in the middle, they are helpful along the way. Given in the end, they are helpful to conclude. Therefore practice them with great diligence without doubt or a conflicted mind. They were received from the guru, the actual Buddha. They attract the actual ḍākinīs. Real qualities arise. They possess the transmission of the lineage. They have the ḍākinīs’ blessings. They are replete with the power of instructions. Practice them! Those with the best faculties will awaken in the fully ripened body, the average in the body of habitual patterns, and the least in the intermediate state—it’s impossible not to get enlightened. I am sure that there is nothing like my transmission legacy and vital instructions in all of India or Tibet.[16]

zhes sogs yang yang bsngags shing grub mtha' ris med pas bsngags pa'i me tog 'thor bas grags pa'i ba dan srid rtser bsnyegs bzhin pa lags mod/ brgyud pa mar la bab pa na gser chos 'di rnams yang na bka' chad/ yang na (235) tshong 'dus kyi 'o ma bzhin tu 'gro bar lung gis bstan pa mngon tu gyur te ltar snang dang bslad can mang pos gzugs brnyan tu gyur pa na/ grol mchog zhabs la nye brgyud kyi bka' babs shing kun mkhyen sgrol ba'i mgon pos man ngag bar ma chad pa'i gnad dang 'khrul med ye shes kyi gzigs pas rin chen rnam bdun gyi dgongs pa phyin ci ma log par gsal bar mdzad pa'i snying po ni 'di kho na'o/ /

He praised them again and again in this way, and impartial adherents of other schools also strew the flowers of praise, raising the banner of fame to the pinnacle of existence. However, it was predicted that when the lineage passed down, these Golden Dharmas would either be interrupted or become watered down like milk sold in the market. {235} This is what has happened. Many imitations and corrupted versions have turned it into a mere reflection. The legacy of the direct lineage fell to Kunga Drolchok and hence to Omniscient Drolwai Gönpo [Tāranātha], who saw with timeless awareness the vital points of the uninterrupted esoteric instructions and so illuminated without deviation the intentions of the Seven Jewels. This is only the essence of that.
[Concluding Verses and Colophon]
shin tu snyigs mar gyur na yang / / gser chos 'di 'dzin grub brnyes kyis/ / rjes su bzung ba skal pa bzang / / yon tan bsam gyin dang re spro/ /
Though it is a very degenerate time, adepts who preserve this Golden Dharma have taken me in. What good fortune! Thinking of their qualities, I am full of faith.
'di bris nongs pa gang mchis pa/ / bla ma sangs rgyas spyan sdar bshags/ / nyams su mi len kha khyer bas/ / spyad na DA ki'i chad pa 'byung / /
Whatever mistakes I’ve made in writing this, I confess before the guru, the Buddha. To engage with mere words and no practice will incur the ḍākinīs’ punishment.
'di mthong thos dang dran pa yang / / bde chen zhing du brdzus skyes te/ / grub chen khyung po yab sras kyis/ / rjes bzung mkha' spyod che 'grub shog /
May seeing, hearing, or recalling this beget miraculous birth in the realm of great bliss. Held by the great adept Khyungpo and his spiritual heirs, may we attain the great celestial realm.

ces pa 'di'ang rdo rje slob dpon chen po'i go 'phang gdod nas grub pa 'jigs bral mkhyen brtse'i 'od zer can gyis snga phyir bka' stsal gnang ba ltar/ khyung rigs su skyes shing shangs chos la mos pas spyod pa yon tan rgya mtshos dpal spungs yang khrod bde chen 'od gsal gling du DA ki 'du ba'i dus tshes grub sbyor dang ldan pa'i snga char grub par bgyis pa dpal ldan shangs pa'i bka' brgyud sa steng khyab pa'i rgyur gyur cig / dge legs 'phel// // (336) (237)

I, Yönten Gyatso, born into the Khyung clan and engaged with interest in the Shangpa teachings, composed this text according to the earlier and later teachings that were given by the fearless, wise, and loving one with light rays, [Jamyang Khyentsé Wangpo], who attained primordially the state of a great vajra master. It was completed at Palpung Monastery, at the isolated retreat Dechen Ösal Ling, on the morning of the day of the ḍākinīs’ gathering, a time of auspicious astrological conjunctions. May it be the cause for the glorious Shangpa Kagyu to spread all over the earth.
@#/ /phyag chen ga'u ma'am rang babs rnam gsum zhes bya ba'i khrid yig bzhugs so/ /
10. Amulet Mahāmudrā or Three Naturally Settled States Guidance Manual[1]
(238)@#/ /na mo gu ru we/ /
namo gurave

phyag rgya chen po ga'u ma'am rang babs rnam gsum zhes bya ba/ ye shes mkha' 'gro ni gu ma'i gdams ngag 'di la/ khrid kyi sngon 'gro dal 'byor rnyed dka'/ mi rtag pa/ sdug bsngal sogs spyi dang mthun/ skyabs 'gro sems bskyed dang / a yi stong ra rnams ni gu chos drug dang 'dra/ thun gyi sngon 'gro bla ma'i rnal 'byor ni/ gzhan sgyu lus dang 'dra ba las maN+Dal mang du 'bul/ bdag 'dzin blo yis thongs bar mdzad du gsol/ dgos med rgyud la skye bar mdzad du gsol/ 'od gsal phyag rgya chen po rtogs par mdzad du gsol/ zhes pa khyad par ro/ /

Amulet Mahāmudrā or Three Naturally Settled States, is an instruction of Niguma, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness. The preliminaries of this guidance, such as contemplations on the difficulty in attaining a free and endowed human birth, impermanence, suffering, and so on, are the same as the standard versions. Going for refuge, arousing the awakening mind, and the Purifying A of Inner Space are the same as in the Six Dharmas. The preliminary to individual sessions is guru yoga. This is otherwise the same as in Illusory Body practice, except that many mandalas are offered and the supplication to recite is: [Precious guru, unified essence of all buddhas of the three times, for the sake of all sentient beings, I supplicate you] that I may relinquish self-fixation, that I may have no needs, that I may realize Lucid Clarity Mahāmudrā.
I.
I. Actual Guidance
khrid dngos la/ sngon 'gro rang babs rnam gsum/ dngos gzhi skyon bzhi rang grol/ rjes sku gsum rang shar gyi khrid do/ /

The actual guidance has three parts: (1) the preliminary, Three Naturally Settled States; (2) the main practice, Naturally Free of Four Faults; and (3) the conclusion, the Naturally Arising Three Kāyas.
dang po
A. The Preliminary, Three Naturally Settled States
['di] la zhi gnas gyi khrid dang / lhag mthong gi khrid gnyis/
This has two parts: (1) the guidance on calm abiding and (2) the guidance on higher insight.
dang po
1. Calm Abiding
['di] la dmigs pa'i gzhi dang / bogs 'don no/ /
This has two parts: (1) the basic visualization and (2) the enhancement.
dang po ni/
a. Basic Visualization
Visualization Round 1

sngar sgo gsum gyi bya ba thams cad (239) don med la dor song 'dug pas/ da phyin chad sgom la brtan pa cung zad cig ma skyes bar mi dge ba dang / lung ma bstan lta ci smos/ spros bcas dge ba yang rtsol ba glod/ lus rnam snang gi chos bdun/ ngag rlung ro lan gsum bsal nas smra brjod lta ci smos rlung 'dzin 'dren tsam yang spong ba'i rang babs/ sems ma bcos pa lhod de glod/ dmigs skor gcig /

You have already abandoned all meaningless activities of body, speech, and mind. {239} From now on, until you have attained a modicum of stability in your meditation, relax your efforts toward intentional virtue, not to mention unvirtuous and neutral acts. Physically, assume the seven-point posture of Vairocana. Verbally, after clearing out the dead air three times, give up even doing breathing exercises, let alone talking, and remain in a settled state. Relax your mind without contrivance. That is the first round of contemplation.
Visualization Round 2
rnam rtog sna tshogs 'phro na lam gyis skyes pa la ngo shes/ 'phro rbad kyis bcad la bzhag / dmigs skor gnyis/
When various discursive thoughts proliferate, recognize them right away, abruptly cut them off, and then settle.
Visualization Round 3

'og 'gyu rgya 'byams su 'gro na/ nam dran dus phyin chad 'di 'dra gtan nas ma byung ba byed snyam zhe dam bya/ rnam rtog byung tsa na dran cing ngo shes pa byed snyam pa byas pas sel te/ dmigs skor gsum/

If the undercurrent of thought becomes excessive, as soon as you become aware of it, promise yourself that from now on, nothing like this will ever happen again. Your resolution to be mindful in recognizing thoughts as they arise will clear this up.
Visualization Round 4

de dus shes pa mi gsal bar song / brjed ngas kyang cher 'gro na bying ba'i skyon yin/ rig pa bsgrim/ mig dpangs gtod/ mthongs dkar ba dang yang thog la sogs par bsgom/ bying ba 'phro bcad de langs ba sogs byed/ (240) yang tshig pa za zhing sbun langs na rgod pa yin pas lhod kyis glod/ lta stangs smad/ 'dod yon la dga' bas sems g.yengs na/ mi rtag sdug bsngal la yid 'byung bar bya ste dmigs skor bzhi pa'o/ /

At that time, if your consciousness becomes unclear and forgetfulness increases, this is the fault of dullness (bying ba). Tighten your awareness, turn your eyes upward, and meditate in open places or on rooftops. Standing up and so forth will eliminate dullness. {240} If you become irritable or restless, it is [the fault of] agitation (rgod pa). You should relax and gaze downward. If your mind is distracted by the pleasures of the senses, develop detachment by recollecting impermanence and suffering.
gnyis pa
b. Enhancement
['di] la lta stangs nges med la bslab pa/ chos spyod sna tshogs la bslab pa/ spyod lam sna tshogs dang bsre ba'o/ /
This has three parts: (1) training with indefinite gazes, (2) training with various dharma activities, and (3) training with various activities.
dang po ni/
i. Training with Indefinite Gazes
Visualization Round 5
mig gi lta stangs mtho ba thag nye ba thog mthil lta bu dang / ring ba ri rtse'am nam mkha'i dbyings lta bu la mnyam par bzhag ste dmigs skor lnga/
Gaze with your eyes high and nearby, such as at the center of the ceiling, or far away, such as at the top of a mountain or the expanse of the sky, and rest in equipoise.
Visualization Round 6
dma' ba nye brtsig 'khris sam ring ba ri rtsib lta bu la mnyam par bzhag ste dmigs skor drug pa'o/ /
Gaze down and nearby, such as at the bottom of a wall, or far away, such as at the base of a mountain, and rest in equipoise.
Visualization Round 7
thad ka nye ba gyang ldan nam ring ba ri ldan lta bu la mnyam par bzhag ste dmigs skor bdun pa'o/ /
Gaze straight ahead at something close, like a wall, or distant, like a mountain scape, and rest in equipoise.
gnyis pa ni/
ii. Training with Various Dharma Activities
Visualization Round 8

mdo 'don/ sngags zlos/ gtam sna tshogs dang bsre zhes ba'i don mdo la sogs pa kha ton byang ba rnams dang thog mar bsre/ rim gyis kha ton thams cad dang bsre gang thub bya ste dmigs skor brgyad pa'o/ /

It is said, “Blend with reciting sutras, repeating mantras, and various conversations.” That is, at first blend with the recitation of sutras and so forth with which you are familiar. Then gradually blend with all kinds of recitation as you are able.
Visualization Round 9
sngags thung ba rnams dang thog mar bsre/ de nas bzlas ba thams cad dang bsre ste dmigs skor dgu pa'o/ /
At first blend with short mantras, then blend with all recitation.
Visualization Round 10

dang por chu sgra sogs 'byung ba'i sgra dang bsre/ de nas mi mang po'i ca co dang sgo 'then sogs dang bsre/ de nas mi gzhan gyis gtam smra ba la bsres te de dag gi sgra lhang lhang ba der had de bzhag ste dmigs skor bcu pa'o/ /

At first, blend with the sounds of the elements, such as water. Then blend with many people chattering and doors shutting and so forth. Then blend with other people’s conversations. Rest with mindless openness on those vivid sounds.
gsum pa spyod lam sna tshogs la bslab ste/
iii. Training with Various Activities
Visualization Round 11

zas za na yang rang babs kyi ngang nas za/ lam du 'gro na yang de bzhin du sbyang / gtam smra na yang rang babs gyis ngang nas ma bral bar bya ste/ dang por sgrim mi dgos bar do gal chung ba rnams la sbyangs pas mthar thams cad la 'byongs pa yin no/ / de bzhin du bde sdug / dga' mi dga'/ yang bag tsha ngo tsha skyug bro sogs mtho dman (241) gyi rnam rtog skye ba'i yul thams cad la rang babs su bsres kyin sbyang / / thams cad kyang sngar ltar dge sbyor gyi ngang du tshud 'ong ste dmigs skor bcu gcig pa'o/ / de ltar na zhi gnas la dmigs skor bcu gcig go /

When eating, eat in a naturally settled state. When walking, also practice that way. Even when speaking, do not abandon that naturally settled state. At first, practice with less weighty subjects that don’t need much concentration. Eventually you can practice with everything. {241} Thus, whether pleasure, pain, joy, sorrow, fear, anxiety, disgust, and so forth—you will practice blending the naturally settled state with all objects that provoke high or low conceptual thoughts. Everything will be included within your previous practice of virtue.
gnyis pa
2. Higher Insight
[a. Preliminary]

lhag mthong gi khrid sems tshol ni/ bla ma'i zhal rgyun las rgyas par 'byung ba'i dbang du byas na/ dang po sngar bzhin rang babs gsum gnad du babs nas lhod kyi klod pa'i ngang nas 'tshol ba ni thams cad kyi sngon 'gro yin no/ /

The higher insight practice of seeking the mind [will be explained] from the point of view of the guru’s oral transmission, where it occurs in detail. First, after resting in the vital points of the aforementioned three naturally settled states, search from within a state of relaxation. This is the preliminary of every [higher insight practice].
[b. Main Practice]

dngos gzhi dmigs thun bdun te/ sems kyi ngo bo la 'tshol ba/ skye 'gag la 'tshol ba/ yul snang la 'tshol ba/ rnam rtog la 'tshol ba/ yul snang yod med kyi khyad par la 'tshol ba/ rnam rtog yod med kyi khyad par la 'tshol ba/ rang bzhin dbyings su thag bcad pa'o/ /

The main practice consists of seven visualization sessions: (1) searching for mind’s essence, (2) searching for its beginning and ending, (3) searching for objective appearances, (4) searching for conceptual thought, (5) searching for the difference between the existence or nonexistence of objective appearance, (6) searching for the difference between the existence or nonexistence of conceptual thought, and (7) gaining certitude in natural basic space.
dang po ni/
i. Searching for Mind’s Essence
Visualization Round 1
sems kyi ngo bo la che re lta zhing zhib tu gzhig pa 'jug pa ste/ der rtsol ba rang zhig la song nas 'di yin brjod du med pa'i nyams skyes pa na rang babs su 'jog ste dmigs skor gcig go /

Look fixedly at mind’s essence and begin a thorough investigation. Once your efforts have ceased of their own accord and you experience that there is no way to say, “This is it,” let go in the naturally settled state. That is the first round of contemplation.
gnyis pa ni/
ii. Searching for Its Beginning and Ending
Visualization Round 2

sems rtog med de kho na la bltas nas skye 'gag gtan mi byed pa'i rtag pa brtan pa zhig 'dug gam/ skye 'gag byed pa'i ci med cang med zhig 'dug / skye 'gag byed na ji ltar skye yin 'dug / gnas na ji ltar gnas/ kha dog dbyibs sogs ji lta bu/ phyi nang gang na 'dug / 'gag na ji ltar 'gag zhes sogs zhib tu brtags pa na/ ngos bzung med pa la zhi ste/ dmigs skor gnyis pa'o/ /

Look at mind only without concept. Is it something stable and permanent that never arises nor ceases? There is nothing at all that causes it to arise or cease. If nothing creates or stops it, how did it arise? When it abides, how does it abide? What is its color and shape? Where is the outside and inside? When it ceases, how does it cease? When you make these kind of analyses, there is no way to identify it. Peace!
gsum pa ni/
iii. Searching for Objective Appearances
Visualization Round 3

mig gis gzugs mthong na/ gzugs su lam mer mthong ba de ngo bo ji ltar 'dug blta/ / de dang sems rig rig tur tur 'di gcig gam/ tha dad khyad ci (242) 'dug zhib tu dpyad/ de bzhin rna bas sgra thos pa sogs la'ang sbyar te/ dmigs skor gsum pa'o/ /

When you see form with your eyes, look for the essence of that vivid sight of forms. Investigate carefully whether that is the same or different from mind’s keen sparkling awareness. {242} Apply the same process to sounds heard by the ears and so on.
bzhi pa ni/
iv. Searching for Conceptual Thought
Visualization Round 4

yang rnam rtog lam gyis 'char ba 'di dang sems kyi rang bzhin la khyad par cig 'dug / de gnyis gcig mi gcig brtag / rnam rtog skyes pa'i tshe ji ltar skye/ skyes nas ma 'gags pa'i skabs yod lugs ga 'dra zhig 'dug / 'gag tsa na 'gag lugs ci 'dra zhig 'dug zhib tu brtags te/ dmigs skor bzhi pa'o/ /

Again, is there a difference between this sudden arising of conceptual thought and the abiding nature of mind? Examine whether those two are the same or not. When thoughts arise, how do the arise? During the time from their arising until their ceasing, what is the manner of their existence? Once they cease, what is the manner of their cessation? Examine this closely.
lnga pa ni/
v. Searching for the Difference between the Existence or Nonexistence of Objective Appearance
Visualization Round 5
mig gis gzugs mthong ba'i dus kyi sems dang ma mthong ba'i dus kyi sems la khyad ci 'dra zhig 'dug / yod na yod lugs dang med na med lugs ji ltar yin brtags te/ dmigs skor lnga pa'o/ /

What is the difference between the mind at the time of seeing form with the eyes and the mind at the time of not seeing form? If that difference exists, examine how it exists, and if it does not exist, examine how it does not exist.
drug pa ni/
vi. Searching for the Difference between the Existence or Nonexistence of Conceptual Thought
Visualization Round 6

rnam rtog skyes pa'i dus kyi sems dang ma skyes pa'i dus kyi sems la bzang ngan gsal mi gsal stong mi stong khyad yod med legs par brtags/ 'tshol thabs de bzhi la'ang mthar dmigs gtad zhig pa zhig 'byung bas de kho na'i ngang bskyongs dmigs skor dgu pa'o/ /

Thoroughly investigate whether there is a difference in the quality, clarity, and emptiness of the mind when thoughts are present and the mind when they are absent. The end of those four methods of searching is the dissipation of the focus, so maintain solely that state.
bdun pa ni/
vii. Gaining Certitude in Natural Basic Space
Visualization Round 7

snang ba 'di thams cad rang gi sems su thag bcad/ sems la legs par brtags pa na ngos bzung ci yang med pa dang de kha'i ngang la bzhag / da rung mang du btsal bas/ ngos bzung med bzhin du ci med cang med kyang ma yin par stong bzhin du sna tshogs su 'char ba'i rig stong rjen ne ba/ wa le khyug ge ba/ hrig ger myong ba/ brjod mi shes pa de la cham gyis bzhag ste dmigs skor bdun pa'o/ /

All these appearances are definitely in your mind. When you examine the mind thoroughly, there is nothing to identify, and you settle within that very state. At this point, the lack of identification when you search a great deal is not that there is nothing at all; while empty, a variety arises. Empty awareness feels naked, vivid, bright, and sharp. Settle fully in that inexpressibility.
de ltar lhag mthong la bdun no/ /
These are the seven [methods] of higher insight.
sngon 'gro rang babs rnam gsum la dmigs skor bco brgyad do/ /
Thus there are eighteen rounds of contemplation in the preliminary practice of the Three Naturally Settled States.

khyung po'i bla ma ni gu mas sngon 'gro la gtso bor mdzad/ mai tri pas dngos gzhi la gtso bor mdzad/ su kha sid+d+hi yi rjes la gtso bor mdzad (243) gsungs te ngon 'gro'i skabs 'dir rtogs pa skye dgos so/ /

Khyungpo said that of his gurus, Niguma primarily created the preliminary, Maitrīpa primarily the main practice, and Sukhasiddhi primarily the concluding practices. {243} In this context of the preliminary practice, you should develop realization.
dngos gzhi la
B. The Main Practice: Naturally Free of Four Faults
[1. Preliminary]

thog mar byin rlabs kyi sgo nas brku thabs su ngo sprod pa ni/ maN+Dal chos 'byung mthing kha zhig bzhengs/ der many+dzi'i steng du gtor ma che ba la mda' dar btsugs shing rgyan bzang pos brgyan pa zhig bzhag / mdun du 'bul gtor dang mchod pa dang tshogs rdzas rnams bsham/ mchod pa byin rlabs spyi dang 'dra/ slob dpon rang gis bde mchog lhan skyes kyi mngon rtogs bsgoms la/ mdun bskyed maN+Dal dang gtor ma su m+b+has bsang / swa b+hA was sbyang / gtor chog ltar mgon por bskyed pa nas bzlas pa'i bar bya/

First is the burglar’s pointing-out method by means of the blessing [empowerment]. Construct a blue source of phenomena as the mandala. There, upon the mañji (tripod), place a large torma, stick in an arrow with silk attached, and adorn it with fine ornaments. In front, arrange offering tormas, general offerings, and feast substances. Consecrate them as usual. The ritual master meditates that he or she is Coemergent Cakrasaṃvara according to the visualization descriptions (mngon rtogs). Cleanse the mandala and tormas in front with sumbha…and purify with svabhāva…(etc.). Recite the torma ritual from the creation of the Protector through the [mantra] recitation.

de nas slob ma rnams la khrus dang me tog bkye bsdu sogs bya/ maN+Dal lan gsum phul la/ slob ma rnams la bde mchog lhan skyes kyi mngon rtogs phog la cung zad sems 'dzin du 'jug / mdun bskyed mgon por skad cig gis bsgom du bcug cing /

Then have the disciples wash. Distribute and collect the flowers and so forth. The disciples offer a mandala three times. Have them focus attention for a little while on themselves as Coemergent Cakrasaṃvara according to the visualization description. Then have them meditate instantly on the Protector in the front visualization.

steng gi cha la brgyud pa'i bla ma thams cad kyis bskor ba'i dbus su/ ye shes mkha' 'gro ni gu ma sku mdog smug nag DA ma ru dang thod pa kha TAM ga bsnams pa gar stabs dang rus pa'i rgyan can/ lang tsho dar la babs pa/ sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' yi dam dkyil 'khor gyi lha tshogs mkha' 'gro sde lnga mkha' 'gro ma bye ba 'bum sde'i tshogs dang bcas pa bzhugs par bsam/

Above the Protector, imagine the lineage gurus all around and in their midst is Awareness Ḍākinī Niguma. She is dark brown, holds a ḍamaru, skull cup, and khaṭvāṅga, and stands in the posture of dance, adorned by bone ornaments. She is in the prime of life. Imagine the presence of buddhas, bodhisattvas, hosts of mandala deities, and hosts of millions of ḍākinīs of the five families.
de rnams la dngos su bshams pa'i maN+Dal 'di nyid stong gsum gyi 'jig rten gyi khams su mos/ de gser gyis bkang zhing 'bul bar bsam/
Imagine that this actual mandala that has been prepared is the realms of the billionfold universe filled with gold, and think that it is offered to all the deities.

dpon slob rnams kyis lhan cig tu tshogs dang gtor ma byin gyis brlab/ byin rlabs kyi chog ni yi dam gang byed kyi nang mchod ltar byin (244) gyis brlab/ oM hriHha ha huM hU~M phaT kyi mthar/ oM a kA ro btags pas dang por bla ma dang yi dam la phul/ de nas gtor chog ltar mgon po 'khor bcas la phul/ oM sarba DA ki nI sa pa ri wA ra a kA ro sogs kyis mkha' 'gro ma la 'bul/

Master and disciples together consecrate the feast and tormas. For the consecration ritual, use the consecration according to the inner offering of any yidam practice. {244} Say oṃ hrīḥ ha ha hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ with oṃ akāro…(etc.) added to the end. First offer to the guru and yidam. Then offer to the Protector and retinue as in the torma ritual. Offer to the ḍākinīs with oṃ sarva ḍākinī saparivāra akāro…(etc.).

snyims pa me tog dang bcas pas gsol 'debs 'di'i rjes zlos mdzod {byas la}/ phyogs bcu na bzhugs pa'i sangs rgyas la skyabs su mchi'o/ / phyogs bcu na bzhugs pa'i chos la skyabs su mchi'o/ / phyogs bcu na bzhugs pa'i dge 'dun la skyabs su mchi'o/ / bla ma dang yi dam gyi lha tshogs ye shes kyi mgon po phyag drug pa'i lha tshogs 'khor dang bcas pa rnams la phyag 'tshal zhing skyabs su mchi'o/ / rtsa ba dang brgyud pa'i bla ma rnams dang yi dam gyi lha tshogs rnams kyis bdag la phyag rgya chen po'i rtogs pa ngo 'phrod par byin gyis brlab tu gsol/ / mkha' 'gro chos skyong ba'i srung ma rnams kyis bdag phyag rgya chen po zhu ba dang nyams su len pa la phyi nang gi bar du gcod pa gang yang mi 'byung bar mdzad du gsol/ / zhes lan gsum gyis gsol ba btab/

While they hold flowers in their joined palms, have the disciples repeat this supplication three times: “I go for refuge to the buddhas present in the ten directions. I go for refuge to the dharma present in the ten directions. I go for refuge to the sangha present in the ten directions. I pay homage and go for refuge to the guru, yidam deities, and Six-Armed Awareness Protector with his retinue of deities. Root and lineage gurus, hosts of yidam deities, please grant me your blessings to directly recognize the realization of mahāmudrā. Ḍākinīs, dharma protector guards: please prevent any outer or inner obstacles to my reception and practice of mahāmudrā.”

rtsa ba'i bla ma la mos gus dung pa byed du bcug / lus gnad bcas rlung rang babs su rgyu ru gzhug / bla ma yi dam mkha' 'gro'i tshogs dang bcas pa thams cad 'od du zhu nas slob ma rang nyid la thim par mos la dar cig lhod kyis glod nas/ sems kyi rang ngo la lhan ner ltos shig byas la yug cig mnyam par 'jog tu bcug / da lta sems ngos bzung thams cad dang bral ba/ rjen ne ye re ba 'di ka rang sems skye med chos sku'am/ tha mal shes pa'am rang babs zhes bya ba yin pas/ da phyin chad 'di ka mnyam rjes thams cad du bzo bcos med par skyongs shig byas/

Encourage [the disciples] to have yearning devotion to the root guru. Have them settle into the natural resting state of the winds with the vital points of physical posture. Then imagine that all the gurus, yidams, and ḍākinīs with their hosts melt into light and dissolve into the disciples themselves. Relax a moment in that. Then say: Look steadily at your own essence. Let them rest in equipoise for a while. The present mind is free of all identification. This naked vividness is itself unborn mind dharmakāya, also called ordinary mind or the naturally settled state. From now on, maintain just that without contrivance at all times during equipoise or subsequently. {245}
maN+Dal 'bul (245) ba dang smon lam btab pa sogs spyi dang mthun/ /
Do the mandala offerings, aspiration prayers, and so on as usual.
gnyis pa ni/
2. The Main Visualization

thun gyi sngon 'gro sngar ltar la/ gnas 'gyu thams cad du dran pas zin pa zhig bya'o/ / zhes yang yang 'dun pa byas nas/ dmigs pa'i dngos gzhi la sems gnas pa'i tshe/ kha nang log tu rang ngo shes pa tsam byas nas/ bzo bcos med pa'i tshul du bzhag / yul snang gi 'char sgo'am/ rnam rtog gi 'char sgo ci byung yang ched gtad dgag sgrub blang dor mi bya bar gang shar de rang ngo shes tsam gyi ngang la mnyam par bzhag pas rnam rtog kho rang ma 'gags bzhin du gsal sing nge ba de'i ngang bskyang / ngo mi shes su gcig kyang ma shor bar bya/ ngo shes dang ma bral phyin chad 'gyu na'ang 'gyu ru bcug / rang log tu 'gro na'ang 'gro ru bcug dran pa la ched gtad du 'bad/ 'di la bsgom du rdul tsam med/ yengs su skad cig kyang med ces bya/ de nyid la skyon bzhi rang grol bar ngo sprad de/ nye drags pas ngo ma shes/ zab drags pas ngos ma zin/ sla drags pas yid ma ches/ bzang drags pas blor ma shong zhes pa'i skyon bzhi las grol ba ste/

The preliminary for the session is as above. Again and again set the intention with “I will recognize with attention all mental stillness and movement.” For the main focus, when mind abides, turn inward and just recognize that. Rest in an uncontrived way. Whatever perceptions of objective appearance or discursive thought occur, don’t particularly pay attention; neither deny nor affirm, accept nor reject. Whatever arises, rest evenly in the mere recognition of it. While not blocking the thought itself, maintain that state of wakefulness. But do not get lost in nonrecognition at all. With constant recognition, from then on when there is mental movement, let it move. If it gets away, let it go. Particularly strive at mindfulness. This is “not an iota of meditation, not a moment of distraction.” This itself is the introduction to natural freedom from the four faults: Too close to recognize. Too profound to grasp. Too easy to believe. Too excellent to comprehend.[2]

dang po ni rang ngo ma shes pa/ gnyis pa ni/ sngar 'chi ba dang shugs chad kyi nyams la sogs pa'i dus su tha mal shes pa rang ngo gsal bar ston pa mang du byung mod kyang / bla ma'i gdams ngag gis ngo ma sprad pa de srid thabs gang gis kyang ma shes pa'o/ / gsum pa ni/ mkhas rmongs thams cad bya ra med la blos ma khel ba'o/ / bzhi pa ni/ sems kyi rang bzhin sangs rgyas yin pa blor ma shong pa'o/ /

The first fault is the lack of self-recognition. The second is that, although our ordinary mind reveals itself on multiple occasions—such as during our previous death or the experience of physical exhaustion—it was not introduced by our guru’s instructions and it cannot be known by any other means. The third is that given the lack of anything to be done by anyone, smart or stupid, we cannot trust it intellectually. The fourth is that we simply cannot comprehend the fact that our mind’s intrinsic nature is that of a buddha.

de la gnas 'gyu thams cad rang ngo shes tsam na rang bzhin stong gsal du 'dug / des na gang shar la bzo bcos byed don med/ rang bzhin gsal (246) stong 'di las logs su 'khor 'das gang yang med par shes tshe skyon de bzhi rang grol ba yin/ /

When you merely recognize all [thought] that moves or abides, there is natural empty clarity. Therefore, it is meaningless to alter or fabricate whatever arises. {246} When you understand that there is nothing whatsoever in all cyclic existence and its transcendence apart from this intrinsic nature of clarity and emptiness, those faults are naturally liberated.
gsum pa rjes sku gsum rang shar
C. The Conclusion: The Naturally Arising Three Kāyas
['di] la/ sku gsum rang shar ngo sprad pa dngos dang / de'i bogs 'don no/ /
This has two parts: (1) the actual introduction to the three kāyas and (2) its enhancement.
dang po ni/
1. Introduction to the Three Kāyas

sngar gyi tha mar shes pa ma bcos so ma de nyid sngon gdod ma nas gsal stong zung 'jug tu rang shar bar rang ngo shes pa nas stong pa chos kyi sku/ gsal ba sprul sku/ zung 'jug longs skur thag bcad nges shes bskyed nas rang babs de ka'i ngang du bskyang bar bya'o/ / de ltar nyams su myong ba'i tshe/ sems skad cig ma gcig kyang sku gsum du ngo 'phrod/ rnam rtog skad cig ma gcig kyang sku gsum gyi rang bzhin no/ / de ltar nyams myong du shar bar byas nas rtag tu skyong dgos pa yin no/ /

Once you self-recognize that the uncontrived freshness of your previous ordinary mind was always the naturally arisen unity of clarity and emptiness from the beginning, you can be certain that its emptiness is dharmakāya, its clarity is nirmāṇakāya, and their unity is saṃbhogakāya. Having engendered certitude, maintain that naturally settled state itself. When you have that felt experience, you recognize each moment of mind as the three kāyas, and each moment of thought as their intrinsic nature. Once you have that kind of experience, you must always maintain it.
gnyis pa
2. Enhancement
['di] la/ bogs 'don dang gegs sel gnyis las/
This has two parts: (1) enhancement and (2) dispelling obstructions.
dang po
a. Enhancement
['di] la mos gus tshad med la brten nas bogs 'don pa/ snying rje tshad med la brten nas bogs 'don pa/ thabs khyad par can la brten nas bogs 'don pa'o/ /
This has three parts: (1) enhancement based on immeasurable devotion, (2) enhancement based on immeasurable compassion, and (3) enhancement based on special methods.
dang po ni
i. Enhancement Based on Immeasurable Devotion

spyir rtogs pa skyes na mos gus shugs 'byung la 'byung / ma rtogs pa'i sems can la snying rje rang shugs kyis skye yang / de la slar yang mos gus dang snying rje bsgom pas me 'bar ba la shing gcer ba bzhin du cher 'phel te lam gyi bogs 'don bla na med par 'gyur ba yin no/ / de ltar yang yang lam phyag rgya chen po bsgom bzhin du mos gus dang snying rje drag tu bsgoms pas mthar thug rtogs pa'i thabs su 'gyur ro/ /

Generally, devotion arises automatically when realization is born and compassion arises naturally for sentient beings who do not have that realization. Nonetheless, to meditate again on devotion and compassion is like adding dry wood to the fire—it increases greatly and becomes an incomparable enhancement of the path. Meditating intensely on devotion and compassion while repeatedly meditating on path mahāmudrā becomes the means to realize the ultimate.

de yang mos gus ni spyir rtsa ba'i bla ma de nyid sangs rgyas dngos yin pa dang / thugs chos kyi sku mdzad spyod phrin las thams cad gzhan don gzugs sku rnam gnyis sangs rgyas byang sems yi dam mkha' 'gro chos skyong (247) thams cad 'dus pa 'ong ba yin par thag gcod/ bdag gnas lugs la dkri bar mdzad pas bka' drin che/ bka' drin la nam yang 'khor ba med snyam pa mos gus kyi gdung shugs drag pos gsol ba rtse gcig tu 'debs/ bla ma'i mos gus kyis yid bsgyur bas rang bzhin spros bral gyi ye shes lhag ger shar ba na/ de kha'i ngang du mnyam par bzhag /

In general, devotion (mos gus) means decisively regarding your root guru as the real buddha, their mind as dharmakāya, all their conduct and awakened activities as the two form kāyas at work for the benefit of others, and their essence as the embodiment of all buddhas, bodhisattvas, yidams, ḍākinīs, and dharma protectors in one. {247} The guru led you to your own nature, so you will never ever be able to repay that incredible kindness. Supplicate one-pointedly with intense devotion. The devotion to the guru will transform your mind so that when natural uncontrived timeless awareness arises vividly, you rest in that state of equipoise.
gnyis pa ni/
ii. Enhancement Based on Immeasurable Compassion

sems can thams cad drin chen gyi pha ma yin par rang sems ngo ma shes pas nyon mongs dang las bsags te 'khor bar 'khyams pa 'di cis kyang snying re rje zhes yid la bsam zhing ngag tu yang brjod/ mthar snying rje bya yul snying rje byed mkhan thams cad ngos bzung dang bral ba'i ngang der cham mer bzhag /

All sentient beings have been your kind parents. Yet since they do not recognize their own minds, with afflictive emotions they accumulate karmic actions and wander around in cyclic existence. Think and also say, “This is certainly lamentable.” Finally, settle serenely in a state free of distinction between the objects of compassion and the one engendering compassion.
gsum pa
iii. Enhancement Based on Special Methods
['di] la gsum las/
This has three points:
dang po ni/

tha mal shes pa rlung dang bsre/ / rnam rtog ma rig 'gag par 'gyur/ zhes pa'i don ni/ sems ma bcos par phyag rgya chen po'i ngang la mnyam par 'jog cing / rlung bum pa can drag tu bzung bas rlung sems 'jug pa gcig pa'i phyir/ rtogs pa gong nas gong du 'phel bar 'gyur/

Blending ordinary mind with vital winds will stop conceptual thought and ignorance. This means to settle into the equipoise of mahāmudrā with an uncontrived mind, and then forcefully hold the vase breathing. Since this causes the vital winds and the mind to converge as one, it increases realization more and more.
gnyis pa ni/ /

'od gsal lha sku rlung dang bsre/ / nyams myong yar ngo bzhin du 'gyur/ / zhes gsungs te/ rang nyid bde mchog lhan skyes chu nang gi zla gzugs ltar snang la rang bzhin med par bsgom/ lha skur snang ba ma 'gag pa de ka ma bcos/ so ma/ 'od gsal phyag rgya chen pos zin par byas la rlung drag tu gcun pas phyag chen la lha skus bogs thon te nyams myong gong 'phel du 'gyur ro/ /

Blending lucid clarity of the deity’s form with vital winds, felt experience will become like the waxing moon. Meditate on yourself as Coemergent Cakrasaṃvara, appearing yet without intrinsic nature, like the moon’s reflection in water. That unobstructed appearance of the deity’s form is itself uncontrived and fresh. To grasp [its] lucid clarity with mahāmudrā, forcefully squeeze the vital winds. The deity’s form thus enhances mahāmudrā and increases experience.
gsum pa ni/ /

zung 'jug shes pa rlung dang bsre/ / 'bras bu sku gsum mngon du 'gyur/ / zhes gsungs te/ rang lha sku gsal stong du bsgom/ gzhan lus shes rab ma'am/ rang lus thabs ldan ltar na gtum mo (248) dang 'od gsal gyi nyams myong gis lha sku la rgyas btab ste/ de nyid phyag chen gyis zin par byas la gzhur te bsgom/ ngag rlung bum pa can drag tu bzung / lha skur gsal ba sprul sku/ phyag chen mi rtog pa chos sku/ bde ba longs sku/ de gsum ka'i grogs rlung gis byas te/ lam dus kyi sku gsum nyams su blangs pas gzhi dus kyi sems kyi rang bzhin 'bras bu'i tshul du mngon du 'gyur ro/ / ji srid du rtsa bral mngon du ma gyur pa de srid 'bad rtsol chen pos 'du 'dzi spangs nas dben par bsgom pa gal che'o/ /

Blending unity consciousness with vital winds actualizes the resultant three kāyas. Meditate on yourself as the clear empty deity’s form and the other’s body as the wisdom partner. Or, according to “one’s own body is the means,”[3] the experiences of Fierce Inner Heat and Lucid Clarity seal the deity’s form. {248} Hold that deity’s form with mahāmudrā and distinguish it, then meditate. In speech, forcefully hold the vase breath. The clear form of the deity is nirmāṇakāya, the nonconceptual mahāmudrā is dharmakāya, and bliss is saṃbhogakāya. The vital winds act as a support for those three.
