de'i skabs su rdo rje'i tshig rkang so so dang / de dag la dngos shugs sbas gsum gyi man ngag gi 'phrul phye ste yongs su rdzogs par gdams shing / khyad par 'khyugs med mkha' spyod dkar dmar gyi 'pho ba shin tu zab pa'i gdams pa dpe gnyis kyi sgo nas ston pa dang bcas pas bka' rgyas btab ste gnang ba de dag nyams bzhes su bstar ba las/ dus skad cig gcig la'ang gcig car du sku lus kyi bkod pa bgrang las 'das par ston pa dang / gzhan gyi sems shes pa mngon par shes pa dang / pha rol po dang rang la 'pho ba mdzad pas dngos su 'pho nus pa (274) sogs grub pa'i zlos gar bsam gyis mi khyab pa mnga' ba de yin la/

On that occasion, she opened the magical esoteric instructions for the individual vajra lines by means of their three [levels of interpretation]: direct, implied, and concealed. In particular, she bestowed the extremely profound instructions on Transference of the Infallible White and Red Khecarīs, together with the teachings by means of two examples sealed by her command. From his practice of these instructions, Tangtong Gyalpo mastered an unimaginable repertoire of attainments, such as the instantaneous display of countless physical forms in a single moment, the clairvoyant knowledge of others’ minds, and the ability to actually transfer his and others’ [consciousness]. {274}

phyis la stod byang gi sa'i cha dpal ri bo cher grags pa grub pa'i bsti gnas gang gi rtser zab lam 'di nyid kyi khrid yig snying po kun 'dus cha lag dang bcas pa mkha' 'gro'i gnang ba stsal te yi ger bkod pa mdzad la/ 'on kyang mkha' spyod dkar dmar gyi 'pho ba zhal gdams dpe gnyis kyis mtshon pa'i dpe'u ris tsam ston pa las zhal shes zin bris su ma mdzad pas yongs su ma grags la/ snying po kun 'dus su/ 'phyugs med mkha' spyod kyi 'pho ba ni/ zhal gdams zur na yod do/ / zhes gsungs pa ni 'di yin te/

Later, on the peak known as glorious Riwoche in Latö Jang, in the adept’s own residence, he was granted permission by the ḍākinī and subsequently committed this profound path to writing as the Collection of Essentials and affiliated texts.[3] However, the oral instructions for the Transference practices of White and Red Khecarīs were transmitted only by drawings illustrating two examples. Apart from those, he had not written a record of the oral advice, and so it was not widely known.[4] He stated in the Collection of Essentials, “There is a separate oral instruction for Transference to the Unerring Celestial Realm.” This is that [instruction].

rang gi lus kyi nang du rtsa dbu ma mda' smyugs ltar drang ba/ dwangs gsal 'od kyi rang bzhin can/ mas sna gsang gnas dang yas sna tshangs bug la gtad pa'i spyi bor rje btsun mkha' spyod ma dkar mo bde ba chen po'i nyams dang ldan pa zhig tshangs bug gi steng du sku smad bzhag par bsgoms/ de nas rang gi smin mtshams yan gyi thod pa 'od du zhu nas mkha' spyod ma'i phyag gi bde skyong gi snod la thim nas gnyis su med par gyur/ de nas rang gi lte ba yan gyi lus kyi sha khrag gdos bcas rnams thod pa bdud rtsir byin gyis brlabs la/ rje btsun ma la mchod par phul/ de'i tshe rtsa dbu ma'i steng du mkha' spyod ma bzhugs pa ni shing rtser bya babs pa lta bu ste dpe dang po'o/ /

Within your body, the central channel is straight as an arrow, radiantly clear, and the nature of light. The lower end reaches the perineum and the upper end faces the cranial aperture. Above your head, Exalted White Khecarī embodies the experience of great bliss. Meditate that her lower body is right above your cranial aperture. Then the inside of your head above the eyebrows melts into light, which dissolves into the vessel that sustains bliss in Khecarī’s hand and becomes indivisible with it. Then your body from the navel up—including all corporeal matter, flesh, and blood—is consecrated as elixir in that skull cup, which is presented as offering to Khecarī. At that time, the Khecarī who sits on your central channel is like a bird landing on a treetop. That is the first example.
lus kyi phyi mi dmigs par dbu ma 'ba' zhig lus pa ni/ mchod rten bdag med zhig pa la srog shing lus pa lta bu dpe gnyis pa yin la/
With the outside of your body not visualized, only the central channel appears. It is like a derelict stupa that has collapsed, leaving only the central axis (srog shing). That is the second example.

spyi bor bsgoms pa'i rje btsun mkha' spyod ma gzhon sha can yid du 'ong ba phra zhing zlum pa'i nu 'bur zung dang ldan pa/ zhabs gnyis rgyab ngos nas phrag pa la bkal ba/ bde ba chen po'i 'byung gnas b+ha ga gsal bar ston pa zhig la shes pa gtad pas/ rnam 'gyur de dag (275) gis shes pa gyen du 'dren pa'i thabs mkhas bla na med pa'o/ /

Exalted Khecarī visualized above your head appears youthful and attractive, with small, round nipples. Her two legs rest on the back of her shoulders, clearly displaying her bhaga, the source of great bliss. Focus your attention there. {275} This image is an unsurpassable skillful method to draw your consciousness upward.
de dag ni grub thob rang gi thun mong ma yin pa'i man ngag dpe'u ris la/ rje btsun rin po che grol mchog zhabs kyis bdag la dges bzhin du gnang ba yin pas rang bzo'i rnyogs pa'i chas ma bslad pa'o/ /

These [teachings represent] the drawn examples of the great adept [Tangtong Gyalpo’s] own uncommon esoteric instructions. They were given to me joyfully by Venerable [Kunga] Drolchok Rinpoche, so they are not muddled by the mud of my own inventions.

ye shes mkha' 'gro'i zhal rlangs ma yal ba'i/ / mkha' spyod 'pho ba'i gdams pa ches zab pa/ / grub pa'i dpa' bo rnams las brgyud pa 'di/ / deng dus bdag gi snying dbus thig ler gnas/ / zhing 'dir zab lam bdud rtsi la dges pa/ / rje btsun ngag gi dbang po'i bkas bskul nas/ / skad gnyis smra lo chen 'gyur med bde chen/ bas rgyal khab chen po ru/ / tshes bcu mkha' 'gro 'du ba'i dus su bkod/ /

The awareness ḍākinī’s moist breath has not faded from the profound instructions of Khecarī Transference that comes from the lineage of the heroic adepts and now rests in the drop in my heart’s center. Thus, delighting in the elixir of this profound path, exhorted by command of Venerable Ngakgi Wangpo,[5] I, the bilingual one (Lochen Gyurme Dechen) in this great nation, compiled this during the tenth day, when the ḍākinīs gather.
sarba mang+ga laM/ / dge'o// // (276) (277)
sarva maṅgalaṃ Virtue!
@#/ /mkha' spyod dmar mo'i 'pho ba bzhugs so/ /
14. Red Khecarī Transference[1]
na mo gu ru/
namo guru
mkha' spyod ma dmar mo'i 'pho ba la sngon 'gro dang / dngos gzhi/ rjes gsum las/
Red Khecarī’s Transference of Consciousness practice has three parts: (1) the preliminary, (2) main part, and (3) conclusion.
dang po ni/
I. Preliminary

maN+Dal dpe chung ltar bzhengs/ gtor ma drug bshams/ mchod pa rnam pa lnga dang / ka pA li la sogs pa sta gon bya/ de nas bla ma rA hu la dang / bla ma shangs pa mjal lugs kyi lo rgyus bshad/ sin+d+hu ra'i man+Dal gyi steng du/ rje btsun ma la/ bla ma brgyud pa dang bcas pas bskor bar bsam mdzod byas la skyabs 'gro sems bskyed bsdus pa bya/

Set up the mandala as in the short text. Arrange six tormas. Do the five offerings and the kapāli and so forth for the prelude. Then relate the story of how Lama Rāhula and Lama Shangpa met.[2] Have [the disciples] imagine Exalted Lady surrounded by the lineage gurus on a mandala of vermilion and do a brief refuge and awakening mind prayer.
II.
II. Main Practice

da 'di ltar du sgoms shig / mdun 'di ru chos 'byung gru gsum sdon po gcig bsam/ de'i nang du hU~M sngon po gcig bsam/ de las 'od zer 'phros pas mngal gyi sgrib pa sbyangs/ tshur 'dus pas ltem gyis zhu ba las rang nyid bde mchog dpa' bo gcig pa g.yas rdo rje/ g.yon dril bu bsnams pa/ snang la rang bzhin med pa 'od zer lnga 'phro ba gcig tu bskyed/ de nas sin+d+hu ra'i maN+Dal chos 'byung gru gsum nyis brtsegs phyi dkar la nang dmar ba/ bde bar rgyu zhing bde bar 'char ba 'od kyi rang bzhin can du bsgom/ de'i nang du rje btsun rnal 'byor ma/ de nas rang nyid bde mchog tu yod pa'i lte bar thig le dkar po a'i ngo bor gnas pa las 'od zer lnga 'phros pas/ gzhan gyi mngal gyi sgrib pa sbyangs par bsam/ de nas ngo bo sems la rnam pa a de lte ba nas yar dkar ye re re byung ste snying gar sleb/ de nas byung ste sna bug g.yon nas phyir zur gyis don nas/ rje btsun ma'i thugs kar thim pas rang lus stong par bsgom/ des rkyen byas pas sgog sgra dang bcas nas rje btsun ma yar te/ mkha' spyod du mda' 'phangs pa bzhin rgyangs kyis song bar bsam/ (278) de 'dra ba'i dmigs pa thebs bdun bsgom du gzhug /

Now meditate like this: Imagine before you there is a blue tetrahedral source of phenomena. Imagine within it a blue hūṃ. Light rays radiate from that and purify the obscurations of the womb. They return and fully melt [the hūṃ], which transforms into oneself as Sole Hero Cakrasaṃvara holding a vajra in the right hand and a bell in the left. Visualize this as appearance without intrinsic nature, radiating light rays of five colors. Then meditate on the vermilion mandala as a double-stacked tetrahedral source of phenomena, white on the outside and red on the inside, made of bliss and arising as bliss with the nature of light. Within it is Vajrayoginī. With yourself as Cakrasaṃvara, imagine a white drop within the navel, the essence of the syllable A. Imagine five-colored light rays radiating from that, purifying the obscurations of the womb for oneself and others. Then the essence of your mind in the form of that A rises up in a flash of white and arrives at your heart. From there it leaves through the left nostril and moves out to melt into Vajrayoginī’s heart, leaving your body empty. With that impetus and the sound of impact [when A strikes the heart],[3] Vajrayoginī rises far up and shoots like an arrow as far as the celestial realm of Khecara. {278} Do this meditation seven times with such visualization.

de'i rjes la rje btsun ma mkha' spyod nas dmar ye re re byon te rang gi spyi bo'i gtsug tu byon nas zhabs gnyis bgrad pas bzhugs par bsam/ de'i pad+ma na mar byang chub kyi sems dmar la dkar ba'i mdangs bde phri li li babs te/ spyi bo'i tshangs bug na mar song nas lus thams cad byang sems kyis mer khengs pa dang / zag pa med pa'i bde ba chil chil rgyas par dmigs pa gtod cig byas la/ ngag tu oM gsum ma bgrang / rol mo bya'o/ /

Afterward, think that Khecarī descends in a flash from Khecara and comes to sit on the crown of your head with her two legs apart. From her lotus a stream of white bodhicitta with a tinge of red trickles down and enters your cranial aperture, filling your whole body with bodhicitta. Focus on the visualization of the expanding wave of undissipating bliss while saying the three-oṃ mantra a number of times and playing music.
byang sems spyi bor slebs nas bum dbang / mgrin par gsang dbang / snying gar shes rab ye shes/ lte bar bzhi pa'o/ / de la sems dar cig bzhag go /

The bodhicitta reaching the crown center is the vase empowerment; the throat is the secret empowerment; the heart is the wisdom-awareness empowerment; and the navel is the fourth empowerment. Rest your mind for a moment in that.

de nas rje btsun ma spyi bo na mar thim nas lte bar slebs pa dang / bde ba la stong pas khyab pa bde stong gnyis su med pa'i nyams skyes par bsam/ de'i ngang du sems ma bcos par bzhag go / da lta yang thun ma chag tsam bsgom mo/ /

Then Vajrayoginī dissolves through your cranial aperture and arrives at the navel. Think that emptiness pervades bliss and the experience of nondual bliss-emptiness is born. Rest within that state without contrivance. Now meditate without a break in sessions.
III.
III. Conclusion

'chi khar sngar bzhin du bsgoms nas rang gi lte ba'i thig le de rje btsun mar bsams nas/ rje btsun ma rnam par shes pa'i ngo bo de mas yar/ lte ba nas rgyangs kyi song ste spyi bo tshangs pa'i bu ga na yar don nas/ mkha' spyod du gshegs pa dang / skye med phyag rgya chen po'i ngang du bzhag go/ / dbugs ma chad tshe dmigs pa rtse gcig tu yang yang bsgom mo/ / des mkha' spyod du 'gro bar 'gyur ro/ /

At the time of dying, meditate as before. Then think of that drop at your navel as Vajrayoginī, the essence of your consciousness. She rises up from the navel and goes far out from your cranial aperture, all the way to Khecara. Rest within unborn mahāmudrā. Until your breath stops, meditate again and again with focused attention on that visualization. That will take you to Khecara.
[Colophon]

skye gnas lnga gcig car du dgag pa thig le'i 'pho ba zhes bya'o/ / bla ma rA hu la'i gdams pa rdzogs so/ / 'di'i dbang thob ba tsam gyis/ skye gnas sngar mi skye ba yin zhes/ nges shes skyed gsung ngo / / mang+ga laM/ /(279)

This completes the instructions of Lama Rāhula called Vital Drop Transference that blocks the five birthplaces all at once. It is said that just by receiving the empowerment, one will not be born in the five birthplaces, so have confidence.
Sukhasiddhi, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness
@#/ /su kha sid+d+hi'i lo rgyus/ rgya gzhung / gsang sgrub lte ba sprul 'khor/ dbang chog rnams bzhugs so/
15. Sukhasiddhi’s Story, Indian Source Text, Secret Sādhana of the Navel Emanation Chakra, and Empowerment Ritual[1]
I. [bde ba'i dngos grub kyi lo rgyus]
I. Sukhasiddhi’s Story[2]
(280) @#/ /rgya gar skad du/ su kha sid+d+hi/ bod skad du/ bde ba'i dngos grub kyi lo rgyus zhes bya ba/
Sanskrit: Sukhasiddhi Tibetan: bDe ba’i dngos grub kyi lo rgyus

dpal rdo rje mkha' 'gro ma la phyag 'tshal lo/ / de la rgya gar kha che na grong khyer chen po 'bum tsho sum cu so brgyad yod pa las/ 'di nub byang kha che'i grong khyer ba yin no/ / de yang grong khyer der bza' mi gnyis la bu gsum/ bu mo gsum dang / kho rang gnyis dang brgyad yod pa las/ shin tu dbul zhing phongs par gyur te/ rgyags 'bras bum pa gang las med pa la de za ma nus par kha bcad de sbas nas bzhag go /

The Story of Dewai Ngödrup, “Spiritual Power of Bliss” Homage to the glorious Exalted Ḍākinī! Of the thirty-eight hundred thousand great cities of Kashmir, this takes place in a northwest city. In that city there lived a couple with three sons and three daughters. Those eight family members were extremely poor and becoming destitute, with nothing but a single jar full of grain for provisions. They wouldn’t eat that, so they covered it and hid it.

de nas bu gsum lho phyogs su zas 'tshol du song / bu mo gsum byang du song / pha nub tu song / de nas ma la dus gcig na/ shin tu phongs pa gcig zas 'tshol du byung nas/ 'bras kyi bum pa kha phye ste btsos nas byin no/ / der phas zas ma rnyed par bkres pas nyen pa da ni khyim gyi 'bras bum pa gang po zos la/ de nas btsal dgos snyam nas log pa dang / bu mo gsum gyis kyang de bzhin du log / bu gsum yang log / der khong (281) rnams gros byas pa bzhin du dus gcig la log nas/ da ni mas 'bras kyi bum pa kha phye la byin cig / bkres pas nyen cing nyam thag par gyur to/ / zhes zer ba la/ ma yis smras pa/ khyed rnams kyis zas rnyed de 'ong snyam nas/ shin tu dbul zhing nyam thag pa cig zas slong du byung nas/ de la byin nas med byas pas/ khyo dang bu gsum po mgrin gcig tu bsdebs nas/ ma la smras pa/ khyod kyis sngar yang 'di ka bzhin byas pas/ nged rnams skyid du ma ster/ da yang khyod kyis zas tshol ba dang mi 'ong ste/ ngos kyis bsags pa rnams kyang med par byas pas/ 'di phyir thon cig zer nas khyim nas bton no/ /

Then the three sons went south in search of food, the three daughters went north, the father went west, [and the mother stayed home]. When a poor starving beggar came asking for something to eat, the mother opened the jar of grain, cooked it up, and gave it to him.[3] Meanwhile, the father, not finding anything to eat, had become famished and thin. He thought, “At home there was that full jar of grain to eat, I need to get that,” and he turned back. The three sons also hadn’t found anything, so they went back. The three daughters hadn’t found anything and likewise returned. {281} As if they had consulted one another, they all returned at the same time. They said, “Mother, please give us the jar full of grain. We have grown thin with hunger and will be depleted.” The mother replied, “I thought you all would return with food, so when a destitute beggar came here begging for food, I gave him the grain; there is nothing left.” The husband and three sons said, as if with one voice, “You did something like this before and it did not make us happy. This time you did not come [with us] to look for food, and you exhausted our stores. Now get out of here.” So they banished her from home.

de nas rgan mo des kha che'i yul nas/ nub phyogs o rgyan yul du phyin pa dang / o rgyan gyi mi rnams ni/ pho skyes pa thams cad ni dpa' bo/ mo skyes pa thams cad ni dpa' mo sha stag tu 'dug pa/ gnas der phyin pa tsam gyis rig pa rang bzhin gyis dwangs par 'dug skad/ dus der 'bras rtsa ba dang 'dzom nas/ 'bras bsgrub pas (282) khal gcig rnyed do/ / de grong khyer du khyer nas chang tshong ma byas so/ /

Then the old woman left Kashmir and traveled west, arriving in the country of Oḍḍiyāna. There in Oḍḍiyāna, all who are born as males are exclusively heroes and all who are born as females are exclusively heroines. It is said that innate awareness is naturally brightened by merely reaching that holy place. Sukhasiddhi gathered some grain seeds and by cultivating them she produced a load of grain. {282} She carried that into the village and became a beer merchant.

de'i dus su o rgyan gyi nags khrod na/ slob dpon nag po bir wa ba zhes kyang bya/ a wa b+hU ti pa zhes kyang bya ba des/ phyag rgya ma a wa d+hu ti ma dang gnyis gsang gcod mdzad cing yod pa las/ rnal 'byor ma des rtag tu chang nyor phyin no/ / de nas rgan mo chang tshong ma de la yang skabs su chang nyos pas/ chang gzhan bas zhim pa sha stag btsongs so/ / der rgan mos smras pa/ rnal 'byor ma khyod chang nyos nas su la khyer ba yin byas pas/ rnal 'byor mas smras pa/ nags khrod na rnal 'byor pa bzang po cig bzhugs pas de la 'dren pa yin zer/ rgan mos smras pa/ da ni khyed la chang rin mi 'dod do zer nas/ 'bras chang nying bsrings byas kyin bskur ro/ /

At that time, there was a black master named Virūpa or Avadhūtipa living in the forest with his mudra (female partner) Avadhūtima, with whom he practiced secret conduct. That yoginī frequently came to purchase beer. When she bought beer from that old woman beer seller, the woman always sold her beer that was more delicious than any other. The old woman asked, “Yoginī, to whom do you convey this beer that you buy?” She replied, “I take it to an excellent yogi who lives in the forest up there.” “In that case, there is no need to pay for it,” said the old woman, who then chose the best of the beer for her to take.

der bir wa pa'i zhal nas/ rnal 'byor ma rin mi dgos par chang zhim po sha stag 'byung ba 'di/ ji ltar byas pa yin gsungs pa dang / der sngar gyi chang tshong ma dang mi 'dra ba'i dad pa can cig 'dug ste/ nga'i bla ma bzang po cig nags khrod na bzhugs yod pas de la 'dren pa yin byas pas/ chang tshong ma dad pa skyes nas bskur ba lags zhus pas/ bir wa pa'i zhal nas/ rnal 'byor ma ci nas kyang rgan mo de khams gsum nas 'dren dgos pas khrid la shog gsungs nas/ rnal 'byor mas rgan mo'i rtsar phyin no/ / der rnal 'byor ma des rgan mo la smras pa/ nga'i bla ma bir wa pa'i zhal nas/ chang tshong ma khrid la shog 'khor ba nas 'dren dgos gsungs pas/ khyod 'dongs dang byas pas/ rgan mo de shin tu mos te/ 'bras chang bum pa gang dang bcas te mjal du phyin no/ / rje btsun bir lba pas dus de nyid du gsang sgrub lte ba (283) sprul 'khor gyi dbang bzhi rdzogs su bskur/ bskyed rdzogs chos drug dang bcas pa/ dbang gi phrin las 'du ba rnam gsum dang bcas pa gsungs pas/ dus de nyid la ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro mar gyur to/ /

Virūpa questioned her, saying, “Yoginī, how is it that you come with only the finest beer without even needing to pay for it?” She replied, “There is a faithful one unlike our previous beer merchants. I [told her] that I take the beer to my excellent guru who lives in the forest. Faith arose in her and she sent the beer.” Virūpa said, “Yoginī, I must definitely deliver that old woman from the three realms. Bring her here.” The yoginī went to the old woman’s place and said, “My guru Virūpa told me to bring the beer seller because he must deliver her from cyclic existence. Will you come?” The old woman was very intrigued and came to meet the yogi carrying a jug full of beer. Venerable Virūpa conferred the complete fourfold empowerment of the Secret Sādhana of the Navel Emanation Chakra right on the spot. {283} He also taught her the creation and completion phases, the Six Dharmas, and magnetizing activity, including the three kinds of gathering.[4] Sukhasiddhi became a ḍākinī of timeless awareness at that time.

de yang bu khyo rnams kyis kha che'i yul nas bton pa'i dus su/ lo lnga bcu rtsa brgyad lon/ o rgyan gyi yul du phyin nas chang tshong tsa na drug cu tham pa/ bir wa pa dang mjal nas dbang bskur byas tsa na/ drug cu rtsa gcig lon no/ /

When her husband and children exiled her from Kashmir, she was fifty-eight years old.[5] After reaching Oḍḍiyāna and becoming a beer merchant, she was sixty. By the time she met Virūpa and received the empowerments, she was sixty-one years old.

der nub gcig la grub pa thob pa'i stobs kyis/ drug cu rtsa gcig lon pa'i rnam smin lus de rang dag la song ste/ 'ja' lus su gyur nas gzhon zhing lang tsho dar la bab pa/ sku mdog shin tu dkar ba/ dbu skra sil bu sku rgyab non pa/ / lo bcu drug lon pa'i na tshod ltar lta bas chog mi shes pa/ shing tA la bdun srid kyi nam mkha' la bzhugs pa'i ye shes mkha' 'gro su kha sid+d+hi zhes bya bar gyur to/ / de yang mkha' 'gro ma de bcom ldan 'das bdag med mar dngos su gyur to/ / bir wa pa dang dgyes mdzad tha dad med pa'i gsang yum kyang mdzad/ da ltar yang 'das grongs mi mnga' bar khams gsum sems can thams cad la ye shes kyi gzigs pa dus drug rtag tu 'jug go / de bas kyang khyad par snang ba dag pa rnams la chos gsungs/ gsang sgrub nyams su len pa dang / gsol ba 'debs pa thams cad la dngos su byin gyis rlob cing / mchog thun mong gi dngos grub thams cad thob par byed do/ / de'i phyir ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro ma de'i rnam thar dang / mtshan thos pa tsam gyis shin tu mos par gyur te/ bdag dad pa'i sa bon gting nas g.yos te/

One evening, on the strength of attaining spiritual powers, her fully ripened body of a sixty-one-year-old was naturally purified and transformed into a rainbow body. She appeared youthful and in the prime of youth, her body utterly white, her silken hair falling loose down her back, like someone at the stage of a sixteen-year-old on whom one could never tire of gazing. She dwells in the sky at the height of seven tāla trees (palmyra) and is known as the Awareness Ḍākinī Sukhasiddhi. That ḍākinī became the actual Bhagavatī Nairātmya. She was also the secret consort of Virūpa, who was identical with Hevajra. Even now, never passing away, she is constantly present in the six times,[6] watching all beings of the three realms with her timeless awareness. Beyond that, she makes a special appearance to those with pure outlook to teach them dharma. For all those who practice the secret sādhana and supplicate her, she actually manifests her blessings and enables them to attain all the supreme and common spiritual powers. Therefore, those who hear the life story of that awareness ḍākinī, or even just hear her name, will develop great devotion.[7]
[Khyungpo Naljor’s account:]

bdag khyung po rnal 'byor gyis rgya gar gyi phyogs thams cad (284) du phyin pas/ tsan+dan gyi sdong po'i nags kyi steng du/ shing tA la bdun srid kyi nam mkha' la 'ja' 'od 'khyil pa'i dbus na/ mkha' 'gro ma dpag tu med pas bskor nas bzhugs pa rgyang nas mthong ngo / /

Deeply moved by the seeds of faith, I, Khyungpo Naljor, traveled all over India. {284} Then, above the forest of sandalwood trees, in the midst of swirling light seven palmyra trees high in the sky, I saw her from afar, surrounded by innumerable ḍākinīs.

de nas drung du phyin te phyag btsal/ bskor ba byas nas gser srang lnga phul nas yang dag pa'i gdams ba zhus pas/ thun mong ma yin pa'i dbang ba'i rdzogs par bskur/ gsang sgrub kyi bskyed rdzogs chos drug 'du ba gsum zhal gdams dang bcas pa dang / khyad par du lo zla tsam gyis sangs rgya ba'i gnad khyad par du 'phags pa dang / / gsang sngags kyi gnad ma lus par gnang ngo / /

Then I came before her and, after prostrating and circumambulating, I offered her five measures of gold and requested authentic instructions. She conferred the complete uncommon empowerment as well as oral instructions on the creation and completion phases of the secret sādhana, the Six Dharmas, and the three gatherings. In particular, she granted the especially elevated vital points to attain buddhahood in just years or months and every vital point of Secret Mantra.

bdag gi rtsa ba'i bla ma bzhi la/ khyad par du drin che ba'i bla ma su kha sid+d+hi yin no/ / de yang dang por drin che ste lung mang po ston/ bar du drin che ste gsang yum mdzad de dbang thams cad ma lus par thob/ tha ma drin che ste dbang lag len zhal gdams dang bcas pa thams cad gnang ngo / /

Of my four root gurus, the one who was especially kind to me was Sukhasiddhi. Her first kindness was to teach me many transmissions. Her middle kindness was to become my secret consort and bestow every empowerment. The final great kindness was to give me all the empowerment practices with oral instructions.

de yang bdag la rgya bod thams cad du 'du 'bral med par byin gyis rlob cing dbang bzhi rdzogs rtag tu bskur ro/ / gsang sngags kyi gnad rnams rgyun chad med par gsungs pas shin tu drin che'o/ / phyi rabs kyi bu slob rnams kyis kyang gsangs nas gsang sgrub 'di bsgrub par bya'o/

Furthermore, she was never apart from me while anywhere in India and Tibet and always grants blessings and confers the complete four empowerments. The really great kindness was to continuously teach the vital points of Secret Mantra. Future generations of disciples will also accomplish this revealed secret sādhana.

bla ma rmog lcog pa'i zhal nas/ sding mar bsgrub pa byas pa'i dus su/ su kha sid+d+hi 'di thog mar zhal mthong / de'i dus su dbang bzhi rdzogs su bskur/ chos mang du gsungs/ de nas rmog cog gi brag logs la sgrub pa byed cing bsdad pa'i dus su/ su kha sid+d+hi byon nas lung bstan mang po mdzad/ de nas gzung nas 'du 'bral cig kyang med gsung ngo / /

Lama Mokchokpa said: One time while I was practicing at Dingma, I saw Sukhasiddhi face to face for the first time. At that time she conferred the complete four empowerments and gave many teachings. Then one time when I was staying in practice on the cliffside of Mokchok, Sukhasiddhi came and made many prophecies. From that time on she has never left me.

bla ma skyer sgang pa'i zhal nas/ ngas lha sa 'phrul snang du phyin pa'i dus su/ su kha sid+d+hi 'dis rdzogs (285) rim gyi chos mang du gsungs/ dus rtag tu dbang bzhi rdzogs su bskur/ 'du 'bral ni skad cig kyang med gsung ngo / /

Lama Kyergangpa said: When I went to the Magical Appearance (Jokhang temple) in Lhasa, this Sukhasiddhi taught me many completion-phase practices. {285} She always confers the complete four empowerments. She is never apart from me for even a moment.

sangs rgyas gnyan ston gyi zhal nas/ skyer sgang du gro thon nas brag kha cig tu bsdad pa'i dus su/ / su kha sid+d+hi zhal mthong / rig pa rten med du zhog dang rnal 'byor pa/ zhes lan gsum gsungs/ de nas da lta yan chod du 'du 'bral med/ dbang bzhi khyad 'phags kyi gdams pa ma lus pa gnang / lung bstan mang po mdzad do/ / khyed bu slob rnams lo zla tsam gyis sangs rgya bar 'dod na/ gnas dben par bsten la gsang sgrub 'di gsang la sgrubs shig gsung ngo / /

Sangye Nyentön said: I had gone to Kyergang and was staying in some caves when I saw Sukhasiddhi face to face. Three times she said, “Yogi, rest awareness without support.” We have not been apart since then. She gave me the specially elevated instructions of the four empowerments and made many prophecies. She proclaimed, “If you and your disciples wish to attain enlightenment in just years or months, stay in remote places and secretly practice this secret sādhana.”

de nas rim pa ltar/ chos rje ston pa/ mkhas grub shangs ston/ mkhas btsun pa/ khyung po tshul mgon/ ri khrod ras chen/ shangs pa dkar po/ sangs rgyas dpal bzang / nam mkha'i mtshan can/ sku skye rin po che sangs rgyas chos kyis kun dga' bkra shis ngag dbang rgyal mtshan dpal bzang po la brgyud de/ dam pa des bdag byams pa rin chen bzang po la brtse bas gnang ngo // // !

The lineage of succession is Chöje Tönpa, Khedrup Shangtön, Khetsunpa [Zhönu Drup], Khyungpo Tsulgön, Ritrö Rechen, Shangpa Karpo, Sangye Palzang, the one named Namkha, and incarnate Rinpoche Sangye Chökyi Kunga Tashi Ngawang Gyaltsen Palzangpo.[8] That holy one gave it to me, Jampa Rinchen Zangpo, with love.
su kha sid+d+hi'i rgya gzhung ni/
II. Sukhasiddhi’s Indian Source Text
rgya gar skad du/ badzra wA ra hi/ gu h+ya sA d+ha nA ma/ bod skad du/ rdo rje phag mo'i gsang ba'i sgrub pa zhes bya ba/
Sanskrit: Vajravārāhīguhyasādhanāma Tibetan: rDo rje phag mo’i gsang ba’i sgrub pa
dpal rdo rje rnal 'byor ma la phyag 'tshal lo/ /
Homage to glorious Vajrayoginī.

mkha' o rgyan du 'gro'i phyogs su kha bltas te/ / maN+Dal ni sin d+hU ra'o/ / rang skad cig gis phag mor gsal ba'i lte bar chos 'byung ngo / / de dbus pad 'dab bzhi'i lte bar oM mo/ / mdun du ha'o/ / g.yas su ri'o/ / rgyab tu ni'o/ g.yon du sa'o/ /

Regarding the subject of the ḍākinī (in Oḍḍiyāna), the mandala is vermilion. You appear as Vārāhī with a (red) source of phenomena at the navel. In its center is a four-petaled lotus with oṃ-mo in its center, ha-’o in front, ri-’o on the right, ni-’o in the back, and sa-’o on the left [petals].

de thams gong ras ljang gu mu khyud dang bcas pa/ cad dmar ba'i mdog can/ myos byed kyi rang bzhin can/ yi ge'i tshogs de rnams las (286) 'od zer dmar ba lcags kyu'i dbyibs can byung ste/ sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' thams cad dang / dpa' bo dang DA ki ma rnams kyi dbang gi nus mthu pad+ma rA ga'i mdog ltar bkug la bstim mo/ /

They are all red in color (with green outlines). They have the nature of intoxicants. Red light rays with the shape of hooks radiate from those sets of letters. {286} They draw in the ruby-colored magical abilities of magnetizing from all buddhas, bodhisattvas, heroes, and ḍākinīs, which dissolve [into those letters].

de'i nus mthu'i 'od dmar ba'i dbyibs can/ dmigs bya'i smin {snying zer ba'ang snang ngo} mtshams dang gsang gnas su btab pas/ kiM shu'i lo ma rlung gis bskyod pa ltar/ sgrub bya 'dod yon dang bcas pa rang dbang med par pad+ma'i steng du'o/ /

Their magical ability has the form of red light. It is planted at the point between the eyebrows (the heart also occurs) and the secret place of the visualized one. Like kiṃśu leaves moved by the wind, the practice consort[9] along with sense pleasures cannot help but gather on the lotus.

de nas chos 'byung kha bsdus te/ yi ge mi g.yo ba'i 'od zer snga ma lta bu'i gnas gnyis su btab pas/ pad+ma {shin tu myur bas} g.yos med pa ltar/ dbang med du myur du 'khor bas/ sgrub bya 'dod yon dang bcas {dmar ldem ldem} li khri lta bur gyur te/ {sgrub byed de nyid kyi lus ngag yid gsum/} gcer bu gsum dang ldan par blta'o/ / {lus ngag yid gsum/} mi gnas gsum la rtse gcig tu 'bad par bya'o/ /

Then the source of phenomena’s opening draws closed. Light rays of the unmoving letters are planted in the two places as before. The lotus ([moves] very quickly), as if motionless. The rapid, uncontrollable circling causes the practice consort along with the sense pleasures to become (thoroughly red) like vermilion. Look with threefold nakedness (of the partner’s body, speech, and mind). Exert effort in single-pointed focus on threefold nonabiding (of body, speech, and mind).

de ni 'du {mi mkha' 'gro zas nor} ba gsum dang 'char lus la bde ba ngag la nus pa sems la rtogs pa/ ba gsum 'byung bar 'gyur ro/ / sngags 'bum phrag bdun gyis 'jig rten gyi bdag por 'gyur ro/ / zla ba drug gis bcu bzhi'i sa thob par 'gyur ro/ / dbang la ni chags pa'i sems kyis so/ / mchog la ni mi rtog pa'i sems kyis so/ / gsang zhing smra ba bcad pa dang / / the tshom med pa ni dam tshig go /

Then the three gatherings (of humans, ḍākinīs, food and wealth) and the three arisings (of physical well-being, verbal ability, and mental realization) will occur. Seven hundred thousand (mantras) will make you the lord of the world. In six months you will attain the fourteenth level. Control comes through a passionate mind. Supreme [powers] come through nonconceptual mind. Keeping secret and silent and free of doubt is the sacred pledge.
gsang sgrub lte ba sprul 'khor zhes bya ba/ DA ki ma su kha ma hA sid+d+his phyung ba'o/ /rdzogs so/
The Secret Sādhana Practice of the Navel Emanation Chakra, [from the Ocean of Vows Latter Tantra],[10] revealed by Ḍākinī Sukhamasiddhi[11] is complete.
lo tsA ba glan dar ma blo gros kyis bsgyur nas/ bdag khyung po rnal 'byor pas nyams su myong bar byas pa'o/ /
Translated by Lotsāwa Lendarma Lodrö. I, Khyungpo Naljor, brought it into my experience.
mang+ga laM// // !
maṅgalaṃ
su kha sid+d+ha'i gsang sgrub lte ba sprul 'khor ni/
III. Sukhasiddhi’s Secret Sādhana of the Navel Emanation Chakra[12]
thugs ni 'od gsal ngang la gnas/ / snang (287) grags sgyu mar mkhyen pa yi/ / zhen med lha skus 'gro don mdzad/ / dpal ldan skyer sgang pa la 'dud/ /
The awakened heart abides within lucid clarity. {287} Knowing appearance and sound as illusion, unattached, the deity’s body enacts the welfare of migrators. I bow to the glorious Kyergangpa.[13]
mkha' 'gro ma gnad kyi gdams pa 'di la/ don rnam pa gnyis te/ bsnyen pa dang / nye bar sgrub pa'o/ /
This instruction of vital points of the ḍākinī has two subjects: [the ritual service of] (1) approach and of (2) near accomplishment.
dang po
A. Approach
['di] la gnyis te/ bskyed rim bzlas pa dang bcas pa dang / rdzogs rim bsgom pa'o/ /
This has two parts: (1) meditation on creation phase with recitation and (2) completion phase.
dang po
1. Creation Phase with Recitation
[;di] la gsum ste/ sngon 'gro dang / dngos gzhi dang / rjes so/ /
This has three parts: (1) preliminaries, (2) main practice, and (3) conclusion [which appears after completion phase].
dang po
a. Preliminaries

ri khrod la sogs pa dben zhing nyams dga' ba'i gnas/ bde zhing 'bol ba'i gdan la/ bsam gtan gyi chos kyis nye bar 'dug ste/ byams snying rje byang chub kyi sems sngon du 'gro bas/ hU~M gis gsol ba lan gsum gdab par bya'o/ /

Stay in a pleasant, isolated place, such as a mountain retreat, and sit on a soft, comfortable seat. Sit tight with the positions of meditative stability. [Develop] love, compassion, and the awakening mind first, then supplicate three times with hūṃ.
gnyis pa
b. Main Practice
dngos gzhi'i nyams len ni/ rgyud las/ a yi 'od kyis bsregs byas nas/ / mi 'grub pa ni gang yang med/ /
The practice of the main part is conveyed in the tantra: Once burned by the light of the letter A, there is nothing at all that will not be achieved.
ces gsungs pa'i don ni/ rang skad cig dran rdzogs kyis rdo rje phag mor wal gyis bsgom/
Meditate on yourself as Vajravārāhī the instant you think of it.

de'i lte ba'i dbus rtsa dbu ma'i nang du pad+ma 'dab ma bzhi pa ze'u 'bru dang bcas pa gcig pu sgoms te/ de yang mdun gyi 'dab ma sngo skya/ g.yas kyi dmar po/ rgyab kyi dkar po/ g.yon gyi ser po/ dbyibs dang kha dog gsal bar bsgom/ dbus kyi lte ba la a dkar po 'od 'phro ba gcig bsam/ mdun gyi 'dab ma la ha sngo skya/ g.yas su ri dmar po/ rgyab tu ni dkar po/ de'i 'og tu sa ser po/ de rnams gsal bar bsgoms la/

Then meditate that within the central channel in the center of the navel is a single four-petaled lotus with anthers. Its front petal is light blue, the right is red, in back is white, and the left petal is yellow. Meditate clearly on the shape and colors. Imagine a white A radiating light in its center. On the front petal is a light-blue ha, on the right is a red ri, in back is a white ni, and below that [on the left] is a yellow sa. Meditate clearly on those letters.

de nas mdun gyi nam mkha' la bcom ldan 'das kyai rdo rje dang / slob dpon nag po bir wa pa gnyis tha mi dad par bsam/ de'i 'og tu rje btsun dam pa rgya gar phyag na sba'i gling bu bsnams nas/ bdag la byin gyis brlabs par bsgom/ de gnyis la sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems (288) dpa' dpag tu med pas sprin gtibs pa bzhin du tham me bskor nas bzhugs par bsgom/ de rnams la dad gus drag po byas pas/ gtso bo kyai'i rdo rje dang / sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' de rnams kyi thugs las/ oM AHhU~M gsum mu tig bstar la brgyus pa bzhin du dam pa'i gling bu mar la phyung / bdag gi spyi bor byon nas tshangs bug nas mar song / dbu ma brgyud nas lte ba'i a la sib sib thim pa dang / zag pa med pa'i bde ba rgyas par bsams la/ skyabs su 'gro ba grub tshad bya'o/ /

Now imagine in the space before you Bhagavat Hevajra indistinguishable from Black Ācārya Virūpa. Below him is Venerable Indian Dampa holding a cane flute (sba’i gling bu) in his hand with which to bless you. {288} Meditate that those two dwell amid immeasurable buddhas and bodhisattvas dispersed around them like massing clouds. Your strong devotional faith in them causes the three letters oṃ āḥ hūṃ, like a string of pearls, to emerge from the hearts of primarily Hevajra, and all of the buddhas and bodhisattvas. The [letters] come through Dampa’s flute and enter through the cranial aperture at the crown of your head and descend down the central channel, finally melting into the A at the navel. Contemplate the expanding undissipating bliss. Do the full measure of going for refuge.
des bdag mkha' 'gro'i dbang du mi 'gro zhing / DA ki ma bdag gi dbang du 'du ba'i gnad yin no/ /
Through that you do not come under the ḍākinī’s control; it is the vital point to bring ḍākima under your control.

de nas yi ge bzhi po gong bas thos tsam du shib shib bzlas pas/ lte ba'i a las 'od zer dkar po 'phros/ yi ge bzhi la thim zhing bsregs pas lcags bsregs pa lta bur song ste/ bde sing sing par bsgoms pas/ 'og gi pad+ma dbang med du g.yon du drag tu 'khor zhing sgo ro ro 'khor bar bsgom/ yi ge mi 'khor pad+ma 'khor ba la dmigs pa de dang ma bral bar bzlas pa ci 'grub bya'o/ /

Now recite the four letters above (ha ri ni sa) at a barely discernible whisper. White light rays radiate from the A at the navel. They dissolve into the four letters and burn them until they become like burning iron. Meditate on scintillating bliss. The lotus below uncontrollably spins counterclockwise intensely; meditate on that going round and round. Constantly maintain that visualization of the lotus spinning as the letters do not spin while doing however much of the recitation.

de las skyon lte ba'i a las 'od 'phros/ dbu ma nas tshangs bug la bton te/ nam mkha' gang ba'i lha'i bu mo thams cad kyi bde ba thams cad bkug / tshangs bug nas brgyud nas lte ba'i a la thim pas/ zag pa med pa'i bde ba rgyas par bsgom/ de bzhin du a'i 'od zer gyis dri za'i bu mo dang bram ze'i bu mo dang / gdol pa'i bu mo dang / klu'i bu mo dang / mi'i bu mo'i bde ba thams cad bkug la sngar bzhin bsgom mo/ / de ni bskyed rim bzlas pa dang bcas pa'o/ /

When you grow tired of that, light radiates from the A at the navel. It travels up the central channel and emerges from the cranial aperture and hooks the bliss of all the goddesses that fill space, pulling it through your cranial aperture. That dissolves into the A at the navel. Meditate on the increasing, undissipating bliss. In a similar way, meditate that the light rays from A draw all the bliss from a ghandarva girl, a brahmin girl, a caṇḍāla girl, a nāga girl, and a human girl. That is the creation phase with recitation.
gnyis pa rdzogs rim ni/
2. Completion Phase
tha mal shes pa rang ga 'di/ / bsgom 'dod rtog pas ma bslad par/ / ma bcos ngang la (289) klong la zhog / ci yang mi dmigs de kho na/ / phyag rgya chen po zhes su brjod/ /
This regular ordinary mind— don’t pollute it with concepts of meditating. {289} Rest relaxed within the uncontrived state. Just being without any frame of reference is called mahāmudrā.
dngos gzhi/ gsum pa rjes kyi bya ba ni/
c. The Main Parts, Concluding Practices

bdag gis de ltar bsgoms pa yis/ / dngos po'i snang grags chos rnams kun/ / sgyu ma lta bur shes byas la/ / zhen pa med pa'i spyod lam gyis/ / lus ngag yid gsum dge la bkol/ / snying rjes sems can don la 'bad/ /

By your meditating in that way, all phenomena, the appearance and sound of things, are understood to be like illusions, so without attachment, daily activities will serve as virtue of body, speech, and mind, compassionately striving for the welfare of beings.
de ltar bsnyen pa rdzogs pa dang / / gnyis pa dran pa bsgrub pa la 'jug ste/
The completion of the [recitation] approach marks the second [stage]—engaging in the close attainment.[14]

de yang bsnyen pa 'bum tsho gsum song nas/ mi 'grub pa ni gang yang med/ / ces bshad pas/ sngon la bsnyen pa 'bum tsho gsum song nas/ de nas nye bar bsgrub pa la 'jug pa ni/ bla ma'i zhal las shes par bya'o/ /

As explained: “Once the approach of three hundred thousand recitations is done, there is nothing at all that will not be accomplished.” That is to say, once three hundred thousand recitations are finished, then you begin the near attainment, which should be learned directly from the guru.
bla ma'i gdams ngag rin po che/ / mkha' 'gro gnad nas bskul byed pa'i/ / ji skad gsung bzhin yi ger bkod/ / de la DA kis mi bkyon 'tshal/ / dge ba sems can don du bsngo/ /
The guru’s precious instructions that solicit the ḍākinī by vital points were written down just as they were spoken. Ḍāki, please don’t scold me for this. The virtue I dedicate to beings’ welfare.
DA ki gnad kyi gsang sgrub rdzogs so// /
The secret sādhana of the ḍāki’s vital points is finished.
su kha sid+d+hi'i dbang chog bzhugs/ /
IV. Sukhasiddhi’s Empowerment Ritual[15]
na mo gu ru/
namo guru

gzhan la byin rlabs byed par 'dod pas/ dben zhing nyams dga' ba'i gnas su phyag dar dang chag chag btab/ bla ma dkon mchog gi rten bkram/ pu tsa bzang du bsham/ sa gzhi bstar ba la/ bdud rtsi lnga dang chang bsres la gru bzhir byugs/ de la pad+ma 'dab bzhi mu khyud dang bcas pa bri/ mdun gyi 'dab ma sngo skya/ g.yas kyi dmar po/ rgyab kyi dkar po/ g.yon gyi ser po gong ras ljang gu/ lte bar mu khyud nag pos bskor/ dbus su hU~M nag po/ mdun g.yas skor du ha ri ni sa kha dog pad+ma dang mthun pa bri/ de'i steng du many+dzi bzhag go / de'i steng du me long la chang dang bdud rtsi bsres pa byugs/ de la sin+d+hu ra (290) dar tshags byas la khod snyoms par byugs/ de la pad+ma 'dab bzhi dang yig 'bru lnga sngar bzhin bri/ many+dzi'i khar gzhug / steng de nas skyabs 'gro sems bskyed byas la/ bdag nyid dgyes rdor du bskyed la bzlas pa bya/ dgyes mdzad g.yon du su kha sid+d+hi bsgoms/ 'og gi yi ge hU~M nag po slob dpon nag po bir wa pa dang / dgyes mdzad tha mi dad par bsgom/ yi ge mkha' 'gro ma bzhi'i ngo bo lhar bltas la/ rnam pa yi ge'i gzugs su bsam/ 'og ma dam tshig sems dpar bsam/

If you wish to confer the blessing on others, find a pleasant, isolated place, sweep it, and sprinkle it with water. Arrange images of the gurus and Jewels. Put up excellent putsa.[16] Apply a mixture of the five elixirs and alcohol to the cleansed ground in the four corners and draw there a four-petaled lotus within a circle. Make the front petal light blue, the right petal red, the back petal white, and the left one green, as above. The center is outlined with a black circle. In the center is black hūṃ. Draw the letters ha ri ni sa from the front clockwise, the same colors as the lotus petals. On top of that place the mañji. {290} Smear a mirror with the alcohol-elixir mixture and cover it evenly with vermilion powder. Draw on it the four-petaled lotus with its five seed syllables as before, and place the mirror on the opening of the mañji. (Then go for refuge, arouse the awakening mind, visualize yourself as Hevajra, and do the recitation.) Meditate on the black hūṃs above [on the mirror] and below [in the mandala] as Black Master Virūpa inseparable from Hevajra. (Meditate that Sukhasiddhi is to Hevajra’s left.) Regard the letters as the essence of the four ḍākinīs and imagine the letters’ forms as their bodies. Imagine the pledge beings below.

'byor na pu tsa lngas tshan bskor/ de ma 'byor na ci tsam 'byor pa bsham/ gtor ma gsum rgyab tu bsham/ thod pa chang gis bkang ba la bdud rtsi ril bu btab la rang gi mdun du bzhag / nang mchod byin gyis spyi ltar/ byin gyis brlabs pa'i mchod pa dang / brlabs/ rdo rje dril bu sta gon bya/ nang mchod dbul/ bstod pa rnams bya/ gtor ma dbul/ bdag 'jug bya/ de nas/ slob ma du yod 'dus byas la gral rim gyis bzhag / rang stan bde ba la 'dug / yi dam lha'i nga rgyal gyis byin gyis brlabs pa'i chang slob ma rnams la gtor zhing bgegs sum+b+ha ni sogs/ bsrung / de nas slob ma rnams blo rim dal 'byor rnyed par dka' ba sogs kyi/ gyis khrid de sdig pa bshags pa dang / skyabs su 'gro ba thun mongs pa dang / sems lam yan lag lnga sogs/ bskyed pa rnams pha rol tu phyin pa'i lugs ltar bya'o/ / de nas slob dpon la phyag btsal te me tog phul/ mos gus drag po bya'o de nas sngags kyi gnang ba sbyin pa la sogs pa yan lag lnga bya/ / bla mas mchod pa bsangs la lha la phul/ byin gyis rlob bir wa pa hU~M/ su kha ma sid+d+hi haM zhes/ par gsol ba gdab/

If you have them, surround [the mandala] with the five kinds of putsa.[17] If not, then arrange whatever you do have. Place the three tormas behind. Put elixir pills in a skull cup full of alcohol and place it in front of you. Consecrate the inner offerings (as usual). Do the vajra and bell prelude. (Present the consecrated offering and the inner offering. Do the praises, present the tormas, and do the self-induction.) Gather the disciples and place them in rows. Settle comfortably on your own seat. With the pride of being the yidam deity, sprinkle the disciples with the consecrated alcohol to protect from obstructors (with sumba ni…etc.). Then lead the disciples through contemplations (of the free and endowed difficult-to-find human birth, etc.), the confession of negative acts, the common going for refuge, arousing the awakening mind, (and the five-branch path, etc.) according to the tradition of the transcendent perfections. Then the disciples do prostrations and offer flowers with sincere devotion. (Then give the permission of the mantra and the other branches.) The guru cleanses the offerings and presents them to the deity. Supplicate for blessings, (saying, “Virūpa hūṃ Sukhamasiddhi haṃ”).
[Then instruct the disciples:]

rang nyid bde mchog tu bsgoms la/ rtsa dbu ma'i nang lte ba'i thad ka tsam du/ pad+ma 'dab ma bzhi pa ze'u 'bru dang bcas pa gcig (291) bsgoms te/ de yang mdun gyi 'dab ma sngon po/ g.yas dmar po/ rgyab dkar po/ g.yon ser po bsam/ dbus kyi lte ba nag po la a dkar po/ mdun du ha sngo skya/ g.yas su ri dmar po/ rgyab tu ni dkar po/ g.yon du sa ser po'o/ / de nas mdun gyi nam mkha' la sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' thams cad bsam/ de'i steng du hU~M las dgyes mdzad bir wa pa dang tha mi dad pa bsgom/ de'i g.yon du hU~M las bdag med ma dang / su kha ma sid+d+hi tha dad med par bsgom/ rang gi spyi bor dam pa phyag na sba'i gling bu rtsa dbu ma la reg ge bsnams/ dam pa'i mdun na bla ma bzhugs par bsams nas/ rje btsun bir wa pa hU~M/ su kha sid+d+hi haM/ zhes gsol ba lan gsum btab pas/ sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' thams cad dang / khyad par du bir wa pa/ su kha sid+d+hi/ dam pa gsum gyi thugs ka nas/ oM AHhU~M mu tig dar la brgyus pa bzhin du dam pa'i gling bu'i nang na mar la song / dbu ma nas brgyud de yi ge bzhi la sib sib thim pas/ nyams chags nus pa smad par bsgoms nas/ bla ma yi dam mkha' 'gro gsum la skyabs su mchi'o/ / zhes skyabs 'gro grub tshad byas la gsol ba gdab bo/ /

Meditate on yourself as Cakrasaṃvara with a four-petaled lotus at the level of the navel inside the central channel. {291} Visualize the front petal of that lotus blue, the right one red, the back white, the left yellow, and the middle is black with a white A. The front petal has a light-blue ha, the right a red ri, the back a white ni, and the left a yellow sa. Then imagine all the buddhas and bodhisattvas in the space in front of you. Above them, from hūṃ, meditate on Hevajra inseparable from Virūpa. To the left of that, from hūṃ, meditate on Nairātmya inseparable from Sukhamasiddhi. Above your head is Dampa holding a cane flute that touches your central channel [at the cranial aperture]. Imagine the guru in front of Dampa and supplicate with “Venerable Virūpa hūṃ Sukhasiddhi haṃ” three times. That causes the three letters oṃ āḥ hūṃ, like strings of pearls, to emerge from the hearts of all of the buddhas and bodhisattvas, primarily the three: Virūpa, Sukhasiddhi, and Dampa. The letters come through Dampa’s flute and descend, entering your central channel, finally slowly dissolving into the four letters. Meditate that this reduces the power of your transgressions. Then say, “I go for refuge in the triad of guru, yidam, and ḍākinī.” Do the full extent of going for refuge in that supplication.

de nas lus bcos te/ gong bzhin dmigs pa rnams bsgom du gzhug cing / bla mas kyang dmigs pa rnams bsgoms te/ gsol ba btab cing rol mo rnams 'bud bkrol bya'o/ / lus ngag yid gsum la phebs lugs spyi dang mthun no/ /

Then with the physical sitting posture, have [the disciples] meditate on the visualization above while the guru also meditates on the visualization. Supplicate and play the music, blowing and rattling [the instruments]. The manner of descent to body, speech, and mind accords with general custom.
dngos gzhi dbang bskur ba
The Actual Empowerment Conferral
['di] la/ bum pa'i dbang bzhi dang / lha mo drug gi dbang bskur ba'o/ /
This has two parts: (1) the four empowerments of the vase and (2) the empowerment conferral of the six goddesses.
dang po bum pa'i dbang gi gsol 'debs ni/ skyob pa'i dkyil (292) 'khor mngon sum du/ / til gyi gong bu bzhin gang bas/ / bdag nyid la ni dbang bskur gsol/ / ces lan gsum gyis gsol ba btab ste/
First, supplicate for the vase empowerment three times: {292} “In the manifest mandala of refuge, full as a bag of sesame seeds: please confer the empowerment on me.”
de nas lha tshogs rnams kyis/ ji ltar bltams pa tsam gyis ni/ / lha rnams kyi ni khrus gsol ltar/ / lha yi chu ni dag pa yi/ / de bzhin bdag gis sku khrus gsol/
Then: Just as the gods bathed him as soon as he was born, just so I bathe your body with pure divine water.
oM sarba ta thA ga ta a b+hi Shiny+tsa tu maM/ ces bum pa'i dbang bskur bar bya'o/ /
oṃ sarva tathāgata vajra abhiṣiñca tu māṃ Saying that, confer the vase empowerment (on the crown, etc.).

gsang dbang gi gsol 'debs ni/ byang chub rdo rje sangs rgyas la/ / ji ltar mchod cing gsol ba ltar/ / bdag kyang rab tu bskyab pa'i phyir/ / nam mkha' rdo rje deng bdag stsol/ ces lan gsum gyis gsol ba btab pa dang /
Supplicate for the secret empowerment three times: “Just as Awakened Vajra granted the great offering to the Buddha, grant me this today, Vajra Space, in order to protect me.”

dkyil 'khor gyi lha tshogs rnams kyis/ phyogs bcu'i gsang gsum las byung ba'i/ / khams gsum kun gyis phyag byas pa/ / rdo rje'i dbang bskur chen po sbyin/ / ces pa sngags dang bcas pas byang sems lce thog tu sbyin no/ /

The hosts of mandala deities from the three secrets of ten directions, honored by all in the three realms, the great empowerment of the vajra is conferred. Say that with the mantra and give the bodhicitta on their tongues.

shes rab ye shes kyi gsol 'debs ni/ phyogs bcu'i sangs rgyas thams cad kyis/ / khams gsum ye shes bdud rtsi ni/ / rdo rje'i lam la rab bsdus nas/ / bde ba chen po'i dbang bskur stsol/ / ces lan gsum gyis gsol ba btab pa dang /

Supplicate for the wisdom-awareness empowerment three times: “All the buddhas of the ten directions gather the awareness elixir of three realms fully into the pathway of the vajra; grant the empowerment conferral of great bliss.”
lha tshogs rnams kyis de dag gi steng du/ bde ba bskyed phyir rigs kyi yum/ rgyal sras ye shes dbang bskur sbyin/ / ces pa sngags dang bcas pas sbyin no/ /
On top of them the hosts of deities bestow the awareness consorts to generate bliss; the wisdom empowerment of the Victor’s heir. Say that with the mantra to give the empowerment.
dbang bzhi pa'i gsol 'debs ni/ kun mkhyen ye shes thugs rje'i bdag / gtso bos bdag la dbang bskur stsol/ / ces lan gsum gyis gsol ba btab pa dang /
Supplicate for the fourth empowerment three times: “Epitome of omniscience, awareness, and compassion: principal one, please confer empowerment on me.”

lus kyi 'khrul 'khor ni/ rkang pa cung zad bsnol/ lag pa g.yon sdigs mdzub byas la thugs kar bzung / g.yas pa mtheb chen dang mthe'u chung gnyis sprad la/ sor mo gsum gdengs (293) pa'i tshul du byas te mig hu re blta'o/ /

Assume the positions of the yogic exercises: slightly cross the legs, hold your left hand at your heart in the threatening gesture, and with your right hand bring the thumb to the little finger [with the other] three fingers raised, and stare with alert eyes. {293}
nam mkha' rig med stong pa la/ / rig bcas sems kyi rtsa ba gcun/ / rtsa ba gcun la lhug par zhog / ces pa dbang bzhi pa'o/ /
In empty space, which lacks awareness, tame the root of mind with awareness. Tame the root and rest relaxed. That is the fourth empowerment.
de nas lha mo drug gis dbang bskur ba ni/
Empowerment by the Six Goddesses

rang nyid bde mchog tu bsgoms pa'i lte ba'i A las 'od 'phros pas/ lha mo sku mdog dkar ba la ser ba'i mdangs chags pa gzi mdangs can bde ba'i nyams dang ldan pa/ gzhon zhing sgeg pa/ bany+tsa li ka dang / rin po che sna tshogs pas brgyan pa'i gsang gnas su 'od zer 'phros pas mdun du byon/ de'i gsang gnas gsal bar bsgoms la/ de nas rang gi dbang po'i rtser hU~M mthing nag las 'od zer lnga 'phros pas/ chos 'byung nang du song / rtsa 'dab khengs pas bde ba rgyas te/ rje btsun ma bde ba'i 'od zer gyis tshur la drag tu bsdus nas/ rang gi dbang po'i nang nas yar rje btsun ma song bas rtsa thams cad khengs/ de'i bde ba rgyas pa dang / 'og rlung drag tu bskum nas bsus pa sbyar/ bde stong gnyis su med par bsgom mo/ / yang gcig hU~M las 'od 'phros nas/ / bde ba gong bzhin bskul ba yis/ / rang lus zag med bde ba rgyas/ /

Meditate on yourself as Cakrasaṃvara. Light radiates from the A at the navel. The goddess appears before you, white with a yellow radiance and a lustrous complexion. She possesses the experience of bliss and is youthful and charming, adorned by rainbow light (pa nya tsa li ka) and various jewels. Imagine light rays radiating from her secret place. Meditate clearly on that secret place. Then five-colored light rays radiate from a blue-black hūṃ in the tip of your organ. They go into [her] source of phenomena and fill all the radial channels, increasing bliss. Exalted Lady is brought toward you intensely by the light rays of bliss. Then from inside your organ [the light] goes up to Exalted Goddess, filling all the channels. Her bliss increases. Press down strongly on the lower winds and compress the belly. Meditate on nondual bliss-emptiness. Again one time light radiates from the hūṃ, invoking the bliss as above. Undissipating bliss expands in your body.
gsal stong gnyis su med par bsgom/ / de nas lha mo rje btsun ma/ / rang la gnyis med 'khyud nas ni/ / thabs dang shes rab bsrub pa yi/ / drod kyis bde ba'i gnad bskul nas/ /
Meditate on nondual bliss-clarity. Then Exalted Goddess embraces you in nondual unity. Method and wisdom churning, warmth evokes the vitality of bliss.
yum gyi rang byung nyi ma'i rgyun/ / bde ba phun sum tshogs pa de/ / rdo rje nas ni khong pa yi/ / nang na yar la song ba dang / / rtsa chen rtsa phran thams cad khengs/ /
The mother’s self-arising sun flow, that abundance of bliss from the vajra, from within the interior moves upward and fills all major and minor channels.
bde bas rgyud ni gang zhing rgyas/ / rang lus zag med bde bas rgyas/ / rang lus rA ga'i mdog ltar gyur/ / de yi yum ni dbang du 'gyur/ /
Bliss fills your being and expands, undissipating bliss increases in your body. Your body changes to the color of ruby; the mother is overpowered.
rang gi kun dA phar 'phros pas/ (293) yum de bde ba rgyas gyur nas/ / dkar la dmar ba'i mdangs chags pas/ / yum gyis yab ni dbang du gyur/ /
de ltar yab yum 'od 'khrug cing / / bde bas rgyud ni gang ba'i tshe/ / 'og rlung drag tu bskum pa dang / /
Thus the couple’s light is stirred up. When bliss fills your being, intensely compress the lower winds.
bde bas stong pa'i don ston cing / / stong pas bde la chags mi bya/ / bde stong gnyis med ye shes mchog / dmar ba yun ring dkar ba thung / /
Bliss reveals the truth of emptiness, emptiness prevents attachment to bliss; nondual bliss-emptiness is supreme awareness. The red lasts long, the white is brief.
gnad kyi mchog tu shes par bya/ / snang stong lha sku bde chen la/ / gsal la rtog pa med par bzhag
Understand supreme vital points. In great bliss of the deity’s empty form, rest without thought in the clarity.
de ltar yab yum gnyis med kyi/ / ngang nas bzlas pa bya ba ni/ / oM ha ri ni sa la sogs bzlas/ /
In this state of the nondual couple, do the recitation of the mantra: oṃ ha ri ni sa and so forth.
de yis lha sku phyag rgya che/ / zhen pa'i dri ma thams cad dag / bral ba rang shar dag tu 'byung / /
de yis gang 'dul lhun gyis grub/ / de ni mthar thug 'bras bu'o/ / dri za bram ze gdol ba dang / / mi dang klu la de bzhin no/ /
Taming anyone is spontaneously present, that is the ultimate fruition. Gandharvī, brāhminī, caṇḍālī, human, and nāgī likewise.
dkar ba la dbang bzhi'o/ / sngo ba la dga' ba bzhi/ smug pa la skad cig ma bzhi/ smug nag la yang dbang bzhi/ rA ga sku bzhi'o/ /
White is the four empowerments. Blue is the four ecstasies. Brown is the four instances. Dark brown again is four [empowerments]. Ruby is the four kāyas.
de nas tshogs longs spyod/ gtor ma dbul/ lhag gtor btang / maN+Dal gyi lha rnams slob ma'i lte bar bsdu'o/ / lhag chad bshags pa ci bder gnas par bya'o/ /

Then enjoy the communal feast. Offer torma. Send out the leftovers. The deities of the mandala are gathered into the master’s navel. Do whatever confessions of omissions and additions that you like, then rest in equipoise.
[Concluding Verse and Colophon]
byin gyis brlabs pa'i man ngag ni/ / bla ma'i gsung bzhin yi ger bkod/ / DA ki rnams la bzod par gsol/ / dge ba sems can don du bsngo/ /
This esoteric instruction of blessings is written down just as the guru spoke it. I request the ḍākis to have patience. I dedicate the virtue to the welfare of beings.
DA ki ma gnad kyi gdams pa dbang gi zin bris rdzogs so// /
The record of the empowerment, vital instructions of the Ḍākima, is finished.
V. [Additional Instructions][18]
na mo gu ru/
namo guru

lte ba'i 'og tu chos 'byung gcig bsgom/ chos 'byung nang du pad+ma 'dab bzhi bsam/ dbus kyi lte ba la oM/ mdun du ha/ g.yas su ri/ rgyab tu ni/ g.yon du sa'am swA hA/ yig 'bru rnams dmar por bsgom/ yig 'bru de rnams las 'od zer 'phros pas/ sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa'/ (295) thams cad la phog / de rnams kyi mthu dang nus pa bsdus nas/ yig 'bru la thim/ chos 'byung kha zum/ steng rlung bag tsam mnan la sngags bgrang /

Meditate on a source of phenomena below the navel. Within the source of phenomena imagine a four-petaled lotus. On its center is oṃ, in front ha, to the left ri, to the back ni, and to the left sa or svāhā. Meditate on those letters as red. Light rays radiate from those seed syllables, striking all the buddhas and bodhisattvas. {295} The light rays draw in all their strength and ability, which dissolve into the seed syllables. The opening of the source of phenomena closes. Press down slightly on the upper winds and repeat the mantra.

lte ba sprul pa'i 'khor lo la brten nas/ mi nor zas gsum dbang du bsdu ba'i gnad/ rang rdo rje phag mor bskyed la/ kha T+waM ga yum pha dar bskyed rang re'i byang chub sems de yum pha la sib sib thim song ba dang / bde phri li li song bar bsgom/ yum pha de'i byang chub sems dmar po rang gi lus la bcug la/ lus dmar yer gyis song bar bsgom/ ngag tu oM ha ri ni sa swA hA/ zhes bzlas so/ / lha'i bu mo'i lte ba'i 'og nas bde ba khug bya'o/ / zab mo'i don yin no/ / gsang ngo // //

The vital point of magnetizing humans, wealth, and food depends on the navel chakra of emanation. Visualize yourself as Vajravārāhī and the khaṭvāṅga as the male consort, each with bodhicitta. The bodhicitta dissolves into the male object.[19] Meditate on scintillating bliss. That male’s red bodhicitta enters your body. Meditate that your body clearly becomes red. Verbally repeat the mantra oṃ ha ri ni sa svāhā. Bliss is drawn from below the navel of the divine girl. This is profound meaning. It is secret. ithi

ngo bo bde mchog rnam par ram/ yum ngo bo rje btsun ma'i rnam pa gang yin te/ rang gi byang sems dkar po yum gyi pad+mar phog pas dkar la dmar ba'i mdangs chags pas bde ba myong bar bsam/ / tshur 'dus rang gi dbang du 'dus pas/ dkar ba la dmar ba'i mdangs chags pas zag med kyi bde ba dang ldan par bsam/ oM ha ri ni sa lha'i bu mo'i lte ba'i 'og nas bde ba khug / ces bzlas kyin bya'o/ / 'jug yul rang la bsdus la phyag rgya chen po bsgom// //

[Visualize yourself] either as the essential form of Cakrasaṃvara or the mother’s essence as Vajravārāhī. Your white bodhicitta touches the mother’s lotus and the white develops a red radiance. Think that you experience bliss. It gathers back and you magnetize it. Imagine that the white with the red radiance imbues you with undissipating bliss. Recite “oṃ ha ri ni sa, bliss is drawn in from beneath the goddess’s navel.” Gather the object of engagement and meditate on mahāmudrā. ithi
na mo gu ru/
namo guru

rang skad cig gis bde mchog bskyed la/ lte ba'i a las 'od zer 'phros nas/ lha'i bu mo dkar la ser ba'i mdangs chags pas/ gos bzang po gon pa/ rin po che'i rgyan thams cad kyis brgyan pa mdun du 'dug la/ rang gi dbang po'i rtse mo nas hU~M mthing nag las/ 'od kha dog lnga 'phros pas mdun gyi lha mo'i pad+mar zhugs/ lha mo bde bas myos par bsam/ tshur 'dus rang gi dbang po'i nang na yar byung bas zag med bde ba rgyas (296) par bsgom/ de'i dus su yang dmigs pa yar na rang drang zhing / 'og rlung 'then pa gal che'o/ /

Visualize yourself instantly as Cakrasaṃvara. Light rays radiate from the A at the navel. Before you is the divine girl, white with a yellow radiance, wearing fine clothing and adorned by all the precious ornaments. Light rays of five colors radiate from the deep-blue hūṃ at the tip of your organ and enter the lotus of the goddess in front. Imagine that the goddess experiences bliss. [The light] gathers back in and enters up your organ. Meditate that undissipating bliss increases. {296} At that time, while the visualization is continuously drawing up, it is important to pull up the lower winds.
de nas mdun gyi lha mo rang la kyud kyis byung ba dang bde ba rang la 'dus nas/ zag pa med pa'i bde stong dbyer med lha sku phyag rgya chen po bsgom par bya'o/ /
Then the goddess in front joins in union with you and you gather the bliss into yourself. Meditate on the undissipating bliss-emptiness inseparable of the mahāmudrā of the deity’s form.
mang+ga laM// // (297)
maṅgalaṃ
@#/ /zab lam su kha chos drug gi brgyud pa'i gsol 'debs bde chen char 'bebs zhes bya ba bzhugs so/
16. Bringing Down the Rain of Great Bliss. A Lineage Supplication for the Profound Path of Sukha’s Six Dharmas[1]
(298) @#/ /bde chen rab dgyes dpa' bo he ru ka / gzhom med dbyings kyi dpa' mo rnal 'byor ma/ / kha sbyor lha yi sku grub bi rU pa/ / sa bcu'i dbang phyug su kha sid+d+hi'i zhabs/ /
Hero Heruka’s great bliss delights the heroine Yoginī of invincible space, their united divine forms: the adept Virūpa and Sukhasiddhi, mighty one of the tenth level.

gangs can mkhas grub kun gtso khyung po rje/ / chig brgyud rdo rje'i bka' babs rmog lcog pa/ / spyan ras gzigs dngos chos kyi seng ge'i zhabs/ / sbas pa'i sangs rgyas gnyan ston ri gong ba/ / rdo rje'i rgya bkrol ston pa 'gro ba'i mgon/ /

Lord Khyungpo, chief of all adepts in the Land of Snows, Mokchokpa, heir of the single-lineage vajra legacy, Chökyi Senge, the real Avalokiteśvara, Nyentön Rigongpa, the hidden buddha, Tönpa Drogön, releasing vajra knots.
gtsang ma shangs ston rig pa'i rdo rje dang / / khu ston tshul mgon 'dren mchog chos dpal bzang / / tshul khrims rgyal mtshan mkhyen rab chos kyi rje/ / gzhon nu chos grub sems kyi mdud grol zhabs/ /
Tsangma Shangtön, Rikpa Dorje, Khutön Tsul[trim]gön, supreme guide Chöpal Zang, Tsultrim Gyaltsen, Khyenrab Chökyi Je, Zhönu Chödrup,[2] Semkyi Dudrol (Kunga Drolchok),
lha dbang grags pa rje btsun sgrol ba'i mgon/ / phrin las dbang mo ye shes rgya mtsho'i ste/ / snying po blo gros grub brnyes kun bzang dbang / / tshe dbang nor bu 'khrul zhig chos dbyings mtshan/ /
Lhawang Drakpa, Jetsun Drolwai Gön (Tāranātha), Trinle Wangmo, Yeshe Gyatso, Nyingpo Lodrö, Drupnye Kunzang Wang, Tsewang Norbu, Trulzhik Chöying,
kun bzang chos 'byor blo bzang mthu stobs dang / / nyi ma chos 'phel blo gsal bstan skyong zhabs/ / 'jam dpal dbyangs dngos mkhyen brtse'i dbang po ste/ /
smin grol lam (299) ston rtsa brgyud bla ma dang / / yi dam DA ki chos skyong tshogs bcas la/ / gsol ba 'debs so byin gyis brlab tu gsol/ / skye med bdud rtsis las nyon sdig sgrib bkrus/ /

Root and lineage gurus who show the ripening and liberating path, yidams, ḍākinīs, with hosts of dharma protectors, I supplicate you! Please grant your blessings. Unborn elixir cleanses karma, afflictions, sins, and obscurations.
lha sngags lam gyis tha mal snang zhen sbyangs/ / 'bar 'dzag 'phrul las zhu bde 'gyur med bskyed/ / rang grol sgyu mas 'khrul pa'i bden 'dzin 'jig / nying 'khrul snang ba lha sku rang shar bsgyur/ /

The path of divine mantra refines attachment to ordinary appearance. Changeless bliss of melting arises from blazing and dripping exercise. Self-liberated illusion destroys fixation on the reality of delusion. Double-deluded appearance naturally arises as divine form.
'od gsal nyi mas gti mug mun pa bsal/ / 'da' ka'i gsang lam mkha' spyod chen por snyegs/ / bar do'i 'khrul snang rgyal ba longs skur shar/ / mi shigs dwangs ma gsum ldan tshe dbang thob/ /

Lucid clarity’s sun dispels the darkness of ignorance. Death’s secret passage hastens one to the great celestial realm. Intermediate state’s delusion arises as the victors’ saṃbhogakāya. Having three indestructible essences brings longevity.
zung 'jug rdo rje 'chang gi go 'phang mchog / tshe 'di nyid la 'grub par byin gyis rlobs/ / ces pa'ang rje dpon gang de'i thugs bzhed skong slad yon tan rgya mtshos bris pa dge/ //

Bless me to attain in this very lifetime the supreme state of Vajradhara unity. Written by Yönten Gyatso in order to fulfill the aspirations of the lord nephew [Jangchub Sempa Lodrö Zangpo, attendant of Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo]. Virtue!
ye shes mkha' 'gro su kha sid+d+hi'i bskyed pa'i lam zab dang / chos drug gi khrid yig zung 'jug myur lam zhes bya ba bzhugs so/ /
17. Fast Path of Integral Unity. Awareness Ḍākinī Sukhasiddhi’s Profound Path of Creation and Guidance on the Six Dharmas[1]
ye shes DA ki'i gtso mo ni/ / bde ba'i dngos grub zhes grags pa/ / sa bcu'i (300) dbang phyug chen mo dang / / dbyer med bla ma la btud nas/ /
Chief Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness known as Spiritual Power of Bliss, {300} great mighty one of the tenth level, I bow to you, inseparable from my guru.
rdo rje 'dzin pa'i gsang ba'i tshig / grub chen khyung po'i thugs kyi bcud/ / snyan brgyud rtog ges ma bslad pa/ / bla ma'i zhal lung gsal bar bya/ /
The secret words of the vajra holders are the great adept Khyungpo’s heart essence. An aural lineage not polluted by sophistry, the guru’s oral transmission is clearly presented.

de'ang bka' brgyud rin chen rnam lnga la gang zag gi tshig dang rtog ge'i blo skyon gyis ma bslad pa'i snyan brgyud rdo rje'i gsang tshig tshe gcig la zung 'jug gi go 'phang 'bad med du ster ba ji snyed cig mchis pa'i nang nas/ snying gi dwangs ma lta bu skal ldan gcig nas gcig tu sbas chos su brgyud pa las khyab brdal du bsgrags par ma mdzad pa'i zab gsang mkha' 'gro'i snying khrag ni 'di yin la/ 'on kyang dus skal gyi dbang gis gzhung yan lag phal cher DA ki'i rang gnas su byon zin kyang / gdams pa'i rtsa ba legs par bzhugs pa de nyid nyams su len bder 'chad pa la gsum/ sngon 'gro/ dngos gzhi/ rjes so/ /

From among the Five Precious Jewels of the [Shangpa] Kagyu lineage that are the secret vajra words of the aural lineage not polluted by the words of ordinary people or the intellectual flaws of sophists, that effortlessly grant in a single lifetime the citadel of integral unity, the one that, like the heart’s radiance, was passed as a concealed teaching in the lineage from one fortunate individual to the next, the profound secret that was not proclaimed all over the place, the ḍākinīs’ heart blood—this is it. However, due to the [scant] fortune of the times, the branches of the source [texts] are mostly kept in the ḍākinīs’ own abode, but the root instruction is well preserved. The explanation of how to conveniently put that into practice has three parts: (1) the preliminaries, (2) the main practice, and (3) the conclusion.
dang po
I. Preliminaries
['di] la gnyis/ thun mong skyabs sems dang / thun min dag byed stong ra'o/ /
This has two parts: (1) common refuge and awakening mind and (2) uncommon purifying inner space.
dang po ni/
A. Going for Refuge and Arousing the Awakening Mind

'di nyid kyi smin byed khyad par bas rgyud smin cing blo ldog rnam pa bzhi rgyud la 'byongs pa'i gang zag gis dben par bde ba'i gdan la bsam gtan gyi chos dang ldan pas 'khod de/ mdun gyi nam mkha' seng ge chen po brgyad kyis btegs pa'i rin po che'i khri sna tshogs pad+ma nyi zla'i gdan la rtsa ba'i bla ma sangs rgyas thams cad kyi sku gsung thugs ye shes rdo rje'i bdag nyid/ sku gzi mdangs mtshungs pa med cing zhal 'dzum bag dang ldan pa/ thugs ting nge 'dzin gyi sgo du ma la mnyam par bzhag pa/ mtshan thos pa tsam gyis 'khor ba dang ngan song las sgrol na/ gsol ba btab pas lta smos kyang ci dgos pa de'i mdun du rang dang pha mas gtsor byas sems can thams cad kyis lhan cig skyabs su 'gro bar mos la/ ma nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i sems can thams cad skyabs kun 'dus kyi ngo bo bla ma rin po che la skyabs su mchi ba lags so/ (301) zhes lan bdun la sogs pa dang /
nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i sems can thams cad kyi don du zung 'jug rdo rje 'chang gi go 'phang 'thob par bya/ de'i ched du lam zab mo nyams su blang bar bgyi'o/ / zhes lan gsum gyis sems bskyed/

For the sake of all sentient beings throughout space, I will attain the unified state of Vajradhara. To that end, I will practice the profound path. Repeat that three times to arouse the awakening mind.
gnyis pa dag byed a'i stong ra
B. The Purifying A of Inner Space
['di] la sbyor ba dang / dngos gzhi'o/ /
This has two parts: (1) the preparation and (2) the main practice.
dang po
1. Preparation
gsol ba gdab pa ni/ rang dang sems can thams cad kyis gsol ba gdab par mos la/
For the supplication, imagine that you and all sentient beings are supplicating:

dus gsum sangs rgyas thams cad kyi ngo bo bla ma rin po che la gsol ba 'debs so/ / sems can thams cad kyi don du bdag gis bdag 'dzin blos thong bar byin gyis brlab tu gsol/ / dgos med rgyud la skye bar= sgyu lus rmi lam 'byongs par= 'od gsal phyag rgya chen po rgyud la skye bar= zhes gsol ba lan mang du btab/ mos gus kyi shugs drag po bskyed pas spyi bo'i bla ma 'od du zhu nas rang la thim/

Precious guru, unified essence of all buddhas of the three times, for the sake of all sentient beings, I supplicate you to bless me that I may relinquish self-fixation, that I may have no needs, that I may cultivate Illusory Body and Dream, and that Lucid Clarity Mahāmudrā arises to me. Supplicate many times. On the strength of your intense devotion, the guru above your head melts into light and dissolves into you.
gnyis pa ni/
2. Main Practice

rang tha mal du gnas pa'i mgo bo'i nang du 'od kyi chos 'byung dkar po zur gsum pa/ zur gcig smin mtshams dang gnyis rna ba g.yas g.yon gyi phyogs su bstan pa/ rtsa ba sra ba mthur du zug cing kha gdengs che ba gyen tu bstan pa/ nang khong stong gi dbus rten med par yi ge a dkar po chos 'byung gi kha mtshams las cung mtho ba zhig bsgoms la sems 'dzin/ a zhes lan nyer gcig brjod pa'i rkyen kyis a las bdud rtsi dkar po'i rgyun bab/ chos 'byung gi nang khrigs mer gyis gang / phyir zham zham lud pas lus kyi phyi nang thams cad gang / tshe rabs thog med nas bsags pa'i nad gdon sdig sgrib thams cad dag ste lus stong gsal 'od kyi rang bzhin tu gyur bar bsam/ /

Remain in your ordinary form. Visualize that inside your head is a white tetrahedral source of phenomena made of light. Of three vertices, one faces the midbrow and the other two face in the direction of the right and left ears. Its narrow apex faces down and the wide opening faces upward. In the center of the empty interior there is an unsupported white letter A that protrudes slightly above the opening of the source of phenomena. Meditate on that and fix it in your mind. The repetition of “A” twenty-one times causes a stream of white elixir to fall from the A. It completely fills up the inside of the source of phenomena. All sickness, spirits, negativities, and obscurations accumulated since beginningless lifetimes are purified. Think that your body becomes empty clarity, the nature of light.
gnyis pa dngos gzhi
II. Main Practice
['di] la gnyis te/ rten bskyed pa'i rim pa dang / brten pa rdzogs pa'i rim pa'o/ /
This has two parts: (1) the phase of creation of the support [of the visualized deity] and (2) the phase of completion of the supported [interior subtle body]. {302}
dang po ni/
A. Creation Phase
bsgom bzlas rkyang pa rgyun (302) khyer lta bur khol 'don byas tshe/ skyabs sems tshad med bzhi sngon du btang / dkyus 'dir dag byed stong ra'i rjes thog tu/ swa b+hA was stong par sbyang /

When doing just the meditation-recitation separately, first do the refuge, awakening mind, and the four immeasurables. Then continue to here with the purifying of empty space. Afterward, add svabhāva…(etc.) to purify in emptiness.

stong pa'i ngang las rdo rje'i sa gzhi ra ba drwa ba gur bla bre ye shes kyi me 'bar ba'i srung ba'i 'khor lo'i nang du/ gzhal yas khang mtshan nyid thams cad yongs su rdzogs pa'i dbus su pad+ma dang zla ba'i steng du/ rang nyid skad cig gis mkha' 'gro ma su kha sid+d+hi sku mdog dung ltar dkar ba/ dbu skra sil bur 'phyang zhing rus pa'i rgyan gyis brgyan pa/ phyag g.yas thod pa bdud rtsis gang ba/ g.yon skye med mtshon pa'i phyag rgya ched du 'phyar tsam mdzad pa/ zhabs gnyis gar stabs kyi rnam pa/ spyan gsum hrig ger gzigs pa/ ye shes kyi sku can/ de'i spyi bor oM/ mgrin par AH thugs kar hU~M/ de las 'od 'phros ye shes pa badzra sa mA dzaH dzaHhU~M baM hoH dam tshig pa dang gnyis su med par gyur/ de la yid gtad de/ oM su kha sid+d+hi hU~M/ zhes thugs rgyud skul pa'i bzlas pa cung zad dang /

From within emptiness—inside a protection circle of the vajra ground, enclosure, latticework, tent, canopy, and blazing fire—is a celestial palace complete in all respects. In its center, upon a lotus and sun, you instantly become Ḍākinī Sukhasiddhi, white as a conch shell. Her hair falls down loose and she is adorned by bone ornaments. She holds a skull cup full of elixir with her right hand and lifts her left hand in the mudra of pointing to the unborn. Her two feet are in a dancing posture. She stares with wide-open three eyes. She has the form of timeless awareness, with oṃ at the head, āḥ at the throat, and hūṃ at the heart. Light radiates from the [letters] and invokes the awareness being—jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ—that becomes indivisible from the pledge being. Focus your attention on that and recite oṃ sukhasiddhi hūṃ a bit to evoke her presence.

rang gi lte bar pad+ma 'dab bzhi'i dbus su a/ 'dab bzhi la ha ri ni sa g.yas bskor du 'khod pa/ thams cad kyang dkar la dmar ba'i mdangs chags par mos/ sngags bzlas pas lte ba'i yi ge las 'od 'phros/ sangs rgyas byang sems rnams kyi mkhyen brtse nus gsum mkha' 'gro sde lnga rgyal chen bzhi phyogs skyong bcu la sogs pa'i dbang gi nus pa/ 'jig rten gyi 'dod yon lnga'i bcud la sogs pa 'od zer dkar dmar gyi rnam par bsdus nas lte ba'i yig 'bru la thim par mos la/ a ha ri ni sa/ zhes yi ge lnga pa ci nus bzla/

In your navel center is a four-petaled lotus with A at its center and ha ra ni sa arrayed clockwise on the petals. Visualize all the letters as white with a red radiance. The mantra recitation makes light radiate from the letters in the navel. The light draws all knowledge, love, and ability of all the buddhas and bodhisattvas, the capacity to magnetize the five classes of ḍākinīs, four great kings, ten direction protectors, and so on, and the vital essence of the world’s five sense pleasures. Imagine them returning in the form of white and red light rays that dissolve into the letters at the navel. Recite the five letters as much as you can: a ha ri ni sa.
khyad par dbang gi las bsgrub na mi gnas pa rnam pa gsum gyi sgo nas dmigs pa'i zab gnad bsgyur tshul yig rnying du gsal/
More particularly, if you will accomplish the empowerment ritual, the transformations of the vital profound visualizations by means of threefold nonabiding[2] is clarified in the ancient texts.
mthar/ / nam mkha' rig med stong pa la/ / rig bcas sems kyi rtsa ba gtun/ / rtsa ba gcun la lhug par bzhag (303) ces pa'i don dran par byas la mnyam par bzhag /
At the end say: In empty space, which lacks awareness, with awareness tame the root of mind. Tame the root and rest relaxed.[3] {303} Recall the meaning and rest in equipoise.

'dir skye med mtshon pa'i phyag rgya zhes pa ni/ g.yon pa'i khu tshur la mdzub mo nam mkhar bsgreng ba phyar tsam mdzad pa'o/ / 'dir mkhyen rab chos rje'i khrid yig las bskyed tshul gzhan 'di ltar la/ phyag g.yas thugs kar rtse gsum phyag rgyas sku gsum mtshon zhing / g.yon sdigs mdzub kyis skye med ston pa/ zhabs tsog pu'i bzhugs stangs can tu bshad de rdzogs rim skabs 'brel chags su mdzad snang /

Here, “mudra pointing to the unborn” just means that [Sukhasiddhi’s] finger of her left hand is lifted up toward the sky. The guidebook of Khyenrap Chöje[4] offers different ways of visualizing as follows: Her right hand is in the trident mudra at the heart, indicating the three kāyas. Her left hand in the threatening gesture reveals the unborn. It states that her two legs are in a squatting position, but this would seem to relate to the context of completion phase.
gnyis pa rdzogs rim
B. Completion Phase
['di] la/ chos drug las/ /
From the Six Dharmas:
1. Fierce Inner Heat
dang po thabs lam gtum mo ni/ lus gnad me thab drug chings bya/
First Fierce Inner Heat, the path of methods, the body’s vital point is to assume the sixfold stove [posture].

rlung ro dgu phrugs lag len ltar 'bud/ rang nyid su kha sid+d+hir gsal ba'i lus nang stong pa dar gyi gur phub pa lta bu'i lte ba'i thad kyi dbus su/ me'i pad+ma dmar po 'dab ma bzhi pa/ de'i lte bar a yig dmar po/ 'dab bzhi la shar du ha/ lhor ri/ nub tu ni/ byang du sa rnams kyang kha dog dmar po/

Exhale as in the practice of the ninefold shake-up of dead air. Visualize yourself as Sukhasiddhi, empty inside like a silk tent. In the center, level with the navel, is a red four-petaled lotus of fire, with a red letter A in its center. Of the four petals, ha is in the east, ri in the south, tu in the west, and sa in the north, all of them red.
