gang la zhen med sems can don/ / rig pa mnyam med ngang la zhog / mkha' 'gro ma yi snying gtam yin/ / yang na bde ba bsdus rjes la/ / tha mal shes pa rang dag ni/ / sgom 'dod rtog pas ma bslad par/ / ma bcos ngang du klod la zhog/

Without attachment to anything, for the sake of beings, rest within the state of unequaled awareness. This is the Ḍākinī’s heart advice. Alternatively, after gathering the bliss, rest in innately pure ordinary mind, unpolluted by thoughts of wanting to meditate, and relax into that uncontrived state.
cir yang mi dmigs de kho na/ / phyag rgya chen po zhes su brjod// // /
Only the absence of any reference whatsoever can be called mahāmudrā. ithi
II.
II. Aural Lineage Instructions
gu ru DA ki na mo/
guru ḍāki namo

snyan brgyud kyi gdams pa 'di la gsum ste/ / dang po bzhag thabs rnam pa lngas dngul dkar gyi me long la bltas pas/ byang kyi dkyil (330) 'khor mthong ba bzhin/ / mkha' 'gro rang sems gnyis phyag rgya chen por ngo sprod pa ni/ /

This instruction from the aural lineage has three parts. (1) Through the five techniques for resting, just as you can see the limpid mandala by looking into a silver-white mirror, {330} the introduction to mahāmudrā of both the ḍākinī and your own mind is this:
lus kyi 'khrul 'khor ldan pa yis/ / nam mkha' ris med stong pa la/ / rig bcas sems kyi rtsa ba gcun/ / rtsa ba gcun la lhug par zhog /
With the physical exercise, in empty space without distinction, tame mind’s root with awareness. Intensify the root, then rest relaxed.
rten med du zhog / 'dzin med du zhog / 'jog mkhan med par zhog /
Rest without support. Rest without fixation. Rest without a rester.
gnyis pa nyams su blangs thabs bcus lam du khyer ba ni/
(2) Integrate the practice on the path through ten methods:

mi phod pa brdzi/ 'khri ba bcad/ zhen pa zlog / snang ba bsgyur/ spyod pa dkrug / mtshang yul nas 'don/ rkyen dngos grub tu shes par bya/ / sdug bsngal chos nyid du shes par bya/ / rig pa khrog phyung / snyan brgyud mi la ma spel/

Overcome inability. Cut entanglement. Reverse attachment. Transform perception. Disrupt behavior. Leave the crowded place. Understand conditions as spiritual powers. Understand suffering as the nature of phenomena. Draw out awareness. Do not spread the aural lineage among people.
gsum pa thag chod lngas rdo rje lta bu'i ting nge 'dzin bskyel pa ni/
(3) Develop vajra-like meditative absorption through five convictions:
sems stong bar thag bcad/ stong pa chos skur thag bcad/ chos sku la rgyun chad med par thag bcad/ re dogs med par thag bcad/ 'khor 'das med par thag bcad/ /

Be convinced that mind is empty. Be convinced that emptiness is dharmakāya. Be convinced that dharmakāya is continuous. Be convinced to be without hopes and fears. Be convinced there is no samsara and nirvana.
su kha sid+d+hi snyan brgyud gcig brgyud las med do/ / rdzogs so/ /
This concludes Sukhasiddhi’s aural lineage, which is none other than the single lineage.
sangs rgyas gnyan ston gyi zhal nas/ snyan brgyud kyi gdams pa kha ru mi 'don/ ngo dgar mi btang / / nor du mi tshong / / ched du mi bzhag / snod dang ldan pa la mi sba bar byin gsungs so/ /

Sangye Nyentön proclaimed that the instructions of the aural lineage should not leave one’s mouth. Do not discriminate. Do not sell for wealth. Do not leave it deliberately. Give it to the worthy without concealing it.
su kha ma sid+d+hi phyag rgya chen po'i ngo sprod/ / zab mo gser gyi chos gus pas zhu bar bya'o/ / rdzogs so// // (331)
I humbly offer Sukhamasiddhi’s Introduction to Mahāmudrā, a profound Golden Dharma. It is complete.

Holders of the golden rosary of profound instructions from the king of learned adepts, Khyungpo Naljor, I supplicate you with intense yearning from my heart. With deep compassion, grant your blessings for spiritual powers.
gtum mo'i bde drod 'bar bar byin gyis rlobs/ / zhen med sgyu ma rang shar byin gyis rlobs/ / rmi lam lha skur 'char bar byin gyis rlobs/ / 'od gsal rgyun chad med par byin gyis rlobs/ /

Bless me that bliss-warmth of fierce inner heat blazes. Bless me that illusion arises by itself without attachment. Bless me that the deities’ forms arise in dreams. Bless me that lucid clarity arises without interruption.

'chugs med mkha' spyod 'grub par byin gyis rlobs/ / bar dor sku gsum thob par byin gyis rlobs/ / mtshan tsam thos kyang srid ba hrul byed pa/ / grub chen khyung po'i go 'phang myur thob nas/ / mkha' khyab 'gro ba 'dren par byin gyis rlobs/ /

Bless me to achieve the unerring celestial realm. Bless me to attain the three kāyas in the intermediate state. Just hearing your name tears existence asunder. Bless me to quickly attain the state of the great adept Khyungpo and then lead all migrators throughout space.

By the command of Jampai Pal, the delightful adept of the profound inner path of yoga, and also drawn from my own respectful desire for something short, Dewai Dorje (Jamgön Kongtrul) made this supplication in the abode of strong yearning. Let virtue prevail.

I. Preliminaries
skyabs su 'gro ba dang sems bskyed pa ste/ / ma nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i sems can thams cad skyabs kun 'dus kyi ngo bo bla ma rin po che la skyabs su mchi ba lags so/ / lan gsum/
To go for refuge, repeat this three times: All sentient beings, my mothers, equal to the reaches of space, go for refuge in the precious guru, the unified essence of all refuges.
sems can thams cad kyi don tu zung 'jug rdo rje 'chang chen po'i go 'phang 'thob par bya/ de'i ched du zab lam lha bzhi dril sgrub nyams su blang bar bgyi'o/ / lan gsum/

To arouse the mind of awakening, repeat this three times: For the sake of all sentient beings, I must attain the unified state of Great Vajradhara. To that end, I will engage the profound dharma, Four Deities Combined Practice.
gnyis pa dngos gzhi
II. Main Practice
['di] la gnyis/ bskyed bzlas dang / thun mong ma yin pa'i dbang len pa'o/ /
This has two parts: (1) creation-phase recitation and (2) taking the uncommon empowerment.
dang po ni/
A. Creation Phase Recitation
oM badzra rak+Sha rak+Sha hU~M phaT/ /
oṃ vajra rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ phaṭ
rdo rje'i srung 'khor me phung 'bar ba'i dbus/ / rang nyid dpal ldan 'khor lo sdom pa'i sku/ / gsal ba'i spyi bor chos 'byung bde ba che/ / phyi dkar nang dmar 'od kyi rang bzhin dbus/ /

In the center of the vajra protection circle and blazing fires, I appear clearly in the form of glorious Cakrasaṃvara. Above my head is a source of phenomena, great bliss, white outside and red inside, the nature of light.
pad+ma 'dab bzhi'i lte bar nyi zla'i steng / / hU~M las rdo rje hU~M mtshan yongs su gyur/ / bla ma (337) rdo rje 'chang chen nam mkha'i mdangs/ / zhal gcig phyag gnyis rdo rje dril bu bsnams/ /

Within is a four-petaled lotus, sun and moon in its center. Upon that, from hūṃ a hūṃ-marked vajra completely transforms into the guru, Great Vajradhara, the radiance of space, {337} with one face and two hands holding vajra and bell, embracing his own light:
rang 'od dbyings phyug gri thod 'dzin mar 'khyud/ / dar dang rus pa rin po che yis brgyan pa/ / byin rlabs ye shes 'od zer mu med klong / / rdo rje'i skyil mo gung gis bzhugs pa'o/ /

Vajradhātviśvarī, who holds a flaying knife and skull cup. They are adorned by silks, bones, and precious jewels, sitting in vajra posture in a boundless expanse of light of blessings and timeless awareness.

de mdun nyi mar tshogs bdag bskyel ba'i gdan/ / hU~M las gri gug hU~M gis mtshan pa las/ / ye shes mgon po zhal gcig phyag drug pa/ / char sprin mdog can spyan gsum mche bzhi gtsigs/ / smar smin dbu skra dmar ser gyen tu 'bar/ /

In front of them, on a seat of sun and suppressed Gaṇapati, from hūṃ a hūṃ-marked flaying knife becomes the Awareness Protector with one face and six arms. He is the color of rain clouds, with three eyes and four snarling fangs, orange beard, eyebrows, and hair blazing upward.
g.yas gsum gri gug thod phreng DA ma ru/ / g.yon gsum thod khrag rtse gsum zhags pa bsnams/ / thod pa skam rlon rus pa sprul rigs dang / / li khri'i thig le dril bu g.yer khas brgyan/ /

He holds flaying knife, skull rosary, and ḍamaru in his three right hands and blood-filled skull cup, trident, and lasso with the three left hands. He is adorned by dry and wet skulls, bones, [five] snake types, a smear of vermilion, bells, and little bells.

spyi bor mi bskyod rgyal po'i cod pan mdzes/ / glang ko'i stod g.yogs stag lpags sham thabs can/ / me phung dbus na bzhengs pa'i stabs kyis rol/ / g.yas su nyi steng hrIHdmar gri gug hrIHsa/ / mtshan pa yongs gyur rdo rje rnal 'byor ma/ (338)

His head is beautifully crowned by royal Akṣobhya. He has an elephant-skin cloak and tiger-skin skirt. He sports a standing posture in the midst of blazing bonfire. To the right, on a sun, red hṛīḥ becomes a hṛīḥ-marked flaying knife that completely transforms into red Vajrayoginī. {338}
dmar mo gzhon tshul zhal 'dzum bzhad pa'i nyams/ / spyan gsum g.yon gzigs lcang lo sil bur 'phyangs/ / phyag g.yas gri gug zur sdigs g.yon pa yis/ / bdud rtsis gang ba'i thod pa steng nas gsol/ /

She is youthful and smiling, with an expression of laughter. Her three eyes glance left, her locks fall loosely. Her right hand holds a flaying knife downward, threatening, and her left holds up a skull cup full of elixir for her to drink.

kha T+wAM ga 'phyang phyag rgya lnga yis spras/ / g.yas brkyang stabs kyis 'jigs dus mnan pa'o/ / rgyab tu zla ba'i gdan la hrIHyig las/ / pad dkar hrIHsa mtshan yongs gyur spyan ras gzigs/ / dkar gsal phyag g.yas skyabs sbyin bum pas mtshan/ / g.yon pas pad dkar sdong bu thugs kar bsnams/ /

She bears a khaṭvāṅga and wears the five symbolic ornaments. She stands with right leg extended, trampling Bhairava and Kālarātri. In back, on a moon seat, hrīḥ becomes a hrīḥ-marked white lotus that completely transforms into pure white Avalokita, his right hand with a vase grants refuge,[2] his left holds a white lotus stem to his heart.
dbu skra sil bu 'od dpag med pas brgyan/ / zhabs g.yas brkyang zhing g.yon bskum stabs kyis bzhugs/ / g.yon phyogs zla steng tAM las ut+pa la/ / tAM mtshan yongs gyur Ar+Ya tA re ljang / /

The locks of his hair are crowned by Amitābha. He is seated in the posture of right leg extended and left drawn in. To the left, on a moon, tāṃ becomes a tāṃ-marked utpala, and completely transforms into green Exalted Tārā.
bcu drug sgeg nyams don grub dbu rgyan can/ / g.yas g.yon skyabs sbyin ut+pal rab rgyas 'dzin/ / rgyan ldan g.yas brkyang g.yon bskum rol pas 'gying / / kun gyi gnas gsum oM AHhU~M gis mtshan/ /

She is charming as a sixteen-year-old, crowned by Amoghasiddhi. Her right hand gives refuge, her left holds a blooming utpala. With ornaments, she deports majestically with right extended and left drawn in. All of the deities are marked with oṃ āḥ hūṃ in their three places.
hU~M las 'od 'phros rtsa gsum dkon mchog gsum/ / bla ma lha bzhi'i rnam par spyan drangs thim/ dzaHhU~M baM hoHskyabs gnas thams cad 'dus pa'i ngo bor gyur/ /

Light radiates from the hūṃs, invoking the Three Roots and Three Jewels in the forms of the guru and four deities, who then dissolve [into the visualized forms]. jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ—they become the united essence of all refuge sources.

bla ma rin po che lha bzhi'i tshogs la bdag gis phyi me tog bdug spos/ / nang sha lnga bdud rtsi lnga/ / gsang ba bde stong gi ye shes/ / yang gsang de kho na nyid kyi mchod pa la sogs pa mchod pa'i khyad par bsam gyis mi khyab pas mchod cing mnyes par bgyi'o/ / bzhes nas byin gyis brlab tu gsol/ /

Precious guru and group of four deities: outwardly I offer flowers and incense; inwardly five meats and five elixirs; secretly the awareness of bliss-emptiness; and more secretly the offering of suchness. These and other special unimaginable offerings I present for your pleasure. Partake of them and please grant your blessings.
byin rlabs ma lus 'byung ba'i sgo/ / dngos grub ma lus thob pa'i gnas/ / bar chad ma lus sel ba'i lha/ / bla ma lha bzhi'i tshogs la 'dud/ /
Door for the entry of every blessing, place of attainment of every spiritual power, deities for dispelling every obstacle: I bow to the guru and four deities.
dam pa kha cig gis mchod bstod 'di'i tshab tu yan lag bdun (339) pa dang maN+Dal 'bul ba'ang bzhed/ /
Some holy masters have suggested substituting a seven-branch service and mandala offering for these offerings and praise. {339}

de nas dbus kyi bla ma la dmigs pa'i mos gus bcas/ na mo bud+d+hA ya/ na mo gu ru he/ badzra bI ra bI ra NI/ shrI DA ka DA ki nI/ dzo ka dzo ki nI/ sarba bud+d+ha bo d+hi sa twA ya sha ra Ni gats+tsha mi kyai/ zhes bzlas/
Focus on the guru in the center with devotion and repeat the mantra: namo buddhāya / namo guruhe / vajra vīra vīriṇī / śrī ḍāka ḍākinī / joka jokinī / sarva buddha bodhisatvāya śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi kyai
bla ma'i sku las bdud rtsi'i chu rgyun bab/ / rang gi spyi bo nas zhugs lus kun gang / / sdig sgrib nyes ltung nad gdon bar chad dag / bla ma'i gsang gsum byin rlabs thob par gyur/

A stream of elixir falls from Guru’s form, enters the crown of my head, fills my body, and purifies negatives, obscurations, faults, downfalls, sickness, spirits, and obstacles. I have attained the blessings of Guru’s three secrets.
mdun gyi mgon po la dmigs te/ / oM badzra ma hA kA la k+ShiM k+She tra bi g+h+naM bi nA ya ka hU~M hU~M phaT phaT swA hA/ zhes bzlas/ /
Focus on the protector in front and repeat the mantra: oṃ vajra mahākāla kṣiṃ kṣetra vighanāṃ vināyāka hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā
mgon po'i sku las bdud rtsi'i chu rgyun bab/ / rang gi spyi bo nas zhugs lus kun gang / / sdig sgrib nyes ltung nang gdon bar chad dag / mgon po'i gsang gsum byin rlabs thob par gyur/ /

A stream of elixir falls from Protector’s form, enters the crown of my head, fills my body, and purifies negatives, obscurations, faults, downfalls, sickness, spirits, and obstacles. I have attained the blessings of Protector’s three secrets.

g.yas kyi rnal 'byor ma la dmigs te/ oM badzra na ra kraM kraM hU~M hU~M phaT phaT swA hA/ zhes bzla ba ni yig rnying gi dngos bstan yin la/ phyis kyi phyag len kha cig tu 'di la oM gsum ma bzla bar gsungs/ /

Focus on Vajrayoginī on the right and repeat the mantra: oṃ vajra nara kraṃ kraṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā This recitation is the actual mantra presented in the ancient texts. In some later practices, it is taught to recite the three-oṃ mantra here.[3]
rnal 'byor ma las bdud rtsi'i chu rgyun bab/ / rang gi spyi bo nas zhugs lus kun gang / / sdig sgrib nyes ltung nad gdon bar chad dag / phag mo'i gsang gsum byin rlabs thob par gyur/

A stream of elixir falls from Yoginī’s form, enters the crown of my head, fills my body, and purifies negatives, obscurations, faults, downfalls, sickness, spirits, and obstacles. I have attained the blessings of Vārāhī’s three secrets.
rgyab kyi spyan ras gzigs la dmigs te/ oM ma ni pad+me hU~M/ oM badzra rak+Sha na maHsa man+ta hU~M phaT/ zhes bzla/ /
Focus on Avalokita in the back and repeat the mantra: oṃ maṇi padme hūṃ / oṃ vajra rakṣa namaḥ samanta hūṃ phaṭ
'phags pa'i sku las bdud rtsi'i chu rgyun bab/ / rang gi spyi bo nas zhugs lus kun gang / / sdig sgrib nyes ltung nad gdon bar chad dag / 'phags pa'i gsang gsum byin rlabs thob par gyur/ /

A stream of elixir falls from Exalted One’s form, enters the crown of my head, fills my body, and purifies negatives, obscurations, faults, downfalls, sickness, spirits, and obstacles. I have attained the blessings of Exalted One’s three secrets.
g.yon gyi sgrol ma la dmigs te/ oM tA re tut+ta re tu re swA hA/ zhes bzla/ /
Focus on Tārā on the left and repeat the mantra: oṃ tāre tuttāre ture svāhā
sgrol ma'i sku las bdud rtsi'i chu rgyun bab/ / rang gi spyi bo nas zhugs lus kun gang / / sdig sgrib nyes ltung nad gdon bar chad dag / sgrol ma'i gsang gsum byin rlabs thob par gyur/ /

A stream of elixir falls from Tārā’s form, enters the crown of my head, fills my body, and purifies negatives, obscurations, faults, downfalls, sickness, spirits, and obstacles. I have attained the blessings of Tārā’s three secrets.

'di'i bsnyen pa ched du byed na/ na mo bud+d+ha cung zad mang ba dang / gzhan bzhi po cha snyoms nas bzla/ (340) mgon po'i bsnyen pa'i thog mar 'di nyid btang skabs mgon bsnyen nyid bungs bskyed par gsungs pa dang / khrid rgyun tu rnal 'byor ma'i oM gsum ma gtso bor bzla bar gsungs pa de ngag gi rnal 'byor gtsor bton pa la dgongs par mngon zhing / 'dir rgyun gyi bzlas par brgya'am bdun la sogs pa cha snyoms pa kho na bzla ba dang / / spros pas mi lcogs pa'i skabs su so so'i dmigs pa'i tshigs bcad rnams dor te bstod pa'i rjes kho nar sngags rnams tshar gsum gsum bzla ba'i tshe/ /

When you do this for the sake of accumulating the recitation, repeat the namo buddha mantra a bit more, and the other four in equal measure. {340} If you do this at the beginning of Protector’s recitation practice, it is said to bolster Protector’s recitation itself. In the course of [other] guidances, it is taught to principally recite Yoginī’s three-oṃ mantra. These [authors] apparently had in mind Yoginī as the main practice. Here, as a daily recitation, just repeat all the mantras in equal numbers, such as one hundred or seven times each. On occasions when you are unable to do the elaborate version, skip the verses of the individual visualizations and after just the praises repeat each mantra three times. Then say:
bla ma lha las bdud rtsi'i chu rgyun bab/ / rang gi spyi bo nas zhugs lus kun gang / / sdig sgrib nyes ltung nad gdon bar chad dag / bla ma lha bzhi'i gsang gsum byin thob gyur/ / zhes so/ /

A stream of elixir falls from the guru and deities, enters the crown of my head, fills my body, and purifies negatives, obscurations, faults, downfalls, sickness, spirits, and obstacles. I have attained the blessings of the guru’s and deities’ three secrets.
gnyis pa ni/
B. Taking the Uncommon Empowerment
rgyas bsdus gang ltar bzlas bsgom grub pa'i thun mthar sngags tshan lnga spel ba'am/ na mo bud+d+ha lan gsum gyis gsol ba btab pas/ /
At the conclusion of either the long or short session of recitation-meditation, augment it with repeating the five mantras or by repeating namo buddha…(etc.) three times, as supplication.

bla ma'i thugs ka'i hU~M las 'od zer 'phros/ / lha bzhi tshur bsdus spyi bor spyan ras gzigs/ / mgrin par sgrol ma thugs kar nag po che/ / lte bar rnal 'byor ma bzhugs slar yang 'od/ / phros pas rgyal ba sras bcas spyan drangs te/ / bla ma'i sku las yongs su gtams par gyur/

Light rays radiate from the hūṃ in the guru’s heart and gather in the four deities: Avalokita to the head, Tārā to the throat, Great Black to the heart, and Yoginī to the navel; light radiates again, invoking the victors and their heirs. They completely fill up the guru’s body.
'og rlung bskum/ rlung bum can nam bar rlung bzung la/ / gsang gnas rlung g.yos lte ba'i gtum mo 'bar/ / tshangs bug nas thon chos 'byung dros pa yis/ / bla ma'i skur phog lha rnams bde bar zhu/ /

Draw up the lower wind and hold the vase breathing or the intermediate breathing. Wind stirs in the secret place, igniting fierce inner heat at the navel. That emerges from the cranial aperture, heats the source of phenomena, strikes the guru’s form, and the deities melt in bliss.
bdud rtsi'i rgyun byung rang gi spyi bo nas/ mgrin pa yan gang lus kyi sdig sgrib dag / bum pa'i dbang thob sku yi byin rlabs zhugs/ / snying ga yan gang ngag gi sdig sgrib dag /

A stream of elixir emerges, enters the crown of my head, fills above the throat, and purifies physical negativities and obscurations. I obtain the vase empowerment; the blessings of awakened body enter. It fills above the heart and purifies verbal negativities and obscurations.
gsang ba'i dbang thob gsung gi byin rlabs zhugs/ / lte ba yan gang yid kyi sdig sgrib dag / shes rab dbang thob thugs kyi byin rlabs zhugs/ / lus kun gang bas sgo gsum sdig sgrib dag /

I obtain the secret empowerment; the blessings of awakened speech enter. It fills above the navel and purifies mental negativities and obscurations. I obtain the wisdom empowerment; the blessings of awakened mind enter. It fills my whole body and purifies negativities and obscurations of all three doors.
bzhi pa'i dbang thob byin rlabs yongs su rdzogs/ / chos 'byung 'od yal bla ma rang la thim/ / sgo gsum rdo rje (341) gsum dang dbyer med gyur/ /
gsum pa rjes
III. Conclusion
['di] la gnyis/ mnyam par bzhag pa dang / thun mtshams kyi bya ba'o/ /
This has two parts: (1) resting in equipoise and (2) the activities in the session breaks.
dang po ni/
A. Resting in Equipoise
bla ma rang sems dbyer med du 'dres de ka'i rang ngo la bzo bcos dgag sgrub med par rang ngo shes tsam gyi ngang ci gnas su bskyang ngo /
Maintain that very state of the inseparable merging of the guru with one’s own mind for as long as it lasts, without any fabrication, restriction, or affirmation—just mere recognition.
gnyis pa ni/
B. Activities in the Session Breaks
de las ldangs pa na shes bzhin gyi dran pa'i rang so ma nyams par/
When you arise from that, without letting mindful awareness dissipate, seal with dedication and aspiration prayers:
kun tu sangs rgyas thams cad kyis/ / rdo rje 'chang chen go 'phang ldan/ / bdag gi dge ba 'dis thob ste/ / 'gro kun gyis kyang thob par shog /
All buddhas at all times possess the state of Great Vajradhara. Through my virtue may I attain that and may all migrators also attain it.

rdzogs pa'i byang chub phyir spyod dang / / rdzogs sangs rgyas nas gang spyod pa/ / byang chub rdo rjes bsngags pa yi/ / spyod de gnyis ka'ang bdag spyod shog / ces sogs bsngo smon gyi rgyas gdab ste spyod lam la 'jug go /
Conduct for the sake of perfect awakening and any conduct after perfect buddhahood was praised by the Awakened Vajra; may I practice those two conducts.[4] Then go about your activities.
[Concluding Verse and Colophon]
gegs sel bogs 'don mchog dngos kyi/ / grub pa lo zlas ster byed pa/ / ches zab rnal 'byor 'di bsgoms nas/ / zhing rdul snyed kyi 'gro sgrol shog/ /
Good for dispelling obstacles and enhancing practice in a matter of years or months, after meditating on this yoga of profound dharma may as many beings be freed as atoms in the realm.

ces pa'ang yang khrod kun bzang bde chen 'od gsal gling gi sgrub la gzhol ba rnams kyi nyams bzhes nye bar mkho bas mtshams sbyar te/ karma ngag dbang yon tan rgya mtshos bla ma'i gsung rgyun bzhin bris pa dge legs 'phel// (342) (343)

Karma Ngawang Yönten Gyatso wrote this according to the guru’s teaching transmission to make the connection with the required practices for those dedicated to accomplishment in the secluded retreat of Kunzang Dechen Ösal Ling. Let virtue prevail!
@#/ /dpal ldan shangs pa bka' brgyud kyi zab chos lha bzhi dril sgrub kyi khrid yig ye shes 'od 'phro zhes bya ba bzhugs so// //
24. Radiant Light of Timeless Awareness. A Guidebook on the Four Deities Combined Practice, a Profound Dharma of the Glorious Shangpa Kagyu[1]
(344)@#/ /na mo gu ru tsa tu rde bA ya/ /
namo guru caturdevāyā
mchog gi grub stsol dpal ldan bla ma dang / / phyi nang gegs sel yon tan bogs 'don pa/ / byin rlabs lha bzhi'i zhabs la phyag byas te/ / de yi khrid rim mdo tsam gsal bar bya/ /

I bow to the glorious guru who bestows supreme spiritual powers, and to the four blessing deities who dispel outer and inner hindrances and enhance good qualities. I will briefly clarify the guidance sequence.

mkhas grub chen po khyung po rnal 'byor pa de nyid kyis ye shes DA ki rnam pa gnyis gtso bor gyur pa'i rgya gar mkhas grub brgya dang lnga bcu'i thugs bcud rdzogs par gsol bas shangs pa bka' brgyud kyi ring lugs 'dzin pa'i skyes chen rnams la mdo sngags kyi zab chos rgya mtsho tsam gyi gzhung dang gdams pa'i bka' yongs su rdzogs pa mnga' zhing mchog gi grub pa nyams 'og tu chud pa sha stag byon pa lags/ / deng sang rgyun bzhugs pa'i gtso bo gdams ngag gi skor bzhi'am lngar grags pa las/ 'dir rgya gar lho phyogs pa 'chi ba med pa'i rig 'dzin brnyes nas mchog gi go 'phang mthon por gshegs pa grub chen rA hu la gup+ta'i gdams pa dang gtso bor 'brel pa lha bzhi dril sgrub kyi khrid kyi rim pa 'chad pa la gnyis/ gang las byung ba brgyud pa'i lo rgyus mdor smos/ de las byung ba khrid rim (345) dngos rgyas par 'chad pa'o/ /

The great learned adept Khyungpo Naljor received the complete heart essence of one hundred and five Indian adepts, principal among whom were the two ḍākinīs of timeless awareness. The great individuals who held this long lineage tradition of Shangpa Kagyu always mastered the perfectly complete precepts of authoritative texts and instructions from the vast ocean of the profound dharma of Sutra and Mantra and were exclusively those who were grounded in the experience of supreme accomplishment. Of the four or five well-known instruction cycles that have continued to the present time, here I will explain the stages of guidance of the Four Deities Combined Practice, the instructions of the great adept Rāhulagupta, with whom this practice is primarily associated. He was a South Indian who had attained the state of an immortal awareness holder and reached the heights of supreme accomplishment. This presentation has two parts: (1) the brief story of the origins of the lineage and (2) the extensive explanation of the actual stages of guidance that came from [that lineage]. {345}
dang po ni/
I. Story of the Origins of the Lineage

grub chen sha ba ri dbang phyug la lha bzhis zhal gzigs shing sgrub thabs gsungs/ de la mnga' bdag mai tri pas gsan te sgrub thabs bkod/ mkhas grub khyung pos 'di las kyang gsan par gsal te byin rlabs lha bzhi 'bral ba med ces 'byung bas mgon po'i gsan yul gtso bor yin pa'i phyir ro/ /

The four deities were revealed in visionary experience to the great adept mighty Śavarῑpa, and he taught their method of accomplishment (sādhana). Master Maitrīpa listened to those teachings and arranged the sādhana. Clearly the learned adept Khyungpo received it from this [master], as he said he had “the constant blessings of the four deities.” Besides, it was primarily from [Maitrīpa that Khyungpo also] received the Awareness Protector.

'on kyang gdams ngag 'di'i brgyud khungs gtso bo ni grub chen rA hu la gup+ta badzra ste/ de nyid rgya gar lho phyogs el b+hi sha zhes pa rdo rje mkha' 'gros byin gyis brlabs pa'i sa gzhir rgyal rigs su sku 'khrungs ma thag nas lha bzhi zhal gzigs shing byin gyis brlabs/ gzhon nu'i skabs su sngon las kyi lhag ma bsnyun drag por smin pas thugs byung ste chos la zhugs shing mdo sngags thams cad la ches mkhas par sbyangs/ gu Na sA ga ra dang rat+na sA ga ra sogs kyi gdams ngag la brten te thun mong gi dngos grub bde blag tu grub/ mthar sku tsho'i rig 'dzin brnyes shing phyag rgya chen po'i mchog grub pa

But the main source of this lineage of instructions is the great adept Rāhulaguptavajra. He was born in the south of India, in a land blessed by Vajraḍākinī called Elabhiśa. As soon as he was born into the royal caste, he saw the four deities face to face and was blessed by them. When he was young, the residual karma from previous lives ripened as severe illness, causing a sense of sadness. He entered the dharma and trained until he was very learned in all sutras and tantras. He relied on the instructions of Guṇasāgara, Ratnasāgara, and others, easily attaining the common spiritual powers. Ultimately he attained the longevity of an awareness holder and the supreme accomplishment of mahāmudrā. {346}

de nyid la grub pa'i (346) bla ma rnams kyi bkas bskul te mkhas grub khyung po rnal 'byor 'phan yul 'jog por chig rir mdzad pa'i skabs chos sgo skyel gyi tshul du rgya gar na nyi ma shar ba dang rdzu 'phrul gyis byon pas bod la nyi ma ma shar ba la pheb/ / ring zhig bzhugs te mgon po dkar mthing / rlung shing rta can la sogs pa'i gdams ngag zab mo du ma dang / / khyad par lha bzhi'i gdams skor cha lag dang bcas pa gnang ba khyung po nyid kyis thugs nyams su bzhes pas slob ma las dag pa rnams la lha bzhi'i skur dngos su snang ba sogs grub pa chen po nyams 'og tu chud/ de nyid kyis rmog lcogs pa sogs la gnang ba nas byin rlabs dang gdams pa'i bka' srol bar ma chad du byon te kho bos rdo rje theg pa'i gsang ba thun mong dang thun mong ma yin pa mtha' dag gi gsang mdzod 'dzin pa la rdo rje 'chang chen po dang dbyer ma mchis pa/ 'phags pa'i sa chen po la bzhugs shing mi las 'das pa'i skyes chen 'jam dbyangs mkhyen brtse'i dbang po la gsol ba btab ste dgyes bzhin bka' drin tu stsal ba yin/ /

Rāhula was requested by his accomplished gurus to [visit] Khyungpo Naljor while Khyungpo was doing a solitary retreat at Penyul Jokpo (’phen yul ’jog po). He was sent off in the manner of a dharma path, leaving India at daybreak and miraculously arriving before the sun rose in Tibet. He stayed a while, giving Khyungpo Naljor many profound instructions, such as White and Deep-Blue Protectors (mgon po dkar mthing), and the Chariot of Vital Winds.[2] In particular, he bestowed the cycle of Four Deities Combined Practice with its supplemental material. Khyungpo took it to heart in practice and became a great adept, such that his disciples with pure karma could actually perceive him in the forms of the four deities. He in turn passed the practice to Mokchokpa and others, and from there the system of transmission of the blessings and instructions has continued without interruption to the present. I supplicated Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo for them. That great person who is inseparable from Great Vajradhara and holds the secret treasury of the entire corpus of common and uncommon mysteries of our Vajrayāna, who dwells on the great level of the exalted ones beyond human [experience], kindly granted it to me.

rmog lcogs pa rin chen brtson 'grus la lha bzhis sgrub thabs dngos su gsungs pa dang / brgyud pa kha cig la DA ki bde ba'i dngos grub mas gnang ba'ang bshad pa'i phyir nye brgyud khyad par ba de dag kyang 'dir 'dul/ 'di la'ang lha bzhi'i sgos sgrub dang dril sgrub gnyis su yod par bshad pa las skabs su bab pa'i 'chad bya ni lha bzhi'i dril sgrub nyid yin no/ /

Here I have gathered the special direct lineage of the sādhana actually imparted to Mokchokpa Rinchen Tsöndru by the four deities and explanations and permissions that Spiritual Power of Bliss (Sukhasiddhi) gave to some lineage holders. In general there are two explanations: the practice of the four deities separately and the combined practice. Of those, the subject to be explained on this occasion will be the Four Deities Combined Practice.
gnyis pa brgyud pa de ldan gyi gdams ngag dngos 'chad pa
II. The Actual Instructions of Those with That Lineage
['di] la'ang gsum/ sngon 'gro/ dngos gzhi/ rjes kyi rim pa'o/ /
This has three parts: (1) the stages of the preliminaries, (2) main practice, and (3) conclusion.
dang po
A. Preliminaries
['di] la gnyis/
1. Session Preliminary
thun gyi sngon 'gro ni/ mal bde bar 'dug / lus gnad spyi mthun bca'/ rlung ro bsal la dran pa mngon tu bzhag /
The session preliminary is to take a comfortable seat and assume the physical vital points of posture as usual. Expel the dead winds and settle into mindfulness.
khrid kyi sngon 'gro
2. Guidance Preliminary
['di] la'ang gnyis/ (347) skyabs su 'gro ba dang sems bskyed pa'o/ /
The guidance preliminary has two parts: (1) going for refuge and (2) arousing the awakening mind. {347}
dang po ni/
a. Refuge

mdun gyi nam mkhar seng khri pad+ma nyi zla'i gdan la dkon mchog skyabs gnas kun 'dus kyi ngo bo rtsa ba'i bla ma nyid rdo rje 'chang chen po'i rnam par bzhugs pa la bdag gzhan nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i 'gro ba mtha' dag sgo gsum 'jug pa gcig tu dril te/ deng nas byang chub ma thob kyi bar du skyabs su 'gro ba'i blo rtse gcig pas/ ma nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i sems can thams cad skyabs kun 'dus kyi ngo bo bla ma rin po che la skyabs su mchi ba lags so/ / zhes grangs ci nus su brjod/

In the space before you, on a lotus-sun-moon seat on a lion throne, your actual root guru, who is the unified essence of the Three Jewels and all refuge sources, appears in the form of Great Vajradhara. You and all others, the whole range of migrators throughout the reaches of space, with your three doors combined in unison, go for refuge with single-pointed mind from now until attaining awakening. Repeat as much as you can: All sentient beings, my mothers, equal to the reaches of space, go for refuge in the precious guru, the unified essence of all refuges.
gnyis pa ni/
b. Awakening Mind

mkha' khyab kyi sems can ji snyed pa de thams cad bdag gi pha ma drin can sha stags yin/ 'di rnams 'khor ba sdug bsngal gyi rgya mtshor thar dus med par 'khyams pa snying re rje/ 'di rnams 'khor ba las bsgral ba'i slad du bdag gis zung 'jug rdo rje 'chang chen po'i go 'phang dus myur ba nyid du thob nges pa zhig bya snyam pa smon pa byang chub kyi sems dang / de 'thob par bya ba'i slad du rdo rje theg pa'i lam rim gyi zab gnad gcig tu bsdus pa'i nye lam grub thob 'ba' zhig pa'i snyan brgyud lha bzhi dril sgrub kyi rnal 'byor zab mo nyams su blangs pas/ bla ma lha bzhi'i go 'phang myur du 'grub pa dang / sems can thams cad de'i go 'phang la 'gong par bgyi'o snyam pa'i 'jug pa byang chub tu sems bskyed la/ ngag tu/ sems can thams cad kyi don tu zung 'jug rdo rje 'chang chen po'i go 'phang 'thob par bya/ de'i ched du zab lam lha bzhi dril sgrub nyams su blang bar bgyi'o/ / zhes lan kha yar brjod/ skyabs yul mi dmigs par bzhag /

Think, “Sentient beings throughout space, however many there are, have all been exclusively kind parents to me. They wander in the ocean of suffering in cyclic existence with no chance to escape—how pitiful! In order to liberate them from cyclic existence, I must definitely attain Great Vajradhara’s state of integral unity quickly.” This is the awakening mind of aspiration. Then think, “In order to attain that, I must cultivate the experience of the profound yoga of Four Deities Combined Practice that comes from an aural lineage consisting exclusively of adepts, a short path that gathers into one profound vital point the stages of the path of Vajrayāna. Through that, I will quickly attain the state of the guru and four deities and place all sentient beings in that state as well.” This is the awakening mind of engagement. Verbally recite: For the sake of all sentient beings, I must attain the unified state of Great Vajradhara. To that end, I will engage the profound dharma, Four Deities Combined Practice. Repeat that a number of times. Then rest without reference to the refuge objects.
gnyis pa dngos gzhi
B. Main Practice
['di] la'ang gnyis/ bskyed bzlas kyi rnal 'byor ngang / zab mo'i dbang len pa'o/ /
This has two parts: (1) the yoga of creation-phase recitation and (2) taking the profound empowerment. {348}
dang po ni/
1. The Yoga of Creation Phase Recitation

oM badzra rak+Sha rak+Sha (348) hU~M phaT/ zhes brjod pa'i rkyen gyis rdo rje'i sa gzhi ra ba dra ba gur bla bre phyi rol du ye shes kyi me 'bar ba dang bcas pa'i srung ba'i 'khor lo'i dbus su/ pad nyi 'jigs dus kyi gdan la rang nyid bcom ldan 'das 'khor lo sdom pa lhan skyes 'od phung gi klong na bzhugs par gsal ba'i spyi bor chos 'byung dwangs gsal rnyogs med 'od kyi rang bzhin phyi dkar la nang dmar ba/ rtsa ba phra ba rang gi tshangs bug tu zug cing kha gdengs g.yel ba/ bde bar 'char zhing bde ba rgyas pa'i dbus su rab tu rgyas pa'i sna tshogs pad+ma 'dab ma bzhi pa/ de'i lte ba'i ze'u 'bru khru gang tsam mtho ba'i steng du nyi zla brtsegs pa'i gdan la hU~M sngon po las rdo rje sngon po hU~M gis mtshan pa yongs su gyur pa las/ ngo bo rtsa ba'i bla ma/ rnam pa rdo rje 'chang chen po sku mdog bai DUr+Ya'i mdangs can/ phyag gnyis kyis rdo rje dang dril bu bsnol thabs su 'dzin pas yum rdo rje dbyings kyi dbang phyug ma gri gug dang thod pa 'dzin pa la 'khyud pa/ yab yum gnyis ka rus pa dang rin po ches brgyan cing dar gyi na bzas klubs pa/ zhabs rdo rje'i skyil mo krung dang pad skyil can/ byin rlabs dang ye shes kyi rang 'od mtha' yas pa spro ba/

By your saying “oṃ vajra rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ phaṭ” there appears a protection circle with vajra ground, enclosure, lattice, tent, and canopy, with a blazing fire of awareness outside. In its center, on a seat of the sun disk with Bhairava and Kālarātri, you appear clearly as Bhagavat Coemergent Cakrasaṃvara within an expansive mass of light. Above your head is a source of phenomena, brilliantly clear and unsullied, the nature of light, white outside and red inside. The lower vertex touches your cranial aperture while the wide opening faces upward. It arises as bliss and expands bliss. In its center is a fully blossomed four-petaled multicolored lotus with stamens that rise a cubit in height. Upon them, on a stacked seat of the sun and moon, blue hūṃ becomes a blue vajra marked by hūṃ. That completely transforms into the essence of your root guru in the form of Great Vajradhara, the color of radiant vaiḍūrya. His two crossed hands hold vajra and bell, embracing Vajradhātviśvarī, who holds a flaying knife and skull cup. They are both adorned by bones and precious jewels, and clothed in silks. They sit in vajra posture and lotus posture [respectively], radiating the boundless light of blessings and timeless awareness.

de'i mdun phyogs kyi pad 'dab la nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor gyi steng du tshogs bdag dkar po gan rkyal du bsgyel ba'i gdan la hU~M nag po las gri gug hU~M gis mtshan pa/ de yongs su gyur pa las myur mdzad ye shes kyi mgon po phyag drug pa/ sku mdog dus mtha'i sprin ltar gnag pa/ spyan gsum dmar la zlum pa/ zhal bsgrad cing mche ba gtsigs pa/ sma ra dang smin ma dbu skra dmar ser me ltar du 'bar zhing gyen du brdzes pa/ dpral bar sin+d+hu ra'i thig les byugs shing spyi bor mi bskyod pas brgyan pa/ phyag g.yas kyi dang pos gnam lcags kyi gri gug / bar pas thod (349) skam gyi phreng ba/ tha mas seng ldeng gi DA ma ru drag tu 'khrol ba/ g.yon gyi dang pos thod pa dmar chen gyis bkang ba/ bar pas mdung rtse gsum pa/ tha mas rdo rje'i zhags pa bsnams pa/ thod pa skam po lnga'i dbu rgyan dang rlon pa khrag 'dzag pa lnga bcu'i dor shal can/ rus pa'i rgyan cha drug dang sbrul chun rigs lnga dang phyag zhabs rnams la dril bu g.yer kha'i phreng bas brgyan pa/ sbom thung lto ba 'phyang zhing yan lag rags pa/ glang chen ko rlon stod la g.yogs shing stag lpags rlon pa'i sham thabs la dar ljang gu'i ska rags bcings pa/ zhabs bzhengs stabs 'gro 'phro la 'chams pa lta bus ye shes kyi me 'bar ba'i klong na bzhugs pa/

On the lotus petal in front, on the sun-disk mandala, white Gaṇapati lies face up.[3] On that seat, black hūṃ becomes a flaying knife marked by hūṃ. That completely transforms into Swift-Acting Awareness Protector, Six-Armed Mahākāla. He is as dark as the clouds at the end of time, with three round red eyes, and fangs bared in his open mouth. His orange eyebrows, whiskers, and hair stream upward like flames of fire. His forehead is smeared with a drop of vermilion, and Akṣobhya crowns his head. He holds a meteorite flaying knife in his top right hand, a skull rosary in the middle hand, {349} and fiercely rattles a sandalwood ḍamaru in the lower right hand. He holds a skull cup filled with human blood in his upper left hand, a trident in the middle hand, and a vajra lasso in the lower left hand. He wears a crown of five dry skulls and a garland of fifty wet skulls dripping with blood. He is adorned by the six bone ornaments and bunches of five types of snake, with bells and small bells on his arms and legs. He is short and stocky, with thick limbs and protruding belly. His upper body is cloaked in a wet elephant skin, and he wears a wet tiger-skin skirt cinched by a green silk belt. His legs are in standing posture, [with right foot raised] as if mobilized to move. He stands in an expanse of blazing flames of timeless awareness.

bla ma'i g.yas phyogs kyi pad 'dab la nyi ma'i gdan gyi steng du hrIHdmar po las gri gug hrIHsa mtshan pa yongs su gyur pa las/ rje btsun rdo rje rnal 'byor ma sku mdog dmar la smug pa'i mdangs chags pa/ lo bcu drug lon pa'i lang tsho can/ zhal 'dzum zhing mche ba nas tsam 'bur ba/ spyan gsum g.yon phyogs su gzigs pa/ phyag g.yas gri gug thur du brkyang zhing / g.yon thod pa bdud rtsis gang ba steng phyogs su bzung nas zhal du gsol ba/ mchan khung g.yon na rdo rje'i kha T+wAM ga dang bcas shing rus pa'i phyag rgya lngas brgyan pa/ zhabs g.yas brkyangs pas 'jig byed g.yon bskums pas dus mtshan ma mnan pa/ ye shes kyi rang zer kun tu 'bar ba/

The lotus petal to the right of the guru has a sun seat upon which a red hrīḥ becomes a flaying knife marked by hrīḥ. That completely transforms into Exalted Vajrayoginī, who is red with a maroon radiance, youthful as a sixteen-year-old. As she smiles, her eyeteeth protrude slightly. Her three eyes glance to the left. Her right hand holds a flaying knife downward, and her left holds up a skull cup full of elixir for her to drink. She has a khaṭvāṅga in the bend of her left elbow and is adorned by the five symbolic ornaments. She stands with right leg extended, trampling on Bhairava, and the left bent, pressing on Kālarātri. The rays of her timeless awareness blaze everywhere.

bla ma'i rgyab kyi pad 'dab la zla ba'i dkyil 'khor gyi steng du hrIHdkar po las pad+ma dkar po hrIHsa mtshan pa yongs su gyur pa las/ 'phags pa spyan ras gzigs zla ba'i mdog can/ zhi zhing 'dzum la dar dang rin po che'i rgyan thams cad kyis brgyan pa/ dbu skra dpung pa'i steng na nag sil le 'phyang zhing 'od dpag med kyi cod pan dang ldan pa/ phyag g.yas mchog sbyin gyi phyag rgyas bum pa bsnams (350) shing g.yon pa'i ma theb srin sbyar bas me tog pad+ma dkar po snyan gyi thad kar kha bye ba'i yu ba thugs kar 'dzin pa/ zhabs g.yas brkyangs shing g.yon bskums pa'i stabs kyis 'ja' zer kyi klong na bzhugs pa/

On the lotus petal in back of the guru is a white hrīḥ on a moon mandala, which becomes a white lotus marked by hrīḥ. That completely transforms into Exalted Avalokita, the color of the moon. He is peaceful and smiling, adorned by all the silks and precious ornaments. His hair is piled on top with locks falling loosely, crowned by Amitābha. {350} His right hand holds a vase with the mudra of supreme generosity, and his left hand grasps the stem of a white lotus flower with thumb and ring finger at his heart; the full blossom is near his left ear. He sits in the position of right leg extended and left contracted, within an expanse of rainbow light.

bla ma'i g.yon gyi pad 'dab la zla ba'i steng du tAM ljang gu las ut+pal ljang gu tAM gis mtshan pa yongs su gyur pa las/ rje btsun sgrol ma sku mdog ljang gu/ lang tsho dar la bab cing lo bcu drug lon pa'i rnam pa can dar dang rin po ches brgyan pa/ phyag g.yas mchog sbyin pus mo'i steng du brkyangs shing g.yon dkon mchog gsum mtshon pa'i phyag rgyas ut+pal ljang gu'i yu ba thugs kar bsnams pa'i 'dab ma snyan gyi thad du kha bye ba/ don yod grub pa'i dbu rgyan can/ zhabs g.yas cung zad brkyangs shing g.yon bskums pa'i stabs kyis rang 'od kyi dbus na bzhugs pa ste

On the lotus petal to the guru’s left, upon the moon, green tāṃ becomes a green utpala flower marked by tāṃ. It completely transforms into Exalted Tārā. She is green and in the prime of youth, in form like a sixteen-year-old, adorned by silks and jewels. Her right hand is extended upon her knee in the mudra of supreme generosity. Her left hand in the mudra indicating the Three Jewels holds at her heart the stem of a green utpala flower that blossoms near her ear. She is crowned by Amoghasiddhi. She sits in the position of right leg slightly extended and the left drawn in, within the light of her own radiance.

gtso 'khor lnga po snang la rang bzhin ma grub pa gsal bar bsgom/ de nas gtso 'khor lnga ka'i dpral par oM dkar po/ mgrin par AHdmar po/ thugs kar hU~M sngon pos mtshan pa/ hU~M las 'od zer 'phros/ bla ma yi dam sangs rgyas byang sems dpa' bo mkha' 'gro chos skyong srung ma'i tshogs thams cad bla ma rdo rje 'chang dang lha bzhi'i rnam par spyan drangs te spyi bo'i lha so so la thim par mos la/ dzaHhU~M baM hoH/ brjod cing spyi bo'i lha de rnams skyabs gnas ma lus pa 'dus pa'i ngo bor mos/

Meditate clearly on those five—the principals and entourage—as appearance with no intrinsic nature. All five are marked with white oṃ at their foreheads, red āḥ at their throats, and blue hūṃ at their hearts. Light rays radiate from the hūṃs, invoking the gurus, yidams, buddhas, bodhisattvas, heroes, ḍākinīs, and hosts of dharma protectors and guards, all in the forms of Vajradhara and the four deities. Imagine that they dissolve into the respective deities visualized above your head. Say jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ and imagine those deities above your head become the unified essence of every source of refuge.

rang gi thugs ka nas sprul pa'i lha mo rnams kyis nyer spyod la sogs pa phyi/ bdud rtsi dang 'dod yon lnga pos nang / snyoms 'jug las skyes ba'i bde stong gis gsang ba'i mchod pa phul bar mos la/ de thams cad rang bzhin gyis dag pa'i spros bral gyi ting nge 'dzin la blo bzhag ste/

Imagine that goddesses emanate from your heart and present the outer sense offerings, the inner five elixirs and five desirables, and the secret offering of the bliss-emptiness arising from intercourse. Rest the mind in the uncontrived meditative absorption of the natural purity [of those offerings, and say:]

bla ma rin po che lha bzhi'i tshogs dang bcas pa la bdag gis phyi me tog bdug spos/ nang sha (351) lnga bdud rtsi lnga/ gsang ba bde stong gi ye shes/ yang gsang de kho na nyid kyi mchod pa la sogs pa mchod pa'i khyad par bsam gyis mi khyab pas mchod cing mnyes par bgyi'o/ / bzhes nas byin gyis brlab tu gsol/ /

Precious guru and group of four deities: Outwardly I offer flowers and incense; {351} inwardly five meats and five elixirs; secretly the awareness of bliss-emptiness; and more secretly the offering of suchness. These and other special unimaginable offerings I present for your pleasure. Please partake of them and grant your blessings.
zhes pa tsam gyi mthar gsol 'debs kyi bzlas pa la 'jug kyang chog la/ bla ma'i gsung rgyun tu 'dir mchod bstod bya bar gsungs pa ltar spro na mchod pa bshad ma thag pas 'thus/ bstod pa rgyas par ni/

After just saying that, it is acceptable to go directly to the recitation [of mantras as] supplication. According to the guru’s teaching transmission, however, it is advised to do [more] offerings and praises at this point. If you are interested, then directly after the offerings described above, do the extensive praises that consist of one verse for each deity:
gang gis= /
One whose [kindness makes great bliss itself arise in that very instant, guru whose body is like a jewel; I bow at the feet of the vajra holder.][4]
srin po'i gzugs kyi= /
Wicked one with a cannibal’s body, [terminator bodhisattva, destroyer of the three-tiered cities; I pay homage to you, fierce one.][5]
dpal ldan rdo rje mkha' 'gro= /
Glorious Vajra Ḍākinī, [wheel wielder of the ḍākinīs, with fivefold awareness and three kāyas; homage to the protector of migrators.][6]
skyon gyis ma gos= /
White body unblemished by flaws, [with the perfect buddha as crown, compassionate eyes look upon migrators; I pay homage to Avalokita.][7]
lha dang lha min cod pan sogs sh+lo ka re res bstod/
Gods and demigods bow their crowns [down to your two lotus feet. You are the liberator from all poverty; homage to Mother Tārā.][8]
bsdu na/ / byin rlabs ma lus 'byung ba'i sgo/ / dngos grub ma lus thob pa'i gnas/ / bar chad ma lus sel ba'i lha/ / bla ma lha bzhi'i tshogs la 'dud/ /
Or a short praise: Door for the entry of every blessing, place of attainment of every spiritual power, deities for dispelling every obstacle: I bow to the guru and four deities.

ces bstod/ 'dir dam pa kha cig gis mchod bstod kyi tshab tu yan lag bdun pa dang maN+Dal 'bul bar bzhed pas de ltar spro na de dag lhag por byas pa la 'gal ba med pas yan lag bdun pa gang yang rung ba'i tshigs bcad dang / maN+Dal bka' rgya ma bcas mchod bstod kyi rjes su bya/ de nas so so'i sngags rnams yid gzhan tu ma yengs par mos gus gdung shugs drag pos gsol 'debs kyi tshul du bzla zhing bdud rtsi 'bebs sbyong gi dmigs pa bsgom ste/ de'ang thog mar bla ma rdo rje 'chang gi sku las bdud rtsi'i rgyun babs/ rang gi spyi bo nas zhugs/ lus gang bas sdig sgrib nyes ltung nad gdon dang bcas pa bkrus shing dag / bla ma'i sku gsung thugs kyi byin rlabs gcig char du thob par mos la sngags/

Regarding this, some holy masters have said that as a substitute for the offerings and praises, one could do the seven-branch service and mandala offering. If you wish to do so, there is nothing contradictory, so recite any appropriate verses for the seven-branch service and the Mandala of the Sealed Word[9] after the offerings and praises. Then, without letting your attention wander to anything else, recite with intense powerful yearning the individual mantras in the manner of a supplication and meditate on the visualization of the elixir falling and purifying. First elixir falls from Guru Vajradhara’s body. It enters the crown of your head and fills your body, cleansing and purifying negativities, obscurations, faults, downfalls, sickness, and bad spirits. Think that you obtain the blessings of the guru’s awakened body, speech, and mind all at once while saying the mantra:
na mo bud+d+ha ya/ na mo gu ru he/ badzra bI ra bI re NI/ shrI DA ka dA ki nI/ dzo ka dzo ki nI/ sarba bud+d+ha bo ng+hi sa twA ya shwa ra NaM gats+tsha mi kyai/ zhes bzla/ des 'gres te/
namo buddhāya / namo guruhe / vajra vīra vīriṇī / śrī ḍāka ḍākinī / joka jokinī / sarva buddha bodhisatvāya śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi kyai Apply the same formula to the rest. {352}

mgon po la mos (352) gus byas pas/ mgon po'i sku las bdud rtsi'i rgyun babs/ spyi bo nas zhugs/ lus gang / sdig sgrib nyes ltung nad gdon thams cad dag / khyad par rang 'dra ba'i sku phra mo dpag tu med pa char phab pa ltar byon nas rang gi lus kyi nang gang / nad gdon sdig sgrib thams cad dmar chems chem zhal du gsol/ mgon po'i sku gsung thugs kyi byin rlabs rgyud la zhugs par mos te/ oM badzra ma hA kA la k+ShiM k+She tra bi g+h+na bi nA ya ka hU~M hU~M phaT phaT swA hA/ zhes bzla/

By your devotion to the Protector, a stream of elixir falls from Protector’s body. It enters your crown, fills your body, and purifies all negativities, obscurations, faults, downfalls, sickness, and bad spirits. In particular, boundless tiny replicas of the Protector arrive, falling like rain, and enter inside your body. They noisily devour raw all your sickness, spirits, negativities, and obscurations. Think that the blessings of Protector’s awakened body, speech, and mind enter your being, and repeat: oṃ vajra mahākāla kṣiṃ kṣetra vighanāṃ vināyaka hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā

yang rnal 'byor ma la gsol ba btab pas/ rdo rje rnal 'byor ma'i gsang gnas nas bdud rtsi dmar po'i rgyun babs/ spyi bo nas zhugs/ lus gang / sdig sgrib nyes ltung nad gdon thams cad dag / rnal 'byor ma'i sku gsung thugs kyi byin rlabs rgyud la thob par mos la/ oM badzra na ra kraM kraM hU~M hU~M phaT swA hA/ zhes bzla/

Then, by your supplicating Yoginī, a stream of red elixir falls from Vajrayoginī’s secret place. It enters your crown, fills your body, and purifies all negativities, obscurations, faults, downfalls, sickness, and bad spirits. Think that you obtain the blessings of Yoginī’s awakened body, speech, and mind in your being, and repeat: oṃ vajra nara kraṃ kraṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā

yang spyan ras gzigs la gsol ba btab pas/ 'phags pa thugs rje chen po'i sku dang phyag gi bum pa las bdud rtsi'i rgyun dkar nar gyis byung / spyi bo nas zhugs/ lus gang / sdig sgrib nyes ltung nad gdon thams cad dag / spyan ras gzigs kyi sku gsung thugs kyi byin rlabs rgyud la thob par mos te/ oM ma Ni pad+me hU~M/ oM badzra rak+Sha na maHsa man+ta hU~M phaT/ zhes bzla/

Then, by your supplicating Avalokita, a stream of white elixir falls from Exalted Great Compassionate One’s body and from the vase in his hand. It enters your crown, fills your body, and purifies all negativities, obscurations, faults, downfalls, sickness, and bad spirits. Think that you obtain the blessings of Avalokita’s awakened body, speech, and mind in your being, and repeat: oṃ maṇi padme hūṃ / oṃ vajra rakṣa namaḥ samanta hūṃ phaṭ

yang rje btsun ma sgrol ma la mos gus byas pas/ sgrol ma'i zhabs g.yas pa'i mthe bong las bdud rtsi'i rgyun babs/ spyi bo nas zhugs/ lus gang / sdig sgrib nyes ltung nad gdon thams cad dag / 'phags ma'i sku gsung thugs kyi byin rlabs rgyud la zhugs par mos la/ oM tA re tut+tA re tu re swA hA/ zhes bzla/ bzlas

Then, by your devotion to Exalted Tārā, a stream of elixir falls from Tārā’s right big toe. It enters your crown, fills your body, and purifies all negativities, obscurations, faults, downfalls, sickness, and bad spirits. Think that the blessings of Exalted Lady’s awakened body, speech, and mind enter your being, and repeat: oṃ tāre tuttāre ture svāhā

dmigs de dag gis thun gyi dngos gzhi 'khyol bar bya/ de'ang phyis kyi gsung rgyun tu rnal 'byor ma la bsnyen pa oM gsum ma bzla ba (353) dang / bzlas pa'i gtso bo'ang de la bya zhing gzhan rnams cung zad re bzla bar bzhed pa dang / kha cig tu mgon po'i bsnyen pa nyi dbungs bskyed par gsungs pa sogs de dang de dag gi rnal 'byor gtsor bton pa la dgongs par mngon zhing / 'dir spyi tsam du/ bla ma'i gsol 'debs kyi bzlas pa cung zad mang ba dang gzhan rnams cha snyoms par bzla'o/ /

Complete the main part of the session with those recitations and visualizations. In the later transmitted teachings, it says to recite primarily the three-oṃ mantra for Yoginī’s recitation practice while reciting the others somewhat less. {353} Some say that this will enhance the Protector’s recitation accumulation, and so forth. These statements were apparently made in relation to those whose practices focus mainly on those particular yogas. Here, in general, do the recitation of the guru’s supplication slightly more and the other recitations in equal amounts.
gnyis pa thun mong ma yin pa'i dbang len pa ni/
2. Taking the Uncommon [Profound] Empowerment

sngags tshan lnga po sprel te gsol 'debs kyi tshul du lan gsum bzlas la mos gus drag tu bskyed pas/ / bla ma rdo rje 'chang gi thugs ka'i hU~M yig las 'od zer 'phros/ 'khor du bzhugs pa'i lha bzhi spyan drangs te/ bla ma'i spyi bor spyan ras gzigs/ mgrin par rje btsun sgrol ma/ thugs kar ye shes mgon po/ / lte bar rdo rje rnal 'byor ma rnams bzhugs par mos/ slar yang bla ma'i thugs ka nas 'od zer 'phros/ phyogs bcu'i bla ma yi dam sangs rgyas byang sems dpa' bo mkha' 'gro ye shes chos skyong srung ma'i tshogs thams cad lha bzhi'i rnam par spyan drangs te bla ma'i sku'i nang thams cad bong ba 'brus khengs pa ltar so so'i cha la gtams par bsam/

Recite the series of five mantras three times in the manner of a supplication and arouse intense devotion. Light rays radiate from the letter hūṃ in Guru Vajradhara’s heart and invoke the surrounding four deities. Imagine Avalokita dwelling at Guru’s crown, Venerable Tārā at the throat, Awareness Protector at the heart, and Vajrayoginī at the navel. Light rays radiate again from Guru’s heart and invoke from the ten directions all the gurus, yidams, buddhas, bodhisattvas, heroes, ḍākinīs, awareness dharma protectors and guards in the forms of the four deities. Think that they fill up the whole inside of the guru’s body, like grain fills a barrel, with their individual aspects.

de nas rang gi lus kyi stong ra'i dbus su rtsa gsum 'khor lo lnga dang bcas pa skad cig gis gsal ba'i dbu ma'i mar snar a shad skyer tshor lta bu/ gsang ba bshang sgo dang nye bar rlung gi dkyil 'khor bcas gsal btab la/ rlung kha sbyor ram/ mi nus na 'og rlung cung zad bskums pa'i ye shes kyi rlung sbyor byas pas/ rang gi gsang gnas nas rlung g.yos/ lte ba'i a shad la phog pas gtum mo ye shes kyi me dmar lhag gis 'bar/ rang gi spyi bo'i tshangs bug nas thon/ chos 'byung la phog pas cher dros/

Then instantly visualize the three channels and five chakras in the center of your empty body. At the lower end of the central channel is an A-stroke like a barberry thorn (skyer tsher). Clearly visualize a wind mandala near the secret and anal openings. Hold the joined breath or, if unable, slightly contract the lower winds to join [them] with the awareness winds. That causes the wind to stir at your secret place, striking the A-stroke at the navel; the red fire of timeless awareness of the inner heat blazes fiercely. It emerges from your cranial aperture and strikes the source of phenomena, greatly heating it. {354}

des lha rnams dros/ (354) de yi rkyen gyis bde chen bzod med du 'bar te lus lha rnams bdud rtsir ltem gyis zhu/ yab yum gyi sbyor mtshams nas bdud rtsi'i rgyun byon te rang gi spyi bo nas zhugs/ mgrin pa yan chad gang / lus kyi sdig sgrib dag / bum pa'i dbang thob/ sku'i byin rlabs zhugs/ snying ga yan chad gang / ngag gi sdig sgrib dag / gsang ba'i dbang thob/ gsung gi byin rlabs zhugs/ lte ba yan chad gang / yid kyi sdig sgrib dag / shes rab ye shes kyi dbang thob/ thugs kyi byin rlabs zhugs/ lus thams cad gang / sgo gsum gyi sdig sgrib dag / dbang bzhi pa thob/ rdo rje gsum gyi byin rlabs ma lus pa zhugs par mos/

That in turn heats up the deities, causing the blazing of unbearably great bliss. All the body deities melt fully into elixir. A stream of elixir emerges from the place of union of the deity couple and enters you through the crown of your head. As it fills above the throat, it purifies physical negativities and obscurations. You obtain the vase empowerment; the blessings of awakened body enter. As it fills above the heart, it purifies verbal negativities and obscurations. You obtain the secret empowerment; the blessings of awakened speech enter. As it fills above the navel, it purifies mental negativities and obscurations. You obtain the wisdom-awareness empowerment; the blessings of awakened mind enter. As it fills the whole body, it purifies negativities and obscurations of all three doors. You obtain the fourth empowerment; every blessing of the three vajras enter you.
mthar chos 'byung nam mkhar rang yal/ bla ma dgyes pa chen pos 'od du zhu nas rang la thim/ rang yang stong nyid du thim/ bla ma rang sems dbyer med du 'dres par mos/

Finally, the source of phenomena vanishes by itself into space. In great delight, Guru melts into light and dissolves into you. You also dissolve into emptiness. Imagine that the guru’s and your own mind blend inseparably.
gsum pa rjes
C. Conclusion
['di] la gnyis/ gnas lugs bskyang ba dang / thun mtshams la 'jug pa'o/ /
This has two parts: (1) maintaining the abiding nature and (2) entering the session breaks.
dang po ni/
1. Maintaining the Abiding Nature

bla ma rang la thim pa'i rjes thog de ma thag par lus gnad chos bdun bca'/ ngag gnad rlung ro dgu phrugs su bsal la rgyu ba gnyis po rang babs su bzhag / sems gnad dus gsum gyi rnam par rtog pa gang gi'ang rjes su mi 'brang / bzang ngan blang dor re dogs gang yang yid la mi byed par shes pa had de chad de'i rang ngo rang shes kyi dran pas dgag sgrub bzo bcos med par bskyangs la/ dang po grim gyis bsgrim/ bar du lhod kyis klod/ mthar gnyug ma'i rang ngo shes bzhin gyi dran pa'i mdangs ma shor ba la bslab cing ci gnas su mnyam par bzhag go /

After the guru dissolves into you, assume the sevenfold position with your body. The vital point of speech is to dispel the dead air with the ninefold shake-up. Let the two movements fall naturally. The vital point of mind is not to follow after any thoughts of the three times nor entertain any ideas of good and bad, affirmation and denial, or hopes and fears. Just maintain wide-open consciousness and self-recognizing mindfulness without any contrivance of acceptance or rejection. Train at first with tight focus, in the middle relax loosely, and finally rest in the awareness of your native state without losing the vitality of mindfulness. Rest in that equipoise as long as it lasts.
gnyis pa
2. Entering the Session Breaks
de las ldangs te thun mtshams kyi spyod lam la 'jug pa ni/ ci snang bla ma yi dam sgyu ma chos nyid kyi shes pa dang ma bral ba'i dang / /
Upon arising from that, begin the activities of session breaks. Always remain in the state of knowledge that whatever appears is the guru, the yidam, illusion, and the nature of phenomena.
Make the following aspiration: {335}
sems can thams cad bde (355) gyur cig / sems can thams cad nad med par/ / sangs rgyas nyid du 'gro ba yi/ / lam de nyid du 'grub gyur cig /
May all sentient beings be happy. May all sentient beings be free of sickness, May they achieve the very path that leads to buddhahood.
ma bsgral ba rnams bdag gis bsgral/ / ma grol ba rnams bdag gis dgrol/ / rnal 'byor gtsug lag bstan bcos la/ / da lta nyid du gnas par shog /
I shall free those not freed I shall liberate those not liberated. May they come to dwell right now in the treatise of yoga’s temple.
ces smon lam btab/ /
Say verses of auspiciousness:
legs pa'i yon tan rab rdzogs pa/ / bla ma yi dam bkra shis shog / phrin las thams cad sgrub mdzad pa/ / mkha' 'gro chos skyong bkra shis shog /
May there be auspiciousness of the guru and yidam, the total perfection of good qualities. May there be auspiciousness of ḍākinīs and dharma protectors. who accomplish all awakened activity.
ces bkra shis brjod/ /
Dedicate the virtue:
dge ba'i tshogs rnams bsags pa kun/ / bdag gis yongs su bzung med par/ / sems can ma lus kun don tu/ / chos dbyings bla na med par bsngo/ /
All my accumulation of virtue I do not at all claim as my own, but dedicate to the supreme realm of reality for the sake of all beings without exception.
zhes sogs kyis dge ba bla na med pa'i byang chub tu bsngos nas chos ldan gyi spyod lam la 'jug go /
After dedicating the virtue to unsurpassed awakening with this and other prayers, undertake your devotional activities.

'dir bla ma rdo rje 'chang gi rnal 'byor gyis mchog gi dngos grub tshe 'di la ster bar byed cing / de sgrub pa'i skabs su gegs sel ba dang bogs 'don pa gnyis la lam gyi rim pa rags las pas/ phyi'i gegs sel mgon po/ / nang gi gegs sel sgrol ma/ phyi byams snying rje'i bogs 'don spyan ras gzigs/ nang bde drod kyi bogs 'don rdo rje rnal 'byor ma rnams mthar thug yin par yongs su grags shing grub pas nyams len thun gcig la rdo rje theg pa'i lam rim yongs su rdzogs pa'i zag gnad khyad par 'phags pa yin par ma zad/ ji skad du/

The yoga of Guru Vajradhara bestows supreme spiritual powers in this life. Since, in doing this practice, the stages of the path depend on both dispelling obstructions and enhancing [meditation], Protector dispels outer hindrances, Tārā dispels inner hindrances, Avalokita enhances outer love and compassion, and Vajrayoginī enhances inner bliss-warmth. These are well known as the culminations [of these practices]. Through practicing them, [one can] in a single session completely perfect the stages of the path of Vajrayāna; thus it is an especially exalted profound vital point. Not only that, as is said:
ma yengs zla ba gsum na 'grub/ / tho rangs thun re ma chags bsgom/ / mchog dang thun mongs dngos grub 'grub/ /
Accomplished in three months without distraction, meditating without fail in each session at dawn accomplishes supreme and common spiritual powers.
ces gsungs te grub pa gnyis lo zla tsam gyis ster bar byed pa yin pas na dam pa'i chos la skal pa mi dman pa'i bsod nams dang blo gros can ngag gis nyams len gyi snying po (356) g.yar dam du bya'o/ /

Since this is what grants the two powers in a matter of years and months, those with sufficient merit and intelligence in regard to the Holy Dharma should undertake this as the heart of their practice. {356}
[Concluding Verse and Colophon]
grub brnyes gser gyi phreng bar mchog sbyin pa'i/ / lha bzhi'i khrid yig grub pa'i zhal lung bzhin/ / 'dus gsal spel 'dir skal bzang kun zhugs nas/ / mchog grub thang mas 'jig rten brdal byed shog /

Four Deities, the supreme gift of the golden garland of adepts, written as a guidebook according to the oral teachings, concise, clear, and shared here for fortunate ones to engage; may their display of its fulfillment pervade the world.

ces pa'ang rigs brgya'i khyab bdag bka' drin mnyam med kun gzigs 'jam dbyangs mkhyen brtse'i dbang po'i zhal snga nas zab khrid byin rlabs bcas bka' drin tu stsal ba'i tshe gsung gis rjes su gnang ba dang / yang khrod kun bzang bde chen 'od gsal gling gi sgrub la gzhol ba rnams kyi nyams len nye bar mkho bas mtshams sbyar te bla ma'i zhal lung rang bzo'i rnyogs pas ma bslad par/ mang thos kyi spong ba pa karma ngag dbang yon tan rgya mtshos de bI ko Ti'i dben khrod du bgyis pa dge legs 'phel/ // (357)

The incomparably kind and all-seeing Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, lord of a hundred families, kindly granted this profound guidance with its blessing [empowerment] and at the same time he granted permission for the writing. It was composed at the upper retreat of Kunzang Dechen Ösal Ling as a requisite practice for those endeavoring in practice there. I, Karma Ngawang Yönten Gyatso, who is steeped in much study, composed this from the teaching transmission of my guru without pollution by the sediments my own fabrications, at the secluded retreat of Devīkoṭi. Let virtue prevail!
Liturgical Practices and Supplications
@#/ /'gro mgon shangs pa bka' brgyud kyi bla ma mchod pa'i cho ga yid bzhin nor bu zhes bya ba bzhugs so// //
25. A Wish-Fulfilling Gem. Offering Ritual for the Lineage Gurus of Shangpa Kagyu, Protectors of Beings[1]
(358)@#/ /na mo gu ru dz+nya na DA ki nI yai/ /
namo guru jñānaḍākinī yai
rdo rje 'chang las de nyid brnyes/ / mi slob zung 'jug grub pa mo/ / ye shes DA ki gnyis dang / / dbyer med bla ma'i zhabs la 'dud/ /
Those who obtained this from Vajradhara, female adepts of integral unity beyond training, the two awareness ḍākinīs inseparable from my guru: I bow at your feet.
mchog dang thun mong dngos grub kun/ / bla ma kho nar rags lus phyir/ / de nyid mnyes byed skal ldan la/ / 'dod pa'i don rnams lhug par 'jo/ /
All supreme and common spiritual powers depend solely upon the guru. So those fortunate to please such a one will have all their desires amply fulfilled.
de bas bya ba gzhan spangs la/ / bla ma mchod pa yang dag brtsam/ / mdo rgyud bstan bcos thams cad dang / / dri med gdams pa'i nying khu yin/ /
Even better, abandon all other acts and undertake the genuine guru offering. It is the heart of flawless instructions and all sutras, tantras, and treatises.

sgrub pa po mos gus dang ldan zhing dkon mchog kun 'dus kyi ngo bo bla ma la yid ches pa'i skal pa can dag gis nyams len snying por bya ba ni 'di yin te/ de'ang 'byor ba yod na/ gnas gtsang mar rgyan dang yo byad kyi bkod pas spras pa'i gung du tshogs kyi rten bris sku la sogs pa bzhugs su gsol ba'i spyan sngar/ maN+Dal/ chu gnyis nyer spyod gtso bor gyur pa'i mchod rdzas ci tsam 'byor ba dag gtsang zhing dag la ser snas ma gos pa dang / khyad par can gyi dus mkhas grub khyung po rnal 'byor chos sku mkha' khyab chen por mngon par byang chub pa'i dus mchod dgun ra ba'i bcu bzhi lta bur tshogs kyi yo byad kyang rgyas par bsham/ 'byor pas dben pa'am/ spros med kyi rnal (359) 'byor lta bur maN+Dal nyer spyod tsam gang 'dzom gyis kyang chog / gtso bor 'khor ba las blo nges par 'byung zhing mchog gi dngos grub don du gnyer ba'i dad pa dang / bla ma brgyud pa'i rnam thar la yid ches kyi mos gus dung nge ba'i sgo nas/ thog mar skyabs su 'gro ba ni/

For practitioners with devotion and the good fortune to believe that the guru is the united essence of all rare and sublime Jewels, this is “the heart of practice.” If you have the resources, decorate a clean place with an arrangement of ornaments and articles. In the middle, place the drawn images and other representations for the feast and request [the holy beings’] presence. Offer a mandala and mainly the two waters and sense objects, along with however much clean and pure offering substance you have on hand, without being stingy. On special occasions, such as the fourteenth day of the first winter month [that commemorates] when the learned adept Khyungpo Naljor attained manifest awakening in great all-pervasive dharmakāya, put up extensive feast substances. {359} If you are bereft of supplies, or you are like a simple yogin, it is sufficient just to offer the mandala and whatever sense offerings you have collected. The main thing is an attitude of definite renunciation of cyclic existence and faith in the goal of supreme spiritual power. With sincere devotion coming from your inspiration from the life stories of the lineage gurus, first go for refuge:
ma nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i sems can thams cad skyabs kun 'dus kyi ngo bo bla ma rin po che la skyabs su mchi ba lags so/ /
All sentient beings, my mothers, equal to the reaches of space, go for refuge in the precious guru, the unified essence of all refuges.
lan kha yar brjod/ sems bskyed pa ni/
Say that a number of times, then arouse the mind of awakening:
sems can thams cad kyi don du zung 'jug rdo rje 'chang chen po'i go 'phang thob par bya/ de'i ched du zab lam bla ma mchod pa nyams su blang bar bgyi'o/ /
All sentient beings, equal to the reaches of space, must attain the unified state of Great Vajradhara. To that end, I will practice the profound path of guru offering.
lan gsum/ bgegs bsal ba ni/
Repeat that three times, then dispel obstructors.
rang nyid skad cig gis dpal 'khor lo sdom pa yum dang bcas pa'i skur gyur/
Instantly I become glorious Cakrasaṃvara and Vajrayoginī.
lha dang lha min gsang ba pa/ / lus srul la sogs gang ci'ang rung / / lus ngag sems la gnas pa yi/ / bgegs kyi tshogs rnams nga la nyon/ /
Gods, demigods, secretists (guhyaka), body putrefiers (kaṭapūtana), and any others, who abide in body, speech, or mind; hosts of obstructors, listen to me!
nga ni dpal ldan rdo rje'i stobs/ / srung ba'i 'khor lo rab sbyor bas/ / rdo rje 'bar ba'i sku yis (360) ni/ / lus gsum las skyes dgas par bya/ /
I have the strength of glorious Vajra, engaging fully the circle of protection, my form of blazing vajras will scatter those born of three bodies.[2]
gal te kha cig bdag las 'da'/ / rnam par brlag 'gyur gzhan du min/ /
If some of you transgress me anyway, you will be totally crushed; nothing else.
sum+b+ha ni brjod la tshan rngam bya/
Fiercely set the boundaries, saying: oṃ sumbha nisumbha [hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ / oṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ / oṃ gṛhṇapāya gṛhṇapāya hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ / oṃ ānayaho bhagavān vidya rāja hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ]
sna tshogs 'od kyi 'phro 'du las/ / phyogs kun rdo rje 'bar ba'i gur/ / phyi rol ye shes me dpung 'bar/ / rab brtan srung ba'i 'khor lor gyur/ /
Multicolored light radiates and gathers, creating a blazing vajra tent in all directions. Outside it the bonfire of awareness blazes, making a totally secure protection circle.
oM badzra tsakra ra b+h+rU~M hU~M/
oṃ vajra cakra rakṣa bhrūṃ hūṃ
mchod pa byin gyis brlab pa ni/ bsangs chu la dmigs te/ /
For the consecration of offerings, visualize the cleansing water:
oM badzra a mr-i ta kuN+Da lI ha na ha na hU~M phaT/
oṃ vajra amṛta kuṇḍalī hana hana hūṃ phaṭ

nyer gcig tsam gyis byin brlabs la 'thor te sngags de nyid kyis bsang / swa b+hA bas sbyang / stong pa'i ngang las gnas khang b+h+rU~M las rin po che las grub pa'i gzhal med khang brtsegs mtshan nyid thams cad yongs su rdzogs pa'i dbus su oM las byung ba'i rin po che las grub pa'i snod yangs shing rgya che ba rnams kyi nang du hU~M zhu ba las byung ba'i lha rdzas las grub pa'i mchod yon/ zhabs bsil/ me tog / bdug spos/ snang gsal/ dri chab/ zhal zas/ rol mo la sogs pa mchod rdzas bzang zhing dge ba nam mkha'i khams thams cad gang bar gyur/

Repeat twenty-one times to consecrate, then sprinkle [the offerings], using that same mantra to cleanse and svabhāva…(etc.) to purify. From within emptiness, from bhrūṃ, the dwelling place becomes a jeweled celestial palace with all levels and characteristics complete. In its center, arising from oṃ, is a vast and wide precious vessel, within which hūṃ melts and becomes the offerings made of divine ingredients—drinking water, washing water, flowers, incense, light, perfume, food, music, and so forth—excellent offering substances that fill the whole sky realm with their virtues.
oM badzra ar+g+haM swA hA/ oM badzra pad+yaM swA hA/ oM badzra puSh+pe AHhU~M/ oM badzra d+hUpe/ A lo ke /g+han+d+he/ nai bid+ya/ shab+da AHhU~M/ zhes rol mos byin dbab/

oṃ vajra arghaṃ svāhā / oṃ vajra padyaṃ svāhā / oṃ vajra puṣpe āḥ hūṃ / oṃ vajra dhūpe āḥ hūṃ / oṃ vajra āloke āḥ hūṃ / oṃ vajra ghandhe āḥ hūṃ / oṃ vajra naividya āḥ hūṃ / oṃ vajra śabda āḥ hūṃ Play music for the descent of blessing.
tshogs rten sgrub pa ni/
Then accomplish the supports for accumulation:
dag pa'i zhing khams rgya che bkod legs shing / / do mtshar rgyan bkod bsam mi khyab pa'i mkhar/ / rdo rje nor bu'i khang brtsegs dpe med pa/ / thar pa chen po'i gzhal yas yangs pa'i dbus/ /
In the vast pure realm perfectly arrayed is an unimaginable mansion marvelously decorated, an incomparable house built of vajra gems. In the middle of this wide celestial palace of freedom,
seng khri pad dkar zla ba rgyas pa'i steng / / rtsa ba'i bla ma ye shes DA ki nI/ / su kha sid+d+hi dkar la dmar ba'i mdangs/ / dbu skra sil bu spyan gsum hrig ger gzigs/ /
on a lion throne, white lotus, and full moon, sits my root guru as the awareness ḍākinī, Sukhasiddhi, white with a red radiance. Her hair is loose, three eyes staring, {361}

phyag g.yas (361) bdud rtsis bkang ba'i thod pa bsnams/ / g.yon pas skye med mtshon pa'i phyag rgya mdzad/ / rus pa'i rgyan ldan zhabs gnyis gar stabs tshul/ / ye shes sku can 'ja' 'od klong na bzhugs/ / de yi spyi bor drug pa rdo rje 'chang / / rdo rje bdag med yum dang mnyam par sbyor/ /

right hand holding an elixir-filled skull cup, left in the mudra of pointing to the unborn, adorned by bones, two legs in dancing stance, her awareness body rests in the midst of rainbows. Above her head the sixth buddha Vajradhara and Vajra Nairātmya are in union.

gtso bo'i mtha' skor mdun sogs phyogs bzhi ru/ / rje btsun mkha' 'gro'i dbang phyug ni gu ma/ / smug nag spyan gsum lta stangs mkha' la gzigs/ / cang te'u thod pa rdo rje'i kha T+wAM 'chang / / rus pa'i rgyan ldan zhabs gnyis phyed skyil bzhugs/ /

Around the principals, in four directions [clockwise], Venerable Ḍākinī Mighty Niguma is in front, dark brown with three eyes gazing at space, holding a hand drum, skull cup, and vajra khaṭvāṅga, adorned by bones, sitting with two legs in half-lotus.
rgyal sras mai tri rnal 'byor spyod pa'i chas/ / rat+na de bI gang+gA d+ha ris brten/ / sgra gcan 'dzin sbas 'chi med grub pa'i tshul/ / bsod nams 'byung gnas dge slong paN chen gzugs/ /
The Victor’s heir Maitrīpa outfitted for yogic conduct, accompanied by Ratnadevī and Gaṅgādhari.[3] Rāhulagupta in the style of an immortal adept, and Puṇyākara as a great paṇḍita monk.
bar mtshams paN chen rnal 'byor mkha' 'gro ma'i/ / chas ldan mkhas grub brgya dang lnga bcu bzhugs/ /
In between are the one hundred and fifty learned adepts in the garb of paṇḍitas, yogins, and ḍākinīs.
de mdun sgrub brgyud mnga' bdag khyung po rje/ / chos gos rnam gsum paN zhwa dmar po gsol/ / phyag g.yas sa gnon g.yon pa ngal gso'i stabs/ / phyed skyil rol pas pad zla'i gdan la bzhugs/ /

In front of them, master of the practice lineage, Lord Khyungpo, wears the three dharma robes and a red paṇḍita hat, his right hand touches earth, his left rests in repose, as he sits on a lotus-sun seat, relaxing in half-lotus.
bka' bab thugs sras chen po rnam drug nas/ / rtsa ba'i bla ma'i bar du rim byon pa'i/ / bka' brgyud nor bu'i phreng ba 'dzin pa rnams/ /
Then the holders of the jewel garland of the precept lineage, from the six great heart sons of the transmission in succession down to my own root guru.
phal cher gtsang sgom ngur smrig 'chang ba la/ / la la rnal 'byor spyod sogs ma nges tshul/ gang la gang 'dul mos pa'i dpal du 'char/ /
Most are pure meditators wearing saffron robes, though some are indefinite, engaging yogic conduct, and so on, interested in whatever tames whomever, they arise in glory.
kun kyang skye med rtogs pa'i gding dang ldan/ / sku gsung thugs kyi gsang ba bsam mi khyab/ /
But they all are confident in realizing the unborn. The mystery of awakened body, speech, and mind is unimaginable.

ting 'dzin sgo brgyar rtag tu snyoms par 'jug / brtul zhugs (362) cho 'phrul phyogs med kun tu grub/ / mdzad pa phrin las phyogs bcu dus gsum khyab/ / byin rlabs thugs rje'i gzi byin tshad med 'bar/ /

They rest in constant equipoise of a hundred doors of absorption, miraculous deliberate conduct always accomplished without bias. {362} Their deeds of awakened activity pervade ten directions and three times. The brilliance of their blessings of compassion blazes immeasurably.

steng phyogs bla ma mtha' skor yi dam lha/ / sangs rgyas byang sems dpa' bo rnal 'byor ma/ / chos skyong dam can rgya mtsho'i tshogs dang bcas/ / dpal ldan bla ma'i gsang gsum rol par shar/ / gang zhig bla ma sangs rgyas yid byed pa/ / de yi mdun na mngon sum bzhugs par gyur/ /

Above the gurus are the yidam deities all around, and buddhas, bodhisattvas, heroes, and yoginīs, with an ocean of dharma protectors and oath-bound ones, arising as the display of the glorious gurus’ three secrets to whomever believes in the guru as buddha; they appear actually present before them.
'dir spyan 'dren bzhugs gsol bya mi dgos kyang las dang po pa'i blo dman rnams la 'char bde ba ltar na/
Although at this point you don’t really need the invocation and supplication to be present, the following is presented for the sake of the less experienced beginners, to make it simple to understand:
skyes mchog gnyis med ye shes spyan can rnams/ / chos kyi sku la gshegs 'byon mi mnga' yang / / gzugs sku brtse ba chen po'i rnam 'phrul gyis/ / dad ldan mchod pa'i zhing du gshegs su gsol/ /

Sublime beings with the vision of nondual timeless awareness have gone to the dharmakāya and won’t arrive here. Yet with great love, may your form kāya emanations please come here as an offering field for the faithful.
rat+na gu ru sa pa ri bA ra badzra sa mA dzaH /
ratna guru saparivāra vajra samājaḥ
mgon po 'gro ba'i don la byon pa legs/ / bdag gi mchod yon 'di nyid bzhes nas kyang / / ji srid mchod pa'i bya ba ma rdzogs bar/ / yid 'ong gdan la bde bar bzhugs su gsol/
Lords, it is good you have come for migrators’ sakes. Partake of these water offerings that I will present and remain comfortably on this pleasing seat until all the acts of offering are complete.
oM pra lba ra sat+ka ra ar+g+haM pra tI ts+tshA swA hA/
oṃ pravara satkara arghaṃ pratīccha svāhā
de bzhin/ pAd+yaM sbyar la chu gnyis phul/
Similarly with…padyaṃ…to offer the two waters.
oM pad+ma A sa ni sa ma ya s+t+waM/ zhes sngar bskyed pa dang gnyis su med par gdan la bzhugs par mos/
Then: oṃ padma āsani samayas tvaṃ Imagine that [those awareness beings] become indivisible with those previously visualized.
dngos su phyag bya ba'am thal mo sbyar te/ /
Then either do actual prostrations or join your palms together:
rnam dag sku ni skyon bral 'khrul pa med/ / phun tshogs gsungs dbyangs shes bya ma lus khyab/ / zab dang rgya che'i de nyid mkhyen pa'i thugs/ / rdo rje gsum dngos dpal ldan bla mar 'dud/ /
Totally pure form, faultless and unmistaken, prolific melodious speech encompassing all knowledge, mind of knowing suchness, vast and profound; I bow to the glorious guru, the actual three vajras.
sgrib gnyis bag chags bcas pa gtan nas sbangs/ / dag pa gnyis ldan yon tan thams cad rdzogs/ / rang gzhan don gyur sku gnyis mngon mdzad pa/ / 'khor 'das ma lus sprul par mdzad la 'dud/ /

You forever forsook two obscurations and habitual patterns and perfected all qualities, possessed of two purities, you manifest two kāyas for the sake of self and others; I bow to the sender of emanations throughout samsara and nirvana.
g.yo med sems kyis bsten na skad cig la/ / byin gyis brlabs pas bla med byang chub lam/ / yang na 'dod pa mchog dang thar pa yi/ (363) dam pa nges par sbyin mdzad khyod la 'dud/ /

If someone follows you with an unwavering mind, instantly blessings bestow the highest path of awakening, or else one’s excellent desires and emancipation; {363} I bow to you who surely gives what is sacred.
