May my aims, absorptions, and activities be as boundlessly deep and fathomless as the realms of beings and depths of the oceans, the reaches of space, and the infinite realm of reality.
'khor los sgyur rgyal dpag med bdag sprul nas/ / 'gro kun re skongs chos kyi rgyal srid skyong / / mkha' mnyam zhing khams kun la dbang bsgyur nas/ / sems can ma lus bde la 'god par shog /
May I emanate countless universal monarchs to fulfill beings’ hopes, rule the dharma domain, gain dominion over all realms throughout space, and place all beings without exception in happiness.
ma 'ongs dus su nad mtshon bskal pa yis/ / sems can sdug bsngal nyam thag gyur pa'i tshe/ / bdag ni sman mchog rgyal por gyur nas kyang / / skad cig nyid la sdug bsngal zhi byed (462) shog /
May I become a sovereign supreme healer instantly to soothe the pains of living beings when they are worn out by suffering in the future age of disease and warfare. {462}
mu ge'i bskal pas bkres skom gyur pa'i tshe/ / bza' btung dar zab gser dngul longs spyod rnams/ / phun sum tshogs pa mkha' mnyam sprin gtibs nas/ / phyogs bcur 'dod yon lnga yi char 'bebs shog /

May I gather thick clouds of abundance to fill the sky and rain down five sense pleasures in all directions, replete with food, drink, fine cloth, silver, gold, and wealth, for the times of hunger and thirst in the age of famine.
byang chub sems kyi spyod pa rlabs chen gyis/ / 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho stongs par ma gyur tshe/ / nam mkha'i mtha' gtugs sems can ma lus kun/ / gang la gang 'dul de la der ston shog /
May the efficacy of my bodhisattva activity teach every being throughout the reaches of space, in whatever way will benefit each one, until the ocean of cyclic existence is empty.
log pa'i lam zhugs stobs ldan dregs pa can/ / phyogs bcu dus gsum rgyal bas ma thul ba'i/ / 'gro kun ma lus bdag gis rab btul nas/ / skad cig nyid la sangs rgyas sar 'god shog /
May I completely subdue all migrators not tamed by the victors of the ten directions and three times, those haughty beings who took the wrong path, and place them instantly in the state of a buddha.
ji srid 'khor bar sems can gnas kyi bar/ / de srid phrin las rtsol med rang shar gyis/ / sems can ma lus smin cing grol byed pa'i/ / 'gro don lhun grub rgyun chad med par shog /
May my effortless self-arising awakened activity, spontaneously beneficial and uninterrupted, mature and liberate all sentient beings so long as they remain in cyclic existence.
phyogs bcu dus gsum rgyal ba rgya mtsho yi/ / so so skye bo byang chub sems dpa'i tshe/ / bskal pa grangs med sems bskyed smon lam btab/ / tshogs gnyis mthar phyin mngon par sangs rgyas nas/ /

Victors of the ten directions and three times, when they were ordinary folks and bodhisattvas, aroused awakening mind, aspired through countless eons, completed two accumulations, and gained enlightenment.
phun sum tshogs mnga' yon tan rgya mtsho yis/ / sems can dpag med smin cing grol mdzad pa'i/ / smon lam phrin las gcig tu bsdoms pa nas/ / bdag gi smon lam phrin las rgya cher shog /
Then they matured and liberated countless beings by mastering vast qualities of excellence. May the full extent of my aspirational activity join as one with their aspirational activity.
gzhan don lhun grub dpag med 'byung gyur pas/ / bdag gi smon lam 'di dag thams cad kun/ / byang chub mchog mos dad pa rab bskyed de/ / gang gis 'debs pa de la yongs rdzogs shog /
May the spontaneous vast benefit for others arising from these aspirations of mine be wholly fulfilled when entreated by anyone filled with faith, devotion, and the awakening mind.
phyogs bcu dus gsum 'khor 'das thams cad kyi/ / bkra shis bde legs phun sum tshogs pa kun/ / rgyun chad med pa chu bo'i gzhung bzhin du/ / bdag gzhan phyogs rnams kun tu khyab par shog /
May all that is excellent, auspicious, and joyful everywhere in cyclic existence and transcendence flow constantly like the course of a great river to suffuse all directions for myself and others.
'phags pa smon lam gyi rgyal po rdzogs so// (463)
This concludes Niguma’s Sovereign of Noble Aspirations.
Songs of Experience
@#/ /dpal ldan shangs pa bka' brgyud kyi do ha rdo rje'i tshig rkang dang mgur dbyangs phyogs gcig tu bsgrigs pa thos pa don ldan byin rlabs rgya mtsho zhes bya ba bzhugs so/ /
30. An Ocean of Blessings Meaningful to Hear. Collected Vajra Lines, Dohas, and Melodious Songs of the Glorious Shangpa Kagyu[1]

(464)@#/ /dpal rdo rje 'chang gi rgyal tshab sa bcu pa'i dbang phyug rtsod pa med pa'i grub thob kyi phreng ba bar ma chad du byon pa 'gro mgon shangs pa bka' brgyud ces 'jig rten gsum na yongs su grags shing khyad par du 'phags pa'i che ba'i yon tan ngo mtshar du mas brgyan pa de dag gi zhabs kyi pad+mo la gus pas phyag 'tshal lo/ /

Glorious Vajradhara’s regents are the mighty bodhisattvas on the tenth level in the unbroken succession of indisputable adepts renowned throughout the three worlds as the protectors of migrators in the Shangpa Precept Lineage (Shangpa Kagyu), adorned by many amazing and exalted qualities. I pay homage and bow respectfully before their lotus feet.

rigs thams cad kyi khyab bdag drug pa rdo rje 'chang gis rdo rje mi shigs panA da'i rang sgras rdo rje gsang ba'i rgyud zab mo gdams ngag dmar khrid kyi tshig rkang du rtsal ba nas bzung ste/ / bka' brgyud rin chen phreng ba rim par byon pa rnams kyis gnas lugs chos sku'i rgyal sa zin te nyams dang rtogs pa'i gzi byin rab tu 'bar ba las dgongs pa zab mo'i nyams skyug do ha rdo rje'i dbyangs kyi gad mo mkha' khyab tu sgrogs pa rnams kyi nang nas/ /

Vajradhara, the sixth lord pervading over all [buddha] families, expressed verses of direct guidance (dmar khrid) of the profound Vajra Secret Tantra via the innate sound of the indestructible vajra nāda.[2] From that time forth, the successive garland of jewel [adepts] in the instruction lineage all captured the realm of the true nature, the dharmakāya, and the brilliance of their experiences and realizations blazed high. Those profound experiences burst forth as the laughter of vajra melodies of doha that resound throughout space.

rnal 'byor ba rnams la dad gus kyi gsos sbyin pa dang / / zhen log nges 'byung gi skul lcag 'debs pa dang / / nyams myong gong nas gong du spel ba dang / rtogs pa'i ye shes la dpa' tshan skyed ba dang / dpa' bo DA ki rnams dgyes pa bskyed pa dang / / gegs dang bar chad kyi 'phrang las sgrol ba dang / / mi dang mi ma yin pa'i 'gro ba mtha' yas pa chos kyi sbyin pa bla na med pas tshims par bya ba'i slad du cung zad cig gus pas bsgrag bar bya (465) ba las/ / thog mar sngon 'gro chos spyod kyi rim pa dang ting nge 'dzin gsal 'debs pa la 'jug par zhu/ /

The purpose of those [spiritual songs] is to inspire yogins’ devotion and faith; to encourage their renunciation and aversion; to enhance greater and greater meditative experiences; to arouse courage in the timeless awareness of realization; to please the heroes and ḍākinīs; to liberate from the perils of obstructions and obstacles; and to satisfy countless human and nonhuman migrators through the supreme gift of the Holy Dharma. Therefore, to respectfully proclaim a small portion [of those songs], {465} I ask you to first commence with the stages of the preliminaries and the visualizations for meditate absorption.
zhes bskul te/ / ma nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i sems can thams cad skyabs kun 'dus kyi ngo bo bla ma rin po che la skyabs su mchi ba lags so/ / lan gsum/

(With that encouragement, repeat the following three times.) All sentient beings, my mothers, equal to the reaches of space, go for refuge in the precious guru, the unified essence of all refuges. (Repeat three times.)
sems can thams cad kyi don tu zung 'jug rdo rje 'chang chen po'i go 'phang thob par bya/ / de'i ched du do ha rdo rje'i dbyangs kyi bzlas rim la 'jug par bgyi'o/ /
For the sake of all sentient beings, I must attain the unified state of Great Vajradhara. To that end, I will engage in the sequence of recitation of the doha vajra melodies. (Repeat three times.)
lan gsum gyis skyabs 'gro sems bskyed bya/ /
With those triple recitations, go for refuge and arouse the mind of awakening.
mgur len pa po rnams tha mal gyi rtog pa spangs te rnal 'byor gyi rim pa la gnas dgos pas de gsal gdab pa'i phyir/
Those who take up these songs must give up their thoughts of being ordinary and dwell in the stages of the yoga. In order to bring that clearly to mind, [recite the following:]

snod bcud dag pa mkha' spyod kyi zhing khams/ / gnas khang thar pa chen po'i gzhal med khang / / phyi nang kun tu rgyan dang bkod pa dang mchod pa'i yo byad dpag tu med pa dang ldan pa/ / tshogs kyi 'dus pa dpal he ru ka lnga'i dkyil 'khor du gyur pa'i thugs ka nas sangs rgyas kyi zhing khams thams cad snang ba'i 'od zer chen po 'phros pas bskul te/ / bla ma rgyal ba sras dang bcas pa'i ye shes kyi 'khor lo mdun gyi nam mkhar gang bar spyan drangs/ badzra sa mA dzaH

The environment and its inhabitants are the pure celestial realm. The dwelling place is the celestial palace of great liberation, completely decorated and arrayed inside and outside, containing immeasurable offering articles. The assembly gathered here becomes the glorious mandala of the five herukas. From our hearts, great light rays that illuminate all buddha realms radiate and invoke the gurus, victors, and their heirs as a circle of awareness that fills the space in front—vajra samājah?.
bla ma rgyal ba sras dang bcas/ / yi dam dpa' bo rnal 'byor ma/ / mkha' khyab chos sku'i rol pa la/ / gshegs (466) bzhugs mtshan ma mi mnga' yang / /
Gurus, victors, and heirs, yidams, heroes, and yoginīs, you play in all-pervasive dharmakāya with no signs of coming or staying. {466}
gang 'dul ye shes sgyu ma'i 'phrul/ / mos pa'i yid mkhar mngon gsal te/ / don mdzad bar du brtan par bzhugs/ / tshogs kyi dkyil 'khor byin gyis rlobs/ /
Yet your magical emanations of awareness to tame whomever appear real to our mind-space of devotion. Remain here until your purpose is accomplished and bless this mandala of the assembly.
pad+ma ka ma lA ya s+t+waM/
padma kamalāya stvaṃ
bkod pa shin tu mdzes pa'i sogs maN+Dal bka' rgya ma phul/ dkon mchog gsum la bdag skyabs mchi sogs kyis rgyun shags bya/

Offer the Mandala of the Sealed Word: “Sublime mandala exquisitely arrayed…” (bkod pa shin tu mdzes pa’i maṇḍal mchog…etc.)[3] and the regular confession: “I go for refuge to the Three Jewels…” (dkon mchog gsum la bdag skyabs mchi…etc.).[4]

de'ang mos gus gsol 'debs dang bcas te mgur gyi sna 'dren/ nyams rtog dpa' ngar dang bcas te mgur gyi gzhung bsrang / dga' spro'i shis brjod dang bcas te mgur gyi mjug sdud pa bka' brgyud rin po che'i phyag bzhes lags pas/ /

Respectful devotional supplication is the lead-in to the songs. The confidence of experience and realization is the follow-through of the songs. Expressing auspicious joy and appreciation is the concluding finale of the songs. This indeed is the practice of the precious precept lineage.

thog mar rtsa brgyud bla ma rgyal ba sras dang bcas pa la mi phyed dad pa'i gdung shugs drag pos tha mal gyi snang ba 'phrog / blo sna btsan thabs su sgyur/ / rtogs pa'i ye shes gong du spor bar nus pa'i gsol 'debs kyi mgur grwa legs par bsgrigs par zhu/

Therefore, begin with intense longing of undivided faith in the root and lineage gurus, victors, and heirs. This has the power to banish ordinary perceptions, forcefully transform our frame of mind, and raise awareness through realization. Please properly prepare that way for the section on the songs with this supplication:
na mo gu ru/
namo guru
rigs kun gyi khyab bdag rdo rje 'chang / / pha drin chen bla mar gsol ba 'debs/ / drwa ba sdom mdzad bde ba'i mchog / dpal he ru ka la gsol ba 'debs/ /
I supplicate the benevolent root guru, Vajradhara, pervading lord of all families. I supplicate glorious Heruka, Cakrasaṃvara who binds the net.
dbyings bde stong zag med dkyil 'khor na/ / ye shes mkha' 'gro ni gu la gsol ba 'debs/ / gnas mkha' spyod longs sku'i zhing khams na/ / yum su kha sid+d+hi la gsol ba 'debs/ /
I supplicate Niguma, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness, in the realm of undissipating bliss-emptiness mandala. I supplicate Mother Sukhasiddhi in the celestial realm of saṃbhogakāya.
gnas gang 'dul sprul pa'i pho brang na/ / mkhas grub brgya dang lnga bcu la gsol ba 'debs/ / rgyud mthar thug lnga ldan DA ki'i sras/ / mkhas grub khyung po rnal 'byor la gsol ba 'debs/ /
I supplicate the one hundred and eight adepts in the emanated palace of taming whomever. I supplicate Khedrup Khyungpo Naljor, ḍākinīs’ son with Five Tantras’ culminations.
srid mtha' ma'i byang sems gcig brgyud 'dzin/ / rje rmog lcogs pa la gsol ba 'debs/ / lha spyan ras gzigs dbang gtsang sgom gzugs/ / rje skyer sgang pa la gsol ba 'debs/ /
I supplicate Venerable Mokchokpa, bodhisattva in his final life, holder of the single lineage. I supplicate Venerable Kyergangpa, Avalokiteśvara in the body of a pure meditator.
rigs drug pa'i khyab bdag sbas pa'i tshul/ / rje gnyan ston chen po la gsol ba 'debs/ / brgyud rin chen bdun gyi rnam thar rdzogs/ / rje sangs rgyas ston (467) pa la gsol ba 'debs/ /
I supplicate Venerable Nyentön the Great, pervasive lord of the six families in a hidden way. I supplicate Venerable Sangye Tönpa, exemplar of the lives of the Seven-Jewel lineage. {467}
bka' brgyud pa'i chu klung 'babs pa'i gzhi/ / rje mkhas grub rnam gsum la gsol ba 'debs/ / ngo mtshar ba'i rnam thar phrin las can/ / dpal 'jag bsam brgyud pa la gsol ba 'debs/ /
I supplicate the three learned and accomplished lords, the ground where the Kagyu rivers fall. I supplicate the lineage of glorious Jak and Sam, who had amazing lives of awakened activities.
rje tshul khrims mgon dang ri khrod pa/ / shangs dkar rin chen rgyal mtshan la gsol ba 'debs/ / rje lkugs lung ba dang nam rgyal ba/ / rgya sgom legs pa rgyal mtshan la gsol ba 'debs/ /
I supplicate Venerable Tsultrim Gön, Ritröpa, and Shangkarwa Rinchen Gyaltsen. I supplicate Venerable Kuklungpa, Namgyalwa, and Gyagom Lekpa Gyaltsen.
mkha' 'gro'i rjes bzung 'chi med 'grub/ / rje thang stong rgyal po la gsol ba 'debs/ / brtul zhugs spyod pas 'gro ba 'dul/ / dpal ldan kun dga' grol mchog la gsol ba 'debs/ /
I supplicate Venerable Tangtong Gyalpo, who achieved immortality nurtured by ḍākinīs. I supplicate glorious Kunga Drolchok, who subdued beings by deliberate conduct.
don chos sku'i dgongs pa mngon tu gyur/ / rje brag stod pa la gsol ba 'debs/ / he ru ka dpal gsang ba'i bdag / rje btsun tA ra nA tha la gsol ba 'debs/ /
I supplicate Venerable [Chöku Lhawang] Draktöpa, who manifested the real intent of dharmakāya. I supplicate Venerable Tāranātha, Heruka, glorious lord of secrets.
dpal shangs pa'i bka' brgyud 'dzin mdzad pa'i/ / skyes mchog rim byon rnams la gsol ba 'debs/ / gnas mi shigs 'khor lo lnga yi dbus/ / yi dam rgyud sde lnga la gsol ba 'debs/ /
I supplicate the succession of sublime persons, holders of the glorious Shangpa Kagyu. I supplicate the yidams of Five Tantras in the centers of the indestructible five chakras.
lus dwangs ma 'od lnga'i thig le ru/ / ye shes mkha' 'gro yab yum la gsol ba 'debs/ / gnas snying rje rnam rol dur khrod nas/ / myur mdzad ye shes mgon po la gsol ba 'debs/ /

I supplicate the ḍākas and ḍākinīs of timeless awareness in the five-colored drops of the body’s subtle essence. I supplicate Swift-Acting Awareness Protector from the charnel ground of compassionate display.
phyi tha snyad 'khrul pa'i snang ba zhig / nang kun rdzob don dam dbyer med rtogs/ / bar chos sku'i rang zhal mngon gyur nas/ / khams gsum gyi 'khor ba dong sprugs shog /

Outwardly, may designations of deluded appearances collapse. Inwardly, may I realize the inseparability of the relative and ultimate. In between, may I actualize the very nature of dharmakāya and empty the pit of cyclic existence in the three realms.
Buddha Vajradhara

rigs thams cad kyi khyab bdag rgyal ba drug pa rdo rje 'chang chen pos rang snang ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro la skye med gnyug ma'i rang sgras 'khor 'das phyag rgya chen po'i rang bzhin tu ngo sprod pa'i gnas lugs rdo rje'i tshigs rkang 'di gsungs so/ /

Great Vajradhara, the sixth sovereign overlord of all the families, sang these vajra lines of the abiding nature to his own appearance as Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness [Niguma] by way of the uncreated natural self-sound, revealing cyclic existence and its transcendence as the nature of mahāmudrā.
bde chen lhun grub 'dus ma byas/ / longs sku rdo rje 'chang chen gyis/ / skye med rang sgra 'di skad thos/ /
tha mal shes pa e ma ho/ / sngon (468) 'gro rang bab rnam pa gsum/ / dngos gzhi skyon bzhi rang sar grol/ / mthar thug sku bzhi rang shar ro/ /
Emaho! Ordinary mind—amazing! {468} The preliminary is three naturally settled states. The main practice is the four faults free in their own ground. The ultimate is the naturally arisen four kāyas.
sngon 'gro'i dam tshig gsang ba'i rdo rje'o/ / bogs 'don snying rje gsol 'debs so/ / lam khyer cir snang de nyid do/ / mngon gyur bsgom med yengs med do/ /

The preliminary’s sacred pledge is a vajra secret. Enhancement is supplication and compassion. Integration is seeing that suchness in whatever appears. Actualization is being without meditation and without distraction.
bsre ba rtog med lam khyer ro/ / 'od gsal lta stangs bogs 'don no/ / sad rjes gsal la rtog med bsre/ / nyin mtshan bar do'i 'od gsal ni/ / sku gsum dbyer med rang shar ltos/ /

Blending is integrating nonthought on the path. The yogic gaze of lucid clarity is enhancement. After waking, blend nonthought with clarity. Lucid clarity in the day, night, and intermediate state: see the natural arising of the three inseparable kāyas.

gang gis mi shes rgyud du sbas pa'i don/ / mthar thug tshig gcig grol ba 'di yin te/ / bsgom med yengs med goms shing brtan pa las/ / sa lam rim pa dus 'dir bgrod byed pa'i/ / yid la mi byed sgrib gnyis rang sar dag /

This is the single word that discloses the ultimate meaning that no one knows is hidden in their mind stream. Familiarize and stabilize nonmeditation and nondistraction. Then you will traverse the grounds and paths right away. With no mental engagement, the two obscurations are pure on their own.

sku gsum rang shar 'bras bu lhun gyis grub/ / mdo rgyud kun tu bstan kyang rang bzhin gab/ / bla ma'i byin rlabs zhal las shes par bya/ / chos sku'i nam mkhar rtogs pa'i sprin tshogs las/ / dug lnga'i glog 'gyu ye shes chen por ltos/ /

The resultant naturally arising three kāyas are spontaneously present. All sutras and tantras teach this, but it is naturally concealed. You should learn it directly from the guru’s blessing. In the dharmakāya sky, lightning of five poisons flashes from the clouds of conceptual thought—see great timeless awareness.
yid la mi byed re dogs kun bral ba'i/ / tha mal shes pa khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/ /
Without mental engagement, free of all hopes and fears, I bow to you, ordinary mind.

zhes rdo rje'i tshig 'di nyid mkhas grub khyung po rnal 'byor gyis ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro ma la gser srang lnga brgya phul nas zhus te mgul gyi ga'u tsit+ta 'dra ba'i nang du mi 'bral bar bcangs pa'o/ /
Khedrup Khyungpo Naljor entreated Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness for these very vajra lines by offering five hundred gold pieces. He put it inside a heart-like amulet box and wore it constantly.[5]
Niguma

ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro ni gup+ta zhes bya ba dpal nA ro tA pa'i lcam mo rang byung gi rnal 'byor ma sa bcu'i dbang phyug rgyal ba rdo rje 'chang dngos kyis rjes su bzung ba de nyid kyis rang grol phyag rgya chen po rdo rje'i tshigs rkang 'di gsungs so/ /

The Awareness Ḍākinī called Nigupta was the sister of glorious Nārotapa. She was a self-manifesting yoginī, a mighty bodhisattva on the tenth level, who was actually nurtured by Vajradhara. She taught these vajra lines of Naturally Free Mahāmudrā.[6]
yid bzhin nor bu lta bu yi/ / sems nyid khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/ / rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas thob 'dod pas/ / tha mal rnam rtog dag bya'i phyir/ / rang lus lhar gsal bla ma la/ /
I bow to you, mind itself, the wish-fulfilling gem. Wishing to attain perfect awakening, visualize your own body as the deity to purify ordinary thoughts.
lhag bsam dag pa'i mos gus bya/ / bla ma yi dam mi bsam zhing / / dngos dang dngos med la sogs pa/ / gang (469) yang yid la mi bya bar/ /
Be devoted with a pure noble heart to the guru. Don’t dwell on the guru or yidam, don’t bring anything to mind, such as whether things are real or not real. {469}
ma bcos gnyug ma'i ngang la bzhag / rang sems ma bcos chos kyi sku/ / de la ma yengs bsgom pa'i gnad/ / mtha' bral chen por rtogs bar bya/ /
Rest within the uncontrived native state. Your mind without distraction is dharmakāya. Nondistraction from that is the vital point of meditation. Realize the great freedom from limitations.
'khor ba'i rgya mtshor skyur byed pa'i/ / chags sdang rtog pa sna tshogs 'di/ / skye med mtshon cha rnon po yis/ / rang bzhin med par bcad par bya/ /
The variety of desirous and hateful thoughts that strand you in the ocean of cyclic existence: sever them as intrinsically nonexistent with the sharp weapon of the unborn.

sdong po'i rtsa ba bcad gyur na/ / yal ga skye bar mi 'gyur ro/ / ji ltar dwangs pa'i rgya mtsho las/ / chu bur byung zhing chu la thim/ / de bzhin rnam par rtog pa yang / / chos nyid min pa gzhan med kyi/ / skyon du ma blta glod la zhog /

If the tree is cut at the root, the branches will not grow. Just as bubbles arise and dissolve in the water of the limpid sea, in that way conceptual thinking is nothing other than the nature of phenomena. Don’t see it as a problem—relax.
gang shar gang skyes de nyid la/ / der 'dzin med pas rang sar grol/ / snang grags chos rnams rang gi sems/ / sems las ma gtogs chos gzhan med/ /
Whatever arises, whatever is born, that itself without fixation is free in and of itself. Appearance, sound, and phenomena are your own mind. Aside from mind, there are no phenomena.
sems ni skye 'gags spros dang bral/ / sems kyi de nyid shes pa des/ / 'dod yon lnga la spyad gyur kyang / / chos nyid ngang las g.yos pa med/ /
Mind is free of the elaborations of arising and cessation. By knowing that suchness of mind, even when engaging in the five sense desirables, you will not leave the nature of phenomena.
dper na gser gling phyin pa yis/ / sa rdo btsal yang mi rnyed ltar/ / mnyam nyid chos dbyings chen po la/ / spang blang mnyam bzhag rjes thob med/ /

For instance, one who goes to the golden isle cannot find dirt and stone even when sought. In the equality of the great realm of phenomena, there is no rejecting or accepting, no equipoise or subsequent attainment.
gang gi tshe na mngon du 'gyur/ / de tshe lhun gyis grub par gyur/ / 'gro ba'i re ba skong mdzad pa'i/ / yid bzhin nor bu lta bur 'gyur/ /
At whatever time this is actualized, at that time it becomes spontaneously present. You become like a wish-fulfilling gem who fulfills the hopes and desires of beings.
gang zag dbang po rab 'bring gsum/ / blo yi rim pas shes par bya/ / zhes gsungs so/ ! /
You should understand this as applicable to the levels of highest, intermediate, and lesser personal capacity.
Sukhasiddhi

ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro su kha sid+d+hi zhes dpal chen bir wa pas sprul pa'i dkyil 'khor du dbang rdzogs par bskur bas nub gcig la sa brgyad pa'i rtogs pa mngon tu gyur nas rdo rje 'chang dngos su mjal te bcom ldan 'das bdag med ma dang dbyer med pa de nyid kyis skal ldan rnams la gdams pa'i snying po stsal ba/ /

Awareness Ḍākinī Sukhasiddhi was fully initiated into the emanated mandala by the great glorious Virūpa. She actualized the realization of the eighth level in a single evening and encountered the real Vajradhara. She became inseparable from Bhagavatī Nairātmya. She granted this essential teaching to her fortunate disciples.
tshogs drug yul du ma spyad pa'i/ / dran med mya ngan 'das pa'i lam/ / rnam par mi tog chos kyi dbyings/ / yid dang bral bas phyag (470) rgya che/ /
Disengaged from the objects of the six senses, nonrecollection is the path to transcendence. No conceptual thought is the realm of phenomena, free of mentation—that is mahāmudrā. {470}
ma sgoms ma sgoms blo ma sgoms/ / blos sgom rtog pa'i 'khrul 'khor yin/ / rtog pas 'khor bar bcings pa ste/ / blo dang bral ba bsgom du med/ /
Don’t meditate! Don’t meditate! Don’t mentally meditate! Mental meditation is the machination of conceptual thought. Concepts bind you to cyclic existence.
nam mkha' rig med stong pa la/ / rig bcas sems kyi rtsa ba gcun/ / rtsa ba gcun la lhug par zhog / ces gsungs so/ ! /
In empty space, which lacks awareness, with awareness tame the root of mind. Tame the root and rest relaxed.
Maitrīpa

grub pa'i dbang phyug chen po dpal sha ba ri pas dngos su rjes su bzung zhing bar do phyag rgya chen po mchog grub par lung bstan pa/ / dpa' bo dang mkha' 'gro ma mtha' yas pa'i gtso bo/ snying po don gyi gnas lugs yid la mi byed pa'i gdams ngag gi bdag po/ / rgyal ba mai tri pa gnyis med rdo rje nyid bi kra ma la shI lar sbas pa'i tshul du bzhugs pa'i tshe chang dang phyag rgya brten pa dge 'dun gyis mthong ste gnas nas dbyung ba na/ chu bo gad+ga la khri snyan sA le'i lpags gdan bting / / sba ber gyis skya ba mdzad nas gshegs te mgur 'di bzhengs so/

The great mighty adept, glorious Śavarīpa accepted him as his disciple and predicted his attainment of supreme mahāmudrā in the intermediate state. Chief of infinite heroes and ḍākinīs, master of instructions in the essential meaning of the abiding nature through mental nonengagement, this is the sovereign Maitrīpa [also known as] Advayavajra. While he was living in a hidden manner at Vikramaśīla Monastery, the other monastics saw him indulging in alcohol and consorts, and they expelled him. So he went to the River Ganges where he spread out a mat of a kṛṣṇasāra pelt (black spotted antelope), used his staff as an oar, and paddled off while constructing this song.[7]
bla ma rje btsun brten na bde/ / gdams ngag bdud rtsi 'thungs na bde/ / de nyid nyams su myong na bde/ / nyams myong ci yang med na bde/ /
To attend a venerable guru is joy. To drink the elixir of instruction is joy. To taste that experience is joy. To have no experience at all is joy.
re dogs med pa'i lta ba bde/ / lhun gyis grub na yongs kyang bde/ / gnyis 'dzin med pa'i bsgom pa bde/ / gza' gtad med na yongs kyang bde/ /
The view without hopes and fears is joy. If it is spontaneous, more’s the joy. Meditation without dualism is joy. If it is without reference point, more’s the joy.
blang dor med pa'i spyod pa bde/ / nyam nga med na yongs kyang bde/ / sems kyis sems la bltas na bde/ / re dogs gol sa bcad na bde/ /
Conduct without moral choice is joy. If it is fearless, more’s the joy. To view the mind with the mind is joy. To sever the deviance of hope and fear is joy.
ri khrod dgon pa 'grims na bde/ / re dogs med pa'i lta ba bde/ / yul dang gnyen 'dun bzhag na bde/ / bsod snyoms zas la bsten na bde/ /
To roam in remote mountain retreats is joy. The view without hope and fear is joy. To leave homeland and relations is joy. To live on alms for food is joy.
bde chen zas su zos na bde/ / 'od gsal gos su gon na bde/ / pho nya lam du khyer na bde/ / dmigs pa sna rtser gtad na bde/ /
To eat the food of great bliss is joy. To wear clothes of lucid clarity is joy. To carry the path of the messenger is joy. To focus the gaze on the nose tip is joy.

zhes gsungs nas chu la thad kar thogs med du gshegs pas thams cad kyis grub pa thob par shes nas 'gyod cing phyi nas phar la phyag byas so/ / bla ma mnga' bdag chen (471) po de nyid lho phyogs dpal gyi ri la rje btsun ri khrod pa'i zhabs kyi rdul la reg nas/ / phyag rgya chen po'i dbang bskur mdzad pa'i dus su/ / dngos po'i gnas lugs gtan la dbab pa'i ched du rdo rje'i glu blangs pa'i/ /

Having said that, he sailed unhindered straight out over the water. Then everyone understood that he was an accomplished adept and with regret prostrated to him from the shore. {471} That great master guru, when he was at the mountains of Śrīparvata in the south, touched the dust from under Venerable Hermit [Śavarīpa’s] feet and requested the empowerment conferral of mahāmudrā. At that time, he sang this vajra song to ascertain the abiding nature of things.
hU~M hU~M/ 'khor dang mya ngan 'das pa dbyer mi phyed/ / chu dang rlabs bzhin du ni gnas pa yin/ / sangs rgyas sems can gnyis su med pa ste/ / dug la sngags kyis btab pa'i khyad par bzhin/ /
hūṃ hūṃ Cyclic existence and transcendence are indivisible, existing like the waves on the water. Buddhas and sentient beings are not two, like poison before and after its mantric antidote.
sems nyid gcig la sna tshogs snang ba ste/ / shel nyid rkyen gyis kha dog bsgyur ba bzhin/ / dngos po sna tshogs shar yang rang sems te/ / chu rnams thams cad rgya mtshor lan tshwa'i ro/ /
Mind itself is one but with many perceptions, like crystals changing colors under different conditions. Various things arise and yet are your own mind, like all waters will taste of salt in the sea.

dngos dang dngos med spangs nas gdod ma'i sems/ / dper na bar snang bya yi rjes bzhin gnas/ / lo stong lon pa'i mun pa 'thug po la/ / sgron me chung du gcig gis sel ba ltar/ / 'khor ba'i rab rib chags sdang 'thug po yang / / rang sems rtogs pa'i skad cig gcig la zhi/ /

Letting go of real and unreal reveals original mind, like the remains of a bird’s tracks in space. As a single small lamp banishes the dense dark of a thousand years, each instant of realizing one’s mind resolves the dense blur of cyclic existence’s passions.
rnal 'byor thabs dang shes rab zung 'jug pas/ / 'khor bar sdug bsngal rba rlabs rtog pa zhi/ / nor bu chu dangs rnyog gseb bcug pa bzhin/ / khyab dang gzugs can ma yin 'gro 'ong med/ /
The yoga of uniting method and wisdom stills the conceptual waves of pain in cyclic existence. A water-purifying gem put in mud disappears, can’t spread, and can’t move.
phyag rgya chen po'i rtogs pa skyes ma thag / khyab cing rgya che nam mkha' lta bu'i sems/ / gsal la mi rtog nam mkha' lta bu ste/ / snang yang rang bzhin med pa chu zla 'dra/ /
But as soon as mahāmudrā realization arises, the sky-like mind pervades and expands. Clarity without concept is like space, appearing without self-nature like a water moon.
'ja' tshon lta bu gsal la 'dzin pa med/ / gzhon nu'i bde ba bzhin du smra mi gtub/ / phyogs su mi gnas mtha' rnams kun dang bral/ / phyogs kyis ma gos gang gi dri ma med/ /
Clarity without fixation, like rainbows, is indescribable, like the pleasure of youth. Without direction, free of all boundaries, untainted by bias, nothing obscures it.
shel sgong 'dams na dri ma med pa bzhin/ / re dogs med pa'i sems ni seng ge 'dra/ / chu bo lta bu chad med bde chen sems/ / nyi zla'i 'od bzhin phyogs cha bral ba ste/ /
Stainless, like a crystal ball in the mud, mind is free of hopes and fears, like a lion. Undivided like a river, the mind of great bliss shines impartially like the light of the sun and moon.
e ma rang byung 'di ni ngo mtshar che/ / gnyug ma nyid du zhog cig rnal 'byor pa/ / 'di la cis kyang bcos par ma byed cig / (472) ma bcos pa ni chos kyi sku nyid do/ /
bcos pa'i skyon gyis 'phags lam mthong mi 'gyur/ / de phyir sems kyi glang po yan du chug / de ltar shes na rnal 'byor snying po ste/ / bsgrub du med par 'bras bu sangs rgyas thob/ /
Contrivance blocks the view of the exalted path, so let the elephant of mind go free. If you know that, it is the heart of yoga; the fruit of awakening is attained without practice.
byas pa med par dka' ba'i las rnams zin/ / bsgrub pa med par rang la dngos grub thob/ / bsgom pa med par don gyi 'bras bu rnyed/ / srid gsum thams cad ye nas grol ba ste/ /
All the hard work is done without acting. You attain spiritual powers without practicing. You gain the ultimate result without meditating. The three existences were liberated since forever.
'di la dgag dang bsgrub pa bya mi dgos/ / lta ba gtan la phab pa rdo rje'i mgur ro/ /
No need to deny or affirm anything here. This is the vajra song ascertaining the view.

e ma ho/ / gnas lugs gnyug ma bsgom par 'dod pa na/ / tshes grangs gza' dang rgyu skar brtsi mi dgos/ / dus kyi rgyal po dran pa'i tshe na yin/ / ri khrod dgon pa ched du mi btsal te/ / rang lus ri bo 'di ni dgon pa'i mchog /

g.yeng ba rnams kyang ched du mi spangs te/ / sna tshogs sems su shes pas grogs su 'char/ / nags la me mched rtswa rnams ji bzhin no/ / mtshams yang mi bcad tho yang mi brtsigs ste/ / smra bcad byas na mtshams kyi mchog tu 'gyur/ / ras bal 'dab ma bzhin tu glod la zhog /

bya ba thong la sems kyi rten ma bca'/ / shes pa ched du ma 'gugs yan par thong / / bying rgod byung na de ka rang la ltos/ / sems la gnod pa'i las rnams khad kyis spongs/ / zhe 'dod byung na bdud du shes par bya/ / ma bcos bzhag pa'i sems ni sangs rgyas yin/ /

Give up doing and creating mental supports; don’t restrain consciousness—let it go. If sinking or agitation arise, look directly at them. Gradually abandon whatever harms the mind. If anger or desire arise, know that it’s a devil. Resting in uncontrived mind is buddha.

'gro 'chag nyal 'dug thams cad lhug par zhog / rnam rtog kun gyi rtsa ba sems yin phyir/ / sems med phyir na rnam rtog yod ma yin/ / lhun gyis grub pa'i rten gcig skyes tsam na/ / rnal 'byor ba la zhe 'dod 'byung mi srid/ / de phyir rtogs pa'i rnal 'byor blo re bde/ /

Rest relaxed during all walking, lying, or sitting. If the root of all discursive thought is mind, since there is no mind, no thought exists. If only a support for spontaneous presence arises, anger and desire cannot arise to the yogin. Therefore, a realized yogin—what a happy mind!

gza' gtad med pa'i lam gcig rnyed tsam na/ / rnal 'byor pa la phyogs cha 'byung mi srid/ / phyogs ris med pa'i shes pa nyams re dga'/ / (473) bcos ma med pa'i rgyun gcig skyes tsam na/ / rnal 'byor pa la blang dor 'byung mi srid/ / dgag bsgrub spong lan med pa dang re spro/ /

If only a way without reference points is found, prejudice cannot occur to the yogin. Consciousness without bias—what a joyful feeling! {473} If only an uncontrived continuum arises, dos and don’ts cannot occur to the yogin. Not to negate or affirm, reject or accept—what fun!

mnyam nyid byang chub sems gcig skyes tsam na/ / rnal 'byor pa la bdag gzhan 'byung mi srid/ / bdag dang gzhan du mnyam pa khod re snyoms/ / srid gsum ye nas grol ba'i ngang la zhog / bsgom pa gtan la dbab pa rdo rje glu'o/ //

If only an awakening mind of equality arises, self and other cannot occur to the yogin. The equality of self and other—what a fair plan! Rest in the state of three existences’ primordial liberation. This is the vajra song ascertaining the meditation. ithi
e ma ho/ / sems kyi bag dang ldan pa spyod pa'i mchog / bag med mi bya dran dang shes bzhin bstan/ / spyod pa gang byed tshad du mi bzung ste/ / gang yang spyod la byis pa lta bur gyis/ /
Emaho! A conscientious mind is the best conduct. Don’t be careless; exhibit mindful awareness. Whatever you do, don’t set limits. Do anything at all, like an infant.
ma bcos spyod pa bu chung lta bur zhog / nyam nga med pa seng ge lta bur spyod/ / the tshom med pa glang chen chur zhugs bzhin/ / gtsang sme med pa khyi phag lta bur rol/ /
Behave without artifice, like a little boy. Be fearless, like a lion. Have no doubts, like an elephant plunging into water. Enjoy clean and unclean, like a dog or pig.

gnas kyi ro snyoms bung ba lta bur spyod/ / rang byung mi dgag smyon pa lta bur zhog / gza' gtad med pa sha za lta bur 'khrungs/ / kun tu rgyu bas 'byung ba rlung bzhin du/ / zhen pa med par 'gro ba 'di ni mchog / gang ltar myong ba skye med rgya yis gdab/ /

Frequent all places in equal taste, like a fly. Don’t suppress what arises, like a crazy person. Be aimless, like a born carnivore. Go everywhere, like the wind element; such movement without attachment is best. Whatever you experience, apply the seal of the unborn.

spyod pa gtan la dbab pa rdo rje'i glu'o/ / re dogs med pa sems nyid gnyug ma des/ / dran pa med pas brjod med ting 'dzin thob/ / skye ba med pas 'gyur med lta ba thob/ / 'dzin pa med pas phyogs med spyod pa thob/ / rkyen dang bral bas blo 'das 'bras bu thob/ / byas pa med pas dka' ba'i las rnams zin/ /

This is the vajra song ascertaining the conduct. In native mind itself without hopes and fears you attain ineffable absorption through nonminding, you attain the changeless view through the unborn, you attain unbiased conduct through nonfixation, you attain inconceivable results through the unconditioned, and all hard work is completed without doing anything.

bsags pa med par zad med gter rnams sogs/ / 'dus pa med par 'bral med grogs dang mjal/ / bum pa bzang dang dpag bsam nor bu ltar/ / 'bras bu rang byung 'di ni ngo mtshar che/ / 'bras bu gtan la dbab pa rdo rje'i glu'o/ /

You’ll meet constant companions without gathering and inexhaustible treasures without accumulating. Like an excellent vase or the wish-fulfilling gem, these self-occurring results are incredible. This is the vajra song ascertaining the result.
Rāhula

'phags yul lho phyogs su sku 'khrungs shing rdo rje rnal 'byor ma sogs khyad par (474) lha bzhis dngos su rjes su bzung zhing byin gyis brlabs/ / 'chi med rdo rje'i sku brnyes nas bod du pheb cing rdzu 'phrul gyis slar rgya gar du gshegs te ri nag po zhes bya ba shing gi ri'i khong gsengs su dngos su bzhugs nas 'gro ba'i don mdzad pa grub brnyes rnal 'byor gyi dbang phyug sgra gcan 'dzin sbas pa'i rdo rje'i zhal snga nas bsam gyis mi khyab pa nyams su len par zhal gyi gdams pa 'di gsungs so/ /

Born in southern India, Vajrayoginī and the other special four deities actually looked after him and granted blessings. {474} After he attained the undying vajra body, he miraculously traveled to Tibet and back again. He still lives in the forested hills of the Black Mountains, accomplishing the welfare of migrators. The mighty yogin adept Rāhulaguptavajra taught this oral instruction on practicing the inconceivable.
[Homage to the bodhisattvas!][8]
bla ma rnams la phyag 'tshal lo/ / dgongs pa mdor bsdus rnal 'byor gyi/ / tshad med bzhi yi nyams len ni/ / bsam gyis mi khyab bshad par bya/ /
Homage to the gurus! Their intentions in short are the practice of the four immeasurables of yoga. Though inconceivable, I will explain.
rgyu 'bras stong pa'i rang bzhin la/ / dngos med gzugs dang gnyis med sgra/ / dmigs med 'bras bu 'bad med 'gyur/ / dper na 'brug med char bzhin no/ /
In the empty nature of cause and effect, immaterial form, nondual sound, and nonreferential result arise effortlessly, as in the example of rain without thunder.
de phyir rang bzhin bdag med kyi/ / brtul zhugs skal ldan rnal 'byor pa/ / snang zhing srid pa sna tshogs 'di/ / dngos med stong pa bdag med de/ / ngo bo nyid kyi rnam par dag /
Therefore fortunate yogins enter the deliberate conduct of selfless nature. This variety of apparent existence is unreal, empty, and without identity; its very essence totally pure.
de lta bu yi snying rje la/ / sangs rgyas sems can gnyis su med/ / mi bsgom mi rtog rang bzhin gsal/ / mtha' dbus bral ba dbu ma'i don/ / de ltar sems kyi rang bzhin bsgom/ /

In the compassion of such a state, buddhas and beings are no different. Nonmeditation, nonthought, natural clarity without center or circumference is the meaning of the middle [way]; meditate on mind’s nature like that.
ma rtogs pa yi sems can la/ / nad 'don snying rje bsgom par bya/ / bdag gi mdun du gang zhig kyang / / mnyam par bzhag ste mnyam par bsgom/ /
Meditate with compassion on the sickness and spirits of the sentient beings who don’t realize that. Rest in evenness and meditate with equanimity on whatever is right before you.
de la rnam pa thams cad kyis/ / gnyis med don ni 'grub 'gyur ro/ / bsgom pa'i snyan brgyud gdams ngag ni/ / sangs rgyas thams cad 'dus pa'i sku/ / kun gyi sems nyid hU~M yig dkar/ /

With that, at all times and circumstances you will accomplish the meaning of nonduality. The meditation[9] instruction of the aural lineage: The form of all buddhas united as one, and the very minds of all are a white letter hūṃ.
bdag dang gzhan gyi snying khar bsgom/ / nyi ma'i gdan steng thig ler bsgom/ / de nyid kyis ni 'gro 'dul ba/ / nyon mongs thams cad sbyangs par bsam/ / de ni gnyis med don yin te/ /
Meditate on that in the hearts of self and others as a vital drop upon a sun seat. Imagine [as it emanates and returns back][10] it is that which tames migrators and purifies all afflictive emotions.
lha yi de nyid rang bzhin med/ / de ltar snying rje bsgoms byas nas/ / bsam (475) mi khyab pa'i byams pa ni/ / phan phyir 'di ltar bsam par bya/ /
rnal 'byor bdag nyid snying kha ru/ / pad+ma 'dab brgyad sran ma'i tshad/ / de nas 'od gsal dkar dmar de/ / bar du me lha'i oM yig ni/ /
In my, the yogin’s, own heart is a pea-sized eight-petaled lotus. From that [comes] white and red clear light, between which is Agni’s white oṃ.
dngos po'i rnal 'byor gang yang med/ / de la ci yang bsam mi bya/ / gang zhig sgom pa'i rnal 'byor de/ / gnyis med ye shes 'grub 'gyur ro/ /
It has nothing to do with physical yoga; it is absolutely unimaginable. Whoever does this yogic meditation will realize nondual timeless awareness.
gsal rig med pa chos kyi sku/ / de ltar phra ba'i rnal 'byor la/ / mngon shes shar te gnyis med rtogs/ / dga' ba'i rang bzhin 'byung gyur la/ / btang snyoms 'bras bu thob pa'o/ /

That clarity without awareness is dharmakāya. In such subtle yoga as this, clairvoyance dawns and nonduality is realized. The intrinsic nature of joy will arise and you will gain the result, equanimity.
kha gcig lha bzhi bsgom ste gnas/ / kha gcig ngag gi 'don par brten/ / gnyis med bsgom pa mi shes so/ /
Some people stay with the meditation of four deities.[11] Some rely on verbal recitation.[12] They do not understand how to meditate on the nondual.
zhal nas zhal du brgyud pa yi/ / zhal gdams gzhan la phan phyir ni/ / rA hu las ni bshad par bya/ / zhes gsungs so/ /
This oral instruction for others’ welfare from the lineage passed from mouth to mouth has been explained by Rāhula.[13]

'chi med grub pa rA hu la gup+ta de nyid bla ma grub thob rnams kyis lung bstan pa ltar/ 'phags yul du nyi ma shar ba la rdzu 'phrul gyis pheb pas bod yul du nam langs ma thag par mkhas grub khyung po rnal 'byor 'phan yul 'jog por thugs dam la bzhugs pa'i sar pheb cing rdzu 'phrul gyi bkod pa bstan/ / zla ba bcu gcig bzhugs nas thun mong dang thun mong min pa'i gdams ngag du ma gnang ste rgya gar du slar pheb pa'i tshe/ / bla ma shangs ba nyid mang yul bar du gshegs skyel 'byon pa na zhal gdams rdo rje'i tshigs drug ma 'di stsal to/ /

In keeping with the predictions of his accomplished gurus, Rāhulagupta, the adept of immortality, left the exalted land of India one morning at dawn. With magical abilities he traveled to Tibet and arrived right at daybreak in Penyul Jokpo, the place where the learned and accomplished Khyungpo Naljor was doing his spiritual practice, thus showing him a miraculous display. Rāhula stayed for eleven months, during which he gave many common and uncommon instructions. When it was time to return to India, Lama Shangpa [Khyungpo Naljor] accompanied him as far as Mangyul, where Rāhula granted these “Vajra Lines in Six [Syllables in Six Verses].”[14]
sdug bsngal rtsa bar gyur pa/ / bdag tu 'dzin pa yin gyis/ / phyogs ris zhe 'dod spongs la/ / mnyam nyid don la zhog cig /
The root of suffering is fixation on self. Without hate or desire, settle in evenness.
tshe 'di mi rtag 'gyur zhing / / phyi ma mi 'chang skye bas/ / rgyu 'bras tshul bzhin srungs la/ / dam tshig brtson par gyis shig /
Life changes and ends but is not done; born again. Care for cause and effect, uphold sacred pledge.
gnas lugs zung 'jug yin pas/ / 'ja' tshon lta bu'i lus 'di/ / snang la rang bzhin med par/ (476) brtag tu dran par gyis shig /
Since nature is union, this rainbow-like body appears without substance. {476} Always remember that.
tshe 'dir dgos 'dod 'byung zhing / / phyi ma lam sna 'dren pas/ / bla ma sangs rgyas lta bu/ / rtag tu dran par gyis shig /
This life’s desires will come, next life’s path will be shown by Buddha-like gurus. Always remember that.
brtan pa ma thob bar du/ / 'du 'dzi'i g.yeng ba rgod pas/ / ri dwags smas ma bzhin du gcig pur nyams su longs zhig /
Until you are stable, you’re busy and upset. Like a wounded gazelle, practice alone yourself.
rtsod ldan dus kyi sems can/ / nga rgyal phrag dog che bas/ / bum nang mar me bzhin du/ / yon tan sems la sbos shig /
Beings in this age of war have great pride and envy. Like a lamp in a vase, hide your good qualities.
ces gsungs nas nam mkha'i lam la gya gyur bzhud pa'i tshul gyis skad cig gis rdo rje gdan gyi tshogs dpon la phebs so/ ! /
Rāhula sang that song and then took his leave by way of the sky. Instantly he arrived at the Vajra Seat and presided at a communal feast.
Khyungpo Naljor
na mo gu ru/ /
namo guru

sangs rgyas kyi zhing khams kun tu mtshan gyis snyan pas yongs su khyab cing / / zhabs sen nor bu'i me long la lha dang bcas pa'i 'jig rten gsum gyi gtsug gi phud bus btud pa/ / gangs can gyi ljongs na 'gran pa'i zla thams cad dang bral ba'i mkhas grub chen po khyung po rnal 'byor tshul khrims mgon po de nyid kyi rnam par thar pa'i snying po mdor bsdus pa tshigs su bcad de bka' stsal pa ni/ /

His name is renowned throughout all the buddha realms, completely pervading them. Beings of the three realms along with the gods bow their hair crowns to the mirror gems of his toes. In the Himalayan regions he was unrivaled and without any comparison. Great Khedrup Khyungpo Naljor Tsultrim Gönpo spoke these verses himself, summarizing the essence of his life of freedom:
bla ma yi dam mkha' 'gro chos skyong la/ / khyung po rnal 'byor bdag gis gus btud nas/ / phyi rabs brgyud 'dzin rnams la phan pa'i phyir/ / rnam thar zur tsam bshad kyi gus pas nyon/ /

I, Khyungpo Naljor, bow with respect to the guru, yidams, ḍākinīs, and dharma protectors. In order to benefit lineage holders of future generations, I will narrate some of my life. Please listen respectfully.
ban chung bdag gi skye sa gangs dkar mda'/ / gnye mo ra mang rje rigs khyung po yin/ / pha ru smos pa khyung rgyal stag skyes dang / / ma ru smos pa mgo bza' bkra shis skyid/ /
I, a humble monk, was born at Nyemo Ramang in Gangkarda, into the noble Khyung clan. My father was called Khyung Gyaltak and my mother was Gozang Tashi Kyi.
de yi rum du bdag nyid zhugs pa'i tshe/ / pha ma yul mi bde skyid ldan par gyur/ / stag gi lo la ma yi rum nas btsas/ / de tshe rgya gar grub thob a mo g+has/ /
When I entered into her womb, my parents and local people became happy. I emerged from the womb in the Tiger year. At that time, the Indian adept Amogha said:
'di ni sprul pa'i sku ste rgya gar bgrod/ / paN+Di ta dang grub thob thams cad kyi/ / thugs bcud bsdus nas 'gro rnams smin grol byed/ / sna tshogs sprul pas gdul bya 'dul bar 'gyur/ /
“This child, an incarnation, will go to India and collect the heart essence of all paṇḍitas and adepts that will mature and liberate all migrators. His various emanations will train disciples. {477}
theg chen snying po mtha' (477) gral chos sgra sgrogs/ / mthar thug gsang sngags bde stong dbyer med kyi/ / seng ge'i nga ro phyogs bcur sgrogs par 'gyur/ / de yi lus ni bde mchog 'khor lo ste/ /
He will proclaim essential Mahayana dharma free of extremes, and the lion’s roar of Secret Mantra, inseparable bliss-emptiness, will be heard in the ten directions. His body will become Cakrasaṃvara,
gsung ni ma hA mA yA'i bdag nyid 'gyur/ / thugs ni dpal ldan dgyes pa rdo rje ste/ / sprul pa'i gnas mchog gsang ba 'dus pa la/ / gsang gnas bde skyong gshin rje'i gshed du 'gyur/ /
his speech the epitome of Mahāmāya, his mind glorious Hevajra, his emanation place supreme Guhyasamāja, and his secret place bliss-holding Yamāntaka.
dkyil 'khor de rnams lus la bkod nas kyang / / gdul bya rnams la dngos su ston par byed/ / gzhan yang yi dam sna tshogs gzugs bsgyur nas/ / gdul dka' skye bo dpag med 'dul bar byed/ /
Once these mandalas are arrayed in his body, they will actually manifest to his disciples. Further, he will transform into various yidams to train innumerable people difficult to train.

lo ni brgya dang lnga bcu 'tsho bar 'gyur/ / de yi mthar ni mdzad pa brtul ba'i tshe/ / ltas dang rdzu 'phrul sna tshogs sta\u0f7cna par 'gyur/ / de nas zhing khams rnam dag bde ba can/ / rgyal ba kun bsngags zhing der sangs rgyas nas/ / theg chen chos kyi 'khor lo bskor bar 'gyur/ /

His life span will be one hundred and fifty years. At the end, when it’s time for vanquishing conduct, various omens and miracles will be displayed. Then he will pass on to the pure realm Sukhāvatī that is praised by all victors and become a buddha, turning the wheel of the Mahayana dharma.
phyi rabs dad ldan gdul bya thams cad kun/ / rgyal ba'i zhing der bgrod par the tshom med/ / de skad gsungs nas bla ma grub thob de/ / mkha' la bya bzhin rgya gar yul du gshegs/ /

Future generations of all people with faith will no doubt also go to that realm of the victors.” After speaking those words, that great adept returned to the exalted land of India like a bird in the sky.
lo lnga lon nas pha mas lung bstan bshad/ / lo bcu lon nas yig rtsis mkhas par shes/ / bcu gnyis lon tshe pha mes bag chags kyis/ / sems phyogs bon bslab rdzogs chen phyag chen bslab/ /

My parents reported this prophecy when I was five years old. By the time I was ten I had mastered writing and calculation. At twelve, as was the custom of my paternal ancestors, I studied the mind teachings of Bön, dzogchen, and mahāmudrā.

de nas rin chen gser phye phongs med khyer/ / gces pa'i srog la ma bltas dga' spyad nas/ / rgya dang bal po'i yul du lan bdun phyin/ / rgya gar mkhas pa brgya dang lnga bcu bsten/ / khyad par mkhas shing grub thob lnga bcu dang / / rtsa ba'i bla ma khyad 'phags rnam bzhi bsten/ / longs sku drug pa rdo rje 'chang chen la/ / dngos su chos gsan ye shes mkha' 'gro gnyis/ /

Then, carrying a decent amount of gems and gold dust, without regard for my own life and with great difficulty, I traveled to the lands of India and Nepal seven times. I studied with one hundred and fifty sages in India, particularly fifty learned and great adepts, four especially exalted root gurus, and two awareness ḍākinīs who truly heard teachings from the saṃbhogakāya, the sixth buddha Vajradhara.
mnyes par byas nas mthar thug gdams ngag zhus/ / sgro 'dogs chod nas (478) rtse gcig bsgrubs pa yis/ / mchog dang thun mong dngos grub rnam gnyis thob/ /
rnam thar mdor bstan yin gyi gus pas nyon/ /
That was a short account of his life. Now listen respectfully.

de ltar ji skad bka' stsal ba'i mkhas grub shangs pa gdu gu pa de nyid thog mar don la mkhas shing dngos grub brnyes de nas 'byung gnas seng ge las rdzogs chen sde gsum/ skor ni ru pa las phyag rgya chen po'i rgyud rgya gzhung sogs gzhung gdams mang du gsan cing thams cad la mkhas pa'i phul du gyur kyang / sngon gyi las 'phro sad de dgung lo lnga bcu pa la rgya gar du pheb/ mkhas grub brgya dang lnga bcu/ rtsa ba'i bla ma rnam bzhi/ ye shes mkha' 'gro rnam pa gnyis sogs las theg pa che chung thun mong thun mong ma yin pa'i chos sgo bsam gyi mi khyab pa gsan cing de dag la mkhas par sbyangs/ mchog thun mong gi dngos grub rdzogs par thob pa las/

As described in his own words, Khedrup Shangpa Dugupa[16] first became learned in the Bön doctrine and attained spiritual powers. Then he heard teachings on the three classes of great completion (rdzogs chen) from Jungne Senge, and studied the Indian source tantras of mahāmudrā, the Great Seal, with Kor Nirupa, and so forth. He studied many such sources and instructions, and became highly proficient in all of them. But his former karma was awakened, and at the age of fifty he left for India. There he studied with one hundred and fifty learned adepts, four root gurus, two ḍākinīs of timeless awareness, and so on. He practiced and learned unimaginable approaches to the dharma from the greater and lesser vehicles, common and uncommon.
thog mar khyad 'phags bla ma rnam bzhi'i ya gyal rdo rje gdan pa puN+ya ka ra gup+ta dang mjal ba'i tshul mgur du bzhengs pa/
First, this song about meeting Vajrāsana Puṇyāgupta, one of his especially exalted four gurus:

kho bo khyung po rnal 'byor gyis/ 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal ma bzod par/ / 'jigs skrag chen po gting nas skyes/ / 'khor ba mtha' med 'di 'dra ba/ / skye 'chi'i sdug bsngal dpag tu med/ / ngan song sdug bsngal bsam mi khyab/ /

I, Khyungpo Naljor, developed a huge and deep fear of samsara’s unbearable sufferings. This never-ending cyclic existence means boundless suffering of birth and death, and unimaginable sufferings of bad existences.
'chi bas mi 'jigs skye bas 'jigs/ / skye ba las kyi rjes su 'brangs/ / rang dbang med par 'khor bar 'khyams/ / bdag dang sems can thams cad kyang / / ces kyang mi phan 'chi ngo shes/ /
Dying is easy; its living that scares me to death. Karma follows into the next life, and we cycle helplessly in samsara. Nothing will help me and all living beings other than getting to know death.

nam yang 'chi ba 'di 'dra la/ / chos phyir srog ni btang snyam nas/ / lus dang srog la ma bltas te/ / bal yul tsam la ma ltos bar/ / sangs rgyas stong gi 'byung gnas sa/ / ston pa mngon par sangs rgyas pa'i/ / rdo rje gdan du tshangs kyis phyin/ /

In the face of death, whose time is uncertain, I ignored my health for the sake of dharma, and without concern for my life or limb, I did not depend only on the country of Nepal but went straight to the home of the thousand buddhas, where our Teacher manifested as Buddha: the Vajra Seat of Bodhgaya, India.
rgyal ba thub pa chen po yis/ / sangs rgyas gnyis par lung bstan pa'i/ / dpal ldan (479) rdo rje gdan pa dang / / dngos su zhal mjal dkon pa yi/ / gu lang gser srang lnga brgya phul/ /

There, I met the one whom the Great Sage had prophesied to be the second Buddha— glorious Vajrāsana. {479} When I actually met him face to face, I offered him five hundred gold pieces from Gulang.[17]

sangs rgyas dngos dang mjal snyam nas/ / ba spu ldang zhing mchi ma 'khrugs/ / mos gus chen po gting nas skyes/ / gus pas thal sbyar 'di skad zhus/ / bstan pa'i rtsa ba dge slong gi / mkhan po mdzad nas 'dul ba zhu/ /

I thought I had met the actual Buddha; my hairs stood on end and tears welled up. Great devotion arose from deep inside me, and I joined my palms and said this: “Once I become a fully ordained khenpo, I request the root of the doctrine, the Vinaya.
byang chub chen por sems bskyed nas/ / theg pa chen po'i chos rnams zhu/ / smin byed gsang sngags dbang bskur nas/ / grol bar byed pa'i bskyed rdzogs zhu/ /
Once I have aroused the mind of great awakening, I request the teachings of the Mahayana. Once I have received ripening empowerment in Secret Mantra, I request liberating creation and completion.”
de skad bdag gi gsol btab pas/ / dpal ldan rdo rje gdan pa yis/ / dgyes pa'i 'dzum bstan 'di skad gsungs/ / srin po gdong dmar mtha' 'khob yul/ / log ltas rgyud dkrugs the tshom can/ /
I entreated him with those words, and the glorious Vajrāsana smiled with pleasure and spoke: “In the hinterlands of the red-faced demons, people are disturbed by wrong views and doubts.
sna tshogs chos tshol sgrub mi nus/ / rang ma smin par gzhan don byed/ / gcig la gcig smra phrag dog can/ / mi nag chos kyi lo rgyus mkhan/ /
They seek various teachings but can’t practice them. Not matured themselves, they try to help others. They are jealous and critical of each other; laypeople who have heard tell of dharma.

de lta bu yi rgyal khams na/ / dad ldan skye 'chis 'jigs pa yi/ / snying stobs ldan pa'i skyes bu khyod/ / ma nor dam chos tshol ba'i phyir/ / srog la mi phongs dka' spyad nas/ / rgya gar yul rnams bgrod byed pa'i/ /
You, who come from such a country, are an intrepid person of faith who fears birth and death. To seek the unerring Holy Dharma you traveled here to India with great hardship at the risk of your life.
skal ldan khyung po rnal 'byor khyod/ / sngon tshe byang phyogs gangs can du/ / nyan thos rdzu 'phrul dpag med ldan/ / rdzu 'phrul chen po zhes byar gyur/ /
You—lucky Khyungpo Naljor. In a former life, in the northern Himalaya, you were a śrāvaka with boundless miraculous powers who became known as Great Miracle Worker.
de tshe log lta mu stegs dang / / lha klu gnod sbyin 'byung po dang / / skye ba'i tshogs rnams 'dul bar byed/ / khyod ni nyan thos tshogs bskor nas/ / mkha' la bya bzhin rnam par rgyu/ /
At that time, you tamed misinformed heathens, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, bhūtas, and all the groups of people. You circled the assembly of śrāvakas and flew to the sky like a bird.

ri dang chu la thogs med cing / / gcig dang du mar snang ba sogs/ / sprul pa sna tshogs gzugs 'chang ba'i/ / dgra bcom chen po nyid gyur pas/ / bdag dang rgya gar mkhas rnams kyis/ / khyed kyi mkhan po byed mi nus/ /

Mountains and water didn’t hinder you. You showed various emanated forms, appearing as one or many and so forth. Since you became that great arhat, I and other wise men of India are unable to be your preceptor. {480}
byang phyogs (480) kha ba can ljongs su/ / glang ri 'od ldan gser mdog can/ / sangs rgyas snang ba mtha' yas kyi/ / sprul pa bzhugs kyi der song la/ / bsnyen par rdzogs pa'i mkhan po zhus/ /
In the north of the Land of Snows lives Langri Öden,[18] of golden color, an emanation of Buddha Amitābha. Go there and ask him to be preceptor for your full ordination.
yul dbus ma ga rdo rje gdan/ / gnas mchog 'di dang gzhan rnams su/ / khyod kyis ji skad zhus pa yi/ / 'dul ba phar phyin gsang sngags rnams/ / ji ltar 'dod bzhin bstan par bya'o/ /
Here at the Vajra Seat in Magadha and other sacred sites, I will grant your requests for Vinaya, the Perfections, and Secret Mantra and teach them however you like.”[19]

zhes gsungs nas dge tshul gyi mkhan po mdzad/ mtshan tshul khrims mgon du gsol bas bla ma rdo rje gdan pa shangs khrag shor nas/ khyung po rnal 'byor las sbo ma nus so/ / de'i dus su bla ma'i zhal nas/ khyung po dzo ki ma hA pha la pa la gsungs nas/ thog mar 'dul ba lung dang / bstan bcos mdo rtsa gsungs/ de nas mdo sngags kyi gzhung gdams thams cad rim par gnang / thams cad las khyad par du 'phags pa rin chen rgya mtsho'i rtsa bshad kyi rgyud rnams la brten pa'i rgyud sde lnga dkyil 'khor gcig tu sgrub pa'i dbang dang gdams ngag gsan pa'i tshul yang 'di ltar gsungs so/ /

He said that and acted as the preceptor for the novice monk ordination, giving him the name Tsultrim Gönpo. However, Guru Vajrāsana’s nose began to bleed, [a sign that] he couldn’t change his name from Khyungpo Naljor. At that point the guru exclaimed, “Khyungpo dzoki mahā phala phala.” First he gave him the reading transmission for the Vinaya and taught him the treatise Vinayasūtra.[20] Then gradually he taught him all the source texts and instructions of Sutra and Mantra. The most excellent of all was the cycle of the Five Tantras’ Deities practiced within a single mandala, which is based on the root and explanatory tantras of the Jewel Ocean Tantra. This is Khyungpo Naljor’s verse about how he received that empowerment and instruction:
de la rgyud sde chen po lnga'i/ / dbang dang rgyud dang sgrub pa'i thabs/ / gdams pa'i mchog gi khyad par ni/ / bde ba mchog gi grol rgyud las/ / rgyu lam 'bras bu bstan pa yang / /

The special features of the sublime instructions, empowerments, tantras, and sādhanas of the Five Great Tantra Classes are these: The liberation tantra of Cakrasaṃvara teaches the cause, path, and result.
bde ba chen po grub pas na/ / byang chub sems kyi rdo rje ni/ / bde ba sgrub pa nyid yin te/ /
To accomplish great bliss, the vajra of awakening mind is the practice of bliss itself.

dpal ldan gsang ba 'dus pa dang / / snying po ma hA mA ya dang / / yang snying dgyes pa rdo rje dang / / dga' chen za nus sgyu 'phrul che/ / dpal ldan 'khor lo sdom pa dang / / drag po rdo rje 'jigs byed rnams/ / mthar thug ston pa lnga po la/ /

Glorious Guhyasamāja, essential Mahāmāya, quintessential Hevajra, great Magical Illusion (Mahāmāya) able to eat great ecstasy, glorious Binder of the Wheel (Cakrasaṃvara), and wrathful Vajrabhairava: these are the five culminating teachers.
thabs dang shes rab gnyis gyi rgyud/ / zung du 'jug pa nyid yin pas/ / dang po smin lam dbang la yang / / phyi nang gsang ba nyid yin no/ /
They are the very integral unity of tantras of both methods and wisdom. First, in the ripening path of empowerment there are outer, inner, and secret [aspects].
lam la rim pa gnyis yin te/ / bskyed rim dang ni rdzogs rim mo/ / (481) bskyed pa snang dang rdzogs pa stong / / dbyer med zung 'jug chu zla bzhin/ /
In the path there are two stages: creation phase and completion phase. {481} Creation is appearance, and completion emptiness, integrated like the moon reflected in water.
rdzogs pa rang lus gzhan lus dang / / zung 'jug bde stong dbyer med do/ / 'bras bu mchog dang thun mong ngo / / thun mong las brgyad grub chen brgyad/ /

Completion involves one’s own body, another’s body, and their union as bliss and emptiness inseparable. The results are supreme and common spiritual powers. The common are the eight actions and eight great feats.
mchog la sku bzhi mdzad par bcas/ / lhun grub gang 'dul rang shar ro/ / gang zag sbyangs pa'i las can gyis/ / rtse gcig ma yengs 'bad gyur na/ / dam tshig ldan pas nges par thob/ /

The supreme are the four kāyas with their activities that arise spontaneously on their own to tame whomever. If trained individuals with karmic connections exert themselves with single-pointed focus and keep sacred pledges, they will surely succeed.

rang lus thabs ldan lam dang ni/ / gzhan lus las kyi phyag rgya'o/ / 'dod yon lam khyer gnad mchog 'di/ / brgyud pa mchog gi rim pa yang / / sangs rgyas lung bstan thob pa yi/ / slob dpon 'phags pa klu sgrub dang / /

One’s own body is the path of means, another’s body is the action mudra. This vital point of integrating desires comes through a sublime lineage: Exalted Master Nāgārjuna who received prediction of Buddha.
'od gsal bsten pa grub pa brnyes/ / kaM pa la zhes bya ba dang / / phyag rgya khyi ru sprul byed pa'i/ / ku ku ri pa chen po dang / /
The one called Kaṃpala who attained mastery based on lucid clarity. Kukuripa the Great who emanated dogs as mudras.
nya lto gsol zhing grub pa thob/ / lo hi pa zhes grags pa dang / / lhag pa'i lha yis byin rlabs pa/ / dpal 'dzin ha ri ke la dang / /
The one called Lūhipa who gained powers eating fish guts. And glorious Harikela[21] blessed by the presiding deity.
de dag rnams las rim brgyud pa/ / Dom+b+hi pa dang ku su lu/ / ma hA badzras legs bsdus te/ /
From all of them the succession came to Ḍombipa, Kusulu, and Mahāvajra, who brought them together.

dpal ldan ye shes sde zhes pa/ / bai ro tsa na rak+Sha ta/ / su ma ti zhes rnal 'byor dang / / ta thA ga ta rak+Shi ta/ / a mo g+ha ni badzra dang / / dpal ldan rdo rje gdan pa rnams/ / rim gyis bdag la brgyud pa'o/ / zhes sogs gsungs so/ /
Glorious Śrījñāna, Vairocanarakṣita, Sumati the yogin, Tathāgatarakṣita, Amoghavajra, and glorious Vajrāsana is the lineage that came down to me.

de nas rje btsun shrI dz+nyA na dang / bai ro tsa na rak+Shi ta/ DA ki ma ka na ka shrI sogs las mdo dang mtshan nyid/ / gsang sngags phyi nang gi rgyud sgrub thabs gdams ngag dpag tu med pa zhus zhing bod du pheb khar ri ma la ya'i rtser bla ma rdo rje gdan pa la gser srang bcu gsum phul nas tshes bcu'i mchod pa mdzad pa'i tshe ltas dang lung bstan byung ba'i tshul gyi tshigs bcad 'di gsungs so/ /

Then from Venerable Śrījñāna, Vairocanarakṣita, Ḍākima Kanakaśrī, and others, Khyungpo Naljor received innumerable teachings on Sutra, [the Mahayana path of] characteristics, and the Secret Mantra sādhanas and instructions on outer and inner tantras. When it was time for him to depart, he offered thirteen pieces of gold to Guru Vajrāsana on the summit of Mount Malaya. During the tenth-day offering rituals, he saw sights and received prophecy. He composed these verses about what happened:

mkha' las me tog char bzhin babs/ / dpa' bo (482) mkha' 'gros bar snang khengs/ / sgra dang 'od dang 'ja' tshon 'khrugs/ / lha rnams mchod pa 'bul ba'i tshe/ / rdo rje gdan pas 'di skad gsungs/ / rigs kyi bu khyod bod du song / /

Flowers fell like rain from the sky, {482} heroes and ḍākinīs filled the space, sounds and light and rainbows trembled. When we made offerings to the gods, Vajrāsana spoke these words: “Son of good family, return to Tibet.
gdul bya kha ba can ljongs kyi/ / sems can mang po grol byed cig / phyi ma'i tshe na chos 'di rnams/ / khyod kyis rgyud 'dzin rnal 'byor pa/ / gcig gis dar bar byed par 'gyur/ /
Liberate many sentient beings, disciples in the Land of Snows. In the future, these teachings will be spread by a yogin who holds your lineage.
chos 'di rnams kyi bka' thob cing / / phan sems ldan pa de yis ni/ / gang byung rgyal sras ma nor ston/ / rab tu mi gnas sa la sbyor/ / rim gyis don rtogs mang du 'byung / /

He will receive all this dharma, and with an altruistic mind, whatever happens he will teach the unerring way of the bodhisattvas and reach the level of complete nonabiding. Eventually there will be many realized disciples.
grub mtha' gzhung chen bzhi nyid las/ / mtshan nyid theg dang rdo rje theg / khyad par rnam par 'byed pa yin/ / rgyu dang 'bras bu'i lam byed pa/ /

“Of the four major classical tenet systems, a difference is fully delineated between the vehicle of characteristics and the vajra vehicle: one takes the cause and the other takes the result as the path.
mngon sum rjes dpag rim pa yis/ / gtan tshigs chen po bzhi la ni/ / mtshan nyid gsum gyis gtan la 'bebs/ / de ni rtsod pa'i lam rim mo/ /
“The stages of direct perception and inference [examined through] the four great axioms are ascertained by the three natures. That is the process for philosophical debate.
pha rol phyin dang gsang ba sngags/ / byang chub phyogs chos sum cu bdun/ / thun mong lam lnga khyad par gnyis/ / zhar spyad don bsdus lam byed pa/ / sgrub pa'i rim pa zhes bya'o/ /

“The vehicle of the perfections and Secret Mantra share the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment and differ in regard to the five paths.[22] To use the incidental concise meaning as the path is called the process for meditation practice.
de dag lam rim gnyis pa'o/ / de nyid mthong lam zhes bya dang / / lta ba ngan pas ma gos pa'i/ / ye shes mngon du byed pa'i lam/ /
“In the second of those graded paths is what is called the path of seeing. It is the path that actualizes timeless awareness that is untainted by mistaken views.
mtha' dang bral ba'i lam nyid ni/ / zung du 'jug par ston pa dang / / dbu ma chen po nyid du 'jug / zhi gnas lhag mthong ting nge 'dzin/ / gong nas gong du lam sbyong ba/ /
“The path free of extremes reveals the integral unity and enters the great middle way. Calm abiding, higher insight, and meditative absorptions increase more and more as the path is refined.
sems kyi lam mchog zhes byar bstan/ / nga dang 'dra bar khyor kyis rtogs/ / rgyal ba'i lung bstan bdag gis thob/ / khyod kyang 'di nas sangs rgyas shing / / bde ba can du 'gro bar 'gyur/ /
This is taught as the supreme path of mind. “You have realization similar to mine. I have received the prophecy of the Victor. You as well will go from this life to the buddha realm of Sukhāvatī.
rtsod ldan gdul dka'i sems can la/ / skyo ba ma byed byang sems sgoms/ / bde mchog rang byon dkyil 'khor gyi/ / sa ru (483) gdul bya khri phrag 'byung / /
“Don’t be discouraged in this age of conflict by obstinate beings—meditate on awakening mind. In the land of Cakrasaṃvara’s self-appearing mandala, tens of thousands of disciples will appear.” {483}
zhes lung bstan to/ /
That was the prediction that Khyungpo Naljor received.

de nas bod yul du byon nas 'gro don thog gcig mdzad gu lang gi gser kha brdol ba thug nas gser mang po phyag tu 'byor ba bsnams nas slar yang bal po dang rgya gar du gshegs te rdo rje gdan pa dang / /rgyal ba mai tri pa dang / d+ha byang chub sems dpa'/ /rje btsun rin chen lha mo/ su ma ti kI rti/ bal po pham mthing ba chen po sogs mkhas shing dngos grub brnyes pa du ma las sngar ma gsan pa'i zab chos dang myur mdzad ye shes mgon po'i skor sogs gdams ngag dpag tu med pa gsan/

He returned to Tibet and did some work for the welfare of migrators. Then he discovered that the gold mine of Gulang was overproducing, so he carried off a lot of gold and went back to Nepal and India. He received many profound teachings there that he had not heard before from Vajrāsana, the Victor Maitrīpa, Dha Bodhisattva, Exalted Ratnadevī, Sumatikīrti, and the Newar Pamtingpa the Great and many other learned and accomplished masters. He received the cycle of the Awareness Protector and innumerable other instructions.

de dag gis thugs ma tshims par gser srang lnga brgya khyer nas rgya gar shar nub lho byang kun tu rgyu zhing / /grub thob kyi bla ma sangs rgyas dngos mjal ba su yod dris pas/ /paN+Di ta dang grub thob rnams mthun par/ /na ro paN+Di ta yi lcam mo ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro ni gu ma zhes bya ba dag pa'i sa gsum la gnas pa rdo rje 'chang chen po la dngos su chos zhu nus pa gcig yod zer bas/ /de gnas gang na bzhugs byas pas/ /

Still not satisfied, Khyungpo Naljor took five hundred pieces of gold and traveled all over India—east, west, south, and north—inquiring after an accomplished guru who had actually met the Buddha face to face. All the paṇḍitas and adepts agreed that there was one awareness ḍākinī known as Niguma, the sister of Nāro Paṇḍita, who had reached the three pure levels [on the bodhisattva path] and who could hear teachings directly from Great Vajradhara. But when he asked where she was, they said:

snang ba dag na gar yang zhal mthong / /snang ba ma dag na gar yang btsal bas mi rnyed de dag pa'i sa la gnas pa dang / /'ja' lus su gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / 'on kyang dur khrod chen po so sa gling gi nags gseb na/ DA ki ma'i tshogs 'khor gyi dpon la res 'ga' 'byon zer bas/

“If your perception is pure, you can see her anywhere. But if your perception is not pure, you can search everywhere and not find her, because she dwells on the pure stages and has transformed to a rainbow body. Nonetheless, she occasionally shows up in the great charnel ground of Sosadvīpa to preside over the ḍākinīs’ communal feasts.”

DA ki ma'i mtshan thos pa tsam gyis mchi ma 'khrug cing ba spu ldang ba'i mos gus skyes nas/ /dus der dur khrod so sa gling gi nags gseb nas yar la/ na mo bud+d+ha'i gsol ba 'debs kyin phyin pa dang / shing tA la bdun srid tsam gyi nam mkha' la mkha' 'gro ma sku mdog smug nag tu yod pa/ / rus pas brgyan pa phyag na kha twAM ga dang thod pa bsnams pa gcig dang du ma la sogs pa'i gzugs sna tshogs ston cing / /gar bsgyur ba mthong nas 'di DA ki ni gu ma (484) yin par 'dug snyams nas phyag 'tshal/ /bskor ba du ma byas nas/ / yang dag pa'i gdams pa zhu 'tshal byas pas/

As soon as Khyungpo Naljor heard the Ḍākinī’s name, he felt such devotion that tears welled up and his hairs stood on end. Right then and there he set out for the forests of Sosadvīpa Charnel Ground, reciting the namo buddha prayer as he went. When he arrived, he saw a brown-skinned ḍākinī in the sky at a height of about seven palmyra trees.[23] She was adorned with bones and held a khaṭvāṅga staff and skull in her hands. She was dancing and displaying multiple images, sometimes singly and sometimes as multiple figures. Khyungpo thought, “This surely is Ḍākinī Niguma.” {484} He did many prostrations and circumambulations and then requested authentic instructions.
nga sha za'i DA ki ma yin/ nga'i 'khor rnams byung na zar 'ong bas myur bar bros shig gsungs so/ /
She said, “I am a flesh-eating ḍākinī. When my entourage arrives, you’ll be devoured. Now run along quickly!”
de nas yang phyag dang bskor ba byas nas gsang sngags kyi gdams pa zhu byas pas/ /
Then again he made prostrations and circumambulations and requested the instructions of Secret Mantra.
theg pa chen po gsang sngags zhu ba la gser dgos pa yin/ /gser yod na bya yi gsungs nas/ /
Niguma said, “To receive the Mahayana Secret Mantra requires gold. If there’s gold, I can do it.”
gser srang lnga brgya phul ba dang / /nags gseb tu gtor ro/ /der 'dir nges par sha za'i mkha' 'gro ma yin nam gser la yang phongs pa mi 'dug snyams pa dang / /
Khyungpo Naljor offered her five hundred gold pieces, but she threw them about the forest. He thought, “Well maybe this is indeed a flesh-eating ḍākinī, as she does not value gold.”

mkha' 'gro ma des spyan nam mkha' la hrig hrig gzigs pa dang / /'khor DA ki ma dpag tu med pa nam mkha' las byung ste/ / 'ga' zhig gis gzhal yas khang sum rim skad cig la bzhengs/ / 'ga' zhig gis rdul tshon gyi dkyil 'khor bzhengs/ / 'ga' zhig gis tshogs kyi yo byad bsags nas/ / tshes bco lnga'i nam srod la sgyu lus rmi lam gyi dbang bskur mdzad nas dbang thon pa dang

When that ḍākinī glanced up into space, her entourage of innumerable ḍākinīs arrived in the sky. Some of them instantly constructed a three-storied celestial palace, some of them made the colored-sand mandala, and some of them collected provisions for a communal feast. That evening of the full moon, the empowerments of Illusory Body and Dream were conferred and Khyungpo received them.

bod kyi ban chung yar 'dongs dang gsungs nas/ / dpag tshad gsum DA ki ma'i rdzu 'phrul la brten nas yud tsam gyis bgrod pa dang / / gser gyi ri mi che ba tsam gcig gi steng gi nam mkha' la/ DA ki ma'i tshogs kyis bskor nas gar bsgyur zhing 'dug go / ri de'i phyogs bzhi nas mar gser gyi chu rgyun bzhi 'bab cing 'dug nas/ gser gyi ri 'di lta bu rgya gar na yod dam/ mkha' 'gro mas sprul pa yin zhus pas 'di gsungs so/

Then she said, “Little Tibetan monk, rise!” Through her miraculous powers, Khyungpo Naljor was transported instantly for three fathoms. He saw a small golden mountain and ḍākinīs in the sky above it who were holding the communal feast and performing the dances. Four rivers of gold flowed down the four sides of the mountain. Khyungpo Naljor asked, “Is this golden mountain in India or is it emanated by the ḍākinīs?” Niguma replied with this:
'khor ba'i rgya mtshor bsgyur ba yi/ / chags sdang rtog pa sna tshogs 'di/ / rang bzhin med par rtogs tsam na/ / thams cad gser gling yin no bu/ /
The variety of desirous and hateful thoughts that strand us in the ocean of cyclic existence, once realized to be without intrinsic nature, makes everything a golden land, my child.
sgyu ma lta bu'i chos rnams la/ / sgyu ma lta bur bsgom byas na/ / sgyu ma lta bur mngon sangs rgya/ / mos gus stobs las 'byung bar (485) 'gyur/ /
If you meditate on the illusion-like nature of all illusion-like phenomena, illusion-like manifest buddhahood will arise through the power of devotion. {485}

ces gsungs nas rgyud sde lnga'i dbang dang rgyud sgrub thabs gdams ngag dpag tu med pa dang / / khyad par chos drug gi khrid rmi lam du lan gcig / dngos su lan gsum gnang nas brgyud pa bdun gyi bar du chig brgyud kyi rgyas btab/ / de nas kyang rim par byin gyi rlob cing lung bstan par zhal gyis bzhes so/ /

After saying that, she granted the empowerment of the Five Tantra Classes and countless tantras, sādhanas, and instructions. In particular, she gave him the guidance on the Six Dharmas one time in a dream and three times in actuality, and then sealed it as a single one-to-one lineage for seven generations. Then she promised that she would bless and grant prophecy to that succession.

de nas slar yang gser srang lnga brgya khyer nas rgya gar nub phyogs su phyin te/ / sangs rgyas dngos dang mjal ba'i bla ma su yod dris pas/ / paN+Di ta rol pa'i rdo rje dang / Ar+Ya de wa dang / DA ki ma su ma ti la sogs pa grub thob bcu gsum gyi zhal nas/ / nged rnams kyis dbang bskur la gdams ngag bstan nas de'i rjes la lung ston bar 'gyur ro gsungs bas/ / gser srang lnga brgya phul nas dbang dang gdams pa mang po zhus so/ /

Once again Khyungpo Naljor took five hundred gold pieces and traveled to the western part of India, asking, “Who is a guru who has met the Buddha in person?” Thirteen adepts, such as Paṇḍita Lalitavajra, Āryadeva, and Ḍākinī Sumati, said, “We will confer empowerment and teach the instructions, and after that we’ll tell you the prophecy.” So he gave them five hundred gold pieces and received many empowerments and instructions.

long rnams kyi zhal nas reng bcu po 'di yi rtsa ba'i bla ma yin/ khyad par du paN+Di ta Ar+Ya de ba la bdag med ma'i nang khrid bstan pas zla ba bdun la sa brgyad kyi rtogs pa la 'god pa'i ye shes kyi DA ki ma su kha sid+d+hi zhes bya ba/ / rdo rje 'chang dang bdag med ma las dngos su chos gsan pa gcig yod kyi/ / des khyod la byin gyis rlobs cing gdams pa ston par 'gyur ro zhes lung bstan to/ /

Then they said, “For we thirteen, the root guru is Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness Sukhasiddhi. In particular, she taught Paṇḍita Āryadeva [the Brahmin] the Inner Guidance of Nairātmya.[24] After seven months he gained the realization of the eighth stage. She is the one who has heard the dharma directly from Vajradhara and Nairātmya. She will grant you blessings and instructions.”
de gang du bzhugs zhus pas/ DA ki ma de snang ba dag na gar yang zhal mthong la/ / snang ba ma dag na btsal pas mi rnyed de/ /
Khyungpo asked where she lived, and they replied, “If your perception is pure, you can see that ḍākinī anywhere. But if your perception is not pure, you can search everywhere and not find her.

res 'ga' ni bde ba sbyin pa'i gnas tsan+dan sman gyi nags tshal zhes bya bar tshes bcu'i dus su DA ki ma rnams kyi tshogs dpon mdzad cing chos ston pa dang / / yang na gsung gi sgo nas chos ston par 'gyur ro/ / der song la gsol ba thob cig / dbang bzhi rdzogs su bskur nas gdams ngag dang rjes su bstan pa mtha' dag ston par 'gyur ro/ / zhes gsungs pas

Sometimes, she goes to the bliss-giving sacred site called the Sandalwood Medicinal Forest on the tenth day of the lunar month and presides over the ḍākinīs’ communal feast and teaches the dharma. Or else she just teaches the dharma by speaking. Go there and entreat her to confer the complete four empowerments along with instructions and all the follow-up teachings.” {486}

gser srang lnga brgya po de khyer nas/ bde ba (486) sbyin pa'i nags gseb nas yar la na mo bud+d+ha ya'i gsol ba 'debs shing phyin pa na/ tsan+dan gyi nags de'i steng gi nam mkha' la DA ki ma sku mdog dkar mo dbu skra sil bus sku rgyab non pa/ / phyag gnyis skye med mtshon pa'i phyag rgya mdzad pa/ DA ki ma'i tshogs kyis bskor nas 'ja' 'od 'khyil pa'i dbus na bzhugs pa mthong ngo / / de mthong ba dang lus la ba spu ldang zhing mchi ma 'khrugs la/ sa dang po lta bu'i dga' ba skyes nas zag med kyi bde ba'i nyams dang ldan par gyur to/ / de nas me tog ut+pa la dang / pad+ma dang / ku mu ta la sogs pa mang po gtor nas phyag dang bskor ba brgya stong du ma byas te gdams ngag zhu 'tshal byas pas/ DA ki ma'i zhal nas 'di gsungs so/ /

He took another five hundred gold pieces and went to the bliss-giving medicinal forest praying with the namo buddhaya supplication along the way. When he arrived, he saw in the sky above the sandalwood forest a white ḍākinī with hair falling down her back, making the mudra that indicates the unborn with her two hands. She was sitting in the midst of rainbow light, surrounded by a host of ḍākinīs. When he saw her, the hairs on his body stood up, tears welled forth, and he had an experience of undissipating bliss like the ecstasy that arises on the first level. He tossed flowers such as utpala, lotus, and kumuta. He did many hundreds of thousands of prostrations and circumambulations and requested instructions. The Ḍākinī said this in response:
bir wa pa dang bdag med ma/ / rdo rje 'chang las dngos su thos/ / gsang sngags mngon sum lam pa yi/ / smin par byed pa'i dbang bzhi dang / / grol ba'i bskyed rdzogs ston pa la/ /
Virūpa and Nairātmya heard this directly from Vajradhara. The real path of Secret Mantra is the four ripening empowerments and the liberating creation and completion.
dkon pa'i rin chen gser phye phul/ / gus pa'i thal sbyor rkyang phyag 'tshol/ / dma' ba'i zhabs mthil gtsug gis longs/ /
