dus 'dir bdag gis grol bar bya/ / de ring rnyed pa mchog rnyed do/ /
At this time I will liberate you; today you’ll discover the best discovery.
rigs kyi bu khyod e ma ho/ / rigs kyi bu khyod e ma ho/ / rigs kyi bu khyod e ma ho/ /
You, son of good family—emaho! You, son of good family—emaho! You, son of good family—emaho!
khyod kyi slob ma yang slob dang / / phyi rabs brgyud 'dzin thams cad la/ / nga yis dngos su byin gyis rlobs/ / dag pa mkha' spyod gnas su 'gro/ / zhes gsungs nas/
I will truly bless your disciples, the disciples of your disciples, and all future generations of lineage holders. They will all go to the pure celestial realm.
dang po sprul pa'i dkyil 'khor du dbang bzhi rdzogs su bskur nas gsang sgrub lte ba sprul 'khor gyi bskyed rdzogs nyams len gyi gnad dang bcas pa thams cad ma lus par gsungs so/ /

First she conferred the complete four empowerments in an emanated mandala. Then she taught him the creation and completion phases of the Secret Sādhana of the Navel Emanation Chakra with all the vital points of practice, leaving nothing out. Khyungpo Naljor said of her:

de la ye shes kyi DA ki ma su kha sid+d+hi 'di dang po drin che ste/ sprul pa'i dkyil 'khor du dbang bzhi rdzogs su bskur/ bar du drin che ste lha'i bu mo dang dbyer med (487) du gsang yum mdzad/ tha mar drin che ste gdams ngag thams cad rdzogs par gnang nas/ bdag nyid bde ba can du bcu bzhi'i sa thob par lung bstan/ slob ma yang slob brgyud 'dzin dang bcas pa thams cad thugs rjes bzung nas/ dag pa bde stong gi mkha' spyod du 'gro bar lung bstan par mdzad do/ /

The first kindness of this Awareness Ḍākinī Sukhasiddhi was to confer the complete four empowerments in the emanated mandala. The middle kindness was to be my secret consort appearing as a daughter of the gods. {487} The final kindness was to fully grant all the instructions. Then she prophesied that I would attain the fourteenth stage while in Sukhāvatī. She also foretold that she would hold my disciples and all the lineage holders with her compassion and that they too would go to the pure celestial realm of bliss and emptiness.
des na bdag gi brgyud 'dzin thams cad kyang kun las khyad par 'phags pas na/ bsags pa yang rab 'ba' zhig 'byung bar 'gyur ro/ / zhes pa'ang gsungs so/ /
Therefore, all my lineage holders will be the most outstanding and exclusively those with excellent accumulations of merit and wisdom.

de nas kun tu bzang mo sogs mkha' 'gro'i dbang phyug rnams dang / / bde ba'i rdo rje/ / rol pa'i rdo rje/ / a ta ya badzra sogs mkhas grub rnal 'byor gyi dbang phyug mtha' yas pa rnams las rgyud dang gdams ngag gi spros pa bcad cing gser gyi me tog gis mnyes par mdzad/ / rdo rje gdan du dus mchod chen po mdzad pa'i tshe ngo mtshar gyi ltas rgya chen po byung bas 'phags yul ba mchog dman mtha' dag mgrin gcig tu bsngags pa brjod/ /

Khyungpo Naljor went on to receive countless tantras and instructions from mighty ḍākinīs such as Samantabhadrī and learned and accomplished yogis such as Sukhavajra, Lalitavajra, and Atayavajra. He resolved his misgivings and pleased them with golden flowers. When making great offerings during the holy-day ritual at the Vajra Seat, there were incredible omens. The Indians, both high and low, all praised him with a single voice.

bod yul du sangs rgyas snang ba mtha' yas kyi rnam 'phrul dge ba'i bshes gnyen glang ri thang pa las bsnyen rdzogs mdzad nas 'phan yul 'jog po rir thugs dam la bzhugs pa'i skabs/ / 'chi med grub pa rA hu la gup+ta rdzu 'phrul gyis pheb ste gdams ngag mtha' yas pa gnang ba las/ / phran tshegs nyer mkho'i man ngag rnam pa brgyad dgos pa'i dbang gis phyis tshogs gral zhig la mgur du bzhengs pa ni/

Upon returning to Tibet, he received full ordination from Geshe Langri Tangpa, a magical emanation of Amitābha. Then while he was doing his practice in retreat at Jokpori in Penyul, the adept of immortality Rāhulagupta arrived miraculously and granted him boundless instructions. From those instructions, [Khyungpo Naljor] composed this song of eight esoteric instructions for minor requisites while participating in the subsequent communal feast:[25]
gzung 'dzin gyi rnam rtog 'di tho co che/ / thim pa rnam gsum gyi gdams pa bdog / gzung 'dzin gyi g.yul ngo de nas bzlog / khyed gzung 'dzin kun ji ltar dgyes dgyes mdzod/ /
This dualistic conceptual thought is ridiculous. I hold instructions on the three dissolutions[26] that will repel the attack of dualism. Now, dualistic concepts, do what you will!
lha chen dpe dkar 'di tho co che/ / thi gu rnam gsum gyi gdams ba bdog / lha chen gyi g.yul ngo de nas bzlog / khyed lha chen kun ji ltar dgyes (488) dgyes mdzod/ /
This great god Pekar is ridiculous. I hold instructions on the three strings that will repel attacks of big gods. Now, all you big gods, do what you will! {488}
klu bdud nag po 'di tho co che/ / thod pa kha sbyor gyi gdams pa bdog / klu bdud gyi g.yul ngo de nas bzlog / khyed klu bdud kun ji ltar dgyes dgyes mdzod/ /
This dark nāga devil is ridiculous. I hold instructions on the joined skulls that will repel attacks of nāga devils. Now, all you nāga devils, do what you will!
mtshan mo'i 'byung po 'di tho co che/ / bdud rtsi thig le'i gdams pa bdog / 'byung po'i g.yul ngo de nas bzlog / khyed 'byung po kun ji ltar dgyes dgyes mdzod/ /
This bhūta spirit of the night is ridiculous. I hold instructions on the vital drops of elixir that will repel attacks of bad spirits. Now, all you spirits, do what you will!
byad stems nag po 'di tho co che/ / rdo leb nag po'i gdams pa bdog / byad stems kyi g.yul ngo de nas bzlog / khyed byad stems kun ji ltar dgyes dgyes mdzod/ /
This evil imprecator is ridiculous. I hold instructions on using black slabs that will repel attacks of imprecators. Now, all you imprecators, do what you will!
'chi bdag nag po 'di tho co che/ / keng rus tar yi gdams pa bdog / 'chi bdag gi g.yul ngo de nas bzlog / khyed 'chi bdag kun ji ltar dgyes dgyes mdzod/ /
This dark death lord is ridiculous. I hold instructions on skeleton sights that will repel attacks of death lords. Now, all you death lords, do what you will!
gza' bdud nag po 'di tho co che/ / rus sbal 'khor lo'i gdams pa bdog / gza' bdud kyi g.yul ngo de nas bzlog / khyed khyab 'jug kun ji ltar dgyes dgyes mdzod/ /
This dark planet devil is ridiculous. I hold instructions on the tortoise shell that will repel attacks of planetary devils. Now, all you rāhula planets, do what you will!
sngar ngag la byin gyis ma brlabs pas/ / sngags bzlas pa rnams la nus ma byung / / dpal A li kA li'i gdams pa bdog / sngags mi 'grub snyams pa'i dogs pa med/ / ces so/ /
Previously your speech was not blessed, so your mantra recitation was ineffective. I hold instructions on glorious ālikāli— don’t worry about not accomplishing mantras.[27]

de nas dpon slob sum stong gis shangs su byon te zhang zhong gis sna drangs pa'i dgon gnas brgya dang rtsa brgyad lo gsum gyi nang du btab/ / chos kyi 'khor lo chen po bskor ba la dbus btsang khams gsum gyi grwa pa khri tsho lnga 'dus pa'i dus su phal cher g.yeng ba shas che bas nyan bshad dang sgom sgrub la g.yel ba'i dus su/ / thams cad ltad mo la khrid nas sum cu rtsa gsum lha dang lha mo mang po'i rtsed 'jo sgrul nas bstan pas dga' zhing chags/ / yang gshin rje'i skyes bu 'jigs su rung ba du mas gsod gcod kyi las byed par sprul pas sngangs skrag brgyal bar gyur pa'i tshe ngo sprod kyi mgur du bzhengs pa ni/ /

Then Khyungpo Naljor with his entourage of three thousand went to Shang and within three years established one hundred and eight monasteries, headed by Zhangzhong. When he turned the great wheel of the dharma, fifty thousand monks came together from U, Tsang, and Kham. But most of them were distracted and careless in study and meditation practice, so Khyungpo Naljor took them sightseeing. He manifested many enticing gods and goddesses of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three, and the monks became delighted and desirous. Again he emanated many frightening death-lord minions whose job is to kill and maim, and the disciples became terrified and fainted. At that time, he sang this song to introduce [mind’s nature]: {489}

chags sdang yul rnams thams (489) cad kyang / / rang gi sems las byung ba ste/ / rnal 'byor pa yi snang ba la/ / sha za la sogs gshin rje'i gzugs/ / mtshon cha sna tshogs lag na thogs/ / tshe srog dus 'dir sdud byed kyang / / sgyu mar shes pas grol bar 'gyur/ /

All objects of desire and hatred come from your own mind. To the yogin, these appearances of death-lord forms, like flesh-eaters, carrying various weapons in their hands to reap our life force right now, are liberating if known as illusions.
lha mo mdzes ma rgyan gyis brgyan/ / glu len snyan pa'i sgra sgrog cing / / yid 'ong mang pos mtha' bskor yang / / rang snang sgyu mar thag chod na/ / de dag gis kyang 'ching mi nus/ /

Even when surrounded by captivating beautiful goddesses adorned with jewels, singing songs with sweet melodies, if you are certain they are self-appearing illusions, they have no power to ensnare you.
ces pa la sogs pa'i chos dang / bar do'i chos bstan pas thams cad nyan bshad dang / sgom sgrub la brtson par gyur to/ /
He gave this and other teachings, including teachings on the intermediate state. After that, everyone applied themselves diligently to study and meditation.

lan gcig rong po dge bshes dkon mchog rgyal kyis 'bul ba chen po phul nas khyed rgya gar du lan gsum byon/ rtsa ba'i bla ma rnam bzhi sogs mkhas grub brgya dang lnga bcu brten nas grub thob tu gyur nas snang ba rang bzhin med par rtogs pa yin zer bas/ brag 'di la phar thal tshur thal 'ga' re gyis la/ nam mkha' la skyil krung gyis la 'dug dang zer pa la/ brag ri de la zang thal du phyin/ nam mkha' la skyil krung bcas nas gcig dang du mar snang ba la sogs pa'i rdzu 'phrul 'ga' re bstan pas/ rong po dang gra ba thams cad shin tu dad de/ / de lta bu'i yon tan de gdams ngag gang bsgoms pa las byung ba yin zer ba la 'di gsungs so/ /

One time Geshe Könchok Gyal of Rong presented many offerings to Khyungpo Naljor and made the following request: “It is said that you’ve gone to India three times and relied on one hundred and fifty learned adepts, including your four root gurus. It is said you are an adept yourself and realize that appearances have no intrinsic nature. So go ahead and pass back and forth through this cliff and sit in vajra position in space.” At that, Khyungpo passed through the mountain cliff, sat in vajra posture in space, assumed single and multiple forms, and displayed some other miraculous feats. Rongpo and all the monks were moved to faith. They asked, “What meditation instruction produces such qualities?” He said this in response:

chos rnams sgyu ma lta bu la/ / sgyu ma lta bur nyams blangs pas/ / sgyu ma lta bur mngon sangs rgyas/ / snang yang bden med chos rnams la/ / byis pas bden par bzung bas 'khrul/ / med bzhin snang ba e ma ho/ /

Experience the illusion-like nature of all illusion-like phenomena to manifest illusion-like buddhahood. Phenomena appear but are unreal. The childish view them as real, causing delusion. Appearing while nonexistent—emaho!
la sogs pa'i chos bshad pas ngang de zla ba bcu gcig na rong pos yi dam lha'i zhal mthong nas snang ba bden med du rtogs so/ /
Khyungpo Naljor gave other teachings as well, inspiring Rongpo’s faith. After eleven months he had a visionary experience of the yidam and realized that all appearance lacks true reality.

yang nye gnas rin chen rdo rjes tha mal rang rgyud bzung nas log lta cung zad re shor ba mkhyen nas yi ge (490) brgya ba dang dag byed a'i stong ra zhag bdun bsgom du bcug nas gzim chung du byung ba dang / / sku lus dgyes rdor mtshon cha can lha bcu gsum du sprul nas bstan pas der mthong / / yang gnas lngar rgyud sde lnga'i dkyil 'khor bkod pas kyang ji lta bar mthong / phyir song pas chos khri brgya rtsa brgyad du chos bstan pa mthong nas ched du brjod pa/ /

Khyungpo Naljor became aware that his attendant Rinchen Dorje had slightly strayed into mistaken views by holding to the [guru as] an ordinary subjective being. He sent him off to meditate on the hundred syllables and Purifying A of Inner Space for seven days. When next he showed up in Khyungpo’s room, Rinchen Dorje saw that he had emanated his body as the Thirteen-Deity Hevajra With Weapons. He also saw precisely the Five Tantras’ deities arrayed in Khyungpo’s five places. When he went outside, he saw Khyungpo Naljor teaching the dharma on one hundred and eight dharma thrones, and made this special verse (udāna):
sku lus sprul pa'i lha dgu la/ / gnas lngar rgyud sde lnga yi lha/ / brgya rtsa brgyad kyi chos khri la/ / blta bas mi ngoms sku lus re/ /
Your awakened body emanated as nine deities, the Five Tantras’ deities in your five places, one hundred and eight dharma thrones, your body on each—I can never look enough!
mtha' bral theg chen chos sgra sgrog / sna tshogs sprul pa phyogs bcur ston/ / rgyal ba rgya mtsho'i thugs sprul pa'i/ / bla ma sangs rgyas khyed la bstod/ /
You proclaim the Mahayana beyond extremes, and display various emanations in ten directions. Heart emanation of the ocean of victors— Guru Buddha, I offer you my praise.
ma rig 'khrul pa'i sems can rnams/ / yang dag lam la gzung du gsol/ / zhes khos bstod pa byas so/ /
Put sentient beings deluded by ignorance onto the authentic path; I entreat you.
de nas log lta skad cig ma skyes par/ ci gsungs nyan pa'i nye gnas su gyur to/ /
Rinchen Dorje praised him in this way. Never again did wrong view arise for even an instant, and he became a faithful attendant on Khyungpo Naljor’s every command.

skabs shig byams pa'i chos lnga dang / gsang ba spyi rgyud bshad pa'i 'tsho ba 'dren pa la/ dbus gtsang khams gsum gyi gra pa rnams ma 'chams par/ dam sel du 'gro bar byung ba dang / rgyal chen rigs bzhi'i lha tshogs rnams byung nas 'di skad zhus so/ /

On one occasion, when Khyungpo was explaining the Five Treatises of Maitreya[28] and the Secret General Tantra,[29] the monks from U, Tsang, and Kham could not agree on who would serve him food. As they were about to breach their sacred pledge, the gods of the four great kings appeared and gave this warning:
thar med gnas su skye ba dang / / thar pa'i gnas gcod byed pa ni/ / mi mthun dag las 'byung bar 'gyur/ / de phyir dam tshig smos ci dgos/ /
Birth in a land without freedom and exile from the free places come from these disagreements— what need to mention [breaching] sacred pledges.
mthun pa'i dka' thub dag la ni/ / tshe gcig sangs rgyas rnyed mi dka'/ / de phyir 'dir 'tshogs lha rnams kyis/ / chos gsung tshe na bsnyen bkur bya/ /
Those able to bear the hardship of living in harmony will gain awakening in this life without hardship. So we gods who are assembled here will serve during the dharma teaching.
ta la bdun srid gcig kyang rung / / mkha' la chos char dbab tu gsol/ / chos kyi dung chen bsgrag tu gsol/ / chos kyi ba dan bsgrer du gsol/ / ces gsol ba btab pas/
Whether seven palmyra trees high or just one, please bring the rains of dharma in the sky. Please sound the great conch of the dharma. Please raise the banner of the dharma.

zla ba bdun mi zas mi za bar dam bcas nas nam mkha' la shing ta la gcig gi tshad tsam la bzhugs te zla ba bdun gyi bar du byams pa'i chos lnga dang / gsang (491) ba spyi rgyud tshar bar byas pas/ dbu ma'i lta ba khong du chud pa mang du byung ba dang / lha rnams kyis mgrin gcig tu 'di skad ces brjod par gyur to/ / bla ma rdo rje gdan pa'i thugs dgongs rdzogs par gyur te/ lha rnams tshims par gyur to/ / mi rnams grol bar gyur to/ / sangs rgyas kyi bstan pa la bya ba chen po byas par gyur to/ / a la la zhes lan gsum brjod cing / me tog gi char chen po phab ste mi snang bar gyur to/ / lan gcig sangs rgyas 'od dpag med kyis bde chen zhing gi bkod pa rnams bstan nas 'di skad gsungs so/ /

He vowed not to eat human-prepared food for seven months, and for those seven months he taught the Five Treatises of Maitreya and the Secret General Tantra from a height of one palmyra tree. {491} Many there integrated the view of the middle way. The gods said these words with one voice: Guru Vajrāsana’s intention is fulfilled! The gods are satisfied! All humans will be liberated! Great acts for the Buddha’s doctrine are done! Alala! They said that three times and a great rain of flowers fell. Then they vanished. One time Buddha Amitābha displayed the arrays of the realm of Sukhāvatī and spoke these words:
khyod kyi skye ba tha ma ste/ / bde ba can gyi zhing khams su/ / sde dang bcas pa'i bdud btul nas/ / mngon par byang chub 'khor lo bskor/ /
This is your final rebirth. In the pure realm of Sukhāvatī you will tame devils of all kinds, gain awakening, and turn the dharma wheel.
gang gis khyod kyi rjes slob cing / / 'od dpag mtshan tsam thos pas kyang / / bde ba can gyi zhing khams su/ / rdzu 'phrul chen pos skye bar 'gyur/ /
Whoever follows after you, or just hears the name Amitābha will be born miraculously in the realm of Sukhāvatī.
khyod kyi brgyud 'dzin rnam pa gsum/ / mngon dga' dang ni bde ba can/ / dag pa'i zhing nas zhing du 'gro/ / der ni mngon par byang chub 'gyur/ /
Your [next] three lineage holders will go from pure realm to realm, Sukhāvatī and Abhirati, and gain manifest awakening there.
zhes pa la sogs pa'i lung bstan mang du mdzad do/ /
He received this and many other prophecies.
yang thugs rje chen po gtso 'khor gsum gyi 'od zer las chos kyi sgra gsan pa ni/
Then he heard these sounds of dharma from the light rays of the Great Compassionate One and the two other [bodhisattvas]:
chos rnams rang bzhin skye med las/ 'gags med snying rje ma shar na/ / 'gro drug sems can ma rgan rnams/ / smin cing grol bar mi nus pas/ /
If unrestricted compassion does not arise from the unborn innate nature of all phenomena, you won’t be able to mature and liberate your old mothers, the six kinds of beings.
'gro 'chag nyal 'dug thams cad du/ / ma yi drin dang sdug bsngal rnams/ / ma yengs dran pa'i lcags kyus zungs/ / tshad med snying rje chen po bskyed/ /
Whether walking, moving, lying down, or sitting, hold with the hook of undistracted mindfulness the kindness and sufferings of those mothers and develop immeasurable great compassion.
byams pa'i gangs ri chen po las/ / snying rje'i chu rgyun bsil ba yis/ / nyon mongs me dpung zhi bar mdzod/ / nga ni snying rje chen po'i sku/ /
The cooling rivers of compassion flow from the great snow mountain of love, extinguishing the fire of the afflictions. I am the form of great compassion.
zhes sogs snying rje mkha' khyab kyi ting nge 'dzin gsungs so/ /
This and other teachings on the meditative absorption of universal compassion were given. {492}
yang o rgyan tu (492) phebs nas rje btsun ma lha lnga'i dkyil 'khor du dbang zhus pa dang / DA ki ma seng ge'i gdong pa can la DA ki ma sde bzhis bskor nas rdo rje'i glu 'di ltar blangs so/ /
Then Khyungpo Naljor went to Oḍḍiyāna and received empowerment in the mandala of Five-Deity Ḍākinīs.[30] The ḍākinīs of the four classes surrounded Ḍākinī Siṃhamukhā and she sang this vajra song:
rdo rje mkha' 'gros bar chad srung / / rin chen mkha' 'gros mi nor spel/ / pad+ma mkha' 'gros bud med sdud/ / phrin las mkha' 'gros las kun sgrub/ /
Vajra Ḍākinī guards against obstacles, Jewel Ḍākinī increases people and wealth, Lotus Ḍākinī gathers consorts, Activity Ḍākinī accomplishes all actions.
'dod sred chags pa'i dbang song bas/ / bdag nyid mkha' 'gro'i dbang du song / / phyi rol mi 'dod gang yang 'byung / / DA ki rang gi sems su shes/ /
Once under the influence of craving and clinging one has fallen under the power of the ḍākinīs. Any unwanted external event can occur; recognize the ḍākinī as your own mind.
sems kyi de nyid shes pa dang / / sems nyid mi rtog rdo rje ste/ / rdo rje DA kis bar chad srung / / chog shes dgos med rin chen gter/ / rin chen mkha' 'gros dgos 'dod sgrub/ /
chags bral mi rtog pad+ma ste/ / pad+ma DA kis mu tra sdud/ / skye 'gags med pa karma ste/ / las kyi DA kis phrin las sgrub/ /
de ltar ma shes rnal 'byor pas/ / bskal bar bsgrub kyang 'grub mi 'gyur/ / de phyir mkha' 'gro rang sems su/ / shes pa gnad kyi mchog yin no/ /
A yogin who does not recognize that will practice for ages without success. Therefore, know ḍākinīs as your own mind; that is the sublime vital point.
zhes pa la sogs 'char pa rnam pa gsum dang / 'du ba rnam gsum gyi gdams ngag rnams gsungs so/ /
They taught this and other instructions on the three arisings and the three gatherings.[31]

de nas bla ma lha dang mkha' 'gro rnams kyis lung bstan pa ltar tshogs pa'i mthar thug khri tsho brgyad la lo du mar chos bstan/ slob ma'i mthar thug drug po la gdams ngag ma lus pa tshar/ sku tshe'i mthar thug brgya dang lnga bcu la babs nas/ zhing khams mthar thug bde ba can tu gshegs par dgongs pa'i tshe rgyal chen bzhi dang klu rgyal ma dros pa/ / dri za'i rgyal po zur phud lnga pa sogs lha klu mi min dpag tu med pa 'dus/ mchod sprin bsam gyis mi khyab pas mchod cing mya ngan las mi 'da' bar gsol ba btab pa la bka' stsal pa ni/ /

Then, in accordance with the predictions of his gurus, deities, and ḍākinīs, Khyungpo Naljor taught dharma for many years to the ultimate assembly of eighty thousand people. He finished every instruction to his six ultimate disciples. He reached the ultimate age of one hundred and fifty years. He intended to depart for the ultimate pure realm of Sukhāvatī. But the four great kings and the nāga king Anavapta, the gandharvan king Pañcaśikha, and innumerable gods, nāgas, and nonhumans presented unimaginable clouds of offerings and begged him not to enter nirvana. He responded with this and other teachings that satisfied them:
bla ma yi dam lung bstan pa'i/ / mthar thug gsum gyi dus la babs/ / da ni zhing khams mthar thug pa'i/ / (493) bde ba can gyi zhing du 'gro/ /
Now the three ultimates are fulfilled that my gurus and yidams had foretold. I will go to the realm of Sukhāvatī, the ultimate pure realm. {493}
dag pa'i longs spyod dpag tu med/ / 'jig rten gser dngul dgos pa med/ / khyed rnams nga la dad gyur na/ / bde ba can du gsol ba thob/ / zhing der skye bar the tshom med/ /
With limitless pure enjoyment, who needs worldly gold and silver? If you have faith in me, pray to be born in Sukhāvatī and you will doubtless be born in that realm.

rdul gcig steng na rdul snyed zhing / / bsam gyis mi khyab rdzogs par snang / / zhing dag ston pa 'khor dang chos/ / dpag tu med pa 'od dpag zhing / / rnam par dag pa bde ba can/ / de phyir the tshom ma byed par/ / zhing der skye ba'i smon lam thob/ /

On a single atom there appear as many pure realms as atoms in the universe, unimaginably perfect. Realms, teachers, retinues, and dharma are infinite in Amitābha’s realm, the totally pure realm Sukhāvatī. Therefore have no doubt and pray to be born there.
zhes pa la sogs pa'i chos bshad nas tshim par mdzad do/ /
de nas tshes bcu bzhi la tshogs su pheb ste nam mkha' la sku lus kyi bkod pa mang po bstan te 'di skad gsungs so/ /
Then Khyungpo Naljor attended the assembly on the fourteenth day of the lunar month and displayed many bodily forms in the sky and said these words:
kye ma 'dus byas mi rtag ste/ / nam mkha'i sprin bzhin 'dus shing gyes/ / bden med sgyu ma'i chos rnams la/ / bden par bzung bas bslus pa yin/ /
Alas! All composite things are impermanent. They gather and disperse like clouds in the sky. To take unreal illusory phenomena as real is to be deceived.
nga yi lus ni rgyal ba'i sku/ / skye 'chi can du ma lta zhig / nga yi ngag ni rgyal ba'i gsung / / brjod bral skye med rang sgra sgrog /
My body is the Victor’s awakened form; do not see it as subject to birth and death. My voice is the Victor’s awakened speech, the innate sound of the inexpressible unborn.
nga yi sems ni rgyal ba'i thugs/ / rtog bral mkhyen pa'i ye shes ldan/ /
My mind is the Victor’s awakened mind with timeless awareness of inconceivable knowledge.
ces gsungs pa dang / nam mkha' thams cad 'ja' dang rol mo'i sgras gang zhing me tog gi char chen po bab par gyur to/ ! /
Thus he spoke and the whole sky was filled with rainbows and the sound of music while a great rain of flowers showered down.
Mokchokpa Rinchen Tsöndru

mkhas grub khyung po rnal 'byor gyi gdams ngag yongs su rdzogs pa'i thugs sras chen po rnam pa drug gi ya gyal gcig brgyud kyi bka' babs 'dzin pa'i phyi bu gcig pu pa/ rmog lcog pa rin chen brtson 'grus zhes bya ba sku tshe de nyid brjes ma thag par shar phyogs 'od 'phro can gyi zhing khams su mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur ba skye ba gcig gis thogs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' chen po de nyid/ / tha snyad bshad pa'i chos la snying po med par gzigs nas/ / khams pa a seng dang / / bur sgom nag po sogs grub thob kyi bla ma (494) gdams ngag che tshad la gtugs shing nyams len mdzad kyang thugs dam mthar phyin pa ma byung / / re zhig gi tshe mkhas grub khyung po rnal 'byor gyis rjes su bzung ste gdams ngag rdzogs par gnang / / dang por sdings mar lo gnyis bsgoms pas sgyu lus rmi lam 'od gsal gyi rtogs pa mthar phyin pa 'khrungs/ shangs pa sku gshegs pas bla ma dwags po lha rje'i spyan sngar dge sbyor dogs gcod la byon pas skye ba du ma'i dpon slob yin gsungs nas shin tu dgyes pas gdams ngag mang po gnang / der phyag rgya chen po'i lta ba la sgro 'dogs chod/ / nyams rtogs gyi rtsal phyogs med du rgyas/ rmi lam sprul bsgyur gyi skabs su rdo rje'i mgur 'di gsungs so/ /

Khedrup Khyungpo Naljor had six main close disciples who received his perfectly complete instructions. Among them, there was only one, the last, to whom the special legacy of the one-to-one lineage fell: Mokchokpa Rinchen Tsöndru. Mokchokpa held [the status of] a great bodhisattva with a single [remaining] lifetime: right after he passed from this life he attained actual perfect enlightenment in the eastern buddha realm of Radiant Light.[32] He had seen that the conventional explanations of the dharma were hollow and that only the instructions of adept gurus such as Khampa Aseng and Burgom Nakpo hit the mark. {494} Though he took those instructions into his experience, he failed to reach consummation in his spiritual practice. But sometime later, Khedrup Khyungpo Naljor took him as a disciple and gave him all the instructions. First he meditated for two years at Dingma and experienced the culminating realizations of Illusory Body, Dream, and Lucid Clarity. Then, since Lama Shangpa had passed away, he went to see Gampopa, the physician guru of Dakpo, in order to clear up doubts in his spiritual practice. Gampopa was very pleased, telling him that they had been master and student for many lifetimes, and he granted many instructions. There Khyungpo resolved his misgivings about the view of mahāmudrā, and the energy of his experience and realization grew in every respect. During the emanation and transformation of a dream, Mokchokpa sang this vajra song:
skye med klod nas 'gags med 'phyo/ / bsam pa tsam gyis thogs pa med/ / gang gis bslur med sgyu ma'i lus/ / rnal 'byor rig pa'i klong nas shar/ / tshe 'di'i rnam rtog yal nas thal/ /

The unobstructed flow from the unborn expanse cannot be encompassed by mere thought. Illusory body, not distorted by anyone, arises from the expanse of the yogin’s awareness. Thoughts of this life fade and vanish.
rnam smin gyi lus la rgyal ba'i sku/ / ngo sprod kyi rje btsun rin po che/ / yid kyi lus la chos kyi sku/ / ngo sprod kyi rje btsun rin po che/ /
The fully ripened body is the Victor’s awakened form— the venerable precious one introduced me to it. The mental body is the dharmakāya— the venerable precious one introduced me to it.
bag chags kyi lus la rgyal ba'i sku/ / ngo sprod kyi rje btsun rin po che/ /
The habitual body is the Victor’s awakened form— the venerable precious one introduced me to it.

zhes bya ba la sogs gsungs shing de nas bzung tshe 'di'i rnam rtog skye ma myong gsungs so/ / de nas bla ma rnams kyi gsung bzhin ri dang ma bral bar byas nas yang na shi ba dang yang na sangs rgya ba gcig la gtad dgos dgongs nas rmog lcog gi brag tu gsol zas nyungs ma tsam la brten nas lo bcu gnyis su bzhugs pa'i tshe su kha sid+d+hi byon nas 'di gsungs so/ /

He said this and other things, and that henceforth he never experienced the concerns of this life. Then, following the advice of the gurus to never leave the mountains, he decided that he should focus either on death or else on awakening. So he remained in the cliffs of Mokchok for twelve years, sustained by very little food. One time, Sukhasiddhi appeared and thrice repeated:
chos nyid mngon tu ma gyur tshe/ mi zas 'tsho bas nyams myong 'grib/ / lto gos 'khri ba bcad nas kyang / / rnam rtog ting 'dzin zas su zo/ /
Until phenomena’s nature is actualized, nourishment by human food obscures experience. Sever the bonds of food and clothing and eat the food of meditative absorption.

ces lan gsum gsungs pas lto gos 'khri ba chod/ ting nge 'dzin bsam gyis mi khyab pa 'khrungs/ de rnams kyi tshe rdo rje'i mgur (495) mang du bzhengs pa las rgyal srid sna bdun rang la tshang ba'i mgur ni/

Thereupon he cut the ties to food and clothing. Unimaginable absorptions arose. {495} During the time of those events, he composed many vajra songs, such as “The Seven Royal Possessions Complete within Oneself”:[33]
las su dgra btul gnyen bskyangs kyang / / dgra la thub pa'i dus kyang med/ / gnyen la mgu ba'i dus kyang med/ / da dgra med gnyen med byed las che/ /
I acted to defeat enemies and protect friends, but at no time were the enemies defeated, and at no time were the friends satisfied. Now my main act is to live without enemies and friends.
las su lha brten 'dre bskrad kyang / lha la mgu ba'i dus kyang med/ / 'dre la 'gro ba'i dus kyang med/ / lha med 'dre med byed las che/ /
I acted to propitiate gods and exorcise demons, but at no time were the gods satisfied, and at no time did the demons leave. Now my main act is to live without gods and demons.
stong pa nyid kyi rjes 'brang yang / / stong nyid kyi lha la thug mtha' med/ /
Though I chased after emptiness, reaching the view of emptiness is endless.
gcig pu rtsa ba gcod las che/ / mi chos kyi phyogs kyi tha ma la/ / lha chos kyi phyogs su rab gcig byung / /
Now my main act is to cut the one root alone. In one who is the least of human virtues, the best of spiritual qualities has arisen.
yang dag don la mi lta bar/ / tshong du sgyu ma'i nor tshol 'khrul/ /
Without seeing the ultimate meaning, we err trying to find illusory wealth.
sems la gang phan mi lta bar/ / tha snyad tshig phyir 'brangs te 'khrul/ /
Without seeing what will benefit the mind, we err following verbal conventions.
dman pa'i cha lugs mi 'dzin par/ / che btsun gyi 'gying ra byas las che/ /
Without keeping to a lowly appearance, we act like a high and mighty lord.
phyogs med ldom bu mi byed par/ / lung stong gi grog tshang bshigs te 'khrul/ /
Without begging for alms aimlessly, we err in empty valleys, ruining anthills.
gcig pur nyams su mi len par/ / mang po'i dpon po byas las che/ / dal 'byor mi lus khebs ldan 'di/ / don med phyal par zad du 'phong / /
Without practicing alone, we act as the leader of many. This fortunate free and endowed human body could be lost in constant meaningless activity.
rang sems nor bu rin chen 'di/ / 'khor ba'i 'dam du bying du 'phong / / bla ma'i gdams ngag bdud rtsi 'di/ / g.yeng ba'i dbang du btang ste 'phong / /
This precious gem of one’s mind could be lost in the swamp of cyclic existence. This elixir of the guru’s instructions could be lost under the sway of distraction.
zung 'jug gsal ba'i sgron me 'di/ / rnam rtog rlung gis bskyod du 'phong / / spyod pa ro snyoms bde chen 'di/ / chos brgyad bdud kyis non du 'phong / /
This radiant lamp of integral unity could be lost in the gale winds of thought. This movement of equal-flavored great bliss could be quashed by the devil of eight concerns.
rang lus rgyal ba'i zhing khams 'di/ / tha mal las la bskol du 'phong / / rnal 'byor pa yi bde skyid 'di/ / tshogs drug gi snang ba grogs su shar/ /
This buddha realm of one’s own body could be lost when given ordinary work. This joy and happiness of a yogin is aided by appearances of six consciousnesses.
'khor 'das la nyam nga ma mchis pas/ / rang sems rgyal po yin no sems/ / rang sems rtogs pa'i rgyal po la/ / rin chen bdun gyi rgyan yang thogs/ / (496)
With no fear of samsara and nirvana, I think, “My own mind is king.” A sovereign who realizes their own mind also holds the seven royal ornaments. {496}
bdag tha snyad kyi tshig phyir mi 'brangs par/ / zab mo'i don la mos par byas/ / nges shes blo yi gting nas skyes/ / de blon po gros kyi phul du byung / /
I did not follow verbal conventions but preferred the profound meaning and certainty arose from deep within: that is the best advice of a minister.
bla ma dam pa'i zhal snga nas/ / gdams ngag zab mo de rang ston/ / rje nA ro pa yi bu brgyud la/ / rgyud lung sgro 'dogs chod cig gsungs/ /
In the presence of the holy guru the profound instructions were shown: “Resolve your doubts in the tantras and scriptures of Lord Nāropa’s spiritual descendants.”
man ngag che dgu btus btus nas/ / 'khor 'das kyi rtsa ba bcad lags pas/ / ma rig pa skye med du yal nas thal/ / rta mchog gis dug lnga dbyings su bskyal/ /
I gathered all the main esoteric instructions and severed the root of samsara and nirvana. Then ignorance vanished in the unborn state: the supreme horse conveyed five poisons to basic space.
lar mang po 'tshogs pa'i 'du 'dzi 'di/ / g.yeng bar 'dug pas ri khrod 'grims/ / bskyed rdzogs gnyis la gzhi byas nas/ / rang gi sems kyi rtsal yang sbyangs/ /
Still, this busyness of big groups was distracting, so I kept to mountain retreats, making creation and completion the basis and training my mind’s creative energy.
khyung phrug mkha' la gshegs dang 'dra/ / de gar 'gyur 'khor lo rin po che/ / tshogs drug gi snang ba had por thal/ / de lta'i don la chog shes pas/ /
Like a young garuḍa turning in space, wherever I go is the precious wheel. Six sense appearances suddenly blank, I knew contentment of the present moment.
longs spyod che la dga' rgyu med/ / bstod smad tshig gis snyan sdug med/ / 'chi bdag bdud kyi cho 'phrul yang / / rang snang yin pas 'jigs rgyu med/ /
With no cause for joy over many enjoyments, I am not disgraced or saddened by praise or insult. Even the apparitions of the death-lord devil are my own projections and cause no fear.
sems nyid rtag chad gnyis dang bral/ / skye shi gnyis la skrag rgyu med/ / de dmag dpon gyis log rtog choms sam sems/ /
Mind itself, free of eternalism and nihilism, leaves no cause to fear birth or death. I think, “Isn’t this the precious general who conquers erroneous ideas?”
de ltar rtogs pa'i rnal 'byor pas/ / sems nyid gdod nas dag pa la/ / snang ba slob dpon du 'char kyin gda'/ / de glang pos dmag dpung bskyod dang 'dra/ /
For the yogin who realizes this, appearances in the primordially pure mind arise and exist as the spiritual master. That’s like the elephant that moves armies.
zhe 'dod dren med ngang yal thal/ / mkha' la bya 'phur rten ma mchis/ / tshogs drug skyes na blo bur ba/ / 'dzin pa med par grogs su shar/ /
Anger and desire vanish within mindlessness. A bird flying in the sky has no support; the six consciousnesses arise momentarily. Without fixation they arise as allies,
bkag pa med par gzigs mor che/ / de btsun mo mdzes ma'i brgyan yang btags/ / de ltar rtogs pa'i rnal 'byor pas/ / khyab pa nam mkha' lta bu la/ / sems kyi khyim pa yangs dog med/ /
great sights without inhibition, fitting ornaments worn by the beautiful queen. For the yogin who realizes this, like the all-pervading sky, mind’s house has no fixed dimension.
ngos gzung med 'dra'i bar snang la/ / 'od gsal sgo la yangs dog med/ / dbyings dang ye shes dbyer med pas/ / (497) sku gsum gyi rgyun la yangs dog med/ /
Like space that cannot be identified, the door of lucid clarity has no fixed dimension. Since basic space and awareness are inseparable, {497} the continuum of three kāyas has no fixed dimension.
'bad med nyi ma lta bu la/ / nyi zer 'char ba phyogs ris med/ / de nor bus dgos 'dod re ba skong / /
Just as the sun without effort shines rays in every direction, the precious gem fulfills hopes and needs.
rin chen bdun gyi nor mchog 'di/ / rnal 'byor pa yi rgyan du che/ / lus dang bral yang 'di mi 'bral/ /
This supreme gem of the seven precious ones is the great ornament of the yogin. Though we leave the body, we don’t lose that.
nor gyi dam pa yin nam sems/ / rgyal po'i longs spyod la smon rgyu med/ / mkhas pa'i tha snyad la dga' rgyu med/ / de shob be yin na 'gum pa lags/ / zhes gsungs so/ /
I think, “Is this not the sacred gem?” I have no need for royal wealth. I take no delight in scholarly sophistry. If this is boasting, then let me die!
yang nyams myong blo blo drug gi mgur ni/
“The Song of Six Attitudes of an Experienced Mind”:
dang por sgro 'dogs chod nas kyang / / da rung skabs su the tshom byung / / blta bas kyang rnal 'byor bslu bslu 'dra/ / da spros bral gyi sems dang mi 'bral 'tshal/ /
At first I resolved my false assumptions, but sometimes doubt still came up. It’s as if even the view tricks the yogin. Now I ask only to keep a simple mind.
dang po skye med rtogs nas kyang / / da rung skabs su snyem byed byung / / bsgom pas kyang rnal 'byor bslu bslu 'dra/ / da ma yengs sems dang mi 'bral 'tshal/ /
At first I realized the unborn, but sometimes inflation still came up. It’s as if even meditation tricks the yogin. Now I ask only to keep an undistracted mind.
dang po 'dzin med du byas nas kyang / / da rung skabs su chags zhen byung / / spyod pas kyang rnal 'byor bslu bslu 'dra/ / da 'dzin med kyi sems dang mi 'bral 'tshal/ /
At first I acted without fixation, but sometimes attachment still came up. It’s as if even the conduct tricks the yogin. Now I ask only to keep an unfixated mind.
dang por rtse gcig tu gnas nas kyang / / da rung skabs su re dogs byung / / 'bras bus kyang rnal 'byor bslu bslu 'dra/ / da lhun grub kyi sems dang mi 'bral 'tshal/ /
At first I rested with one-pointed mind, but sometimes hopes and fears still came up. It’s as if even the fruition tricks the yogin. Now I ask only to keep a spontaneous mind.
dang por thod rgal byung nas kyang / / da rung skabs su nyam nga byung / / chos brgyad kyis rnal 'byor bslu bslu 'dra/ / da smyon pa'i sems dang mi 'bral 'tshal/ /
At first I made surpassing progress, but sometimes anxiety still came up. It’s as if even the eight concerns trick the yogin. Now I ask only to keep a crazy mind.
dang por gnyen 'dun spangs nas kyang / / da rung skabs su ngo srung byung / / da yang ngo srung mi bgyid 'tshal/ /
At first I renounced loving relatives, but sometimes face-saving still came up. [line missing] Now I ask only to keep from saving face.
dang por dad pa skyes nas kyang / / da rung skabs su btang snyoms byung / / le los kyang rnal 'byor bslu bslu 'dra/ / da brtson 'grus dang rnal 'byor mi 'bral 'tshal/ /
At first faith was born, but sometimes complacency still came up. It’s as if laziness tricks the yogin. Now I ask only to keep diligent and yogic.
lha gcig dkon mchog gsum po la/ / dad gus kyi skyong la mi bgyid 'tshal/ / (498) pha gcig bla ma dam pa la/ / mos gus rgyun chad med par 'tshal/ /
May I not grow weary of faith and devotion to the one deity, the Three Jewels. May my devotion be uninterrupted to the one parent, the holy guru. {498}
gdams ngag thugs kyi nying khu la/ / tshig tshogs kyi lhad kyis ma bslad 'tshal/ / lar mkhas pa bas kyang bsgrub pa gces/ / gcig pur sdod la nyams su longs/ /
May I not corrupt with extraneous words the essence of the heart’s instructions. Again, practice is more dear than scholarship. I will stay by myself and keep practicing.
[“Eight Hardships”:][34]
'khor ba'i skyon gyis sun phyung la/ / chos mya ngan 'das la mos pa dka'/ / rgyu 'bras chos la yid ches nas/ / skyo ngal med pa'i dad pa dka'/ /
It’s hard to tire of the faults of cyclic existence and be devoted to transcendent dharma. It’s hard to believe in the dharma of cause and effect and then to have faith without sorrow.
na ba tsha ba kun spangs nas/ / bkol du gtub pa'i mi lus dka'/ / lung rig man ngag dang ldan pa'i/ / thugs rje can gyi bla ma dka'/ /
It’s hard to reject all sickness and pain and then put this human body to use. It’s hard to find a compassionate guru who has scripture, reason, and esoteric instruction.
'du 'dzi g.yeng ba kun spangs nas/ / nyams su len pa'i slob ma dka'/ / chags sdang zhe sdang kun spangs nas/ / gazhan don byed pa'i snying rje dka'/ /
It’s hard to find a disciple who rejects distractions and then cultivates meditative experience. It’s hard to abandon all attachment and aversion and then compassionately work for others’ welfare.
gzung 'dzin rnam rtog dang bral ba'i/ / rtse gcig gnas pa'i bsam gtan dka'/ / dka' ba rnam brgyad gdams ngag 'di/ / chos byed rnams la 'di tsho gces/ /
It’s hard to meditate single-pointedly, free of dualistic conceptual thinking. This instruction on the eight hardships is valuable to all who practice dharma.
'di tsho 'dzom pa brgya la 'ga'/ / de phyir byang chub thob pa dka'/ /
Only a few out of a hundred get them all; that’s why attaining awakening is so hard.
[“Eight Great Ornaments”:]
da sgro 'dogs sems la chod pa la/ / mtha' bral gyi lta ba mi zer ram/ / de lung rig dang 'brel ba rgyan du che/ /
Don’t they say that the view free of extremes is to sever assumptions in the mind? Adding scripture and reason to that is a great ornament.
rnam rtog chos skur shar ba la/ / rang byung bsgom pa mi zer ram/ / de nyams myong dang 'brel ba gnad du che/ /
Don’t they say that naturally occurring meditation is conceptual thought arising as dharmakāya? Adding experience to that is a great vital point.
tshogs drug rang sar grol ba la/ / chags med kyi spyod pa mi zer ram/ / dus tshod dang 'brel pa rgyan du che/ /
Don’t they say that conduct without attachment is the six consciousnesses free in their own ground? Adding a timely element is a great ornament.
stong nyid kyi nyams myong dang 'brel ba la/ / snyan brgyud kyi gdams ngag mi zer ram/ / de dbang dang 'brel ba rgyan du che/ /
Don’t they say that the instruction of the aural lineage is to connect with the experience of emptiness? Adding empowerment to that is a great ornament.
stong nyid kyi gsal snang skye ba la/ / sa lam gyi rim pa mi zer ram/ / de la ma rtags dang 'brel ba rgyan du che/ /
Don’t they say that the sequence of levels and paths is the arising of clear appearances of emptiness? Adding the path signs to that is a great ornament.
rang sems zad sar skyal ba la/ / tshe gcig sangs rgyas mi zer ram/ / de sku bzhi dang 'brel ba rgyan du che/ /
Don’t they say that buddhahood in one lifetime is to convey one’s mind to the point of exhaustion? Adding the four kāyas to that is a great ornament.
mtshan nyid gsum ldan gyi gang zag la/ / brgyud ldan gyi bla ma mi zer ram/ / de gdams ngag dang 'brel (499) pa rgyan tu che/ /
dad ldan shes rab che ba la/ / snod ldan gyi slob ma mi zer ram/ / de mos gus dang 'brel pa rgyan du che/ /
Don’t they say that a worthy disciple is one with great faith and wisdom? Adding devotion to that is a great ornament.
[“The Mountain of the Precious Guru”:]
bla ma rin chen gyi ri bo la/ / gdams ngag dam pa'i chu mig bdog / dad pa skyo ngal med pas 'thung nus na/ / nyes skyon kun las thar bar nges/ /
On the mountain of the precious guru there are springs of sacred instructions. If you can drink from them with unflagging faith, you will surely be freed from all faults.
'dus byas lus kyi bum nang na/ / lhan cig skyes pa'i sgron me bdog / ting nge 'dzin thob pas chog shes na/ / phyi nang chos skur gsal bar nges/ /
Inside the vase of the composite body there is a lamp of coemergence. If you are content with meditative absorption, you will surely illuminate outer and inner dharmakāya.
rang lus sgyu ma'i ri bo la/ / rnam par shes pa'i seng phrug rtse/ / tshogs drug zhen med du sbyong shes na/ / 'khor 'das zil gyis non par nges/ /
On the mountain of your own illusory body, the lion cub of consciousness plays. If you train the six consciousnesses without attachment, you will surely outshine existence and transcendence.
ma rig pa yi tshang nang na/ / rnam par shes pa'i khyung phrug bdog / thabs shes kyi gshog pa sbyor nus na/ / 'gro drug mkha' la 'phur bar nges/ /
Inside the nest of ignorance is the fledgling garuḍa of consciousness. If you can engage the wings of method and wisdom, you will surely fly in the sky of the six migrators.
[“Mind! Mind!”:]
blo blo phyi yi yul la ltos/ / phyi yi yul la bltas tsam na/ / me long nang gi gzugs brnyan bzhin/ / snang la rang bzhin med par gda'o/ /
Mind! Mind! Look at the outer objects. When you have seen outer objects, they are like reflections in a mirror, appearing without intrinsic nature.
blo blo nang gi sems la ltos/ / nang gi sems la bltas tsam na/ / mar me rlung gis ma bskyod bzhin/ / gsal la rtog pa med par gda'/ /
Mind! Mind! Look at the inner mind. When you have seen the inner mind, it’s like a lamp unmoved by wind, clarity without conceptual thought.
blo blo phyi nang mtshams su ltos/ / phyi nang mtshams su bltas tsam na/ / mkha' la nyi shar ji bzhin du/ / mtshan ma rang sar grol nas gda'o/ /
Mind! Mind! Look at the border of outer and inner. When you have seen the border of outer and inner, it’s like the sun rising in the sky, characteristics released on their own.
blo blo thabs lam zab mo bsgoms/ / thabs lam zab mo bsgoms tsam na/ / ded dpon bzang pos byed pa bzhin/ / sems 'dod pa'i gnas su skyol gin gda'o/ /
Mind! Mind! Meditate on the profound path of methods. When you have meditated on the profound path of methods, it’s like being led by an excellent guide, mind is conveyed to the place of its desires.
blo blo phyag rgya chen po bsgoms/ / phyag rgya chen po bsgoms tsam na/ / nags la me lce mched pa bzhin/ / cir snang grogs su 'char gin gda'o/ /
Mind! Mind! Meditate on mahāmudrā. When you have meditated on mahāmudrā, it’s like a flame spreading in the darkness; everything appears and arises as your ally.
blo blo phyogs med ldom bu gyis/ / phyogs med ldom bu byas tsam na/ / mtsho la kha ba bab pa bzhin/ / rnam rtog thad kar chos gin gda'o/ / zhes gsungs so/ /
rje nyid la (500) dwags po'i slob ma bcu gsum gyis rnam rtog gis mi gnod pa'i phyag rgya chen po zhu zer ba la 'di gsungs so/ /
Thirteen disciples of Gampopa came to see the Venerable One and asked for a mahāmudrā instruction that would prevent harm from discursive thought. He said this:
skye 'gags med pa'i chos nyid la/ / rnam rtog bya ba ci la zer/ / mi rtog pa dang rtog pa gnyis/ / chu dang chu bur lta bur ltos/ /
In the nature of phenomena without birth or cessation, what is this so-called discursive thought? Look upon both thought and nonthought as water and water bubbles.
zhes sogs gsungs pas/ khong rnams kyi rnam rtog gzhi med rtsa bral du rtogs/ glo bo'i dge bshes zhig gis yi dam gang bsgrub kyang zhal mthong ba'i thabs shig zhu zer ba la 'di gsungs so/ /

He said that and other teachings, and they all realized that conceptual thought is baseless and rootless. Geshe [Gyal] of Lowo requested a method to actually see whatever deity he practiced, and Rinchen Tsöndru replied with this:
'jig rten bya ba blos thongs la/ / yid gnyis the tshom med pa yis/ / lha sku gsal la rtog med bsgom/ / 'dzad med kyi long gtam ma byed par/ / grags stong sngags kyi bzlas brjod kyis/ /
Mentally forsake worldly deeds, and without doubt or indecision meditate without concept on the deity’s clarity. Don’t engage in endless idle chatter; recite the mantra as empty sound.
de ltar byas na lha yi sku/ / myur du mthong bar the tshom med/ /
If you do this, there is no doubt you will quickly see the deity’s form.
ces gsungs pas khong shin tu nges shes skyes/ / zla ba gsum du bsgrubs pas sgrol ma'i zhal mthong ngo / /
The geshe developed deep confidence and after three months of practice saw Tārā.

yang rnam thar zhal gsungs ma las/ / dbyar gcig mu ge chen po byung ba dang / / yul mi ltog po rnams gros byas te/ / bla ma la bka' phab zhu dgos zer nas/ / nga yi 'bul skyel dang grwa pa bcom pas/ / mgon g.yag gis grong la bltas/ / grwa pa rnams ni ser dmag byed par 'dug nas/ nyin gcig mang bkol gyis byas pas thams cad 'dus pa dang / / dang po'i ber dug de gyon/ chos khug de rgyab tu khur nas 'di skad ces smras so/ /

The following story in Rinchen Tsöndru’s own words is recounted in his biography:[35] One summer, there was a terrible famine. The local people held a council to counteract it and decided to ask the guru’s advice. But since [they] carried off my offerings and overpowered the monks, the protector yak set his sights on the village. The monastics all readied themselves to be warrior monks, so one day I insisted on a public hearing and gathered everyone together. But first I put on my cloak and loaded my backpack with my ritual items. Then I spoke these words:
lam mkhan bla ma rje la zhus pas/ / lam rgyus mkhas pa'i tshad gcig byung / / blo phug dam pa'i chos la gtad pas/ / gros mgo thon pa'i tshad gcig byung / /
Consultation with the lord guru as a guide is the measure of skill in traversing the path. A deep sincere focus on the Holy Dharma is the measure of showing initiative.
sgro 'dogs rang gi sems la bcad pas/ / nges shes skyes pa'i tshad gcig byung / / ci byed dam pa'i chos dang bstun pas/ / dge sbyor 'phel ba'i tshad gcig byung / /
The resolution of hyperbole in your own mind is the measure of your self-assurance. Harmony with the Holy Dharma in whatever you do is the measure of increasing virtuous activity.
rgyal kha 'go ba gzhan la byin pas/ / blo sna 'byongs pa'i tshad gcig byung / / gzhan sems ma bzung rang sems bzung bas/ / ngo srung (501) chung ba'i tshad gcig byung / /
To give the victory to the other people is the measure of your mental training. To control your own mind and not that of others is the measure of your disregard for saving face. {501}
gang du bsdad kyang mgron po bgyis pas/ / chags zhen chung ba'i tshad gcig byung / / pham kha lto rgyab gnyis la bskur bas/ / lus sems dal ba'i tshad gcig byung / /
To behave as a guest wherever you stay is the measure of your diminished attachment. To give food and clothes to the defeated is the measure of peace in body and mind.

mgur de blangs nas ri khrod la bros pas/ / grwa pa rnams kyis ser dmag bshol/ / mgon g.yag kyang yar byung ba dang / / thugs rje chen po'i zhal nas/ / zhe sdang me dpung chen po de/ / byams pa'i chu yis bsil bar byas/ / shin tu legs so rnal 'byor pa/ / 'khor 'das chags sdang rtsa ba yin/ / chags zhen skyungs shig rnal 'byor pa/ / gsungs so/ /

After singing that song, Rinchen Tsöndru departed for mountain retreat, the monks gave up their battle plans, and the protector yak came back. The Great Compassionate One made an appearance and said: With the water of love you’ve doused the huge bonfire of anger. Very well done, yogi! Anger and desire are the root of samsara and nirvana. Cast out desire and attachment, yogi!

de nas rta'i zla ba la mtshams byas nas mi zas ma zos/ / dbang bskur ma byas pas 'od gsal gyi snang ba mched nas/ / grwa pa thams cad kyi byed spyod dang / tshe stod smad kyi legs nyes thams cad shes par byung ste/ / snying rje dang sha tshas gang la gang legs kyi gros gdab pas phal cher nges shes skyes nas dge sbyor mthar phyin pa byung ba la/ / ngom shod bla mchod la sogs pa mi nyan pa mang po byung ste kho yul du phyin pas khyim thab tu song nas nga 'chi ka la mi 'phrad par 'dug pas yul du ma 'gro byas pas ma nyan pa la yi mug nas kho'i lag pa nas bzung nas mgur 'di blangs so/ /

Then in the month of the horse I entered retreat. I abstained from human food and conferring empowerments. The appearances of lucid clarity increased and I came to know the actions of all the monks and the good or bad acts of the early and later part of their lives. Thus with compassion and affection I was able to offer appropriate advice to each of them. Most of them developed certainty and perfected their virtuous practices. However, there were many that did not listen, such as Ngomshö Lachö. He decided to return home and enter the life of a householder. As this would mean not meeting him again before dying, I asked him not to go. I was pained that he would not listen, so I took his hand and sang this song:
sangs rgyas sems can gyi mes po yin/ / dam chos sems can gyi spyi nor yin / / mi dad ldan bgo bsha' byed tsa na/ / nor skal chad pa'i snying med po/ /
Buddha is the ancestor of sentient beings. Holy Dharma is the shared wealth of sentient beings. Once it is apportioned to a person of faith, to ignore this inheritance is pointless.
dus gsum sangs rgyas kyi rtsa ba de/ / brgyud ldan gyi bla ma yin par nges/ / 'di phyi'i dgos 'dod sgrub mkhan la/ / mos gus med pa'i snying med po/ /
The root of the buddhas of the three times is certainly the guru with a lineage who fulfills desires in this life and the next; to be without devotion is pointless.
tshes yongs su gtugs pa'i lhag ma la/ / yengs med brtson 'grus mi rtsom par/ / mgu ba med pa'i phan sems kyis/ / tshe don med du skyel ba'i snying med po/ /
Not to engage in undistracted diligence for life’s remainder before it runs out, but to help those who don’t want it and waste life’s meaning is pointless.
rig pa shing kha'i byi chung la/ / 'chi bdag bdud kyi bskul ma 'ong / / sngar bsags (502) las kyi steng du 'gro/ / sdig pa byed pa'i snying med po/ /
phung po zag bcas sdug bsngal snod/ / skye rgas na 'chi kun gyi gnas/ / lus rdza gog bzhin du 'dor ba la/ / rtag tu re ba'i snying med po/ /
The conditioned body is a vessel of pain, where dwell birth, old age, sickness, and death. This body will be discarded like a clay cup; to hold out hope for its endurance is pointless.
zas nor sgyu ma'i rang bzhin la/ / rang gzhan don du mi spyod par/ / sngar 'dris ser sna'i gar sbyin gyis/ / 'bul mi phod pa'i snying med po/ /
Not to use for your own and others’ benefit food and wealth that is by nature illusory, but not be able to bear parting with gifts due to your age-old miserliness is pointless.
rnam rtog gdon gyi sun ma la/ / chos nyid bskul ma mi lta bar/ / lus sems bral gyis dogs pa yis/ / sems 'phrig gtsum byed pa'i snying med po/ /
Not to hear the call to phenomena’s nature in the spirit escort of discursive thought, but to fear the separation of body and mind and become agitated is pointless.
las rnams 'grub pa'i gsang sngags la/ / ma yengs thun bzhir mi bsgom par/ / 'dzad pa med pa'i long gtam la/ / dus 'da' ru 'jug pa'i snying med po/ /
Not to meditate constantly in four sessions on the Secret Mantra that accomplishes all actions, but to waste your time in endless talk while life passes you by is pointless.
sems nyid yid bzhin nor bu la/ / sku gsum 'bral med mi bsgom par/ / ri dwags smig rgyu snyegs pa bzhin/ / tshig phyir 'breng ba'i snying med po/ /
Not to meditate on the three kāyas as inseparable from the wish-fulfilling gem of mind itself is like a deer chasing a mirage; pursuing words is pointless.
chos nyid gtan yul mi 'dzin par/ / bdag 'dzin mel tshe byed byed po/ / rigs drug gi grong khyer sgyu mar bzung / / tshe thug med du 'khyams pa'i snying med po/ / zhes gsungs so/ /

Without inhabiting the firm land of phenomena’s nature, to constantly keep watch over self-fixation and grasp at the illusory cities of six classes of beings, wandering in infinite regress, is pointless.
lta sgom spyod 'bras kyi rdo rje'i mgur/ /
“The Vajra Song of View, Meditation, Conduct, and Result”:
skye 'gags med pa'i don rtogs na/ / lta ba kun mtho rung ma mtho rung / / gza' gtad med pa'i ngang du zhog / gnyis 'dzin med na lta ba yin/ /
If you realize the meaning of no birth or cessation, it doesn’t matter if your view is the highest or not. Rest in a state without reference points— not clinging to duality, it is the view.
sku gsum 'bral med don rtogs na/ / gnas ba kun brtan rung ma brtan rung / / 'bad pa med pa'i ngang du zhog / gsal la ma yengs sgom pa yin/ /
If you realize the meaning of ever-present three kāyas, it doesn’t matter if your abiding is stable or not. Rest in a state without effort— not wavering from clarity is meditation.
'gro 'chag nyal 'dug ma yengs na/ / spyod pa kun rtsing rung ma rtsing rung / / nyam nga med pa'i ngang du zhog / chags zhen med na spyod pa yin/ /
If you are undistracted when walking, moving, lying, or sitting, it doesn’t matter if your behavior is the crudest or not. Rest in a state without fear— to be without attachment is the conduct.
gsal la dngos med don rtogs na/ / nyams myong 'bar rung ma 'bar rung / / brjod du med pa'i ngang du zhog / nges shes yod na nyams myong yin/ /
If you realize the meaning of insubstantial clarity, it doesn’t matter if your experience shines or not. Rest in a state that is ineffable— to have absolute certainty is meditative experience.
re dogs med pa'i don rtogs na/ / (503) chos sku thob rung ma thob rung / / zhe 'dod med pa'i ngang du zhog / gdod nas grub pa 'bras bu yin/ / zhes gsungs so/ /
If you realize the meaning of no hopes and fears, {503} it doesn’t matter if you attain dharmakāya or not. Rest in a state without anger or desire— the primordially existent is the result.
sems 'chi med rdo rje'i mgur/ /
“The Vajra Song of Immortal Mind”:
mdo rgyud man ngag nyams myong gis/ / ma bsgoms sangs rgyas 'chi med gnad/ / 'di ltar rnam smin lus 'di la/ / ye shes lus ni rang dgar 'byung / /

Sutras, tantras, esoteric instructions, and experience contain the vital point of immortality, buddhahood without meditation. Thus this fully ripened body arises by itself as the body of timeless awareness.
rnam smin lus la lha yi sku/ / gsal la der 'dzin med par bsgom/ / de nyid sems dang dbyer med de/ / sems la ngo bo ma grub pas/ /
Meditate without grasping to the clarity of the fully ripened body as the deity’s body. That very body is inseparable from your mind, and in mind there is no real essence.
de la 'chi rgyu ga la yod/ / 'chi ba zhes bya rnam rtog yin/ / rtog tshogs 'khor 'das chos ma grub/ / 'pho bya 'pho byed rang sar grol/ /
So where is the cause of death? So-called death is just a concept. Thoughts do not exist, nor do samsara and nirvana. Transference and the transferred are self-liberated.
rnam shes gang la don pa don/ / 'chi med mtha' bral 'bras bu'i mchog / dran pas mngon sangs rgya ba ni/ / DA ki'i srog snying srog ltar 'chang / /

Wherever consciousness goes, it goes. This is the supreme result, boundless immortality. This is the ḍākinī’s vital heart that brings manifest buddhahood just by recollecting it; hold it as dear as your life.
rang sems 'chi med rang grol rje btsun rat+na bIr+Ya pas mdzad pa rdzogs so/ / bla ma shangs pa la gser srang lnga bcu phul nas zhus te nyams su myong bar byas so/ //
“The Natural Liberation of One’s Mind as Immortal” by Ratnavīrya (Rinchen Tsöndru) is complete. I offered Lama Shangpa fifty gold pieces to request it and have brought it into my own experience. ithi
mya ngan las 'da' kar 'brong bu btsan rgod la zhal chems su gdams pa/ /
When Rinchen Tsöndru was about to pass away, he gave as his final testament these instructions to the wild tsen spirit Drongbu:[36]
bu tha snyad kyi sgro 'dogs gcod pa na/ / tha snyad kyi chos la dgos pa med/ / bslab pa dka' la brjed pa skyen/ /
Child, when you resolve misconceptions of verbal designations, you’ll have no need for conventional teachings— so difficult to learn but so easy to forget.
chos kyi sgo mo brgyad khri bzhi stong yang / / sems nyid kyi steng du gzhol zhing 'bab/ / chos ji ltar bsam kyang gnas lugs dang / / ma bcos gnyug ma'i ngang la zhog /
Though there are eighty-four thousand dharma gates, they all come down to mind itself. Whatever dharma you contemplate, rest in the abiding nature, the uncontrived native state.
snang ba sems su shes par gyis/ / sems kyi rang bzhin skye ba med/ / skye med rtogs na 'od gsal dang / / blo sna de la 'gro tshad thong / /
Know that appearance is mind, and that mind’s nature is unborn. If you realize the unborn, it is lucid clarity. Place all your attention on that.
rgyu rkyen rten 'brel mi bslu bas/ / bu yi don gcig 'grub de mchi/ / zhes gsungs so/ ! /
Since interdependent cause and effect never fails, practice for this one thing, child.
Öntön Kyergangpa Chökyi Senge

skyes rabs kun tu 'phags mchog thugs rje chen pos rjes su bzung zhing sku tshe 'dir yang brtson 'grus (504) drag pos bsgrubs pas mtshams sbyar te 'phags pa nyid dang dbyer med pa'i mchog grub pa/ / byang chub kyi sems rin po che rnam pa gnyis rtsol med chu bo'i rgyun lta bu mnga' ba/ / rje btsun rmog lcog pa las mkha' 'gro'i chig brgyud thob cing shar phyogs bai DUr+Ya snang ba'i zhing khams su de bzhin gshegs pa dri med nam mkha'i dpal zhes bya bar 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur ba'i skyes mtha'i byang sems dbon ston skyer sgang pa chos kyi seng ge la rgyal ba sras bcas kyi chos sgo mtha' yas bstsal ba las mtshon pa tsam ni/ rje btsun sgrol ma'i zhal nas/

He was nurtured by sublime Exalted Avalokiteśvara in all his lifetimes. In this lifetime he became accomplished through intense discipline and again made that connection, finally attaining the supreme power of inseparability with that Exalted One. {504} The twofold mind of awakening flowed through him effortlessly like a river. From Venerable Mokchokpa he received the Ḍākinī’s single lineage and would ultimately attain awakening in the eastern buddha field of Vaiḍūryaprabha as the tathāgata Glory of Immaculate Space. In his final life as a bodhisattva, Öntön Kyergangpa Chökyi Senge was graced with infinite dharma gates opened by the buddhas and their heirs. For example, Exalted Tārā said:
sgyu lus bden med gnad yin a 'thas shig / rmi lam 'dun pa'i gnad yin lam du khyer/ / 'od gsal mos gus gnad yin gsol ba thob/ / gzhan don snying rje'i gnad yin phyogs 'dzin spongs/ /

The vital point of Illusory Body is its lack of reality; destroy reification. The vital point of Dream is intentionality; integrate it on the path. The vital point of Lucid Clarity is devotion; attain it through prayer. The vital point of altruism is compassion; renounce prejudice.
zhes dang / gnyis 'dzin spangs na 'dod chags ngang gis zhi/ / pha mar shes bas zhe sdang rang sar grol/ / gsal la rtog med gti mug dbyings su thim/ /
And: When dualism is abandoned, desire is calmed within. Knowledge [of beings] as parents frees anger on its own. In nonconceptual clarity, stupidity dissolves into space.
'gags med dug gsum rang sar 'ching byed 'di/ / der 'dzin med par rang sar grol bar nges/ / nyon mongs rang shar rang grol nyid du ltos/ / zhes gsungs/ /
This binding of the wanton three poisons in their own ground, without fixating there, will surely liberate them in their own ground. Watch the afflictions as they self-arise and self-liberate.
thugs rje chen po'i zhal nas/ /
Avalokiteśvara said:
'du 'dzi g.yeng ba bdud kyi bar chad yin/ / chags sdang sna tshogs grogs su mi 'char bas/ / rkyen ngan dben pa'i dgon pa rtag tu bsten/ / tshe la long med 'chi ba bsam par rigs/ / zhes gsungs/ /

Distraction in busyness is a devilish obstacle. Until the variety of love and hate arises as an ally, always rely on seclusion, far from adverse conditions. It is wise to reflect on life’s brevity and think of death.
rgyud sde lnga'i lha tshogs kyi zhal nas/ /
The Five Tantras’ deities said:
dbang bzhi ma rdzogs smin par ga la nus/ / dbyer med bskyed rim ma bsgom grol mi srid/ / thob 'dod re bas 'bras bu mi 'byin pas/ / rang grol rang shar sku gsum dbyer med ltos/ / zhes gsungs/ /

Maturation does not happen without the complete four empowerments. Liberation is impossible without meditating on creation [and completion] inseparable. Since the results won’t come through hope and desire to attain them, regard self-liberation on arising as inseparable from the three kāyas.

bla ma rmog lcog pa zhi bar gshegs pa'i tshe/ rje btsun ma'i zhal nas/ nam mkha' 'di la skye 'chi med pa ltar/ / bla ma la yang skye 'chi ga la yod/ / mos gus (505) stobs kyis 'bral med gnas pa yin/ /

After Lama Mokchokpa had entered peace, Vajrayoginī said: Just as there is no birth or death in this sky, how could the guru be subject to birth and death? The guru remains constant through your devotion. {505}
mya ngan ma byed rgyun du gsol ba thob/ / ces gsungs so/ / rang sems bla mar ngo sprod pa'i rdo rje'i mgur bzhengs pa ni/
Don’t grieve, supplicate! “The Vajra Song Introducing One’s Mind as the Guru”:
gu ru bo d+hi tsit+ta na mA mi/ /
guru bodhicitta namā mi
bla ma mnyam med sems nyid ngo sprod pa'i/ / rang don mthar phyin gzhan don nang du lon/ / phyogs med mkhyen pa'i thugs rje kun la snyoms/ / bla ma drin can rnams la phyag 'tshal lo/ /
Homage to all the benevolent gurus, incomparable teachers who introduce mind itself. Their own aims achieved, they assume others’ welfare and show unbiased wise compassion equally to all.
yin lugs mtshon pa'i bla ma khyed rnams lags/ / gnas lugs shar ba'i bla ma nang na bzhugs/ /
Indeed all you gurus demonstrate the way things are, but the guru who arises as the abiding nature dwells within.

rang sems bla ma'i mtshan nyid 'di ltar lags/ / rgyu las ma byung rang bzhin lhun gyis grub/ / rkyen gyis mi 'jig gnyen po kun dang bral/ / 'gro 'ong mi bdog dus gsum 'pho 'gyur med/ / dngos dang dngos med brjod pa'i mtha' las 'das/ /

This now is the characteristic guru of one’s own mind: Not arisen from causes but spontaneously present, unaffected by conditions and without need of antidotes, not going or coming or changing in the three times, beyond extremes of being described as real or unreal.
dbang po lnga la mthong ba'i dngos po med/ / med bzhin sna tshogs 'char ba'i byung khungs yin/ / bltas shing bcos kyang 'di zhes ngos bzung med/ / ma btsal bzhag kyang rang bzhin cing yang 'char/ /

No thing that is perceived by the five senses, nonexistent and yet the source of everything, though I look and contrive, I cannot pinpoint “It is this.” But when I give up trying, it is present everywhere.
dge sdig las kyi dbang du de mi 'gyur/ / kun las 'phags shing gang la'ang zhen pa med/ / kun dang bral bas kun gyi dngos gzhi yin/ / blo dang bral bas don med blo la gsal/ /

Not subject to the influence of good or bad actions, exalted above all but unattached to anything, separate from everything, yet the actual ground of all, free of intellect, yet for no reason it is clearly in mind.
phyogs med de la phyogs med sna tshogs 'byung / / byung yang gang gi phyogs su nges pa med/ / de ltar 'di zhes kho nar ma gyur pa'i/ / ji bzhin de nyid rang gi bla ma yin/ /
In that lack of direction, diversity arises anywhere, arising but without any definite location. It is not enough to say, “It’s like this.” That is precisely my guru.

bla ma'i rnam thar bshad na 'di ltar bdog / bla ma de la nye ring mi bdog pas/ / des ma khyab pa'i sems can gcig kyang med/ / bla ma de nyid smon lam dag pa'i phyir/ / kun kyang de yi rigs su ma gyur med/ /

If I were to recount the guru’s life story, there’s this: That guru is neither near nor far, yet there is not a single being not pervaded. That guru, due to pure aspirations, does not exclude anyone from its family.
bla ma de nyid thugs rje che ba'i phyir/ / ye sangs rgyas la ma bkod gcig kyang med/ / bla ma de nyid mdzad pa stobs che bas/ / 'khor 'das kun la 'jug cing rang dbang sgyur/ / (506)
That guru, because of great compassion, does not exclude anyone from original awakening. That guru, with great powerful deeds, enters samsara and nirvana with total control. {506}
bla ma de la 'pho 'gyur mi bdog pas/ / log par bltas kyang don de gnas par yin/ / bla ma de dang skad cig 'bral ma myong / / 'grogs yun ring ste sus kyang zhal mthong dka'/ /
That guru does not transfer or change, so even when viewed wrongly, remains the same. That guru has never been apart for an instant, but everyone struggles to see this longtime friend.
bla ma de la 'das grongs mi mnga' bas/ / gtan gyi bya ra zin pa ngo mtshar che/ / de lta bu yi rang sems bla ma la/ / rang ngo rang gis shes pa'i zhal ras blta/ /
That guru who is not subject to dying, watches constantly—what an amazing guru! This is the guru of one’s own mind; gaze upon its countenance and recognize yourself.
the tshom som nyi bral ba'i gsol ba gdab/ / ma bcos rang sar 'jog pa'i mos gus bya/ /
Supplicate without doubt or hesitation, and cultivate devotion of resting in its uncontrived state.
rgyun du ngang la gnas pa'i zhabs tog bya/ / gsal stong ched 'dzin med pa'i zhal zas drangs/ / dran yengs dbyer med rtogs pa'i zhal skyems drangs/ / snang grags sgyu mar shes pa'i na bza' gsol/ /

Serve this guru by always dwelling in its true nature, bring the food of empty clarity without fixation, serve the drink of realizing inseparable attention and distraction, and clothe with the knowledge of appearance and sound as illusion.
zag med bde ba'i 'bol stan 'og tu bting / / ma btsal ye nas yin pa'i dbu zhwa gsol/ / ci shar ched 'dzin med pa'i zang zing phul/ /
Place underneath the soft mat of undissipating bliss, crown with the hat of what, unsought, was always there, and present the gifts of whatever arises without fixation.
kun mkhyen bdag 'dzin med pa'i gzim khang du/ / 'khor 'das dbye bsri med pa'i 'khor gyis bskor/ / dus gsum rgyun chad med par bzhugs nas kyang / / rang snang lhug pa'i gdams ngag rgyun du gsol/ /

In the bedroom of omniscience without self-fixation, surrounded by a retinue of indivisible samsara-nirvana, the guru dwells continuously in the three times, always illuminating self-manifesting instructions.
ngo mtshar che'o rang sems bla ma nyid/ / slar yang thugs rjes bzung ba bka' drin che/ / tshe sngon sbyangs pa'i rnal 'byor las 'phro che/ / de yang thugs rjes mi gtong ngo mtshar che/ /
So very wonderful, this guru of my own mind! Once again kindly nurture me with compassion, a yogin with karmic propensity from past life training. Amazing that you have not relinquished compassion.
bla ma de la bsten lugs de byas pas/ / bla ma'i byin rlabs 'di ltar 'byung gin gda'/ / 'khor ba'i 'dam nas ma bros pa ru thar/ / sangs rgyas sa ru ma phyin pa ru sleb/ /
To rely on the guru in that fashion elicits the guru’s blessings in these ways: You’ll escape without fleeing the swamp of existence. You’ll arrive at awakening without going anywhere.
'khor 'das gnyis la bzang ngan med par go/ / sangs rgyas sems can rtogs ma rtogs kyi khyad/ / sems kyi mtshan nyid ma nor rtogs gyur cing / / thag chod mngon du gyur na sangs rgyas zer/ /

You’ll know there’s no good or bad in samsara or nirvana. The difference between buddhas and beings is realization. To realize mind’s characteristics without error and to manifest that conviction is called “buddha.”
de yi yon tan brjod ba'i mtha' las 'das/ / gzhan du bla ma bstan yang 'di ltar 'byung / / sems nyid ji bzhin pa ru ma rtogs pas/ / de ma yin la der 'dzin shes (507) pa zhugs/ /
Its qualities are beyond expression. To rely on another guru will have these results: You won’t realize mind itself as it is but cling to what it is not and get stuck there. {507}
rjes phyir 'brangs pas sdug bsngal las la spyod/ / de la sems can zhes su btags pa yin/ / da ni rang gi bya ra rang gis byed/ / 'khor ba'i rjes phyir ma 'brangs snga ma sun/ /
Following after that, you’ll create the karma of suffering. That is to be designated as “sentient being.” Now, be your own caretaker. Don’t retrace your steps in samsara ad nauseam.
mya ngan 'das pa mi bsgrub rtsol ba che/ / sems nyid rang sa bzung nas rang gar sdod/ /
Don’t accomplish nirvana with great effort. Hold mind itself in its own ground and just be.
'di zhes ngos bzung med pa'i sems nyid 'di/ / ma la ma go 'di yis sbyangs nas byung / / de yang mtshan nyid go ba 'di yis 'tshengs/ /
This mind itself that is not identified by saying “this” will occur through refining this unknowing. Now, this knowledge of those characteristics is gratifying.
'tshengs lugs de bzhin bsten na 'di ltar lags/ / stong nyid rang chas chos sku btsal mi dgos/ / cir snang rang shar gzugs sku dgag ma dgos/ / sems nyid rang 'gros sku gsum bcos mi dgos/ /

To rely on this manner of gratification is like this: You needn’t seek the dharmakāya integral to emptiness. You needn’t block the rūpakāyas that self-arise as anything. You needn’t contrive the three kāyas that are mind’s own movement.
'khor ba'i gzhi rtsa chod pas dor mi dgos/ / rang sems sangs rgyas yin pas re mi dgos/ / ye nas yin pas blo yis bsgom mi dgos/ / khyed kyang 'di ltar mdzad na mi legs sam/ /

You needn’t discard samsara that is already severed at its root. You needn’t hope for buddhahood that is already one’s own mind. You needn’t meditate mentally on what was there since forever. Wouldn’t that be fine if you could do this?
ma yengs sems la lta ba'i rtogs ldan rnams/ / lta ba'i blo dang bral na cis mi rung / / ma bral rgyun du sgom pa'i sgom chen pa/ / sgom mkhan rang thog grol na cis mi rung / /

Realized ones who watch the mind without distraction: What’s wrong with being free of the watching mind? Great meditators who are constantly meditating: What’s wrong with liberation directly on that meditator?
rtag tu byang chub sgrub pa'i sgrub pa po/ / ma bsgom lhun grub go na cis mi rung / / bcos med bya ra byed pa'i rnal 'byor pa/ / rang sems gtan la phab na cis mi rung / /

Practitioners who always cultivate the mind of awakening: What’s wrong with knowing spontaneous nonmeditation? Yogins who stand guard over the uncontrived: What’s wrong with ascertaining your own mind?
mtshan ldan bla ma mang du bstan lags kyang / / bla ma re la gsung sgros re re 'byung / / de rnams rtsa ba sems la thug nas 'dug /
Though I attended many qualified gurus, each guru gave their own words of advice, but they all came down to one point: the mind.
de nas rang sems bla ma de nyid la/ / zhal lta gsung nyan gdams ngag mang du zhus/ / drin che'i bla ma bdun la gsol ba btab/ / bstod pa phul zhing byin rlabs zhus pa yis/ /
So with that very guru, my own mind, I looked at its face, listened to its speech, and took much instruction. I supplicated before this guru, offered praises, and requested blessings.
rang sems bla ma yin pa'i rtogs pa zhig / nang nas shar ba'i go lugs yi ger bkod/ / 'gal dang 'khrul par mthong lags na/ / tshig la ma blta don la ltos/ /
I realized within that my own mind is the guru, so I have written down my understanding. If you see contradictions or mistakes, don’t look at the words; look at their meaning.
smyon pas mu cor (508) smras pa yin/ / gang la'ang bzod par mi gsol lo/ / bzod gsol 'bul ba'i yon ma mchis/ / zhes gsungs so/ /
rang sems bla ma zhes bya ba rin po che skyer sgang bas mdzad pa / /
That concludes “One’s Mind as the Guru” by precious Kyergangpa. ithi
sems 'chi med du ngo sprod pa'i rdo rje'i mgur/
“The Vajra Song of Introducing Immortal Mind”:
na mo gu ru/
namo guru
nyin par snang stong lha yi sku/ / na dang 'chi ba med par rtogs/ / 'chi khar spyan tsam gsal bas kyang / / gnad gcod rang dag longs sku thob/ /

In the daytime, empty appearance is the deity’s form. I realize that it has no sickness or death. At death, even if only its eyes appear, death’s interruption is self-purified and saṃbhogakāya attained.
brgya la gsal bar ma gyur kyang / / gsal dwangs rdzing bur rdo brgyab bzhin/ / sngar gyi gnad kyis bar ma dor/ / bde chen longs sku rang shar 'byung / /
If even one in a hundred does not appear, the import of previous training will go on unabated, like ripples of a stone thrown in a deep pond. The saṃbhogakāya of great bliss will arise of itself.
'khor ba stong par ma gyur tshe/ / gzhan don dpag med lhun grub 'byung / /
Until such time as cyclic existence is emptied, boundless benefit for others will arise spontaneously.

rang sems 'chi med rang grol rje btsun d+harma sing has mdzad pa'o/ / mnyam med rin chen la gser srang brgya dang / / 'bri sum cu/ / ber thul gcig rnams phul nas zhus te nyams su myong bar byas so/ ! /

“The Natural Liberation of One’s Mind as Immortal” by Venerable Dharmasiṃha is complete. I offered the incomparable Rinchen one hundred gold pieces, thirteen female yaks, and one fur cloak to request it, and have brought it into my own experience.
Rigongpa Sangye [Nyen] Tönpa

dpon ston skyer sgang pa chen pos chig brgyud gsang ba'i mdzod gtad cing mkhas pa dang grub pa'i mngon rtogs mthar phyin pa/ / sa lam gyi yon tan rdzogs pas sku tshe gcig gis zung 'jug chen po'i rgyal sar rang dbang du sgyur ba sku tshe de nyid kyi phyi mar shar phyogs sangs rgyas kyi zhing khams me tog bkram par rgyal ba pad+ma'i dpal zhes bya bar 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur ba'i srid mtha'i byang sems ri gong pa chen po sangs rgyas ston pa chos kyi shes rab la bu slob rnams kyi gsol ba btab pas mtshams sbyar te tshes bcu'i tshogs 'khor gyi skabs su rdo rje'i mgur bzhengs pa ni/ /

He received the secret treasury of the one-to-one lineage from Öntön Kyergangpa the Great and reached the culmination of manifest realization in scholarship and practice. He perfected the qualities of the levels and paths, and thereby gained mastery of the domain of great integral unity in a single lifetime. So right after that life, he was born in the eastern buddha field of Avakīrṇakusuma and became enlightened as Victor Padmaśrī, Glorious Lotus. In his last existence as a bodhisattva, he was the great Ringongpa Sangye Tönpa Chökyi Sherap. At a tenth-day communal feast, in response to the entreaty of many disciples, he composed this vajra song:
chos dbyings mkha' la sangs rgyas sras/ / skyed mdzad bde ster ni gu dang / / dbang bzhis smin byas bslab gsum ldan/ / bla ma mchog bsten de nyid mkhyen/ / rje btsun rat+na bIr+Ya dang / /

In the sky of phenomena’s realm, Niguma birthed the Buddha’s heirs and bestowed bliss. Venerable Ratnavīrya (Rinchen Tsöndru), matured by four empowerments, endowed with three trainings, attended a supreme guru and realized suchness.
snang grags sgyu mar mkhyen mdzad pa'i/ / zhen med lha skus 'gro don mdzad/ / (509) sku gsum ngo bo chos kyi rje/ / mnyam med skyer pa sgang pa la/ /
skyo ngal med pa'i dad pa yis/ / 'du 'bral med par gsol ba 'debs/ / 'dir tshogs dad ldan skyes bu kun/ / dbyangs 'di la dar cig gsan par zhu/ /
I supplicate them with unflagging faith, not subject to meeting or parting. All faithful ones gathered here, please listen a moment to this melody.
brgyud ldan bla ma dam pa de/ / dus gsum sangs rgyas yin par nges/ / bla ma chos skur rtogs pa des/ / mdo rgyud don la ma rmongs shing / /
The holy guru possessed of lineage is definitely the buddhas of the three times. Whoever realizes the guru as dharmakāya is not ignorant of the meaning of Sutra and Tantra.
lus gsum gnas lugs 'di ltar rtogs/ / da lta rnam par smin pa'i lus/ / bskyed pa yid kyis bskyed pa yin/ / 'di la brten nas bag chags sogs/ / 'khor ba bde sdug tsam du snang / /

Realize the abiding nature of the three bodies like this: The current body of fully ripened [karma] was born as a product of the mind. Based on that, habitual patterns and so forth create cyclic existence, the mere appearance of joy and sorrow.
snga ma la ltos 'bras bu la/ / phyi ma la ltos rgyu ru gsungs/ /
As is said, “For the result, look to the past [life]; for the cause, look to the next [life].”[37]
nyin mo'i bag chags rlan gyis ni/ / skyon yon sna tshogs rmi pa de/ / bag chags lus su btags pa yin/ /
The habits of the daytime saturate dreams of various faults and qualities. This is termed the habitual body.

bar do yid kyi lus po de/ / thogs med dbang po kun tshang nas/ / snga ma 'dra ba'i lus su snang / / las kyi rjes su 'brang bar byed/ / rang bzhin rtogs na bde chen sku/ / ma rtogs srid pa'i rjes su 'jug /

The mental body of the intermediate state is unhindered and complete in all its senses, so it is experienced as the previous living body. It follows after your karma. If its nature is realized, it is the great-bliss kāya. If not, you just reenter existence.
'khor ba khrag gi rgya mtsho 'dir/ / de snga chags sdang rlabs kyis bskyod/ / a 'thas zhen pa'i skyes bu de/ / sdug bsngal nyam thag don re chung / /
This bloody ocean of cyclic existence is churned by waves of previous anger and desire. That person with reified attachment, weary of suffering, has little purpose there.
'byung bzhis bsdus pa'i rnam smin lus/ / rnam smin lus la len lugs mang / / ma rtogs rigs drug 'khor mar len/ /
