The fully ripened body is a collection of four elements. There are many ways to assume a fully ripened body— without realization, it’s in the round of the six kinds of beings.
nga dag pa'i sgyu lus 'di ltar len/ / rnam smin lus la rgyal ba'i sku/ / bsam pa tsam gyis don rnams 'grub/ / dmigs med kyi sgyu lus 'khyams po yin/ / rang sems bla mas de skad gsungs/ /

I assumed the pure illusory body in this way: The fully ripened body is the Victor’s kāya; it accomplishes all purpose by thought alone. I am a wanderer in this illusory body with no reference. The guru of my own mind taught me that.
yid kyi lus la rgyal ba'i sku/ / bsam pa tsam gyis don rnams 'grub/ / dmigs med kyi sgyu lus 'khyams po yin/ / rang sems bla mas de skad gsungs/ /
The mental body is the Victor’s kāya; it accomplishes all purpose by thought alone. I am a wanderer in this illusory body with no reference. The guru of my own mind taught me that.
bag chags lus la rgyal ba'i sku/ / bsam pa tsam gyis don (510) rnams 'grub/ / dmigs med kyi sgyu lus 'khyams po yin/ / rang sems bla mas de skad gsungs/ /

de ltar nyams su blangs pa las/ / 'bras bu sku gsum 'di ltar 'char/ / chos sku spros bral gnyug ma'i don/ / ngo bo ngos bzung kun dang bral/ / mtshan nyid blo yi yul las 'das/ / chos sku'i ngo bo de ltar lags/ /

As a result of practicing like that, the three kāyas arise like this: Dharmakāya, the unembellished native state, is unidentifiable as to its essence and its characteristics are beyond objects of mind. Indeed that is the essence of dharmakāya.
mkha' ltar dag pa'i chos sku las/ / gzugs sku rnam pa gnyis po de/ / dpag bsam shing dang nor bu ltar/ /
From the dharmakāya, pure as space, come the two form kāyas, like a wish-fulfilling tree or gem.
ji srid 'khor ba ma stongs bar/ / de srid gzhan don rgyun mi 'chad/ / sa bcu'i byang chub sems dpa' la/ / mtshan dpes brgyan pa'i longs skur snang / /
Until cyclic existence is emptied, they continuously work for others’ welfare. The saṃbhogakāya adorned by marks and signs appears to bodhisattvas on the ten levels.
so so skye bo la sogs dang / / gdul bya ma dag nyan thos la/ / gang 'dul sprul sku'i snang ba 'char/ /
The nirmāṇakāya appears to whomever is to be tamed: to ordinary people and so forth, and to impure beings, and śrāvakas.
de gsum dbyer med zung 'jug la/ / bde chen sku zhes gsungs pa yin/ / ye shes mkha' 'gro ni gu ma'i/ / smin grol sgyu lus gdams ngag yod/ /
Those three as an inseparable integral unity are called the sukhakāya, body of bliss. I have Awareness Ḍākinī Niguma’s maturing and liberating illusory-body instructions.
grangs med gsum bral blo re bde/ / dgyes rdor bde mchog la sogs pa'i/ / yi dam lha yi lus bstan yod/ / gdams 'di'i gnad rnams ma lus yod/ /
I’m happy not waiting three incalculable eons. I have prophecies from the yidam deities— Hevajra, Cakrasaṃvara, and others— and every vital point of the instructions.
the tshom med pas blo re bde/ / gsang sgrub lte ba'i sprul 'khor dang / / sbyin pa rnam bzhis 'gro don byed/ / log 'tsho mi dgos blo re bde/ /
I’m happy to be without doubts. I have the Secret Sādhana of the Emanated Navel Chakra, and the four kinds of generosity to help migrators. I’m happy not to depend on wrong livelihood.
'khor lo bcing grol shing rta can/ / bum pa can gyi gdams pa yod/ / skad cig ma re bsgom pas kyang / / bde drod rgyun chad med par 'bar/ /
I have instructions on vase breathing, the chariot that binds and liberates chakras. Every instant of meditation on that makes bliss-heat continually blaze.
bde stong ldan pas blo re bde/ / ye shes skar khung 'pho ba yod/ / sdig can gyis 'chi khar dran tsam na/ / mkha' spyod 'gro bas blo re bde/ /
I’m happy having that bliss-emptiness. I have transference through the Skylight of Timeless Awareness. Even the sinful who recall it at death go to the celestial realm, so I’m happy too.
chos skyong ye shes mgon po dang / / las mgon k+She tra pA la yod/ / sangs rgyas bstan pa srung ba'i phyir/ / bran bzhin nyan pas blo re bde/ /
I have the dharma protectors: Awareness Protector and the activity protector Kṣetrapāla. Since they guard the Buddha’s doctrine, I’m happy that they obey me like servants.

dus khyad par can tshes bcu yar gyi ngo / / mkha' 'gro 'du ba'i tshogs gral du/ / (511) snying dang 'dra ba'i bu slob kyis/ / gsol ba btab nas zhus pa'i ngor/ / bde thob yangs pa'i dbyangs 'di blangs/ /

At this special time of the tenth-day waxing moon, participating in the feast where ḍākinīs gather, {511} in response to the supplications and requests of my disciples, who are like my own heart, I sang this spacious melody of attaining bliss.
'di la mkha' 'gro'i byin rlabs chags/ / dbyangs 'di thos par gyur pa rnams/ / bla ma chos skur rtogs pa dang / / lha sku phyag rgya chen po rnams/ / 'bad rtsol med par rtogs par shog /
It has the blessings of the ḍākinīs. May all those who hear this melody realize the guru as dharmakāya, and may they realize without effort the mahāmudrā of the deity’s form.
dus gsum bsags pa'i dge ba rnams/ / thams cad byang chub chen por bsngo/ / zhes gsungs so/ /
All virtue accumulated in the three times is dedicated to the great awakening of all.
yon sgom tshong 'dus la skyel thung mdzad pa'i dus 'gro chos zhig gnang ba zhu zhus pas 'di gsungs so/ /
Rigongpa accompanied Yöngom for a short way on his trip to the marketplace and said this in response to his request for teaching:
rgyal ba'i dgongs pa rin chen mdzod/ / ma rig mun sel sgron ma'i 'od/ / rnam dag don gnyis lhun grub pa'i/ / chos rje'i thugs kyis bkra shis shog /

The precious treasury of the Victor’s intent is the lamplight that dispels the darkness of ignorance. May there be the auspiciousness of the dharma lord who spontaneously accomplishes the two pure purposes.
rnam smin lus la 'od gsal dang / / lha sku 'dres pa'i sems de la/ / na rgyu 'chi rgyu med par shes/ /
In the fully ripened body, the mind that blends lucid clarity with the deity’s form knows no cause for sickness or death.
de yi dbugs chad 'chi ba'i tshe/ / gnad gcod sdug bsngal rang dag nas/ / 'od gsal lha sku 'dres gyur te/ / bsgom bya sgom byed rang sar grol/ /

When the breath stops at the time of death, the suffering of life’s interruption is self-purified and lucid clarity blends with the deity’s form. Meditation object and meditation are liberated in their own ground.
skye med 'od gsal nam mkha' la/ / rang shar gzugs sku rnam gnyis kyis/ / 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho ma stongs par/ / gzhan don lhun grub rgyun chad med/ /
Unborn lucid clarity arises by itself in space as the two forms of rūpakāya. Until the ocean of cyclic existence is empty, they constantly create spontaneous welfare of others.
'chi brod gdams pa de ltar lags/ / ye shes mgon po phyag drug pa/ / bran bzhin nyan pa'i bka' bsgo byas/ / bu gtsang du bzhud pa'i rdzong ba mdzod/ /
Such is the instruction for courage at death. Six-Armed Awareness Protector, who obeys like a servant, has received my command. Take him with you on your trip to Tsang, my son.
tshad med bzhi dang sems bskyed la/ / nan tan mdzad cing ci bder bzhud/ / bdag pha yang myur du mjal bar zhu/ / bkra shis pa'i mchod dbyangs de la mdzod/ / ces so/ /
Apply the four immeasurables and awakening mind with diligence and go wherever you like. Please quickly come to see me, your father. This is my melody of offering auspiciousness.
dge slong gzhon nu seng ges gsol ba btab pa'i ngor rnam par thar pa gsal bar gsungs pa'i mjug sdom du rdo rje'i zhal chems stsal ba ni/
As recounted at the conclusion of his life story,[38] this vajra testament was granted at the request of the monk Zhönu Senge:
bdag gi slob ma yang slob dang / / 'brel par gyur pa thams cad kun/ / (512) log pa'i bsam pa spangs byas nas/ / 'bral ba med pa'i mos gus gyis/ /
My disciples and their disciples and all who have connection with me {512} should abandon misguided thinking and trust in our ongoing relationship.
nga yi lus dang rgyal ba'i sku/ / tha dad ma yin rnal 'byor pa/ / bdag gi ngag dang rgyal ba'i gsung / / dbye ba med do rnal 'byor pa/ /
My body and the Victor’s awakened form are no different, yogin. My speech and the Victor’s awakened speech are not separate, yogin.
kho bo'i sems dang rgyal ba'i thugs/ / gnyis med gcig tu rtogs par gyis/ / 'bras bu rang shar lha sku dang / / sku gsum dbyer med bde chen yin/ /
My mind and the Victor’s awakened mind should be known as one, not two. The result, the natural arising of a deity’s form inseparable from the three kāyas, is great bliss.
lar tshad med mos gus ma skyes na/ / bla ma'i yon tan mthong mi 'gyur/ /
And yet if unlimited devotion does not arise, you will not see the guru’s good qualities.
mos gus mthar thug skyes gyur na/ / bla ma dus gsum sangs rgyas kyi/ / sku gsung thugs nyid mi zad pa/ / rgyan gyi 'khor los sems can rnams/ / smin cing grol bar byed pa yin/ /
If ultimate devotion does arise, the awakened body, speech, and mind of the guru and buddhas of the three times is the inexhaustible ornamental wheel that matures and liberates sentient beings.
phrin las phun sum tshogs par rtogs/ / bla ma dam pa de nyid kyi/ / rnam par thar pa gang la yang / / dag pa'i snang ba ma gtogs pa/ /
Realize this as the excellent awakened activity. No matter what, hold only a pure view of that holy guru and the guru’s life story,

log rtog skad cig skye mi 'gyur/ / bla ma chos skur ma rtogs tshe/ / sgrub pa mchog la 'bad par gyis/ / de yi yon tan rdzogs par 'char/ / rnam thar mthar thug mos gus yin/ / dag snang skyed cig bu slob kun/ / ces gsungs so/ /

without an instant of wrong view. Until you realize the guru as dharmakāya, make an effort in excellent practice. [The guru’s] perfect qualities will arise; this is the ultimate devotion to the liberated life. Develop pure view, all you students of mine.
sems 'chi med du ston pa'i rdo rje'i gsung ni/ /
“The Vajra Song That Reveals Immortal Mind”:
rang grol bde chen 'dus ma byas/ / d+harma si haM'i zhabs la 'dud/ / rnam smin lus la 'od gsal dang / / lha sku 'dres pa'i sems de la/ / na rgyu 'chi rgyu med par rtogs/ /

Naturally free unconditioned great bliss; I bow at the feet of Dharmasiṃha.[39] In the fully ripened body, the mind that blends lucid clarity with the deity’s form knows no cause for sickness or death.
'khor 'das spang blang rang grol lo/ / de ltar skad cig tsam shes shing / / dbugs chad dus su gnad gcod sogs/ / sdug bsngal thams cad rang dag nas/ / 'od gsal lha sku dang 'dres te/ /

Rejecting or accepting samsara and nirvana is freed. If you know that for even an instant, then when the breath stops, all the suffering of transition and so forth will be self-purified and lucid clarity will merge with the deity’s form.
skye shi med cing dgag sgrub med/ / rtogs bya rtogs byed thams cad bral/ / bsgom bya sgom byed rang grol te/ /
There is neither birth nor death, neither cessation nor existence. Freed of something realized or a realizer, meditation and meditator are self-liberated.
gzugs sku gnyis kyis ji srid du/ / 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho ma stongs par/ / de srid gzhan don lhun grub ni/ / (513) rgyun chad med par 'byung bar 'gyur/ /
The two form kāyas will last until the ocean of cyclic existence dries up, spontaneously accomplishing others’ welfare, {513} appearing constantly without interruption.
lo zla tsam gyis 'tshang rgya ba'i/ / gdams pa bla ma skyer sgang pa'i/ / drin gyis ji lta ba bzhin rtogs/ /
These instructions lead to awakening in a matter of years or months. By the grace of Guru Kyergangpa, I realized them for what they were.
tshe 'di blos btang rnal 'byor gyis/ / zhag bdun bsgoms pas grol bar 'gyur/ /
The yogin who renounces this life will be liberated by a week’s meditation.

rang sems 'chi med rang grol rje btsun d+harma pra dz+nyAs mdzad pa rdzogs so/ / dpal ldan skyer sgang pa la gser zho bcu/ / ber thul gcig phul nas zhus te nyams su myong bar byas so/ / bla ma gsum gyis mdzad pa'i rang sems 'chi med rang grol gyi man ngag zab mo yang dag pa / ! /

“The Natural Liberation of One’s Mind as Immortal” by Venerable Dharmaprajña is complete. I offered the glorious Kyergangpa ten measures (zho) of gold and one fur cloak to request it, and I have brought it into my own experience. Three gurus have composed authentic profound esoteric instructions on the Natural Liberation of One’s Mind as Immortal. ithi
Drogön Sangye Tönpa TSöndru Senge

rdo rje 'chang nas rim par byon pa'i brgyud pa rin chen bdun pa chig brgyud rdo rje'i rgya bkrol pa por ye shes mkha' 'gros lung bstan pa brnyes shing / lha dang bcas pa'i 'jig rten kun na yongs su khyab pa'i phrin las can 'gro mgon sangs rgyas ston pa brtson 'grus seng ges rang gis rang la brtson 'grus bskul ba'i lcag btab pa ni/

He was prophesied by the Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness as the one who would break the vajra seal of the single lineage of the succession of Seven Jewels that began with Vajradhara. He performed awakened activity throughout all worlds, including that of the gods: Drogön Sangye Tönpa Tsöndru Senge. Here he applies the whip of encouragement for diligence to himself.
byin rlabs thugs rje'i bdag nyid can/ / bla ma sangs rgyas zhabs la 'dud/ / brtson 'grus chung la the tshom che/ / lus sems gnyis la gros shig 'debs/ /
I bow at the feet of the Guru Buddha, the epitome of blessings and compassion. I have little diligence and great doubt; I give this advice to my body and mind.
tshe thung gi bya bzhag zin med la/ / yengs pa med pa mthong tsam na/ / gtan gyi so nam sgom sgrub la/ / yengs nas 'dug go sgom chen pa/ /
If you just see, without wandering off, that you made endless plans for this short life, instead you’ll practice meditation for a safe harvest. Wander into that, great meditator!
bla ma'i byin rlabs sprin phung la/ / mos gus kyis thugs rje ma bskul na/ / nyams rtogs kyi char rgyun mi 'bab pas/ / gsol ba thob cig rnal 'byor pa/ /
If you don’t evoke the compassion with devotion from the clouds of the guru’s blessings, the rain of experiential realization won’t fall. Supplicate the guru, yogin!
yi dam dngos grub sprin phung la/ / bsnyen sgrub kyis thugs rje ma bskul na/ / mchog thun mong gi dngos grub mi 'bab pas/ / bsgom bzlas la 'bungs shig rnal 'byor pa/ /

If you don’t evoke the compassion with approach and attainment from the yidam’s clouds of spiritual powers, the supreme and common powers won’t fall. Apply yourself to meditation and recitation, yogin!
chos skyong phrin las kyis sprin phung la/ / gtor tshogs kyi thugs rje ma bskul na/ / phrin las kyi char rgyun mi 'bab pas/ / gtor tshogs 'bungs shig rnal 'byor pa/ / (514)
gsol 'debs bskyed rdzogs nyams len tshe/ / rnam rtog dbang du ma shor bar/ / thob 'dod re ba spangs byas nas/ / yengs med sgoms shig rnal 'byor pa/ /
When practicing supplication, creation, and completion, don’t fall under the influence of discursive thought; give up hopes and desires for attainment and meditate without distraction, yogin!
gzhan don rtsa ba snying rje yin/ / rang bde ma bsam gzhan bde soms/ / sems can blos spang ma byed par/ / phan sems skyed cig rnal 'byor pa/ / zhes gsungs so/ /
The root of others’ welfare is compassion. Don’t think of your own happiness but that of others. Don’t abandon sentient beings in your mind. Develop a helpful attitude, yogin!
bu slob dad ldan rnams la gdams pa dgos pa bcu gnyis kyi rdo rje'i mgur ni/
“The Vajra Song of Instruction in Twelve Necessities for Faithful Disciples”:
rje bla ma rnams la phyag 'tshal lo/ / dgos bka' drin can la gsol ba 'debs/ / de la gong ma'i bstod pa mdzod/ / 'di la dar cig gsan par zhu/ /
Homage to all the lord gurus. I supplicate the kind one, whom I need. I honor those that went before. Please listen to me for a moment.
skye 'chis 'jigs pa'i dad pa la/ / brgyud par ldan pa'i bla ma dgos/ / the tshom med pa'i gdams ngag la/ / yengs pa med pa'i brtson 'grus dgos/ /
Faithful ones who fear birth and death need a guru possessed of lineage. For instructions that are beyond doubt, you need unwavering diligence.
tshe thung bsdad long med pa la/ / blo sna rtsab rtsub med pa dgos/ / dben pa'i ri khrod 'grim pa la/ / rgyun du bsring ba'i sdug bsran dgos/ /
For this short life without leisure, you need unhurried attention. To remain in isolated mountain retreat, you need ever-prolonging patience with hardship.
cir snang bsgom du 'char ba la/ / gser 'gyur rtsi yi gdams ngag dgos/ / spyod pa ma bcos rang byung la/ / chos brgyad rang sar grol ba dgos/ /
For anything to arise as meditation, you need instruction in alchemy. For self-occurring uncontrived conduct, you need the eight concerns freed on their own.
'bras bu rang shar lhun grub la/ / re dogs rang sar grol ba dgos/ / tshe gcig sangs rgyas bsgrub pa la/ / mos gus rgyun chad med pa dgos/ /
For a spontaneous self-arising result, you need hope and fear freed on its own. To accomplish awakening in one lifetime, you need unceasing devotion.
bla ma chos skur mthong ba la/ / log lta rang sar grol ba dgos/ / gzhan snang thul ba'i 'gro don la/ / tshad med snying rje chen po dgos/ /
To see the guru as dharmakāya, you need wrong view freed on its own. To help migrators by taming their minds, you need immeasurable great compassion.
dgos pa bcu gnyis dbyangs chung 'di/ / sgrub pa byed pa'i mthun rkyen yin/ / ces gsungs so/ /
This little song of twelve necessities is a harmonious condition for practice.[40]
'gro mgon sangs rgyas ston pa shar phyogs sangs rgyas kyis zhing me tog bkram par gshegs pa'i tshul ston par bzhed pa'i tshe slob ma rnams la zhal gdams snying por dril nas gsungs pa/

When Drogön Sangye Tönpa was intending to demonstrate his departure for the eastern buddha field of Avakīrṇakusuma, he spoke this verse, which captures the essence of his oral instructions, to his disciples:
bla ma yi dam mkha' 'gro chos skyong gis/ / tshad med thugs rjes bu bzhin skyong bar mdzod/ / (515) dad gus ldan pa dbus gtsang khams gsum gyi/ / grwa pa rnams kyis nyams len 'di bzhin mdzod/ /

Guru, yidam, ḍākinīs, and dharma protectors, protect me as your child with boundless compassion. {515} The faithful of three places—U, Tsang, and Kham— and all monks should practice according to this.
zin med 'jig rten bya ba blo yis thongs/ / mgu ba med pa'i sems 'dzin gdung sems skyungs/ / dge sbyor dus 'da' long gtam 'dzad med shol/ / snga phyi'i rjes bsnyag re dogs rtog pa spongs/ /

Mentally forsake these endless worldly deeds. Discard your focused fixation on those you can’t please. Spend your time in virtue and defer inexhaustible conversation. Spurn thoughts of hope and fear that strive after past and future.
tshe la long med tha snyad thug pa med/ / ri dwags smig sgyus mi ngoms bdud rtsi 'thung / / rang don ma grub gzhan don mi 'byung bas/ / thog mar rang don sgrub pa rtse gcig gyis/ /

There’s no leisure in life; sophistry is pointless. Deer are not quenched by a mirage—drink elixir! Your own purpose not achieved, you can’t help others. At first, give undivided attention to your own purpose.
skye ba 'di phyi'i gzhan don lhun grub kyis/ / 'gro ba kun la tshad med snying rje bskyed/ / rang 'dod 'khri sems skad cig med pa yis/ / ci byed sems can don du sems bskyed bya/ /

Spontaneous welfare of others in this and future lives occurs through immeasurable compassion for migrators. Without a moment of entanglement in your own desires, arouse the spirit of helping beings in whatever you do.
'chi ba mi rtag rgyun chad med par soms/ / cis kyang dgos med tshe 'di blos thongs 'gyur/ / don gnyis lo zlas 'grub kyis rang lus 'di/ / snang stong zhen bral lha sku 'bral med sgoms/ /
nyams rtogs rtsol med 'char gyis bla ma la/ / gdung shugs ldan pas 'bral med gsol ba thob/ / 'di dang 'chi ka bar do phyi ma'i tshe/ / bar chad bsrung phyir mkha' 'gro chos skyong bsten/ /

With the unsought arising of experience and realization, constantly pray to the guru with intense longing. Rely on ḍākinīs and dharma protectors to guard against obstacles in this life, at death, in the intermediate state, and in the next life.
rang sems phyir gyur sangs rgyas sems can med/ / ci phyir ci snang sems su shes par gyis/ / sems 'di snang stong lha sku sgyu ma ste/ / sgyu 'dzin bral ba 'od gsal phyag rgya che/ /

Outside of your mind there are no buddhas or beings; therefore know whatever appears as your own mind. This mind, the empty appearance of the deity’s illusory form, not fixated on illusion, is Lucid Clarity Mahāmudrā.
dgag sgrub skye 'chi yod med blo las 'das/ / sgom med yid la byar med 'khor 'das bral/ / las dang las rnams smin cing rang sar grol/ / gnyis 'dzin bral ba zung 'jug chen por ltos/ /

Beyond ideas of denying or affirming, birth or death, being or not being; without meditation or mental engagement, samsara and nirvana are freed. Karma and karmic ripening are released in their own ground. Free of dualistic clinging, look at great integral unity.
e ma ma bcos tha mal shes pa 'di/ / kun la yod kyang ma shes drin gyi rtogs/ / da ni 'dri bar mi bya thag chod nges shes skyes/ / lhun grub rnam gsum dbyer med mngon gyur to/ / zhes gsungs so/ /

Ema! Everyone has this uncontrived ordinary mind without knowing it; realize it through [the guru’s] kindness. Now don’t question; be decisive and develop certitude. Actualize the inseparable threefold spontaneous presence.[41]
sems (516) 'chi med kyi zhal gdams gnang ba ni/
He gave oral instructions on immortal mind: {516}
rgyal ba dus gsum sangs rgyas kyi/ / 'chi med ye shes khyod la 'dud/ / sems bskyed bla ma'i rnal 'byor dang / / ldan pas gsol ba btab byas nas/ / rang lus snang stong lha sku sems/ /

I bow to the immortal timeless awareness of all victorious buddhas of the three times. Supplicate while endowed with awakening mind and the practice of guru yoga, then think of your own body as the empty appearance of the deity’s form.
sems dang lha sku dbyer med pa'i/ / ngo bo stong nyid sangs rgyas kyis/ / ma gzigs mi gzigs gzigs mi 'gyur/ / de la na rgyu 'chi rgyu dang / / 'khor ba myang 'das dgag sgrub bral/ /

Mind and the deity’s form are inseparable: an empty essence that even buddhas do not see, did not see, and will not see. In that there is no cause of sickness or death, no rejecting and accepting of samsara and nirvana.
de don skad cig rtogs pa'am/ / dran thos rig par gyur pa de/ / mtshams sbyor ngan zhing dran nyams kyang / / gnad gcod sdug bsngal rang dag nas/ /
If you get that meaning for even an instant, or recall, hear, or become aware of it, even during a bad transition where mindfulness falters, the end-of-life suffering will be self-purified.
bar do dang po 'od gsal dang / / longs sku dbyer med sprul sku yi/ / gzhan don lhun grub rgyun chad med/ / rgyal ba'i dgongs pa 'chi med 'di/ / slob ma mchog gi don du bkod/ /

Then, in the first intermediate state, lucid clarity inseparable from saṃbhogakāya and nirmāṇakāya will always be spontaneously present for others’ welfare. This teaching on immortality, the Victor’s intent, was arranged for the sake of my excellent students.
dge des mkha' mnyam sems can rnams/ / 'chi med ye shes don rtogs shog /
By that virtue, may sentient beings throughout space realize the meaning of immortal timeless awareness.

rang sems 'chi med rang grol rje btsun bIr+Ya sing has/ / bu dam pa slob ma yang rab kyi don du yi ger bkod pa 'di rdzogs so/ / nas khal lnga brgya/ gser zho bdun/ mdzo gcig / mon ras kyi na bza' phrugs gcig phul nas zhus te nyams su blangs bar byas so/ ! /

“The Natural Liberation of One’s Mind as Immortal” that was written down by Venerable Vīryasiṃha (Tsöndru Senge) for the sake of the most excellent students, the spiritual heirs, is complete. I offered five bags of barley, seven measures of gold, one hybrid yak, and a bolt of fine fabric from Mön to request it, and I have brought it into my own experience.
Khedrup Tsangma Shangtön

mkhas grub gtsang ma shangs ston ces 'jig rten gsum na snyan par grags shing mthong thos dran reg thams cad rnam par grol ba'i dpal la sbyor bar mdzad pa de nyid kyis/ mkhas btsun 'jag chen rgyal mtshan 'bum la zhal gdams su stsal ba ni/

The one known as Khedrup Tsangma Shantön was famous throughout the three worlds. He gained the glorious state of one who brings total liberation to anyone when they see, hear, recall, or touch him. He granted these instructions to Khetsun Jakchen Gyaltsen Bum:
nyes skyon ma gos ye shes ldan/ / mthong thos dran pas sdug bsngal sel/ / rang sems chos skur ngo sprod pa'i/ / bla ma rje la phyag 'tshal lo/ /
Homage to the lord guru, wise one, unsullied by imperfections, you dispelled suffering by seeing, hearing, or recalling, and introduced my mind as dharmakāya.
sems can don kun bsgrub pa'i phyir/ / sangs rgyas thob par 'dod pa yis/ / dge ba'i tshogs rnams bsags (517) byas te/ / byang chub mchog tu sems bskyed bgyi/ /
In order to achieve all welfare for sentient beings with the desire to attain buddhahood, one must accumulate all the collections of virtue {517} and arouse the supreme mind of awakening.
rtag 'dzin 'du shes ldog pa dang / / dge la brtson pas 'jug pa dang / / chags sdang blo dang bral ba'i phyir/ / 'chi ba mi rtag yang yang bsgom/ /
In order to reverse the belief in permanence, to enter into virtue with diligence, and be rid of mental attachment and aversion, meditate again and again on death and impermanence.
bzod med 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal bsam/ / bde dang sdug bsngal 'byung ba'i rgyu/ / dge sdig gnyis la blang dor bya/ / 'bras bu mi bslu 'byung bar 'gyur/ /

Contemplate the unbearable suffering of cyclic existence and the causes that produce happiness and suffering. Make the right choices between virtue and nonvirtue. The corresponding results will inevitably arise.
tha mal lus zhen zlog pa'i thabs/ / snang la rang bzhin med pa yi/ / lha sku gsal la rtog med bsgom/ / rgyal ba longs sku rang shar 'byung / /

The way to reverse clinging to the ordinary body is to meditate without concept on the clarity of the deity’s form, which appears and yet has no intrinsic nature. The victors’ saṃbhogakāya will arise naturally.
dngos grub ma lus ster ba'i dpal/ / 'jigs pa kun las skyobs pa'i mgon/ / dpal mgon bla ma dam pa la/ / 'bral ba med par mos gus bya/ / rgyun chad med par gsol ba gdab/ /
The glory that bestows every spiritual power is the protector who gives refuge from all fears. Cultivate constant devotion and always supplicate the glorious protector and holy guru.
cir snang rmi lam sgyu mar bsgom/ / dad 'dun gnyis kyis lam khyer bya/ / chags sdang rang sar grol nas mchi/ / zhen med sgyu ma rang shar 'byung / /

Meditate on whatever appears as dream and illusion. Integrate that through both faith and intention. Once anger and aversion are liberated in their own ground, the illusory nature will arise naturally without attachment.
sgyu 'dzin blo dang bral ba'i phyir/ / ma bcos gnyug ma'i ngang la bzhag / gzung 'dzin rtog pa rang sar grol/ / gsal stong 'dzin med rang shar 'byung / /

In order to free yourself from clinging to illusion, rest in the uncontrived native state. Dualistic concepts will be liberated in their own ground. Empty clarity without fixation will arise by itself.
shes bya gshis kyi gnas lugs la/ / skyon dang yon tan med pa'i phyir/ / de nyid rtogs pa'i rnal 'byor pas/ / blang dor med pa'i don la spyod/ /
The abiding nature of the knowable is without faults or qualities. So the yogin who realizes that engages its meaning without accepting or rejecting.
snang ba rten cing 'brel 'byung 'di/ / skye med yum gyi ngang du rdzogs/ / gsal stong 'dzin med bde bar shar/ / 'bras bu sku bzhi lhun gyis grub/ /
These appearances of interdependent origin are complete within the unborn Mother. Clear empty bliss without fixation arises; the resulting four kāyas are spontaneously present.
de las byung ba'i dge ba des/ / 'gro ba kun dang thun mong du/ / dmigs med byang chub chen por bsngo/ / theg chen chos kyi khyad chos yin/ /
I dedicate the virtue arising from this to the great unconditioned awakening of all migrators in common. That is the special feature of Mahayana.
bla ma shangs ston rin po ches/ /slob dpon rgyal mtshan 'bum la gsungs pa rdzogs so/ ! /
That completes the teaching that Lama Shangtön Rinpoche gave to Master Gyaltsen Bum.
Tangtong Gyalpo

ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro ni gu mas mngon sum du rjes su bzung (518) ba'i 'gran zla dang bral ba'i grub thob chen po shangs chos nye brgyud kyi bka' babs thang stong rgyal po gtsang rgyas sde thang na gsang spyod la bzhugs pa'i skabs ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro ma sde lngas phrin las ci bzhed sgrub par zhal gyis 'chas shing don dang mthun pa'i mtshan gsol ba ni/ /

He was nurtured in person by Niguma, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness. {518} He became an unrivaled great adept and received the transmission of the direct lineage of Shangpa teachings. One time when Tangtong Gyalpo was engaging in the secret conduct on the Gyede Plain in Tsang, five awareness ḍākinīs promised to accomplish whatever actions he requested and bestowed [these five] names of suitable meaning on him:
rgyas sde thang na bzhugs pa yi/ / ya mtshan che ba'i mi 'di la/ / 'dir 'tshogs bu mo rnam lnga yis/ / don dang mthun pa'i ming re 'dogs/ /
We five girls gathered here will each give a suitable name to this most incredible man staying on the Gyede Plain.
khyab gdal chen po'i thang chen na/ / stong nyid rtogs pa'i rnal 'byor pa/ / 'jigs med rgyal po lta bur bzhugs/ / de phyir thang stong rgyal por thogs/ /
On the great plain of the vast expanse, the yogin who has realized emptiness dwells without fear like a king. Therefore I name you Tangtong Gyalpo, King of the Empty Plain.
mnyam nyid spros bral lung pa na/ / snang stong dbyer med lta ba can/ / spang blang bral ba'i smyon pa la/ / lung stong smyon pa zhes su thogs/ /
In the valley of unembellished equanimity, with the view of appearance-emptiness inseparable, is a madman free of accepting and rejecting. I name you Madman of the Empty Valley.
ro brgya ldan pa'i zas skom dang / / mi gtsang ngan skyugs gang byung la/ / phan gnod bral ba'i bcud len mkhan/ / zas rnams bcud len mkhan du thogs/ /
Food and drink of a hundred flavors or bad nauseating filth—whichever comes up, you extract the nutriment without benefit or harm. I name you Extractor of Food’s Nutriment.
sna tshogs rkyen rnams gang byung yang / / rmi lam brag cha ltar rtogs nas/ / chos brgyad zil gnon ro snyoms pa/ / rkyen rnams ro snyoms mkhan du thogs/ /
Whatever different conditions arise, you realize them as like dreams or echoes with equal taste that overwhelms the eight concerns. I name you One Who Tastes All Conditions as Equal.
'khor 'das chos rnams thams cad kun/ / snang yang chu nang zla ba ltar/ / rkyags gtad med par rab mkhyen pa'i/ / chos rnams rgyags gtad med par thogs/ /
All phenomena of samsara and nirvana appear and yet they are like water moons; you fully understand them without offense. I name you All Things Without Offense.
'gran zla bral ba'i rnal 'byor pa/ / tshad med phrin las rgyas bya'i phyir/ / bde ba'i thang la 'gro ba rnams/ / da lta 'dren pa'i dus la babs/ / zhes ched du brjod do/ /
Yogin beyond compare, to spread your immeasurable activities now is the time to lead all migrators onto the plain of happiness.[42]
rje de nyid kyis mkhas btsun pad legs pa la rang grol phyag rgya chen po'i zhal gdams rdo rje'i dbyangs su bsnyad pa ni/
The lord himself related this vajra melody of oral instructions on Naturally Free Mahāmudrā to Khetsun Delek Pal:[43]
bu nyon dang mkhas btsun bde legs dpal/ / sngar yang gti mug mun pas 'gribs/ / chos bya snyam ngang la chos brgyad 'dres/ /
Listen son, learned monk Delek Pal. Previously obscured by thick stupidity, your thoughts to practice dharma were mixed with the eight worldly concerns. {519}
phyi ma'i 'dun (519) ma sgrub pa la/ / lag len bsam pa 'di tsho 'tshal/ / tshe 'di'i 'dun ma lings kyis bskyur/ / chos brgyad zhen pa cham gyis thongs/ /
To accomplish your aims in future lives, please consider these ideas for practice. Totally cast out your aims for this life. Utterly discard clinging to eight concerns.
sems 'dzin ngo bsrung cham gyis grol/ / nye ring 'brel thag rbad kyis chod/ / bdag 'dzin srid pa'i phur pa thon/ / re dogs bsam pa lhod kyis glod/ /
Thoroughly release fixation and face-saving. Decisively sever ties to those close and distant. Extract the stake of existence: self-fixation. Relax thoughts of hope and fear.
lto gos gnyis kyi 'khri ba chod/ / che 'dod ma byed dman sa zung / / nges 'byung sdug bsngal dang du longs/ / chags sdang 'gran sems rgyangs la dor/ /
Cut off cravings for food and clothing. Don’t desire status; keep a low profile. Take on the sufferings of renunciation. Throw attachment, aversion, and rivalry far away.
g.yo sgyu bsam ngan yul nas thon/ / za 'dod tshul 'chos rang sar zhog / sdom gsum dam tshig drang por srungs/ / nga rgyal rlom sems khong khro thon/ /
Banish evil thoughts of deceit and deception, and leave hypocritical extortion alone. Honestly keep the three vows and sacred pledges. Expel pride, conceit, and anger.
kun gyis brnyas kyang bzod pa sgoms/ / tha mal dgra rgod yan par thon/ / zhe sdang rang rgyud nang du thul/ / gsog 'jog ser sna'i bsam pa spongs/ /
Cultivate patience, though all despise you. Let loose the ordinary wild enemies and tame the anger within yourself. Reject thoughts of miserly hoarding.
byams sems snying rje rgyud la rten/ / lha chos mi chos thams cad la/ / rang gi sems 'di dpang du tshugs/ /
Rely on love and compassion in your being. Establish your own mind as witness in the dharma of gods and of humans.[44]
da len 'dun ma ma bsgrub na/ / phyis nas re yang re thag chad/ / gnyug ma'i ngang du lhod kyis glod/ / 'khrul pa'i gzhi rtsa rtsad nas chod/ /
If you don’t achieve your aims this time, you’ll hope for next time, but hope will be gone. Relax within the native state. Cut the taproot of delusion.
yengs med rang gi sems la ltos/ / brjod med dran pa tsir gyis zungs/ / rang ngo rang gis ma shes na/ / sdug bcir byas kyang nyon re mongs/ /
Look unwaveringly at your own mind. Firmly seize mindfulness that never forgets. If you don’t know your own face, you can try relentlessly but remain afflicted.
gnyid dus 'od gsal ma zin na/ / sems ngo 'phrod kyang don re chung / / bar dor 'od gsal ma zin na/ / gnad gcod sdug bsngal sha re g.ya'/ /

If you don’t grasp lucid clarity at sleep, your introduction to mind was not very useful. If you don’t grasp lucid clarity in the intermediate state, you’ll tremble with the suffering of life’s interruption.
rang sems rang dbang ma thob na/ / bskal par bsgom kyang thang re chad/ / rnam rtog snga ma 'gags pa'i rjes/ / phyi ma ma skyes had de ba/ /
If you don’t gain control over your own mind, an eon of meditation will just wear you out. Right after one thought ceases, before the next one arises, there’s a gap.
gsal la rtog pa med pa'i ngang / / rten med gzhi rtsa bral ba yi/ / da lta'i shes pa so ma 'di/ / rang sems chos sku spros bral yin/ / (520)
Within the state of clarity without concept, without support, free of basis and root, this fresh awareness of the present moment is your mind of unembellished dharmakāya. {520}
cir snang thams cad rang gi sems/ / rang sems spros bral chos kyi sku/ / des na rnam rtog chos sku'i rtsal/ / snang ba mi 'gegs stong par grub/ /
Whatever arises is all your own mind, and your mind is unembellished dharmakāya. So thoughts are dharmakāya’s dynamic energy, unceasing appearance established as empty.
gang skyes gang shar dran pas zung / / lhod kyis glod pa chem gyis thongs/ / rang ngo shes na yang yang mthud/ / ma bcos ma yengs rang sar zhog /
Hold whatever arises and appears with mindfulness, relax utterly, and let go. If you recognize yourself, prolong this again and again. Uncontrived and undistracted, leave everything alone.
'gro 'ong skye 'gag gnas gsum bral/ / 'di ni phyag rgya chen po yin/ / yengs med lam du khyer ba gces/ / rtsol med lhug par skyong ba gces/ /
Free of going and coming, or from arising, ceasing, and remaining: this is mahāmudrā. It’s crucial to integrate this without wavering. It’s crucial to maintain it effortlessly.

de ltar nyams su longs pa gyis/ / nga phyogs med rgyal khams bskor ba yin/ / zhen pa bral ba'i rnal 'byor dang / / gling bzhi bskor ba'i nyi ma gnyis/ / sos dal sdod long med do ang / / zhes gsungs so/ /
Practice like that. I wander aimlessly through the country. Both the yogin free of attachment and the sun that circles the continents move slowly with no time to linger.
sems 'chi med rang grol gyi rdo rje'i mgur/ /
“The Vajra Song of the Natural Liberation of One’s Mind as Immortal”:
rje btsun bla ma sangs rgyas la/ / sgo gsum gus pas gsol ba 'debs/ / 'chi ba ltar snang rnam rtog 'di/ / rang bzhin ma grub gnyug ma'i 'gros/ /
Venerable Guru Buddha, I respectfully supplicate with body, speech, and mind. This idea of death is but a semblance and has no intrinsic nature in its native mode.
'chi bar btags pa'i lus dang sems/ / 'chi med rang grol phyag rgya che/ / rnam smin bem po 'chi ba med/ / bag chags rmi lam ji ltar 'chi/ /
Body and mind designated as mortal are immortal; naturally liberated mahāmudrā. The fully ripened physical body is deathless, for how can the habitual dream body die?

sems nyid rang gdangs lha yi sku/ / gsal stong 'dzin med chu zla 'dra/ / gshis lugs stong pa spros bral la/ / na ba med cing 'chi ba med/ / myang 'das med cing 'khor ba med/ / thams cad rang sems 'khrul pa'i rtsal/ /

Mind’s natural radiance is the deity’s form, empty clarity without fixation like a water moon. The basic condition is empty and unembellished, without sickness and without death, without nirvana and without samsara: all of it is the deluded energy of one’s own mind.
rtsal snang gsal la 'gags pa med/ / 'gags med skye med dbyings su thim/ / skye 'gag gnas gsum bral ba yi/ / 'chi med ye shes ngo mtshar che/ /
The clarity of that energy’s display is unceasing; the unhindered unborn dissolves into basic space. Without arising, ceasing, or remaining, this wisdom of immortality is amazing!

myong ba 'dzin med ngang du bzhag / spyod lam kun dang bsres la bsgom/ / de ltar yun ring sus goms pa/ / 'chi ba chos sku'i dbyings su thim/ / bar do rgyal ba longs sku 'grub/ / sprul pas 'gro ba 'dren par (521) byed/ / skal ldan rnams kyis nyams su longs/ /

Rest within experience without fixation. Meditate by blending it with all activity. Whoever becomes accustomed to that will dissolve into dharmakāya space at death, achieve the victors’ saṃbhogakāya in the intermediate state, and guide migrators with emanations. {521} Take this into experience, fortunate ones.
rje grub thob chen po'i 'chi med rang grol rdo rje'i gsung / !
Venerable Great Adept spoke these vajra words on the Natural Liberation of One’s Mind as Immortal. ithi
Kunga Drolchok

ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro ni gu mas rjes su bzung bas shin tu nye brgyud kyi bka' babs 'jam mgon grub pa'i dpa' bo dpal ldan kun dga' grol mchog blo gsal rgya mtsho'i sde'i zhal snga nas stsal ba'i ni gu'i rgyab chos glu'i phreng ba las/ / chos kyi khungs dang 'brel par brjod pa'i rdo rje'i mgur/ /

Niguma, Ḍākinī of Timeless Awareness, nurtured him with the transmission of a very direct lineage. Glorious Kunga Drolchok Losal Gyatsoi De was a gentle protector and heroic adept. From his garland of songs spoken in support of Niguma’s teachings, these are vajra songs that express the connection with that dharma source.
shrI badzra d+ha ra sA d+hu pA da pra Na myaM/
śrī vajradhara sādhu pāda prāṇamayaṃ
rje bka' brgyud kyi dgung gnam mthon po la/ / pha grub thob kyi bla ma rgyu skar tsam/ / dbyings 'gags med kyi nyi zla 'od po che/ / de nA ro dang ni gu ma lags sam/ /
At the zenith of the noble Kagyu’s midnight sky, the adept gurus are as plentiful as the stars. The brightest sun and moon unhindered by space must surely be Nāropa and Niguma.
khong lcam sring gi sgrub brgyud chu bo'i rgyun/ / dus da lta'i skal ldan yongs kyi skom/ / yid tshim pa ster ba'i sman chab de/ / chos nA ro dang ni gu ma lags sam/ /
The river flow of practice lineages from those siblings fully refreshes the fortunate ones even now. That quenching gift of curative waters is surely the teachings of Nāropa and Niguma.
lugs rnam gnyis kyi bka' srol skyong ba'i rje/ / dpal 'gran zla bral ba sprul pa'i sku/ / nged rtogs ldan mang po'i gtsug rgyan gcig / mgon dwags shangs kyi bka' brgyud rnam gnyis lags/ /
The lord protectors of those two traditions were glorious unrivaled emanated bodies, single crown jewels of our many realized ones in the two Kagyu lineages of Dakpo and Shangpa.
sngon te l+li dang nA ros sna drangs nas/ / mar pa dang mi las rjes bskyangs te/ / gnad zab mo nA ro chos drug la/ / rtags mngon gyur grub thob grangs las 'das/ /
Formerly led by Tilo and Nāro, later preserved by Marpa and Mila, the profound vital teaching of Nāro’s Six Dharmas produced innumerable adepts with signs of success.
dus deng sang tshong dus 'o ma'i dpe/ / tshig ma nges smyon pa'i bla bcol bzhin/ / don mi 'dra rang blo'i lam 'dren pas/ / mi kho bo'i sems rtsa cung ma tshim/ /

These days, as in the case of [watered-down] market milk, the words are uncertain, like the babble of a lunatic, random meanings led by personal ideas, that left this man’s mind somewhat dissatisfied.
lcam mkha' 'gro'i gsang tshig snying po'i bcud/ / tshig ma bcos thems yig rdo rje'i mdud/ / don snying la 'bab pa dngos po'i gshis/ / sprang yid bde'i thar lam gsos su shar/ /

Sister Ḍākinī’s secret words of innermost potency were uncorrupted in The Inventory, [sealed by] a vajra knot. The meaning, the true nature of reality, fell into my heart and gladdened my lowly mind, reviving the path to liberation.
ming rjes 'brang ba'i blo yod na/ / sdug btsir la sgom du mi 'dzin zhing / / khong yus la sgrub par mi 'jog pa'i/ / gu yangs kyi snying gtam (522) glu ru len/ /
If you have a mind to follow me, don’t think your painful tension is meditation. Don’t present your accomplishments for show. I put this carefree heartfelt advice to song. {522}
dngos grub kyi rtsa ba bla ma skad/ / bla ma de sangs rgyas dngos byon skad/ / ci mdzad legs par blta dgos skad/ / mdzes mdzes su smras kyang sgra skad lags/ /
They say the root of spiritual powers is the guru. They say the guru is the actual Buddha. They say one must regard the guru’s acts as good. They say beautiful things, but it’s just noise.
dngos grub la thob rung ma thob rung / / sangs rgyas dang sems can ci yin rung / / mdzad pa la legs nyes ci ston rung / / mi nga la snyems 'phrigs rdul tsam med/ /
Whether or not I attain spiritual powers, whether [the guru] is a buddha or sentient being, whether good or bad deeds are displayed, I personally have not an iota of egotistical doubt.
ya ki shed 'og min pho brang na/ / chos sku la rdo rje 'chang chen ces/ / mthing ka la 'od zer lham me ba/ / sems blo chung gi 'dren pa ya re cha/ /
In the upper region, in the Akaniṣṭha palace, dharmakāya is so-called Great Vajradhara, deep blue in an effulgence of light rays. This draws in the small-minded—how incredible!
ma gi shed shangs phu'i rmog lcog gi / pho brang de spang po'i spyil bu na/ / mi gzugs la zhu bde'i 'od 'bar ba/ / rgya sgom rdo rje 'chang chen de na bzhugs/ /
In the lower region, in Mokchok of Shangpu, inside the palace of a renunciant’s thatched hut, a human form blazes with light of melting bliss: Great Vajradhara Gyagom dwells there.
khyod gdod ma'i gzhi la dbyer med kyang / / 'phral sbas pa'i brtul zhugs sgrib g.yogs mkhan/ / mi skal ldan gyis cer mthong ma lags sam/ / bum nang gi mar me ji bzhin snang / /
You are inseparable from the primordial ground, temporarily clothed as a hidden one of deliberate conduct. But don’t the fortunate see you clearly as a lamp shining within a vase?
bdag snga ma'i las 'phro mi dman pas/ / chung chung nas sgyu ma'i rang rtsal rdzogs/ / ma mkha' 'gro'i zhal bzang mthong na yang / / sems ma tshims sgyu ma'i rang snang tsam/ /
My past karmic propensity was not meager: I understood illusion’s own dynamic display from youth and I saw Mother Ḍākinī’s sublime face. But I was still unsatisfied; it was just illusion’s guise.
pha legs rgyal zhal bum rnyed tsa na/ / blo khu 'phrigs thams cad rang sar grol/ / yid the tshom spangs pa'i nges shes gcig / dus de tshe 'pho 'gyur med par skyes/ /
When I first discovered the visage of Father Lekgyal,[45] all my mental obsessions freed up by themselves. A single certitude devoid of doubt was born which has not changed since that time.
mnyam bzhag la rjes thob kyi 'dzin pa yal/ / thun mtshams dang thun tshod kyi snang ba brjed/ / 'di yin dang 'di min gyi dgag sgrub zhig / rang gzhan dang phyogs cha'i nye ring stor/ /

Fixation on equipoise and subsequent attainment faded, I forgot the distinction of meditation sessions and breaks, let go of judgment whether “this is it” or “this isn’t it,” and lost the biases of self and other, close and distant.
kun khyab kyi gsal stong 'od po che/ / rang rig me long la shar tsam na/ / tshig tha snyad tshig gi 'byed 'grel de/ / nam dgos dus sleb pa'i spobs pa thob/ /

When the great light of all-pervading empty clarity arose in the mirror of my intrinsic awareness, I gained the confidence that the terms of designations, distinctions, and analyses would show up if needed.
rje mkhyen pa can gcig ma lags pa/ / mi blun po mkhas par ci la gtong / / khyod byin rlabs can gcig ma lags pa/ / skyes grol gyi rang mtshan ci la ston/ / (523)
Lord, if you are not possessed of knowledge, how did you make a stupid fellow like me wise? If you are not the one endowed with blessings, how did I show signs of liberation upon arising? {523}
da dus gsum gyi sangs rgyas byon lags kyang / / zhu dag gi spros pa mi bdog pas/ / blo dran pa rang shar nam mkha' la/ / bya lam rjes med kyi ngang la bzhud/ /
Now, even if the buddhas of the three times arrived, I would have no further issues to resolve. Natural thought, like a bird’s path in the sky, travels freely without leaving a trace.
sgom byas kyang pha yi rang snang tsam/ / res 'jog med pa'i rnal 'byor la/ / sal le dang sing nger 'jog lags pas/ / mthor gtong dang dmar gtong khyod rang shes/ /
Even meditation is just the guru’s natural appearance. It would be well to rest in clarity and openness, and to experience yoga and not sporadic practice. Whether I go high or low, you will know.
gsol 'debs kyi dbyangs rta snyan na yang / / yid gnyis kyi 'phyang mor spyod pas na/ / blo phar bltas na chung 'phyon ma'i glus/ / mi shes ldan snying khong 'dren lags sam/ /
Although supplications may be melodious, if engaged with a hesitant divided mind, in the long run, wouldn’t it just be the song of a prostitute to seduce the clueless?
tshig mu cor smra ba'i ngu lab la/ / gzugs med kyi lha 'dre snying rtsa 'dar/ / pha dran pa'i yus chen rgyang 'bod la/ / khyed dbyings nas thugs rje cis mi g.yo/ /
Nonsensical words that speak indirectly agitate the hearts of formless gods and demons. Fervently recalling the guru and calling from afar; how could your compassion not stir from basic space?
pha bdag dang bdag gir byas pa'i bu/ / yid gcig tu 'dres pa'i spun grogs la/ / re sa dang ltos sa ma mchis pas/ / rje khyed rang gi rnam thar 'khyongs par shog /
I, the father, those who have become my children, and spiritual siblings joined in a single intention have no other place of hope or reliance than you: Lord, please prolong your life of liberation.
mos gus nyag gcig dran pa lam rdzogs kyi bla ma'i rnal 'byor dang rjes su bzung ba'i rgyab chos glur blangs pa /
This was a teaching that supports the guru yoga by means of which one perfects the path through a singular thought of devotion, expressed here in a song. ithi
skyabs zur 'tshol med pa'i rgya sgom la/ / blo rtse gnyis med par skyabs su mchi/ / pha nor ba med pa'i bla ma rje/ / bdag bu gcig pa'i blo sna chos la sgyur/ /
Refuge that I needn’t seek elsewhere, Gyagom, I take refuge in you with mind undivided. Father, unerring lord guru, turn your one child’s mind to dharma.
las 'jig rten pa'i bsam sbyor lhur blangs nas/ / lus btsun btsun byas kyang sems kyis khrel/ / ming chos par btags pa bsnyon dor mkhan/ / 'di thugs rjes gzigs dang bla ma'i gtso/ /
In action, I diligently pursued worldly thoughts, my body disciplined, yet my mind shameful. In name I’m called religious, but I am a hypocrite. This you see with your compassion, my chief guru.
gnas 'khor ba'i rang mtshang go bzhin yang / / sems g.yeng g.yeng dgos med gyi nar spyod/ / yid nem nur ri khrod phyi shol lus/ / 'di blo btang lags sam mkhyen pas gzigs/ /

The place, samsara, though I seem to know its faults, my mind is ever wandering in useless activity. Mentally suspicious, my body is left behind in retreat. This should be abandoned; please see it with wisdom.
gshis thag chod gyong po'i 'dug tshugs la/ / 'phral col chung kun gyi ngo ma yogs/ / rang rang gis bslus pa'i (524) mgo 'khor la/ / yab brtse ba'i spyan chab mi bskrun nam/ /
In character, I am decidedly tough. On the spot, I don’t hide from nonsense. I am betrayed by myself, turning my own head. (524} Father, doesn’t this just stir your tears of love?
chos go rig shes pa'i rdzun sob la/ / yid bde mor sems pa'i col chung po/ / sgom kha ltar song ba'i mdo med la/ / pha thugs kyis brnag pa mi gnang ngam/ /
In dharma, my fiction of knowledge and awareness mentally pleases me with my own childish prattle. Of meditation and the like I take little account. Father, does this not concern you?
las 'char sgo'i blo la zad pa med/ / gshis 'khor ba'i 'dam la chod pa med/ / dus da lta'i yid shes ngos bzung med/ / 'di med lta'i glu dbyangs ring mor gda'/ /
Karma’s impressions in my mind are inexhaustible. My character is not detached from samsara’s swamp. Present-time consciousness has not been recognized. This song of what I’m missing is getting long!
he ban gzugs tho yor mig 'phrul la/ / spyang glen gyi rtog dpyod gtong ba 'khrul/ / btsun tshugs mdzes chos 'ja' snang la/ / zhen rtog gi legs nyes dpyod pa dman/ /

Hey! This piled-stone illusion of a monk’s form, intelligent or stupid—it’s deluded to analyze it. The venerable image of lovely qualities is a rainbow. Fixated concepts analyzing its value are vulgar.
'khor ba ngan skyugs kyi khron pa la/ / dri zhim gyi 'dzin blos reg pas phung / / sems nges med kyi 'char sgo rgya 'byams la/ / yin min gyi so 'phrang 'dzugs pa smyo/ /
Samsara’s pit of nasty vomit is ruinous when touched with the idea that it’s delicious. Mind’s indefinite perceptions are pervasive. To take a tenuous stand on their existence is crazy.
dran pa nyag gcig gi yid shes la/ / chos min gyi bya ra byed pa rtsing / / gang byas sgyu ma'i me long la/ / bden rdzun gyi zhal lces g.yeng ba brdzun/ /

In mindfulness with singular mental consciousness, witnessing [my own] nondharmic [thoughts] was rough. Whatever I’ve done is reflected in illusion’s mirror. By the code of true or false, it was all distraction and deceit.
ci byas thar pa'i so nam la/ / rtog dpyod kyi than pas bsregs pa pham/ / ngas shes pa tsam la ma bzhag ste/ / sgom ming stong du skad cig bzhag pa med/ /
What I’ve done has destroyed the crops of emancipation, scorched by the drought of my conceptual analysis. I understand but will not leave it at that, nor ever leave meditation as an empty word.
da shi yang legs la gson yang rung / / 'dun ma dge mthar phyin pa go/ /
Now if I die it is good; living is also okay. My aim, I know, is to consummate virtue.
zhes dran bskul gyi lcag 'debs thol skyes las brtsams pa'i rgyang glur smras pa /
This long-distance [calling] expressed as song was composed spontaneously as a whip to encourage my vigilance. ithi
dbyings chos sku rtag brtan g.yung drung la/ / mdangs 'gags med kun snang yi ge'i dngos/ / dbyings gzhom med nA da'i rang sgra gcig / yid 'gyu stong a yi ngo bor shar/ /

The expanse of dharmakāya, everlasting svāstika,[46] its radiance, unimpeded appearance, is the actual letter, a vowel, the invincible natural sound of nāda, mind’s empty movement arising in essence as A.
e chos kyi 'byung gnas seng ge'i khrir/ / don stong chen yig lnga'i pho brang na/ / waM bde chen 'od gsal 'dus ma byas/ / nang thig le yig drug 'dus pa'i lha/ /

E becomes the source of phenomena, the lion throne, meaning the great emptiness, the palace of five letters. Vaṃ is great bliss, unconditioned lucid clarity. Within, the vital drops of six letters are the gathered deities.
ming bde gshegs snying por grags pa gcig / yongs sems (525) can kun la khyab pa'i bdag/ / rang rnal 'byor yid bde dam pa'i dpal/ / dus 'gyur ba med pa'i dkyil 'khor las/ /
The name buddha nature is one that is known, {525} the one that completely pervades all sentient beings. I, myself, the yogin, am delighted by this sacred glory. Timeless unchanging mandala produces
chab dag pa bdud rtsi'i char rgyun gyis/ / blo kun rtog gi ri mo bag la nyal/ / las nyon mongs kun 'byung bkrus nas kyang / / sems rang rig rang gsal 'od po che/ /
pristine water, a falling rain of elixir. Mind’s latent patterns of conceptual thought, karma, and afflictions’ origins are cleansed. Mind’s own awareness and clarity is a great radiance.
yid phar bltas chos sku nyag gcig la/ / blo tshur gzhal dran pa'i rgyun lam chad/ / yid had de chad de wal le ba/ / deng yid kyi ri mo yal nas thal/ /
Mentation from afar is the single dharmakāya. Intellect turning back is the end of analytical process. Mentation becomes open, spacious, and vivid.[47] Now the mental patterns fade and vanish.
lus sha khrag dri med gzha' 'dra'i sku/ / ngag smra bsam brjod 'das lkugs pa'i tshul/ / yid bya lam rjes bral nam mkha'i ngang / / don 'char sgo dang po'i ye shes yin/ /

The body of flesh and blood is pure rainbow-like form. Speech is beyond word, thought, and expression; mute. Mind is a state without tracks, like a bird in the sky. The meaning is the arising of original timeless awareness.
gzhi ma rig mun pa'i khang chung brdibs/ / las nyon mongs dri ma'i bag chags gtor/ / ming so so skye bo'i yul las 'das/ / sgom blo 'das chen po'i lam dang mjal/ /

The ground is the collapse of the small dark house of ignorance. Habitual patterns of impure karma and afflictions are expelled. The name ordinary individual is transcended. Meditation is met on the great path beyond intellect.
chos brgyad khri bzhi ston ar bsdus nas/ / lha shAkya mu nes gsungs lags kyang / / gnad dril don 'di ltar ma shes na/ / tshig yi ge bzlas kyang brjod pa yin/ /
Eighty-four thousand dharmas were contained in A, surely taught by the divine Śākyamuni. But without understanding this summation of vital points, repeating the words and letters is just recitation.
ces dag byed stong ra'i skabs las bsgrags pa'i glu /
This was a song proclaimed for the occasion of practicing the Purifying A of Inner Space. ithi
sgrib med kyi rang gzugs lha ru shar/ / lha rnal 'byor ma dpal mkha' 'gro'i gtso/ / nyams bde stong myos pa'i lang tsho ma/ / sems bdag po'i phang par cung kyis byung / /

Unobscured natural form arises as the deity: Goddess Yoginī, chief of the glorious ḍākinīs, the experience of youthful intoxication with empty bliss, produced in the mind by the essence on the lord’s lap.
phyi snang ba lha yi gzhal yas la/ / nang dar dmar gur khyim srab la dwangs/ / logs me dpung 'bar ba'i thig le bzhi/ / gnad lte ba'i 'khor lo mgal me bzhin/ /

Outwardly, appearance is the divine celestial palace. Inwardly, [the body] is a red silk tent, smooth and bright. To the sides there are four spheres of blazing fire. Crucially, it is like a fire brand at the navel chakra.
raM sum mdor 'phros pa'i me lce yis/ / glog dbu ma'i rgyu lam yangs po nas/ / steng dkar gsal spyi bo'i rgya mthongs las/ / dpe skar mda' mkha' la bgrod pa bzhin/ /
Flames radiating from raṃ at the triple junction shoot lightning up the wide central channel, passing, white and clear, out the cranial aperture like shooting stars zooming through space.
rje bla ma'i sku las bdud rtsi'i chab/ / sgo tshangs pa'i lam nas rab zhugs te/ / lam dbang bzhi'i (526) rten 'brel bsgrig bzhin tu/ / bla ma dang rang sems dbyer ma shes/ /

Liquid elixir flows from the lord guru’s body and enters fully through your cranial aperture, {526} setting up connections for four empowerments on the path. Your mind and the guru’s become inseparable.
gtum mo las brtsams pa'i glu /
That was a song for commencing Fierce Inner Heat. ithi
blo cir snang dang ci shar sgyu ma'i nyams/ / 'ol thol skyes gyi dran pa byang chub lam/ / gnad gzer bu 'debs pa bla ma'i gsung / / 'di brjed pa med pa'i gzungs su 'dzin/ /

Mind’s appearances and whatever arises experienced as illusion. Spontaneous mindfulness is the path of awakening. The vital point that nails it is the guru’s teaching. Hold the retention of not forgetting this.
'dzin bcas kyi dran shes gsar bu'i sgom/ / sgom yid dpyod kyi lam mkhan gnas skabs kyi chos/ / chos yin lugs kyi byar med gu yang gcig / gcig shes kun grol ngo mtshar rmad/ /

Grasping with mindful awareness is beginner’s meditation. The path of analytic meditation is a situational teaching. A spacious state of inaction in the nature of phenomena is liberating all things by knowing one thing—it’s amazing!
sgyu lus skabs /
That was a song for the practice of Illusory Body. ithi
rmi lam gyi 'char sgo nyams kyi sne/ / 'dun pa yi yid shes mtshams sbyor gyi ngag / thig le'i bzhi 'gros rten 'brel gyi gnad/ / ma ye shes mkha' 'gro'i gsang ba'i gtam/ /

The perception of dreams is the edge of experience. Intentionality is joined with speech of mental cognition. Four movements of vital drops are the vital point of interdependence. This is the secret advice of the Mother Ḍākinī of Awareness.
sems 'khyams po la gtad so ma dmigs phyir/ / steng dga' ldan du 'gro ba thag mi ring / / yid kun snang la mi 'char med pa'i dpe/ / 'phral gang dgos su bde bsgyur rnal 'byor pa'i nyams/ /

The vagrant mind has no fixed reference point, so it’s not far to go up to Tuṣita heaven. For example, there’s nothing that cannot arise in the mind that illuminates everything. Ease of changing instantly into what is needed is the yogin’s experience.
nyams byung rgyal la dgag sgrub mi bgyid par/ / dus rgyun mi 'chad dran pa'i kha lo bsgyur/ /
Accept all experiences without judgment. Always guide mindfulness without interruption.
rmi lam gyi skabs /
This was a song for the practice of Dream. ithi
gzhi 'od gsal 'gyur med rtag pa'i sku/ / lam 'od gsal 'gags med bde ba'i cha/ / mthar 'bras bu mngon gyur rdzogs sangs rgyas/ / gnad gzhi lam 'bras bu'i mtshams sbyor lags/ /

The ground lucid clarity is unchanging, eternal body. The path lucid clarity is the unimpeded bliss aspect. The ultimate result is manifest perfect buddhahood. This joins the vital points of ground, path, and result.
[This was a song for the practice of Lucid Clarity.]
lam 'pho ba ma bsgom sangs rgyas la/ / yid ar la gtad pa'i dran pa'i mda'/ / sgo tshangs pa'i lam nas rgyangs bton te/ / blo ma yengs chos skur lhan gyis 'jog /

The path of Transference is buddhahood without meditation. With intense mental focus [on A], the arrow of mindfulness shoots far out from the path of the cranial aperture and without mental wavering, remains fully in dharmakāya.
[This was a song for the practice of Transference.]
dus da lta'i las snang ji snyed pa/ / gshis ma grub chu nang zla ba bzhin/ / don 'di yang nges shes skyes pa na/ / phyis bar do rgyal ba longs sku 'grub/ /

Whatever karmic appearances are occurring right now are fundamentally nonexistent, like the moon in water. When the import of this arises with certainty, you gain the victors’ saṃbhogakāya later in the intermediate state.
bar do'i skabs / !
This was a song for the practice of the Intermediate State. ithi
Jamyang Khyentse Wangchuk[48]

gnas gsar pa 'jam pa'i dbyangs mkhyen brtse'i (527) dbang phyug bstan pa'i rgyal mtshan dpal bzang po'i gsung mgur dpal ldan shangs pa'i gser chos kyi lam rim snying por dril ba'i gsol 'debs snying gi bdud rtsi zhes bya ba/

Nesarpa Jampaiyang Khyentsei Wangchuk Tenpai Gyaltsen Palzangpo’s song of supplication summarizes the essence of the graded path of the Golden Dharmas of the Glorious Shangpa. {527} It is called “The Heart’s Elixir.”[49]
na mo gu ru be/
namo guruve
rje rgyal ba kun dngos rdo rje 'chang / / chos sgrub brgyud yongs kyi gtsug rgyan mchog / pha 'brel tshad don ldan dkar rtsi ba/ / bu pha dang mnyam par byin gyis rlobs/ /

1. Lord Vajradhara, embodiment of all victors, supreme crown jewel of all dharma practice lineages; Father with whom I have meaningful connection, Kartsipa,[50] bless me that the son becomes equal to the father.
tha mal gyi shes pa so ma 'di/ / skyon bzhi yi dbang du ma song bar/ / rang ngo bo rjen par mthong ba yis/ / gzhi phyag chen rtogs par byin gyis rlobs/ /
2. This fresh ordinary mind not swayed by the four faults[51] sees its own essence nakedly; bless me to realize ground mahāmudrā.
'og lte ba'i a thung 'od 'bar la/ / srog rtsol gyi rlung gi bsrubs pa las/ / gzung 'dzin gyi bud shing sreg byed pa'i/ / lam gtum mo 'byor bar byin gyis rlobs/ /
3. Below the navel, short A blazes with light, churned by the winds of vital energy,[52] it burns the fuel of subject-object dualism; bless my training on the path of Fierce Inner Heat.
snang srid dang 'khor 'das gnyis snang kun/ / med bzhin du du mar 'char ba yi/ / rang stong gi rang mtshangs rtogs byed pa'i/ / lam sgyu lus 'byong bar byin gyis rlobs/ /

4. All dualistic appearance of apparent existence and samsara-nirvana, while nonexistent, arises as a multitude. To realize the hidden nature of intrinsic emptiness, bless my training on the path of Illusory Body.
nying 'khrul gyi bag chags tshan po che/ / shar tsam nas rang ngo shes pa dang / / bden med kyi rtsal snang 'bar ba yi/ / lam rmi lam 'byong bar byin gyis rlobs/ /
5. Strong habitual patterns of double delusion can be recognized upon arising, the manifestation of unreality blazes; bless my training on the path of Dream.
ma rig bag chags a 'thas kun/ / stong nyid kyi dbyings su thim pa las/ / 'gags med kyi stong gzugs 'od po che/ / lam 'od gsal 'byong bar byin gyis rlobs/ /
6. When all patterns of ignorant reification dissolve into the expanse of emptiness, shining forms of emptiness arise unhindered; bless my training on the path of Lucid Clarity.
'khrul snang gi lus gsum rgyal ba'i skur/ / gdod ma nas bzhugs par ngo shes pas/ / gnyis snang gi 'jigs skrag rang sar grol/ / lam bar do 'byong bar byin gyis rlobs/ /

7. Three bodies of deluded appearance are the victors’ kāyas. The recognition of their primordial presence liberates fear of dualistic appearance in its own ground; bless my training on the path of the Intermediate State.
tshe 'di yi zhen pas ma bcings bzhin/ / 'chi ba la 'jigs pas mi sun bar/ / chos dbyings kyi nam mkhar thogs med bgrod/ / lam 'pho ba 'byong bar byin gyis rlobs/ /
8. Not bound by attachment to this life, not depressed with the fear of death, I’ll transit freely to the realm of reality; bless my training on the path of Transference.
snang srid kun bla ma'i rol pa las/ / spang blang gi spro bsdu mi dgos par/ / (528) bral med kyi gdung shugs drag po yis/ / lam bla mas bgrod par byin gyis rlobs/ /
9. As all apparent existence is the guru’s display, no need to accept or reject, complicate or simplify. {528} Through my constant intense longing, bless me to traverse the path by way of the guru.
'khor 'das kun rgyal ba'i dkyil 'khor la/ / tha mal gyi 'dzin pas ma bcings par/ / yul gang shar lha skur ye shes su/ / lam yi dam gyis bgrod par byin gyis rlobs/ /

10. As all samsara and nirvana is the victors’ mandala, I am not bound by fixation on the ordinary. With awareness of whatever arises as the deity’s form; bless me to traverse the path by way of the yidam.
cir snang kun bden med sgyu ma la/ / a 'thas kyi rtog pas ma bcings shing / / sgyu 'dzin gyi zhen pas ma gos par/ / lam sgyu mas bgrod par byin gyis rlobs/ /
11. In knowing all appearance as unreal illusion, I am not bound by reifying fixation. Untainted by attachment to fixating on illusion; bless me to traverse the path by way of illusion.
rang sems 'di stong nyid rnal 'byor ma/ / nang rtsal du phag mo sgyu ma'i gar/ / rdzas gsang sngags tshogs kyis mnyes byas nas/ / gshis mkha' spyod 'grub par byin gyis rlobs/ /
12. This emptiness of my mind is Yoginī, its dynamic energy is Vārāhī’s illusory dance. I pleased her with feast substances of Secret Mantra; bless me to achieve the celestial realm of basic nature.
mchog yan lag lnga bsdu'i sbyor ba yis/ / ma dag pa'i mngal sgo sbyang byas te/ / stong nyid kyis b+ha gar rtse bas rol/ / lam zung 'jug rtogs par byin gyis rlobs/ /

13. Application of the supreme five branches [and] dissolution,[53] purifies the gate to the impure womb [birth]; I playfully frolic in the bhaga of emptiness. Bless me with realization of the path of integral unity.
rnam shes kyi bzhon pa las kyi rlung / / 'khrul 'khor gyi sbyor bas bcings pa las/ / don rtsa rlung thig le dbang 'dus nas/ / lus 'chi med 'grub par byin gyis rlobs/ /
ma bcos pa'i shes pa sgyu ma'i sku/ / yab yum gyi rol gar bde chen gyi ngang / / ma yengs pa'i rang ngo bskyangs pa las/ / sems 'phyugs med 'grub par byin gyis rlobs/ /
15. Uncontrived consciousness is illusory form, in a state of great bliss; the dance of father and mother. Maintaining one’s own essence without distraction; bless me to accomplish Infallible Mind.
dpal ye shes mgon po spyan ras gzigs/ / rten phyi nang gsang bas mchod cing brten/ / lam bskyed rdzogs bzlas pas dbang 'dus nas/ / las gang brtsam 'grub par byin gyis rlobs/ /

16. Glorious Awareness Protector Avalokita, with outer, inner, and secret offerings I rely on you. Controlled by the path of creation, completion, and recitation; bless me to achieve the actions I request.
don mkha' 'gro'i snying gtam rdo rje'i tshig / chos zab mo'i gser chos rnam pa lnga/ / lan brgya phrag bshad sgrub dpal 'byor gyis/ / bu snod ldan smin par byin gyis rlobs/ /
17. The meaning is the Ḍākinī’s heart advice of vajra words, in the Five Golden Dharmas of profound teaching, a hundredfold wealth of theory and practice; bless me to mature into a worthy vessel.
dus 'di nas sangs rgyas ma thob bar/ / rje khyed dang nam yang mi 'bral zhing / / thugs ci mnyes bya ba sgrub bzhin du/ / lam 'di nyid (529) bsgom par byin gyis rlobs/ /
mi bdag cag ltos par bcas pa la/ / rje khyed kyi thugs rjes byin brlabs nas/ / gshis rang bzhin 'od gsal chos kyi sku/ / dpal bde mchog 'grub par byin gyis rlob/ /
19. Bless me and those who look to me with your great compassion. Bless us with the accomplishment of glorious Cakrasaṃvara, the lucid clarity of our true nature: dharmakāya.
zhes bla ma shangs pa'i ser chos kyi smon lam shugs 'byung glur blangs pa / !
This was a song of spontaneous aspirations for the Golden Dharmas of Lama Shangpa. ithi
Tāranātha

'phags yul gyi grub pa'i dbang phyug rnams dang spang rtogs dbye ba med cing rtsod pa'i dus kyi rdo rje 'chang chen po/ / dpal de bI ko Tir ye shes mkha' 'gros gsang ba'i mdzod gtad pas zab lam shin tu nye brgyud kyi bka' babs shing rta chen po kun dga' snying po'am mtshan yongs su grags pa rje btsun thams cad mkhyen pa tA ra nA thas rdo rje'i do ha ji snyed cig stsal ba las/ / dgung lo nyer gsum par bsam sdings su bzhugs pa'i tshe rang la skul pa'i gros 'debs su gsungs pa ni/ /

His renunciation and realization were indistinguishable from the mighty adepts of India. He was Great Vajradhara for this age of conflict. At glorious Devīkoṭa, the Awareness Ḍākinī granted him her secret treasury, making him the great champion of the profound path of this very direct transmission. Kunga Nyingpo, or more famously known by the name Jetsun Tamche Khyenpa Tāranātha, (“Venerable All-Knowing Tāranātha”) composed many vajra dohas. At the age of twenty-three, while residing at Samding, he gave this counsel to himself as an incentive.[54]
oM swa sti/
oṃ svasti
skyabs gnas rin chen gsum la gus btud nas/ / rang gi sems la shar ba'i tshig 'di smra/ / dben pa'i ri bor mnyam bzhag byed do skad/ / gzhan gyi mig ngor pho tshugs bzang na yang / /
I bow to the three precious sources of refuge and say these words that dawned in my mind. You tell of meditating in mountain retreats, which makes a good impression in others’ eyes.
brtags na sems dang chos su ma 'dres pa/ / 'di 'dra dam chos gsha' ma ga la yin/ / da ni snying nas sgrub pa byed re ran/ / tshe 'di'i mdun ma skyungs dang snying med po/ /
But on closer examination, your mind is not joined to dharma. How can this be the honest Holy Dharma? Now it’s time to practice from the heart. Discard this life’s goals, hollow man!
thos bsam lta rtog chos bshad rem na yang / / rkyen ngan bag re'i steng du dam chos 'dor/ / mkhas par grags kyang mi tshe stong zad mkhan/ / 'di 'dra bshes gnyen dam pa ga la yin/ /

You hasten to teach, supervising study and contemplation, but at the slightest adversity abandon the Holy Dharma. Renowned as a scholar, you’re a waste of a human life. How can someone like you be a good spiritual mentor?
da ni rang gi sems rgyud 'dul re ran/ / mdzub mo nang du khug dang snying med po/ / 'khor ba'i gnas tshul 'phral 'phral mthong na yang / / yid ches cung zad med pa'i tshod med po/ /
Now it’s time to tame your mind. Point your finger inward, hollow man! You see the fleeting nature of cyclic existence but really don’t believe it and become negligent.
pha rol 'gro tshe gding drod mi gda' na'ang / / bsam mno mi gtong smyon pa rgya yan mkhan/ / da ni phyi ma'i grabs (530) shoms byed re ran/ / blo kha chos la sgyur dang snying med po/ /
When it’s time to pass on, you will not feel confident, yet you don’t worry about it; a careless madman. {530} Now it’s time to prepare for the next life. Turn your mind to the dharma, hollow man!

mkhos ka 'di las med kyang chags sdang can/ / yon tan 'di la nga rgyal ri rab tsam/ / mgu mkhan su yang med kyang mthun 'jug mkhan/ / byas pa chung la re ba che ba khyod/ / da ni 'jig rten chos brgyad spong re ran/ /

You need nothing more, yet you harbor attachment and aversion. Your pride in your qualities is as big as Mount Meru. You conform to social norms, though no one is impressed. You who have done so little but expect so much: now it’s time to reject the eight worldly concerns.
gang shar ro snyoms gyis dang snying med po/ / chos phyir gnyid thum re yang gcog mi nus/ / da lo da bzod byed snyams ngang ring po/ / myong rtags 'phral la dgos pa'i stong yus can/ /

Whatever happens has the same value, hollow man! You can’t give up even a little sleep for the sake of dharma. Later this year will do, you think with good-natured forbearance. You want instant signs of experience, you empty braggart.
zas nor snyan grags 'dod pa'i blo ma khugs/ / da ni 'dun ma chig 'gril byed re ran/ / gting nas re dogs skyungs dang snying med po/ / gzhon nu'i dus nas lang tsho yol zhing nyams/ /

You don’t control your desire for food, wealth, and fame. Now it’s time to concentrate on a single intention. Be rid of your deepest hopes and fears, hollow man! After adolescence, youth fades and deteriorates.
'khor 'dabs kun gyis phan lan gnod pas 'jal/ / da dus sun pa med pa'i blo rgya can/ / mi shes bzhin du tshe 'di'i 'dun grabs byed/ / da ni snying nas bya btang byed re ran/ /
All your followers just repay benefit with harm, yet you are still open-minded and not sick of it. You plan for this life as if you don’t know better. Now it’s time to wholeheartedly stop activities.
phyogs med rang blo sbyongs dang snying med po/ / bla ma'i ming can rnams kyang chos mi byed/ / slob ma rnams kyang dam tshig srung mkhan med/ / skye bo kun kyang ngo tsha khrel gzhung med/ /

Train your mind to be impartial, hollow man! All who bear the title of guru don’t practice the dharma. All their disciples are not keepers of sacred pledge. All the people even lack shame and conscientiousness.

sangs rgyas bstan pa nyams pa'i dus ngan 'dir/ / gzhan la phan thabs ji tsam byas na yang / / phal cher mi phan rang la gnod par 'dug / rang nyid chos la brtan pa thob phan chad/ / gzhan don rgyun mi chad pa 'byung bas na/ /

In these hard times of decline of the Buddha’s doctrine, no matter how many ways you try to help others, mostly it just harms yourself and does not help them. Once you gain stability in the dharma, the benefit for others will arise continuously.
re zhig tshe 'di khong la gcags pa yi/ / gzhan don ltar snang bor la rang don mchog / dam pa'i chos la sgril ba'i dus su gda'/ / de ltar lags pas da dung bsam mno thong / /
Give up the sporadic semblance of helping others in this life and concentrate on yourself. This is the time to embrace the Holy Dharma. Since that is indeed the case, keep it in mind.
zhes gsungs so/ /
bu slob kyi mchog gyur gangs dkar ba dad can nyi ma rnam rgyal la ngo sprod kyi snying po gnang ba/
The following essential introduction was given to Tāranātha’s excellent student from Gangkar, the faithful Nyima Namgyal.[55]
rje rdo rje 'chang chen grub thob tshul/ / mtshan thos pa tsam gyis don chen ldan/ / bdag bu slob kyi (531) blo sna chos la sgyur/ / khyed thugs rje'i gter la gsol ba 'debs/ /
dus da res mi lus thob pa dang / / mtshan ldan gyi rje dang mjal skabs 'dir/ / nyams len la 'bad 'bungs ma bton na/ / mi tshe don med du 'gro nyen gda'/ /
At this time, you have obtained a human birth and met a qualified spiritual master. If you don’t strenuously apply yourself to practice, you are in jeopardy of a meaningless life.
nyams len gyi rgyal po mos gus yin/ / mthun rkyen gyi rgyal po nges 'byung yin/ / bya byed kyi rgyal po byar med yin/ / mnyam gzhag gi rgyal po rang shar yin/ /
Devotion is the sovereign of practice. Renunciation is the sovereign of favorable conditions. Nonaction is the sovereign of activity. Self-arising equipoise is the sovereign of equipoise.
rgyal po bzhi ldan gyi gdams ngag 'di/ / mtshan ldan bla ma'i gsung ngag yin/ / grub thob yongs kyi thugs bcud yin/ / tA ra nA tha'i nyams myong yin/ /
This esoteric instruction possessed of four sovereigns is the speech of the qualified guru. It is the whole heart’s essence of the adepts. It is Tāranātha’s personal experience.
mtshan bcas kyi nyams len phyogs re ba/ / sdug dus mi phan pa'i skyid chos de/ / thabs mkhas kyi bkri tshul yin mod kyang / / sangs rgyas lag bcangs su gtod mi thub/ /
Practice with attributes is insufficient; a happy dharma of no help in times of suffering. Sure, it is a skillful way of guidance, but it can’t bring buddhahood within reach.
rang zhal rjen par lta ba la/ / mtshan ldan rje la mos gus dgos/ / bla ma sangs rgyas skad pa'i kha snyan dang / / ci mdzad legs par lta dgos kyi sdug zhen can/ /
To see your own face nakedly, you need devotion to a qualified master. It is sweet talk to say the guru is buddha, and loyal to say you must see what the guru does as good.
ma byas bsam byung tsam gyi mos gus de/ / khog zhe nas ltem 'gyang log ge ba/ / chos rang gis byed snyam tshugs bzang yang / / de sgra skad tsam las don mi mthong / /
That devotion is just unproductive thought; the reverse of the fullness from deep within. Even an excellent resolve of “I will practice dharma” is not seeing the meaning beyond the words.
sangs rgyas dang sems can gyi 'then phyogs med/ / thugs chos sku skye med nyag gcig la/ / mdzad spyod nyes na'ang nyes go chod/ / phyogs med kyi 'gro don rgya re che/ /
With unbiased assessment of buddhas and beings by the mind in the single unborn dharmakāya, even faulty actions can be useful; the unbiased welfare of migrators is huge.
byin rlabs zhugs rung ma zhugs rung / / dngos grub thob rung ma thob rung / / skyabs gnas gzhan na med do zhes/ / blo thag chod la gsol ba thob/ /
Whether blessings enter you or not, whether you attain spiritual powers or not, supplicate with a decisive mind: “I have no other place of refuge.”
thugs yid dbyer med du mnyam par zhog / sgom mi skye ba'i rang dbang ga la yod/ / zas gos 'dzom pa'i skyid 'dod de/ / dge sbyor 'chag la g.yeng ba che/ /
mthun (532) rkyen du ming btags rnam g.yeng de/ / rnal 'byor pa la dgos pa med/ / yid nges 'byung skyo shas drag po de/ / rang gcig pur sdod na skyo rogs yin/ / lus na tsha byung na nad g.yog yin/ /

To assign it the name “favorable conditions” is a total distraction that the yogin doesn’t need. Strong renunciation and disillusionment are your consolers when you live alone and your nurses when you are sick.
zas gos dran pa'i rnam g.yeng la/ / gdod zlog byed pa'i mthun rkyen yin/ / sdar ma byas pa cig med pa la/ / byas tshad 'khor ba'i g.yos su song / /

The distraction of obsessing over food and clothes is the “favorable condition” of reversing your progress. There is not a single thing you have not done before, yet all you’ve done has been food for cyclic existence.
da byar med kyi ngang du lhod de zhog / gtan gyi btsan sa zin te mchis/ / blos byas kyi dge sbyor brtson na yang / / 'gyur med kyi gtan sa zin pa med/ /
Now, just rest and relax in nonaction. That is how to reach the permanent safe place. Even if you strive at mind-made virtue, you won’t reach the changeless safe place.
dbyings 'pho 'gyur med pa'i gnad ka des/ / rang babs su bzhag na 'gyur med thob/ / rang shar la bzo bcos mi 'tshal te/ / bcos min la ngo shes gal re che/ /

With that vital point of basic space without change, if you just let go, you will attain an unchanging state. Do not seek to fabricate natural arising; it’s extremely important to recognize the uncontrived.

sems rnam rtog med par rang gsal na/ / gsal ba gsal zhing stong pa de/ / rang ngo shes na chos skur 'dug / rang gis rang ngo shes dus na/ / rtog pa'i cho 'phrul ci che yang / / bde sdug gi 'char sgo gang mang yang / / thams cad chos sku'i yo langs yin/ /

In mind’s own clarity, free of discursive thought, that clarity is lucid and empty. If you recognize your own nature, it is dharmakāya. When you know that as your own nature, no matter how great the apparitions of concept or how many perceptions of joy and suffering, they are all the shifting display of dharmakāya.
rtog pa dang mi rtog khyad par med/ / gnas pa dang 'gyu ba'i rang mtshang zhig / chab rom chu ru zhu ba ltar/ / gang snang rang sems su lhang nge ba/ /
There’s no difference between thought and nonthought. The faults of abiding or moving [thoughts] are destroyed. Like ice melting into water, whatever appears is vividly your own mind.
snang dus nas rjes med yul yul po/ / stong tsam gyi 'char sgo ma 'gags pa/ / ya ki sangs rgyas kyi sku gsum nas/ / ma ki dmyal khams yan chad kun/ / thams cad mi 'char bya ba med/ /
Object and subject are unhindered perceptions of mere emptiness. From the buddhas’ three kāyas above down to the hell realms below, don’t act to prevent anything arising.
ci ltar shar yang spros dang bral/ / ngag brjod pa kun gyi yul las 'das/ / sems rang rig bde ba chen por myong / /
Let whatever arises be free of embellishment. Beyond the purview of all verbal expression, experience the great bliss of your intrinsic awareness.
slar spros bcas kyi dge ba gong 'phel bya/ / thams cad phyag chen gyi yo langs yin/ / thabs shes rab tshogs gnyis rdzogs pa las/ / sangs rgyas kyi dgongs pa rtogs pa yin/ /
de nyams su (533) blangs na bdud rtsi 'dra/ / kha ltar shor na stong shob yin/ / rgyud thog tu nyams su longs pa cig 'tshal/ / nyams len la rang byan tshud pa cig zhu/ / zhes gsungs so/ /
If you cultivate that experience, it is like elixir, but if it is just loose talk, it is meaningless. Seek to practice directly in your mind stream. I ask you to assimilate this as your practice.
yang nges 'byung skul ba'i lcag 'debs zhal gdams su stsal ba/ /
Again Tāranātha granted this personal advice to crack the whip of renunciation.[56]
na mo gu ru b+h+yaH
namo guru bhyaḥ
pha rdo rje 'chang la phyag 'tshal nas/ / 'dir snying gtam tshig gsum smra ba ni/ / tshe 'di'i snang ba ni 'ja' tshon dang 'dra/ / 'di yi rjes 'ded mi 'tshal lo/ /
I pay homage to Father Vajradhara and express here three words of heartfelt advice. The appearances of this life are like a rainbow; please don’t chase after them.
snang ba 'di dang sems kyi byed pa gcig lags/ / tha dad du 'dzin zhen mi 'tshal lo/ / rig pa zhen med du ma shar na/ / sgom byas tshad bzang rdzur 'gro nyen gda'/ /
These appearances are surely a creation of mind; please don’t fixate on them as separate. If intrinsic awareness does not arise without attachment, your successful meditation could be a sham.
