stong pa'i ngang las/ mdun tu hU~M yig las byung ba'i srung 'khor gyi nang mi bzad pa'i dur khrod chen po'i dbus su/ paM las pad+ma dang / raM las nyi ma'i steng du/ gaM dkar po 'od du zhu ba las/ dpal tshogs kyi bdag po sku mdog dkar po glang po che'i dbu la spyan gsum pa phyag g.yas sa'i snying po la phug lo ma dang bcas pa zhal du gsol ba/ g.yon thod pa bdud rtsis gang ba 'dzin pa/ dar dang rin po ches brgyan pa nyal stabs su gnas pa/ de'i steng du hU~M mthing nag las gri gug hU~M gis mtshan pa/ de las 'od zer 'phros/ dgra bgegs gdug pa can thams cad tshar bcad/ 'phags pa mchod/ sems can gyi don byas/ slar 'dus te thim pa yongs su gyur pa las/ myur mdzad ye shes kyi mgon po (631) phyag drug pa/ skye 'gro'i re ba tshul bzhin du skong ba/

From within emptiness, the letter hūṃ in front becomes the protection circle with the unbearable great charnel ground. In its center a lotus arises from paṃ and a sun from raṃ. Upon that, white gaṃ melts into light and becomes glorious Gaṇapati, white, with an elephant head and three eyes, holding in his right hand a leafy daikon radish, the essence of earth, which he is eating. In his left hand is an elixir-filled skull cup. He is lying down, adorned with silks and precious jewels. Upon him, blue-black hūṃ becomes a flaying knife marked with hūṃ. Light rays radiating from that terminate all enemies, obstructors, and noxious spirits. The light makes offerings to the exalted ones and helps sentient beings. It again returns and dissolves, completely transforming into Swift-Acting Six-Armed Awareness Protector, {631} the perfect fulfiller of the hopes of living beings.

sku mdog dus mtha'i sprin ltar rab tu gnag pa/ zhal gcig phyag drug pa/ dmar la zlum pa'i spyan gsum sdang mig tu gzigs pa/ zhal gdangs shing mche ba gtsigs pa/ ljags 'dril ba/ rab tu bzhad pa/ sma ra dang smin ma dang / dbu skra dmar ser gyen du brdzes pa/ dpral bar sin+d+hu ra'i thig les byugs pa/ spyi bor mi bskyod rgyal pos rgyas btab pa phyag g.yas dang pos rdo rje gri gug dang / g.yon dang pos thod pa khrag gis gang ba thugs kar steng 'og tu 'dzin pa/ g.yas par pas thod skam gyi phreng ba/ tha mas DA ma ru drag tu 'khrol ba/ g.yon gnyis pa na mdung rtse gsum pa/ tha ma na rdo rje zhags pa bsnams pa/

He is very black, like the clouds at the end of time. He has one face and six arms. He glares angrily with three round, red eyes. His gaping mouth reveals his bared fangs and curled tongue as he laughs fiercely. His orange beard, eyebrows, and hair stream upward. His forehead is anointed with a drop of vermilion and his head crowned by King Akṣobhya. He holds a vajra[-handled] flaying knife in his top right hand and a blood-filled skull cup with the left, one hand above the other at his heart. In his middle right hand is a rosary of dry skulls, and in the lower one he fiercely rattles a ḍamaru. He holds a trident spear in his second left hand and a vajra lasso in the last left hand.

zhabs gnyis srid gsum rnam par gnon pa'i shugs can mnyam pa'i stabs krig krig zhabs kyis bgegs kyi rgyal po mnan pa/ stag lpags kyi sham thabs la/ dar ljang gu'i ske rags bcings pa/ sbrul sngon pos dbu skra bcings shing / dmar po'i snyan cha/ khra bo'i dpung rgyan/ dkar po'i mgul rgyan/ ser po'i lag gdub/ ljang gu'i do shal/ dkar po'i rkang gdub dang ska rags can/ phyag zhabs thams cad dril bu g.yer kha'i phreng ba dang ldan pa/ sbom thung yan lag hrag pa/ gzi brjid mtha' yas pa/ mi mgo skam po lnga'i dbu rgyan rin po che'i rtse phran can dang / rlon pa khrag 'dzag lnga bcu'i do shal byas pa/ rus pa'i rgyan drug gis mdzes pa/ 'jigs pa'i nga ro 'brug ltar sgrogs pas/ bdud dang bgegs thams cad brlag par mdzad pa/ bskal pa'i me lta bu'i ye shes kyi me dpung 'bar ba'i dbus na bzhugs shing / tsan+dan gyi sdong po la rgyab brten pa'o/ /

His two legs, with the strength to totally suppress the three existences, stand in a perfectly straight, even position pressing down on the Obstructor King. He wears a tiger-skin skirt tied with a green silk sash. Blue snakes bind his hair, and he has red snake earrings, striped snake armbands, white snake collar, yellow snake bracelets, green snake necklace, and white snake anklets and belt. On all his arms and legs there are strings of large and small bells. He is short and fat, with thick limbs. He has boundless charisma. He has a crown of five dry human skulls topped with jewel finials and a garland of fifty fresh skulls dripping with blood. The six bone ornaments beautify him. His terrifying roars resound like thunder, annihilating all devils and obstructors. He stands amid a bonfire of timeless awareness like the fire at the end of the eon, supported by the trunk of a sandalwood tree.

de'i g.yon du khrag zhags 'khrugs pa'i rgya mtsho'i dbus su/ b+h+yoHlas dpal ldan lha mo 'dod pa khams kyi dbang phyug ma/ sku mdog nag mo phyag g.yas bdud kyi khram shing nag po (632) phyar shing / g.yon nad kyi rkyal pa 'dzin pa/ me rlung 'tshubs ma'i dbus na bzhugs shing / dre'u rta rkang gsum la chibs pa/ 'khor sha za dang ma mo mkha' 'gro 'bum sdes bskor ba'o/ /

To his left, in the middle of an ocean of turbulent blood and fat, bhyoḥ becomes Śrīdevī, mighty queen of the desire realm. She is black, waving a devil’s black cross-scored board in her right hand and grasping a bag of pestilence with her left. {632} She stands in the midst of a conflagration of fire and wind, riding on a three-legged mule. Her retinue of one hundred thousand flesh-eating ḍākinīs surrounds her.

gtso bo'i mdun du hU~M las gnod sbyin k+She tra pA la/ sku mdog mthing nag kha gdangs shing mche ba gtsigs nas dgra la 'o dod 'bod pa/ shangs nas dus mtha'i rlung ldang ba/ phyag g.yas gri gug nam mkha' la phyar bas lha dang lha ma yin thams cad skrag par byed pa/ /g.yon thod khrag dgra bgegs kyi snying dang bcas pa gtso bo'i zhal du stob pa/ dom nag smyon pa la chibs pa/

In front of the principal figure, hūṃ[9] becomes Yakṣa Kṣetrapāla, blue-black with a gaping mouth and bared fangs, bellowing at his enemies. Winds of the end-times rise from his nose. With his right hand he brandishes a flaying knife to the sky, terrifying all the gods and demigods. With his left hand he feeds the principal’s mouth from a blood-filled skull cup containing the hearts of enemies and obstructors. He rides a crazed black bear.
g.yas su b+h+yo las dbang phyug dzi na mi tra sku mdog dmar nag / g.yas DA ma ru 'khrol zhing / g.yon thod khrag 'dzin pa/
To the right, bhyoḥ becomes dark-red Īśvara Jinamitra fiercely rattling a ḍamaru with his right hand and holding a blood-filled skull cup with the left.
rgyab tu dzaHlas gshin rje Ta k+ki rA dza sku mdog dmar nag / phyag g.yas zhags pa dgra la 'phen cing / g.yon sdigs mdzub gnod byed la sdigs pa/
In back, from jaḥ, dark-red Yama Ṭakkirāja throws a lasso at enemies with his right hand and points at harm-doers with his left hand in the threatening gesture.

g.yon du las bdud mgon chen po trak+shad sku mdog nag po phyag g.yas su mtshon mdung dmar rtse gsum pa dgra bo'i snying gar bsnun pa/ g.yon thod pa khrag gis gang ba bsnams pa/ ya sos ma mchu mnan pa/ dar nag gi 'jol ber dang / sag ti'i lham yu ring gsol ba/ gser gyi ske rags bcings pa/ bdud rta nag po rting dkar la chibs pa/ bzhi ka'ang khro bo las mkhan gyi cha byad yongs su rdzogs pa'o/ /

To the left, from du, the great devil lord black Trakṣad pierces the enemies’ hearts with a red three-pronged ensign spear in his right hand and holds a blood-filled skull cup in this left. He bites his lower lip. He wears a black cloak, high rawhide boots, and a golden belt. He rides a black devil horse with white fetlocks. All four are completely perfect in the garb of wrathful emissaries.

de'i phyi rol du shar du brgya byin/ shar lhor me lha/ lhor gshin rje/ lho nub tu srin po/ nub tu chu lha/ nub byang du rlung lha/ byang du gnod sbyin/ byang shar du 'byung po/ steng du tshangs pa/ 'og tu sa bdag ste phyogs skyong bcu/ gzhan yang lha chen po brgyad/ klu chen po brgyad/ gza' chen po brgyad/ 'jigs byed chen po dgu/ rgyu skar nyi shu rtsa brgyad/ rgyal po chen po bzhi ste/ gtsang rigs kyi mgon po bdun cu rtsa lnga po (633) thams cad kyang 'khor bye ba bye ba'i tshogs kyis bskor ba/ de'i phyi rol du dam can rgya mtsho'i dmag tshogs sha la dga' ba/ khrag la rol ba/ snying rje med pa/ kha gdangs pa/ mig rtsa dmar ba/ lag na gdug pa'i mtshon cha sna tshogs pa thogs pa skad cig la skye 'gro thams cad kyi srog dbugs sdud pa/ gnod sbyin dang / srin po dang / gshin rje dang / bdud dang ma mo'i cha lugs can/ sa gzhi bar snang nam mkha'i dbyings thams cad yongs su gang ba/ thams cad kyang sgrub pa po'i re 'dod tshul bzhin du skong bar mdzad pa'o/ /

The ten direction protectors are outside of them: Śakra in the east, Agni in the southeast, Yama in the south, Rākṣasa in the southwest, Varuṇa in the west, Vāyu in the northwest, Yakṣa in the north, Bhūta in the northeast, Brahmā above, and Bhūpati below. All around them are the eight great gods, the eight great nāgas, the eight great planets, the nine great terrifiers (bhairavas), the twenty-eight constellations, the four great kings, [and the ten direction protectors]. All these seventy-five protectors of pure clans are each surrounded by a retinue of millions. {633} Outside of them are the armies of an ocean of the oath-bound—loving flesh, reveling in blood, merciless, open-mouthed, bloodshot-eyed, and bearing various lethal weapons in their hands—in an instant they can suck the life force out of all living beings. They wear the garb of yakṣas, rākṣasas, yāmas, māras, and mātṛkās. They completely cover the ground and fill all the sky and space. All are fulfilling the hopes and desires of practitioners.

de thams cad kyi dpral bar oM dkar po/ mgrin par AHdmar po/ thugs kar hU~M sngon po/ rang gi thugs ka'i hU~M las 'od zer 'phros/ shar lho dur khrod chen po bsil ba'i tshal/ tsan+dan gyi shing rkang gcig pa'i drung nas/ myur mdzad ye shes kyi mgon po phyag drug pa/ steng na rtsa brgyud kyi bla ma/ g.yas na dpa' bo ngar dang bcas shing / g.yon na dpa' mo 'dzum dang bcas pa/ bka' sdod zhing skyong pho nya/ dam can rgya mtsho'i dmag tshogs dang bcas pa thams cad skad cig nyid la DA ma ru dang dril bu g.yer kha'i sgra si li li/ khro lo lo/ 'ur 'ur chem chem byon par gyur/ /

They all have white oṃ at the forehead, red āḥ at the throat, and blue hūṃ at the heart. Light rays radiate from the hūṃ in your own heart, invoking Swift-Acting Six-Armed Awareness Protector from in front of the single trunk of the sandalwood tree in the great charnel ground Cool Grove in the southeast. He arrives instantly with the root and lineage gurus above him, grimacing heroes on his right, smiling heroines on his left, and all the armies of obedient ones, realm protectors, messengers, and an ocean of the oath-bound, accompanied by the sounds of ḍamarus, bells, and small bells: si li li, khro lo lo, ur ur, chem chem.
hU~M/ dad pa dang ni dam tshig gis/ / tshur gshegs ma hA kA la che/ / dpal ldan mgon po 'khor dang bcas/ / dkyil 'khor gnas 'dir gshegs su gsol/ /
hūṃ By faith and by sacred pledge, great Mahākāla, come here. Glorious Protector with your retinue, please approach this mandala site.
k+She tra pA la la sogs pa/ / 'khor gyi bka' nyan gnod sbyin tshogs/ / bstan pa bsrung par zhal bzhes pa'i/ / dam can rgya mtsho gshegs su gsol/ /
Kṣetrapāla and the others, retinue of attendants, hosts of yakṣas, you who promised to guard the doctrine, ocean of the oath-bound, please approach.
dkyil 'khor gnas 'dir gshegs nas kyang / / rgyan gyi gtor ma 'di bzhes la/ / rtags dang mtshan ma ston pa dang / / bcol ba'i phrin las grub par mdzod/ /
When you come to this mandala site, partake of this decorated torma, show yourselves in signs and forms, and accomplish the entrusted activity.

oM badzra ma hA kA la sa pa ri wa ra ces pa'i rjes su / k+ShiM ring po nyi shu rtsa gcig brjod/ / de nas k+ShiM gi gnas su e h+ye hi bcug pa dang / badzra sa mA (634) dzaH bcug pa rnams lan gsum gsum brjod pas/ myur mdzad 'khor bcas spyan drangs/
oṃ vajra mahākāla saparivāra…(etc.). Add kṣiṃ to that twenty-one times. Then in place of kṣiṃ insert e hye hi and vajra samājaḥ three times each. {634} Swift Actor and retinue are invoked.
dzaHhU~M ba~M hoH gnyis su med par thim/ /
jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ—they dissolve indivisibly.
hU~M/ bdud 'dul dmag dpon nag po che/ / rab brjid 'khor gyi tshogs dang bcas/ / dgra bgegs ma lus 'dul ba'i phyir/ / nag po chen po bzhugs su gsol/ /
hūṃ Great Black One, commander who tames devils, so magnificent, surrounded by retinues, in order to subdue every enemy and obstructor, Great Black One, please remain here.
pad+ma ka ma la staM/ oM shrI ma hA kA la ya sa pa ri wA ra ar+g+haM pra tI ts+tsha swA hA/
padma kamalāyastvaṃ oṃ śri mahākālaya sapārivāra arghaṃ pratīccha hūṃ svāhā
de bzhin du+u pA d+yaM/ puSh+pe/ d+hU pe/ A lo ke gan+d+he/ nai bi d+ya/ shab+da zhes sbyar ro/ / snying po'i mthar 'bru gsum btag la nang mchod 'bul/
Similarly, add padyaṃ…puṣpe…dhūpe…āloke…gandhe…naividyā…śabda. Present the inner offerings by adding the three seed syllables to the essence mantra.
chos dbyings ngang las ma g.yos kyang / / gdug pa 'dul phyir khros pa'i sku/ / bstan pa'i ru dra 'joms mdzad pa'i/ / nag po che la phyag 'tshal bstod/ /
Without stirring from the realm of reality, yet your wrathful form to subdue the vicious vanquishes the rudra of the doctrine; homage and praise to Great Black One.
de nas gsol 'debs ni/
Then the supplication:
na mo bud+d+hA ya/ na mo gu ru he/ badzra bI ra bI re Ni/ shrI DA ka DA ki nI/ dzo ga dzo gi nI/ sarba bud+d+ha bo d+hi sa twa ya sha ra NaM gats+tsha mi/ kye kye
namo buddhāya / namo guruhe / vajra vīra vīreṇī / śrīḍāka ḍākinī / joka jokiṇī / sarva buddha bodhisatvāya śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi kyai kyai

phyogs bcu dus gsum na bzhugs pa'i rtsa ba dang brgyud par bcas pa'i dpal ldan bla ma dam pa rnams kyis byin gyis rlobs shig / yi dam dkyil 'khor gyi lha tshogs rnams kyis byin gyis rlobs shig / dpa' bo dang dpa' mor bcas pa rnams kyis=
Holy root and lineage gurus dwelling in the ten directions and three times, bless me! Yidam deities of the mandala, bless me! Heroes and heroines, bless me!
sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyis= dpal ye shes kyi mgon po phyag drug pa'i lha tshogs/ ye shes la sgrib pa mi mnga' ba/ thugs rje la phyi bshol mi mnga' ba/ /
Buddhas and bodhisattvas all, bless me! Glorious Six-Armed Awareness Protector and deities, bless me! Do not veil your timeless awareness. Do not delay your compassion.
mthu dang nus pa la thogs pa mi mnga' ba/ byin rlabs la rgyang ring thung mi mnga' ba/
Do not block your power and ability. Do not distance your blessings.
khyed rnams kyi sku'i sgo nas byin gyis rlobs shig / gsung gi sgo nas= thugs kyi sgo nas=
All of you, bless me through your body, bless me through your speech, bless me through your mind!
sku gsung thugs yon tan phrin las mi zad pa'i sgo nas= da lta nyid du= myur pa nyid du= 'dug sa 'di nyid du byin gyis brlab tu gsol/ /
Bless me through your unlimited awakened body, speech, mind, qualities, and activities! Bless me right now! Bless me quickly! Bless me on this very seat!
bla ma mgon po dbyer med la/ / bdag ni dad pas gsol 'debs kyi/ / bdag dang sems can thams cad kyi/ / nyon mongs ma lus bsal ba dang / / dngos grub ma lus stsal du (635) gsol/ /
Guru-Protector inseparable, I supplicate you with faith: dispel every affliction of myself and all sentient beings. Please grant every spiritual power. {635}
de nas bshags pa bya ba ni/ /
rdo rje sems dpa'i yi ge brgya pa lan nyi shu rtsa gcig bzlas pa'i mthar/
Repeat Vajrasattva’s hundred syllables twenty-one times. Afterward recite:

rdo rje 'chang dang dpal ldan shA bA ri/ / rgyal ba mi tra grub chen rA hu la/ / a mi de ba lo ke shwa ra dang / / ha ya grI ba pad+ma 'byung gnas dpal/ / khyung po dzo ki rat+na bir+Ya dang / / d+harma sing+ha d+harma pra dz+nyA dang / / bir+Ya sid+ha mkhas grub chos rje sogs/ / rin chen brgyud pa'i bla ma dgongs su gsol/ /

Vajradhara and glorious Śavari?, sovereign Maitrīpa, great adept Rāhula, Amideva, Lokeśvara, Hayagrīva, glorious Padmākara, Khyungpo Yogi, Ratna Vīrya, Dharma Siṃha, Dharma Prajñā, Vīrya Siṃha, Khedrup Chöje, and the others, gurus of the jewel lineage, please think of me.
'gro ba'i re skong yon tan rab rdzogs pa'i/ / brgyud ldan bla ma dus gsum sangs rgyas la/ / dag pa gnyis ldan chos skur ma rtogs par/ / 'jig rten rtog bcas dbang gyur mthol lo bshags/ /

I did not realize that the guru with a lineage of perfected qualities that fulfill beings’ hopes was the embodiment of doubly pure buddhas of the three times: I confess falling under the influence of worldly thought.
sku gsung thugs dang yon tan phrin las dang / / phyi nang gsang ba'i lha rnams dgongs su gsol/ / bdag cag theg mchog sngags kyi sgor zhugs nas/ / rtsa ba yan lag 'gal nyams mthol lo bshags/ /

All outer, inner, and secret deities with awakened body, speech, mind, qualities, and activities, please think of me. Once I entered the door of Supreme Vehicle Mantra, I confess my transgressions and damages of its root and branch pledges.
mthu stobs nus pa phrin las phun tshogs shing / / skad cig dran pas bar chad thams cad sol/ / 'du 'bral med par dngos grub ster mdzad pa'i/ / ye shes mgon po phyag drug dgongs su gsol/ /

With your abundant activity of power and capability, just recalling you for an instant dispels all obstacles. Giver of spiritual powers without meeting or parting, Six-Armed Awareness Protector, please think of me.
dur khrod nags 'dabs chu gling bas mtha' ru/ / phyi nang rten dang dam rdzas tshogs gyur nas/ / bsnyen sgrub bskang bshags tshul bzhin ma grub par/ / le lo g.yeng ba'i dbang gyur mthol lo bshags/ /

In secluded charnel grounds, forests, and islands, I collected the outer and inner supports and pledge substances but did not properly do the recitations, fulfillments, and confessions; I confess falling under the influence of laziness and distraction.
khyad par gsang ba'i rten mchog bla na med/ / bla ma mgon po dbyer med bde chen sku/ / khyod la yid ches mos gus 'bral med kyis/ / rnam dag chos skur ma rtogs mthol lo bshags/ /

In particular, I did not realize that the supreme secret support is the great-bliss kāya of Guru-Protector inseparable. Through constant devotion and belief in you, I confess not realizing you as totally pure dharmakāya.

bdag ni ma rig 'khrul pa'i dbang gyur te/ / bla ma mgon po 'khor dang bcas rnams kyi/ / sku gsung thugs dang 'gal ba ci mchis pa/ / gnong zhing 'gyod pa'i sems dang bcas nas kyang / / lha mchog khyod kyi spyan sngar mthol lo bshags/ /

Whatever I have done under the influence of ignorant delusion that opposes the body, speech, and mind of Guru-Protector and retinue, with a mind full of sorrow and regret I confess before your eyes, sublime deity.
ye shes bka' sgrub las kyi pho nya mdzad/ / k+She tra pA la dzi na mi tra dang / / TA k+ki rA dza trak+shad re ma tI/ / phyogs skyong bcu dang gtsang rigs dgongs (636) su gsol/ /
Awareness beings who carry out my commands, activity messengers Kṣetrapāla, Jinamitra, Ṭakkirāja, Trakṣad, and Rematī, protectors of the ten directions and pure regions, please think of me. {636}
ji ltar khyed kyis khas blangs dam bcas bzhin/ / bdag gi phrin las yengs med sgrub pa la/ / yi chad bgyis shing sha khrag gtor tshogs kyis/ / gtong rag dus su ma thongs mthol lo bshags/ /
True to your word and commitment, straight away you accomplished my activities, but sadly I did not offer a flesh-and-blood torma feast; I confess not giving thanks in a timely way.
mngon shes med pas nyes skyon ma rtogs par/ / bstan pa 'jig dang bla ma'i sku dgra la/ / drag po'i las kyis tshar gcod ma bgyis par/ / gsang ba bsgrags shing byams bgyis mthol lo bshags/ /

With no clairvoyance, I did not realize the faults and mistakes of the doctrine’s destroyers and the guru’s lethal enemies, and so I did not destroy them with wrathful activity; I confess disclosing the secrets and loving them.
dam nyams gtam 'dres grib phog zas zos dang / / rgyu chung phud nyams 'gal 'khrul nor la sogs/ / nyes skyon 'khrul pa'i tshogs rnams ci mchis pa/ / gnong zhing 'gyod pa'i sgo nas mthol lo bshags/ /

Whatever errors, faults, and delusions I have committed, such as being contaminated by talking or eating with vow-breakers, or meager offerings, spoiled select portions, and confused rituals; I confess with shame and regret.
sku yi dam tshig nyams pa mthol lo bshags/ / gsung gi= / thugs kyi= / rtsa ba'i= /

I confess violating the sacred pledges of awakened body. I confess violating the sacred pledges of awakened speech. I confess violating the sacred pledges of awakened mind. I confess violating the root sacred pledges.
yan lag= / tshor te= / ma tshor= /
I confess violating the branch sacred pledges. I confess consciously violating the sacred pledges. I confess unconsciously violating the sacred pledges.
nyams grib dag phyir bshags pa 'di byas pas/ / dpal ldan mgon po 'khor dang bcas rnams kyis/ / pha ma bu tsha bzhin du bzod bzhes la/ / dngos grub thams cad bdag la dus 'dir stsol/ /

I have confessed in order to purify the defilement of violation; Guru and Protector with your entourage, please be patient with me, as parents with their child, and now grant me all the spiritual powers.

bshags dang bshags par bya ba mi dmigs kyang / / rnam par rtog pa'i bag chags dag bya'i phyir/ / rje btsun dam pa yul gyi mchog rnams la/ / rab tu bshags pas bde chen thob gyur cig / gsol 'debs dang bshags pa'ang mi spyon bor bas kyang rung ngo / /

Though the acts I confess and the act of confession are nonexistent, in order to purify the habitual patterns of discursive thought, I fully confess before the sublime object of my venerable guru. May I thereby attain great bliss. If you don’t wish to do the supplication and confession, you may skip them.
de nas bzlas pa ni/
Then the recitation:

rang gi thugs ka'i hU~M las sngags kyi phreng ba rnams kha dog nag po 'od zer dmar po 'phro ba phreng rdog ltar gnas pa la 'od zer sna lnga phrer thag gi tshul du brgyus pa rang gi zhal nas thon mgon po'i zhal du zhugs/ mgon po'i thugs ka'i hU~M la thim/ yang hU~M las byung / mgon po'i lte ba nas thon/ bdag gi lte bar zhugs/ snying ga'i hU~M la thim/ de ltar rtag tu 'khor lo ltar 'khor ba ra bsams la/ oM badzra ma hA kA la k+ShiM k+She tra big+h+nAn bi na ya ka hU~M hU~M phaT phaT swA hA/ ces snying po ci 'grub bzlas/

A black mantra garland with red light rays emerges from hūṃ in my heart. It appears like rosary beads while the five-colored light rays thread them like a rosary string. It emerges from my mouth and enters Protector’s mouth, dissolving into the hūṃ in his heart. It arises again from hūṃ, emerges from Protector’s navel, enters my navel, and dissolves in the hūṃ at my heart. It circulates continuously in that way. oṃ vajra mahākāla saparivāra kṣiṃ kṣetra vighnān vināyaka hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā Repeat that however many times.

drag po'i bzlas pa dmigs pa gsal btab ste/ oM shri ma hA ka (637) la shA sa na/ u pa ha ri Ni/ e Sho pany+tsi ma/ kA lo‘yaM i daM rat+na tra yA ya/ a pa ka rI NaM/ ya ti pra ti dz+nyA/ sma ra si tA dA/ i daM duSh+TaM/ khA hi khA hi/ mA ra mA ra/ gr-ih+Na gr-ih+Na/ ban+d+ha ban+d+ha/ ha na ha na/ da ha da ha/ pa tsa pa tsa/ dI na me ke na mA ra ya hU~M phaT/ zhes pa ni drag sngags te 'bod rbad bsad gsum yang 'di la tshang bar bshad do/ /
oM shrI de wi hU~M phaT/ lha mo'i mtshan sngags so/ /
Śrīdevī’s namesake mantra: oṃ śrīdevī hūṃ phaṭ

oM k+She tra pA la big+h+nan hU~M phaT/ oM dzi na mi tra pa shaM ku ru hU~M phaT/ oM Ta k+ki rA dza sa ma ya b+h+yoHdu dza hU~M phaT/ oM du yo ga dza ma hA kA la trak+shad hU~M phaT/ las mkhan bzhi'i snying po'o/ /
The essence mantras of the four workers: oṃ kṣetrapāla vighnān hūṃ phaṭ oṃ jinamitra vāśaṃ kuru hūṃ phaṭ oṃ ṭakkirāja samaya bhyoḥ du jaḥ hūṃ phaṭ oṃ du yog ja mahākāla trakṣad hūṃ phaṭ

de ltar bzlas pa ci 'grub byas nas/ mthar mchod gtor/ badzra a mr-i ta sa bsang / swa b+hA lba sa sbyangs/ stong pa'i ngang las/ yaM las rlung / raM las me/ ka~M las mi mgo'i skyed bu gsum/ de'i steng du a las thod pa mtshan ldan yangs shing rgya che ba'i nang du b+h+rUM AM dzriM khaM hU~M rnams las sha lnga/ lA~M mA~M pA~M tA~M ba~M rnams las bdud rtsi lnga/ steng gi nam mkha' la oM dkar po a las zla ba/ hU~M las rdo rje rnams brtsegs pa/ rlung g.yos me sbar/ sha lnga bdud rtsi lnga 'od du zhu/ yi ge 'bru gsum las bdud rtsi'i rgyun babs/ de rnams kyi 'od kyis sangs rgyas thams cad kyi rdo rje gsum ye shes kyi bdud rtsir spyan drangs te thim/ oM dang zla ba rdo rje rnams kyang 'od du zhu zhing thim pas/ kha dog dri ro nus mthu phun sum tshogs pa zad mi shes pa bdud rtsi'i rgya mtshor gyur/

From within emptiness, wind comes from yaṃ, fire from raṃ, three human-head hearthstones from kaṃ. Upon that, from A, a vast and wide genuine skull cup containing the five meats arisen from bhrūṃ - āṃ - jiṃ - khaṃ - hūṃ and five elixirs from lāṃ - māṃ - pāṃ - tāṃ - vaṃ. In the space above them is a white oṃ [on] a moon from A and a vajra from hūṃ all stacked up. Wind blows, fire burns—the five meats and five elixirs melt into light. A stream of elixir flows from the three seed syllables. Light from all of that invokes the awareness elixir from the three vajras of all buddhas, which dissolves [into the skull cup]. The oṃ, moon, and vajra also melt into light and dissolve into it. It becomes an inexhaustible ocean of elixir with the most excellent color, scent, taste, potency, and power.
oM AHhU~M lan gsum brjod pas byin brlabs/
oṃ āḥ hūṃ (Repeat three times to consecrate.)
mgon po 'khor dang bcas pa'i ljags hU~M las byung ba'i rdo rje dmar po'i 'od kyi sbu gus gtor ma drangs te gsol bas thugs rgyud zag med kyi bde bas tshims nas dgyes par gyur/

The tongues of the Protector and retinue become tubes of red vajra light arisen from hūṃ, through which they suck up the torma and drink it. They are satisfied and delighted by the undissipating bliss in their mind streams.

snying po'i mthar/ i daM ba liM ta kha kha khA hi khA hi/ oM badzra ma hA kA la k+ShiM k+She tra big+h+nAn bi nA ya ka traka rak+mo ba liM ta maM sa rak+ta ru ti ra kha kha khA hi khA hi/ de bzhin du 'khor rnams la snying po'i mthar/ i daM ba liM ta kha kha khA hi khA hi/ zhes btags la/ lan gsum gsum gyis phul/ oM ma hA kA la sa pa ri wA ra ar+g+haM sogs kyis mchod/ /

After the essence mantra, add idaṃ baliṃta kha kha khāhi khāhi oṃ vajra mahākāla kṣiṃ kṣetra vighanen vināyaka trakrakmo baliṃta māṃsa rakta rutira kha kha khāhi khāhi Similarly, after the retinue’s essence mantras, add idaṃ baliṃta kha kha khāhi khāhi and offer three times each. Then offer with mahākāla sapārivāra arghaṃ…(etc.) and do the inner offering as before. {638}

nang mchod sngar bzhin phul la/ dpal ye (638) shes kyi mgon po legs ldan nag po/ bdud gcod kyi skyes bu/ srog gcod kyi shan pa/ bdud 'dul gyi dmag dpon/ srin po lang+ka pu ri'i grong khyer sum brtsegs brlag par mdzad pa/ rnal 'byor pa'i dgra lha/ rig 'dzin gyi srung ma/ dam nyams kyi srog bdud chen po 'khor dang bcas pa rnams dam rdzas rgyan dang ldan pa'i gtor ma 'di bzhes la/ sangs rgyas kyi bstan pa srungs/ dkon mchog gi dbu 'phang bstod/ dge 'dun gyi chos 'khor skyongs/ / bla ma'i sku tshe srings/ khyad par du dkon mchog gsum la gnod par byed pa dang / bdag cag 'khor dang bcas pa la bsam sbyor ngan par byed pa thams cad zhi bar mdzod cig / gal te zhi bas 'dul du ma 'tshal na bsad pa dang / bskrad pa dang / dbye ba dang / rengs pa dang / gzir ba dang / sdigs shing dpa' skong ba la sogs pa drag po'i phrin las kyis tshar bcad du gsol/ /

Glorious Awareness Protector, Excellent Black One, great being who cuts off devils, butcher who cuts the life force, commander who conquers devils, destroyer who thrice burned the rākṣasa city of Laṅkāpuri, war god of yogins, guardian of awareness holders, great devil of oath-breakers’ life force and retinue: please accept this sacred substance of decorated torma. Guard the Buddha’s doctrine, uplift the status of the Three Jewels, protect the dharma councils of the sangha, and prolong the life of the guru. In particular, pacify those who harm the Three Jewels or harbor evil in thought or deed toward us and our retinues. In case the peaceful methods do not subdue them, then please annihilate them with wrathful awakened activity such as killing, banishing, dividing, paralyzing, tormenting, intimidating, and terrorizing.

bla ma mgon po 'khor bcas la/ / bdag gis mchod gtor phul ba yis/ / dkon mchog dbu 'phang smad pa dang / / theg pa chen po sun 'byin dang / / bstan pa 'jig dang dbyen byed dang / / bla ma'i sku la bsdo ba dang / / rnal 'byor bdag la sdang ba rnams/ / de kun nag po chen pos sgrol/ / mA ra ya phaT/ sa ma ya/

Guru-Protector and retinue, since I present this offering torma, those who degrade the Three Jewels, discredit the Vajrayāna, destroy or divide the doctrine, threaten the guru’s body, or hate us yogins: Great Black One, liberate them! māraya phaṭ / samaya
bstod pa ni/ /
The praise:

hU~M/ myur mdzad spyan ras gzigs la phyag 'tshal lo/ / zhabs gdub dang bcas bi nA ya ka mnan/ / nag po chen po stag gi sham thabs can/ / phyag drug sbrul gyi rgyan gyis rnam par brgyan/ / g.yas pas gri gug bar pas phreng ba 'dzin/ / tha mas DA ma ru ni drag tu 'khrol/ /

hūṃ Homage to Swift-Acting Avalokita. Your bangled feet trample Vināyaka. Great Black One in a tiger-skin skirt, six arms well adorned by snake ornaments, top right hand holding flaying knife, the middle a rosary, and the last fiercely rattling a ḍamaru.

g.yon pas thod pa dang ni mdung rtse gsum/ / de bzhin zhags pa bzung nas 'ching bar byed/ / drag po'i zhal gdangs mche ba rnam par gtsigs/ / spyan gsum drag po'i dbu skra gyen du 'bar/ / dpral bar sin+d+hu ra yi thig les byugs/ /

Your left hands hold a skull, a trident, and a lasso that catches and binds. Your wrathful gaping mouth fully bares fangs. You have three eyes, wild hair streaming upward, and a spot of vermilion anoints your forehead.

spyi bor mi bskyod rgyal pos rgyas btab brtan/ / khrag 'dzag mi mgo lnga bcu'i (639) do shal can/ / rin chen thod skam lnga yis dbu la brgyan/ / shing las byon nas gtor ma len mdzad pa'i/ / dpal ldan phyag drug pa la phyag 'tshal bstod/ /

King Akṣobhya is the seal above your head. You wear a garland of fifty blood-dripping human heads and a crown of five skulls with jewel finials. {639} Come from your tree to accept the torma. Glorious Six-Armed One, I pay homage and praise.
b+h+yoH khrag mtsho chil chil khol ba'i klong dkyil na/ / tsho chen dre'u'i steng na gzi brjid 'bar/ / mthing nag sku la zhal gcig phyag gnyis ma/ / bdud kyi khram shing nad kyi rkyal pa bsnams/ /

bhyoḥ In a vast lake of bubbling, boiling blood, you sit astride a sturdy mule, ablaze with charisma. Dark blue, with one face and two arms, you hold a devil’s cross-scored board and a bag of pestilence.
sku yi sprul pas sangs rgyas bstan pa srung / / gsung gi sprul pas khams gsum g.yo bar byed/ / thugs ni mi 'gyur 'gro ba'i don mdzad ma/ / ma gcig re ma tI la phyag 'tshal lo/ /
Emanations of your body guard the Buddha’s doctrine. Emanations of your speech shake the three realms. Your immutable mind accomplishes beings’ welfare. Sole Mother Rematī: I pay homage to you.
hU~M/ dpal ldan mgon po'i phyogs bzhi'i bka' nyan pa/ / ye shes bka' sgrub las kyi pho nya mdzad/ / ma rungs kun 'dul sprul pa sna tshogs 'gyed/ / las byed pho nya bzhi la bdag cag bstod/ /

hūṃ Attendants in four directions around the glorious Protector, action messengers who accomplish Awareness’s commands, spreading various emanations to subdue all malevolent forces, four action messengers, I praise you.
dbang po gshin rje chu lha gnod sbyin dang / / me lha srin po rlung lha 'byung po dang / / steng gi tshangs pa sa yi lha mo ste/ / sprul pa'i phyogs skyong bcu la phyag 'tshal bstod/ /
Śakra, Yama, Varuṇa, Yakṣa, Agni, Rākṣasa, Vāyu, Bhūta, Brahmā above, and Earth Goddess: ten emanated direction protectors, I pay homage and praise.

dpal mgon bdun cu rtsa lnga dang / / dam can rgya mtsho'i dmag tshogs rnams/ / sha khrag gtor ma 'di bzhes la/ / rnal 'byor bdag cag 'khor bcas kyi/ / mi mthun rkyen dang bar chad sol/ / mthun pa'i dngos grub stsol ba dang / / bcol pa'i phrin las grub par mdzod/ /

Seventy-five glorious protectors and armies of an ocean of the oath-bound: accept this flesh-and-blood torma and dispel adverse conditions and obstacles, grant favorable spiritual powers, and accomplish all entrusted activity for us yogins and our retinues.

de nas 'og nas 'byung ba'i ting nge 'dzin gyi dbang bskur nyid dmigs pas bdag 'jug tu blangs/ slob ma'i rgyud byin gyis brlab pa'i don du 'dir yang bzlas pa cung zad bya/ slob ma rnams khrus bya/ gral la 'khod pa la me tog bkye bsdu byas te/ slob dpon gyis/

Then, with the visualization for the conferral of the absorption empowerment presented below, perform the self-induction. For the purpose of consecrating the mind streams of the disciples, also do some recitation here. Have the disciples wash and take their seats. Distribute and gather the flowers. The ritual master reads the following:

nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i sems can thams cad dpal he ru ka'i go 'phang la 'god par bya/ de'i ched du gnas skabs su phyi nang gsang ba'i bar chad gdon bgegs thams cad tshar gcod cing / rnam bzhi'i phrin las ci 'dod lhun gyis grub pa dang / mthar thug myur mdzad spyan ras gzigs kyi go 'phang mngon du bya ba'i slad du dpal (640) ye shes kyi mgon po phyag drug pa'i bka' gtad byin rlabs kyi rim pa gsan snyam pas ma yengs par lhag pa'i thugs bskyed gsal btab ste gsan par zhu/

You must establish all sentient beings equaling the reaches of space in the state of glorious Heruka. To that end, in the short term, all outer, inner, and secret obstacles of malicious spirits and obstructors must be severed and whatever desired awakened activity of the four kinds must be spontaneously achieved. Ultimately you must actualize the state of Swift-Acting Avalokita. In order to do that, think that you will listen to the stages of the entrustment blessing of glorious Six-Armed Protector without distraction while clearly imagining the higher thought of awakening. {640} So I ask you to pay attention.

de yang 'phags pa spyan ras gzigs dbang phyug chen po 'di nyid/ nges pa'i don du rgyal ba thams cad kyi 'char gzhi ste rgyal ba kun gyi yab tu gyur kyang / thun mong gi snang ngor rgyal ba'i sras kyi tshul bstan skabs/ / bskal ba mang por tshogs bsags sa bcu pa khyad par can brnyes/ 'od zer chen po'i dbang bskur thob/ rgyal sras thu bo'i gral du bzhugs skabs shig thugs bskyed kyi dam bca' 'di lta bu mdzad de/

Now, in terms of definitive meaning, Exalted Avalokiteśvara is certainly the basis of manifestation of all the victorious ones, and thus the father of all victors. However, to the perceptions of common folk, when manifesting in the manner of an heir of the victors, he gathered the accumulations for many eons and attained the tenth level [of a bodhisattva]. He received the empowerment of the great light rays. One time while remaining in the ranks of the powerful heirs of the victors, he took an oath of awakening mind such as this:

phyogs bcu rab 'byams mu med pa'i 'jig rten gyi khams 'dir/ bdag gis sems can gyi don bya/ sems can thams cad 'khor ba las bdag gis sgrol dgos pa las/ 'khor ba'i gnas 'dir sems can gcig kyang ma lus pa sangs rgyas kyi sa la ma 'khod bar du bdag sangs rgyas thob par mi bya/ sems can gcig kyang ma lus pa sangs rgyas kyi sa la bkod zin pa na/ de'i rjes su bdag nyid sangs rgyas thob na legs kyi/ gzhan du na bdag 'khor ba nyid du gnas te sems can gyi don bya'o/ / gal te bdag dam bca' 'di las 'das na lus tshal pa stong du 'gas par gyur cig ces dbu bsnyung mdzad/

In this world realm in the manifold universe, I will work for the welfare of sentient beings. I need to liberate all sentient beings from cyclic existence. Moreover, until I establish every single sentient being now in this place of cyclic existence in the state of a buddha, I myself will not attain buddhahood. When every sentient being, without a single exception, is placed in the state of a buddha, if I thereafter attain buddhahood, then it is all right. Barring that, I will remain in this cyclic existence and work for the welfare of sentient beings. Should I transgress this oath, may my body shatter into a thousand pieces. Thus he swore upon his head.

de nas brtsams te ri bo po ta lar bzhugs nas sprul pa mtha' yas pas skad cig re rer sems can dpag tu med pa smin grol du mdzad na gzhan tshad bzung bar ga la nus/ de lta bu bskal pa ji snyed gcig song nas/ dus lan gcig / da ni sems can mang po thar grol byung yod dgongs/ mngon shes kyis gzigs pas/ sems can gyi khams la 'phel 'grib med/ nyung du ma song ba'i khar sems can rnams snyigs ma lnga bdo bas gdul dka' bar gzigs nas da ni bdag gis sems can gyi don bya bar mi nus dgongs sngar gyi thugs bskyed (641) dam bca' btang ba'i tshul mdzad pa na sku lus tshal pa stong du gas skad/ der 'phags pa nyid kyi dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni 'od dpag med pa yin pas mngon sum du byon te/ rigs kyi bu khyod kyis de lta bu'i sems bskyed btang ba de ma legs/ da dam bca' slar gso ba sogs kyi don du sngar gyi de bas rgya che ba'i sems bskyed gyis shig gsungs/ sku lus tshal ba stong dbu bcu gcig ngang phyag stong du byin gyis brlabs so/ /

From that time on, he stayed on Mount Potala and with infinite emanations matured and liberated countless sentient beings every second. How could others ever measure up to that? In this way, a number of eons passed. Then one time he believed that now many sentient beings must be free and liberated, so he looked with his supernormal cognition. The number of beings in the realm had neither increased nor decreased. Regarding the fact that they had not diminished, he saw that sentient beings were difficult to train because they were subject to the proliferation of the five degenerations. He thought, “Now I am not capable of enacting the welfare of beings.” {641} As previously he had taken a solemn oath of awakening mind and proclaimed that [if transgressed] his body should shatter into a thousand pieces, now Avalokiteśvara’s own spiritual master Amitābha arrived in person and spoke: “Son of a good family, your arousal of the mind of awakening was no good. Now for the sake of repairing and restoring that solemn oath, you must generate a mind of awakening even greater than you did before.” Then he blessed him by splitting his body into a thousand parts: eleven heads and one thousand arms.

de nas dgongs pa slar yang rgya bskyed de snyigs ma lnga bdo ba'i sems can ma rungs pa rnams drag pos 'dul ba dang / chos byed rnams kyang bar do'i 'jigs pa las mi thar bar gzigs nas bar do las skyob pa dang / snyigs dus skye bo rnams dbul phongs kho na sdug bsngal che bas de'i gnyen por bsam pa tsam gyis dgos 'dod 'byung ba ste/ phrin las rnam pa gsum gyi sgo nas thugs bskyed snga ma las lhag pa'i tshul du dgongs/

Then again Avalokiteśvara aroused an even more vast mind of awakening: to wrathfully tame the intractable sentient beings during this proliferation of the five degenerations; to give protection from the intermediate state after he saw that even dharma practitioners were not escaping from its terrors; and to fulfill the needs and desires of living beings just by thinking of them as an antidote to the greatest single suffering of the degenerate age: poverty. By means of these three awakened activities, he realized that his arousal of awakening mind could be better than before.

'phags pa spyan ras gzigs kyi thugs ka nas hU~M gcig byung ste/ de nyid myur mdzad ye shes kyi mgon por gyur pa na/ zhing khams thams cad du sa rnam pa drug tu g.yos/ bcom ldan 'das 'od dpag tu med pa la sogs pa phyogs bcu'i de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyis mgrin gcig tu bsngags pa brjod/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi sku gsung thugs yon tan phrin las kyi sprul pa'i khro bo chen por dbang bskur zhing mnga' gsol lo/ / de nas brtsams te sangs rgyas kyi zhing khams thams cad du bstan pa bsrung zhing bzhugs pa lags/

A single hūṃ arose from Exalted Avalokita’s heart. Then that hūṃ became Swift-Acting Awareness Protector, and all the realms quaked six times. Bhagavat Amitābha and all the other tathāgatas in the ten directions sang praises with one voice. They invested him with the power of a great wrathful emanation of the body, speech, mind, qualities, and activities of all buddhas. Indeed, since that time he has remained to guard the doctrine in all the realms of the buddhas.

ye shes kyi mgon po chen po 'di nyid kyi sgrub skor 'phags bod kyi phyogs 'dir dar ba'i tshul dang / grub pa'i skyes bu rnams kyis rtags mngon gyur du bstan pa'i ngo mtshar rnam thar brjod las 'das shing / de dag gi lo rgyus rgyas pa rje btsun thams cad mkhyen pa'i gsung rabs sogs su gsal ba (642) la/

The manner in which the practice cycle of this great Awareness Protector spread in India and Tibet, and the life stories of great practitioners who displayed manifest wondrous signs [of his practice] are beyond telling. They are clearly described in exhaustive histories in the writings of omniscient Venerable [Tāranātha] and elsewhere. {642}

mdor bsdu na/ sangs rgyas shAkya thub pa mya ngan las 'das nas lo drug brgyar nye ba na/ grub thob chen po sha ba ri pa byon te grub pa brnyes/ mgon po 'di nyid zhal gzigs te srog sngags sgrub skor dang bcas pa gnang / phrin las thogs med du sgrub/ dpal sha ba ris/ rje btsun mai tri pa la gnang / rje mai tri pa ni/ bi kra ma shI lar bzhugs dus bskyed pa'i rim pa la brtan pa thob kyang gnas lugs kyi de nyid ma rtogs nas/ lhag pa'i lha la gsol ba btab pas/ lho phyogs dpal gyi rir song zhig / ri khrod mgon pos rjes su 'dzin par 'gyur zhes lung bstan pa ltar byon/ grub thob sha ba ris kyang phyag rgya chen po'i gdams pa mtha' dag stsal zhing dbang sgrub skor rnams gnang / gnas lugs kyi gzigs pa nam mkha' dang mnyam/ chos skyong bran bzhin khol bar gyur to/ / mai tri pa chen pos/ mkhas grub chen po khyung po lo tsA ba la gnang ste/

But in short, about six hundred years after the nirvana of Buddha Śākyamuni, there was a great adept called Śavarīpa who gained accomplishment. He directly perceived this protector in person and was given the life-force mantras and sādhana cycles. He accomplished boundless awakened activity. Glorious Śavariīpa bestowed these on Venerable Maitrīpa. Lord Maitrīpa, while in residence at Vikramaśīla, had attained stability in the creation stages but had not realized the suchness of the abiding nature. He supplicated his special deity, who replied, “Go south to the glorious mountain. The hermit protector will take care of you.” In accordance with this prophecy, he went there and the great adept Śavariīpa [“the Hermit”] granted all the instruction of mahāmudrā and gave him the empowerments and sādhana cycles. Then his vision of the abiding nature became as vast as the reaches of space. The dharma protector acted as his servant. Maitrīpa the Great gave all to the great learned adept Khyungpo Lotsāwa.

khyung po lo tsA ba de ni rus khyung po/ 'khrungs yul snye mor ram/ dang por bon dang / de nas chos rdzogs pa chen po gsan te nyan bshad sgom sgrub mdzad/ de nas kor ni ru pa bsten dgyes rdor dang phyag chen gyi skor mtha' dag gsan/ dgung lo lnga bcu nga gnyis bzhes pa la bal po dang rgya gar du phebs snga phyir rgya bal bod gsum du 'byon bzhugs mdzad/ thun mong dang thun mong ma yin pa'i bla ma brgya dang lnga bcu tsam bsten te/ gtso bo rdo rje gdan pa bsod nams 'byung gnas/ mai tri pa/ sbas pa'i rnal 'byor pa/ rA hu la/ ye shes kyi mkha' 'gro ma chen mo ni gu ma/ su kha sid+d+hi ste drug po de rnams rtsa ba'i bla ma mchog tu mdzad de/ bla ma dam pa de rnams kyi thugs bcud longs shing / mdo rgyud gzhung lugs man ngag thams cad la mkhas grub 'gran zla dang bral bar gyur/ bod du byon khar rje mai tri pa la bdag cag bod longs spyod chung bas nor sgrub myur la byin (643) rlabs che ba zhig zhu zhus pas/ mgon po 'di'i lo rgyus gsungs shing / gdams pa khyad par can yid bzhin kyi nor bu lta bu yin gsungs te dbang man ngag rnams gnang zhing lung bstan pa yang mdzad do/ /

Khyungpo Lotsāwa was born into the clan Khyung (garuḍa). His birthplace was Nyemo Rama[ng]. At first he adhered to Bön, but then he heard the teachings of the great completion and practiced their fine explications and meditations. Then he attended Kor Nirupa and received all the cycles of Hevajra and mahāmudrā. At the age of fifty-two he traveled to Nepal and India. Before and after he spent his time in India, Nepal, and Tibet. He attended one hundred and fifty common and extraordinary gurus, primarily Vajrāsana Puṇyākara, Maitrīpa, Hidden Yogi (Abhayākara), Rāhula, and the great Ḍākinīs of Timeless Awareness Niguma and Sukhasiddhi. Those six he adopted as his supreme root gurus. He took the heart essence of those holy gurus and became an unrivaled adept learned in Sutra, Tantra, and all the esoteric instructions of the source traditions. As he was about to return to Tibet, he asked Maitrīpa, “In my country Tibet, there is very little prosperity, therefore please grant me a blessing for the speedy attainment of wealth.” {643} Maitrīpa told him the story of this protector, saying that this special precept was like a wish-fulfilling gem. Then he gave him the empowerments and esoteric instructions, as well as making a prophecy.

grub thob chen po khyung po 'di ni sku lus kyi bkod pa brgya rtsa brgyad cig car ston pa dang / brag ri la thogs pa med par bzhud pa dang / yi dam dang mgon po rtag tu zhal gzigs/ sprul pa'i dmag bkye nus pa sogs rnam thar ngo mtshar dpag par dka' ba ste ches che ba'i grub thob yongs su grags pa dang / khyad par mgon po 'di nyid zhag bcu gsum sgrub pa'i tshul mdzad pas zhal mngon sum du bstan cing / de phyin chad bran bzhin du 'khol ba dang /

This great adept Khyungpo could display one hundred and eight emanations of his body at once, pass unhindered through mountain cliffs, and continually meet yidams and protectors in person. He had the ability to dispatch emanated armies and other feats in his amazing life story that is hard to fathom, bringing him the greatest fame as an accomplished adept. In particular, after following this protector’s custom of thirteen days of practice, Protector truly revealed himself. From then on, he could be recruited as a servant.

rdo rje gdan pa'i drung du gser srang brgyad cu'i tshogs 'khor chen pos grub thob rnams nyin zhag mang du mchod de bla ma yi dam mkha' 'gro chos skyong gi skal bzhus pa'i skabs su'ang / thams cad gcig bsdus mgon po 'di nyid kho na ched du bsngags shing / rigs kyi bu khyod dang khyod kyi slob ma brgyud 'dzin dang bcas pa la dbang bskur byin gyis brlab cing phrin las rnam pa lnga bsgrub par bya'o zhes mi 'gyur rdo rje'i tshig gis zhal 'ches pas/

Khyungpo Naljor went before Vajrāsana with eight hundred measures of gold for a great communal feast, which was offered to the adepts for many days. On the occasion of offering the share to the gurus, ḍākinīs, and dharma protectors, all together as one they commended this protector alone with the immutable vajra words of a final testament: “Fortunate son, you and your disciples who hold this lineage should confer empowerment blessings and accomplish the five awakened activities.”[10]

dpal ldan shangs pa bka' brgyud pa gtso bor gyur pa'i ye shes mkha' 'gro ni gu'i gdams pa nyams su len pa rnams la chos skyong 'dis ma bsgrubs par yang phrin las rnam bzhi thogs med du bsgrub pa/ sgrub pa po la zhal ston pa sogs ches cher 'go ba yin no/ /

Those who take up the practice of the instructions by Awareness Ḍākinī Niguma, who is the main source of the glorious Shangpa Kagyu, even without practicing this dharma protector, will accomplish the four awakened activities without hindrance. For practitioners, there are greater acts of his patronage, such as his revealing himself and so forth.

de lta bu'i ye shes mgon po'i chos skor phran tshegs ci rigs mkhas grub khyung pos slob ma gzhan dang gzhan la gnang ba yod mod kyang / la stod pa dkon mchog mkhar/ rtogs ldan zhang sgom chos seng / rmog lcogs pa rin chen brtson 'grus gsum la rdzogs par gnang bas snga ma las brgyud pa la mgon po lha dgu/ phyag stong (644) spyan stong rgyan can gyi skor mang po la sogs pa byin rlabs kyi sgo chen po dang ldan pa mtha' yas par bzhugs pa la ni mgon po stod lugs su grags la/ phyi ma gnyis kyi gdams ngag mtha' dag dbon ston skyer sgang ba chen po la 'dus/ des sangs rgyas gnyan ston/ des 'gro mgon sangs rgyas ston pa la gnang / de nas gcig brgyud kyi bka' rgya grol bas/ mkhas grub gtsang ma shangs ston dang bsam ldings pa gzhon nu grub/ ri gong gdan sa pa/ slob dpon a'i seng ge la sogs pa skal ldan rnams la 'chad 'gyur gyi bka' la sogs pa rgya cher stsal ba la mgon po smad lugs su grags pa ste/ de ltar bka' srol gtso bor gnyis las 'dir smad lugs yin/

Although Khedrup Khyungpo gave whatever minor parts of the Awareness Protector’s dharma cycle as appropriate to this or that person, there were three to whom he granted the complete cycle: Latöpa Könchok Khar, Tokden Zhangom Chöseng, and Mokchokpa Rinchen Tsöndru. {644} The lineage of the former [includes the practices of] Nine-Deity Protector, many cycles of Thousand-Armed Thousand-Eyed with Ornaments, and other countless [versions] that were great gates for blessings. This became known as the upper tradition. All the instructions of the latter two [lineages] were collected by Öntön Kyergangpa and passed to Sangye Nyentön, who in turn gave them to Drogön Sangye Tönpa. Then the seal of the one-to-one lineage was released [and the teachings were received] by Khedrup Tsangma Shangtön, Samdingpa Zhönu Drup, Rigong Densawa, Master Ayi Senge, and others. The explicated precepts and so forth that had been granted to these fortunate ones spread widely and became known as the lower tradition.

de la'ang gdan sa pa nas phag mo gru pa dang tshogs sde bzhi sogs la brgyud de dbus su dar rgyas chen po byung ba dang / bsam sdings lugs la lho gcod gnyis/ shangs ston slob ma 'jag pa la stod smad bar brgyud gsum sogs byung / de dag las mched de mgon po dkar mthing gi skor rnams sa kar gnyis kyis mtshon pa'i chos sde du mar 'phel/ rje btsun tsong kha pa yab sras kyis 'jag pa'i slob brgyud rnams las gsan te mgon po 'di'i phrin las bod dang bod chen po/ rgya sog gi rgyal khams tshun chad du da lta'i bar du rgya che la rgyun chags pa dang /

Of those two primary precept systems, here we are concerned with the lower tradition. That also passed from Densapa to the Pakmo Drupa and the four monastic communities.[11] Thus that lineage spread widely in Central Tibet. The Samding tradition has two sections: South (lho) and Severance (gcod). From Shangtön’s disciple Jakpa came three lineages: upper, lower, and middle. Branching out from those, many cycles of White and Deep-Blue Protectors (dGon po dkar mthing) arose, and many sets of teachings proliferated, as exemplified in both Sakya and Kagyu. The father-son line of Venerable Tsongkhapa received [these teachings] from Jakpa’s lineage disciples. This protector’s awakened activity thus spread widely, including in Tibet, Greater Tibet, China, and other countries, and continues to the present.

khyad par rin chen rnam bdun phyi ma nas jo nang rje btsun rin po cher bka' babs shing rje btsun nyid kyis thun mong ma yin pa'i chos skyong gi gtso bor mdzad/ de lta'i bar du byin rlabs kyi gzi byin ma nyams par bzhugs pa yin la/ de ltar mkhas grub byung po nas bzung brgyud pa'i bla ma rim par byon pa thams cad kyang shes bya kun la mkhyen pa rgyas shing mkhas btsun bzang po'i phul du gyur/ 'jig rten chos brgyad la ni thugs log / 'khor 'das thams cad ni sgyu ma lta bur gzigs/ gnas lugs kyi rtogs pa nam mkha' (645) dang mnyam/ byams snying rje phyogs med du khyab/ yi dam dpag tu med pa zhal gzigs/ chos skyong srung ma bran bzhin 'khol/ gzhan phan 'gro don rang shar lhun gyis grub pa ste/

In particular, from the Later Seven Jewels [of the Shangpa lineage] it fell as a special legacy to Jonang Jetsun Rinpoche. That Venerable [Tāranātha] himself made this extraordinary dharma protector his main one. Until now, the brilliance of the blessings remains undiminished. Since the time of Khedrup Khyungpo, all the gurus in the lineage of succession have possessed vast knowledge of all there is to know and have been exceedingly learned, righteous, and good. They turned away from the eight worldly concerns, saw all of cyclic existence and its transcendence as illusory, possessed realization of the abiding nature as vast as space, {645} were suffused with unbiased love and compassion, directly saw countless yidams, recruited dharma protectors and guards as if they were servants, and spontaneously accomplished self-arising altruistic benefit for others.

de lta bu'i skyes bu dam pa de rnams kyis thugs nyams su bzhes pa'i ye shes kyi mgon po chen po 'di la sgrub thabs kyi rigs bsam gyis mi khyab pa zhig bzhugs na'ang / rtsa bar gyur pa ni/ drag po mthu sgrub dang / zhi ba nor sgrub gnyis lags/ de gnyis kyi yang gtso bo drag po mthu sgrub yin cing / 'di la yang bka' rigs mi gcig pa mang du yod na'ang / de rnams kyi rtsa ba'i dbang bka' ni bar chad kun sel gyi bka' 'di nyid yin pas/

Such holy beings as these practiced an inconceivable variety of sādhanas of this great Awareness Protector. The main ones, however, were certainly the wrathful sādhana for magical power and the peaceful sādhana for wealth. Of those two, the primary one was the wrathful power sādhana, which has many different kinds of permission rituals. However, the root permission empowerment is this very permission of Removing All Obstacles.
'di sgrub par byed pa la slob dpon gyi bya ba rnams sngon du song / slob ma'i ngo skal du gyur pa yang sbyor dngos rjes gsum las/
In accomplishing this, the ritual master’s acts have already been done; now it is the disciples’ turn. This has three parts: (1) preparation, (2) main part, and (3) conclusion.
dang po sbyor ba la yang / maN+Dal 'bul ba/ gsol ba 'debs pa/ rtog pa bsdu ba/ thun mong ma yin pa'i skyabs 'gro sems bskyed pa/ thun mong ma yin pa'i gsol ba gdab pa ste drug yod pa las/
The preparation has six parts: (1) mandala offering, (2) supplication, (3) gathering thoughts, (4) uncommon refuge, (5) uncommon awakening mind, and (6) uncommon supplication.

dang po bla ma dang mgon po dbyer med pa'i spyan sngar ting nge 'dzin gyi dbang bskur zhu ba'i don du maN+Dal phul mdzod/ ces brda sbyar slob ma rnams kyis shangs lugs maN+Dal bka' rgya ma'am/ mi shes na spyi 'gro zhig phul/

First, in the presence of the Guru-Protector inseparable, offer a mandala in order to request the conferral of the meditative absorption (samādhi) empowerment. Indicate to the disciples to recite the Mandala of the Sealed Word from the Shangpa tradition.[12] If they do not know it, then they can do the general one.

gnyis pa gsol ba 'debs pa 'di'i rjes zlos mdzod/ rdo rje 'dzin pa dgongs su gsol/ / bdag ni 'gro la phan don du/ / gtso chen khyod la gsol 'debs kyi/ / mgon po'i dbang bskur bdag la stsol/ / lan gsum/

Second, repeat this supplication three times after me: “Vajra holder, please consider me. For the sake of benefiting migrators, I supplicate you, great principal one. Grant me the Protector’s empowerment.”
gsum pa rtog pa bsdu pa 'di gsan pas khyab bo/ /
Third, listen to this to gather your thoughts and fully receive it:
rtog pa thams cad legs par bsdus nas ni/ / shin tu bsam pa bzang dang ldan pas nyon/ / brjed ngas blo la rdo rje sems dpa' sogs/ / bde bar gshegs pa rnams kyis byin mi rlob/ /
Gather well all of your thoughts, and listen with an utterly good attitude. Vajrasattva and the other sugatas will not bless a forgetful mind.
zhes de ltar na snod kyi skyon gsum spangs te gsan 'tshal/
Thus give up the three faults of a vessel[13] and listen well. {646}

bzhi pa khyad par can gyi skyabs 'gro'i (646) don ni/ bla ma mgon po dbyer med la skyabs su 'gro ba yin pas 'di'i rjes zlos mdzod/ / phyogs bcu na bzhugs pa'i sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' thams cad dang / slob dpon dgongs su gsol/ bdag rig pa 'dzin pa zhes bgyi ba/ phyogs bcu na bzhugs pa'i bla ma la skyabs su mchi/ phyogs bcu na bzhugs pa'i sangs rgyas la= phyogs bcu na bzhugs pa'i chos la= phyogs bcu na bzhugs pa'i dge 'dun la= yi dam dkyil 'khor gyi lha tshogs dang ye shes kyi mgon po phyag drug pa'i lha tshogs 'khor dang bcas pa rnams la phyag 'tshal zhing skyabs su mchi'o/ / lan gsum/

Fourth, the meaning of the special refuge is that it is going for refuge to the guru inseparable from the Protector. Therefore, repeat this three times after me: “All buddhas and bodhisattvas dwelling in the ten directions, and the master, please consider me. I, who am called an awareness holder, go for refuge to the gurus who dwell in the ten directions. I go for refuge to the buddhas who dwell in the ten directions. I go for refuge to the dharma that dwells in the ten directions. I go for refuge to the sangha who dwells in the ten directions. I pay homage and go for refuge to the yidam mandala deities and to the deities of Six-Armed Awareness Protector and retinue.”
lnga pa rgyun bshags bya ba 'di'i rjes zlos mdzod/ dkon mchog gsum la bdag skyabs mchi/ / sogs gsum/
Fifth, repeat this regular confession three times after me: “I go for refuge in the Three Jewels…(dkon mchog gsum la bdag skyabs mchi…etc.).”

drug pa thun mong ma yin pa'i gsol ba gdab pa la yid kyis sprul pa'i mchod pas mchod par bsam la 'di'i rjes zlos mdzod/ bla ma dang myur mdzad ye shes kyi mgon po dbyer ma mchis pa la/ phyi me tog bdug spos/ nang sha lnga bdud rtsi lnga/ gsang ba bde stong gi ye shes/ / yang gsang de kho na nyid kyi mchod pa dam pa rnams 'bul lo/ / bzhes nas bdag la dbang bzhi rdzogs par bskur du gsol/ / lan gsum/ de dag gis dbang gi sbyor ba grub pa yin/

Sixth, for the uncommon supplication, think that you present mentally emanated offerings and repeat this three times after me: “Guru inseparable from the Swift-Acting Awareness Protector, to you I offer sublime outer flowers and incense, inner five meats and five elixirs, secret timeless awareness of bliss-emptiness, and the most secret suchness offering. Please accept and confer the complete four empowerments on me.” This completes the preparation for the empowerments.
gnyis pa dngos gzhi dbang dngos bskur ba la yang / / ye shes dbab pa/ sku gsung thugs kyi byin gyis brlab pa/ sku dngos kyis byin gyis brlab pa/ sngags gtad pa'i rjes gnang ste bzhi yod pa las/

Second, the main practice of the actual empowerment conferral has four parts: (1) descent of awareness; (2) blessing of awakened body, speech, and mind; (3) blessing of the actual awakened body; and (4) subsequent authorization focused on mantra.
dang po la dkyil 'khor du gzhug cing lha ngo bstan pa'i don dkyil 'khor gsal 'debs pa dang / ye shes phab pa dngos gnyis las/
The first of those involves the induction into the mandala and introducing the deities. It has the two parts of (1) visualizing the mandala and (2) the actual descent of the awareness beings.

dang po ni/ slob dpon dang mdun bskyed dbyer ma mchis pa mgon po 'khor bcas gsal 'debs pa yin te/ khyed rang rnams kyi mdun gyi nam mkhar srung ba'i 'khor lo'i nang mi bzad pa'i dur khrod chen po'i (647) dbus su/ pad+ma dang nyi ma'i steng du dpal tshogs kyi bdag po sku mdog dkar po glang po che'i dbu la spyan gsum la/ /

First, [the descent of awareness] is the visualization of the master as inseparable from the Protector and retinue in front. In the space before you, within a protection circle, is the unbearable great charnel ground. {647} In its center is a lotus and sun upon which is white Gaṇapati with a three-eyed elephant head.

phyag g.yas sa'i snying po la phug lo ma dang bcas pa zhal du gsol ba/ g.yon thod pa bdud rtsis gang ba 'dzin pa/ dar dang rin po ches brgyan pa nyal stabs su gnas pa/ de'i steng du myur mdzad ye shes kyi mgon po phyag drug pa/ skye 'gro'i re ba tshul bzhin du skong ba/ sku mdog dus mtha'i sprin ltar rab tu gnag pa/ zhal gcig phyag drug pa/ dmar la zlum pa'i spyan gsum sdang mig tu gzigs pa/ zhal gdangs shing mche ba gtsigs pa/ ljags 'dril ba/ rab tu bzhed pa/ sma ra dang smin ma dbu skra dmar ser gyen du brdzes pa/

In his right hand he holds at his heart a leafy daikon radish, the essence of earth, which he is eating. In his left hand he holds an elixir-filled skull cup. He is adorned with silks and precious jewels and is lying prone. Upon him stands Swift-Acting Six-Armed Awareness Protector, the perfect fulfiller of the hopes of living beings. He is very black, like the clouds at the end of time. He has one face and six arms. He glares angrily with three round, red eyes. His gaping mouth reveals his bared fangs and curled tongue as he laughs ferociously. His orange beard, eyebrows, and hair swirl upward.

dpral bar sin+d+hU ra'i thig les byugs pa/ spyi bor mi bskyod rgyal pos rgyas btab pa/ phyag g.yas dang pos rdo rje gri gug dang / g.yon dang pos thod pa khrag gis gang ba thugs kar steng 'og tu 'dzin pa/ g.yas bar pas thod skam gyi phreng ba/ tha mas DA ma ru drag tu 'khrol ba/ g.yon gnyis pa na mdung rtse gsum pa/ tha ma na rdo rje zhags pa bsnams pa/ zhabs gnyis srid gsum rnam par gnon pa'i shugs can mnyam pa'i stabs krig krig zhabs kyis bgegs kyi rgyal po mnan pa/

His forehead is anointed with a drop of vermilion. King Akṣobhya crowns his head. He holds a vajra flaying knife in his top right hand and a blood-filled skull cup with the left; one above the other at his heart. In his middle right hand is a rosary of dry skulls, and in the lower one he fiercely rattles a ḍamaru. He holds a trident spear in his second left hand and a vajra lasso in the last left hand. His two legs, with the strength to totally suppress the three existences, stand in a perfectly straight, even position, pressing down on the Obstructor King.

stag lpags kyi sham thabs la/ dar ljang gu'i ske rags bcings pa/ sbrul sngon pos dbu skra bcings shing / dmar pos snyan cha/ khra bos dpung rgyan/ dkar po'i mgul rgyan/ ser po'i lag gdub/ ljang gu'i do shal/ dkar po'i rkang gdub dang ska rags can/ phyag zhabs thams cad la dril bu g.yer kha'i phreng ba dang ldan pa/ sbom thung yan lag hrag pa/ gzi brjid mtha' yas pa/ mi mgo skam po lnga'i dbu rgyan rin po che'i rtse bran can dang / rlon pa khrag 'dzag lnga bcu'i do shal byas pa/ rus pa'i rgyan drug gis mdzes pa/ (648) 'jigs pa'i nga ro 'brug ltar sgrogs pa/ bdud dang bgegs thams cad brlag par mdzad pa/ bskal pa'i me lta bu'i ye shes kyi me dpung 'bar ba'i dbus na bzhugs shing / tsan+dan gyi sdong po la rgyab brten pa'o/ /

He wears a tiger-skin skirt tied with a green silk sash. Blue snakes bind his hair, and he has red snake earrings, striped snake armbands, white snake collar, yellow snake bracelets, green snake necklace, and white snake anklets and belt. On all his arms and legs are strings of large and small bells. He is short and fat, with thick limbs. He has boundless charisma. He has a crown of five dry human skulls topped with jewel finials and a garland of fifty fresh skulls dripping with blood. The six bone ornaments beautify him. {648} His terrifying roars resound like thunder, annihilating all devils and obstructors. He stands supported by the trunk of a sandalwood tree amid a bonfire of timeless awareness like the fire at the end of the eon.

de'i g.yon du khrag zhag 'khrugs pa'i rgya mtsho'i dbus su/ dpal ldan lha mo 'dod pa khams kyi dbang phyug ma/ sku mdog nag mo phyag g.yas bdud kyi khram shing nag po phyar zhing / g.yon nad kyi rkyal pa 'dzin pa/ me rlung 'tshubs ma'i dbus na bzhugs shing / dre'u rta rkang gsum la chibs pa/ 'khor sha za dang ma mo mkha' 'gro 'bum sdes bskor ba'o/ /

To his left, in the middle of an ocean of turbulent blood and fat, is Śrīdevī, mighty queen of the desire realm. She is black, waving a devil’s black cross-scored board in her right hand and grasping a bag of pestilence with her left. She stands in the midst of a conflagration of fire and wind, riding on a three-legged mule. Her retinue of a hundred thousand flesh-eating mātṛkās and ḍākinīs surrounds her.

gtso bo'i mdun du gnod sbyin k+She tra pa la/ sku mdog mthing nag kha gdangs shing mche ba gtsigs nas dgra la 'o dod 'bod pa/ shangs nas dus mtha'i rlung ldang ba/ phyag g.yas gri gug nam mkha' la phyar bas lha dang lha ma yin thams cad skrag par byed pa/ g.yon thod khrag dgra bgegs kyi snying dang bcas pa zhal du stob cing dom nag smyon pa la chibs pa/

In front of the principal, Yakṣa Kṣetrapāla, blue-black with a gaping mouth and bared fangs, bellows at his enemies. Winds of the end-times rise from his nose. With his right hand he brandishes a flaying knife to the sky, terrifying all the gods and demigods. With his left hand he feeds the principal’s mouth from a blood-filled skull cup containing the hearts of enemies and obstructors. He rides a crazed black bear.
g.yas su dbang phyug dzi na mi tra sku mdog dkar nag g.yas DA ma ru 'khrol zhing / g.yon thod khrag 'dzin pa/
To the right, dark-red Īśvara Jinamitra fiercely rattles a ḍamaru with his right hand and holds a blood-filled skull cup with the left.
rgyab tu gshin rje TAk+ki rA dza sku mdog dkar nag / phyag g.yas zhags pa dgra la 'phen cing / g.yon sdigs mdzub gnod byed la sdigs pa/
In back, the gray Yama Ṭakkirāja throws a lasso at enemies with his right hand and points at harm-doers with his left hand in the threatening gesture.

g.yon du bdud mgon chen po trak+shad sku mdog nag po phyag g.yas su mtshon mdung dmar rtse gsum pa dgra po'i snying gar bsnun pa/ g.yon thod pa khrag gis gang ba bsnams pa/ ya sos ma mchu mnan pa/ dar nag gi 'jol ber dang / sag ti'i l+h+wam yu ring gsol ba/ gser gyi ske rags bcings pa/ bdud rta nag po rting dkar la chibs pa/ bzhi ka'ang khro bo'i las mkhan gyi cha byad yongs su rdzogs pa'o/ /

To the left, the great devil lord black Trakṣad pierces the enemies’ hearts with a red three-pronged ensign spear in his right hand and holds a blood-filled skull cup in this left. He bites his lower lip. He wears a black cloak, high rawhide boots, and a golden belt. He rides a black devil horse with white fetlocks. All four are completely perfect in the garb of wrathful emissaries.

de'i phyi rol du shar du brgya byin/ shar lhor me lha/ lhor gshin rje/ lho nub tu srin po/ nub tu (649) chu lha/ nub byang du rlung lha/ byang du gnod sbyin/ byang shar du 'byung po/ steng du tshangs pa/ 'og tu bdag ste phyogs skyong bcu/ gzhan yang lha chen po brgyad/ klu chen po brgyad/ gza' chen po brgyad/ 'jigs byed chen po dgu/ rgyu skar nyi shu rtsa brgyad/ rgyal po chen po bzhi ste/ gtsang rigs gyi mgon po bdun cu rtsa lnga po thams cad kyang 'khor bye ba bye ba'i tshogs kyis bskor ba/ de'i phyi rol du dam can rgya mtsho'i dmag tshogs sha la dga' ba/ khrag la rol pa/ snying rje med pa/ kha gdangs pa/ mig rtsa dmar ba/ lag na gdug pa'i mtshon cha sna tshogs thogs pa skad cig la skye 'gro thams cad kyi srog dbugs sdud pa/ gnod sbyin dang / srin po dang / gshin rje dang / bdud dang ma mo'i cha lugs can/ sa gzhi bar snang nam mkha'i dbyings thams cad yongs su gang ba/ thams cad kyang sgrub pa po'i re 'dod tshul bzhin du skong bar mdzad pa'o/ /

The ten direction protectors are outside of them: Śakra in the east, Agni in the southeast, Yama in the south, Rākṣasa in the southwest, Varuṇa in the west, {649} Vāyu in the northwest, Yakṣa in the north, Bhūta in the northeast, Brahmā above, and Bhūpati below. All around them are the eight great gods, the eight great nāgas, the eight great planets, the nine great terrifiers, the twenty-eight constellations, and the four great kings. All these seventy-five protectors of the pure clans are each surrounded by a retinue of millions. Outside of them are the armies of an ocean of the oath-bound—loving flesh, reveling in blood, merciless, open-mouthed, bloodshot-eyed, and bearing various lethal weapons in their hands—in an instant they can suck the life force out of all living beings. They wear the garb of yakṣas, rākṣasas, yāmas, māras, and mātṛkās. They completely cover the ground and fill all the sky and space. All are fulfilling the hopes and desires of practitioners.

de lta bu'i bla ma mgon po dbyer med pa la/ mos gus dung pa byas pas thugs ka nas 'od zer bun gyis 'phros/ khyed rang rnams kyi lus la phog pas lus ngag yid gsum gyi sdig sgrib thams cad bsregs/ ma dag pa'i snang ba thams cad sbyangs nas 'od phung du gyur pa'i mos pa mdzod/ de nyid la slob dpon gyis/ oM swA b+hA lba nas haM/ zhes brjod pas 'od gsal stong pa nyid du gyur/ stong nyid de'i ngang las khyed rang rnams kyi go sar pa~M las pad+ma dang / raM las nyi ma'i steng du/ gaM dkar po 'od du zhu ba las dpal tshogs kyi bdag po sku mdog dkar po glang po che'i dbu la spyan gsum pa phyag g.yas sa'i snying po la phug lo ma dang bcas pa zhal du gsol ba/ g.yon thod pa bdud rtsis gang ba 'dzin pa/ dar dang rin po ches brgyan pa nyal stabs su gnas pa/ de'i steng du khyed rang rnams kyi sems nyid hU~M mthing nag las gri gug hU~M gis mtshan pa/ de las 'od zer (650) 'phros/ dgra bgegs gdug pa can thams cad tshar bcad/ 'phags pa mchod/ sems can gyi don byas/ slar 'dus te thim pa yongs su gyur pa las/ khyed rang rnams myur mdzad ye shes mgon po sogs nas/ tsan+dan gyi sdong po la rgyab brten pa'o/ /

Your yearning devotion to Guru-Protector inseparable causes a haze of light rays to radiate from the heart. It strikes your body and incinerates all negativities and obscurations of your body, speech, and mind. Imagine that all impure appearances are refined and become masses of light. That turns into lucid clarity-emptiness when the master says oṃ svabhāva…(etc. to)…haṃ. From within that emptiness, a lotus from paṃ and a sun from raṃ appear in your stead. Upon that, a white gaṃ melts into light and becomes glorious Gaṇapati, white with a three-eyed elephant head, holding in his right hand a leafy daikon radish, the essence of earth, which he is eating. In his left hand is an elixir-filled skull cup. He is adorned with silks and precious jewels and is lying down. Upon him, your mind itself is a blue-black hūṃ, from which comes a flaying knife marked with hūṃ. {650} Light rays radiate from that and terminate all enemies, obstructors, and noxious spirits. The light makes offerings to the exalted beings and helps sentient beings. It again returns and dissolves, completely transforming you into Swift-Acting Awareness Protector…(etc. to)…like the fire at the end of the eon.

de ltar gsal ba'i dpral bar oM dkar po/ mgrin par AHdmar po/ thugs kar hU~M sngon po/ slob dpon gyi thugs ka'i hU~M las 'od zer 'phros/ shar lho dur khrod chen po bsil ba'i tshal/ / tsan+dan gyi shing rkang gcig pa'i drung nas myur mdzad ye shes kyi mgon po phyag drug pa/ steng na rtsa brgyud kyi bla ma/ g.yas na dpa' bo ngar dang bcas shing / g.yon na dpa' mo 'dzum dang bcas pa/ bka' sdod zhing skyong pho nya/ dam can rgya mtsho'i dmag tshogs dang bcas pa thams cad skad cig nyid la/ DA ma ru dang dril bu g.yer kha'i sgra si li li/ khro lo lo/ 'ur 'ur chem chem byon te khyed rang rnams kyi lus la gnyis su med par thim/

In that clearly visualized appearance, white oṃ is at the forehead, red āḥ at the throat, and blue hūṃ at the heart. Light rays radiate from the hūṃ in the master’s heart and invoke Swift-Acting Six-Armed Awareness Protector from in front of the single trunk of the sandalwood tree in the great charnel ground Cool Grove in the southeast. He arrives instantly with the root and lineage gurus above him, grimacing heroes on his right, smiling heroines on his left, and all the armies of obedient ones, realm protectors, messengers, and an ocean of the oath-bound, accompanied by the sounds of ḍamarus, bells, and small bells—si li li, khro lo lo, ur ur, chem chem. He dissolves indivisibly into your body.
rol mo'i sgra cher bya/ dam rdzas spos kyi dud pa brtul/
Play loud music. Circulate the incense smoke of pledge substances.

oM badzra ma hA kA la sa pa ri wA ra k+ShiM k+ShiM k+ShiM sogs nyer gcig / k+ShiM gyi gnas su e h+ye hi bcug pa dang / badzra sa mA dzaH bcug pa rnams lan gsum gsum/ myur mdzad 'khor bcas spyan drangs/ slob ma'i lus la dzaHhU~M baM hoH gnyis su med par thim par gyur/ zhes brjod de ye shes dbab pa'i rim pa'o/ /

oṃ vajra mahākāla saparivāra kṣiṃ kṣiṃ kṣiṃ…(etc.) (Repeat kṣiṃ a total of twenty-one times. In place of kṣiṃ insert) e hye hi (and) vajra samājaḥ (three times each). Swift Actor and retinue are invoked—jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ—they dissolve indivisibly. With that, the stage of the descent of awareness beings is done.

gnyis pa sku gsung thugs kyi byin gyis brlab pa'i don du dmigs pa 'di bzhin mdzod/ bla ma dang mdun bskyed mgon po dbyer ma mchis pa'i spyi bor oM dkar po/ mgrin par AHdmar po/ thugs kar hU~M mthing ga gsal btab la/ dbang bzhi rdzogs par bskur du gsol/ khyad par bum pa'i dbang bskur du gsol snyam pa'i yid kyis gsol ba dung dung btab pas/ bla ma mgon po dbyer med kyi dpral ba'i oM las 'od 'phros/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi sku'i byin rlabs thams cad 'od zer dkar po'i rnam par tshur bsdus te oM la thim/ oM las 'od zer dkar po dpag tu med pa byung ste khyed rang rnams kyi dpral ba'i oM la thim pas bum dbang thob (651) pa'i mos pa mdzod/

Second, for the blessing of awakened body, speech, and mind, do the following visualization: In Guru inseparable from the Protector in front, white oṃ appears clearly in the head, red āḥ in the throat, and blue hūṃ in the heart. Think, “Please confer the complete four empowerments. Please confer the vase empowerment in particular.” Your yearning mental supplication causes light rays to radiate from the oṃ in the forehead of the Guru-Protector inseparable. They gather up all the blessings of all buddhas’ awakened body in the form of white light rays, which return and dissolve into the oṃ. Immeasurable white light rays emerge from the oṃ and dissolve into the oṃ in your forehead. Imagine that you receive the vase empowerment. {651}
brjod la rol mo bya/
Say that and play music.

yang gsang dbang bskur du gsol/ mgrin pa'i AHgsung gi byin rlabs/ mgrin pa'i AHlas 'od zer dmar po/ khyed rang rnams kyi mgrin pa'i AHla thim pas gsang dbang thob pa'i mos pa mdzod/ / ces 'don 'gyur rigs 'gre/

“Now, please confer the secret empowerment”…light rays radiate from the āḥ in the forehead…blessings of all buddhas’ awakened speech…red light rays emerge from the āḥ in the throat and dissolve into the āḥ in your throat. Imagine that you receive the secret empowerment. In this way apply the same pattern:

shes rab ye shes kyi dbang bskur du gsol/ thugs ka'i hU~M/ thugs kyi byin rlabs/ thugs ka'i hU~M las 'od zer mthing ga/ khyed rang rnams kyi snying ga'i hU~M la thim pas/ sher dbang thob pa'i mos pa mdzod/

“Please confer the wisdom-awareness empowerment”…light rays radiate from the hūṃ in the heart…blessings of all buddhas’ awakened mind…dark-blue light rays emerge from the hūṃ in the heart and dissolve into the hūṃ in your heart. Imagine that you receive the wisdom empowerment.

yang dbang bzhi pa bskur du gsol snyam pa dang / bla ma mgon po dbyer med la mos gus dung ba byas pas/ gnas gsum gyi yi ge 'bru gsum po de nyid rgyangs kyis chad nas byon/ khyed rang rnams kyi gnas gsum yi ge 'bru gsum la thim/ khyed rang rnams kyi snying ga'i hU~M mgrin pa'i AHla thim/ de yang spyi bo'i oM la thim/ oM yang nam mkha' la 'ja' yal ba bzhin du gyur/ des lus ngag yid gsum tha dad du 'dzin pa'i sgrib pa dag nas/ dbang bzhi pa thob pa yin pas/ sems spros bral phyag rgya chen po la zhog mdzod/

Again think, “Please confer the fourth empowerment.” Your yearning devotion to Guru inseparable from the Protector causes [a second set of] the three seed syllables in his three places to break off completely and dissolve into the three seed syllables in your three places. The hūṃ in your heart dissolves into the āḥ in your throat. That also dissolves into the oṃ in your head. The oṃ vanishes like a rainbow in the sky. That purifies the obscuration of fixating on the distinctions of body, speech, and mind, and you receive the fourth empowerment. Rest in mahāmudrā free of mental embellishment.
rol mo/
Play music.

gsum pa sku dngos kyi byin gyis brlab pa ni/ gtor ma 'di nyid myur mdzad ye shes kyi mgon po 'khor bcas su gsal ba la mos gus dung pa byas pas/ 'ur 'ur chem chem rang gi spyi bor byon/ bla mas khyed rang rnams kyi bar chad bsrung ba dang / mthun rkyen sgrub par bka' bsgos pa'i tshe/ khyed rang rnams kyi nad gdon dgra bgegs thams cad mgon po'i zhal du sha chom rus chom du gsol zhing / rigs kyi bu khyod kyi bar chad bsrung ba dang / mthun rkyen sgrub par ngas bya'o/ / zhes gsung lhang lhang byon par bsgom mdzod/

Third is the blessing of the actual awakened body. Visualize that the torma itself is Swift-Acting Awareness Protector with retinue, and through your yearning devotion they arrive above your head with a great rush and rumble. When the guru gives the command to guard against obstacles and achieve favorable conditions, Protector chomps the flesh and chomps the bones, consuming all your sickness, bad spirits, enemies, and obstructors. Meditate that he arrives and loudly declares: “Child of good family, I will guard against your obstacles. I will achieve your favorable conditions.”

ces gtor ma slob ma'i spyi bor bzung la/ rol mo dang bcas pas bka' bsgo ba ni/ mgon po 'khor bcas kyi sngags brjod pa'i mthar/ dpal ye shes kyi mgon po nag po chen po phyag drug pa/ (652) ma gcig 'dod pa khams kyi dbang phyug ma/ 'khor gnod sbyin k+She tra pA la/ dbang phyug dzi na mi tra/ gshin rje TAk+ki rA dza/ bdud mgon trak+shad nag po/ phyogs skyong bcu/ gtsang rigs kyi dpal mgon bdun cu/ dam can rgya mtsho'i dmag tshogs dang bcas pa/ khyed rnams kyis rgyal ba khyab bdag rdo rje 'chang chen po/ dpal ldan sha ba ri dbang phyug / grub chen mai tri pa chen po/ rA hu la gup+ta/

Hold the torma on the disciples’ heads and with music do the exhortation: say the mantras of Protector and entourage, and Glorious Six-Armed Awareness Protector, {652} One Mother mighty queen of the desire realm, and retinue of the Yakṣa Kṣetrapāla, Īśvara Jinamitra, Yama Ṭakkirāja, black devil-lord Trakṣad, ten direction protectors, and the glorious seventy-five of the pure clans, all with your armies of an ocean of oath-bound protectors, do not contravene the commands and commitments to these glorious gurus: Pervasive Lord Great Vajradhara, mighty glorious Śavarīpa, great adept Maitrīpa, Rāhulagupta,

mkhas grub khyung po lo tsA ba/ rmog lcog pa rin chen brtson 'grus/ skyer sgang pa ye shes seng ge /gnyan ston spas pa'i rnal 'byor/ chos rje sangs rgyas ston pa/ shangs ston rin chen 'bum/ khyung po tshul khrims snying po/ grub chen sangs rgyas seng ge /mkhas btsun shangs dkar ba rin chen rgyal mtshan/ /lkug lung pa sangs rgyas dpal bzang / grub dbang nam mkha' rgyal mtshan/ rgya sgom legs pa rgyal mtshan/ rnal 'byor sems kyi mdud 'grol/ chos sku lha dbang grags pa/ rje btsun sgrol ba'i mgon po/ kun dga' bstan pa'i rgyal mtshan/ ngag dbang kun dga' lhun grub/ rwa pa ngag dbang phrin las/ chos rje kun bzang dbang po/ rig 'dzin tshe dbang nor bu/ bka' brgyud phrin las shing rta/ bstan 'dzin chos kyi nyi ma/ bka' brgyud phrin las rnam rgyal/ rtsa ba'i bla ma byams mgon rdo rje 'chang pad+ma nyin byed dbang po'i bar du byon pa'i dpal ldan bla ma de rnams kyi bka' dang dam las ma 'da' bar/ rdo rje slob ma 'di dag gi lus dang grib ma bzhin du 'grogs la/

Khedrup Khyungpo Lotsāwa, Mokchokpa Rinchen Tsöndru, Kyergangpa Yeshe Senge, Nyentön Bepe Naljor, Chöje Sangye Tönpa, Shangtön Rinchen Bum, Khyungpo Tsultrim Nyingpo, Drupchen Sangye Senge, Khetsun Shangkarwa Rinchen Gyaltsen, Kuklungpa Sangye Palzang, Drupwang Namkha Gyaltsen, Gyagom Lekpa Gyaltsen, Naljor Semkyi Dudrol, Chöku Lhawang Drakpa, Jetsun Drolwai Gönpo, Kunga Tenpai Gyaltsen, Ngawang Kunga Lhundrup, Rwapa Ngawang Trinle, Chöje Kunzang Wangpo, Rikzin Tsewang Norbu, Kagyu Trinle Shingta, Tenzin Chökyi Nyima, Kagyu Trinle Namgyal, up to my root guru Jamgön Dorjechang Pema Nyinje Wangpo—all the glorious holy gurus: do not transgress their commands and vows. Accompany these vajra disciples like a shadow follows the body.
